chain_steps.what_happens: Sensors and humans generate raw observations: EO/IR and SAR imagery, full-motion video, GMTI radar, SIGINT/ESM intercepts, air-defense radar plots, acoustic, HUMINT reports, blue-force position reports, logistics status. Collection is tasked by collection managers but much is continuous (radars, SATCOM ISR, ADS-B-like tracks).
chain_steps.who_performs: ISR crews (RC-135, MQ-9, E-2D, P-8), satellite operators (NRO, SDA tracking layer, commercial EO), radar operators (Patriot/THAAD/AN-TPQ-53 crews), small-UAS operators at platoon-company (Ghost-X class), scouts/forward observers, SIGINT teams; echelons from squad to national agencies.
chain_steps.hardware: Satellites (NRO Starshield-based constellation; SDA tracking layer), aircraft sensors, ground radars (AN/TPQ-53, TPY-6), sUAS (Ghost-X named in NGC2 Ivy Sting feeds), soldier devices (ATAK end-user devices), vehicle sensors.
chain_steps.software: Sensor firmware and payload controllers; MISB KLV metadata encoders for FMV; radar plot extractors; collection management tools (e.g., within DCGS family, Maven Smart System collection views - inferred).
data_formats_protocols: STANAG 4609 / MISB ST 0601 KLV (FMV metadata) - verified via open-source parsers (paretech/klvdata, QGISFMV)
STANAG 4607 (NATO GMTI format) - verified (MITRE paper; pentlandedge/s4607)
NITF / STANAG 4545 (still imagery) - verified via codice/alliance, bradh/jim
STANAG 4658 (ESM) - single snippet only, LOW confidence
Cursor on Target (CoT) XML for sUAS/soldier reports - verified (MITRE Event.xsd v2.0, 2003)
chain_steps.human_in_loop: Sensor operators steer payloads; collection managers prioritize; FMV/GMTI mostly machine-generated, HUMINT fully human.
chain_steps.latency_sources: Sensor revisit rate, satellite downlink windows (mitigated by laser crosslinks - NRO says minutes-to-seconds), aircraft datalink availability, operator queueing.
chain_steps.comms_dependencies: Downlink/backhaul (SATCOM, CDL, line-of-sight datalinks, mesh radios) to move raw data off the sensor.
chain_steps.when_connectivity_disappears: Sensor continues recording locally (store-and-forward); tactical sensors publish to local mesh/TAK server; national/airborne ISR products become unavailable to disconnected units.
chain_steps.interoperability_requirements: Standard container/metadata formats (KLV, 4607, NITF) so downstream PED tools can ingest; CoT for tactical SA.
chain_steps.security_domain: Ranges from Unclassified/CUI (sUAS FMV) through S and TS/SCI (national ISR, SIGINT). Coalition releasability determined at collection tagging.
chain_steps.owning_organizations: NRO/NGA/NSA (national), SDA (space transport/tracking), service ISR wings (ACC ISR, Navy VP/VQ, Army MI brigades), PEO IEW&S (Army sensors), PEO Aviation; Marine MIGs.

chain_steps.security_domain: Crypto-separated enclaves by classification; Link 16 is Secret-level; coalition networks (CENTRIXS/BICES/SABRE) separately keyed.

cross_cutting_observations.observation: The Army has converged NGC2's ingest/normalize/store layers on a two-vendor baseline (Lattice tactical, Foundry cloud) plus Raft registries; every future NGC2 app is expected to run on it.
cross_cutting_observations.evidence: Army statement June 22, 2026; Palantir and Anduril releases; Raft named by MeriTalk.
cross_cutting_observations.label: FACT

cross_cutting_observations.observation: NGC2 cost is large and unbounded publicly: >$1B for 4ID full stack; potentially several $B per year; $3.3B identified through FY26; ~$904M FY27 RDT&E requested; no lifecycle cost estimate or unit-by-year schedule; goal 11 divisions and 4 corps by FY2032.
cross_cutting_observations.evidence: GAO report Aug 20, 2026; Military Times Aug 4, 2026.
cross_cutting_observations.label: FACT

cross_cutting_observations.observation: Contract ceilings dominate headlines and must not be read as revenue: Anduril's Army enterprise agreement carries a $20B ceiling; Maven ceiling ~$1.3B through 2029; TITAN actual production obligation is $192M for 8 systems.
cross_cutting_observations.evidence: Benzinga/Anduril June 23, 2026; DefenseScoop May 2025; Military Times Sept 2, 2026.
cross_cutting_observations.label: FACT

cross_cutting_observations.observation: Field results at PC-C6 (July 20-29, 2026; ~9,000-10,000 personnel, six brigades, 90+ technologies) showed 'common visualization' success but intermittent connectivity and equipment overheating; the Army's evaluation criteria include kill-chain speed, survivability, jamming effects, cognitive load and allied interoperability.
cross_cutting_observations.evidence: Secondary reports citing Axios; Business Insider July 29-30, 2026; National Defense Aug 18, 2026.
cross_cutting_observations.label: FACT

cross_cutting_observations.observation: Policy, not technology, is the binding constraint on cross-service and coalition data sharing, per GAO (overly restrictive classification) and an industry panelist at AFA 2026 ('not actually a technological impediment... policy impediments').
cross_cutting_observations.label: FACT

cross_cutting_observations.observation: Fire-control-grade fusion remains a separate, hardware-coupled world (IBCS in full-rate production since Nov 2025, Aegis, Link 16) from the software COP world; Link 16 and C2BMC are described by FDD as purpose-built workarounds rather than unified C2.
cross_cutting_observations.label: FACT

cross_cutting_observations.observation: Space transport is arriving but late: SDA Tranche 1 Transport had 63/126 satellites on orbit by July 16, 2026 after a months-long pause; cross-vendor laser mesh not yet demonstrated; SpaceX won a $2.29B LEO backbone award (May 2026).
cross_cutting_observations.evidence: SpaceNews July 16 and May 26, 2026; Tech Times July 14, 2026.
cross_cutting_observations.label: FACT

cross_cutting_observations.observation: Autonomy C2 is a demonstrated failure point: Replicator delivered hundreds, not thousands, of systems by Aug 2025, hobbled partly by software unable to command large heterogeneous drone sets; DIU issued C2/ACT software prototype awards to seven companies (Nov 2024).
cross_cutting_observations.evidence: Tech Times citing CRS, July 16, 2026; Aviation Today Sept 4, 2025.
cross_cutting_observations.label: FACT (secondary)

cross_cutting_observations.observation: The app layer on the new data platforms is where non-prime startups are visibly winning slots: Onebrief (planning), Air (sustainment), Striveworks (MLOps), Govini, Rune, RII, Instant Connect, Ditto (DDIL sync, USMC).
cross_cutting_observations.evidence: Vendor releases June-July 2026 naming NGC2 partner sets.
cross_cutting_observations.label: FACT (vendor-stated participation; contract values undisclosed)

cross_cutting_observations.observation: Anduril publishes Lattice SDKs in six languages (since Aug 2024) with an entity model including MIL-STD-2525C and mil_view.disposition overrides, and an AI-skills repo (July 2026); technical openness of the API is real, but commercial terms, data rights and government-side licensing are not public.
cross_cutting_observations.label: FACT + INFERENCE

cross_cutting_observations.observation: TAK/CoT is a government-owned, open de facto standard with a large OSS ecosystem (TAK Server, FreeTAKServer, OpenTAKServer, pytak, Meshtastic ATAK plugin), which lowers barriers for SA integrations but also commoditizes the COP layer.
cross_cutting_observations.evidence: GitHub star counts Sept 2026; TAK protobuf verified.
cross_cutting_observations.label: FACT

cross_cutting_observations.observation: Maven is positioning as the joint developer platform (25,000 builders; a program of record chose to run on Maven) and DoD directed component transition on an aggressive timeline; Palantir's DoW TTM revenue is still <25 bps of the Pentagon budget.
cross_cutting_observations.evidence: Palantir Q2 2026 earnings call Aug 3, 2026; DefenseScoop Apr 15, 2026.
cross_cutting_observations.label: FACT (company statements)

cross_cutting_observations.observation: Two divergent prototype stacks (Lockheed/25ID vs Anduril/4ID) forced the Army to declare a common baseline within a year; app portability and cross-stack data sharing were the real pain, and the Army now explicitly wants divisions to 'reuse applications'.
cross_cutting_observations.label: INFERENCE

cross_cutting_observations.observation: Sensor-to-shooter timelines are quoted in vendor materials (under one minute for 26 M777 missions; 'minutes to seconds') but no independent, exercise-published measurement was found; treat as unverified.
cross_cutting_observations.label: HYPOTHESIS (vendor-claimed)

cross_cutting_observations.observation: Assessment (ASSESS) is the weakest step publicly: no named systems, GAO says DoD cannot measure CJADC2 progress, and lessons-learned sharing is limited.
cross_cutting_observations.label: FACT

cross_cutting_observations.observation: The DAF side is converging on the same pattern: PAE C3BM owns the DAF Battle Network; CBC2 fusion vendor (SciTec) selected; TOC-L MR2 kits due by end 2026; DASH sprints test human-machine teaming and then transition to classified networks.
cross_cutting_observations.evidence: af.mil Sept 8 and Aug 24, 2026; Air & Space Forces Magazine Sept 22, 2026; Firefly Q2 2026 call.
cross_cutting_observations.label: FACT

cross_cutting_observations.observation: Allied markets are deliberately multi-vendor: NATO NCIA reportedly selected Palantir, Anduril and Athea for next-gen air C2 (July 2026) 'to avoid dependence on a specific supplier'; Thales launched HexaForce (Sept 2026) with FMN/DCS.
cross_cutting_observations.label: FACT (LOW confidence on NCIA details)

chain.where_value_is_moving: From monolithic programs of record (CPCE, DCGS-A, AFATDS-era) toward a commercially owned two-layer data platform (Lattice edge + Foundry cloud, Maven at joint level) with an app ecosystem on top. Value is moving (1) up into warfighting-function apps and workflows on those platforms (planning, sustainment, fires, airspace, C-UAS), (2) down into DDIL-tolerant sync, transport-agnostic networking and edge compute hardware integration (TITAN shelters, TOC-L kits), (3) sideways into data-centric security/releasability for coalition and cross-domain (policy-bound but underserved), (4) into test/instrumentation, EW emulation and human-machine-teaming evaluation, and (5) into commercial LEO transport (Starshield/MILNET, SDA). The platform layer itself is consolidating under enterprise agreements with very large ceilings (not obligations), which shrinks greenfield for new middleware startups but raises the number of integration points that need third-party software.

keep: tactical comms (with the split noted below)

change.recommendation: Split into (a) planning/collaboration/workflow apps, (b) execution apps by warfighting function (fires, airspace, protection, sustainment) that run on the data layer, and (c) fire-control C2 (IBCS/Aegis class) as a separate, hardware-coupled sub-segment.
change.why: Evidence shows very different buyers, certification regimes and incumbents: Onebrief-type planning apps enter via OTA partner sets; fire control is in full-rate production under primes with safety certification; lumping them hides the accessible part.

change.recommendation: Rename to 'data layer and adjacent services' and scope to registries, schema transformation, federation, DDIL sync and cross-stack app portability - not new core platforms.
change.why: The core platform decision has been made for Army (Lattice/Foundry, June 2026) and joint (Maven directed transition, Apr 2026); the surviving startup space is services around those platforms (Raft, Ditto).

change.recommendation: Split into 'enterprise PED' (Maven/NGA) and 'edge PED/targeting nodes' (TITAN, TOC-L), and treat edge PED jointly with 'edge compute/AI'.
change.why: TITAN production (Sept 2026) shows edge PED is now a hardware-plus-software integration market distinct from enterprise analytics.

change.recommendation: Separate 'track management/fusion' (belongs with FUSE; fire-control-adjacent, Link 16/IBCS) from 'geospatial SA/COP' (commoditized by TAK and platform UIs).
change.why: They have different technical difficulty, buyers and standards (STANAG 4676/Link 16 vs CoT/2525).

change.recommendation: Treat as cross-cutting requirement plus a concrete product category: releasability labeling, data-centric security, FMN gateways and translators; merge governance with identity/zero-trust/cross-domain into 'data-centric security and releasability'.
change.why: GAO and AFA panel evidence shows the blocker is policy/labeling, which is where tooling can help; pure 'interop' is not a product.

change.recommendation: Split into 'transport hardware/waveforms/SATCOM' (capital-intensive, prime and SpaceX dominated) and 'network orchestration/PACE/transport-agnostic routing software'.
change.why: Software-only entrants (NetAgility-type, mesh sync) can play in the second; not in the first.

change.recommendation: Add 'MLOps for classified/edge and model assurance' as the startup-accessible sub-slice; keep hardware kits with edge PED.
change.why: Striveworks and SciTec wins indicate MLOps/fusion algorithms are procured separately from platforms.

Coverage is thin or absent for: fires C2 (AFATDS/JADOCS/JFN 2026 status), GCCS-J/JPES, DCGS-N/AF/MC, cross-domain solution procurement, EMBM, logistics C2 systems, PNT, Navy Overmatch 2026 specifics, the April 2026 Maven transition memo text, the reported 2025 NGC2 security-risk memo, SBIR/DIU C2 solicitations, and comptroller budget justification line items; these are marked 'Public evidence insufficient' and should be closed by the S01/S05/S09/S10/S12/S14 segment agents. segments.research_method_note: WebSearch budget was exhausted after 8 queries and WebFetch was blocked by the egress proxy for every external domain attempted (gao.gov, army.mil, sam.gov, congress.gov, defensescoop.com, breakingdefense.com, businesswire.com, wikipedia, tak.gov, etc.). The remaining evidence was gathered via GitHub code search over public mirrors of primary documents (army.mil press releases, GAO summaries, DoD budget justification books, Reuters/CNBC article text, company press releases, LinkedIn posts by program participants, Anduril Lattice SDK repos, TAK plugin repos). Every claim below cites the original source URL as it appeared inside those mirrors; publication dates are as recorded there. Because full documents could not be read, several numbers are labeled MEDIUM/LOW confidence and should be re-verified against the original PDFs by a later stage.
segments.what_it_does: The C2 application layer is the software commanders and staffs actually touch: it (1) renders a common operational picture (COP) from friendly-force position reports (PLI), enemy tracks, graphics/overlays and unit status; (2) supports deliberate and crisis planning (MDMP/JPP) producing orders, synchronization matrices, task organizations and COAs; (3) coordinates and deconflicts fires (AFATDS/AXS), airspace (TAIS, ACO/ATO), air and missile defense (AMDWS/IBCS), deep-operations targeting (JADOCS/JTIC2S) and sustainment (GCSS-Army, TyrOS); (4) manages tasks, requests for information and reports across a headquarters battle rhythm; (5) pushes orders and situational awareness down to mounted (MMC/JBC-P) and dismounted (ATAK/Nett Warrior/SBMC) users; and (6) increasingly hosts decision aids (Maven Smart System, Thunderforge, JSDT). It sits above the data layer/data fabric (S02) and transport (S05) and depends on both; in 2025-2026 the Army (NGC2), Navy (Overmatch), DAF (Battle Network/CBC2/KRADOS) and Space Force (Kobayashi Maru) are all converging toward architectures in which a government-owned or vendor-led integrated data layer exposes APIs and third-party apps plug in, rather than each warfighting function owning a stovepiped program of record.

sub_taxonomy.name: S01a COP / situational awareness and track display
sub_taxonomy.note: CPCE/Command Web, MMC/JBC-P, ATAK/WinTAK, Lattice UI, Maven map, CBC2, CAC2S. Evidence suggests this sub-layer is now commoditized (TAK is free/open, Lattice and Maven bundle it); differentiation has moved to the data layer and to workflow apps.

sub_taxonomy.name: S01b Collaborative planning and staff workflow (MDMP/JPP, orders, battle rhythm)
sub_taxonomy.note: Onebrief is the clear category leader (HQ to division, now inside NGC2 as the planning layer); Word/PowerPoint/email/chat remain the incumbent 'system' at most echelons. Battalion-and-below and DDIL variants are less mature.

sub_taxonomy.name: S01c Functional coordination apps (fires, airspace, AMD, targeting, sustainment)
sub_taxonomy.note: AFATDS 7.0 / Artillery Execution Suite, TAIS, AMDWS, JADOCS and its containerized successor JTIC2S, IBCS-M, GCSS-Army, TyrOS. Legacy programs of record being re-hosted/converged on NGC2 and TAK-compatible baselines; most manual re-entry pain lives here.

sub_taxonomy.name: S01d Decision support / AI-enabled analysis on top of C2 data
sub_taxonomy.note: Maven Smart System (now a designated Pentagon program of record), Thunderforge (DIU/Scale AI), JSDT (DIU/ASI, Watchtower), Raft AI Mission System, Palantir AIP. Fastest-growing budget line (FY27 PB requests $2.3B/5yr for Maven + Joint Fires Network).

sub_taxonomy.name: S01e Mobile / dismounted / mounted C2 clients
sub_taxonomy.note: ATAK-MIL and CIV plus plugin ecosystem (TAK Product Center Third Party Pipeline), Nett Warrior, SBMC (IVAS successor: Anduril EagleEye, Rivet), MMC. Most open to third-party developers of any sub-layer.

sub_taxonomy.name: S01f Joint/theater/space C2 suites
sub_taxonomy.note: GCCS-J and JPES (replacing JOPES, FOC targeted Q2 CY2026), KRADOS at AOCs (replacing TBMCS/ATOMS), CBC2 at NORAD sectors, Kobayashi Maru space C2 portfolios. Government software factories are the integrators; startups enter as component vendors.

users.role: Division/corps commander and command group
users.what_they_do: Consume the COP and staff estimates, approve plans/orders, make targeting and risk decisions; in NGC2 exercises (Ivy Sting/Ivy Mass, Lightning Surge) they direct sensors and fires through a unified data platform.

users.role: G3/S3 current-operations and plans staff (planners, battle captains, battle NCOs)
users.what_they_do: Run MDMP, build and synchronize orders and graphics, maintain the battle rhythm and RFIs; historically in PowerPoint/Word/email, now in Onebrief where fielded (4th ID compressed MDMP to 24 hours; planning cycles from hours to ~30 minutes in NGC2 experiments).

users.role: Fires cell / FDO / FDC
users.what_they_do: Process calls for fire, target validation, airspace clearance and fire orders in AFATDS/AXS; in Lightning Surge 2 the call for fire traveled over private 5G from FDO to guns with voice-driven AI workflows for deconfliction.

users.role: Airspace/ADAM cell and air defense operators
users.what_they_do: Deconflict airspace lanes and issue safe-to-fire cues (TAIS, AMDWS, IBCS-M, CAC2S); demonstrated as a unified NGC2 interface at Balikatan 2026.

users.role: Intelligence/CEMA/targeting analysts
users.what_they_do: Feed EW/ELINT detections and targets into the COP and targeting workbenches (Maven, JADOCS/JTIC2S); NGC2 made CEMA data visible to sister warfighting functions for the first time at 25th ID.

users.role: Sustainment/G4 and vehicle maintainers
users.what_they_do: Track ammunition, fuel, readiness and resupply; increasingly automated via vehicle telemetry (Shift5) and predictive logistics (Rune TyrOS) feeding the C2 layer, replacing manual reporting cycles and spreadsheets.

users.role: Squad/platoon leaders and dismounted soldiers, SOF, first responders
users.what_they_do: Use ATAK/iTAK/WinTAK and (future) SBMC headsets for PLI, chat, 9-line CAS/CASEVAC, HLZ selection and drone control; plugin ecosystem extends function per mission.

users.role: Joint/combatant command staffs and coalition partners
users.what_they_do: Global force management and deployment planning in GCCS-J/JPES, joint targeting via Maven (CENTCOM ~13,000 accounts, ~2,500 regular users per 2024 reporting), coalition sharing via Mission Partner Environment and Five Eyes Overmatch agreement.

users.role: AOC and space operations crews
users.what_they_do: Build and execute the ATO/ACO in KRADOS/TBMCS; NORAD sector crews run homeland-defense air battle management in CBC2; Space Force crews use Kobayashi Maru portfolios for space domain awareness, tasking and defensive cyber.

current_architecture.description: Two generations coexist. Legacy: warfighting-function programs of record (AFATDS, TAIS, AMDWS, JADOCS, GCCS-A/J, CPOF then CPCE/Command Web, JBC-P then MMC) each with its own server stack, message formats and ATO, converged over 2018-2023 into CPCE for the command post and MMC for vehicles. Emerging (2024-2026): NGC2 as an 'ecosystem of transport, infrastructure, data and applications' where a common data layer (Anduril Lattice edge-to-cloud mesh, Palantir Foundry cloud data layer, Raft data/services registries and federation, established as the Army baseline June 22 2026) exposes APIs to applications from many vendors (Onebrief planning, Accelint/Lyntris mission command interface, Govini, Striveworks, Instant Connect, Research Innovations, Shift5 telemetry, Rune TyrOS logistics, Microsoft cloud). Legacy PoRs are being re-hosted (AFATDS 7.0 Java rewrite, AXS microservices, containerized MMC-Software and JTIC2S) and forced to expose APIs (Operation Jailbreak / 'Right to Integrate', May 2026: ~600 participants, >50 companies, APIs documented across >70 Army capabilities including IBCS-M). Navy (Overmatch), DAF (Battle Network with CBC2 and KRADOS) and Space Force (Kobayashi Maru) follow the same pattern with government software factories as integrators. TAK remains the de facto dismounted/mobile SA client across services and agencies, with an open plugin model.

current_architecture.security_domain: Predominantly SECRET (SIPR) for Army tactical C2 and NGC2; UNCLASS/CUI for TAK-CIV, public-safety and many prototypes; Onebrief and Maven span NIPR/SIPR/JWICS/coalition; homeland CBC2 and NORAD are classified. The Sept 2025 Army CTO memo found NGC2 prototype lacked role-based access control and audit logging so 'any user can potentially access and misuse sensitive' classified information; remediation was claimed by the Army CIO.
current_architecture.connectivity_dependency: High. NGC2 is cloud-native with edge compute (Anduril Voyager Tactical Edge Compute ran the full stack in vehicles 'disconnected when required' at Ivy Sting 5); Onebrief and Maven are web apps requiring at least intermittent links; private 5G served as primary transport for calls for fire at Lightning Surge 2 with satellite radios secondary.
current_architecture.what_breaks_when_disconnected: Cloud-hosted planning and Foundry-side analytics stall; COPs go stale and diverge between nodes until resync; staffs revert to voice, chat and paper. NGC2 design goal is DDIL operation per echelon with local compute and data mesh replication, but an industry critique (LinkedIn, 2026) argued vendors still treat DDIL as an edge case rather than the baseline; Joint Staff budget language since FY2019 stresses 'denied-disconnected, intermittent, low-bandwidth' capability at CJTF level as an unmet demand.

technical_difficulty.summary: Building a COP or planning UI is not hard; the difficulty is (a) integrating with dozens of legacy message formats and PoRs whose APIs were only documented in 2026, (b) keeping state consistent across DDIL nodes (conflict-free replication, bandwidth-aware sync, local compute), (c) meeting Army cybersecurity expectations (RBAC, audit logging, supply-chain scanning) that the flagship prototype itself failed in Sept 2025, and (d) surviving the ATO/accreditation and network-access process. Domain fidelity (doctrinal workflows, symbology, fires safety) is a hard requirement that generic SaaS teams underestimate.
required_expertise: Distributed systems and offline-first sync
Military data formats (CoT, VMF, Link 16/JREAP, USMTF, MIL-STD-2525)
Secure software supply chain and RMF/cATO practice
Geospatial engineering
Doctrinal knowledge of MDMP, fires, airspace and sustainment workflows
Edge deployment on Android/rugged compute (TAK plugin SDK, Lattice SDK)
LLM/agent engineering for staff workflows (increasingly)
technical_difficulty.hardest_problem: Bidirectional, trusted integration between a planning/COP app and execution systems (AFATDS/AXS, TAIS, IBCS-M, GCSS-Army) under DDIL conditions without manual re-entry, while preserving fires-safety semantics and classification/releasability rules.
technical_difficulty.commodity_parts: Map rendering, symbology libraries, chat, PLI tracking, CoT plumbing and TAK servers are open source or freely licensed; cloud IL5/IL6 hosting is available from hyperscalers and Second Front; Lattice and TAK SDKs are public.

capital_intensity.proof_of_concept_usd: $50k-$250k (TAK plugin or Lattice SDK integration demonstrated on ATAK-CIV/TAK Server with synthetic or public-safety data)
capital_intensity.credible_military_demo_usd: $1M-$4M (12-18 months: cleared advisor, participation in an NGC2 CSO window, Jailbreak-style sprint or Project Convergence, IL5 hosting via a partner, initial RMF artifacts)
capital_intensity.first_production_deployment_usd: $5M-$20M (ATO on SIPR or ride on a team lead's authorization, sustained field support with a unit, 24/7 engineering, FOCI-clean structure; Onebrief needed ~$100M+ and a $322k sponsor contract to get on secure networks before scaling)
capital_intensity.assumptions: Assumes software-only, no hardware; assumes entry as a component under an NGC2 team lead, TAK plugin or Overmatch Armory rather than as a prime; assumes U.S.-person engineering for CUI/ITAR-adjacent work; costs rise sharply if classified development environments are required from the start.

regulatory_access.prototype_with_commercial_unclassified_d: yes - ATAK-CIV, TAK Server and the Lattice SDKs are public; public-safety (wildfire, SAR) and allied unclassified exercises provide realistic data; CoT/2525 formats are open
regulatory_access.government_data_required: Needed for anything beyond a demo: unit task organizations, fires data, real sensor feeds and network access are CUI or classified and only reachable through a sponsor (unit, PM, DIU, team lead)
regulatory_access.itar_ear: C2 software touching fires/targeting or integrating with defense articles is likely ITAR/EAR-controlled technical data; TAK Third Party Pipeline excludes Denied Parties; ATAK-MIL and government SDK access is restricted. Specialist export-control review required before a non-U.S. person works on military integrations.
regulatory_access.cui_likely: Yes at first customer engagement (unit data, interface specs, Jailbreak API documentation)
regulatory_access.classified_integration_eventually: Yes for Army/NGC2 (SIPR), NORAD, Overmatch; Onebrief and Maven operate on SIPR/JWICS; a facility clearance (FCL) and cleared staff become necessary within 12-24 months for production
regulatory_access.cleared_personnel_at_mvp: No for a TAK-CIV/Lattice-SDK MVP; yes for an NGC2 component at PC-C6-type events (at least one cleared engineer/advisor)
regulatory_access.non_us_person_founder_note: A non-U.S.-person co-founder (Indonesian national) creates FOCI, export-control (ITAR deemed-export) and clearance-sponsorship constraints for the U.S. entity; a German founder becoming a permanent resident can hold a clearance only after citizenship in most cases. Mitigations to review with counsel: keep the non-U.S. person in a commercial/public-safety product line or allied (NATO/EU) subsidiary, use a U.S.-person-only cleared team, or target Five Eyes/NATO customers first. Not a legal judgment; requires specialist review.

why_not_solved.explanation: Until 2025-2026 each warfighting-function PoR owned its data and interfaces; the Army had to run Operation Jailbreak to force API exposure. Third parties could not integrate without the prime's cooperation.

ATO, network access and facility clearance are the 'three barriers' cited by Onebrief's founder; the flagship NGC2 prototype itself failed a security assessment, which will make authorizing officials stricter, not looser, about third-party apps.
Buyers are split across PEOs, DIU, CDAO, service software factories and units with GPC cards; a $25k pilot does not lead to a program line without a sponsor who owns budget.
Fires/airspace semantics, message standards and classification rules make plan-to-execution automation risky; nobody wants software that mis-clears airspace.

COP/SA is commoditized (TAK, Lattice, Maven); HQ-level planning is being solved by Onebrief; data-layer plumbing is now owned by Anduril/Palantir/Raft under Army designation. Remaining whitespace is narrower than the headline budgets suggest.
Prototype OTAs are small ($26M-$100M for whole teams) and split among many members; sustained revenue depends on production decisions the Army has not scheduled (GAO).

attractiveness.bull: Largest, most visible C2 modernization in decades with explicit third-party app ecosystems (NGC2 CSO with rolling windows, Jailbreak API marketplace, TAK Third Party Pipeline, Overmatch Software Armory), FY26-27 requests in the billions, unit-level buyers who iterate with vendors in days, and proof that a 2019 startup (Onebrief) can reach $2B+ valuation and an Army enterprise contract on a single workflow wedge. AI/agentic staff tooling is the fastest-growing budget line.
attractiveness.bear: The platform and data layers are now assigned (Anduril, Palantir, Raft) and the planning layer is claimed (Onebrief); remaining openings are components inside someone else's stack with small dollar values, dependent on team leads and a production timeline GAO says does not exist. Security scrutiny after the 2025 memo raises the bar for unknown vendors. Access constraints (ITAR, clearances, FOCI) are severe for a team with a non-U.S.-person founder and a student-scale budget. Absence of visible competitors in a niche is not evidence of demand.
attractiveness.verdict: Medium overall for a well-connected U.S. team; low-to-medium for these founders. Enter only through an existing on-ramp (TAK plugin, Lattice SDK component, NGC2 CSO component proposal, Jailbreak-style sprint) with a narrow workflow wedge, or target allied/public-safety TAK users first.

candidate_gaps.title: Assurance pipeline for third-party C2 apps (continuous security assessment, RBAC/audit conformance, SBOM) that plugs into NGC2, Lattice, TAK and Overmatch onboarding
candidate_gaps.problem_one_sentence: The Army wants an open app ecosystem but its flagship prototype hosted third-party apps that had never been assessed (25-200+ vulnerabilities each) with no RBAC or logging, and every ecosystem (TAK TPP, Overmatch Armory, NGC2 team leads, Jailbreak API marketplace) is re-inventing onboarding checks by hand.
candidate_gaps.user: NGC2 team-lead integration engineers, TAK Product Center pipeline operators, Overmatch Software Armory, Army authorizing officials, and small vendors seeking to get an app accepted
candidate_gaps.current_workflow: 1) Vendor builds app against Lattice/Foundry/TAK SDK; 2) submits binary or source to a team lead or TPP; 3) manual scans (OWASP dependency-check, Fortify) and ad hoc review; 4) app deployed in prototype; 5) Army CTO assessment after the fact finds RBAC/logging/vuln gaps; 6) remediation and re-deployment; 7) each new ecosystem repeats the process.
candidate_gaps.current_solution: TAK Third Party Pipeline (build+sign+SAST), Overmatch RAISE cATO, Second Front Game Warden hosting, Platform One Iron Bank containers, team-lead internal reviews.
candidate_gaps.failure_point: Checks are per-ecosystem, binary-level and after-the-fact; nothing enforces role/attribute-based access and auditability inside the app, and Army AOs cannot 'see what users are doing' across apps from different vendors.

candidate_gaps.why_startups_havent_solved: It sits between DevSecOps vendors (Second Front, Platform One), platform owners (Anduril/Palantir) and government pipelines; no single buyer owns 'cross-ecosystem app assurance', and the requirement was only made visible by the Sept 2025 memo.

candidate_gaps.technical_wedge_hypothesis: A policy-as-code SDK plus scanner that proves an app enforces role/attribute-based access, emits standardized audit events and ships an SBOM, with attestations consumable by NGC2 registries (Raft), TPP and Armory; sold to team leads and small vendors as 'pass the AO the first time'.
candidate_gaps.mvp_sketch: Open-source ATAK plugin and Lattice-SDK app linters plus an audit-event library; demonstrate on ATAK-CIV and Lattice sandbox; publish conformance reports; pilot with one NGC2 component vendor.

candidate_gaps.integration_requirement: TAK TPP submission format, Lattice SDK, Raft/NGC2 service registry schemas, Iron Bank/Game Warden pipelines.
candidate_gaps.entry_vehicle: Sell to NGC2 component vendors and team leads; SBIR/xTech; DIU cybersecurity CSO; TPC cooperative agreement.

candidate_gaps.title: Plan-to-execution glue: automated, safety-checked translation of planning products (Onebrief/COP graphics, airspace coordination measures, fire support plans) into execution systems (AFATDS/AXS, TAIS, IBCS-M, GCSS-Army) and back
candidate_gaps.problem_one_sentence: Plans are built in one environment and 'pushed into the specialized systems that execute them' by humans re-entering data, so fires, airspace and sustainment status still require manual reconciliation and phone/chat coordination.
candidate_gaps.user: Fires cells, ADAM/airspace cells, current-ops battle captains and G4 planners at brigade through corps
candidate_gaps.current_workflow: 1) Planners build scheme of maneuver and fire support plan in Onebrief/PowerPoint; 2) fires cell re-enters targets and control measures in AFATDS; 3) ADAM cell enters ACMs in TAIS and coordinates by chat/phone with aviation; 4) sustainment status reported by spreadsheet/LOGSTAT; 5) changes in one system are re-keyed into others; 6) discrepancies discovered during rehearsals or live fire.

segments.research_method_note: The session's WebSearch budget was already exhausted (200/200) when this agent started, and the egress proxy blocked every non-GitHub domain attempted (gao.gov, army.mil, sam.gov, sbir.gov, diu.mil, defense.gov, media.defense.gov, comptroller.defense.gov, congress.gov, dvidshub.net, tak.gov, anduril.com, palantir.com, teamraft.com, ditto.com, tangramflex.com, rti.com, defensescoop.com, breakingdefense.com, reuters.com, wikipedia, csis.org, rand.org, dote.osd.mil, linkedin.com, DuckDuckGo and Bing). Evidence was therefore gathered from (a) GitHub code search (33 queries) over public mirrors of primary documents (army.mil releases, DoD contract announcements, DAU/WarU webinar transcripts, SASC hearing captions, company press releases and LinkedIn posts, Palantir earnings transcripts, USAspending-derived dossiers), (b) raw.githubusercontent.com fetches of those mirrors, and (c) sibling-agent files in the shared scratchpad (S01, S08, S09, E01, E02, B01/B02/B07/B08, buyers/army.json, buyers/joint.json) whose own source URLs are cited. Original URLs are cited as they appear in the mirrors; several numbers are labeled MEDIUM/LOW confidence and should be re-verified against the primary PDFs by a later stage.
segments.what_it_does: The data layer sits between transport (radios, SATCOM, 5G, DDS/IP networks) and the applications commanders touch (COP, planning, fires, intel, logistics). It (1) ingests heterogeneous feeds (radar/EO-IR tracks, PLI, Link 16 J-series, VMF, USMTF, Cursor-on-Target, STANAG 4607/4609/4676 ISR products, vehicle telemetry, logistics and enterprise records); (2) normalizes them into a shared data model or ontology (entities/tracks/tasks/objects in Anduril Lattice, object types/links/actions in Palantir Foundry, 'data products' with mandatory metadata under the Army Unified Data Reference Architecture); (3) publishes them over an event bus or pub/sub mesh with store-and-forward and conflict-free replication so nodes keep working when links are denied, degraded, intermittent or limited (DDIL); (4) exposes registries, catalogs, APIs and SDKs so third-party apps and sensors can plug in; (5) federates queries and synchronizes state across echelons, security enclaves and coalition networks; and (6) enforces tagging, access control and releasability so the same data can move from a vehicle to a division cloud to a partner network. In 2025-2026 the U.S. Army formally baselined this layer for NGC2 as an Anduril-led 'edge-to-cloud data mesh' (Lattice at the edge, Foundry as the cloud data layer) with Raft providing data/services registries, transformation tools and federation; the joint level is converging on Maven Smart System plus a CDAO 'Edge Data Mesh', and the enterprise layer (Advana, renamed War Data Platform in Jan 2026) is being rebuilt.

sub_taxonomy.name: S02a Tactical edge data mesh / pub-sub replication (DDIL-first)
sub_taxonomy.note: Entity/track/task replication across vehicles, command posts and mobile devices with store-and-forward and CRDT-style convergence. Owned today by Anduril Lattice Mesh (Army NGC2 baseline lead, CDAO $100M Edge Data Mesh OTA, Space Force SDANet), with Ditto (ATAK Edge Sync plugin, USSOCOM per company) and Raft ([R]DP synchronization claims at Lightning Surge) as the other named players. Government interest is documented in PM Mission Command's DDIL TAK data-services requirement and the DEVCOM C5ISR zero-trust 'data pillar in DDIL' RFI.

sub_taxonomy.name: S02b Cloud/enterprise data layer, ontology and semantic layer
sub_taxonomy.note: Palantir Foundry/Ontology (NGC2 cloud data layer; Army Vantage/ADP with >100k users; Maven), Advana/War Data Platform (Accenture Federal $821M integration task order, July 2026), Databricks/C3 AI on Advana. Highest lock-in: once workflows and security rules are modeled in an ontology they are expensive to move (INFERENCE).

sub_taxonomy.name: S02c Registries, catalogs, schema/format translation and federation
sub_taxonomy.note: Data and services registries, transformation and federation (Raft Data Platform in the NGC2 baseline), Army UDRA 'data product' metadata and mesh services, DoD AI memo's 30-day federated data catalogs, Tangram Flex (formal-methods interface code generation between STANAG-4586/LMCP/etc.), Picogrid Legion (vendor-neutral integration API). This is where 'custom integrations' live today.

sub_taxonomy.name: S02d Standards-based interoperability interfaces (government-owned)
sub_taxonomy.note: Cursor on Target / TAK Server and plugin pipeline (Army-led TAK Product Center), Link 16 J-series, VMF, USMTF, MIL-STD-2525, JREAP, NATO STANAGs (4586, 4607, 4609, 4676, 5636 core metadata, 4774/4778 labeling), OMS/UCI, FACE/SOSA, NSA TDF/EDH for data-centric security. The government insists on owning these interfaces (Open DAGIR, NGC2 'government-approved non-proprietary APIs', Operation Jailbreak / Right to Integrate). Largely commoditized; a startup cannot charge for the standard itself.

sub_taxonomy.name: S02e Cross-domain, tagging and releasability-aware data movement
sub_taxonomy.note: Attribute-based access control, machine-readable labels, cross-domain solutions at the edge (TACDS filters, NEWT body-worn CDS), coalition sharing via Mission Partner Environment / INDOPACOM Mission Network. Policy, not technology, is the binding constraint (GAO-25-106454; IMN 'thumb drives'). Overlaps S08 (coalition) and S09 (ATO).

sub_taxonomy.name: S02f Track/entity management and correlation across fabrics
sub_taxonomy.note: De-duplicating and correlating the same object reported through Lattice, TAK, IBCS, Link 16, Maven and partner systems, with provenance and quality signals. Government notices (C-sUAS 4-10 Hz track updates; Mar 2026 'Data Fusion Correlator' notice on SENSEI limitations) show this is still bought piecemeal. Overlaps S03 (fusion).

buyers.note: Built the Rainmaker tactical data fabric prototype (2020-2022) and issued a 2025 RFI on zero-trust 'data pillar' protection for tactical data-in-use inside DDIL; buys small S&T prototypes and SBIRs.

buyers.organization: Chief Digital and AI Office (CDAO), now under USD(R&E)

current_architecture.description: Three generations coexist. Legacy (still fielded): each program of record (AFATDS, TAIS, AMDWS, JADOCS, CPCE, JBC-P/MMC, DCGS-A, IBCS, GCCS-J) keeps its own data store, message formats (VMF, USMTF, Link 16, proprietary) and ATO; cross-system flow relies on bespoke adapters, CoT gateways and humans. Bridging generation (2020-2024): Army Project Rainmaker tactical data fabric, Palantir Army Vantage/ADP (~180 sources, >100k users), CDAO Advana enterprise platform, TAK/CoT as the de facto tactical interchange, ABMS Digital Infrastructure. Emerging (2025-2026): the Army's NGC2 four-layer architecture (transport, infrastructure, data, applications) with a common data layer baseline set on June 22 2026: Anduril Lattice provides the edge-to-cloud mesh, Palantir Foundry the cloud data layer, Raft the data/services registries, transformation tools and federation; apps from Onebrief, Accelint/Lyntris, Govini, Striveworks, Rune, Shift5, Microsoft, AWS and others attach through APIs; legacy PoRs are being forced to expose APIs (Operation Jailbreak / Right to Integrate, May 2026). At the joint level Maven Smart System (program of record, March 2026) and CDAO's Edge Data Mesh (Anduril, $100M OTA) are the CJADC2 cornerstone; Advana is being split into the War Data Platform. Navy Overmatch, DAF Battle Network and Space Force SDANet follow the same pattern with government software factories as integrators.

data_formats_protocols: NITF, STANAG 4607 (GMTI), 4609 (motion imagery), 4676 (tracks), 4586 (UAS control), 5636 (core metadata), 4774/4778 (confidentiality labels/binding)
NSA Trusted Data Format (TDF) / Enterprise Data Header
Protocol Buffers over gRPC and REST (Lattice SDK Entities/Tasks/Objects)
Palantir Ontology SDK (OSDK) and Foundry APIs
DDS (OMG) and MQTT for platform/embedded pub-sub (e.g., RTI Connext in weapon systems; MQTT in TAK/IoT)
Kafka-style event streaming in cloud tiers
OMS/UCI, FACE, SOSA for platform mission systems
current_architecture.security_domain: Unclassified/CUI for development and enterprise readiness data; Secret (SIPR/tactical Secret enclaves) for NGC2 division data layers; Secret-releasable for MPE/IMN; SCI for intel feeds into Maven/TITAN. NGC2 prototypes drew an Army memo citing 'very high risk' security deficiencies (Reuters, Oct 3 2025; Palantir rebutted). Zero-trust target-level deadline Sept 2027 forces machine-readable tagging.
current_architecture.connectivity_dependency: Cloud tiers (Foundry, Advana, Maven) assume reachback; edge meshes (Lattice, Raft, Ditto, TAK) are designed for DDIL with local replication. Critics at Ivy Sting 5 argued treating DDIL as an edge case 'proves Anduril are still thinking like a cloud company' (LinkedIn, 2026, single practitioner opinion).
current_architecture.what_breaks_when_disconnected: Cloud-only ontologies and enterprise catalogs become stale or unreachable; cross-echelon federation queries fail; cross-domain and releasability services hosted centrally stop; track duplication and divergence grow until reconnection; AI decision aids hosted in the cloud (Maven) are unavailable to the edge. Mesh products mitigate by store-and-forward and CRDT convergence, but conflict resolution policy (who wins, which classification applies) is immature (INFERENCE).

technical_difficulty.summary: Building a pub/sub data layer with schemas, APIs and cloud sync is commodity engineering; what is hard is (1) DDIL-first replication with deterministic conflict resolution across thousands of nodes and mixed radios, (2) semantic interoperability across dozens of legacy message standards without losing fidelity ('compression-induced information loss' was a Rainmaker-era finding), (3) doing both under classification and releasability rules that must be machine-enforced (ZT deadline Sept 2027), (4) track/entity de-duplication with provenance across independently fused pictures, and (5) getting the artifact through an ATO and onto a government-controlled baseline. The incumbents' advantage is less the algorithms than the accumulated adapters (Anduril '100+ sensor types' claim; Picogrid '100+ systems'), the deployed node footprint and the ATO reciprocity.
required_expertise: Distributed systems (CRDTs, gossip/epidemic replication, store-and-forward, delay-tolerant networking)
Schema/ontology engineering and message-standard translation (CoT, Link 16, VMF, USMTF, STANAGs, protobuf/gRPC)

technical_difficulty.hardest_problem: Policy-aware convergence: making replicated state converge across DDIL partitions while every replica respects classification, releasability and role rules, and while conflicting reports of the same entity from different fabrics are reconciled with auditable provenance. No public evidence that any vendor has solved this generally; Lattice, Raft and Ditto each claim pieces (INFERENCE).
technical_difficulty.commodity_parts: Cloud data lakes, Kafka-style buses, REST/gRPC gateways, catalogs (DataHub/OpenMetadata-class), CoT parsing, Kubernetes, MQTT brokers, DDS implementations, MIL-STD-2525 rendering libraries, open-source ATAK plugins, LLM-based mapping assistants.

capital_intensity.assumptions: PoC: two founders, ATAK-CIV/CoT and open message specs, synthetic tracks, optional Foundry developer tier or Lattice SDK sandbox (access gated by an Anduril representative - may not be granted). Credible demo: a SBIR/STTR Phase I-II or NSIN/xTech path, participation in an exercise or hackathon (Jailbreak-style, PC-C, Lightning Surge) as a team-lead subcontractor, CUI handling, one cleared advisor, rugged edge kit, travel; 12-18 months. First production: hosting on Game Warden/UDS/Platform One or the team lead's environment to inherit ATO, IL5/IL6 evidence, FSO and facility clearance (or a cleared partner), 24/7 support for a division, sustainment engineers; assumes riding an existing enterprise agreement or OTA rather than a new competition. Ranges are INFERENCE from comparable startups (Picogrid $12M seed to Phase III in ~2 years; Rune $24M Series A to two NGC2 teams).

regulatory_access.prototype_with_commercial_unclassified_d: partly - CoT/TAK, STANAG-style schemas, open protobuf definitions and synthetic feeds allow a real prototype; but the government's actual schemas (NGC2 API baseline, IBCS, Maven ontology) are CUI or vendor-gated, and Lattice environments require an Anduril relationship.
regulatory_access.government_data_required: Yes for anything beyond a demo: real sensor/PoR message samples, NGC2 API specifications, unit data; obtainable only inside a sponsored event (Jailbreak, PC-C, SBIR with a TPOC) or as a team-lead subcontractor.
regulatory_access.itar_ear: Middleware itself is usually EAR-controlled software, but adapters to specific weapon/C2 systems (IBCS, Link 16 crypto-adjacent, fire control) can become ITAR technical data; a startup with a non-U.S.-person founder must get an export-control determination before touching PoR interface control documents. Requires specialist legal review; not a definitive judgment.
regulatory_access.cui_likely: Yes - interface control documents, network diagrams, exercise data are CUI at minimum; CMMC Level 2 practices expected.
regulatory_access.classified_integration_eventually: Yes - NGC2 division data layers run at Secret; Maven/TITAN feeds involve SCI; coalition variants at Secret-releasable.
regulatory_access.cleared_personnel_at_mvp: Not required for an unclassified MVP; required (Secret at least) to participate in exercise integration and production support; facility clearance needed to hold classified contracts.
regulatory_access.non_us_person_founder_note: A non-U.S.-person co-founder with equity/control triggers Foreign Ownership, Control or Influence (FOCI) review for any facility clearance, may bar SBIR/STTR eligibility (majority U.S.-owned rule) and complicates ITAR deemed-export handling of interface data; personnel clearances require U.S. citizenship, so the German founder cannot hold one until naturalized and the Indonesian founder cannot hold one at all. Mitigations to review with counsel: structure so U.S. persons hold control and cleared roles, keep the non-U.S. founder on unclassified commercial/international (NATO/EU) product lines, or pursue the German/NATO market (S08) first. Describe, do not conclude - this needs a FOCI/export attorney.

why_not_solved.explanation: For two decades each PoR and prime owned its data and interfaces; only in May 2026 did the Army run Jailbreak to force API exposure. Now the replacement is itself vendor-led (Lattice/Foundry) with SDK access gated by the vendor, so lock-in is shifting rather than disappearing.

GAO (2025) found restrictive classification the main hindrance to sharing C2 data and no owner of the problem; tagging is manual and inconsistent; the ZT data pillar deadline (Sept 2027) is the first forcing function.

Dozens of message standards with lossy translations, hundreds of sensor types, and no standard vehicle/health protocol; every new sensor or PoR is a bespoke adapter (Shift5 two months; Jailbreak needed 600 people).

Buyers split across CPE C2IN, PM MC, C5ISR, CDAO, NAVWAR, PEO C3BM, SSC, DISA and units; data-layer money is not a line item but buried in NGC2, Maven, Advana and MPE portfolios; SBIR winners (Tangram, Cougaar, Securboration) rarely reach a program.

CRDT-based offline-first sync, cheap rugged edge compute (Voyager/Menace-T), protobuf/gRPC schema registries and LLM-assisted schema mapping matured 2018-2024; the MWI article (Feb 2026) explicitly ties the 2024-2026 data-mesh awards to CRDTs.

Government prefers to own interfaces (Open DAGIR, UDRA) and to buy the fabric from a platform vendor under an enterprise agreement; a standalone middleware company has no price point between 'free government standard' and 'platform bundled by Anduril/Palantir'.

For Army division-and-below the data-layer plumbing was designated in June 2026 (Anduril/Palantir/Raft), joint fusion is Maven, tactical interchange is TAK. What remains unsolved is the seams: onboarding legacy/third-party systems, policy-aware DDIL sync, releasability tagging, cross-fabric entity reconciliation and the catalog at tactical echelons.

attractiveness.bull: The data layer is where the Army is now spending (NGC2 ~$3B FY26 portfolio, Maven $2.3B five-year request, $30B of enterprise-agreement ceilings across Anduril and Palantir) and where the government has publicly conceded the seams are unsolved: undocumented APIs (Jailbreak), classification-blocked sharing (GAO), manual tagging (ZT PfMO), thumb-drive coalition workflows (IMN), and a mesh that stops at division. Team leads (Anduril, Lockheed) actively recruit small vendors into their stacks (Rune, Shift5, Accelint, Striveworks joined within months), the TAK plugin pipeline and Tradewinds are open doors, and government-owned interface policy (Open DAGIR, R2I) means a startup that builds the conformance/adapter tooling the government wants to own can be pulled through without competing with the platform owners.
attractiveness.bear: The platform itself is taken: Anduril leads the Army baseline, Palantir owns the ontology and Maven, Raft holds registries/federation, Ditto has the CRDT niche, and all of them can absorb any adapter, catalog or sync feature a startup demonstrates. Contract values for the small players in this layer are undisclosed or SBIR-scale, several data-translation SBIR firms never transitioned, Advana shows enterprise data programs churning for years, and every meaningful integration requires CUI/Secret access, an ATO and a cleared team - a structural problem for a two-student team with a non-U.S.-person founder. Absence of a visible competitor in a sub-niche mostly reflects that the incumbents have not prioritized it yet, not an open market.
attractiveness.verdict: Medium-low for a standalone data-fabric play; medium for a narrow 'seam' product (policy-aware sync, releasability tagging, onboarding/conformance tooling, cross-fabric entity reconciliation) sold through a team lead or the TAK/Tradewinds doors, with the explicit expectation that the exit is acquisition by or licensing to a platform owner.

market_stage.rationale: Within roughly five years the segment moved from S&T prototypes and RFIs (2020-2023) through competitive prototype OTAs (2024-2025) to enterprise production vehicles and a designated Army baseline (2025-2026), with repeat orders (Space Force additional sites, Maven ceiling raise, Vantage extension). It is 'Transitioning' rather than 'Mature' because scaled fielding schedules and life-cycle costs are undefined (GAO Aug 2026), the joint enterprise layer is mid-restructure (WDP), and coalition/tactical-echelon extensions remain at RFI stage.

proto_purgatory.notes: Two-tier pattern. The platform tier escaped purgatory in 2025-2026: Lattice went from CDAO pilot to Army baseline and a $20B vehicle; Palantir from Vantage contracts to a $10B ESA and Maven PoR; Raft from a subcontract to a named baseline role. The component tier shows classic purgatory: Tangram Flex (AFRL Phase III since 2020, no fielding evidence), Cougaar/Securboration/Machina Cognita translation SBIRs with no transition, Ditto with repeated SBIR phases and company-asserted use, Picogrid with 26 SBIR awards before a $9.3M Phase III, and government programs themselves (Rainmaker superseded; Advana paused, recompete canceled, renamed; MPE 'starting small' after a decade).
proto_purgatory.opportunity_or_warning: Warning for standalone middleware startups: SBIR-after-SBIR without a team-lead sponsor is the modal outcome. Opportunity only for components that a designated platform owner or a government software factory wants to pull in (the Shift5/Rune/Accelint pattern), or that ride a government-owned door (TAK plugins, Tradewinds awardable, Jailbreak API marketplace).

candidate_gaps.title: Self-service onboarding and conformance tooling for legacy systems and third-party sensors onto the government-baselined data layer
candidate_gaps.problem_one_sentence: Every new sensor, vehicle or program of record still needs a bespoke, vendor-built adapter and a human-run integration event to join the NGC2/TAK/Maven data layer, because interface documentation, schema mapping and conformance testing are not productized.
candidate_gaps.user: Program-office and unit integration cells; small vendors trying to join a team lead's stack; TAK Product Center plugin developers
candidate_gaps.current_workflow: 1) Vendor obtains ICDs or reverse-engineers messages (often CUI, often undocumented). 2) Engineers hand-write a translator to CoT/Lattice entity/Foundry object schema. 3) Integration is validated at an in-person event (Jailbreak, Ivy Sting, Lightning Surge) with firewall and ATO surprises. 4) The adapter is maintained by that vendor only; the next unit or exercise repeats the work.
candidate_gaps.current_solution: Team-lead engineers (Anduril translators, Raft transformation tools), Picogrid Legion, Tangram Pro code generation, TAK plugin pipeline, manual API documentation produced at Jailbreak.
candidate_gaps.failure_point: Time-to-integrate is measured in weeks to months per system (Shift5 two months; Jailbreak needed 600 people for 70 systems); no independent conformance test exists for 'is this feed NGC2-baseline compliant'; knowledge is trapped inside the platform vendor.

candidate_gaps.problem_one_sentence: Edge meshes can replicate data through outages, but no public product converges replicated state while enforcing per-attribute classification, releasability and role rules across partitions and across two vendors' fabrics.

candidate_gaps.current_workflow: 1) Data is replicated within one vendor mesh (Lattice, Raft, Ditto) with vendor-specific conflict rules. 2) Cross-enclave or cross-partner movement goes through a CDS or is re-entered by hand on the releasable enclave. 3) After reconnection, duplicates and stale objects are cleaned manually or ignored.
candidate_gaps.current_solution: Anduril Lattice Mesh, Raft [R]DP sync, Ditto CRDTs, TAK Server federation; CDS guards (TACDS, NEWT) at boundaries.
candidate_gaps.failure_point: Convergence and policy are handled by different products; releasability markings do not aggregate by dominance, so guards apply the most restrictive rule and data is lost or delayed; each mesh is proprietary so two fabrics cannot converge.

candidate_gaps.problem_one_sentence: The same object reported through several independently fused pictures becomes duplicate or conflicting tracks with no auditable provenance, and there is no tactical-echelon catalog that tells a consumer which data product to trust.
candidate_gaps.user: Battle captains and air-defense/C-UAS operators; data-layer administrators; UDRA data stewards
candidate_gaps.current_workflow: 1) Each fabric fuses its own tracks. 2) Bridges (CoT gateways, Link 16 forwarders) re-inject tracks into other systems creating duplicates. 3) Operators mentally de-duplicate or a 'Data Fusion Correlator' is bought per program. 4) Catalogs exist at enterprise level (Advana, Vantage) but UDRA data products at lower echelons are by exception only.
candidate_gaps.current_solution: Vendor-internal correlation (Lattice, IBCS, Maven), JFN object-based common data layer, government 'Data Fusion Correlator' buys, Raft registries in the NGC2 baseline.
candidate_gaps.failure_point: No cross-vendor track identity or provenance model; quality signals and feedback loops absent (UDRA 'Diet Coke' analogy: no labeling, quality or anti-tamper indicators); enterprise catalog connected sources without agreements (IG on Advana).

evidence.claim: Government buys a separate 'Data Fusion Correlator' because SENSEI sensors have coverage, accuracy and clutter limits
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: UDRA presenter listed missing attributes: discoverable products, quality signals, anti-tamper indicators, feedback mechanisms, automated computational governance
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: DoD AI memo requires federated data catalogs within 30 days
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: JIATF-401 selected Lattice as common C-UAS C2 backbone integrating 'hundreds of Joint and Army systems' - implying reconciliation across many track sources
evidence.label: INFERENCE

evidence.claim: Raft assigned NGC2 data and services registries; DoD IG found Advana connected 78 of 387 sources without data-sharing agreements
evidence.label: FACT

candidate_gaps.why_startups_havent_solved: Correlation across proprietary fabrics needs access to each vendor's entity model and to classified track data; the platform owners each prefer to be the single fabric; catalogs are unglamorous.
candidate_gaps.incumbent_response_risk: High: Raft's baseline role covers registries and federation; Anduril owns the entity model. Defensible only as an independent quality/provenance auditor the government wants to own.
candidate_gaps.technical_wedge_hypothesis: A provenance and identity-resolution service that assigns cross-fabric stable IDs to entities, records lineage and quality metrics per producer, and publishes a UDRA-conformant catalog usable at brigade/division on edge compute.
candidate_gaps.mvp_sketch: Ingest CoT from TAK and entities from a Lattice sandbox or mock, resolve duplicates with configurable rules, expose a catalog with quality scores and lineage; demo at a C-UAS-themed hackathon.
candidate_gaps.data_requirement: Synthetic multi-source tracks; later real exercise captures (CUI/Secret).
candidate_gaps.integration_requirement: Lattice SDK, TAK Server, Raft registry APIs, JFN/IBCS interfaces (not public).
candidate_gaps.entry_vehicle: JIATF-401 CSO, xTech hackathon (sensor integration problem area), Tradewinds, DIU Blue Object Management Challenge follow-ons.
candidate_gaps.why_now: Multiple funded fabrics now coexist (Lattice, Foundry, Raft, Maven, JFN) and must interoperate; C-UAS urgency; catalog mandate.
candidate_gaps.killer_risk: Becomes a feature of Raft or Lattice; overlaps S03 fusion vendors; access to classified track data.

candidate_gaps.title: Build a competing general-purpose military data fabric / data mesh platform
candidate_gaps.problem_one_sentence: Services still lack a single interoperable data fabric across echelons and domains, which superficially suggests room for a new platform.
candidate_gaps.user: Program offices seeking an alternative to Anduril/Palantir lock-in
candidate_gaps.current_workflow: Government designates platform vendors under enterprise agreements and integrates through team leads.
candidate_gaps.current_solution: Anduril Lattice (Army baseline lead, $20B vehicle), Palantir Foundry/Maven ($10B ESA, PoR), Raft, Lockheed (25th ID), CDAO WDP.
candidate_gaps.failure_point: Not a failure of supply: the Army baselined its data layer in June 2026 and both incumbents hold decade-long enterprise vehicles; the enterprise layer is being rebuilt by a $821M integrator.

evidence.claim: Army designated Anduril (with Palantir, Raft) to lead the NGC2 common data baseline
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: Anduril $20B and Palantir $10B enterprise ceilings consolidate 120+ and 75 procurement actions respectively
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: Even well-funded government platforms churn (Advana paused, recompete canceled, renamed, IG findings)
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: Anduril valued at $61B and Palantir at ~$441B market cap; both can outspend any startup on the layer
evidence.label: FACT

candidate_gaps.why_startups_havent_solved: It has been 'solved' by designation; absence of alternatives reflects buyer consolidation, not a gap.
candidate_gaps.incumbent_response_risk: Existential.
candidate_gaps.technical_wedge_hypothesis: None credible for a $250k two-founder team.
candidate_gaps.mvp_sketch: Not recommended.

candidate_gaps.entry_vehicle: n/a

segments.saturation_statement: Research appears near saturation for what is reachable under this session's constraints because: (1) the same primary facts (June 22 2026 baseline; Anduril/Palantir/Raft roles; the $10B and $20B enterprise ceilings; the $100M Edge Data Mesh OTA; Maven PoR; Advana/WDP churn; UDRA v1.0) recur across independent mirrors with consistent dates and numbers; (2) the government-side pain evidence converges from four unrelated sources (GAO, DoD CIO ZT PfMO, INDOPACOM, Army UDRA RFI and Jailbreak) on the same seams - undocumented interfaces, classification/releasability, tagging, and a mesh that stops above the tactical echelon; (3) additional GitHub queries on Raft/DAF, SBIR data-fabric awards and Cursor-on-Target fabric integration returned nothing new, indicating the public record on small-vendor traction in this layer is thin rather than unsearched. Gaps that a later stage should close with direct access: Raft's funding and contract values; obligations under the Palantir and Anduril enterprise agreements (USAspending); the FY2026-FY2027 Army and CDAO justification-book lines for the data layer; the text of the Common Data Fabric RFI (Dec 2024) and PM MC RFIs; Ditto's actual DoD contracts; and DOT&E/GAO assessments of NGC2 data-layer performance at PC-C6.

segments.what_it_does: The collection layer converts physical phenomena (reflected light, thermal emission, radar backscatter, RF emissions, sound, seismic vibration, AIS/ADS-B broadcasts, open web content) into data products (imagery, tracks, detections, emitter geolocations, signals metadata) that downstream processing, exploitation and dissemination (PED), fusion, and command-and-control layers consume. It spans sensors (EO/IR cameras, SAR, GMTI radar, passive RF receivers, microphone arrays, unattended ground sensors, sonobuoys), the platforms that carry them (satellites, Group 1-5 UAS, crewed aircraft, ships, USVs, towers, dismounted soldiers), the tasking/collection-management function that decides where sensors look, and the commercial data marketplaces that increasingly sell collection as a service. The economically decisive shift of 2022-2026 is that collection is now partly a bought commodity (NRO EOCL/RCA, NGA Luno, Space Force TacSRT, Army UAS marketplace) rather than only a government-owned capability.

sub_taxonomy.name: Space-based commercial EO/IR (Planet, BlackSky, Vantor/ex-Maxar, Albedo, Satellogic, Hydrosat, Pixxel)
sub_taxonomy.note: Bought under NRO EOCL (2022-2032) and NGA Luno A/B; 3 EOCL primes hold the production position. Highest capital intensity, NOAA-licensed, effectively closed to a $250k team as a builder.

sub_taxonomy.name: Space-based commercial SAR (Capella, Umbra, ICEYE US)
sub_taxonomy.note: NRO Commercial Radar Capabilities study (2022-2025) converted to sole-source Radar Commercial Augmentation operational contracts effective 2026-08-01. Three of five entrants passed.

sub_taxonomy.name: Space-based RF/SIGINT-adjacent (HawkEye 360, Spire, Unseenlabs; Kleos failed)
sub_taxonomy.note: HawkEye 360 has NGA and NRO contracts and filed for IPO in 2026 (FACT: S-1/424B4 on EDGAR). Only unclassified RF geolocation is publicly researchable; classified SIGINT collection is out of scope (Public evidence insufficient).

sub_taxonomy.name: Airborne crewed/large UAS ISR (MQ-9, MQ-1C, HADES, ARES/ARTEMIS/ATHENA, MQ-4C, P-8, RC-135)
sub_taxonomy.note: Prime-dominated (GA-ASI, SNC, L3Harris, Leidos, Northrop, Boeing). Army is transitioning from RC-12/ARL to contractor-owned bridging jets and HADES. No startup wedge in the airframe or sensor; some in the PED software.

sub_taxonomy.name: Small UAS (Group 1-3) organic reconnaissance sensors (Skydio X10D, Teal, Parrot, Vantage, Skycutter, Group 3 additions)
sub_taxonomy.note: Army SRR program of record, Army UAS marketplace ($750M ceiling, expanded to Group 3 and mission payloads in 2026), Drone Dominance and SkyFoundry (goal 10,000/month). The Blue UAS list moved from DIU to DCMA US-X on 2025-12-03. Sensors are commodity (Teledyne FLIR Boson+ 640x512).

sub_taxonomy.name: Passive RF and radar airspace/C-UAS sensing (Hidden Level, DroneShield, Dedrone/Axon, Echodyne, SRC, BlueHalo/AeroVironment, Anduril)
sub_taxonomy.note: Hidden Level received a $100M OTA on 2026-07-30 after T-REX 25.2 and Falcon Peak 25.2. Installation and border defense is the funded demand; dismounted detection is an open RFI.

sub_taxonomy.name: Acoustic detection (Squarehead Discovair, Ukrainian Sky Fortress/Zvook-style networks, Sentrycs adjacent)
sub_taxonomy.note: Army C5ISR Center RFI of 2026-01-14 seeks acoustic detection of Group 1-2 UAS for dismounted troops. Poland tested seven systems in April 2026. No US production program found.

sub_taxonomy.name: Unattended ground sensors (McQ, ARA, Textron, Anduril Sentry towers for CBP)
sub_taxonomy.note: Mature and small (US market on the order of $0.2B/yr per Tier-4 market research, LOW confidence). No 2025-2026 US UGS program award found this session; SOCOM Tactical X 2026 RFI is the nearest signal.

sub_taxonomy.name: Maritime sensing (Saildrone, sonobuoys, USVs, AIS feeds via Spire/Kpler, Windward)
sub_taxonomy.note: Task Force 59 / 4th Fleet style experimentation, largely Saildrone-dominated for USV ISR. RECALL - not re-verified this session.

sub_taxonomy.name: Commercial and open-source intelligence feeds (Dataminr, Recorded Future, Babel Street, Janes, Ursa Space, Vannevar Labs, Danti)
sub_taxonomy.note: Software-only, unclassified, lowest barrier. NGA Luno A/B is the buying vehicle for analytic services; Ursa TrueSight ($21M) and NV5 Almanac ($4.5M) are examples.

sub_taxonomy.name: Collection management, tasking and data access (TacSRT/Global Data Marketplace, JCO, NGA commercial tasking, SkyFi/SkyWatch/UP42 style aggregators)
sub_taxonomy.note: This is where the GAO Aug 2026 report finds missed opportunities (licensing cost, perceived use restrictions, long-term access). TacSRT was zero-funded in the FY2026 request while HASC pushed to make it a program of record.

current_architecture.description: A layered but stove-piped collection enterprise: national/commercial space (NRO-managed EOCL/RCA feeds flowing through NGA and Maven), theater airborne ISR (MQ-9, HADES/ATHENA, Triton) with service PED cells, brigade-and-below organic sUAS whose EO/IR video mostly terminates at the controller or a TAK client, and installation/base sensors (radar, passive RF, acoustic, towers) feeding C-UAS C2 (FAAD C2, Anduril Lattice, Dedrone, etc.). Commercial tasking reaches tactical users through TacSRT and the Global Data Marketplace, or through NGA channels; licensing tiers govern redistribution. TITAN is the Army's designated node to pull space, high-altitude, aerial and terrestrial sensor data into targeting.

current_architecture.security_domain: Commercial space and OSINT products are unclassified with license-tier restrictions (EOCL/Luno tiers govern redistribution to allies); tactical sUAS video is typically unclassified/CUI; TITAN, Maven and airborne multi-INT operate up to SECRET/SCI with cross-domain guards; passive RF and acoustic C-UAS sensors at installations operate unclassified but their detection libraries and performance data become CUI or classified.
current_architecture.connectivity_dependency: Space and airborne collection depend on satellite downlink and enterprise networks; TITAN and brigade cells depend on SATCOM/tactical networks that are bandwidth-limited; sUAS depend on line-of-sight RF links that are jammed; commercial tasking marketplaces are cloud-hosted and reachable only with internet or enterprise connectivity.
current_architecture.what_breaks_when_disconnected: Commercial tasking requests and product downloads stall (products are cloud-delivered); TITAN loses the space and high-altitude feeds it exists to fuse; sUAS video cannot be forwarded beyond the controller; C-UAS sensor nets fall back to local alerting without cross-cueing; analysts revert to manual, local exploitation (INFERENCE from architecture; no session-verified exercise quote).

technical_difficulty.summary: Building sensors and platforms is hard and capital-heavy (optics, SAR RF chains, radiation-tolerant electronics, launch, NOAA licensing, ITAR); the software adjacent to collection (tasking, cataloging, edge detection, sensor onboarding, ML classification of acoustic/RF signatures) is moderately hard and dominated by integration and data-access problems rather than algorithms. Passive RF and acoustic detection are signal-processing and ML problems on commodity hardware, but their credibility is proven only in government test events (T-REX, Falcon Peak, Eastern Shield), which cost time and relationships rather than money.
required_expertise: Remote sensing physics and photogrammetry
SAR processing and RF engineering (for SAR/RF sensing)
Array signal processing and beamforming (acoustic/passive RF)
Embedded ML on Jetson/FPGA at the edge
Geospatial data engineering (STAC, COG, NITF, KLV)
sUAS payload/gimbal integration (MAVLink, proprietary SDKs)
MISB/STANAG standards compliance
Cybersecurity for Blue UAS Framework listing
Collection-management doctrine (ATP 2-01, ISR synchronization)
technical_difficulty.hardest_problem: Detecting and classifying small, RF-silent (fiber-optic or autonomous) UAS at useful range with near-zero false alarms from a dismounted or vehicle-portable passive sensor, and doing it cheaply enough to field at platoon scale; on the space side, the hardest unsolved problem is not collection but timely, license-compliant delivery of commercial products to tactical users without connectivity.
technical_difficulty.commodity_parts: MEMS microphones, SDR receivers (USRP, RTL/Lime class), Jetson-class edge compute, Teledyne FLIR Boson/Hadron thermal cores, COTS gimbals, LTE/mesh radios, cloud GEOINT stacks (STAC catalogs), open-source CV models; commercial imagery itself via vendor APIs at hundreds to thousands of dollars per tasking.

capital_intensity.proof_of_concept_usd: Software-only (tasking aggregation, catalog/search, edge CV on existing sUAS video): $30k-$150k. Acoustic or passive-RF sensor node prototype on commodity hardware: $100k-$400k. Sensor payload for Group 1-2 UAS: $150k-$600k. Any satellite: $5M+ before launch and not feasible at $250k.
capital_intensity.credible_military_demo_usd: Software: $200k-$800k (Blue UAS Framework listing, ATO-adjacent hardening, participation in a JCO or Army test event, travel and GFE integration). Passive sensor hardware: $1M-$4M (ruggedized units, multi-site test at T-REX/Falcon Peak-type events, FCC/NTIA coordination if any emission). Satellite: $30M-$150M.
capital_intensity.first_production_deployment_usd: Software: $1M-$5M (ATO, sustainment, on-site integration engineers). Sensor hardware at installation scale: $5M-$25M working capital (Hidden Level required roughly a decade and multiple test events before a $100M OTA). Constellation: $100M+.
capital_intensity.assumptions: Assumes two founders with $250k can reach POC only in the software or commodity-sensor lanes; assumes access to a sponsor for test events, which is unpriced but rate-limiting; assumes no classified facility. Hardware estimates are INFERENCE from comparable startups' disclosed raises (Hidden Level, Squarehead, Echodyne) and are LOW-MEDIUM confidence.

regulatory_access.prototype_with_commercial_unclassified_d: yes - commercial imagery (Planet, BlackSky, Umbra open data), open AIS/ADS-B, public drone acoustic datasets and self-collected sUAS video allow a full unclassified prototype; note that a credible C-UAS prototype needs live drone flights under FAA Part 107 and, for detection ranges, access to a test range.
regulatory_access.government_data_required: Not for POC. Required for a credible demo: government test events (T-REX, Falcon Peak, JCO demos, Eastern Shield-type allied tests) and, for tasking products, access to TacSRT/GDM or NGA licensing terms. Classified signature libraries are required only for SIGINT-adjacent work (out of scope).
regulatory_access.itar_ear: Remote sensing spacecraft fall under USML Category XV; many IR/thermal imaging systems above thresholds and fire-control-adjacent sensors under Category XII; military UAS and payloads under Category VIII; SIGINT/RF surveillance electronics under Category XI. Commercial-grade thermal cores (Boson class) and SDRs are typically EAR 6A/5A controlled rather than ITAR. Software that is purely commercial-imagery tasking/search is generally EAR99 or EAR-controlled at most. A specialist export-control review is required before any hardware or defense-article software work; this is a description, not a legal judgment.
regulatory_access.cui_likely: Yes for anything touching installation sensor layouts, detection performance, Blue UAS cybersecurity artifacts, or unit collection plans; commercial-imagery tasking metadata is often CUI once tied to military users.
regulatory_access.classified_integration_eventually: Likely for TITAN, Maven and airborne multi-INT integration (SECRET/SCI); avoidable if the product stays on the commercial-data and unclassified installation-security side, as Hidden Level and BlackSky's unclassified Luno services show.
regulatory_access.cleared_personnel_at_mvp: No for unclassified commercial-data or sensor MVPs; a cleared engineer or partner becomes necessary at first classified integration.
regulatory_access.non_us_person_founder_note: A German founder who becomes a US permanent resident is a US person for ITAR/EAR deemed-export purposes and SBIR ownership counting; an Indonesian founder who is not a US person cannot receive ITAR technical data or certain EAR technology without a license, cannot hold a personnel clearance, and creates FOCI questions for any facility clearance. SBIR/STTR eligibility requires the concern to be more than 50% owned and controlled by US citizens or permanent residents (or eligible US entities), so the cap table matters. Mitigations to review with counsel: keep the product on commercial, unclassified data (EAR99-adjacent), assign the non-US founder to commercial/international roles, use a technology control plan, and consider allied-market (NATO, Indonesia is not a close partner for ITAR purposes) go-to-market. These are constraints requiring specialist legal review, not conclusions.

why_not_solved.explanation: Sensors and satellites need $30M-$1B; the three EOCL primes and three RCA holders already absorbed that capital and hold multi-year positions. New entrants compete for NRO study money, not operational buys.

Collection is bought by NRO, NGA, Space Force (TacSRT/JCO), Army PEOs, SOCOM and CBP under different vehicles and license regimes; TacSRT's zero FY2026 request shows no single budget owner for tactical commercial ISR.
The most valuable collection (SIGINT, GMTI, national imagery) is classified, so the unclassified startup wedge is confined to commercial data, C-UAS and OSINT lanes.
Vendor tasking APIs, Skydio's closed payload/cloud ecosystem, Palantir's TITAN/Maven stack, and Anduril's Lattice each own an integration seam and have little incentive to open it.
Blue UAS listing, ATOs, NOAA remote-sensing licenses and export controls slow every hardware entrant; the DIU-to-DCMA move is an admission the process did not scale.

Cheap edge ML, commodity SAR, and mass drone production (SkyFoundry) are 2023-2026 developments; RF-silent fiber-optic FPVs only became a mass threat in 2024-2025, creating the acoustic/passive-RF demand now reflected in the 2026 RFI.

For space-based EO/SAR/RF supply, the market is served and consolidating (Capella acquired, HawkEye IPO, Vantor rebrand). For installation-level passive RF, Hidden Level is scaling. Absence of startups in those lanes is not opportunity.

attractiveness.bull: Collection is now a bought commodity with real, recurring money (EOCL, RCA, Luno orders, $76.8M via GDM, $192M TITAN, $52M X10D, $100M Hidden Level OTA). The Army is flooding units with drones and sensors faster than it can ingest their data, DCMA is turning Blue UAS into a marketplace that needs vetted sensors and software, and the Army is openly asking for dismounted acoustic detection. Commodity hardware plus ML lets a small team prototype a passive sensor or a sensor-data product for well under $250k, and the government's own GAO says commercial data is underused because of access friction, which is a software and licensing problem.
attractiveness.bear: Every funded lane already has a scaled or scaling incumbent (Vantor/Planet/BlackSky, Capella/Umbra/ICEYE, HawkEye, Palantir, Anduril, Skydio, Hidden Level). Building sensors is capital-intensive and ITAR-adjacent, which is poor fit for a $250k team with a non-US-person founder. The tasking/aggregation gap is being filled by the government itself (TacSRT/GDM) and by the vendors' own platforms, and TacSRT's budget history shows tactical commercial ISR still lacks an owner. Dismounted acoustic detection is at RFI stage with no US program, and NATO-fielded Squarehead is ahead. Data access to sUAS video and TITAN is controlled by primes.
attractiveness.verdict: Low-to-medium for this team. Do not build sensors or satellites. The only defensible wedges are software that sits between commodity or commercial collection and the user: (a) acoustic/passive detection ML on commodity hardware aimed at the Army's 2026 dismounted RFI, accepting hardware exposure, or (b) sensor-agnostic ingestion/indexing of organic sUAS collection, which depends on OEM data access. Both are MEDIUM-confidence hypotheses that later stages should red-team.
