market_stage.rationale: Across five years the sequence shows study/pilot vehicles converting into production or operational buys (EOCL, RCA, TITAN, SRR, Luno orders, Hidden Level OTA), which is the signature of a transitioning market; the exception is tactical commercial ISR access (TacSRT), which has demonstrated demand but no stable budget line, and acoustic/dismounted C-UAS, which is at RFI stage.

proto_purgatory.notes: TacSRT: pilot since 2023, praised as working, expanded in 2025, then zero-funded in the FY2026 request and rescued only by HASC language; that is a pilot-after-pilot pattern caused by budget ownership, not technology. Commercial SAR: four years of study contracts before operational awards, and 2 of 5 entrants dropped. VLEO/hyperspectral/thermal startups (Albedo, Pixxel, Hydrosat) remain on NRO SCE study contracts and SBIR/STRATFI awards without production (RECALL, LOW). Blue UAS: many listed vendors, but orders concentrate on Skydio. Counter-example: Hidden Level moved from test events to a $100M OTA within about a year of T-REX 25.2/Falcon Peak 25.2.
proto_purgatory.opportunity_or_warning: Mixed. For tactical commercial ISR access it is a warning (no budget owner; the government builds its own aggregator). For passive/acoustic C-UAS it is closer to opportunity (fresh RFI, recent conversion precedent). For new space sensors it is a warning for a small team.

candidate_gaps.title: Dismounted low-cost passive (acoustic + RF) detection of Group 1-2 and RF-silent UAS
candidate_gaps.problem_one_sentence: Small units have no cheap, non-emitting way to detect and classify small drones, including fiber-optic/autonomous RF-silent ones, and the Army opened an RFI for it in January 2026.
candidate_gaps.user: Dismounted squads/platoons, forward CPs, convoy escorts; secondary: installation security and allied forces
candidate_gaps.current_workflow: 1) Soldier hears or sees a drone. 2) RF detectors (DroneShield, Dedrone) alert only if the drone emits. 3) Radar is vehicle or site mounted and emits. 4) Alert is shouted or pushed to ATAK if a C2 link exists. 5) Engagement by small arms or handheld effector.
candidate_gaps.current_solution: Vehicle/site radars (SRC, Echodyne), RF detectors, installation passive RF (Hidden Level), NATO-fielded Squarehead Discovair, improvised Ukrainian phone-based acoustic nets
candidate_gaps.failure_point: RF detection fails on RF-silent drones; radars emit and are not dismount-portable; acoustic systems are either large arrays or unfielded in US service; false alarms and range are unproven at platoon scale

evidence.claim: Army C5ISR Center RFI seeks acoustic detection of Group 1 and 2 UAS for dismounted troops to inform requirements and prototyping
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: DoD awarded a $100M OTA to Hidden Level after T-REX 25.2 and Falcon Peak 25.2 for passive sensing that detects RF-silent aircraft, showing budget and procurement path for passive detection at installation scale
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: Poland tested seven acoustic detection systems under Eastern Shield; Norway contracted Discovair; UNIFY.C2 integrated Squarehead in Sep 2026: multiple companies attempting partial solutions, none scaled in the US
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: Ukraine fielded thousands of cheap acoustic sensors (Sky Fortress-type) to detect Shahed-class and small UAS, demonstrating a low-cost architecture
evidence.label: INFERENCE (RECALL - not re-verified this session)

candidate_gaps.why_startups_havent_solved: Detection performance must be proven at government test events that take a year or more to enter; acoustic classification needs large labeled datasets of drone signatures in realistic noise; incumbents bundle detection into C2 suites; the US requirement only crystallized in 2026.
candidate_gaps.incumbent_response_risk: High: Hidden Level can add microphones; DroneShield/Dedrone can add acoustic modules; Squarehead can enter US via a partner (already with UNIFY.C2).
candidate_gaps.technical_wedge_hypothesis: ML classification on a commodity MEMS microphone array plus SDR on a Jetson-class board, sold as a cheap networked node with CoT/ATAK output, competing on cost per node and software rather than array hardware; data flywheel from many deployed nodes.
candidate_gaps.mvp_sketch: Four-to-eight mic array plus SDR in a ruggedized box under $1,500 BOM; on-device classifier trained on self-collected and public drone acoustic datasets; publishes detections as CoT to ATAK; demo against Part 107 flights of representative Group 1 drones, then seek C5ISR Center or JCO test slot.
candidate_gaps.data_requirement: Labeled acoustic and RF signatures across drone types, distances and noise environments; self-collectable for commercial drones, but military-relevant signatures require test-event access
candidate_gaps.integration_requirement: CoT/ATAK, FAAD C2 or Lattice/other C-UAS C2 interfaces; Blue UAS Framework-style cyber vetting for software; MOSA/SOSA optional
candidate_gaps.entry_vehicle: C5ISR Center RFI follow-on prototyping, JCO demonstrations, Army xTech, SBIR (subject to ownership eligibility), allied tests (Eastern Shield-type)
candidate_gaps.why_now: RF-silent fiber-optic drones since 2024-2025; Army Drone Dominance and C-UAS reorganization; 2026 RFI; DCMA marketplace lowers listing friction
candidate_gaps.killer_risk: Hardware-intensive with a non-US-person founder (ITAR Category XI/XII exposure if it becomes a defense article) and range/false-alarm physics that a small team may not beat; incumbents add acoustic as a feature.

candidate_gaps.title: Tactical access to commercial ISR: license-aware discovery, tasking and delivery for units below the CoCom J2
candidate_gaps.problem_one_sentence: Commercial imagery and analytics are underused because of licensing cost confusion, perceived use restrictions, long-term access doubts and cloud-only delivery, and the pilot that fixes it (TacSRT) has no stable budget owner.

candidate_gaps.current_workflow: 1) Unit identifies a need. 2) Requests via NGA channels (national tasking) or, if eligible, TacSRT/GDM marketplace. 3) Vendors bid; product delivered to a cloud portal. 4) Analyst checks license tier before sharing with partners. 5) Product downloaded over enterprise network and re-hosted locally. 6) Repeat per vendor portal.
candidate_gaps.current_solution: TacSRT/Global Data Marketplace, NGA EOCL/Luno delivery, vendor portals (BlackSky Spectra, Planet, Vantor), commercial aggregators (SkyFi, SkyWatch, UP42)
candidate_gaps.failure_point: No single license-aware, DDIL-tolerant, unit-level tasking and delivery layer; budget for it was zeroed in FY2026 request; GAO documents underuse

segments.what_it_does: PED is the layer that turns raw sensor collection (full-motion video, EO/IR still imagery, SAR, SIGINT/ELINT cues, radar tracks, OSINT/PAI) into usable intelligence products and machine-readable tracks/detections. Processing = format conversion, georegistration, orthorectification, decompression and metadata normalization (e.g., MISB KLV, NITF/GeoTIFF, STANAG 4607 GMTI). Exploitation = human and algorithmic detection, classification, identification, change detection, track initiation/maintenance, multi-INT correlation, and analyst judgement producing reports, target packets and annotated products. Dissemination = pushing products, alerts and tracks to consumers (targeting cells, fires systems, common operating pictures, coalition partners) across security domains and bandwidth-limited links. The 2024-2026 shift is from human-in-the-loop 'ISR analysis' to platform-mediated, AI-assisted workflows (Maven Smart System, TITAN, AIDP) that must run from enterprise cloud to disconnected tactical nodes.

sub_taxonomy.name: Imagery/FMV computer vision (detection, classification, change detection)
sub_taxonomy.note: Object/event detection on EO/IR/SAR and FMV; the most commoditized algorithmic sub-layer (Maven, RAIC Labs, BlackSky Spectra, Matroid). Data and labeling access, not model architecture, is the differentiator.

sub_taxonomy.name: GEOINT commercial analytics (facility monitoring, feature extraction, economic indicators)
sub_taxonomy.note: NGA's Luno A (imagery analysis) and Luno B (commercial AI products) are the buying vehicles; vendors are largely imagery operators (BlackSky, Ursa Space) and analytics firms.

sub_taxonomy.name: Multi-INT / track fusion and target development
sub_taxonomy.note: Correlating detections and tracks across sensors into targetable entities; TITAN and Maven Smart System own this at division/corps and joint echelons. Fusion is where classification and program-of-record ownership are heaviest.

sub_taxonomy.name: Analyst workflow, collaboration, automated reporting and prioritization
sub_taxonomy.note: Tasking-to-product workflow tooling, alerts, queue prioritization, report generation; historically DCGS-A/AF DCGS/DCGS-N; now Maven Smart System, AIDP (Palantir), Vannevar Labs. This is where 'swivel-chair' pain is documented (MIPB 2026).

sub_taxonomy.name: Edge / DDIL PED (on-platform and tactical-node processing, data reduction)
sub_taxonomy.note: Processing at or near the sensor to reduce bandwidth and work disconnected; AIDP's 2026 Call for Solutions explicitly requires 72-hour autonomous operation on tactical edge nodes with later sync to Maven. Fewest scaled products; most startup-shaped.

sub_taxonomy.name: AI/ML lifecycle for PED models (labeling, T&E, deployment, drift)
sub_taxonomy.note: Army's Project Linchpin (PM IS&A) and Maven's model onboarding (Open DAGIR) define this; it is an enabling sub-layer rather than an end-user product.

technical_difficulty.summary: Detection models on imagery are commoditized; the hard parts are (a) operating with sparse, shifting, classified training data, (b) robust georegistration and track continuity across sensors, (c) running and updating models on constrained edge hardware without connectivity, (d) integrating into Maven/AIDP/TITAN data models and cross-domain guards, and (e) earning analyst trust (calibration, provenance, low false-alarm rates). Difficulty: medium for a niche edge or workflow product; very high for a fusion/targeting platform.
required_expertise: computer vision on EO/IR/SAR/FMV incl. MISB metadata handling
geospatial engineering (projections, georegistration, STAC/OGC)
edge ML deployment and model compression (Jetson/Xavier-class, FPGA-optional)
distributed systems with intermittent sync (CRDT-style or store-and-forward)
data engineering/labeling pipelines
intelligence analysis tradecraft and targeting workflow
DevSecOps for IL5/IL6/cATO
cross-domain solution constraints
technical_difficulty.hardest_problem: Delivering trustworthy, low-false-alarm detections and consistent tracks under DDIL conditions with models that must be trained on data the startup cannot access until it is already inside a program - a data-access chicken-and-egg that favors Palantir, NGA-Maven and imagery operators.
technical_difficulty.commodity_parts: Object detectors (YOLO/DETR families), foundation vision models, orthorectification libraries (GDAL), STAC catalogs, TAK plugins, Kafka/streaming, cloud IL5 hosting patterns, MISB KLV parsers.

capital_intensity.proof_of_concept_usd: $100k-$400k (commercial imagery and open FMV datasets, cloud GPUs, 2-3 engineers for 6-9 months)
capital_intensity.credible_military_demo_usd: $1M-$4M (SBIR Phase II or OTA-scale: rugged edge hardware, exercise participation such as Scarlet Dragon/PC-C, IL5 hosting, initial ATO artifacts, one FSE, Secret-cleared staff)
capital_intensity.first_production_deployment_usd: $5M-$25M (cATO/ATO on SIPR, SCIF/facility clearance, cleared engineers, 24/7 support, MSS/AIDP integration certification, multi-site fielding)
capital_intensity.assumptions: Software-only product; no proprietary sensors; leverages commercial imagery for PoC; assumes onboarding through Open DAGIR or AIDP subcontract rather than standalone program; ranges are INFERENCE from SBIR/OTA sizes seen (Danti $1.2M/$1.9M; TITAN prototype $178M at platform scale).

regulatory_access.prototype_with_commercial_unclassified_d: partly - commercial EO/SAR imagery, open FMV datasets and NGA Luno-style unclassified analytics allow a real PoC; but tactical FMV, SIGINT cues and targeting workflows are not reproducible without government data.
regulatory_access.government_data_required: Yes for anything beyond commercial GEOINT: MISB FMV from RPAs, TITAN/AIDP data models, labeled military datasets (Maven/Linchpin). Access usually comes only via SBIR Phase II, OTA or a prime's subcontract.
regulatory_access.itar_ear: Software specially designed for military ISR exploitation or targeting can be a defense article/technical data under ITAR (e.g., USML Cat XI) or fall under EAR 600-series/other ECCNs; a non-US-person founder or engineer triggers deemed-export analysis. Requires specialist export-control counsel before any government data or spec is shared with non-US persons.
regulatory_access.cui_likely: Yes - nearly all program documentation (AIDP CfS attachments, GFI lists, product demonstration plans) is CUI; requires NIST 800-171/CMMC posture.
regulatory_access.classified_integration_eventually: Yes - MSS, TITAN and AIDP operate at Secret/TS; production deployment requires cleared personnel, facility clearance (FCL) and likely a cross-domain path.
regulatory_access.cleared_personnel_at_mvp: Not strictly required for a commercial-imagery MVP or SBIR Phase I; required by Phase II/OTA demo stage for FMV/targeting work (INFERENCE from program security domains).
regulatory_access.non_us_person_founder_note: An Indonesian founder who is not a US person cannot hold a US security clearance, would be a deemed-export concern for ITAR/EAR technical data, and could trigger FOCI review for facility clearance if holding significant ownership/control. The German founder's status improves after permanent residency for export purposes (US person) but clearances generally require citizenship. Mitigations (segregated corporate structure, US-person control, proxy/SSA agreements) exist but need FOCI/export counsel; this is a first-order constraint for S04 specifically because the valuable data and integration points are classified.

why_not_solved.explanation: Palantir is prime on MSS, AIDP and TITAN; integration seams, ontologies and app-onboarding are controlled by one vendor and the government's Open DAGIR effort is the only counterweight. Startups must build on, not around, this.

Military FMV, SAR, SIGINT cues and labeled targeting data live on SIPR/JWICS; models cannot be trained or validated on them without being inside a program. Commercial imagery is available but is where imagery operators already bundle analytics.
Production PED runs at Secret/TS; cleared staff, facility clearance and cross-domain approvals gate every deployment, adding 12-24 months and millions in cost.
Dozens of formats (MISB, NITF, STANAG 4607/4676, CoT, Link 16, USMTF) and legacy DCGS interfaces; the 'swivel chair' problem is an integration and governance failure more than an algorithm failure.
Foundation vision models, few-shot detection and edge inference hardware capable of DDIL operation matured only 2022-2025; the requirements (AIDP 72-hour autonomy) are being written in 2026.
Army (AIDP/TITAN), CDAO (MSS), NGA (Luno), AF (DCGS/AFWERX), Navy (DCGS-N) buy separately; small vendors accumulate SBIRs across buyers without a single transition owner.

Task orders for commercial analytics are tens of millions spread across 10-13 vendors; sustaining a cleared engineering team on that revenue is marginal, which is why several startups (Rebellion, Primer) retreated.

attractiveness.bull: Real production money is arriving (TITAN $192M, MSS program of record, Luno TOs) and OSD is mandating consolidation, which creates an app-ecosystem opportunity (Open DAGIR, AIDP 'partner environments' and edge nodes) where small vendors can plug specialized capabilities into a funded platform. DDIL edge PED and workflow automation are explicitly demanded in 2026 solicitations and are not owned by a scaled startup. Commercial imagery allows an unclassified MVP.
attractiveness.bear: The layer is consolidating around Palantir/Anduril with government backing; startups without clearances and government data are structurally locked out of the valuable (classified, fused, targeting) parts. Commercial-analytics niches are crowded by imagery operators and 23 Luno vendors, task orders are small, and SBIR-only companies (Danti, RAIC) show proto-purgatory. For this founder team, the non-US-person constraint hits S04 harder than most segments.
attractiveness.verdict: Medium-low overall; medium for a narrow DDIL-edge or analyst-workflow component sold into AIDP/MSS/TAK ecosystems; low for anything platform-shaped or targeting-adjacent.

market_stage.rationale: The full RFI -> prototype -> production -> repeat sequence is visible for the platform tier (Maven, TITAN) within 2022-2026, so the segment is past prototyping for incumbents. candidate_gaps.user: Brigade/battalion S2 sections, MDTF and SOF intelligence teams, small-UAS operators
candidate_gaps.current_workflow: 1) Organic sensors (small UAS, ground sensors, radios) record locally; 2) when a link exists, raw video/imagery is pushed to brigade or enterprise DCGS-A/AIDP or Maven; 3) enterprise models detect/annotate; 4) analyst reviews and builds products; 5) products are pushed back down over the same congested link; 6) when disconnected, steps 2-5 stall and analysts screen video manually and hand-plot in TAK or slides.

segments.what_it_does: The transport layer of C4ISR: it moves voice, data, video and machine-to-machine traffic between sensors, shooters, command posts and higher echelons when there is no fixed infrastructure and an adversary is jamming, geolocating and cyber-attacking the links. Concretely it comprises (1) tactical radios and waveforms (narrowband voice/data, wideband MANET such as TSM, Wave Relay and Silvus MN-MIMO), (2) beyond-line-of-sight transport (GEO/MEO/pLEO SATCOM incl. Starlink/Starshield, troposcatter, HF), (3) commercial cellular/5G bubbles, (4) gateways that translate between waveforms and data links (e.g., BACN, Link 16 gateways), (5) the IP/network layer that stitches these together (routing, encryption, SD-WAN style multi-path transport, PACE - primary/alternate/contingency/emergency - plan execution), and (6) NetOps: planning, monitoring, spectrum management and cyber defense of the tactical network. In 2025-2026 the U.S. Army explicitly separates a 'transport layer' from the data, integration and application layers of Next Generation Command and Control (NGC2), and the Space Force is buying a proliferated-LEO backbone (SDN Backbone / MILNET) as the space segment of that transport.

sub_taxonomy.name: Wideband MANET radios and waveforms
sub_taxonomy.note: Silvus StreamCaster (Motorola Solutions since Aug 2025), Persistent Systems MPU5/Wave Relay, TrellisWare TSM (Viasat), Doodle Labs Mesh Rider, Rajant Kinetic Mesh, goTenna. Requires deep RF/waveform/DSP and crypto expertise plus hardware manufacturing; the least accessible sub-segment for a software-first two-founder team. Label: FACT for vendor list, INFERENCE for accessibility.

sub_taxonomy.name: Program-of-record tactical radios (HMS, Falcon, IMBITR)
sub_taxonomy.note: L3Harris AN/PRC-158/163/167/171, Collins AN/PRC-162, Thales AN/PRC-148C. NSA Type-1 certified, ITAR, decade-long IDIQs. Effectively closed to startups except as waveform or app partners (RECALL - not re-verified this session, MEDIUM).

sub_taxonomy.name: SATCOM transport (GEO/MEO/pLEO, Starshield, MILNET/SDN Backbone)
sub_taxonomy.note: Space Force pLEO IDIQ ceiling raised to $13B in Oct 2024; SpaceX reported to hold ~97% of pLEO task orders; SpaceX won $2.29B SDN Backbone award May 2026. Dominated by SpaceX, Viasat/Inmarsat, SES, Hughes, Iridium; startup room is in terminals, management/orchestration and multi-orbit routing, not capacity.

sub_taxonomy.name: Gateways and cross-link translation
sub_taxonomy.note: Airborne gateways (Northrop BACN on E-11A), Link 16 gateways (Viasat BATS-D, Collins), ABMS gatewayONE experiments, Fuse Integration airborne networking pods. Mixed RF + software; the software-defined translation layer is increasingly software.

sub_taxonomy.name: Multi-path transport orchestration / automated PACE
sub_taxonomy.note: Software that chooses and fails over between MANET, LEO, GEO, 5G, HF transports transparently to applications (Aalyria Spacetime under DIU ORIENT/HSA, Persistent Cloud Relay, Anduril Lattice Mesh, Navy Overmatch software-defined networking). Mostly software/networking expertise; RF knowledge helpful but not gating.

sub_taxonomy.name: Tactical NetOps, monitoring and spectrum awareness
sub_taxonomy.note: Army Unified Network Operations (UNO) and Tactical Network Operations (TNO) prototypes (RII prime with CodeMettle subcontractor, Phase II Oct 2025); goal is to cut the number of tools S6/G6 use. Software expertise dominant.

sub_taxonomy.name: DDIL-tolerant data movement (store-and-forward, sync, compression)
sub_taxonomy.note: Middleware such as Ditto (AFLCMC ceiling $28M FFP contract, 2025) and Anduril/Palantir edge sync; overlaps with the data fabric segment but the pain originates in transport constraints. Software expertise dominant.

sub_taxonomy.name: Tactical cellular/5G bubbles and private LTE
sub_taxonomy.note: Fenix Group, Oceus, Nokia/Ericsson tactical kits; Nett Warrior next-gen EUD RFI (2026) asks for 5G plus multiple Army MANET waveforms in one device. RF + software mixed (RECALL for vendor names, MEDIUM).

current_architecture.description: Army tactical transport today is a layered mix: Integrated Tactical Network (ITN) fielded to brigades since 2021 in capability sets combining program-of-record two-channel leader radios (AN/PRC-163, AN/PRC-148C) and manpacks with commercial MANET radios (Silvus StreamCaster, Persistent MPU5, TrellisWare TSM radios), a secure-but-unclassified enclave for Nett Warrior/ATAK, commercial LEO (Starlink/Starshield terminals) and GEO SATCOM, and unit-level routing/encryption. C2 Fix (2024-2026) is the bridge that simplified this for Transformation-in-Contact brigades; NGC2 (Anduril-led team for 4th ID, Lockheed-led team for 25th ID) defines a four-layer stack (transport, data, integration, application) with Persistent Wave Relay selected as network foundation for the NGC2 prototype (Oct 2025) and an $87.5M Army contract to Persistent (Feb 2026). Army plans a division-level NGC2 production ecosystem in FY27 and service-wide fielding by a tentative 2032. Above the tactical edge sit DISA/Space Force SATCOM (pLEO IDIQ, WGS, MUOS), SDA Transport Layer and the SpaceX-built SDN Backbone. Air: Link 16, BACN, ABMS gateways. Navy: CANES afloat network plus Overmatch software-defined networking on CSGs. NetOps is fragmented across vendor tools; UNO/TNO aims to unify.

current_architecture.security_domain: Mixed: SBU/unclassified commercial enclaves (ITN 'secure but unclassified'), SECRET (most PoR radios, Link 16), and TS/SCI for MILNET/NRO transport. Zero trust is an explicit AUNP 2.0 objective.
current_architecture.connectivity_dependency: This layer IS connectivity; upper layers (COP, fires, logistics) assume it. Commercial LEO dependence on a single provider (SpaceX ~97% of pLEO task orders) is itself a documented concentration risk (INFERENCE from Quilty and Breaking Defense reporting).
current_architecture.what_breaks_when_disconnected: Voice reverts to line-of-sight only; cloud-hosted C2 apps lose sync; PLI and chat stall; NetOps loses visibility; units fall back to manual PACE execution and runners. DIU ORIENT problem statement: swarms must keep operating as a system of systems in disrupted, low-bandwidth environments.

technical_difficulty.summary: Bimodal. Building radios/waveforms is very hard (RF front ends, MIMO/anti-jam DSP, NSA crypto certification, ruggedization, supply chain) and dominated by well-funded incumbents. Building the software above the radios - multi-path transport orchestration, PACE automation, NetOps visibility, DDIL data movement, gateway translation - is hard but tractable for strong distributed-systems/networking engineers, and is exactly where NGC2's 'transport-agnostic' direction and UNO create demand. The catch: software must work against proprietary radio APIs, on classified or CUI enclaves, and be proven in field exercises.
required_expertise: IP networking and routing in lossy/asymmetric links (OLSR/BATMAN-class MANET routing, QoS, multicast)
SDN/SD-WAN and policy-driven path selection
Distributed systems and eventual consistency for DDIL sync
Cryptography integration (IPsec, HAIPE, CSfC) and zero trust
Radio and SATCOM management APIs (SNMP/REST of Silvus, Persistent, Starlink, Kymeta)
Embedded Linux on SWaP-constrained edge boxes
RF fundamentals and spectrum management (important, not gating for software plays)
Waveform/DSP/FPGA (critical only if building radios)
TAK/CoT and Link 16/VMF message handling for gateways
technical_difficulty.hardest_problem: Making a heterogeneous, multi-vendor, multi-orbit transport self-configure and fail over under jamming and movement without a signal soldier in the loop, while proving it through a security accreditation and a division-scale exercise - and doing so without radio vendors closing their APIs.
technical_difficulty.commodity_parts: COTS MANET radios, Starlink/Starshield terminals, 5G kits, rugged x86/ARM edge compute, open-source routing (FRR, BATMAN-adv), WireGuard/IPsec, TAK Server, MQTT/NATS, DTN implementations.

capital_intensity.proof_of_concept_usd: $100k-$400k for a software-only orchestration/NetOps/DDIL-sync prototype using 6-12 COTS radios and Starlink terminals in a lab or field test (assumes two founders, no clearance, unclassified data).
capital_intensity.credible_military_demo_usd: $1M-$4M: engineers with tactical network experience, export-controlled radio loans or purchases ($10k-$50k per Silvus/MPU5 node), participation in NetModX/Cyber Quest/Project Convergence-type events, initial cyber accreditation work, SBIR Phase I/II or DIU CSO funding.
capital_intensity.first_production_deployment_usd: $5M-$20M for software fielded to a division (ATO, CSfC/crypto integration, 24/7 support, training) ; $30M+ if any hardware radio/gateway product must be manufactured and certified.
capital_intensity.assumptions: Software-first play; hardware avoided; assumes SBIR/OTA non-dilutive funding covers demos; $250k founder capital reaches only proof of concept and initial customer discovery.

regulatory_access.prototype_with_commercial_unclassified_d: partly - orchestration, NetOps and sync prototypes can be built on unclassified COTS radios and Starlink, but realistic waveform behavior and PoR radio integration need CUI/ITAR technical data
regulatory_access.government_data_required: Not for MVP; needed later: radio management APIs (some ITAR-controlled), network topologies (CUI), exercise data.
regulatory_access.itar_ear: Military MANET radios and Type-1 radios are ITAR (USML XI) or EAR 5A001-class; pure networking software is often EAR (5D002 encryption) but any defense-specific integration can pull into ITAR. Requires specialist export-control review before any non-U.S.-person founder touches technical data.
regulatory_access.cui_likely: Yes - network plans, PACE plans, and exercise results are CUI at minimum.
regulatory_access.classified_integration_eventually: Yes - SECRET enclaves for PoR radios and Link 16; TS for MILNET/NRO transport.
regulatory_access.cleared_personnel_at_mvp: No for unclassified MVP; yes (SECRET) for anything touching PoR radios or NGC2 classified enclaves within 12-24 months.
regulatory_access.non_us_person_founder_note: An Indonesian founder who is not a U.S. person cannot access ITAR technical data or defense-article source code without an export license, and a facility clearance would trigger FOCI mitigation (possibly a proxy board or SSA) if that founder holds significant ownership/control. A German founder becoming a permanent resident becomes a 'U.S. person' for ITAR/EAR purposes on obtaining green card status but still needs citizenship for a personnel clearance. Workable structure: non-U.S.-person founder owns equity but is walled off from controlled technical data via a technology control plan; all of this needs specialist legal review - no definitive judgment here.

why_not_solved.explanation: Each MANET vendor (Silvus, Persistent, TrellisWare) owns its waveform, routing and management plane; cross-vendor orchestration threatens their lock-in, and PoR radios are Type-1 boxes with restricted interfaces.
Anything in the encrypted path needs NSA/CSfC approval and an ATO; waveform changes need lab and field certification; this slows software iteration to program timelines.
Army (PEO C3N), Space Force (CSCO/SDA), Navy (Overmatch), USAF (AFLCMC/ACC), DIU and SOCOM each buy transport separately; GAO-25-106454 documents CJADC2 isolation.

Affordable pLEO (Starlink since ~2021, MILNET 2025-26), cheap wideband MANET and edge compute only now make transport-agnostic, software-defined tactical networks realistic; NGC2's four-layer stack is 2025-2026 vintage.
Real networks mix SECRET and SBU enclaves, coalition partners, legacy SINCGARS/Link 16 and commercial IP; no single vendor sees or controls all of it.

Pure tactical-network software has a small buyer set; dual-use (public safety, mining, energy, autonomy) exists for radios (Rajant, Silvus) but less for military PACE/NetOps tooling, limiting venture appetite.
Real jamming performance, spectrum plans and Overmatch/MILNET architectures are classified; startups build against sanitized proxies.

attractiveness.bull: The Army has committed roughly $3.3B through FY2026 to C2 Fix/NGC2 and is explicitly buying a 'transport-agnostic' stack that needs software to orchestrate mesh, LEO and 5G; UNO/TNO is moving to a fieldable MVP and an IDIQ; Space Force is spending billions on a LEO backbone whose tactical edge integration is unsolved; DIU's ORIENT problem (mesh-to-long-haul bridging for swarms) drew 130 proposals, proving demand; Silvus's $4.4B+ exit shows this layer generates real M&A outcomes; software layers can be prototyped with COTS gear for under $500k.
attractiveness.bear: Radios are closed to a two-person team; the software layer is being contested by Anduril (now NGC2 data-layer lead), Aalyria, Persistent (Cloud Relay), Motorola/Silvus and RII/CodeMettle, all with head starts and cleared staff; everything of value requires ITAR/CUI access and eventually SECRET clearances, which collides with the non-U.S.-person founder; sales cycles run through OTAs and exercises measured in years; DIU HSA has been in prototype since 2022 with a pilot only in 2026 (purgatory signal); SpaceX's vertical integration removes much of the SATCOM software opportunity.
attractiveness.verdict: Medium attractiveness for a software-only wedge (NetOps/automated PACE, DDIL data movement, gateway translation) sold as a subcontractor into NGC2/UNO teams; low attractiveness for hardware/RF plays; the founder immigration/ITAR profile is the single biggest structural risk and should be legally scoped before any pursuit.

market_stage.rationale: The sequence RFI -> OTA prototype -> follow-on award -> announced FY27 production for NGC2, plus a $13B services vehicle and a $2.29B backbone award in space, shows the segment crossing from prototyping into production. However, GAO flags missing life-cycle costs, and startup-facing DIU efforts remain in pilot, so 'Transitioning' rather than 'Mature'.

proto_purgatory.notes: Program-level purgatory is low: NGC2 moved from OTA prototypes (2025) to an $87.5M follow-on and an FY27 production plan within ~18 months. Startup-level purgatory is visible: DIU HSA awards in July 2022 reached only a 2026 pilot; UNO has iterated RFI (2024) -> OTA Phase I/II (2025) with IDIQ awards 'planned early 2026' unconfirmed; Aalyria has accumulated HSA and ORIENT prototypes without a disclosed production program; Fuse Integration's last verifiable milestone is a 2022 IDIQ seat.
proto_purgatory.opportunity_or_warning: Warning for space/orchestration startups selling to DIU alone; opportunity for teams that attach to an NGC2 or UNO prime already headed to production, because those vehicles now have a fielding date and budget scrutiny (GAO) that favors delivered software over more pilots.

candidate_gaps.title: Vendor-agnostic automated PACE / multi-path transport orchestration at brigade and below
candidate_gaps.problem_one_sentence: Units carry three to five transports (MANET, Starlink/pLEO, GEO, 5G, HF) but path selection and failover are still planned on paper and executed by signal soldiers, so applications stall during jamming or movement.
candidate_gaps.user: S6/G6 NetOps cells and platform crews at brigade and below; NGC2 transport-layer integrators
candidate_gaps.current_workflow: 1) S6 writes PACE plan in a spreadsheet/OPORD annex; 2) each radio/terminal configured in its own vendor tool; 3) link degrades; 4) soldier notices via user complaints; 5) manual switch to alternate transport, re-key, re-address; 6) apps re-sync or data is re-entered.
candidate_gaps.current_solution: Vendor-specific tools (Silvus Spectrum Dominance, Persistent Cloud Relay), Aalyria Spacetime (prototype), Anduril Lattice Mesh, Navy Overmatch SDN (classified), manual PACE.
candidate_gaps.failure_point: No cross-vendor, policy-driven controller that sees all transports and moves flows automatically; each fix is single-vendor and re-introduces lock-in.

candidate_gaps.why_startups_havent_solved: Radio vendors guard management APIs; testing requires export-controlled radios and exercise slots; buyers prefer the NGC2 prime to own orchestration; security accreditation of a controller in the encrypted path is slow.
candidate_gaps.incumbent_response_risk: High - Anduril leads NGC2 data layer and can bundle orchestration; Motorola/Silvus and Persistent can extend proprietary controllers.
candidate_gaps.technical_wedge_hypothesis: An open, radio-agnostic transport controller (policy engine + per-flow path selection + link quality telemetry) that runs on the existing edge box, speaks each radio's SNMP/REST API, and exposes a simple PACE-as-code interface; sell as a component to NGC2/UNO teams rather than a standalone program.
candidate_gaps.mvp_sketch: Linux appliance/container with adapters for Silvus, MPU5, Starlink and a 5G CPE; measures latency/loss/jitter per link; applies PACE policy; demonstrated with 8-10 nodes and induced jamming in a field test; TAK/CoT traffic as the app.

candidate_gaps.killer_risk: Radio vendors close APIs or the NGC2 prime builds it in-house; founders cannot access ITAR technical data due to non-U.S.-person status.

segments.what_it_does: The edge compute/edge AI layer is the forward-deployed compute substrate and software stack that lets C2, ISR and fires applications run when the enterprise cloud is unreachable. It spans (1) rugged servers and vehicle/dismount-form-factor compute (x86, ARM, NVIDIA Jetson/GPU) hosted in command posts, vehicles, aircraft, ships and on soldiers; (2) container/Kubernetes orchestration and air-gapped software delivery (image registries, package bundles, updates over constrained links); (3) local AI inference (ATR/computer vision, RF classification, LLM assistants) and the lifecycle of those models (packaging, distribution, validation, retraining); (4) data-tier services for DDIL operation: local caching, store-and-forward, conflict-free synchronization when links return, prioritization of what data leaves the node; (5) observability/fleet management for tens to hundreds of nodes without saturating tactical links. In the Army NGC2 architecture this layer is the 'hub' (command-post compute hosting apps locally) and 'spoke' (vehicle nodes) tier of the data mesh; in the Air Force it is the base/ABMS edge node; in the Navy it is shipboard Overmatch compute.

sub_taxonomy.name: S06.1 Rugged edge hardware
sub_taxonomy.note: Vehicle/CP/dismount compute chassis and servers (Klas Voyager now under Anduril, Atmos ATMOS2 selected for NGC2, Crystal Group, Dell rugged/XR, HPE Edgeline, Cubic DTECH, Parsons TECN, Curtiss-Wright/Mercury for airborne, Jetson-based boxes). Largely commoditized at the silicon level; differentiation is SWaP-C, MIL-STD qualification, vehicle integration and program-baseline position.

sub_taxonomy.name: S06.2 Air-gapped delivery and edge orchestration
sub_taxonomy.note: Kubernetes distributions and disconnected delivery: Defense Unicorns UDS/Zarf, Platform One Big Bang/Iron Bank, Rancher Government (RKE2/K3s), Red Hat MicroShift/Device Edge, Spectro Cloud Palette Edge, SUSE/ZEDEDA. The most mature commercial-to-DoD sub-segment; one unicorn already exists.

sub_taxonomy.name: S06.3 Edge AI inference and model lifecycle
sub_taxonomy.note: On-device/on-node ATR, CV, RF and LLM inference plus model packaging, distribution, validation and retraining at the edge: TurbineOne Frontline, Striveworks Chariot, EdgeRunner AI, Ozni AI (SBIR), Palantir (edge Foundry/AIP), Anduril Lattice, Army Project Linchpin (MLOps pipeline). Less mature; first large FFP award (TurbineOne, $98.9M, Sep 2025) signals transition.

sub_taxonomy.name: S06.4 DDIL data synchronization and prioritization
sub_taxonomy.note: Local-first data, CRDT/peer-to-peer sync (Ditto), pub-sub in DIL (WPL VERBENA SBIR), hub-and-spoke reconciliation as demonstrated in Ivy Mass. Partially solved inside the NGC2 data mesh primes; standalone commercial products exist but evidence of scaled military deployment is thin.

sub_taxonomy.name: S06.5 Edge observability and fleet operations
sub_taxonomy.note: Health, version, and security state of many nodes (65+ in Ivy Sting 5) without radiating or saturating links; day-2 operations by soldiers rather than DevOps engineers. Least evidenced sub-segment; mostly INFERENCE that this is a pain.

sub_taxonomy.name: S06.6 Integration/accreditation of apps onto edge platforms
sub_taxonomy.note: Getting third-party apps onto accredited edge platforms (cATO, Iron Bank hardening, Game Warden). Overlaps S06.2; commercial vendors include Second Front, Defense Unicorns, Anchore, RegScale.

technical_difficulty.summary: Hardware is commoditized (Jetson/x86 in MIL-STD chassis from a dozen vendors). Orchestration for air-gapped delivery is largely solved by open-source Zarf/UDS plus Big Bang, with the residual difficulty being fleet-scale day-2 operations by non-experts. The genuinely hard, under-solved problems are (a) model lifecycle at the edge under DDIL (safe, bandwidth-aware distribution; validation against sensor/environment drift; soldier-driven retraining with provenance), (b) principled data prioritization and conflict resolution across partitions at scale (65+ nodes), and (c) doing all of this inside classification, accreditation and EMCON constraints that commercial edge tooling ignores (no telemetry home, no license phone-home, multi-level enclaves, cross-domain).
required_expertise: Kubernetes internals and air-gapped delivery (Zarf/UDS, Big Bang, RKE2/K3s)
Distributed systems: partition tolerance, CRDTs, gossip/pub-sub under intermittent links
Edge ML deployment (TensorRT/ONNX on Jetson, quantization, on-device training) and MLOps
Tactical networking (bandwidth budgets, EMCON, mesh radios, PACE plans)
DoD security architecture (cATO, Iron Bank hardening, IL levels, CDS interfaces, STIGs)
Hardware sympathy: thermal/power envelopes of vehicle-mounted compute
technical_difficulty.hardest_problem: Keeping tens to hundreds of heterogeneous edge nodes at a known-good software and model state, and reconciling their data, when links are intermittent, bandwidth is contested, radiating is dangerous and the operators are soldiers rather than SREs - while every artifact remains accreditable.
technical_difficulty.commodity_parts: Rugged chassis and servers; NVIDIA Jetson/GPU modules; Kubernetes distributions; container registries; basic OTA update mechanisms; standard CV models; commercial fleet-management dashboards.

capital_intensity.assumptions: PoC: two founders, consumer/Jetson devkits, open-source K8s and public CV datasets, simulated DDIL links. Credible demo: 3-6 engineers for 9-18 months, 2-4 rugged nodes ($15k-$60k each), MIL-STD/EMI pre-testing, exercise participation costs (travel, a lab), an IL4/IL5 dev environment, SBIR Phase I/II or DIU CSO funding covering most of it. First production: cATO/Iron Bank hardening, integration onto NGC2/Overmatch baselines through a prime, 24/7 support, FSO and possibly a cleared facility, 12-24 months of sales cycle burn. Ranges are HYPOTHESIS grounded in comparable startup trajectories (TurbineOne raised $36M before a $98.9M FFP; Defense Unicorns raised $15M STRATFI before scaling).

regulatory_access.prototype_with_commercial_unclassified_d: yes - orchestration, sync and model-lifecycle tooling can be built and demonstrated on open-source stacks and public datasets; realism comes from partnering with a unit or SBIR sponsor for CUI data later.
regulatory_access.government_data_required: Not for the platform layer; required for ATR model quality (sensor-specific imagery) and for proving value on real mission threads. CUI and later SECRET data become necessary at the integration stage.
regulatory_access.itar_ear: Generic edge software and COTS compute are typically EAR (EAR99 or 5D002 for crypto). Software 'specially designed' for military ATR, fire control or C2 integration can fall under ITAR USML Category XI(d)/XXI or be treated as defense articles by primes; hardware in military chassis may be Category XI. Requires export-control counsel; deemed-export rules affect the non-US-person founder.
regulatory_access.cui_likely: Yes - any work touching NGC2 data models, unit SOPs, exercise results or program documentation will be CUI; requires NIST SP 800-171/CMMC posture.
regulatory_access.classified_integration_eventually: Yes - brigade-and-above C2 runs on SECRET networks; production integration will require cleared personnel and a facility or a prime/host partner with one.
regulatory_access.cleared_personnel_at_mvp: No for MVP; yes by first production deployment (INFERENCE from NGC2 security domain).
regulatory_access.non_us_person_founder_note: The Indonesian founder (not assumed a US person) creates deemed-export exposure for any ITAR/EAR-controlled technical data, potential FOCI concerns if they hold significant equity/control, and ineligibility for personnel clearances. SBIR/STTR requires the small business to be more than 50% owned and controlled by US citizens or permanent residents (the German founder qualifies once an LPR). DIU CSOs and OTAs have no citizenship requirement per se but ITAR authorization is still needed to share controlled data. Mitigations to review with counsel: keep the non-US founder on the EAR99/open-source platform side, structured equity, technology control plan, or a US-person-controlled entity. Not a legal judgment - specialist review required.

why_not_solved.explanation: For the hardware substrate and air-gapped delivery mechanics, the problem is substantially solved: commodity rugged compute from many vendors, Zarf/UDS/Big Bang for delivery, and NGC2 hubs demonstrated local operation with later sync. Startups entering here compete against an incumbent unicorn and a vertically integrated prime (Anduril+Klas).

On-device training/inference on Jetson-class hardware, CRDT sync libraries and LLM-based sense-making at the edge became practical only since ~2022-2024, which is why model lifecycle and DIL data services are still SBIR/first-award stage.

NGC2 data mesh internals (Lattice, Foundry, Raft) are vendor-controlled; third-party edge services must integrate through the prime's APIs and registries, which limits standalone products and pushes startups into subcontract roles.

Every container, model and node must be accreditable (cATO, Iron Bank, STIGs, CDS). Commercial edge tools that phone home for licensing, telemetry or registries fail these constraints, and re-engineering them for EMCON/air-gap is slow.

Heterogeneous radios, vehicles, enclaves and legacy programs of record (per GAO, services in isolation) mean every deployment is a bespoke integration; this is why Picogrid earns a stream of small integration contracts rather than one large product buy.
PEO C3N, PEO IEW&S, AFLCMC, NAVWAR, MCSC, CDAO and DIU each buy edge capability separately; there is no single edge compute program office, so scaling requires multiple parallel captures.

Rugged hardware margins are thin and volumes small; software value accrues to whoever owns the data layer. Point solutions (sync, observability) are features from the prime's perspective and are hard to sell standalone.

attractiveness.bull: Real money is now moving: $99.6M NGC2 prototype, June 2026 baseline award, $98.9M FFP for edge ATR, $136M Series B for air-gapped delivery, repeated Phase III awards. The Army has an explicit organization (PM C2 Infrastructure) for edge compute and a serialized exercise cadence (Ivy Sting, Ivy Mass, PC-C6) that gives startups concrete integration events. Model lifecycle and DIL data prioritization are recognized but immature - a small, technically strong team can build a credible open-source-based wedge on unclassified data and enter via SBIR Phase I/II, DIU CSO or a prime's NGC2 team.
attractiveness.bear: Hardware is commoditized and consolidating (Anduril bought Klas; Atmos is the NGC2 hardware baseline). Delivery/orchestration is owned by a $1B incumbent with a GSA vehicle. Data mesh and model tooling inside NGC2 are controlled by Anduril/Palantir/Raft/Striveworks, and the June 2026 baseline award makes that team the gatekeeper. Remaining gaps look like features, not companies. Classification and accreditation force cleared staff early, and the non-US-person founder complicates ITAR and SBIR ownership rules. Absence of a visible standalone competitor in observability/sync is not evidence of demand.
attractiveness.verdict: Medium-low for a $250k two-founder team as a standalone edge platform; medium as a narrow, prime-integrated software wedge (edge model validation/distribution or bandwidth-aware data prioritization) pursued via SBIR/DIU with a subcontract path onto NGC2 or Overmatch.

candidate_gaps.title: Edge model lifecycle under DDIL: validate, distribute and roll back ATR/CV models across many nodes over contested links
candidate_gaps.problem_one_sentence: Once ATR/CV models are trained or updated at the edge, there is no evidenced, accredited way to validate them against the local sensor/environment, distribute deltas over constrained links to 65+ nodes, track which model version is running where, and roll back safely.
candidate_gaps.user: Brigade/division S2 sections and unit tech teams running Frontline-class ATR and NGC2 decision tools; PEO IEW&S/PM C2 Infrastructure as program owners.
candidate_gaps.current_workflow: 1) Model trained centrally (Linchpin-style pipeline) or on-device by soldiers; 2) packaged as container/ONNX; 3) pushed via Zarf/UDS bundle or vendor-specific data mesh when a link exists; 4) node operators manually confirm version; 5) performance drift discovered anecdotally during exercises; 6) retraining loop closed by sending data back when bandwidth allows.
candidate_gaps.current_solution: Vendor-integrated: TurbineOne (on-device training), Striveworks Chariot (MLOps) inside Team Anduril, Palantir AIP, Anduril Lattice model deployment; generic: Zarf bundles.
candidate_gaps.failure_point: No independent validation gate for models arriving at a node; full-model pushes exceed bandwidth budgets; version state across nodes is opaque after partitions; rollback is manual; provenance/T&E evidence for accreditation is ad hoc (INFERENCE from architecture and public statements; no primary document describes the failure explicitly).

evidence.claim: Army paid $98.9M FFP for on-device ATR where all data is processed on soldiers' devices, signalling that cloud-dependent model pipelines are unacceptable at the edge
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: Team Anduril scaled to 65+ edge nodes and 20+ applications at Ivy Sting 5, creating the fleet-scale version-management problem
evidence.label: FACT (company-reported)

evidence.claim: ATEC is transforming test and evaluation for NGC2, implying that evaluating continuously updated software/models is an open institutional problem

candidate_gaps.why_startups_havent_solved: Model tooling is being absorbed into the NGC2 primes' stacks (Striveworks/Palantir/Anduril); standalone MLOps vendors lack edge/DDIL and accreditation focus; the problem became real only when node counts and on-device training scaled in 2025-2026.
candidate_gaps.incumbent_response_risk: High - Striveworks and Palantir can add validation/distribution features; Anduril controls the data layer APIs.
candidate_gaps.technical_wedge_hypothesis: A bandwidth-aware model distribution and validation service: delta/patch model updates with per-node validation against a held-out local sensor sample, signed provenance manifests usable as accreditation evidence, and a partition-tolerant version ledger; delivered as a Zarf-packaged component that runs beside any inference runtime.
candidate_gaps.mvp_sketch: Open-source-based prototype on 3-5 Jetson nodes with simulated DDIL links (tc/netem): delta model updates, local validation harness on public datasets (e.g., xView/DOTA), CRDT version ledger, dashboard that works over kilobit links; demo rollback after a bad model.
candidate_gaps.data_requirement: Public overhead/EO datasets for MVP; CUI sensor imagery from a sponsor unit for credibility; eventually SECRET for program integration.
candidate_gaps.integration_requirement: Must integrate with Zarf/UDS or Big Bang packaging and expose APIs to Lattice/Foundry/Chariot; hardware-agnostic (Jetson, x86 GPU).
candidate_gaps.entry_vehicle: Army/AF SBIR Phase I-II (edge AI topics), DIU CSO, or subcontract to a Team Anduril/Lockheed member for PC-C6; xTech-style competitions.
candidate_gaps.why_now: Node counts and on-device training are scaling (65+ nodes), NGC2 baseline award (Jun 2026) fixes the platform to integrate against, and July 2026 Pace-Setting demonstrations create demand for evidence of model trustworthiness.
candidate_gaps.killer_risk: The primes treat this as a feature and close it within 12 months; without a data-layer position the startup is a subcontractor with no pricing power.

candidate_gaps.title: Bandwidth-aware data prioritization and reconciliation across partitioned edge nodes
candidate_gaps.problem_one_sentence: When links are intermittent, nodes need a policy-driven way to decide what data leaves first, at what fidelity, and how conflicting COP edits are reconciled on reconnection - today this is handled by vendor-specific mesh logic and manual deconfliction.
candidate_gaps.user: Division/brigade G6/S6, hub operators, fires and intel cells whose products compete for the same links.
candidate_gaps.current_workflow: 1) Hub loses division cloud; 2) apps keep local state; 3) on reconnection the data mesh replicates whatever it can; 4) operators deconflict duplicate/conflicting track and graphic objects by hand; 5) large products (FMV, imagery) are pushed opportunistically or not at all.
candidate_gaps.current_solution: Anduril/Palantir data mesh replication inside NGC2; Ditto CRDT sync in pilots; SBIR-stage pub-sub (WPL VERBENA).
candidate_gaps.failure_point: Prioritization is not policy-driven by mission phase; replication logic is opaque to operators; conflict resolution semantics for C2 objects are vendor-specific (INFERENCE).

segments.what_it_does: This layer turns positions, sensor detections and reports into a shared, map-based picture that people and machines can act on. It comprises (1) foundation geospatial data (basemaps, imagery, elevation/3D terrain, feature data, symbology standards such as MIL-STD-2525), (2) position reporting and blue-force tracking (BFT) that publishes own-force locations over radios/SATCOM, (3) track management that ingests detections from radars, EO/IR, RF, and data links, correlates/deduplicates them into single tracks with identity (friend/hostile/unknown) and track-quality, (4) the common operational picture (COP) application that fuses those layers with overlays (graphics, control measures, geofences, airspace) and lets operators annotate, chat and task, and (5) the plumbing that synchronizes all of the above across servers, radios and edge devices in disconnected, degraded, intermittent and limited (DDIL) conditions. In the U.S. force the dismounted/tactical COP is dominated by the government-owned Team Awareness Kit (TAK: ATAK/WinTAK/iTAK/TAK Server), the mounted COP by JBC-P/Mounted Mission Command, the air-and-missile-defense track picture by IBCS/CEC/Aegis/Link 16, and the theater/joint picture increasingly by Palantir (Maven Smart System) and Anduril (Lattice, NGC2 data layer).

sub_taxonomy.name: Foundation geospatial data and services
sub_taxonomy.note: Basemaps, imagery, elevation, 3D terrain/3D Tiles, feature data, map production and serving (NGA, Army Geospatial Center, Esri, Vantor/Maxar, Cesium/Bentley, One World Terrain). Largely commoditized at the data layer by NGA/commercial contracts; differentiation lies in currency, resolution, 3D, and delivery to the edge.

sub_taxonomy.name: Blue-force tracking and position reporting
sub_taxonomy.note: JBC-P/MMC over BFT-2 L-band SATCOM and terrestrial radios; ATAK over Nett Warrior/MANET/mesh (goTenna, Somewear, Persistent Systems). Includes GPS-denied position integrity, which overlaps the PNT segment.

sub_taxonomy.name: Track management and correlation (air/missile/maritime)
sub_taxonomy.note: IBCS, FAAD C2, Aegis, CEC, Link 16 / JREAP, JTMC. Fire-control-quality tracks, dual-track resolution, track identity. Historically prime-dominated and classified; highest technical bar.

sub_taxonomy.name: COP applications and clients
sub_taxonomy.note: TAK family (government-owned, free), JBC-P/MMC-S, CPCE, SitaWare, Palantir Gotham/Maven, Anduril Lattice, Immersive Wisdom. Commoditizing at the basic map-and-icons level; value migrating to data layers and workflow/plugins.

sub_taxonomy.name: Sensor-to-map workflows and overlays
sub_taxonomy.note: Georegistration of drone/ISR video to maps, rapid 3D reconstruction at the edge (Reveal Farsight), automated change detection (Vantor Luno B), c-UAS sensor tracks onto the tactical map (FAAD C2, Lattice), overlays/geofences/airspace measures (TAIS/ADAM cell).

sub_taxonomy.name: DDIL synchronization and offline geospatial
sub_taxonomy.note: TAK Server federation, offline tile packages (MBTiles/GeoPackage), delta sync of overlays, low/no-bandwidth collaboration (Immersive Wisdom), edge-to-cloud data mesh (NGC2). This is where founders report the most manual workaround today (INFERENCE).

sub_taxonomy.name: Coalition/partner COP federation and releasability
sub_taxonomy.note: Mission Partner Environment, ASCA, NATO standards (APP-6, ADatP-3, JC3IEDM/NVG), TAK federation across national servers, Ukraine Delta. Heavy on security/cross-domain accreditation.

current_architecture.description: A layered but fragmented architecture. At the dismounted/tactical edge, ATAK on Android end-user devices exchanges Cursor-on-Target (CoT) messages peer-to-peer or through TAK Server (federated, TLS, with mission packages and data sync). Mounted forces use JBC-P/Mounted Mission Command on Leonardo DRS MFoCS hardware with Viasat BFT-2 L-band SATCOM transport, being modernized under MMC-S (software) and MMC-T (transport). Command posts use CPCE and, in the NGC2 divisions, an Anduril Lattice / Palantir Foundry edge-to-cloud data mesh with third-party applications. Air and missile defense runs fire-control-quality track management on IBCS (Army), Aegis/CEC (Navy), FAAD C2 (c-UAS/SHORAD) connected via Link 16/JREAP and, experimentally, JTMC. Foundation data flows from NGA (Map of the World, commercial imagery via Luno/EOCL), Army Geospatial Center, One World Terrain (3D Tiles/Cesium) and Esri ArcGIS servers, typically pre-packaged to the edge as MBTiles/GeoPackage/KMZ. Theater/joint COPs increasingly use Palantir Maven Smart System. Interoperability between these stacks depends on translation gateways and standards (CoT, VMF, Link 16 J-series, ASCA, NATO NVG/APP-6), and in practice on liaison officers and manual re-entry (INFERENCE).

current_architecture.connectivity_dependency: High. BFT-2 depends on L-band SATCOM; ATAK depends on MANET/mesh/cellular or SATCOM to reach TAK Server; NGC2 data mesh assumes intermittent links with edge nodes; track management for air defense demands low-latency dedicated links (IFCN, Link 16, CEC DDS).
current_architecture.what_breaks_when_disconnected: Positions go stale and units disappear from the COP; overlays and mission packages diverge between servers and devices; imagery/3D terrain not pre-cached cannot be viewed; duplicate or conflicting tracks persist because correlation requires shared history; chat and tasking revert to voice; on reconnection, bulk resync saturates the link (INFERENCE from architecture; low-bandwidth pain acknowledged by USAF sole-source purchase of Immersive Wisdom and by Bold Quest network-limitation reporting).

technical_difficulty.summary: Basic COP functionality (map, icons, chat, overlays) is a solved, commoditized problem: TAK provides it free with source available, and Esri/Cesium provide the GIS and 3D substrate. The hard problems are (a) fire-control-quality multi-sensor track correlation with identity under latency and adversarial conditions, (b) keeping many devices and servers consistent over DDIL links without flooding them, (c) scaling the picture to thousands of friendly and hostile small drones without operator overload, (d) coalition federation with releasability controls and cross-domain accreditation, and (e) integrating with legacy message standards (VMF, Link 16) whose specifications are controlled. Difficulty is medium for edge/DDIL data sync and plugin work, high for track correlation at fire-control quality and for cross-domain federation.
required_expertise: Geospatial engineering (projections, tiling, 3D Tiles, GeoPackage/MBTiles, symbology)
Distributed systems and CRDT/delta-sync for intermittent networks
Tactical networking (MANET, SATCOM budgets, TAK Server federation, radio integration)
Multi-target tracking and data association (Kalman/IMM, JPDA/MHT, track-to-track fusion)
Android/Kotlin and TAK SDK plugin development; TAKX/web front ends
Cybersecurity and ATO/RMF, STIGs, IL5/secret enclave practices
Message standards (CoT, VMF, Link 16 J-series, NATO STANAGs)
Computer vision/photogrammetry for sensor-to-map workflows (optional but valued)
technical_difficulty.hardest_problem: Correlating and deduplicating tracks from heterogeneous, unsynchronized sensors (drones, c-UAS radars, BFT, Link 16) at the tactical edge with enough confidence to support fires or c-UAS engagement decisions, while degrading gracefully under DDIL and jamming. This sits between what TAK does (position sharing) and what IBCS/CEC do (fire-control networks) and is currently done by liaison officers, JICOs and vendor-specific fusion (Lattice) rather than an open layer.
technical_difficulty.commodity_parts: Map rendering (Mapbox/MapLibre, Cesium), basemap/imagery supply (NGA, Vantor, Planet), the COP client itself (ATAK/WinTAK/TAKX), TAK Server, symbology libraries, tile packaging, chat/messaging, GPS position reporting, cloud hosting at IL5.

capital_intensity.assumptions: Software-only product built as ATAK/TAKX plugin or TAK Server-side service using ATAK-CIV, public TAK Server source and commercial/open imagery; two founders plus 2-4 engineers; demo cost includes SBIR/OTA cycles, a government sponsor for TAK-MIL access, exercise participation (travel, hardware, radios), CUI-compliant infrastructure (NIST 800-171/CMMC) and a cleared advisor; production includes ATO/IL5 hosting, cybersecurity assessment, sustained engineering, integration with a PoR (NGC2 app ecosystem, MMC or SBMC), and 12-24 months of sales cycle. Hardware-inclusive plays (radios, edge compute) would double or triple these ranges. Track-correlation products aimed at fires/air defense need classified test venues and would exceed the top of these ranges.

regulatory_access.prototype_with_commercial_unclassified_d: yes - ATAK-CIV, TAK Server source, OpenStreetMap/commercial imagery, Cesium ion and public MIL-STD-2525 allow a full unclassified prototype; DHS/first-responder TAK users are an unclassified proving ground.
regulatory_access.government_data_required: For military relevance: TAK-MIL builds and plugin SDK (government sponsorship required), JBC-P/VMF and Link 16 message specs (controlled), operational position data (CUI or classified), exercise data. Realistic access comes only with a sponsor (SBIR TPOC, AAL, AFWERX, DIU) or via a prime/Anduril-NGC2 ecosystem partner.
regulatory_access.itar_ear: Commercial mapping software is generally EAR-controlled at low levels, but military-specific TAK-MIL plugins, Link 16/VMF implementations, fire-control track algorithms and anything designed for a defense article can fall under ITAR (USML Category XI/XXI) or 600-series ECCNs. Whether a specific product is ITAR-controlled requires a commodity jurisdiction analysis by export counsel; do not assume ATAK-CIV licensing extends to MIL features.
regulatory_access.cui_likely: Yes - almost any operational integration produces CUI; expect NIST SP 800-171 / CMMC Level 2 obligations early.
regulatory_access.classified_integration_eventually: Likely for track management (IBCS/Link 16/CEC), NGC2 division data and coalition MPE; not necessarily for DDIL map/overlay sync or plugin businesses focused at CUI level or on DHS/allied civil users.
regulatory_access.cleared_personnel_at_mvp: No for an unclassified TAK plugin MVP; yes (at least one cleared FSO/engineer and a facility clearance path) before production integration with secret-level systems.
regulatory_access.non_us_person_founder_note: A non-U.S.-person founder (Indonesian, not a permanent resident) cannot be given access to ITAR technical data or TAK-MIL export-controlled SDKs without a license or exemption, which are rarely granted for this use; a German founder gains U.S.-person status only upon permanent residency. SBIR/STTR eligibility requires the small business to be more than 50 percent owned and controlled by U.S. citizens or permanent residents, so cap-table structure matters. Facility clearance would raise FOCI mitigation questions if non-U.S. ownership or control is material. All of this needs specialist export-control and government-contracts counsel; this file describes the constraints, not a legal conclusion.

why_not_solved.explanation: The basic COP (map, positions, overlays, chat) is solved by government-owned TAK at zero license cost, which removes the commercial market for a new COP client. Any startup must sit on top of or beside TAK, not replace it.

TAK (TPC), mounted (PM MC), soldier-worn (PEO Soldier), division data layer (NGC2), air defense (PEO M&S), foundation data (NGA/AGC/PEO STRI) are separate buyers with separate money; no single office owns the end-to-end picture, as GAO-25-106454 documents at the joint level.

Fire-control track management lives inside IBCS, Aegis/CEC and FAAD C2, whose interfaces and message specs are controlled; Lattice and Foundry are becoming the division-level integration points, giving Anduril/Palantir gatekeeper power over what apps run in NGC2.
The most valuable track and coalition data is secret or higher, so unclassified startups cannot see the real problem until they have sponsors, clearances and enclaves.
Legacy standards (VMF, Link 16, ADatP-3), radio-specific transports and vendor-specific APIs make each integration bespoke; exercises still rely on translation gateways and liaison officers.
TAK plugin work is services-priced; the biggest TAK services house (PAR Government) sold to Booz Allen for a modest sum (RECALL), signaling limited venture-scale product margins in plugins.

Edge GPUs, on-device photogrammetry, CRDT-style sync and cheap commercial 3D terrain (OWT/3D Tiles) only recently made offline 3D and delta-sync practical on soldier devices, so DDIL data logistics is genuinely fresh ground.
Open, vendor-neutral track correlation for dense small-drone environments below the fire-control tier does not exist as a product; JTMC and IBCS address the high end, TAK the low end.

attractiveness.bull: The picture is being rebuilt around data layers (NGC2, Maven, Lattice) and around a free, ubiquitous client (TAK, 500k+ users, TAKX in 2026), which lowers distribution cost for anyone shipping a plugin or server-side service. Real money is moving now: $354M SBMC prototypes, roughly $200M of NGC2 OTAs with a June 2026 baseline decision, repeat OWT and Luno awards, and a five-year sole-source for low-bandwidth collaboration. Drone density and DDIL create new pain that legacy architectures were not designed for, and a two-person team can build a credible unclassified prototype on ATAK-CIV, TAK Server and commercial 3D data for well under $250k.
attractiveness.bear: The client and basemap layers are commoditized by the government itself; Anduril and Palantir now own the division-level integration points and can absorb any adjacent feature; track management at fire-control quality is classified, prime-dominated and beyond a seed-stage team; the buyer landscape is fragmented and slow; TAK plugin businesses are services-priced; and a non-U.S.-person co-founder cannot touch TAK-MIL SDKs or ITAR technical data without licenses. Prior small entrants mostly landed in SBIR/STRATFI or modest sole-source ceilings rather than programs of record.
attractiveness.verdict: Medium overall, with a bimodal split: low for a new COP client, basemap or generic plugin business; medium-to-high for a narrow software wedge in DDIL geospatial data logistics or dense-sensor track deduplication delivered as a TAK/TAKX-native service and positioned to plug into NGC2 and SBMC ecosystems. Not a fit for a two-person team without a U.S.-person technical lead and a government sponsor.

signal_sequence.event: prototype demonstration - JTMC links IBCS and CEC at WSMR; GAO-21-99 flags friendly force tracking gaps
test/evaluation - DOT&E FY2023 assessment of MMC-S; CJADC2 minimum viable capability declared (RECALL)
repeat/production data buys - OWT Phase 4 (Mar), Luno A $290M (Sept); Booz Allen acquires PAR Government (RECALL)
prototype solicitation and awards - Luno B (Jan), GAO-25-106454 (Apr), SBMC RFS (Apr), NGC2 Anduril OTA $99.6M (Jul), Lockheed NGC2 (Sept), SBMC $354M (Sept), TAK 500k users and TAKX roadmap (Nov)

follow-on toward production - Vantor Luno B order (Feb), Vantor OWT up to $217M (Feb), Anduril selected to lead NGC2 common data layer baseline (Jun), PC-C6 (Jul), Anduril SBMC redesign (Aug), JIATF-401 c-sUAS guide (Sept)

market_stage.rationale: Foundation data and the TAK client are mature with repeat buys; the integrating data layer (NGC2) and soldier-worn device (SBMC) are moving from prototype to baseline/follow-on within 12-18 months of award, which is the transition phase. Track management for air defense is mature/production. The segment as a whole is therefore transitioning, with the consolidation point being who controls the division data layer and the TAKX ecosystem.

proto_purgatory.notes: Mixed. Small entrants show classic purgatory patterns: Reveal Technology went SBIR to STRATFI ($33.6M) without a visible program of record; Immersive Wisdom went SBIR to a sole-source ceiling contract and an MDA IDIQ slot; Edgybees and Danti remain in SBIR. Soldier-worn SA itself cycled seven years of IVAS prototypes before restarting as SBMC prototypes. Counter-examples exist: NGC2 moved from a July 2025 OTA to a June 2026 baseline selection, and OWT/Luno show repeat production-style buys, but those went to Anduril/Palantir and Vantor, not to seed-stage companies.
proto_purgatory.opportunity_or_warning: Warning for standalone small vendors selling to program offices; opportunity if the wedge rides an ecosystem that is already transitioning (NGC2 application layer, SBMC/ATAK plugins, TAKX migration) so the startup is pulled into a baseline rather than pushing its own program.

candidate_gaps.title: Open track deduplication and correlation for drone-dense tactical pictures below the fire-control tier
candidate_gaps.problem_one_sentence: Brigade-and-below COPs now receive overlapping detections of the same small drones from c-UAS radars, RF sensors, EO/IR, BFT and partner feeds, and no vendor-neutral layer correlates them into single, identified tracks with confidence before the operator is overloaded.
candidate_gaps.user: ADAM/BAE cell, battle captain, c-UAS operator at company through division; JICO at higher echelons.
candidate_gaps.current_workflow: 1) Each sensor or system publishes its own track/CoT to TAK Server, FAAD C2 or Lattice. 2) Operators see multiple icons for the same object with different IDs. 3) A human (often a liaison or JICO) decides which is real, deletes or merges by hand or via vendor-specific fusion. 4) Friendly drone flights are deconflicted through airspace control measures updated by broadcast, not by automated blue-drone tracking. 5) Engagement decisions wait for confirmation by voice.
candidate_gaps.current_solution: IBCS/JTMC (fire-control tier, heavy, classified), Anduril Lattice fusion (proprietary, tied to Anduril sensors and NGC2), FAAD C2 correlation (Northrop, limited to its sensor set), manual JICO management on Link 16.
candidate_gaps.failure_point: Dual tracks and identity ambiguity multiply with sensor count; correlation logic is siloed in proprietary stacks; nothing runs at the edge in DDIL with open interfaces (CoT/TAK) and explainable confidence.

evidence.claim: Services pursue C2 projects in isolation without clear goals; cross-organizational issues unaddressed.
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: Friendly force tracking between ground and air remains inadequately integrated (fratricide risk).
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: Industry (AeroVironment) argues 2026 drone swarms are being fought with Cold War C2 architecture; MWI notes deconfliction doctrine lags.
evidence.label: INFERENCE

evidence.claim: JIATF-401 issued a 2026 c-sUAS quick reference guide, showing institutional effort to standardize c-UAS response including C2.
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: JTMC exists only at the fire-control network tier (IBCS-CEC), demonstrated in 2021; no tactical-tier equivalent found.
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: Multiple companies (Anduril, Northrop, Systematic, Helsing) attempt fusion within their own stacks; none is open or vendor-neutral at brigade and below.
evidence.label: INFERENCE

candidate_gaps.why_startups_havent_solved: Needs labeled multi-sensor track data that lives at CUI/secret level, sensor vendor cooperation, and a test venue with real drones and radars; validation requires exercises; incumbents keep correlation inside their products as a moat.
candidate_gaps.incumbent_response_risk: High. Anduril can extend Lattice fusion to any sensor and now leads the NGC2 data layer; Northrop can extend FAAD C2. A startup wins only if it becomes the neutral, certified correlation service that program offices want to avoid vendor lock-in.
candidate_gaps.technical_wedge_hypothesis: A TAK-Server-side and TAKX plugin service that ingests CoT and c-UAS sensor feeds, performs track-to-track association with explainable confidence and blue-drone identity via Remote ID / flight-plan cross-referencing, and publishes merged tracks back over CoT; runs on an edge box in DDIL.
candidate_gaps.mvp_sketch: Ingest simulated and DHS/civil drone-detection feeds plus ATAK-CIV positions; demonstrate dedup rate, latency and false-merge metrics on a test range; publish as an open CoT extension.
candidate_gaps.data_requirement: Recorded multi-sensor drone detection data (initially civil/commercial c-UAS and Remote ID), later CUI exercise data via a sponsor.
candidate_gaps.integration_requirement: TAK Server, CoT, FAAD C2 or Lattice interfaces (proprietary; require partnership), Link 16 gateway later.
candidate_gaps.entry_vehicle: Army xTech / AAL, AFWERX SBIR, DIU c-UAS solicitations, JIATF-401 demonstrations, DHS S&T (unclassified path).
candidate_gaps.why_now: Army intent to field very large numbers of small drones and the JIATF-401 stand-up create a track-density problem that did not exist in 2022; NGC2 is defining an application layer that third-party services could plug into.
candidate_gaps.killer_risk: Anduril/Northrop absorb the function inside NGC2/FAAD C2 before a startup gets an exercise slot; fires-adjacent correlation needs classified validation.

candidate_gaps.title: DDIL geospatial data logistics: delta-sync and prioritized distribution of basemaps, 3D terrain and overlays to the edge
candidate_gaps.problem_one_sentence: Units still pre-load maps and 3D terrain by hand and lose overlay consistency across devices and servers when links drop, because no fielded service versions, prioritizes and delta-syncs geospatial data across TAK Server federations and NGC2 edge nodes.
candidate_gaps.user: Brigade/battalion geospatial engineers, TAK Server administrators, S6, team leaders loading devices before missions.
candidate_gaps.current_workflow: 1) Geospatial cell downloads imagery/OWT/terrain, builds MBTiles/GeoPackage/KMZ packages. 2) Packages are sideloaded to end-user devices or pushed as TAK mission packages, often by hand or USB (sneakernet). 3) Overlays are edited on multiple servers; on reconnection, conflicts are resolved manually or overwritten. 4) Bulk resync after outages saturates SATCOM/MANET links. 5) Updates to 3D terrain are rarely propagated during the operation.
candidate_gaps.current_solution: TAK Server federation and data sync (whole-object, not delta-optimized; RECALL), Immersive Wisdom for low-bandwidth collaboration, Anduril/Palantir edge-to-cloud mesh inside NGC2, manual packaging by geospatial cells.
candidate_gaps.failure_point: No content-aware prioritization or delta encoding for tiles/3D Tiles/overlays across intermittent links; no consistent versioning of the picture across federated servers; edge devices cannot request just what they need.

evidence.claim: USAF sole-sourced a five-year, up to $25M contract specifically for no/low-bandwidth collaborative operations software.
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: Bold Quest 2025 interoperability was limited by network challenges during a short deployment window.
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: OWT 3D terrain is integrated into ATAK and is procured at scale (up to $217M, Feb 2026), increasing the volume of data that must reach edge devices.
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: NGC2 is explicitly built as an edge-to-cloud data mesh for intermittent links, showing the Army recognizes the sync problem.
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: Reveal Technology's edge 3D reconstruction won STRATFI and was rushed to a brigade before JRTC, indicating demand for offline terrain that fielded systems do not meet.
evidence.label: INFERENCE

evidence.claim: Manual pre-loading and USB distribution of map packages is the standard practice in TAK units.
evidence.label: INFERENCE

candidate_gaps.why_startups_havent_solved: Unglamorous infrastructure; buyers assume TPC or the data-layer prime will handle it; hard to demo without radios and a field exercise; economics look like a feature, not a product.
candidate_gaps.incumbent_response_risk: Medium-high: TPC could add delta sync to TAK Server; Anduril/Palantir own NGC2 transport. Mitigant: TPC moves slowly and is understaffed relative to its user base (INFERENCE), and a neutral service that works across TAK, NGC2 and coalition servers has a role.
candidate_gaps.technical_wedge_hypothesis: A content-addressed, priority-aware sync engine for geospatial artifacts (tiles, 3D Tiles, overlays as CRDT documents) exposed as a TAK Server plugin/federation peer and an ATAK/TAKX plugin, with bandwidth-budgeted scheduling per link.
candidate_gaps.mvp_sketch: Two TAK Servers and ten ATAK-CIV devices over a throttled, lossy link; show 5-10x reduction in bytes to converge overlays and OWT-like 3D tiles versus native data sync, with conflict-free overlay merges.
candidate_gaps.data_requirement: Open basemaps, Cesium ion or OSM 3D, synthetic overlays; no government data needed for MVP.
candidate_gaps.integration_requirement: TAK Server plugin API (public source), ATAK SDK (CIV then MIL), later NGC2 data layer APIs via partnership.
candidate_gaps.entry_vehicle: Army xTech, AFWERX SBIR, TPC engagement through a sponsor, DHS/CBP or allied (e.g., NATO, Australia) TAK users as unclassified first customers.
candidate_gaps.why_now: TAKX migration (2026) reopens the client ecosystem; OWT/3D data volumes are exploding; NGC2 needs a third-party application ecosystem to prove openness.
candidate_gaps.killer_risk: TPC ships an equivalent in TAK Server, making the product a free feature; or the Army treats sync as the data-layer prime's job.

candidate_gaps.title: Coalition COP federation with releasability-aware filtering
candidate_gaps.problem_one_sentence: Sharing positions, overlays and tracks with partners still depends on translation gateways, liaison officers and manual sanitization because no service tags COP objects with releasability and enforces partner-specific views across TAK, SitaWare and national systems.
candidate_gaps.user: Coalition liaison officers, MPE administrators, foreign disclosure officers, partner-nation battle captains.
candidate_gaps.current_workflow: 1) Each nation runs its own COP/servers. 2) Data is bridged via ASCA/NFFI gateways or exported and re-imported. 3) Foreign disclosure review is manual. 4) Cross-domain solutions move sanitized subsets between enclaves. 5) Liaison officers re-key what cannot cross.
candidate_gaps.current_solution: TAK Server federation (technical connectivity only), NATO standards, Systematic SitaWare, accredited cross-domain solutions, MPE enclaves.
candidate_gaps.failure_point: Releasability is not a first-class attribute on COP objects; enforcement is by enclave rather than by object; setup time per exercise is long; network fragility compounds it.

candidate_gaps.incumbent_response_risk: High; cross-domain vendors and primes own accreditation relationships.

candidate_gaps.mvp_sketch: Federate two TAK Servers representing two nations; enforce policy-driven filtering and audit; demonstrate at a NATO or Five Eyes unclassified interoperability event.
