candidate_gaps.title: TAK plugin and integration business (commoditized government-owned ecosystem)
candidate_gaps.problem_one_sentence: Units want mission-specific TAK plugins and integrations, but the ecosystem is government-owned, approval-gated and services-priced, so it does not support a venture-scale product company.
candidate_gaps.user: SOF teams, brigade S6, DHS/CBP units, allied TAK users.
candidate_gaps.current_workflow: 1) Unit identifies need. 2) Contracts a TAK services house (Booz Allen/PAR, small integrators) or uses in-house developers. 3) Plugin built against TAK SDK, submitted to TPC for MIL approval. 4) Distributed via tak.gov or unit sideload. 5) Maintained across ATAK releases and now TAKX migration.
candidate_gaps.current_solution: Booz Allen/PAR Government, numerous small SDVOSB integrators, TPC-funded plugins, open-source community (CivTAK).
candidate_gaps.failure_point: Not a failure of capability but of economics: no license revenue, TPC gatekeeping, release churn.

candidate_gaps.title: Sensor-to-map at the edge: georegistered drone video, rapid 3D and change overlays without reach-back
candidate_gaps.problem_one_sentence: Small units collect drone video and images that cannot be quickly turned into georegistered overlays, 3D models and change alerts on their TAK map without cloud reach-back or a GEOINT cell.
candidate_gaps.user: Platoon/company drone operators, company intelligence support teams, brigade geospatial cells.
candidate_gaps.current_workflow: 1) Drone captures video/photos. 2) Operator screenshots or describes location by voice. 3) Data is later uploaded when connectivity exists; 3D products come back hours to days later from higher echelons or commercial vendors. 4) Change relative to prior imagery is judged by eye.
candidate_gaps.current_solution: Reveal Farsight (edge 3D, STRATFI), Edgybees (georegistration), Vantor Luno B change detection (enterprise, not edge), OWT (pre-computed), vendor-specific drone ground stations, Palantir/Maven at theater level.
candidate_gaps.failure_point: Products are point solutions tied to specific drones or need GPUs/cloud; none is a standard TAK-integrated pipeline from any MISB-compliant feed to overlay in minutes offline.

evidence.claim: Reveal secured a $33.6M STRATFI to scale edge 3D modeling and supported 101st Airborne for JRTC.
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: NGA is paying for automated change detection under Luno B (Vantor $5.3M, Feb 2026), evidencing demand for the capability at enterprise level.
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: OWT 3D data is integrated into ATAK, establishing 3D on the tactical device as expected capability.
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: Multiple companies (Reveal, Edgybees, Blackshark, Vantor) attempt parts of the pipeline; none has become a program of record at the tactical edge.
evidence.label: INFERENCE

candidate_gaps.why_startups_havent_solved: Edge compute constraints, drone heterogeneity, and the fact that better-funded competitors already occupy the space with prototypes; buyers are fragmented between PEO Soldier, PEO Aviation (UAS), and intelligence.
candidate_gaps.incumbent_response_risk: High; drone vendors bundle mapping (Skydio), and Vantor/Palantir cover enterprise.
candidate_gaps.technical_wedge_hypothesis: Drone-agnostic, MISB-KLV-driven georegistration and incremental 3D update streamed as 3D Tiles into ATAK/TAKX offline, with change alerts against OWT baselines.
candidate_gaps.mvp_sketch: Process commercial drone footage with KLV into georegistered overlays on ATAK-CIV within minutes on a laptop-class edge box; benchmark accuracy against RTK ground truth.
candidate_gaps.data_requirement: Commercial drone video with metadata; OWT-like baseline (Cesium ion or open 3D).
candidate_gaps.integration_requirement: ATAK plugin, 3D Tiles, STANAG 4609/MISB, drone ground stations.
candidate_gaps.entry_vehicle: AFWERX/Army SBIR, xTech, PEO Soldier soldier touchpoints, allied programs.
candidate_gaps.why_now: Edge GPUs and neural reconstruction (Gaussian splatting) make minute-scale 3D feasible on portable hardware.
candidate_gaps.killer_risk: Crowded field with a STRATFI-funded leader (Reveal) and drone OEM bundling; hard to differentiate as a two-person team.

segments.what_it_does: This layer lets forces from different nations, services and agencies exchange operational information (friendly/enemy tracks, orders, geometries, targeting data, intelligence products, logistics status, chat/voice/email) despite owning different C2 systems, different networks, different classification regimes and different national disclosure rules. Technically it spans (1) mission-partner networks and enclaves (CENTRIXS variants, Pegasus for Five Eyes, CFBLNet for lab federation, BICES for NATO/partner intelligence, SIPR-REL / Secret-Releasable, NATO's Federated Mission Networking), (2) cross-domain solutions and guards that move data between security domains under releasability rules, (3) standardized data exchange formats and profiles (STANAG 5525/JC3IEDM and MIP, NFFI, NVG, ADatP-3/USMTF, VMF, Link 16/22, TAK Cursor-on-Target, FMN spiral profiles), (4) federated identity/access (ICAM for partners), and (5) the human/procedural layer (foreign disclosure officers, liaison officers, joining/membership/exit instructions). The recurring failure mode is that information exists in system A on network X at classification Y and cannot legally or technically reach system B on network Z, so people swivel-chair it, re-key it or re-create it at a lower level.

sub_taxonomy.name: Mission-partner network and enclave provisioning (MPE/CIE, CENTRIXS, Pegasus, CFBLNet, SABRE, APAN)
sub_taxonomy.note: Network-centric today; DISA states a shift to a data-centric Coalition Information Environment by early 2027 (FNN, 2026-08-13). Dominated by services integrators (Trace Systems MPE-S, GDIT EMITS 2).

sub_taxonomy.name: Cross-domain transfer and releasability enforcement (CDS, guards, data tagging)
sub_taxonomy.note: Accredited hardware/software guards from Everfox/Forcepoint, Owl Cyber Defense, General Dynamics Mission Systems, Northrop Grumman (CHORD for partner networks). Startup entry requires NCDSMO-class accreditation; evidence of manual product movement persists (SAIC; MIPB 2025).

sub_taxonomy.name: Standards-based C2 data exchange and translation (MIP/JC3IEDM, NFFI, NVG, ADatP-3, VMF, Link 16/22, CoT, FMN spirals)
sub_taxonomy.note: Where allied C2 products compete on 'most interoperable': Systematic SitaWare, HAVELSAN, Terma, ThalesRaytheon AirC2. Annual NATO CWIX is the de facto proving ground; NATO is building INSPECT for continuous conformance testing.

sub_taxonomy.name: Tactical (brigade-and-below) multinational situational awareness bridges
sub_taxonomy.note: Unit-built workarounds (2nd Cavalry Regiment Mission Partner Kit at SBU level) and vendor bridges (Booz Allen Sit(x) connecting Lattice to TAK/partner systems). This is the most accessible sub-layer for a small team because standards are public and data can be unclassified.

sub_taxonomy.name: Coalition intelligence sharing and foreign disclosure workflow (BICES, REL NATO production, FDO review)
sub_taxonomy.note: Evidence shows intelligence produced at collateral Secret cannot be shared and must be regenerated on a lower enclave; BICES does not talk to mission-command systems (MIPB 2025). Institutional and accreditation-bound.

sub_taxonomy.name: Alliance-level C2 programs (NATO ACCS, Maven Smart System NATO, AFSC/airborne C2, LC2IS)
sub_taxonomy.note: Multi-decade NATO programs; ACCS integration 'remains incomplete' after >20 years (Atlantic Council, 2026-06-10). NATO bought Palantir MSS in six months (NCIA, 2025-03-25), showing a faster sole-source path for proven products.

users.what_they_do: Reviews products for release to specific partners; applies most-restrictive-marking rules (NOFORN dominates REL FVEY in combined objects). Human-in-the-loop bottleneck for anything crossing to a partner enclave.

users.what_they_do: Produces and consumes intelligence across US-only, MPE and BICES networks; in WFX 24-03 had to regenerate intelligence on the MPE lower enclave with REL NATO markings because the primary simulation output was collateral Secret (MIPB, 2025).

users.what_they_do: Carries a Mission Partner Kit or national C2 terminal into a partner HQ and manually bridges the picture; 2CR's MPK is explicitly 'enabled by trained liaison officers' (army.mil, 2025-03-25).

users.role: G6/J6 network engineer standing up an episodic mission network
users.what_they_do: Builds and accredits partner enclaves, federates identity, configures guards; DISA says historical practice produced many vertically integrated, domain-specific partner networks now being consolidated (FNN, 2026-08-13).

users.what_they_do: Passes geometries and targets between national C2IS and fire-control systems; in a 2025 coalition warfighter exercise some nations' C2IS 'couldn't seamlessly pass data to their national Fire Control Systems' (Small Wars Journal, 2025-11-19). WADS/PADS controllers integrated with RAAF 3CRU at Talisman Sabre 25 (USAF, 2025-07-28).

users.what_they_do: Plans reception, staging and sustainment across nations (Steadfast Dart 26: 10,000 troops, 13 nations, Germany as hub). Public evidence insufficient on specific coalition logistics data-exchange tooling failures.

current_architecture.description: Network-centric federation of separately accredited enclaves. U.S. side: CENTRIXS communities of interest per coalition, Pegasus for Five Eyes, CFBLNet for lab/experimentation federation, APAN (unclassified, cloud), SABRE/Secret-Releasable environments, Army SBU MPE, all historically under the Air Force MPE-IS program office and moved to DISA in 2025. NATO side: Federated Mission Networking (spiral specifications) with national systems conformance-tested at CWIX; BICES for intelligence; ACCS for air C2; NCIA-run core services; Maven Smart System NATO for AI-enabled fusion at ACO. Data crosses domains through accredited cross-domain solutions or by humans. DISA's stated direction is a data-centric Coalition Information Environment with zero-trust and attribute-based access, targeted for early 2027 (FNN, 2026-08-13). FACT for the components; INFERENCE for the end-to-end picture, which is not published in one place.

current_architecture.security_domain: Spans Unclassified/SBU (APAN, Army SBU MPE, MPK), Secret-Releasable (CENTRIXS, SABRE, SIPR-REL), NATO Secret (MPE accredited to process NATO Secret intelligence per MIPB 2025), and national Secret (SIPRNet, national systems) with CDS bridges. current_architecture.connectivity_dependency: Enterprise MPE/CENTRIXS services are cloud/data-center hosted with reach-back over SATCOM or terrestrial links; tactical bridges (MPK) explicitly rely on government-approved commercial cloud, so they degrade without connectivity. FMN federations depend on core services at national/NATO nodes.
current_architecture.what_breaks_when_disconnected: Cloud-hosted partner COPs and chat stop; partner identity federation cannot authenticate; cross-domain transfers queue or revert to sneakernet/voice; units fall back to liaison officers and voice. Public evidence on DDIL-specific coalition failures beyond general statements is insufficient.

technical_difficulty.summary: The hard part is not parsing formats; most exchange standards (MIP/JC3IEDM, NFFI, NVG, ADatP-3, CoT) are documented and libraries exist. The difficulty is (a) enforcing releasability semantics on structured, aggregated data objects so that they can cross an accredited guard automatically; (b) federating identity and attributes across nations; (c) doing both in DDIL conditions at brigade and below; and (d) passing accreditation for every enclave and guard involved. Link 16 J-series and national fire-control interfaces are export-controlled and closed.
required_expertise: NATO/FMN standards and profiles
cross-domain solution design and NCDSMO 'Raise the Bar' accreditation
classification and releasability marking (ISM/NTK, REL/NOFORN aggregation rules)
federated identity (SAML/OIDC, ABAC, PKI across nations)
tactical data links and gateways (Link 16/22, VMF)
TAK ecosystem and CoT
zero-trust architecture in disconnected environments
RMF/ATO and NATO security accreditation
technical_difficulty.hardest_problem: Automating foreign-disclosure decisions on combined/aggregated data (where the most restrictive marking dominates) in a way accrediting authorities and FDOs will accept; the policy, not the code, is the constraint.
technical_difficulty.commodity_parts: Message parsers/serializers for public STANAGs, TAK servers and plugins, map/COP front ends, chat/email/web core services, cloud hosting at IL5/IL6, PKI.

capital_intensity.first_production_deployment_usd: $3M-$15M (software bridge at SBU/Secret-Releasable); $10M-$30M+ if an accredited cross-domain component is required
capital_intensity.assumptions: PoC: two engineers for 6-9 months building a standards bridge (CoT/NFFI/NVG/MIP) with synthetic data. Demo: a government sponsor for CWIX or Bold Quest participation (nations pay their own way), travel, a small integration with one allied C2 product, initial security documentation. Production: ATO/RMF or NATO accreditation, IL5/IL6 hosting, cleared staff, sustainment; CDS accreditation historically takes years and is why incumbents dominate. Ranges are INFERENCE from comparable software-only defense deployments, not from disclosed program costs.

regulatory_access.prototype_with_commercial_unclassified_d: partly - open standards (JC3IEDM/MIP, NFFI, NVG, CoT/TAK, ADatP-3 elements) and synthetic scenarios allow an unclassified prototype; Link 16 J-series, national fire-control interfaces and real releasability policy cannot be prototyped without government access.
regulatory_access.government_data_required: For anything beyond a demo: exercise data, real marking policy, partner enclave access; MPE/CENTRIXS work is on classified networks.
regulatory_access.itar_ear: Link 16/MIL-STD-6016 and many C2 integrations are ITAR-controlled; exporting a bridge to allied customers needs licensing; AUKUS ITAR exemptions cover only UK/Australia. Needs specialist review.
regulatory_access.cui_likely: Yes - FMN joining instructions, exercise architectures and most program documents are at least CUI or NATO Restricted.
regulatory_access.classified_integration_eventually: Yes - the highest-value flows are Secret-Releasable and NATO Secret; a durable product must reach those enclaves.
regulatory_access.cleared_personnel_at_mvp: Not for an unclassified/SBU tactical bridge MVP; required for any Secret-Releasable or CDS integration.
regulatory_access.non_us_person_founder_note: A non-U.S.-person founder (Indonesian national, not a NATO or Five Eyes national) cannot hold a U.S. clearance and could create FOCI and export-control issues for U.S. classified or ITAR-controlled work; a German founder could plausibly participate in NATO/EU work through a European entity (NATO DIANA is open to allied-nation firms) but NATO-classified work is also nationality-gated. The unclassified/SBU tactical bridge sub-segment is the only path that does not immediately collide with these constraints. All of this requires specialist legal review; nothing here is a legal judgment.

why_not_solved.explanation: The binding constraint is national disclosure policy and human FDO review, not software; data produced on national Secret systems without releasability markings cannot legally flow, so it gets regenerated or re-keyed (MIPB 2025; GAO-25-106454).
Every enclave and guard needs its own accreditation; cross-domain accreditation is slow and dominated by a handful of vendors, so new automated paths take years to authorize.

Each coalition, COCOM and service built its own partner network out of necessity (DISA, 2026); NATO capability development has 'delays measured in years' (Atlantic Council, 2025-03-13); nations buy national C2 independently.

No single buyer owns coalition interoperability end to end: DISA owns MPE, Joint Staff owns Bold Quest, NATO ACT owns FMN/CWIX, NCIA buys NATO systems, nations buy national systems, and FDOs own policy.
Dozens of national C2 systems, tactical links, simulation federations and message standards; CWIX ran >25,000 tests across ~600 capabilities in 2025 just to find and fix mismatches.
ACCS (ThalesRaytheon), SitaWare, Lattice and Foundry each aim to be the 'spine'; partner bridges are offered by incumbents (Booz Allen Sit(x) on Menace) which narrows the whitespace.

Data-centric security (attribute-based access, object-level tagging, zero trust) is only now being adopted by DISA (target 2027) and NATO's digital backbone, which is what makes automated releasability plausible at all.
There is no civilian analogue for multinational classified releasability; total addressable spend is program-office services money, which favors integrators over product startups.

For unclassified/SBU tactical SA, government-owned TAK plus commercial cloud (MPK) and vendor bridges (Sit(x)) already work; the residual problem at that level is fielding and training, not invention.

attractiveness.bull: Real, repeatedly documented pain across GAO, Army professional journals, DISA leadership and NATO analysis; DISA's data-centric CIE pivot (2027) and NGC2's data-layer approach create a window where object-level releasability tagging and standards-native bridges become procurable; NATO DIANA and allied sovereign clouds give a European founder a lawful entry path; exercise cadence (CWIX, Bold Quest, PCC, Talisman Sabre) provides visible proving grounds; open standards allow an unclassified MVP.
attractiveness.bear: The binding constraints are policy, accreditation and nationality-gated access, none of which a student-founded startup can change; the paying customers are program offices that buy services from Trace, GDIT, SAIC and Booz Allen; incumbents (Anduril, Palantir, Systematic, Booz Allen) already ship partner bridges; CDS is an accredited oligopoly; a non-NATO-national co-founder blocks U.S. classified and much NATO work; unit-level demand (MPK) has no budget line; SBIR-funded translation tools have not transitioned in ~20 years.
attractiveness.verdict: Medium-low for the segment overall; medium only for a narrow, unclassified/SBU tactical multinational SA bridge or for standards-conformance tooling sold to allied vendors and nations, with a required plan for eventual Secret-Releasable integration through a partner with clearances.

market_stage.rationale: The enterprise network layer is mature and in sustainment (large services IDIQs), while the data-centric layer (CIE, NGC2 data mesh, NATO digital backbone) is mid-transition with prototypes being tested in 2026 and a 2027 target. Tactical multinational bridges remain at unit-prototype stage. This mix is best described as Transitioning rather than Emerging or Mature.

proto_purgatory.notes: Two patterns: (1) data-translation SBIRs (IET Quik-Speak, Securboration C2OSIF, Cougaar BattleFish, Machina Cognita NOVA, RTI) spanning many years with no production transition found; (2) exercise demonstrations (ACIS 2018, MPK 2024-2025, Project Overmatch participation by small vendors with 'no definitive contract awards' per an OPT 10-K) that repeat without programs of record. Counter-evidence: MPE-S, EMITS 2, NGC2 and Maven NATO show that production money flows to integrators and platform incumbents, not to point translation tools.
proto_purgatory.opportunity_or_warning: Warning for translation-tool and 'universal adapter' startups; opportunity only where a product rides an existing production vehicle (NGC2 data layer, DISA CIE task orders, allied C2 vendor partnerships) or a NATO sole-source style buy after proven exercise performance.

candidate_gaps.title: Born-releasable structured data: object-level releasability tagging and automated disclosure decision support for C2/intel objects
candidate_gaps.problem_one_sentence: Information created on national-Secret systems lacks machine-enforceable releasability, so it cannot cross to partner enclaves without humans regenerating or re-keying it.
candidate_gaps.user: Multinational intelligence cell analysts, foreign disclosure officers, CJTF battle managers
candidate_gaps.current_workflow: 1) Product or track is created on SIPR/national system at collateral Secret. 2) Analyst or FDO reviews for release. 3) Product is re-created or sanitized on the MPE/REL enclave (WFX 24-03: switched simulation feed to IEWTPT on the lower enclave). 4) Transfer through an accredited CDS or manual re-entry. 5) Partner ingests via its national system if formats align.
candidate_gaps.current_solution: Human FDO review; CDS with static filters; policy of producing at the lowest level; DISA's planned data-centric CIE with zero trust (2027).
candidate_gaps.failure_point: Markings are document-level and non-aggregating (NOFORN dominates), so structured/aggregated data cannot be auto-released; every new automated path needs accreditation.

segments.what_it_does: This layer is the substrate that lets any C4ISR application (C2, COP, fusion, PED, AI models) actually reach a military network and stay there. It comprises (1) accredited compute/storage environments at each Impact Level (IL2/IL4/IL5 unclassified-to-CUI, IL6 Secret, and TS/SCI regions) delivered through enterprise cloud vehicles such as JWCC, Army cArmy, and Air Force Cloud One, plus on-prem and tactical-edge compute; (2) DevSecOps platforms and 'software factories' (Platform One's Iron Bank hardened images, Big Bang Kubernetes baseline, Party Bus CI/CD; Kessel Run; Navy Black Pearl/The Forge) that build, scan, sign and deploy containers; (3) the authorization regime (RMF-based ATO, continuous ATO, FedRAMP/DISA provisional authorizations, and the 2025 SWFT and CSRMC reform initiatives) that decides whether software may run on a given network; (4) packaging and delivery tooling for air-gapped, denied/degraded (DDIL) and cross-domain (low-to-high) promotion (Zarf, UDS, Big Bang bundles, CDS-mediated transfers); and (5) marketplaces/app-store-like intake channels (Game Warden, Palantir FedStart, Tradewinds Solutions Marketplace, JWCC/AWS Marketplace listings) that let vendors reach DoD buyers with pre-accredited hosting. Functionally, it is the 'ship-and-stay-authorized' layer between code and the warfighter.

Dominated by hyperscalers and integrators; large obligated dollars; JWCC Next is being restructured into a 'Unified Cloud Marketplace' (UCM) with a hyperscaler 'Core' solicitation (Sept 2026) and a second solicitation for non-hyperscaler vendors.

sub_taxonomy.name: DevSecOps platforms / software factories (Platform One, Kessel Run, Black Pearl, Army Software Factory, Space Force factories)
sub_taxonomy.note: Government-owned platforms with contractor support; DoD CIO's State of DevSecOps (Mar 2025) counts 50+ software factories delivering to production. Evidence of consolidation pressure and pivots (Kessel Run 2025) but no single enterprise mandate found.

sub_taxonomy.name: Authorization regime and its automation (RMF/ATO, cATO, FedRAMP reciprocity, SWFT, CSRMC, eMASS/Xacta/GRC, SBOM/scanning)
sub_taxonomy.note: Policy in active flux: cATO memo (Feb 2022) -> SWFT memo (Apr 2025) -> CSRMC tenets (Sept 2025) -> FedRAMP 20x rules (mandatory Jan 2027). This is the sub-layer with the most documented pain and the least settled architecture.

sub_taxonomy.name: Accredited hosting / marketplace intermediaries (Game Warden, Palantir FedStart/PFCS Forward, Tradewinds, AWS Marketplace for JWCC)
sub_taxonomy.note: Commercial 'ATO-as-a-service' hosts that inherit controls so ISVs can deploy in weeks rather than a year; increasingly extending to IL6 and to on-prem/edge (PFCS Forward Feb 2026).

sub_taxonomy.name: Air-gapped / DDIL / cross-domain delivery and day-2 operations (Zarf, UDS, Big Bang at edge, OpenShift/Rancher at edge, CDS-mediated promotion)
sub_taxonomy.note: The least mature sub-layer: open-source tooling exists (Zarf 2.0k stars, actively released Sept 2026) but fleet-scale update, certificate/registry lifecycle and re-accreditation across many disconnected clusters remain largely manual per available evidence (INFERENCE).

sub_taxonomy.name: AI/model deployment and accreditation (GenAI.mil, CDAO, model registries, edge model updates)
sub_taxonomy.note: GenAI.mil delivers frontier models at IL5 in cloud; a formal, repeatable 'model ATO' pathway for edge-deployed models is not documented publicly (Public evidence insufficient).

technical_difficulty.summary: The individual technologies are commodity (Kubernetes, OCI, GitOps, SBOM, scanning, signing). Difficulty is in (a) making the whole chain provably compliant and reproducible under STIG/FIPS constraints, (b) operating it across air gaps and DDIL links with no external control plane, and (c) generating authorization evidence that a human AO will accept and that another AO will reciprocally accept. The hard engineering is distributed-systems reliability under disconnection plus evidence provenance, not novel algorithms.
required_expertise: Kubernetes internals and distribution hardening (RKE2/K3s/OpenShift), GitOps
Supply-chain security: SBOM, signing, provenance, vulnerability triage/VEX
RMF/NIST 800-53, STIG/SRG, FedRAMP, DISA CC SRG impact levels, cATO evidence design
Air-gap packaging and registry/PKI lifecycle (Zarf-class tooling)
Cross-domain solution constraints and classified network operations
Site reliability engineering for many small edge clusters
Federal contracting mechanics (OTAs/CSOs, SBIR, marketplace listings)
technical_difficulty.hardest_problem: Fleet-scale, auditable day-2 operations for disconnected clusters: pushing image, model and certificate updates to dozens of air-gapped/DDIL nodes, proving what ran where and when, and keeping the authorization boundary valid without persistent reachback (INFERENCE from tooling gaps; no primary DoD document quantifying this was retrievable in-session).
technical_difficulty.commodity_parts: Container build/scan/sign pipelines (Syft/Grype/Anchore, cosign), Big Bang/UDS Core baselines, OpenShift/Rancher, hyperscaler IL5/IL6 regions, GRC systems (eMASS/Xacta), and SBOM generation are all available off the shelf or open source.

capital_intensity.assumptions: PoC can run entirely on open-source (Big Bang mirror, UDS Core, Zarf, MITRE SAF) with commercial cloud and no government data. A credible demo needs an IL4/IL5 environment (via Game Warden/FedStart hosting fees or a government software factory sponsor), a signed CRADA/SBIR Phase I-II, and at least one US-person engineer able to handle CUI. First production implies an authorization (own package or inherited), 24/7 support, incident response, likely FedRAMP Moderate/High or IL5 via a host, and possibly cleared staff for IL6; hosting intermediaries charge recurring six-figure-per-year fees (INFERENCE; pricing not public). Ranges are estimates, not quotes.

regulatory_access.prototype_with_commercial_unclassified_d: yes - the entire stack (Big Bang GitHub mirror, UDS Core, Zarf, OSCAL/SAF, public STIGs) can be prototyped with synthetic workloads and no government data; Iron Bank/repo1 access may require DoD identity for some content.
regulatory_access.government_data_required: Not for the platform itself; required to demonstrate a real ATO package or a real edge deployment (CUI system security plans, network diagrams).
regulatory_access.itar_ear: Pure DevSecOps/deployment tooling is generally EAR (encryption items, e.g., 5D002/ENC) rather than ITAR, but any bundled mission software, CDS components or classified-network artifacts can be ITAR/USML-controlled; a specialist export-control review is required before any non-US person touches deployment artifacts (do not treat this as a legal determination).
regulatory_access.cui_likely: Yes: ATO packages, SSPs, POA&Ms, network diagrams and most pilot engagements are CUI; DFARS 7012/CMMC will apply to the company handling them.
regulatory_access.classified_integration_eventually: Yes for IL6/Secret hosting, cross-domain promotion, and most C4ISR production deployments; facility clearance (FCL) and cleared staff become necessary, which triggers FOCI mitigation if foreign ownership/control exists.
regulatory_access.cleared_personnel_at_mvp: No for an unclassified MVP; yes within 12-24 months for any classified/edge production path.
regulatory_access.non_us_person_founder_note: An Indonesian (non-US-person) co-founder cannot be assumed to access CUI-marked ATO artifacts, export-controlled deployment bundles, or classified environments; a German founder pending US permanent residency is also a non-US person until residency is granted. Company structure (US entity, board control, FOCI mitigation such as SSA/proxy if an FCL is needed), data segregation, and role design (business/product roles kept away from controlled technical data) need specialist legal review (immigration, export control, NISPOM/FOCI). This layer is more exposed than most because its product literally is the deployment path into DoD networks.

unsolved_pain.pain: ATO is the longest step in delivering software; process takes months or years and costs are borne by taxpayers per program.

why_not_solved.explanation: Authorization is a human risk-acceptance decision distributed across hundreds of AOs with personal accountability; tools can generate evidence but cannot compel acceptance or reciprocity. Every prior fix (cATO 2022, SWFT 2025, CSRMC 2025) has been a policy change, and policy is still moving, so vendors build to a target that shifts yearly.

Each service runs its own cloud (cArmy, Cloud One, Navy JWCC orders), its own factories (50+), and its own AO chain; a startup must win the same argument repeatedly, which favors incumbents with capture teams.

Platform One (government-owned), Palantir (FedStart/Apollo/PFCS Forward) and hyperscalers already occupy the accredited-hosting and deployment control points; Palantir's Feb 2026 move to IL5/IL6 on-prem/edge and Defense Unicorns' $136M raise show the 'obvious' gaps are being filled by well-capitalized players.
Edge deployment is entangled with program-specific hardware, tactical networks, PKI and CDS approvals; a generic tool without a program sponsor cannot be exercised on real equipment.

Government-owned platforms are free to programs and open source (Big Bang, Zarf, UDS Core, SAF) commoditizes tooling; monetization has therefore concentrated in services (integrators) or in accredited hosting (rent on the ATO), leaving thin room for pure-software startups.
The most painful problems (low-to-high promotion, IL6/TS updates) can only be observed and fixed by cleared, US-person teams inside classified facilities, which excludes most early-stage teams.

For unclassified/IL5 SaaS delivery the problem is substantially solved commercially: Game Warden and FedStart provide inherited controls and marketplace access; JWCC provides regions at every level. The residual gaps are edge/DDIL day-2 operations, cross-domain promotion, evidence automation under a still-changing regime, and model accreditation.

attractiveness.bull: Policy tailwinds are real and dated: SWFT (Apr 2025), CSRMC (Sept 2025), FedRAMP 20x (2026-27) and the JWCC UCM marketplace (2027) all push toward automated, evidence-based, marketplace-style software intake, and DoD is publicly soliciting AI for ATO automation. Open-source building blocks let a two-person team prototype at near-zero cost, and hosting intermediaries let an unclassified MVP reach IL5 without owning an ATO. Defense Unicorns' $136M/$1B+ round proves investors will fund deployment-layer companies with real DoD traction.
attractiveness.bear: The layer is crowded at every profitable control point (hyperscalers, Palantir, Second Front, Defense Unicorns, integrators, GRC vendors) and the customer-owned alternative (Platform One) is free. The regulatory target moves every 12 months, the true buyer (the AO) is not a purchaser, and the hardest residual problems (edge day-2 ops, cross-domain, model accreditation) require US-person, often cleared, hands-on access that this founding team (one non-US person, one pending PR) does not have. Absence of a single dominant edge-ops vendor is not proof of demand.
attractiveness.verdict: Medium-low for this team as a primary bet: attractive as an enabling capability to master (every C4ISR startup must pass through this layer) and as a narrow wedge (evidence automation or edge day-2 ops delivered through an existing host such as Game Warden/FedStart or a P1 partner), but unattractive as a standalone 'ATO platform' or 'tactical cloud' company given incumbency, policy flux and access constraints.

candidate_gaps.title: Auditable day-2 operations for fleets of disconnected/DDIL edge clusters
candidate_gaps.problem_one_sentence: Once C2/ISR software is fielded on tactical edge nodes, pushing image, model, certificate and policy updates across many air-gapped or intermittently connected clusters, and proving what ran where for the authorization boundary, is still largely manual and unsupported by enterprise tooling that assumes reachback.
candidate_gaps.user: Signal/G6 platform teams at brigade to corps; software factory SREs supporting fielded units; program offices owning the edge ATO boundary
candidate_gaps.current_workflow: 1) Build and scan in a connected factory (P1/UDS). 2) Bundle into an OCI package (Zarf/UDS bundle). 3) Move by approved media or CDS to the target enclave. 4) Manually load into a local registry, hand-run upgrades per node, rotate certs by hand. 5) Manually record what was deployed for the ISSM. 6) Repeat per site with no fleet view.
candidate_gaps.current_solution: Zarf/UDS (Defense Unicorns), Big Bang bundles, OpenShift/Rancher with vendor edge managers (Spectro Cloud Palette), Palantir Apollo/PFCS Forward for Palantir-hosted apps; integrator labor for everything else.
candidate_gaps.failure_point: Registries, control planes, policy servers and CAs become single points of failure when disconnected; no vendor-neutral fleet update/attestation layer spans JWCC-hosted and edge nodes; continuous-monitoring evidence stops when links drop, so cATO status decays (INFERENCE).

segments.segment_name: Identity / Security / Zero Trust / Cross-Domain Infrastructure
segments.what_it_does: This layer decides WHO (person or non-person entity) may touch WHICH data or service, under WHAT policy, and HOW data may cross security or national boundaries. It spans: (1) identity, credential and access management (DoD PKI/CAC, enterprise directories such as DISA's Global Federated User Directory, Army Enterprise ICAM, MFA, non-person-entity certificates); (2) zero-trust access and enforcement (policy decision/enforcement points, ZTNA/SASE, micro-segmentation; DoD's 7 pillars, 45 capabilities and 152 activities of which 91 are 'target level' due by FY27); (3) authorization and policy engines (RBAC to ABAC using user, device and data attributes); (4) data-centric security and tagging (classification/releasability labels, IC-TDF -> OpenTDF/ZTDF, ACP-240 coalition labels, key-access services) so protection travels with the object; (5) cross-domain solutions (NSA/NCDSMO-baselined transfer and access guards, one-way transfer devices, tactical CDS) that move data between classification levels or coalition enclaves; and (6) coalition identity federation and foreign-disclosure/releasability enforcement in Mission Partner Environments. In the C4ISR chain it is cross-cutting: it gates every TRANSPORT, PROCESS, FUSE and DISSEMINATE_TASK hop, and it is the reason 'the data exists but cannot be shared' is the most common C4ISR failure mode documented in exercises.

sub_taxonomy.name: Enterprise ICAM (PKI/CAC/PIV, derived credentials, MFA, directories, NPE identity, federation)
sub_taxonomy.note: DoD PKI + DISA GFUD/DEAS + service ICAM programs (Army EICAM, Navy Flank Speed/Entra). Largely commoditized by Microsoft/hyperscaler identity stacks; still manual for coalition/guest identities. Restructured from the assignment's 'credentialing' bullet to include NPE (machine) identity because ZT strategy and NGC2 make device/sensor identity the growth edge.

sub_taxonomy.name: Zero-trust access/network enforcement (ZTNA, SASE, segmentation, policy enforcement points)
sub_taxonomy.note: Thunderdome (DISA/Fourth Estate), Flank Speed (Navy), service SD-WAN/SASE deployments; production stage; dominated by Booz Allen, Microsoft, Zscaler-class vendors. Not startup whitespace.

sub_taxonomy.name: Authorization / policy engines (PDP, ABAC, dynamic and risk-based access)
sub_taxonomy.note: The DoD ZT 'Data' and 'User' pillars require ABAC; DAU webinars from 2023 (ABAC) to 2026 (ICAM powers ZT) show components still migrating from RBAC to ABAC. Accessible to software startups (OPA/Cedar/OpenTDF-style engines) but integration-heavy.

sub_taxonomy.name: Data-centric security and tagging/labeling (TDF/ZTDF/OpenTDF, IC-TDF, ACP-240, markings, key access services)
sub_taxonomy.note: Recurring DoD CIO ZT PfMO topic (data tagging webinars Apr 2024, Sep 2025). Open standards exist (OpenTDF spec, ZTDF for Five Eyes/NATO) but tagging of live C2 data at source is nascent. Most accessible sub-problem for an unclassified prototype.

sub_taxonomy.name: Cross-domain solutions (transfer/access guards, one-way transfer, tactical/low-SWaP CDS, CDS-as-a-service)
sub_taxonomy.note: Governed by DoDI 8540.01, CNSSI 1253 CDS overlay and NSA/NCDSMO 'Raise the Bar'; only NCDSMO-listed products may be used (NIST AC-4(20)). Incumbent oligopoly (Everfox, Owl, GDMS, Northrop, Lockheed Radiant Mercury); immediately classified and export-controlled.

sub_taxonomy.name: Coalition identity federation and releasability enforcement (MPE ICAM, foreign disclosure workflow, NOFORN/REL handling)
sub_taxonomy.note: Joint Staff J6 and DISA are still demonstrating ZT + data-centric security for partners beyond FVEY (FY27 justification book); MPE remains 'network-centric' until ~2027 per DISA. Policy-bound and classified at the edges but with unclassified workflow/tooling openings.

sub_taxonomy.name: Tactical / DDIL zero trust (edge PDP, offline credential validation, data-in-use protection)
sub_taxonomy.note: Added because DEVCOM C5ISR's 2025 'Tactical Data in Use Security' RFI explicitly asks for ZT Data-pillar capabilities that work in DDIL; enterprise ZT designs assume connectivity to identity providers and key servers.

sub_taxonomy.name: ZT assessment, evidence and continuous-authorization tooling (ZT Overlays, 91 target activities, cATO evidence)
sub_taxonomy.note: Program offices must prove target-level ZT by 30 Sep 2027; DoD CIO cATO guide and NSA ZIGs (Jan 2026) create a compliance-evidence workload. Accessible but crowded with integrators and GRC vendors.

current_architecture.description: Enterprise identity is anchored on DoD PKI (CAC/PIV, NPE certificates) and enterprise directories (DISA GFUD/DEAS; service Active Directory/Entra tenants such as Navy Flank Speed). Zero-trust enforcement is delivered as SASE/ZTNA overlays (Thunderdome for DISA and the Fourth Estate; hyperscaler-native conditional access for Flank Speed) with policy decision points that are still largely role-based and network-centric outside the leading programs. Data-centric security exists as standards (IC-TDF, OpenTDF, ZTDF, ACP-240) and pilots rather than as enterprise-wide tagging at source. Movement across classification levels and to coalition partners runs through a small set of NCDSMO-baselined cross-domain solutions (enterprise CDES at DISA; program-specific guards such as BICES TNE; tactical CDS on aircraft, vehicles and expeditionary nodes), with manual review, removable media and liaison officers as the fallback. Coalition access uses separate enclaves (CENTRIXS, BICES, MPE/Coalition Information Environment) rather than federated identity with attribute-based release.

current_architecture.security_domain: Spans unclassified (NIPR/IL2-IL5), Secret (SIPR/IL6), TS/SCI and coalition Secret-REL enclaves; the segment's core products (CDS, CSfC) are by definition multi-domain and immediately classified/export-controlled, while tagging, policy and observability tooling can be built unclassified.
current_architecture.connectivity_dependency: Enterprise ZT and ICAM assume reachability of identity providers, policy decision points, certificate revocation services and key access servers; Flank Speed and Thunderdome are cloud/enterprise-hosted. Tactical CDS are local hardware, but their filter updates and audit offload assume periodic connectivity.
current_architecture.what_breaks_when_disconnected: Token/certificate validation, attribute retrieval and key release fail or fall back to cached trust; users lose access to cloud identity services; data tagged for ABAC cannot be decrypted without key servers; cross-domain transfers revert to manual/removable-media processes. DEVCOM C5ISR's 2025 RFI for 'Tactical Data in Use Security' in DDIL is direct government acknowledgement of this gap.

technical_difficulty.summary: Bimodal. The enterprise half (SSO, ZTNA, conditional access, directories) is commodity engineering assembled from hyperscaler and vendor components; the differentiator is integration, accreditation and scale, not novel technology. The hard half is (a) high-assurance cross-domain filtering that must satisfy Raise the Bar (redundant, independent, always-invoked, non-bypassable filter pipelines, normalized-format regeneration) and pass NSA lab assessment; (b) consistent attribute semantics across federated authorities (DoD, services, coalition) so that ABAC decisions are the same everywhere; (c) automated releasability decisions where markings do not aggregate by dominance (any NOFORN element blocks foreign release); and (d) making ZT work when the identity provider, PDP and key server are unreachable (DDIL).
required_expertise: PKI and X.509/OIDC/SAML federation internals
Policy engines and ABAC modeling (OPA/Rego, Cedar, XACML lineage)
Cryptography and key management (TDF/ZTDF key access services, HSMs, CNSA 2.0)
High-assurance systems engineering, formal methods and separation kernels for CDS
Content filtering, data format descriptions (DFDL), USMTF/CoT/Link-16 message schemas
Classification and foreign disclosure policy (DoDM 5200.01, CAPCO, ACP-240, NATO STANAG labels)
DevSecOps and cATO evidence automation (NIST 800-53 rev5, ZT Overlays)
Tactical networking and offline-first distributed systems
technical_difficulty.hardest_problem: Getting an automated, policy-consistent releasability and access decision on machine-generated tactical data (tracks, reports, video) across US-only, coalition and partner enclaves without a human in the loop, while satisfying NCDSMO assurance requirements and surviving disconnection. Today this is solved by people, liaison officers and regeneration workarounds.
technical_difficulty.commodity_parts: Identity providers, MFA, ZTNA/SASE, SIEM, OPA/Cedar policy engines, OpenTDF SDKs and key access server, Kubernetes with policy-as-code, FedRAMP/IL5 hosting via Game Warden or hyperscalers.

capital_intensity.first_production_deployment_usd: $3M-$15M for software tooling (tagging/policy/observability); $10M-$40M and 3-5 years if the product itself must become an NCDSMO-baselined CDS
capital_intensity.assumptions: PoC assumes two founders building on OpenTDF/OPA with synthetic or unclassified C2 data (CoT, USMTF samples). Credible demo assumes an SBIR Phase I/II or xTech award, IL4/IL5 hosting through an accredited intermediary, DoD PKI test credentials, and participation in an Army/Joint experiment (T-REX, Project Convergence, Bold Quest) with a government sponsor such as DEVCOM C5ISR. First production assumes ATO/cATO on a service enclave, FedRAMP High or IL5 reciprocity, 3-6 cleared or clearable staff, and 18-36 months. CDS route assumes NSA lab-based security assessment, hardware/software development to RTB, and export-control compliance; incumbents' sole-source IDIQs show the buyer will not run new competitions frequently.

regulatory_access.prototype_with_commercial_unclassified_d: yes for data tagging, policy engines, ZT observability and ICAM integration tooling (OpenTDF, synthetic CoT/USMTF); no for cross-domain solutions and CSfC-type products, which have no meaningful unclassified market and require NSA processes
regulatory_access.government_data_required: Not for a first prototype; needed for credibility: DoD PKI test certificates, sample marked data and access to a service enclave, typically via SBIR/OTA sponsor or an exercise.
regulatory_access.itar_ear: CDS and high-assurance guards are treated as export-controlled (NSA RTB explicitly covers 'all cross domain solutions being sold for export'); encryption products fall under EAR Cat. 5 Part 2 and may be USML-controlled when designed for military use; tagging/policy software built on open standards can be EAR99 or 5D002 depending on crypto. Needs export-control counsel before any foreign-national access to controlled technical data.
regulatory_access.cui_likely: yes; any real customer data (attributes, network topology, marking rules) will be CUI at minimum and drive CMMC Level 2 obligations
regulatory_access.classified_integration_eventually: yes for anything touching SIPR, coalition Secret-REL or CDS; the segment's value concentrates at classification boundaries
regulatory_access.cleared_personnel_at_mvp: no for unclassified tooling MVP; yes (Secret at minimum, often TS/SCI) for CDS, CSfC integration, coalition MPE work and most production deployments
regulatory_access.non_us_person_founder_note: An Indonesian citizen without U.S. person status cannot hold a U.S. security clearance and generally may not access ITAR-controlled technical data or export-controlled encryption source without licenses; a company with a foreign owner/officer may raise FOCI questions in facility clearance and some SBIR eligibility contexts. A German founder who becomes a lawful permanent resident is a 'U.S. person' for ITAR/EAR deemed-export purposes but still cannot hold a clearance until naturalized. Practical implication: structure the company so the non-U.S.-person founder owns product/business functions on unclassified, non-export-controlled work, keep controlled technical data segregated, and obtain specialist immigration, export-control and FOCI legal review before pursuing CDS, CSfC or classified integration. This is a description of constraints, not legal advice.

why_not_solved.explanation: Any product that moves data across classification boundaries must pass NSA/NCDSMO lab-based assessment against Raise the Bar and be listed before use (NIST AC-4(20)); CSfC components need NIAP validation and a trusted integrator. This takes years and specialized staff, which is why the CDS market is an oligopoly.
The highest-value use cases (SIPR, coalition Secret-REL, TS/SCI) require cleared people, facilities and government-furnished environments; startups cannot iterate with real data.
Everfox, Owl, GDMS, Northrop and Lockheed hold program-embedded CDS and sole-source IDIQs; Booz Allen and Microsoft hold the ZT reference deployments. The buyer rarely re-competes.

ABAC only works if attributes mean the same thing across DoD PKI, service directories, cloud tenants and coalition authorities; every service runs its own ICAM and ZT program, so semantics and APIs diverge.

DoD CIO sets policy but does not buy; DISA, each service CIO, PEOs and combatant commands each own pieces; coalition sharing additionally depends on national policies (NATO ACCS integration took over two decades).

OpenTDF (2021-2024), ZTDF, NSA ZIGs (Jan 2026), cATO guidance and policy-as-code engines make source-tagging and continuous evidence practical only now; Flank Speed's target-level certification (Oct 2024) is the first proof that the enterprise half is achievable.

CDS procurement lines are small (CDES roughly $1-2M/yr) and unit volumes low; the money is in integration services and platform programs, not in software licenses, which discourages venture-backed entrants.
Enterprise ZTNA/identity for connected users is largely solved by Thunderdome and Flank Speed using commercial stacks; that sub-layer is not startup whitespace.

Automated, dominance-aware releasability on machine-generated tactical data and ZT enforcement in DDIL remain open; demonstrations recur annually (Bold Quest, CWIX, JS J6 assessments) without a program of record.

attractiveness.bull: The FY27 target-level deadline, NSA's Jan 2026 implementation guidelines, NGC2's scale-up and Joint Staff's coalition data-centric-security demos create a 2026-2028 window where every program office needs data tagging, ABAC policy and ZT evidence tooling. Open standards (OpenTDF/ZTDF, ACP-240) let a two-person team build an unclassified prototype in weeks; DEVCOM C5ISR has issued a named RFI for tactical data-in-use security; accredited hosting (Game Warden, JWCC marketplace) shortens ATO; and the pain is documented in GAO, Army journals and DAU webinars rather than only vendor marketing.
attractiveness.bear: The layer's value concentrates exactly where a student startup cannot go: classified enclaves, NSA-assessed CDS, coalition policy. Enterprise ZT and ICAM are already delivered by Booz Allen, Microsoft and large integrators with sole-source follow-ons; ZT compliance tooling is crowded; data tagging demand is real but the buyer has been 'demonstrating' it since 2022 without a program of record; one non-U.S.-person founder blocks clearances and complicates export control and FOCI; and revenue in CDS is low-volume and services-heavy.
attractiveness.verdict: Selectively attractive: pursue only the unclassified, standards-based sub-problems (interoperable tagging/labeling automation for C2 data, offline-capable policy/key enforcement for DDIL, ZT evidence automation) as a wedge, with an explicit plan to partner with an accredited CDS or ZT integrator rather than becoming one. Avoid building a CDS, CSfC product or enterprise ICAM competitor.

market_stage.rationale: Enterprise ZT/ICAM has moved through prototype -> production -> repeat within four years and is Mature; cross-domain hardware/guards are Mature-to-Stagnant (sole-source follow-ons, small budgets); data-centric security, coalition ZT and tactical/DDIL ZT are in the RFI/demonstration phase with no production program of record, hence Transitioning overall.

proto_purgatory.notes: Coalition data-centric security and interoperable tagging have been 'demonstrated and assessed' annually (Bold Quest, CWIX, Joint Staff J6 CJADC2 assessments, DAU webinars since Dec 2022) without a fielded standard or program of record; MPE consolidation is still 'starting small' in 2026 and expected to stay network-centric until ~2027. By contrast, enterprise ZT (Thunderdome, Flank Speed) escaped purgatory quickly because a single owner (DISA, DON) controlled budget, network and ATO. Tactical CDS shows the opposite pattern: SBIR Phase II to sole-source Phase III IDIQ (Owl) and prototype OT to production OT (PMAT), i.e., transition happens but only for incumbents already inside the accreditation moat.
proto_purgatory.opportunity_or_warning: Warning for coalition/releasability products (policy-bound, multi-owner); opportunity for tooling that a single program office can buy and deploy on its own authority (tagging at source, ZT evidence, offline policy enforcement), provided it attaches to a funded program (NGC2, Flank Speed edge, DEVCOM C5ISR S&T) rather than to the multinational demonstration circuit.

candidate_gaps.title: Offline-capable policy and key enforcement for tagged data at the tactical edge (ZT Data pillar in DDIL)
candidate_gaps.problem_one_sentence: Zero-trust access and TDF-style data protection stop working when the identity provider, policy decision point or key server is unreachable, so tactical units either fall back to implicit trust or lose access to protected data.
candidate_gaps.user: Battalion/brigade S6 and data managers, NGC2/tactical cloud node operators, expeditionary targeting cells
candidate_gaps.current_workflow: 1) Users authenticate to enterprise IdP when connected; 2) data is protected by network enclave rather than object tags; 3) when disconnected, applications run on cached credentials or local accounts with static role permissions; 4) tagged/encrypted objects cannot be opened without the enterprise key service; 5) on reconnection, audit logs are backfilled manually.
candidate_gaps.current_solution: Enterprise ZT (Thunderdome, Flank Speed) plus shipboard/edge extensions that assume periodic SATCOM; local ACLs; no fielded edge PDP/KAS with attribute caching and delegated key release.
candidate_gaps.failure_point: Enforcement is either bypassed (local accounts) or blocks the mission (no key release); attributes go stale; no revocation while disconnected.

candidate_gaps.why_startups_havent_solved: Requires crypto/key-management rigor plus tactical networking knowledge; incumbents sell connectivity-dependent enterprise ZT; the sponsor (DEVCOM C5ISR) is S&T, not a PEO with production dollars.

candidate_gaps.technical_wedge_hypothesis: An edge PDP/KAS node that caches signed attribute bundles and time-boxed key grants, enforces ABAC on OpenTDF/ZTDF objects offline, and reconciles audit and revocation on reconnect.
candidate_gaps.mvp_sketch: Two-node demo: enterprise KAS + edge KAS on a laptop; CoT/USMTF messages tagged and encrypted at source; cut the link and show continued policy-correct access and denial; reconnect and replay audit. Unclassified, synthetic data.

candidate_gaps.integration_requirement: OpenTDF SDKs, OIDC IdP, Kubernetes at edge (UDS/Zarf style), NGC2 or TAK ecosystem APIs.

candidate_gaps.title: Interoperable security labeling automation for machine-generated C2/ISR data (ACP-240/ZTDF/IC-TDF conformance, dominance-aware release computation)
candidate_gaps.problem_one_sentence: Tracks, reports and video are produced without machine-readable, interoperable classification/releasability tags, so ABAC and cross-domain filters cannot make automated decisions and staff regenerate products by hand.
candidate_gaps.user: Intelligence and fires staff producing REL products, foreign disclosure officers, CDS filter engineers, NGC2/data-layer integrators
candidate_gaps.current_workflow: 1) Producer creates product in a national system at collateral Secret; 2) FDO reviews and re-marks; 3) product is recreated on the lower enclave or MPE with REL markings using a different tool; 4) CDS transfer with manual review of failures; 5) partner receives hours later.
candidate_gaps.current_solution: Document-centric labeling tools (Titus/Boldon James, Purview), manual marking guides, vendor-specific CDS filters; standards exist (ACP-240, ZTDF) but are tested in demos.
candidate_gaps.failure_point: Labels are absent or inconsistent at source; fused objects inherit the most restrictive marking and become unreleasable; humans become the throughput limit.

candidate_gaps.incumbent_response_risk: Medium-high: Virtru and Everfox are natural owners; a labeling library could be absorbed into NGC2 data layer vendors (Palantir/Anduril).
candidate_gaps.technical_wedge_hypothesis: A 'label compiler' service: ingests C2/ISR messages, derives ISM/ACP-240 labels from schema fields and source attributes via declarative rules, emits ZTDF/IC-TDF assertions, computes dominance/releasability sets per partner, and produces CDS-filter-ready metadata plus a conformance linter for exercises.

candidate_gaps.killer_risk: Marking policy changes or DoD mandates a single vendor format; buyers keep tagging in the demo circuit (proto-purgatory) without funding a product.

segments.what_it_does: The PNT layer produces, protects, fuses and distributes four-dimensional state (x, y, z, and time) for every platform, weapon, radio and C2 node. It underpins the rest of C4ISR: sensor georegistration, track correlation, fires targeting, network time for Link 16/SATCOM/crypto, and the common operating picture all consume PNT. Technically it comprises (1) space and terrestrial signal sources (GPS incl. encrypted M-code, LEO-PNT, eLoran/VLF, signals of opportunity), (2) onboard relative sensors (IMUs, clocks, odometry, vision, magnetometers, celestial, quantum sensors), (3) a fusion engine that estimates position/velocity/attitude/time and, increasingly, an assurance/integrity verdict per source (Army PNT Reference Architecture v1.0, 2018), (4) NAVWAR defensive functions (anti-jam antennas, interference detection, spoof rejection) and (5) time transfer across networks so that platforms can exchange USNO-traceable time without GPS. Policy requires every platform with a validated PNT requirement to have a DoD-approved primary source (GPS PPS) plus at least one GPS-independent alternate (OPNAVINST 9420.1C para 5.a(3); DoDI 4650.08 NAVWAR compliance).

sub_taxonomy.name: Space-based signal sources (GPS III/IIIF, M-code, OCX ground control, LEO-PNT such as Xona and Iridium STL, NTS-3 experiments)
sub_taxonomy.note: Capital-intensive, prime-dominated; startups appear only as LEO-PNT constellation builders or payload/waveform experimenters.

sub_taxonomy.name: Terrestrial and signals-of-opportunity positioning (eLoran/VLF, 900 MHz NextNav TerraPoiNT, cellular/TV/LEO comm SoOP)
sub_taxonomy.note: GAO-21-320SP lists VLF (about 500 m, sufficient for ships) and LEO signals of opportunity; DoD policy bars civil/commercial/foreign sources as PRIMARY for combat without waiver (DoDI 4650.08 1.2.d), so these enter as complementary sources.

sub_taxonomy.name: Onboard relative sensors (MEMS/FOG/RLG inertial, chip-scale and optical atomic clocks, quantum inertial and magnetometers, silicon-photonic gyros)
sub_taxonomy.note: Deep physics and manufacturing; GAO notes thermal-beam atomic sensors need high-precision assembly and CSACs cost about $2,000 with 100x worse precision than GPS after one day.

sub_taxonomy.name: Map-matching absolute navigation (magnetic anomaly navigation, vision/terrain-referenced navigation, automated celestial)
sub_taxonomy.note: GAO reports demonstrated accuracies of about 100 m (magnetic), about 10 m (terrestrial image analysis) and about 50 m (celestial); weather, featureless terrain and platform magnetic noise are the limits. Software-heavy but data-dependent (maps, imagery).

sub_taxonomy.name: Fusion engine and open architecture (pntOS government-owned fusion engine, ASPN 2023 message standard, MOSA PNT reference architectures, plugin compliance toolkit)
sub_taxonomy.note: Restructured as its own sub-layer because the 2026 public release of ASPN-ICD and the pntOS C API on GitHub makes this the first part of the PNT stack that a small software team can build against without ITAR hardware.

sub_taxonomy.name: PNT assurance, integrity monitoring and NAVWAR situational awareness (spoof/jam detection, composite confidence, interference reporting to EW, fleet-wide interference maps)

current_architecture.description: GPS remains the core: DoD's 2020 PNT S&T Roadmap and GAO-21-320SP state GPS will stay the primary source with alternative sources complementing it and cross-checking each other. Platforms carry a GPS receiver (SAASM today, M-code via MGUE cards as they arrive), an inertial unit and a clock; the Army's MAPS/DAPS and the Navy's GPNTS add a fusion engine that ingests multiple sources and outputs a single assured PVT plus assurance. The Army leads a DoD-wide MOSA: service PNT reference architectures (Army v1.0 July 2018; Navy; Air Force nascent in 2021), the DARPA-originated All-Source Positioning and Navigation (ASPN) interface standard, and the government-owned pntOS fusion engine with vendor plug-ins. In 2026 the ASPN 2023 YAML data model and the pntOS C API became publicly downloadable on GitHub (Open-PNT org), with a separate government-only ASPN message set behind a citizenship/contractor gate (aspn.us). Time is distributed by GPS, holdover clocks and network time transfer over Link 16/TTNT/PTW/CDL; a Navy-led initiative seeks to make every comms system able to pass USNO-traceable time. NAVWAR compliance is a milestone gate for any system producing or using PNT (DoDI 4650.08 Section 3).

current_architecture.security_domain: Mixed. GPS PPS/M-code keys and crypto are classified/COMSEC (crypto network assignments handled by NSA and Space Force per DoDI 4650.08); NAVWAR threat assessments and PNT Oversight Council reports are classified (GAO-21-320SP fn 36). The government ASPN message set is access-controlled (citizenship + contractor verification). The Navy operator-awareness topic is explicitly CUI-only with 'no plan for work at higher classification' and no facility clearance expected for Phase II (NP004 Q&A 2026-08-28 and 2026-09-01). Civil PNT-integrity work (DHS/NIST) is fully public.
current_architecture.connectivity_dependency: The layer is designed to work with NO connectivity: onboard relative sensors carry the solution through outages. However absolute corrections (GPS, LEO-PNT, SoOP, celestial/magnetic map updates 'days to months', corrections) and fleet-wide interference awareness depend on RF or network reach. The Navy requires the awareness capability including all analytics and AI inference to run 100% air-gapped aboard individual ships with no reliance on shore or cloud (NP004 Q&A 2026-08-20).
current_architecture.what_breaks_when_disconnected: Without GPS/absolute sources, inertial and clock errors grow unbounded (GAO fig. 6): CSACs are about 100x worse than GPS after a day; ships tolerate 500 m-class fixes but munitions and fires need frequent absolute updates. Network time drifts, which eventually breaks crypto synchronization and Link 16 net entry (INFERENCE from GAO 3.3.1). Operators today must reconcile several fragmented displays manually to decide whether to switch sources or drop to INS-only (NP004 Q&A). Alternative PNT technologies that rely on communications links may themselves be unavailable in a degraded environment (GAO 4.1.7).

technical_difficulty.summary: Split sharply by sub-layer. Signal sources and quantum/photonic sensors are deep-physics, manufacturing-limited problems (GAO: thermal-beam atomic sensors need 'many high-precision components and specialized assembly'; new clock architectures blocked by light-source and vacuum-chamber manufacturing). Map-matching navigation is mostly software plus data (magnetic maps, imagery) with platform-noise calibration. The fusion/assurance/awareness sub-layers are classic estimation, integrity monitoring (RAIM-like consistency, multi-source consensus, ICD-compliance checks as in the DHS PNT Integrity Library) and HMI/decision-support engineering, now buildable against public ASPN/pntOS schemas with synthetic data. The Navy explicitly wants no new sensors or algorithms for NP004, only software architecture, data integration, UX/HMI, analytics and decision support.
required_expertise: Kalman/particle-filter state estimation and INS error modeling
GNSS observables, RAIM and spoof/jam detection methods (Psiaki & Humphreys class literature; TEXBAT datasets)
ASPN/pntOS message modeling and plugin development (C API, meson)
Human-centered design for watchstanders; ECDIS/S-52 symbology and IMO bridge-alert conventions
Containerized air-gapped deployment (Iron Bank/Platform One, Kubernetes) and CMMC Level 2 practices
Explainable decision support and auditable event logging
For hardware paths: atomic physics, photonics, RF front-end and antenna design, magnetometry, precision manufacturing
technical_difficulty.hardest_problem: Deriving a trustworthy composite confidence across 3-8 heterogeneous sources when 'untrustworthy does not always mean the current solution is incorrect' (DHS CF) and when the adversary can also corrupt the maps/models alt-PNT relies on (GAO 4.1.7); doing this with sub-second latency, offline, and with rationale the operator trusts. Army officials told GAO that assurance determination 'is an active research area' with source-level and consensus approaches both immature (GAO-21-320SP 3.3.2).
technical_difficulty.commodity_parts: Open-source GNSS-SDR software receiver (GPL-3), gnss-lib-py (Stanford NavLab, PyPI 1.1.0), DHS PNT Integrity Library (BSD-3), MagNav.jl and USAF open flight data, ASPN 2023 YAML schemas, pntOS-C API, MapLibre/PMTiles for offline charts, IHO S-57 test cells, NIST/USNO holdover references, commercial MEMS IMUs, CSACs (about $2,000 each per GAO 2021), Iron Bank base images.

capital_intensity.proof_of_concept_usd: Software (assurance/awareness/tooling): $50k-$150k for a synthetic-ASPN simulator, fusion/consistency checks and an ECDIS-like HMI demo. Hardware/quantum sensor: $3M-$15M lab and team.
capital_intensity.credible_military_demo_usd: Software: $0.3M-$2M, i.e., one Navy SBIR Phase I ($315k max) plus Phase II ($2M max) including a PNTAX or fleet demonstration with GPNTS ICDs. Hardware/quantum: $15M-$60M including flight/sea trials and ruggedization.
capital_intensity.first_production_deployment_usd: Software: $2M-$8M for GPNTS/pntOS integration, Iron Bank hardening, ATO/certification, fleet training and sustainment. Hardware: $50M-$200M+ for qualified production, consistent with Infleqtion's public-market scale and SandboxAQ's funding (RECALL).
capital_intensity.assumptions: Two founders, $250k, U.S.-based; Phase I performable entirely on synthetic ASPN/pntOS data (NP004 Q&A); no facility clearance for Phase II; integration costs dominated by government-furnished ICDs and certification rather than hardware. Hardware ranges are order-of-magnitude judgments (HYPOTHESIS) informed by GAO manufacturing findings and public funding sizes.

regulatory_access.prototype_with_commercial_unclassified_d: yes - for the fusion/assurance/awareness sub-layers: 'In Phase 1, vendors may use synthetic data that adheres to open-source standards (ASPN/pntOS)' (NP004 Q&A 2026-08-28); public GPS ICDs, DHS/NIST frameworks, USCG/MARAD interference advisories and open flight data (MagNav) are all unclassified. No for M-code/PPS receiver work (COMSEC keys) and for real NAVWAR threat data.
regulatory_access.government_data_required: Post-award only: GPNTS ICDs and message types, the government ASPN message set (citizenship + contractor verification at aspn.us), representative Navy data sets in Phase II, and JNWC standardized threat conditions. Real jamming/spoofing signatures come from PNTAX/JNWC or civil sources (TEXBAT, Jammertest).
regulatory_access.itar_ear: Military GNSS receivers with anti-jam/PPS/M-code and associated technical data are USML-controlled (Category XII(d) class, RECALL) and M-code cryptography is COMSEC; MAPS/DAPS-type hardware is ITAR. The NP004 topic carries no ITAR banner (Q&A 2026-08-28 contrasts it with NP003) and is CUI/CMMC L2. Inertial and quantum sensor designs may be USML or EAR 7A/7E controlled. DoDI 4650.08 1.2.f restricts foreign transfer of equipment relying on civil/commercial/foreign PNT sources. Specialist export-control classification is required before a non-U.S.-person founder touches receiver or sensor technical data.
regulatory_access.cui_likely: Yes. 'All NP004 Phase I data and activity is controlled unclassified information' (Q&A 2026-08-28); CMMC Level 2 (Self) at award; DFARS 7012 handling.
regulatory_access.classified_integration_eventually: For operator awareness on Navy ships: the government says no plan for higher classification and no facility clearance expected in Phase II (Q&A 2026-09-01). For anything touching M-code keys, NAVWAR threat assessments (classified per GAO), Link 16 time transfer or JNWC biennial assessments, yes.
regulatory_access.cleared_personnel_at_mvp: Not for the awareness/fusion-tooling MVP (per Navy Q&A). Required for M-code receiver, crypto, or threat-library work.
regulatory_access.non_us_person_founder_note: Three distinct constraints need counsel: (1) SBIR/STTR eligibility requires a small business more than 50% owned and controlled by U.S. citizens or permanent residents (SBA policy directive; the German founder's pending permanent residency and the Indonesian founder's status both matter); (2) CUI/CMMC and the aspn.us government message set gate on citizenship/contractor verification, so a non-U.S.-person co-founder may be excluded from the government-only schema and from Phase II data even though the work is unclassified; (3) ITAR technical-data access for any receiver/sensor path is a deemed-export issue. None of this is a definitive legal judgment; it is the checklist for an export-control and government-contracts attorney.

why_not_solved.explanation: No central alt-PNT program office; each service and each platform sets its own PNT requirements, so vendors face 'a range of requirements' and a market too small for economies of scale (GAO-21-320SP 4.1.1, 4.1.3, 4.1.4). The awareness layer sat between navigation, EW and C2 owners with nobody responsible.

Fielded receivers are closed systems delivered by one prime; 'because of this proprietary nature, there are few opportunities to integrate alternative PNT technologies' (GAO 4.1.6). Until ASPN/pntOS became public in 2026 there was no open surface for third-party software.

The pntOS C API (April 2026) and ASPN 2023 public release (January 2026) plus the Navy's decision to accept synthetic ASPN/pntOS data for Phase I make a software-only entry possible for the first time; quantum sensors and LEO-PNT are still manufacturing- and constellation-limited.

DoD funded the integration/MOSA fix at $17M over five years against $783M of PNT S&T; experts warned it would 'peter out' without sustained funding, and hardware vendors have little incentive to open interfaces.

NAVWAR compliance must be determined at every milestone and fleet PNT systems certified as-designed and as-installed; GAO found OT&E policy for MOSA-type systems 'a challenge' and no PNT-specific MOSA certification path, which slows any modular newcomer.

Threat conditions, PNT Oversight Council reports and PPS crypto are classified, so integrity algorithms are often tuned inside cleared prime environments rather than in open competition; civil (DHS) work stays separate.

Composite multi-source assurance is still 'an active research area' (GAO 3.3.2) and DHS CF Level 3-4 behaviors (bounded degradation, automatic recovery without disrupting output) are aspirational for most fielded equipment.

attractiveness.bull: For a two-person software team the 2026 opening is unusually clean: a named Navy transition owner (GPNTS) has published a software-only open topic with CUI-only work, no clearance expected through Phase II, synthetic ASPN/pntOS data allowed, multiple Phase I awards planned, $315k Phase I and $2M Phase II Prototype OTs, and a stated preference for commercially derived data-integration/decision-support platforms. The same assurance and awareness engine has civil analogs (DHS conformance levels, critical-infrastructure timing, maritime GNSS interference advisories) that reduce single-customer risk. Public ASPN/pntOS schemas plus open-source integrity libraries (DHS PNT Integrity, GNSS-SDR, MagNav data) mean the MVP needs no ITAR hardware. Persistent GAO findings since 2017 and daily GPS-denied testing show demand will not evaporate.
attractiveness.bear: The NP004 topic will draw many bidders (NAVWAR states multiple awards) including incumbents around GPNTS and firms with ECDIS/HMI pedigrees; SBIR ownership rules and CUI/citizenship gates cut against a team with a non-U.S.-person founder; PNT is 'nobody's business' inside DoD, so a Phase III could stall in proto-purgatory as alt-PNT S&T has for years; the deep-value hardware layers (M-code, quantum sensors, LEO-PNT, timing) are capital-intensive and prime-dominated and out of reach for $250k; and the awareness layer could be absorbed into GPNTS or a future NGC2-style C2 data layer as a feature rather than a product.
attractiveness.verdict: Attractive only in the software sub-layers (multi-source assurance/awareness, pntOS/ASPN tooling and NAVWAR test harnesses); MEDIUM-HIGH for those, LOW for sensors, signals and timing hardware. The Navy NP004 topic is the single best-documented near-term entry vehicle in this segment, but the founders' eligibility must be cleared first.

market_stage.rationale: Hardware assured-PNT (MAPS/DAPS) has reached production and repeat buys (RECALL), M-code is late but funded, and alternative sources sit in prototype awards; that is 'Transitioning' overall. The software assurance/awareness sub-layer is 'Emerging/Prototyping': its first dedicated solicitation appeared in August 2026 and its open interfaces were published only in 2026.

proto_purgatory.notes: GAO records that alternative PNT technologies 'can be demonstrated to show that they work, but few successfully transition to operational systems' (PNT Roadmap via GAO-21-320SP 4.1.6), with $783M of S&T over FY2020-2024 and only a $17M integration initiative expected to 'peter out'. The DAF-MIT MagNav project has formally concluded with no public transition record. DIU TQS vendors (2024) have not shown public production orders by mid-2026 (RECALL). Counter-examples: TRX DAPS and Collins MAPS moved to production (RECALL), and NP004 names a program of record as transition owner, which is the strongest anti-purgatory signal for the software layer.
proto_purgatory.opportunity_or_warning: Warning for novel-sensor startups (institutional pattern of demos without transition, plus classified/PoR-owned integration). Opportunity for software that lowers the integration/certification cost that causes the purgatory (pntOS plugins, synthetic-data test harnesses, assurance dashboards), provided the team ties itself to a PoR early.

candidate_gaps.title: Unified assured-PNT operational awareness and decision support (single pane for source health, composite confidence, threat triage and fallback recommendation)
candidate_gaps.problem_one_sentence: Navigation operators must mentally fuse several fragmented displays of GPS/INS/alternate-source health to decide whether they are jammed, spoofed or broken and which fallback to take, with no composite confidence, no recommendation and no audit trail.
candidate_gaps.user: Navy ETV/ETSW and navigation team on surface combatants (initial); analogous roles on Army MAPS-equipped vehicles, aircraft and coalition ships later.
candidate_gaps.current_workflow: 1. ETV mans the station during contested transits. 2. Watches separate GPS, INS, GPNTS and alternate-source indicators plus ECDIS. 3. Notices divergence or alarms. 4. Manually infers cause (fault vs jam vs spoof) from raw indicators and experience. 5. Consults TTPs/checklists and OOD. 6. Selects alternate source or INS-only. 7. Records actions in navigation workbook; reports interference to NAVCEN/EW cell by voice or message.
candidate_gaps.current_solution: Individual system HMIs (GPNTS, INS, receiver front panels), ECDIS, paper/PDF procedures, celestial/radar/DR fixes as backup; no unified confidence or decision aid (Navy states this in the topic).
candidate_gaps.failure_point: Slow, error-prone triage under workload; wrong fallback selection; no explainable rationale or replay; interference information not automatically passed to electronic support as OPNAVINST 9420.1C 5.a(11) intends.
