candidate_gaps.incumbent_response_risk: MEDIUM-HIGH: the GPNTS prime or IS4S could add an awareness screen; ECDIS-N vendors could extend the chart display; Navy could keep it government-developed. Mitigation: be the composite-assurance analytics and replay engine, not just a dashboard, and hold the synthetic-scenario library.
candidate_gaps.technical_wedge_hypothesis: A source-agnostic 'PNT integrity graph' that ingests ASPN measurement and integrity fields from 3-8 sources, runs consistency/ICD-compliance/consensus checks (DHS PNT Integrity-style plus INS-GNSS divergence and clock-drift models), emits a composite confidence with attributed evidence, and renders on an S-52-conformant chart layer with bridge-alert-management style alerts; deterministic, explainable, replayable, containerized.
candidate_gaps.mvp_sketch: Synthetic strait-transit scenario generator (GNSS jam/spoof, INS drift, clock holdover) emitting ASPN 2023 messages; integrity engine; ECDIS-like web HMI with alert banner, source cards, composite confidence gauge, recommended fallback with rationale, event timeline/replay; Docker/Kubernetes deployment offline; user study with former ETVs measuring speed-to-decision and fallback accuracy (Navy's stated metrics).
candidate_gaps.data_requirement: Phase I: synthetic ASPN/pntOS streams, public GPS ICDs, TEXBAT/Jammertest-type spoof/jam signatures, NOAA ENC cells. Phase II: GPNTS ICDs and representative Navy data sets (government-furnished post-award).
candidate_gaps.integration_requirement: ASPN/pntOS ingest; GPNTS message types (Phase II); optional NMEA/IEC 61162 bridge bus; Iron Bank container images; Navy ECDIS-N symbology conventions; eventual interface to EW reporting (NAVCEN, electronic support).
candidate_gaps.entry_vehicle: Navy SBIR 26.5 topic DON26BX05-NP004 (closed 2026-09-23; expect re-issue or Phase II path), then Navy STP and Phase III via GPNTS; Army analog via PM PNT/xTech or C5ISR Center pntOS plug-in community; civil analog via DHS/CISA and maritime operators.
candidate_gaps.why_now: First-ever dedicated solicitation (Aug 2026), public ASPN/pntOS (2026), ASPN moving to an industry consortium (Jul 2026), GPS-denied testing and real-world interference at record levels, and explicit government acceptance of commercially derived platforms.
candidate_gaps.killer_risk: Founder eligibility (SBIR >50% U.S.-person ownership; CUI/citizenship gates on the government ASPN message set) and single-customer dependence on GPNTS; also a crowded Phase I field with multiple awards diluting the win.

candidate_gaps.title: Formation- and theater-level PNT interference and integrity picture (crowd-sourced NAVWAR situational awareness feeding the C2/EW COP)
candidate_gaps.problem_one_sentence: Individual MAPS/DAPS/GPNTS units detect jamming or spoofing locally, but there is no unified, near-real-time aggregation of those reports across a formation into the EW/C2 common operating picture, so commanders cannot see where PNT is being denied or trust which tracks are position-corrupted.
candidate_gaps.user: EW/spectrum planners and battle captains at battalion through theater; JNWC and Space Force NAVWAR cells; coalition navigation warfare officers.
candidate_gaps.current_workflow: 1. Platform receiver flags interference. 2. Crew reports by voice/chat or not at all. 3. EW cell manually plots reports; JNWC compiles assessments after the fact. 4. Civil channels (NAVCEN, MARAD, ADS-B community maps) run in parallel. 5. Commander infers denial areas from anecdotes.
candidate_gaps.current_solution: JNWC operational field assessments and biennial assessments (DoDI 4650.08); EW planning tools; RF-geolocation constellations (RECALL: HawkEye 360); civil GPS jamming maps from ADS-B; MARAD/NAVCEN advisories.
candidate_gaps.failure_point: Latency (hours to days), manual re-entry, releasability barriers between platforms/coalition, and no link between interference geometry and the trustworthiness of tracks in the COP.

evidence.claim: Policy expects PNT systems to feed interference information to electronic support efforts to 'detect, identify, and resolve interference issues'.
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: JNWC is tasked with PNT operational field assessments and a biennial DoD PNT/NAVWAR assessment; Services must coordinate threat vignettes with JNWC, NGA and DIA.
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: GAO: 'more attention should be given to determine threats to PNT'; knowledge gap on vulnerabilities of alternative PNT; adversaries could corrupt maps/models.
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: Civil authorities run parallel reporting (NAVCEN report-a-problem, NATO Shipping Centre interference reporting) because disruption is global and frequent.
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: Army fires RFI now requires systems to 'operate and protect itself against attacks on... PNT capabilities' in DDIL, i.e., PNT threat awareness is a cross-cutting C2 requirement.
evidence.source_url: see research/evidence/E02.json finding 31 (SAM.gov Mobile-Long Range Precision RFI)
evidence.label: FACT (captured by another agent)

evidence.claim: Commercial RF-geolocation and ADS-B-derived jamming maps exist but are not integrated into tactical COPs (RECALL).
evidence.source_url: Public evidence insufficient in this run
evidence.label: HYPOTHESIS

candidate_gaps.why_startups_havent_solved: Receiver telemetry is program-owned and often CUI/classified once aggregated with threat data; the output looks like an EW product, so it falls to EW primes and JNWC; releasability across coalition partners is unresolved (see S06/S08 segments).
companies_near: EW planning tool vendors (Army EWPMT lineage, RECALL)
candidate_gaps.incumbent_response_risk: HIGH: NGC2 data-layer teams and EW primes can add an interference layer; JNWC may build in-house.
candidate_gaps.technical_wedge_hypothesis: A lightweight interference-report schema (ASPN integrity fields + receiver C/N0/AGC + geometry) published over TAK/CoT and NGC2 data APIs, with edge aggregation into denial-area polygons and per-track PNT-trust scores that C2 apps can consume.
candidate_gaps.mvp_sketch: ATAK plugin + edge service that ingests receiver integrity messages from MAPS/DAPS-class units or COTS receivers, geolocates jammers from multi-node C/N0 gradients, and pushes MIL-STD-2525 interference overlays and trust-tagged tracks; validated at PNTAX or a Project Convergence-type event.
candidate_gaps.data_requirement: Receiver integrity telemetry (government-furnished or COTS), exercise ground truth from PNTAX/JNWC, civil interference reports.
candidate_gaps.integration_requirement: TAK/CoT, NGC2/CPCE data layer, EW planning tools, JNWC reporting formats; coalition releasability policies.
candidate_gaps.entry_vehicle: Army xTech/SBIR with PM PNT or PM EW&C; PNTAX participation; DIU CSO if issued; JNWC cooperative research (RECALL that JNWC engages industry at assessments).
candidate_gaps.why_now: NGC2 data-layer programs are being architected in 2025-2026 and MAPS/DAPS Gen II units with interference detection are fielding at scale (RECALL).
candidate_gaps.killer_risk: Classification of aggregated threat pictures pushes the product into cleared-facility territory and away from a non-U.S.-person founder; absorbed as a feature by NGC2 integrators.

candidate_gaps.title: pntOS/ASPN developer tooling: synthetic-scenario generators, plug-in conformance testing and NAVWAR-compliance evidence harness for alternative PNT vendors and programs
candidate_gaps.problem_one_sentence: Every alt-PNT vendor and every PNT-using program must now prove ASPN/pntOS conformance and NAVWAR compliance, but the government's planned compliance toolkit, M&S fidelity and field-test capacity are thin, so integration remains bespoke, slow and expensive.
candidate_gaps.user: Alt-PNT sensor vendors (DIU TQS cohort, LEO-PNT, MagNav, vision-nav), platform integrators, PM PNT/NAVWAR test engineers, NAVWAR-compliance reviewers.
candidate_gaps.current_workflow: 1. Vendor obtains ASPN/pntOS docs (public C API; government messages after vetting). 2. Writes plug-in with ad hoc test data. 3. Waits for PNTAX or a program lab slot. 4. Program runs M&S with low-fidelity alt-PNT models. 5. MDA demands NAVWAR compliance evidence at milestone; evidence assembled manually.
candidate_gaps.current_solution: Spirent/Safran Skydel RF simulators (hardware-in-the-loop, costly), Army MDQDA and GIANT/CIGNM (government-internal), annual PNTAX, vendor-specific test rigs.
candidate_gaps.failure_point: No affordable software-only conformance/scenario harness for the new open ecosystem; alt-PNT model fidelity 'poorer'; OT&E policy for MOSA systems unresolved; field tests need airspace closures.

evidence.claim: Army plans 'a compliance toolkit that can automatically verify that plug-ins for the PNT Operating System comply with its architecture'; OT&E policies 'are a challenge to fielding capabilities enabled by MOSAs'.
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: Alt-PNT M&S fidelity is poorer than GNSS models; engagement-level multi-technology trade tools 'do not yet exist'; field tests are expensive and need civil airspace closures.
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: NAVWAR compliance must be determined and reported to the MDA at each milestone with T&E plans sufficient to validate it; fleet PNT systems must be certified as-designed and as-installed.
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: pntOS-C and ASPN-ICD became public in 2026 with minimal adoption signals (3 stars/4 forks on 2026-08-26), indicating an early ecosystem needing tooling.
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: Navy accepts synthetic ASPN/pntOS data for Phase I and states 'innovation required on the ingestion of disparate types of APNT data sources and how to standardize those types of data'.
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: The DoD MOSA initiative was funded at only $17M FY2020-2024 and may 'peter out', leaving tooling under-resourced.
evidence.label: FACT

candidate_gaps.why_startups_havent_solved: Interfaces were not public until 2026; the customer set (vendors + programs) is small and the government intends to own the compliance toolkit; simulator incumbents focus on RF hardware.
candidate_gaps.incumbent_response_risk: MEDIUM: C5ISR Center may release its own toolkit; Spirent/Safran can add ASPN outputs.
candidate_gaps.technical_wedge_hypothesis: Software-only 'PNT digital twin' that generates ASPN 2023 streams for GNSS/INS/clock/magnetic/vision sources under JNWC-style threat conditions, scores plug-ins for schema and behavioral conformance (DHS CF levels), and auto-produces NAVWAR-compliance evidence packages.
candidate_gaps.mvp_sketch: Open-core scenario generator + conformance test suite for pntOS plug-ins with a hosted evidence report; first users are alt-PNT vendors preparing for PNTAX; dual use for the S11-G1 HMI testing.
candidate_gaps.data_requirement: Public ICDs, ASPN schemas, open flight data (MagNav), TEXBAT-class spoof datasets; later government threat conditions (CUI/classified).
candidate_gaps.integration_requirement: pntOS C API, ASPN YAML, CI pipelines, Iron Bank for government use.
candidate_gaps.entry_vehicle: B2B sales to alt-PNT vendors (no eligibility barrier), then Army SBIR/xTech with PM PNT; PNTAX participation; possible ISTO PNT Standards Consortium membership.
candidate_gaps.why_now: Public API release and consortium transfer in 2026; growing vendor cohort from DIU TQS and LEO-PNT needing conformance.
candidate_gaps.killer_risk: Government keeps tooling in-house and free; market too small (a few dozen vendors) to fund a company.

candidate_gaps.title: Non-GPS time distribution and holdover assurance for tactical networks and C2 nodes
candidate_gaps.problem_one_sentence: When GPS is denied, radios, crypto and C2 servers lose their common time reference within hours to a day (CSAC holdover is about 100x worse than GPS after one day), and the Navy-led initiative to distribute USNO-traceable time over every comms link remains an S&T effort.
candidate_gaps.user: Network/timing engineers, Link 16 net managers, SATCOM/crypto custodians, data-center operators at battalion through theater.
candidate_gaps.current_workflow: 1. GPS disciplines a master clock. 2. On loss, rubidium/cesium holdover; NTP/PTP over the LAN. 3. Link 16/TTNT/PTW carry time within their nets. 4. Operators manually monitor drift and re-sync when GPS returns.
candidate_gaps.current_solution: Safran/Microchip timing servers and clocks, Iridium STL for indoor/timing, two-way satellite time transfer, network-specific time transfer; no unified cross-network timing assurance.
candidate_gaps.failure_point: Specialized time-transfer modems per network; no common monitoring of holdover state across radios and servers; policy requires USNO traceability certification.

evidence.claim: DoD S&T initiative (Navy lead) aims to enable all communications systems to distribute USNO-traceable time platform-to-platform to minimize specialized time transfer modems; time-transfer techniques exist per network (CDL, CEC, Link 16, LORAN, PTW, TTNT).
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: CSAC precision about 100x worse than GPS after one day; optical clocks could give GPS-level time for a day but need 10-20x the power; new clock architectures blocked by manufacturing.
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: Navy policy lists alternate precise-time sources (rubidium/cesium clocks, NTP, HF voice, two-way and one-way satellite time transfer) and requires USNO-certified clocks with documented traceability.
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: DHS CF gives a timing resilience example (Level 3, 1.8 microsecond threshold, 80 s recovery) showing measurable timing-assurance behaviors are expected of equipment.
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: Iridium (public) has built a PNT/timing line via Satelles; NextNav and others pursue terrestrial timing (RECALL).
evidence.label: FACT (listings) / RECALL (strategy)

candidate_gaps.why_startups_havent_solved: Time transfer lives inside waveforms and crypto (classified, prime-owned); clocks are a mature hardware oligopoly; the integrating customer is diffuse.
candidate_gaps.incumbent_response_risk: HIGH
candidate_gaps.technical_wedge_hypothesis: Software-only cross-network timing observability (holdover state, drift, source lineage) exposed as ASPN-style time-integrity messages to C2; hardware-agnostic.
candidate_gaps.mvp_sketch: Agent that reads timing status from NTP/PTP servers and radios' management interfaces and produces a time-trust map for the network operations cell.
candidate_gaps.data_requirement: Device management telemetry; access to radio/net management interfaces (often controlled).
candidate_gaps.integration_requirement: Radio and crypto management planes, NTP/PTP, Link 16 net management; certification with USNO.
candidate_gaps.entry_vehicle: Only via a prime or DISA/NIWC SBIR; no open solicitation identified in this run.
candidate_gaps.why_now: GPS-denied exercises increasing; but no procurement signal specific to timing assurance software surfaced.
candidate_gaps.killer_risk: Access to classified waveform/crypto interfaces; product becomes a feature of timing-server vendors.

candidate_gaps.title: Novel-physics alternative PNT sources (quantum inertial/clocks, magnetic navigation, LEO-PNT constellations)
candidate_gaps.problem_one_sentence: GPS-independent absolute and relative sources that match GPS-class performance do not exist ('none can match the performance of GPS'), and the ones in development face manufacturing, map-data and constellation-scale barriers.
candidate_gaps.user: All platforms; especially aircraft, ships, munitions and long-endurance UAS.
candidate_gaps.current_workflow: Programs default to GPS + INS; alt sources are evaluated in PNTAX/DIU TQS and flight trials; transition to PoRs is rare.
candidate_gaps.current_solution: Funded startups and primes: Infleqtion (public), SandboxAQ, Q-CTRL, Xona, Anello, Vector Atomic (IonQ), Iridium STL, NTS-3 experiments, R-GPS concepts.
candidate_gaps.failure_point: Manufacturing of atomic sensors and clocks; magnetic maps and platform noise; weather/featureless terrain for vision; constellation capex and DoDI 4650.08 primary-source restrictions for commercial LEO-PNT; few transitions to PoRs.

evidence.claim: GAO technology table: magnetic about 100 m, celestial about 50 m, terrestrial image analysis about 10 m, VLF about 500 m; atomic sensors 'challenging to produce'; clock manufacturing barriers.
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: DAF-MIT AIA MagNav project concluded; open data licensed only for non-profit research or government purposes, limiting commercial reuse.
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: Infleqtion listed on NYSE 2026-02-17 with about $3.2B market cap and 204 employees; NextNav about $2.0B; Iridium about $5.2B, showing capital scale required.
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: Reliance on civil/commercial/foreign sources as primary PNT for combat is not authorized without waiver; they may be complementary subject to NAVWAR compliance.
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: 'new technologies can be demonstrated to show that they work, but few successfully transition to operational systems' (PNT Roadmap via GAO).
evidence.label: FACT

candidate_gaps.why_startups_havent_solved: They are trying, with hundreds of millions of dollars; the barriers are physics, manufacturing and transition, not lack of attempts.
candidate_gaps.incumbent_response_risk: HIGH (Honeywell, Northrop, Collins, L3Harris, Safran all invest in inertial/clock/quantum).
candidate_gaps.technical_wedge_hypothesis: None suitable for a $250k two-person team; the only software-adjacent wedge is map/data services (magnetic anomaly maps, reference imagery) and denoising algorithms sold to sensor makers.
candidate_gaps.mvp_sketch: Not recommended for these founders.
candidate_gaps.data_requirement: Magnetic surveys, reference imagery, flight data under government licenses.
candidate_gaps.integration_requirement: Platform-level integration via primes; ITAR/EAR controls.
candidate_gaps.entry_vehicle: DIU TQS-style CSOs, AFWERX/Army SBIR Phase I/II (hardware), venture capital at $10M+ scale.
candidate_gaps.why_now: Quantum sensing maturity and Ukraine-driven urgency, but capital and time horizons exceed the founders' means.
candidate_gaps.killer_risk: Capital intensity and proto-purgatory; export controls for a non-U.S.-person founder.

candidate_gaps.title: GPS-denied visual/terrain navigation software for small UAS and ground vehicles as a standalone PNT product
candidate_gaps.problem_one_sentence: Cheap drones and vehicles need absolute positioning without GPS, and DoD has demonstrated 10 m-class terrestrial image navigation, but the capability is being delivered inside autonomy stacks (Skydio, Shield AI, Auterion, Maxar Raptor) rather than as an open, platform-agnostic PNT source that feeds pntOS/ASPN.
candidate_gaps.user: sUAS operators and platoon leaders; vehicle crews; autonomy developers.
candidate_gaps.current_workflow: Operators fly with GPS; under jamming they rely on the vendor's built-in visual navigation or lose the aircraft; ground vehicles fall back to MAPS/INS and map-compass.
candidate_gaps.current_solution: Vendor-embedded visual navigation (Skydio X10D, Shield AI Hivemind, Auterion Skynode), Maxar Raptor (RECALL), Vermeer (RECALL), academic SLAM.
candidate_gaps.failure_point: Weather/featureless terrain, reference-imagery currency and licensing, and lack of an ASPN-conformant interface so the source can be fused and assured by the platform's PNT manager.

evidence.claim: DoD demonstrated terrestrial image analysis on aircraft to about 10 m; limits are clouds and featureless areas; reference imagery available from state DOTs, NGA and Google.
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: Army SRR Tranche 2 platform (Skydio X10D) carries GPS-denied visual navigation; $52M/2,500+ order (captured by another agent).
evidence.label: FACT (per other agent's capture)

evidence.claim: Auterion claims target lock in jammed/GPS-denied conditions raising FPV effectiveness (company claim, not audited).
evidence.label: INFERENCE

evidence.claim: ASPN 2023 includes visnav and image message types, so a standards-conformant vision source is technically possible.
evidence.label: FACT

candidate_gaps.why_startups_havent_solved: The value accrues to the platform/autonomy vendor; buyers procure drones, not navigation modules; imagery licensing and compute constraints.
candidate_gaps.incumbent_response_risk: VERY HIGH
candidate_gaps.technical_wedge_hypothesis: ASPN-conformant vision-nav plug-in for pntOS with integrity outputs, sold to platform makers lacking in-house capability.
candidate_gaps.mvp_sketch: Open-source-based visual localization against satellite basemaps emitting ASPN visnav messages; demonstrate at PNTAX on a Blue UAS airframe.
candidate_gaps.data_requirement: Licensed reference imagery/DEMs; flight data.
candidate_gaps.integration_requirement: pntOS plug-in; flight-controller integration (PX4/ArduPilot); Blue UAS compliance.
candidate_gaps.entry_vehicle: AFWERX/Army SBIR; drone OEM partnerships.
candidate_gaps.why_now: Ukraine demand and Army drone push (2025-2026), but the space is already crowded (see segment on autonomy C2).
candidate_gaps.killer_risk: Crowding and platform-vendor absorption; this is largely covered by other segments.

segments.saturation_statement: Research is NOT saturated. It is saturated for the policy/architecture spine of the segment (GAO-21-320SP full text, DoDI 4650.08, OPNAVINST 9420.1C, DHS CF v2.0, ASPN/pntOS public artifacts) and for the single best 2026 demand signal (Navy topic DON26BX05-NP004 with its complete dated Q&A). It is thin or unverified for: Army MAPS/DAPS contract values and 2026 fielding status, Space Force R-GPS/OCX/MGUE 2026 status, NTS-3 experiment results, DIU TQS outcomes, every startup's funding and contract claims (SandboxAQ, Q-CTRL, Xona, Anello, Vermeer, TRX, Safran, Iridium STL, NextNav), FY2026-2027 budget lines, and exercise after-action language from PNTAX/Project Convergence/Baltic and Ukraine reporting. Those items are labeled RECALL and must be re-run with WebSearch/WebFetch access to army.mil, ssc.spaceforce.mil, diu.mil, sam.gov, usaspending.gov, comptroller.defense.gov and the trade press before investment-grade use.

segments.segment_name: Electronic Warfare / Spectrum Awareness adjacent to C4ISR
segments.what_it_does: This layer senses, characterizes, geolocates and visualizes the electromagnetic environment (friendly, neutral, adversary emitters and interference), plans and deconflicts friendly spectrum use (frequency assignment, Joint Restricted Frequency List, EMI resolution), and connects electronic-support (ES) sensing to command and control so commanders can see their own electromagnetic signature, detect and locate adversary emitters, and task electronic-attack or maneuver responses. In C4ISR terms it is the RF-domain COLLECT/PROCESS/FUSE feed into the common operating picture (COP), plus the spectrum-management workflow (DoD Spectrum XXI / GEMSIS / EMBM-J at the enterprise level, EWPMT and Raven Claw and now EWPMT-X on TAK at Army tactical echelons, USMC Spectrum Services Framework, Navy Real Time Spectrum Operations). Kinetic or effects layers (jammers, HPM such as Epirus Leonidas) are adjacent but not C4ISR.

sub_taxonomy.name: Tactical spectrum situational awareness (own-signature and threat emitter sensing)
sub_taxonomy.note: Low-cost networked RF sensors (Army S2AS, Heaviside MOTH, RII Dragonfly, Distributed Spectrum, CACI/Mastodon manpacks, Anduril Pulsar as sensor-effector) feeding a unit-level EM COP. This is where 2025-2026 Army money is moving (REWSI production IDIQs Aug-Sep 2026).

sub_taxonomy.name: Electromagnetic battle management / EW planning (EMBM)
sub_taxonomy.note: Planning, course-of-action analysis, effects visualization and EW tasking: Army EWPMT (Raytheon) and Raven Claw, now pivoting to EWPMT-X on the TAK framework with USMC; DISA Electromagnetic Battle Management-Joint (EMBM-J) for the joint level.

sub_taxonomy.name: Spectrum management and frequency assignment (enterprise and tactical)
sub_taxonomy.note: DISA Defense Spectrum Organization GEMSIS program of record (Spectrum XXI, Joint Spectrum Data Repository, E2ESS, Integrated Spectrum Desktop), NTIA frequency assignment workflow, JRFL building, EMI resolution; USMC Spectrum Services Framework; Navy RTSO/AESOP. Legacy, enterprise-hosted, connectivity-dependent.

sub_taxonomy.name: Passive RF sensing for airspace / C-UAS and installation protection
sub_taxonomy.note: Hidden Level ($100M OTA Aug 2026), Dedrone/Axon, SkySafe, BlueHalo (AeroVironment). Overlaps C-UAS segment; buyer is often JIATF-401, NORTHCOM installations, ranges, border.

sub_taxonomy.name: Interference detection and geolocation (dual-use)
sub_taxonomy.note: Commercial and government spectrum monitoring networks (CRFS RFeye, Rohde & Schwarz, Keysight, KrakenSDR TDOA/AoA), spectrum-sharing enforcement in bands DoD shares with commercial users (context: GAO-26-107873 on DoD-NTIA sharing studies).

sub_taxonomy.name: EW mission data / reprogramming and emitter libraries
sub_taxonomy.note: Air Force 350th Spectrum Warfare Wing, service reprogramming centers; classified threat libraries pushed to sensors and jammers. Mostly classified; least startup-accessible.

sub_taxonomy.name: Effects (electronic attack, HPM, directed energy)
sub_taxonomy.note: Adjacent, not C4ISR: Epirus Leonidas IFPC-HPM, Anduril Pulsar jamming modes, Raytheon NGJ, Lockheed/Northrop SEWIP, BAE aircraft EW. Included for incumbent mapping only.

current_architecture.description: A two-tier architecture. Enterprise tier: DISA DSO's GEMSIS family (Spectrum XXI for frequency assignment requests to NTIA and engineering analysis; Joint Spectrum Data Repository; E2ESS; Integrated Spectrum Desktop) plus the cloud-hosted, service-oriented Electromagnetic Battle Management-Joint (EMBM-J) being built on the GEMSIS foundation. Tactical tier: service-specific tools, chiefly Army EWPMT (Raytheon) with the Raven Claw laptop variant that works without a host server, now being re-hosted as EWPMT-X on the TAK framework with the USMC, and USMC Spectrum Services Framework and Navy RTSO said to interoperate through a common data layer. Sensors (TLS-BCT Manpack, TLS-EAB, MFEW-AL pod on Gray Eagle from 2026, MOTH, Dragonfly on Intrepid 1200 UAS, CACI manpacks, Pulsar) feed detections into ATAK/TAK and the CEMA cell; S2AS adds own-signature sensing and visualization for command posts. Integration between sensor detections, TAK COP, EWPMT planning and the enterprise frequency database is partial and largely manual (INFERENCE from the EWPMT cancellation rationale and the EMBM RFI).

data_formats_protocols: VITA 49 / VRT and SigMF for SDR IQ streams and recordings (RECALL)
Standard Frequency Action Format (SFAF) and Joint Restricted Frequency List (JRFL) records via Spectrum XXI / JSDR (RECALL)
USMTF / joint messaging and Link 16 J-series for EW tracks at the joint level (RECALL, LOW)
CMOSS / C5ISR Modular Open Suite of Standards and Modular Open RF Architecture (MORA) mandated for Army TLS-class hardware (RECALL)
Vendor APIs: Anduril Lattice, CRFS RFeye, KrakenSDR open-source DF software
current_architecture.security_domain: Mixed. Own-signature sensing, commercial-band interference hunting and open spectrum monitoring are unclassified/CUI. Threat emitter libraries, EW mission data, SIGINT-derived detections, JSDR frequency assignments and operational spectrum plans are CUI to SECRET and above; joint EMBM runs on classified networks. Coalition sharing constrained by releasability.
current_architecture.connectivity_dependency: Enterprise spectrum tools (Spectrum XXI, EMBM-J cloud) require reach-back; Raven Claw was created specifically because EWPMT needed a host server and reliable connectivity. Sensor networks depend on tactical radios or mesh for TDOA/AoA fusion; DDIL degrades geolocation accuracy and timeliness.
current_architecture.what_breaks_when_disconnected: Frequency assignment and JRFL updates stall (manual paper/spreadsheet workaround); distributed geolocation loses time-synchronized cross-sensor data; EM COP goes stale; EW tasking reverts to voice and chat; own-signature reporting to higher echelons is delayed.

technical_difficulty.summary: Building a single spectrum sensor or a dashboard is easy; building a calibrated, time-synchronized, low-SWaP sensor network that geolocates emitters accurately in cluttered terrain under DDIL, classifies unknown or LPI/LPD waveforms, and fuses into TAK/EWPMT/JSDR with proper security handling is hard. RF hardware expertise (receiver front-ends, calibration, antennas), signal processing (TDOA/AoA/FDOA, detection in dense environments), distributed systems (edge-cloud sync, mesh), and security architecture (CUI/classified data segregation) are all required. Own-signature awareness (S2AS-type) is the most software-tractable sub-problem; adversary emitter identification against classified libraries is the least.
required_expertise: RF systems and SDR (receiver chains, calibration, antenna arrays)
DSP and emitter geolocation (TDOA, AoA, FDOA, multilateration, propagation modeling over terrain)
RF machine learning (modulation recognition, anomaly detection, open-set classification)
Distributed edge computing and time synchronization (GPS-denied timing)
Tactical networking and DDIL-tolerant data sync
TAK/ATAK plugin development and CoT
Geospatial visualization and propagation modeling (ITM/Longley-Rice, SPLAT-like tools)
Security architecture for CUI/classified data and cross-domain flows
Ruggedization and EMC of small sensors
technical_difficulty.hardest_problem: Accurate, trustworthy geolocation and identification of adversary emitters from cheap, imperfectly synchronized sensors in real terrain, delivered to the COP within seconds under contested networks, without leaking friendly information - and doing it against waveforms whose signatures are classified.
technical_difficulty.commodity_parts: SDRs (USRP, Sidekiq, AIR-T, KrakenSDR), GPS-disciplined clocks, Jetson-class edge GPUs, GNU Radio/SigMF tooling, open-source propagation models, TAK server and plugin SDK, cloud GIS stacks.

capital_intensity.assumptions: PoC assumes 4-10 COTS SDR nodes, a TAK plugin and a cloud/edge fusion service built by two founders plus contractors. Credible demo assumes ruggedized enclosures, participation in an Army TiC exercise or JIATF-401/C-UAS test event, SBIR Phase I/II or an AFWERX open topic, one cleared advisor and initial ITAR compliance program. First production assumes tens to hundreds of sensors, environmental qualification, ATO/RMF, sustainment, and 12-24 months of working capital before IDIQ task orders fund deliveries. Hardware-heavy plays (Hidden Level, Distributed Spectrum) needed $25M-plus equity before a $100M-class ceiling award; a pure software/TAK plugin play could stay under $3M through first fielding.

regulatory_access.prototype_with_commercial_unclassified_d: partly - own-signature sensing, ISM/commercial-band interference, range and installation monitoring, and public SigMF datasets are unclassified; adversary emitter identification, threat libraries and operational spectrum plans are not.
regulatory_access.government_data_required: For an EM COP or spectrum-management tool: JSDR/Spectrum XXI frequency assignments (CUI), JRFL, unit task organization and emitter parametrics (CUI to SECRET). For own-signature and interference tools: mostly government-owned emissions recorded at exercises under CUI handling.
regulatory_access.itar_ear: ITAR USML Category XI covers military electronics including EW, SIGINT and direction-finding systems and software specially designed for them, plus related technical data; commercial spectrum-monitoring software on COTS SDRs may fall under EAR (e.g., 5A001/5D001 or EAR99) depending on design intent and specifications. Classification is jurisdiction-specific and needs a commodity jurisdiction/classification review by export counsel - no definitive judgment here.
regulatory_access.cui_likely: yes - nearly all DoD-specific data (frequency plans, unit signatures, sensor positions) will be CUI from the first exercise onward.
regulatory_access.classified_integration_eventually: yes for adversary emitter ID, EW mission data, joint EMBM and most SIGINT-adjacent use; possibly avoidable for own-signature, interference geolocation and C-UAS passive sensing.
regulatory_access.cleared_personnel_at_mvp: Not strictly required for an unclassified TAK plugin or interference tool; required within 12-24 months to integrate with EWPMT-X/EMBM-J or classified emitter data.
regulatory_access.non_us_person_founder_note: If the product is ITAR-controlled (likely for anything marketed as EW/ES/DF for military use), disclosure of technical data to a non-U.S.-person co-founder is a deemed export requiring DDTC authorization or a compartmented structure; the German founder's status as a future permanent resident changes his position (U.S. person under ITAR once lawfully admitted for permanent residence) but not the Indonesian founder's. Foreign ownership/control by non-U.S. persons can also trigger FOCI mitigation for any facility clearance and affect SBIR eligibility (majority U.S.-owned requirement). Scoping the initial product to EAR-controlled or EAR99 dual-use spectrum monitoring is the usual mitigation, but all of this requires specialist export-control and immigration counsel.

why_not_solved.explanation: Cheap wideband SDRs, edge GPUs and RF ML matured after 2018; the Army's 2014-era EWPMT architecture predates them, and the sensor density needed for an EM COP only became affordable around 2023-2025 (Distributed Spectrum, MOTH).

Sensors (PEO IEW&S programs and REWSI), planning software (EWPMT-X), enterprise spectrum data (DISA DSO GEMSIS), joint EMBM (DISA/JEMSOC), and C-UAS passive sensing (JIATF-401) are bought by different offices with different vehicles; no single buyer owns the end-to-end spectrum picture.

EWPMT was a single-prime development; GEMSIS/Spectrum XXI is a decades-old code base; sensor vendors expose proprietary formats. The move to TAK (EWPMT-X) is the Army's explicit fix, which also lowers the barrier for third-party plugins.

Adversary emitter parametrics, EW mission data and much SIGINT-derived detection live in classified enclaves, so a commercial startup cannot build or test the highest-value fusion without cleared staff and facilities.

Fusing detections from heterogeneous sensors with different time bases, security labels and formats into TAK, EWPMT and JSDR while under DDIL is an integration problem no single vendor has been contracted to own.

Outside DoD, spectrum monitoring buyers (regulators, telcos, ranges) are few and price-sensitive; Aurora Insight's RF-mapping-as-data model ended in a Maxar acquisition rather than scale, so venture capital historically avoided the segment until 2024-2025.
Army, USMC, Navy, Air Force and DISA each have their own spectrum tools and data layers; a joint solution requires governance that GAO (2021) and AOC (2026) say is still missing.

attractiveness.bull: 2026 shows real money moving from prototypes to production for low-cost spectrum sensors (REWSI ~$196M IDIQs, Hidden Level $100M OTA) and the Army has publicly re-platformed its EW planning stack onto the open TAK framework, creating a plugin ecosystem a small team can enter. Own-signature awareness (S2AS) is unclassified, urgent (Ukraine lessons) and heading to a rapid fielding decision; interference geolocation is dual-use with regulators and spectrum-sharing needs (GAO-26-107873). Venture investors are now funding the space (Distributed Spectrum $25M Series A, March 2025).
attractiveness.bear: The obvious sensor-network play already has funded, contracted leaders (Distributed Spectrum, Heaviside, RII, Hidden Level, Anduril Pulsar) and the Army just wrote nine-figure ceilings to two of them; the software/COP layer is being absorbed into government-owned TAK and DISA's EMBM-J, shrinking the room for a proprietary product; most high-value fusion requires classified emitter data and cleared people; and anything labeled EW/DF for military use is likely USML Category XI, which is a serious problem for a founding team with a non-U.S.-person co-founder. Ceilings are not revenue: REWSI and OTA figures are ceilings with unknown obligations.
attractiveness.verdict: Medium attractiveness overall; low for a hardware sensor-network startup entering in late 2026, medium for a narrowly scoped unclassified software wedge (own-signature awareness or interference geolocation delivered as a TAK plugin and sensor-agnostic fusion service), contingent on resolving export-control structure before writing any EW-specific code.

follow-on / limited fielding - Raven Claw laptop variant of EWPMT
strategy and oversight - DoD EMS Superiority Strategy; GAO-21-64 on EMSO governance; TLS-BCT prototype OTA (RECALL)
prototype award - Lockheed TLS-EAB prototype; STRATCOM creates JEMSOC; DISA releases cloud EMS visualization tool (Dec 2023)
re-plan - EWPMT RS3 task order competition cancelled, EWPMT-X TAK pilot; TLS-BCT funding realigned to manpack; DISA GEMSIS sustainment sources sought (Sept); EMBM RFI

sources sought and prototype testing - S2AS FY25 new start sources sought; S2AS in TiC exercises; division EW prototypes; Distributed Spectrum Series A (Mar); Epirus Gen II $43.5M (Jul); Army FY26 EMFP $9.1M request

production - REWSI call for solutions (Apr) then $99M and $96.9M production IDIQs (Aug 27, Sep 3); Hidden Level $100M OTA (Aug 5); GAO-26-107873 (Jun); AOC JEMSO CSA proposal (Feb); S2AS rapid fielding decision targeted Q2 FY26

market_stage.rationale: Sensors have crossed from prototype to production-type vehicles in 2026 (repeat orders not yet observable), while the planning/COP software layer is mid-transition (EWPMT-X pilot, S2AS rapid fielding decision pending) and the enterprise spectrum-management layer is in sustainment-plus-enhancement mode. That mix is Transitioning, not Mature.

proto_purgatory.notes: EWPMT ran ~10 years of capability drops (2014-2024) and ended with a cancelled follow-on and a re-host on TAK; TLS-BCT was restructured repeatedly; MFEW-AL is entering service roughly seven years after its prototype award. Distributed Spectrum's public traction is a series of sub-$10M awards. Counter-signal: in 2026 the Army broke purgatory for sensors by issuing production IDIQs within five months of a call for solutions, and DoD issued a $100M OTA to Hidden Level.
proto_purgatory.opportunity_or_warning: Both. Sensors are exiting purgatory (opportunity for sensor-agnostic software riding the newly bought fleet), but planning/COP software is where purgatory has been chronic (warning: a proprietary EMBM product risks repeating EWPMT's fate unless delivered as a TAK plugin the government can own and re-compete).

segments.what_it_does: The software layer between human commanders and fleets of uncrewed/autonomous platforms (air, ground, surface, undersea, launched effects, loitering munitions). It (1) exposes each vehicle's state and payload data to a controller/COP, (2) lets a human or an automated planner assign missions, tasks and rules of engagement to one or many heterogeneous vehicles (task allocation, route/behavior selection, human-on-the-loop approval), (3) coordinates collaborative behaviors between vehicles (relay, search, track, strike) including when links to the operator are degraded or denied, (4) manages fleet identity, health, airspace/waterspace deconfliction and blue-force tracking, and (5) publishes vehicle-derived tracks and sensor data into existing C2/fires systems (TAK, FAAD C2/IBCS, Maven, NGC2, Link 16). It sits above vehicle flight/autonomy stacks (PX4/AuterionOS, Hivemind/EdgeOS, Lattice on-vehicle, FANTOM Core) and below joint C2. In practice it is five sub-layers: on-vehicle mission autonomy; vehicle-to-controller protocol; ground/common control station; multi-vehicle orchestration/task allocation; and C2/COP integration.

sub_taxonomy.name: On-vehicle mission autonomy and collaborative behaviors
sub_taxonomy.note: Software running on the platform (Shield AI Hivemind/EdgeOS, Anduril Lattice on-vehicle, Auterion AuterionOS/Nemyx, Applied Intuition/EpiSci, government-owned SOCOM FANTOM Core, USAF A-GRA-conformant autonomy). Government increasingly asserts ownership of the reference architecture (A-GRA, FANTOM Core) while vendors supply behaviors. FACT (A-GRA, FANTOM Core from 2026 sources).

sub_taxonomy.name: Vehicle-to-controller interface protocols
sub_taxonomy.note: MAVLink (commercial small UAS, PX4/ArduPilot), STANAG 4586 (NATO UAS control interface, Levels of Interoperability 1-5), UMAA (Navy maritime DDS-based service architecture, PMS 406), IOP/JAUS (Army ground robots), UCI/OMS (USAF Open Mission Systems / Universal C2 Interface), Cursor-on-Target (TAK). Mandated open standards exist per domain but are inconsistently enforced across programs; commercial small-drone fleets largely arrive with vendor apps. INFERENCE.

sub_taxonomy.name: Control station / common controller
sub_taxonomy.note: Where the operator sits: vendor GCS apps (AeroVironment/Tomahawk Kinesis, Auterion Mission Control, Anduril Lattice UI), government efforts to own it (Navy Common Control System, NAVAIR PMA-263 Unmanned Common Controller sources sought, Army Universal Robotic Controller study, older BCT Common Controller). The recurring 15-year pattern of common-controller efforts without a universal fielded controller is the clearest proto-purgatory signal in this segment. FACT/INFERENCE.

sub_taxonomy.name: Multi-vehicle orchestration / mission-level tasking
sub_taxonomy.note: Vehicle-agnostic assignment and coordination of many heterogeneous systems: Anduril Lattice for Mission Autonomy (Replicator selection Nov 2024), Auterion Nemyx (multi-manufacturer swarm, launched Sept 2025), Shield AI multi-aircraft Hivemind for CCA, and the DIU/DAWG/Navy Autonomous Vehicle Orchestrator prize challenge (Jan 2026, up to $100M) explicitly seeking a vehicle-agnostic C2 layer. FACT.

sub_taxonomy.name: Integration into existing C2, fires and counter-UAS
sub_taxonomy.note: Publishing autonomy-derived tracks and accepting tasking from COP/fires/C-UAS systems: TAK/ATAK, FAAD C2 (Northrop) and its planned replacement by Lattice as common C-UAS C2 (JIATF-401, March 2026), IBCS, Maven Smart System, Army NGC2, Ukraine Delta as the reference model for a drone-fed kill web. FACT.

sub_taxonomy.name: Autonomy test, evaluation, simulation and data
sub_taxonomy.note: Simulation-based validation of collaborative behaviors, conformance to A-GRA/UMAA/IOP, flight-test data capture, and post-mission exploitation of vehicle logs for ML. Applied Intuition is the commercial reference; government T&E capacity is a known constraint. INFERENCE.

users.role: Joint/theater battle manager
users.what_they_do: Consumes autonomous-platform tracks and allocates autonomous mass to operational objectives (DAWG orchestration vision); rarely tasks individual vehicles directly.

current_architecture.description: Fragmented by domain and vendor. Small commercial drones use MAVLink/PX4-derived stacks with vendor apps; Army Group 2-3 UAS and launched effects use STANAG 4586-style GCS software from platform vendors plus emerging common controllers (Kinesis, Lattice); Navy uses UMAA on-vehicle services with CCS for operator control; Air Force CCA uses a government reference architecture (A-GRA) with vendor mission autonomy. Multi-vehicle orchestration is delivered mostly by Anduril Lattice (Replicator/DAWG, SOCOM, Army C-UAS), with Auterion Nemyx and Shield AI Hivemind as multi-vehicle alternatives, and the government now trying to procure a vehicle-agnostic orchestrator (AVO prize challenge). Integration to the COP is typically via TAK/CoT, Link 16/JREAP gateways, or vendor APIs. Human-on-the-loop remains the policy default; engagement approval flows through fires/C-UAS systems rather than the autonomy layer.

current_architecture.security_domain: Mixed: commercial small-UAS control at unclassified/CUI; Army/Navy program controllers at SECRET-capable enclaves; CCA and C-UAS C2 integrate into SECRET networks; on-vehicle autonomy code and behaviors are typically ITAR/CUI even when hardware is commercial. INFERENCE.
current_architecture.connectivity_dependency: High for human-on-the-loop tasking and video; vendors explicitly design for comms/GNSS-denied operation (Anduril Replicator selection language; Ukraine EW reality). Mesh radios and relay drones are common workarounds. FACT/INFERENCE.
current_architecture.what_breaks_when_disconnected: Operator loses vehicle state and video; re-tasking impossible unless behaviors are pre-delegated onboard; engagement approval chains stall; deconfliction and blue-force awareness of friendly drones degrade, raising fratricide risk with C-UAS effectors. INFERENCE.

technical_difficulty.summary: High. Real-time coordination of heterogeneous vehicles across radios with intermittent links, safety-critical engagement logic with human-on-the-loop, deterministic behavior under GNSS/comms denial, and integration with dozens of legacy protocols. Individual pieces (MAVLink control, mission planning UIs, CoT publishing) are commodity; the hard parts are certifiable multi-vehicle behaviors, DDIL-tolerant state synchronization, and trustworthy delegation of engagement authority.
required_expertise: distributed systems and consensus under partition
robotics/autonomy (behavior trees, task allocation, path planning)
tactical datalinks and mesh radio behavior
MAVLink/STANAG 4586/UMAA/CoT protocol engineering
safety assurance and T&E for autonomy (A-GRA/UMAA conformance)
cybersecurity and cross-domain data handling
HMI design for supervisory control
simulation and hardware-in-the-loop
technical_difficulty.hardest_problem: Vehicle-agnostic orchestration that survives denied links while keeping a human accountable for lethal effects, across vendors who each control their own autonomy stack and controller. The DIU/DAWG/Navy AVO prize challenge exists precisely because no fielded vehicle-agnostic layer has been accepted. INFERENCE
technical_difficulty.commodity_parts: MAVLink/PX4 control, basic GCS UIs, video streaming, CoT/TAK plugins, cloud mission logging, simulation with Gazebo/AirSim-style tools; Blue UAS-listed airframes and radios.

capital_intensity.assumptions: PoC: software-only orchestration or integration demo using COTS Blue UAS drones and MAVLink in simulation plus a few live vehicles; two founders plus 1-2 engineers for 6-9 months. Credible demo: participation in an Army/Navy/AUKUS experiment or a DIU/DAWG challenge with 5-20 vehicles from at least two vendors, rugged edge compute, mesh radios, safety case, travel and range costs, and early cleared/US-person hires. First production: ATO/CMMC/IL5 accreditation, ITAR compliance program, integration into Lattice/TAK/NGC2 or FAAD C2 successors, 24/7 support, and hardware kits for a battalion-scale fleet. Ranges are HYPOTHESIS calibrated on Auterion ($130M Series B to scale production) and typical defense software startups.

regulatory_access.prototype_with_commercial_unclassified_d: partly - MAVLink/PX4 fleets, Blue UAS hardware and simulated missions allow an unclassified prototype; realistic tasking doctrine, threat behaviors and datalink parameters are CUI/ITAR
regulatory_access.government_data_required: Not for PoC; needed for credible demo: unit CONOPS, radio configurations, C2 message formats (VMF/Link 16), and access to government reference architectures (A-GRA, FANTOM Core, UMAA specs are partly public via AUVSI).
regulatory_access.itar_ear: Military drone autonomy and C2 software is very likely ITAR-controlled (USML Cat VIII(h)/XI(d) technical data) or EAR 600-series; commercial PX4-based work may be EAR99 until specifically designed for military use. Needs specialist counsel; do not rely on this note.
regulatory_access.cui_likely: Yes as soon as integration with government C2 or program-specific behaviors begins; CMMC Level 2 likely required for DoD contracts handling CUI.
regulatory_access.classified_integration_eventually: Yes for CCA, C-UAS C2, Navy fleets and any fires integration; SECRET facility or partnering with a cleared prime/integrator required.
regulatory_access.cleared_personnel_at_mvp: Not required for PoC; at least one cleared US-person lead is practically required by the credible-demo stage.
regulatory_access.non_us_person_founder_note: An Indonesian founder who is not a US person cannot receive ITAR technical data without a DDTC license (deemed export), which typically excludes them from the autonomy behaviors, datalink and C2-integration code; a German founder who becomes a lawful permanent resident is a US person for ITAR and counts toward SBIR ownership. SBIR/STTR requires >50% ownership by US citizens or permanent residents; FOCI mitigation would be needed for a facility clearance if a non-US person holds significant ownership or control. Structure options (US-person majority, walled-off roles, EAR99 commercial line first) require specialist export-control and immigration counsel; no legal judgment is made here.

why_not_solved.explanation: Each platform vendor (AeroVironment, GA-ASI, Anduril, Shield AI, Auterion) ships its own controller and autonomy stack; the controller is where vendor lock and data ownership live, so incentives oppose a neutral orchestrator. Anduril's success has made Lattice the de facto common layer for several buyers, which is itself a proprietary answer.

Air (PEO Aviation, AFLCMC), maritime (PMS 406, NAVAIR), ground (PEO GCS), SOF (SOCOM), C-UAS (JIATF-401) and OSD (DIU/DAWG) each own standards and controllers; no single buyer can mandate one layer, hence parallel A-GRA, UMAA, IOP, FANTOM Core, STANAG 4586.

Cheap edge compute, mesh radios and mature open flight stacks (PX4/MAVLink) only enabled multi-vendor collaborative autonomy at scale around 2023-2025 (Nemyx Dec 2025 demo; CCA autonomy flight tests Feb 2026).

Lethal effects with delegated autonomy require safety cases, human-on-the-loop policy compliance (DoDD 3000.09) and airworthiness/range approvals; every vendor integration re-triggers T&E, slowing any universal layer.

Fielded C2 (FAAD C2, IBCS, TAK, Link 16, NGC2) and dozens of radios/waveforms must be bridged; each bridge is bespoke and CUI/classified, so open-source or commercial-only players cannot finish the last mile.

Partially: for C-UAS tactical C2 and CCA mission autonomy the government has picked production vendors (Anduril; Anduril/Shield AI/Collins). What remains unsolved is cross-service, cross-vendor orchestration and squad-to-battalion small-UAS fleet control and deconfliction.

attractiveness.bull: The FY2027 DAWG request ($54.6B) and Drone Dominance (200,000 drones by 2027) create unprecedented budget signal for software that orchestrates and integrates mass; the government is actively procuring vehicle-agnostic C2 (AVO challenge, UCC sources sought, FANTOM Core M2M APIs) and asserting open reference architectures, which lowers the moat around incumbents' controllers; integration, deconfliction and training tooling for the small-UAS long tail is fragmented and under-served.
attractiveness.bear: The core orchestration layer is being won by Anduril (Replicator/DAWG, SOCOM, Army enterprise agreement, CCA) with Shield AI and Auterion as scaled alternatives, all with hundreds of millions in capital and cleared workforces; the government's own reference architectures (A-GRA, FANTOM Core, UMAA) further commoditize the layer a startup would sell; ITAR/CUI make a mixed US/non-US founding team structurally constrained at exactly the code that matters; common-controller efforts have cycled for 15 years without production, a proto-purgatory warning; $250k buys a PoC only.
attractiveness.verdict: Medium-low for a direct orchestration or common-controller play; medium for narrow adjacent wedges (small-UAS fleet integration/deconfliction into unit C2, autonomy T&E/conformance tooling, autonomy data pipelines) that can be built commercially first and sold into or alongside Lattice/TAK/A-GRA ecosystems.

market_stage.rationale: Within ~5 years the segment moved from RFIs and standards to prototype awards (2024) and, by 2026, production-style awards for two sub-layers (C-UAS tactical C2, CCA mission autonomy). Cross-domain vehicle-agnostic orchestration remains at prize-challenge/prototype stage, and small-UAS fleet control is being fielded faster than the C2 layer around it. Hence Transitioning, not Mature.

proto_purgatory.notes: The common-controller sub-layer shows classic purgatory: BCT Common Controller (2010s), Navy CCS, Army URC study, PMA-263 UCC sources sought, ROS-M and IOP - repeated efforts, no universal fielded controller. Replicator itself was dissolved after ~2 years without delivering the promised mass and re-launched as DAWG with a new orchestrator challenge. By contrast, C-UAS C2 and CCA autonomy have reached production awards, showing purgatory is sub-layer-specific.
proto_purgatory.opportunity_or_warning: Warning for any startup whose product is the universal controller or orchestrator sold to the government as a program of record; opportunity for tooling that makes whichever controller wins interoperable, testable and trainable (adapters, conformance, deconfliction, data), sold to primes/integrators and units.

segments.what_it_does: The sustainment/logistics C2 layer converts transactional logistics records (requisitions, maintenance work orders, ammunition/fuel stock levels, personnel/medical status, cargo movements) into a time-relevant common operating picture and decision support for commanders and sustainers, and pushes resulting tasks back out (resupply missions, movement orders, maintenance priorities). It sits between enterprise ERPs and transportation systems (GCSS-Army, LMP, GCSS-MC, Navy ERP/NOSS, DLA EBS, USTRANSCOM IGC/GDSS) and operational C2/COP tools (CPCE, NGC2, Onebrief plans, JADC2 data fabrics). Core functions: data collection from ERPs, sensors and RFID/ITV feeds; fusion into logistics status and running estimates (days of supply, consumption forecasts, readiness rates); distribution and movement planning; predictive maintenance; and dissemination of sustainment orders. Its distinctive difficulty is that the source systems are centralized, connectivity-dependent business systems while the consumers operate at the tactical edge under DDIL conditions.

sub_taxonomy.name: Enterprise logistics ERPs and data warehouses
sub_taxonomy.note: GCSS-Army, LMP, AESIP hub, GFEBS, GCSS-MC, Navy ERP/NOSS (NOBLE), DLA EBS, Army LIW/LDAC. Transactional backbone, not C2; owned by PEO EIS, PEO MLB, DLA J6. Startups do not displace these; they read from them.

sub_taxonomy.name: Enterprise logistics analytics and data platforms
sub_taxonomy.note: Army Vantage / Army Data Platform (Palantir), Advana and USTRANSCOM Pegasus (CDAO/Booz Allen), Air Force BLADE (RECALL), Govini Ark. Readiness and supply-chain dashboards for headquarters; connectivity-dependent.

sub_taxonomy.name: Tactical sustainment COP and reporting
sub_taxonomy.note: LOGSTAT workflows, CPCE sustainment tools / Logistics Reporting Tool (RECALL), USMC CLC2S, Rune Technologies TyrOS (startup). Where the plan-versus-reality disconnect is most visible; DDIL-exposed.

sub_taxonomy.name: Movement, in-transit visibility and transportation C2
sub_taxonomy.note: USTRANSCOM IGC, GDSS, TC-AIMS II, RFID/ITV networks, Operation Turbo Fusion (2025), USTRANSCOM CSO AoI 001 ITV Modernization (May 2026). Joint-level, single dominant buyer (USTRANSCOM).

sub_taxonomy.name: Sustainment planning and estimation
sub_taxonomy.note: OPLOG Planner-style consumption estimation, JOPES/JPES TPFDD feasibility, fuel and ammunition planning, Onebrief planning integrations. Ties logistics reality to operational plans; eventually SIPR.

sub_taxonomy.note: C3 AI PANDA (Air Force RSO, RECALL), Uptake (Army pilots, RECALL), Army Precision Sustainment / predictive logistics (CL CFT portfolio), CBM+ sensors. Historically a SBIR/pilot-heavy sub-segment.

current_architecture.description: Service-siloed transactional ERPs feed enterprise data lakes and dashboards (Army Vantage/ADP, Advana/Pegasus, BLADE), while the tactical sustainment picture is assembled largely by staff from LOGSTAT reports, spreadsheets, email and voice, then re-entered into C2 tools (CPCE) or briefing slides. Transportation C2 is separate (IGC for ITV, GDSS for air mobility, TC-AIMS II for unit movement). Joint plans (JOPES/JPES TPFDD) are loosely coupled to actual stock and movement data. The Army's attempt to consolidate the ERPs (EBS-C) was effectively paused in May 2026 when the Army declined the second-year option, leaving the integration problem open and shifting emphasis to modernizing existing systems.

current_architecture.security_domain: Predominantly NIPR/CUI (IL4-IL5) for ERPs and readiness dashboards; SIPR for OPLAN-linked sustainment feasibility, theater and joint COPs, TPFDD and JLOC operations; some analytics mirrored to SIPR/JWICS (Advana - RECALL). Coalition sharing is ad hoc.
current_architecture.connectivity_dependency: High. ERPs are centralized and require reach-back; GCSS-Army disconnected operations are limited to tablet-based store-and-forward (RECALL). Enterprise dashboards (Vantage, Advana) are unusable without connectivity. Tactical reporting falls back to FM voice, email, JBC-P free text and spreadsheets.
current_architecture.what_breaks_when_disconnected: LOGSTATs revert to voice and Excel; requisitions queue and later collide; ITV goes dark between nodes; commanders lose days-of-supply and readiness visibility; on reconnect, duplicate or conflicting entries must be reconciled by hand; plan assumptions drift from reality for hours to days.

technical_difficulty.summary: Moderate core software difficulty, high integration difficulty. The algorithms (days-of-supply math, consumption factors, routing, forecasting) are well understood; the hard parts are (1) offline-first data synchronization and conflict resolution across intermittently connected nodes, (2) canonical data modeling across SAP/Oracle ERPs, DLMS transactions, RFID/ITV feeds and free-text LOGSTATs, (3) producing trustworthy fused status when sources disagree or are stale, and (4) meeting ATO/IL5 and eventually SIPR requirements while keeping a modern UX.
required_expertise: Offline-first distributed systems (CRDTs, store-and-forward, delta sync over low-bandwidth links)
Enterprise integration with SAP/Oracle and DLMS/EDI transaction standards
Data engineering and schema mapping / entity resolution
Sustainment doctrine (FM 4-0, ATP 4-90, OPLOG planning factors, LOGSTAT reporting)
DoD security engineering (NIST 800-171/CMMC, RMF ATO, IL4/IL5 hosting)
Frontend/HMI for staff workflows under stress
Light ML for demand forecasting and anomaly detection
technical_difficulty.hardest_problem: Bidirectional, trustworthy synchronization between the connectivity-dependent enterprise ERPs and edge nodes that must keep operating (and issuing requests) while disconnected, then reconciling without creating duplicate requisitions or corrupting the enterprise system of record.
technical_difficulty.commodity_parts: Dashboards, mapping, generic forecasting models, cloud hosting, mesh/satellite transport hardware (from others), RFID readers, LLM summarization of reports.

capital_intensity.assumptions: PoC: two founders, synthetic data conforming to public doctrine formats (LOGSTAT, OPLOG planning factors) and simulated GCSS-Army exports; no ATO. Credible demo: SBIR Phase I/II or OTA-funded, participation in a warfighter exercise or NGC2/Project Convergence-style event, CUI-capable environment, a GovCloud IL4/IL5 sandbox, one integration (e.g., GCSS-Army extract or CPCE/NGC2 API), 4-8 staff for 12-18 months. Production: ATO/IL5, CMMC Level 2, integration with AESIP/GCSS-Army via the program office, sustainment/helpdesk, possibly SIPR instance, 15-30 staff over 2-3 years. Government-funded R&D can offset a large share; the $250k founder capital covers PoC only.

regulatory_access.prototype_with_commercial_unclassified_d: partly - doctrine, forms, planning factors and exercise scenarios are public and allow a convincing synthetic PoC, but real GCSS-Army/LIW/IGC data is CUI and requires a government sponsor and data-use agreement.
regulatory_access.government_data_required: Yes for credibility beyond PoC: GCSS-Army/LMP extracts, LIW readiness data, ITV feeds, unit LOGSTATs; typically arranged through a sponsoring unit, CFT or program office under CUI handling rules.
regulatory_access.itar_ear: Generic logistics software is usually not ITAR-controlled, but maintenance/technical data about specific weapon systems and some military-critical logistics information can be export-controlled (ITAR or EAR/CUI export-controlled category). Needs specialist review before any non-US person touches the data or code paths handling it.
regulatory_access.cui_likely: Yes - nearly all real inputs are CUI (readiness, stock levels, unit locations); NIST SP 800-171/CMMC Level 2 will be required in contracts.
regulatory_access.classified_integration_eventually: Yes - theater/joint sustainment tied to OPLANs, TPFDD and JLOC operate on SIPR; a tactical-echelon product can stay unclassified longer than a joint planning product.
regulatory_access.cleared_personnel_at_mvp: Not required for an unclassified MVP; at least one cleared (Secret) engineer/founder becomes necessary for exercise integration and SIPR deployment; facility clearance needed for classified contracts.
regulatory_access.non_us_person_founder_note: Constraints to review with counsel, not legal conclusions: (1) SBIR/STTR eligibility requires the company to be more than 50% owned and controlled by US citizens or permanent residents - an Indonesian founder who is not a US person counts against this, so cap-table structure matters (the German founder's permanent residency would count once granted); (2) CUI handling and export-controlled technical data may restrict a non-US person's access to data and certain code, requiring a technology control plan; (3) security clearances require US citizenship, so the non-US founder cannot hold one; (4) significant foreign ownership/control can trigger FOCI mitigation requirements for cleared work; (5) many DoD program offices informally prefer all-US-person teams for logistics data access. A structure where the non-US-person founder leads commercial/product and stays segregated from CUI/export-controlled data is common but needs specialist legal review.

why_not_solved.explanation: Sustainment data lives in SAP and Oracle ERPs with decades of customization, DLMS transaction routing and service-specific schemas; every C2 integration is a bespoke, program-office-mediated project. The 2026 EBS-C retreat shows even the Army with a $1B-ceiling SI could not push consolidation through.

The ERP owner (PEO EIS/PEO MLB), the C2 owner (PEO C3T), the data owner (AMC/LDAC), the requirements owner (CL CFT/CASCOM/G-4) and the joint movement owner (USTRANSCOM) are different organizations with different budgets; no single buyer owns the plan-to-reality bridge.

Palantir Vantage/ADP and Advana are the sanctioned enterprise data layers; new entrants are expected to plug into them, and the Palantir EA makes extending the incumbent the path of least resistance for the Army.

Offline-first sync (CRDTs), cheap mesh/satellite links (Starlink-class), and modern open C2 data layers (NGC2) only matured 2022-2026, making a tactical sustainment product that survives DDIL practical now.

Tactical sustainment software is a small dollar market compared with fires/ISR C2; large integrators prioritize O&M task orders; VCs favored ISR, autonomy and fires. Result: few well-capitalized entrants (Rune is a rare exception).
Real readiness/stock data is CUI and controlled by AMC/LDAC, DLA and program offices; startups cannot train or validate without a sponsor, slowing iteration.
Plan-coupled sustainment (OPLAN feasibility, TPFDD) lives on SIPR, pushing the highest-value use cases behind clearance and facility barriers.

Predictive logistics/maintenance has cycled through SBIR and pilots (Uptake, SBIR performers) without a scaled tactical product; enterprise dashboards exist but the edge-to-enterprise loop remains manual - not for lack of trying but for lack of an owner and a survivable architecture.

attractiveness.bull: Real, documented, repeatedly acknowledged pain (2018 COP article, 2025 swivel-chair, 2026 ITV CSO, GAO Indo-Pacific reports); an unprecedented number of open procurement doors for software (Palantir EA, Onebrief and Govini enterprise IDIQs prove the Army will put commercial software on enterprise vehicles); NGC2 explicitly opens an integration layer where sustainment data has to land; the EBS-C collapse leaves an integration void that will be filled by middleware, not a new ERP; Rune's funding shows investors will back tactical logistics software; the core algorithms are unglamorous but tractable for a strong engineer; a small team can produce a credible exercise-ready prototype on SBIR money.
attractiveness.bear: Palantir (Vantage/ADP, EA) and Anduril/Lockheed (NGC2) sit exactly where a bridge product would live and can absorb the feature; Rune Technologies has a multi-year head start with ex-Marine founders; all valuable data is CUI and sponsor-gated; a non-US-person co-founder complicates SBIR eligibility and data access; the buyer is fragmented and slow; predictive-logistics sub-segment shows proto-purgatory; the total addressable market at tactical echelon is modest, so the realistic exit is acquisition by an integrator, not a standalone company; competing with SI incumbents on ERP integration is not viable for two students.
attractiveness.verdict: Medium attractiveness: a legitimate wedge exists at the enterprise-to-tactical sustainment status bridge and at plan-coupled consumption forecasting, but it is a narrow, integrator-dependent, sponsor-gated market where the founders' immigration profile and lack of operational credibility are real handicaps; pursue only with a uniformed sustainment co-founder/advisor and an NGC2/CL CFT sponsor.

market_stage.rationale: Enterprise analytics/planning software has crossed into production vehicles (Palantir EA, Govini and Onebrief IDIQs) while the tactical/ITV edge is still at the solicitation-and-prototype stage (TRANSCOM CSO May 2026, NGC2 prototypes) and the ERP consolidation attempt regressed in 2026. Mixed signals across sub-segments indicate a transitioning market: mature at enterprise data layer, prototyping at the edge, stagnant in predictive logistics point solutions.

proto_purgatory.notes: Predictive logistics/maintenance shows classic purgatory: Uptake Army pilots (~2019, RECALL), C3 AI PANDA enterprise contract with uneven fleet adoption (RECALL), multiple SBIR Phase I/II awards (Forward Edge-AI, Modus Operandi, PacMar, Navy blockchain logistics, USSF ASCN) without verified production transitions. Contested logistics CFT has produced demonstrations but no software program of record found. Counter-signal: planning/data platforms (Onebrief, Govini, Palantir) did escape purgatory via enterprise IDIQs and an EA in 2025-2026.
proto_purgatory.opportunity_or_warning: Warning for standalone predictive-analytics or blockchain point solutions; opportunity for workflow products that ride an existing enterprise vehicle (NGC2 ecosystem, Onebrief/Govini partner integrations, Palantir EA) and solve a staff workflow rather than promising AI insight.

candidate_gaps.title: Edge-to-enterprise sustainment status bridge (LOGSTAT-to-COP automation under DDIL)
candidate_gaps.problem_one_sentence: Battalion-to-division sustainment status (Class I/III/V, maintenance, medical) is still hand-assembled from GCSS-Army extracts, voice reports and spreadsheets and re-entered into C2 tools, so the commander's sustainment picture lags hours to a day and collapses when disconnected.
candidate_gaps.user: Battalion S4, BSB SPO, division G4/DSB staff; NGC2 users at 4th ID/25th ID; USMC CLE staff
candidate_gaps.current_workflow: 1) Company XO/1SG estimates or pulls GCSS-Army status when connected; 2) S4 fills LOGSTAT spreadsheet/DA form; 3) sends via email, JBC-P free text or FM voice; 4) BSB SPO consolidates by hand and computes days of supply; 5) G4 re-enters into CPCE, a sync matrix or PowerPoint; 6) commander briefs from slides; 7) on reconnect, requisitions submitted offline are re-keyed into GCSS-Army.
candidate_gaps.current_solution: CPCE sustainment widgets / Logistics Reporting Tool (RECALL), Vantage dashboards (enterprise, connectivity-dependent), CLC2S (USMC, web app), Rune TyrOS (early stage), and manual staff work.
candidate_gaps.failure_point: No offline-first, doctrinally structured sustainment ledger that syncs to both the ERP and the C2 data layer; duplicates and stale data on reconnect; no bidirectional link between plan and stock reality.

candidate_gaps.title: Multi-source in-transit visibility fusion for contested movement
candidate_gaps.problem_one_sentence: USTRANSCOM lacks near real-time, end-to-end ITV that fuses RFID, satellite trackers, carrier EDI and manifests into a trusted COP that survives contested and disconnected legs.
candidate_gaps.user: USTRANSCOM DDOC/Fusion Center, 618th AOC, theater distribution centers, TSC distribution management
candidate_gaps.current_workflow: 1) Cargo tagged (RFID/barcode) and manifested in service systems (TC-AIMS II etc.); 2) reads flow into IGC ITV server with gaps between nodes; 3) staff query IGC, carrier portals and email; 4) Pegasus/Advana analytics on aggregated, delayed data; 5) manual phone/email chasing for high-priority items.
candidate_gaps.current_solution: IGC ITV, GDSS, carrier EDI, Pegasus on Advana; Turbo Fusion trialed NADACS/mesh.
candidate_gaps.failure_point: Latency and gaps between tracking sources; no fusion of heterogeneous feeds; dependence on fixed RFID infrastructure; not designed for contested legs.

joint.research_caveat: Research channels were curtailed in this session: the shared WebSearch budget was exhausted after 14 successful queries (4 further queries refused), every WebFetch to .mil/.gov/news domains was blocked by the network egress proxy, and the Bigdata.com news index returned out-of-credits. Claims marked 'VERIFIED-SEARCH' rest on search-result snippets and URLs retrieved in this session; claims marked 'RECALL' rest on the analyst's prior knowledge (cutoff mid-2026) and could not be re-verified here. Treat RECALL items as MEDIUM confidence at best and re-verify against the cited primary sources before investment use.

organizations.name: Office of the Secretary of War / Office of the Secretary of Defense (Secretary and Deputy Secretary)
organizations.parent: Department of War (secondary title adopted Sept 2025; legal name remains Department of Defense)
organizations.portfolio: Department-wide acquisition transformation (Portfolio Acquisition Executives, Warfighting Acquisition System), software-acquisition-pathway-by-default policy, requirements reform, direction of flagship AI/C2 programs (Maven program-of-record memo, Advana transformation memo), unmanned-systems consolidation memo.
organizations.current_status_2026: VERIFIED-SEARCH: Budget justification documents for FY2026 and FY2027 are now hosted at comptroller.war.gov, evidencing the Department of War secondary designation. Secretary Pete Hegseth directed the Pentagon-wide acquisition reform (Nov 2025) that replaced PEOs with Portfolio Acquisition Executives in the Army (Nov 7, 2025) and the Air Force (17 portfolios, completed July 2026). Deputy Secretary Steve Feinberg signed the March 9, 2026 memo designating Maven Smart System a program of record and a Jan 12, 2026 Advana transformation memo. RECALL (not re-verified): Hegseth's March 6, 2025 memo 'Directing Modern Software Acquisition to Maximize Lethality' made the Software Acquisition Pathway the default for software and CSOs/OTs the default solicitation approach; an Aug 2025 memo terminated JCIDS in favor of a Requirements and Resourcing Alignment Board and a Mission Engineering and Integration Activity under R&E.
organizations.leader_title: Secretary of War/Defense (Pete Hegseth); Deputy Secretary (Steve Feinberg)
key_programs: Maven Smart System program of record (Mar 2026)
organizations.startup_relevance: Sets the rules of the road: commercial-first, OT/CSO-default, portfolio managers with budget-trade authority. A two-founder startup does not sell to OSD leadership directly; it benefits from the policy tailwind but must find a PAE, CDAO, DIU or COCOM sponsor.

organizations.name: Under Secretary of War/Defense for Acquisition and Sustainment
organizations.portfolio: Acquisition policy (DoDI 5000 series, Adaptive Acquisition Framework incl. Software Acquisition Pathway), OT policy, Defense Pricing and Contracting, industrial base, oversight of PAE construct across components.
organizations.current_status_2026: VERIFIED-SEARCH: The PAE construct is being implemented service-by-service under the Hegseth reform plan; Congress (FY2026 appropriations report language) endorsed the plan but urged workforce investment and expressed skepticism about broad budget flexibility. RECALL: USD(A&S) is Michael Duffey (confirmed 2025); verify.
organizations.leader_title: Under Secretary for Acquisition and Sustainment
key_programs: Adaptive Acquisition Framework / Software Acquisition Pathway
organizations.startup_relevance: Policy owner, not a buyer. Relevant for understanding that prototype OTs (10 USC 4022) with follow-on production OTs are the sanctioned fast path.

organizations.name: Under Secretary of War/Defense for Research and Engineering (Chief Technology Officer)
organizations.portfolio: Since Aug 2025 the parent of CDAO; parent of the Office of Strategic Capital (cto.mil/osc); DARPA reports through R&E; RECALL: also parent of the Mission Engineering and Integration Activity created in the 2025 requirements reform, and Emil Michael served as acting DIU director Aug 2025-Mar 2026.
organizations.current_status_2026: VERIFIED-SEARCH: CDAO authority transferred from the Deputy Secretary's office to USD(R&E) in Aug 2025; Feinberg gave Emil Michael 120 days (Aug 2025) to recommend a path for Advana and Maven; a Dec 2025 DefenseScoop report described R&E's plan to 'deliver AI at scale'. The March 2026 Maven memo directs R&E to assume authorizing-official responsibility for MSS from NGA.
organizations.leader_title: Under Secretary for Research and Engineering / CTO (Emil Michael)
organizations.startup_relevance: R&E now controls the department's AI/C2 software center of gravity (CDAO + Maven PoR). Entry is via CDAO vehicles (Tradewinds, CSOs) rather than R&E itself.

organizations.name: Chief Digital and Artificial Intelligence Office
organizations.parent: USD(R&E) since Aug 2025 (previously reported to the Deputy Secretary)
organizations.portfolio: Advana enterprise analytics; Maven Smart System Program Office (from NGA, 2026); Open DAGIR multivendor ecosystem (launched May 2024); Global Information Dominance Experiments (GIDE, ~90-day cadence); Tradewinds Solutions Marketplace; AI Rapid Capabilities Cell (RECALL: launched Dec 2024 with ~$100M); CJADC2 data-integration layer ('minimum viable capability' declared Feb 2024, RECALL).
organizations.current_status_2026: VERIFIED-SEARCH: Realigned under R&E Aug 2025. March 9, 2026 Feinberg memo makes MSS a program of record, moves MSS administration from NGA to a 'CDAO MSS Program Office' within 30 days, and moves all MSS contracts onto the existing Army Enterprise Agreement vehicle; components face an 'aggressive' transition timeline before FY2026 ends Sept 30, 2026. April 3, 2026 Feinberg directive sets AI-enabled decision-making via Maven as 'the cornerstone' for CJADC2. Tradewinds Revision 10 (May 1, 2026) accepts monthly submissions through May 2027. RECALL: Chief Digital and AI Officer Douglas Matty appointed April 2025; verify incumbent.
organizations.leader_title: Chief Digital and Artificial Intelligence Officer
organizations.startup_relevance: The single most relevant joint-level buyer for C2/ISR software. Two doors: Tradewinds (5-minute video, monthly, 'awardable' status usable by any DoD buyer) and Open DAGIR onboarding onto the Maven data environment (which in practice means integrating with Palantir's platform). Warning: 'awardable' is not a contract and Open DAGIR onboarding is not a purchase.

organizations.name: Department of War/Defense Chief Information Officer
organizations.portfolio: Cybersecurity and authorization policy (Software Fast Track / SWFT, cATO, SBOM requirements), zero trust strategy (target-level ZT by FY2027), DISA oversight, spectrum, C3 policy, Mission Partner Environment policy.
organizations.current_status_2026: VERIFIED-SEARCH: SWFT announced by memo May 2, 2025 (Katie Arrington, performing the duties of CIO), implemented June 1, 2025; vendor/industry sources report SWFT moved from pilot to an evolving requirement in Jan 2026 with contract language for cATO/reciprocity-eligible software expected late 2026 (MEDIUM; vendor-blog sourced). RECALL: Kirsten Davies nominated as CIO in 2025; verify confirmation and current incumbent.
organizations.startup_relevance: SWFT determines how fast a startup's software can be authorized: SBOMs, third-party assessment, continuous monitoring artifacts. A startup should design for SWFT/cATO evidence from day one; riding a platform with an existing ATO (Maven/Palantir FedStart, JWCC CSP enclaves) is the practical shortcut.
