organizations.name: Defense Innovation Unit
organizations.parent: Reports to the Secretary of Defense (direct report since 2023, RECALL); Emil Michael (USD R&E) served as acting director Aug 2025-Mar 2026 (RECALL)
organizations.portfolio: Commercial Solutions Opening (CSO HQ0845-20-S-C001 / HQ0034-20-9-DIU, Amendment 0001 effective Mar 13, 2026); prototype OTs with production follow-ons; absorbed NSIN and NSIC (fall 2024); Blue UAS list origin (vetting later moved out of DIU); DIU 3.0 (2023) refocus on scaling; 2026: portfolios being collapsed from seven to three priorities 'where speed, scale and lethality intersect'; designated primary commercial-industry liaison for the new DRPM-UxS unmanned portfolio (memo of Jun 29, 2026).
organizations.current_status_2026: VERIFIED-SEARCH: Owen West became DIU director Mar 2, 2026 vowing to 'narrow' investment priorities; July 2026 reporting describes collapsing seven portfolios into three and a focus on reducing 'cost per kill'; Sept 2026 Washington Technology describes DIU as the Pentagon's 'one door' for drone tech. The names of the three new priority areas were not captured in retrievable snippets: Public evidence insufficient.
organizations.startup_relevance: Historically the best joint-level door for commercial software with an existing product. 2026 narrowing toward autonomy/lethality means a pure C2/COP software startup must map to one of the three priorities (INFERENCE: autonomy and C2-for-autonomy likely remain in scope). DIU expects a working commercial product and a path to scale; a pre-product team is early for DIU.

organizations.name: National Security Innovation Network
organizations.portfolio: University- and early-stage-focused programs (hackathons, Starts, Propel, Foundry/Vector), problem-sourcing from military units; continues to run events under DIU (e.g., 'DIU Presents: Project G.I.' listed for Dec 31, 2025).
organizations.current_status_2026: VERIFIED-SEARCH: NSIN's work was fully incorporated into DIU in fall 2024 (DIU 3.0 plan had targeted Feb 2024); nsin.mil remains live and lists 2025 events under DIU branding.
organizations.leader_title: Program lead within DIU (title not verified)

procurement_pathways.how_it_works_here: DIU posts problem statements under its standing CSO; vendors submit a short solution brief, selected firms pitch, then submit a proposal; awards are prototype OTs (10 USC 4022) with a follow-on production OT available without re-competition if the prototype succeeds. Amendment 0001 (Mar 13, 2026) is the current baseline. In 2026 DIU is narrowing to three priorities and is the front door for the DRPM-UxS unmanned portfolio.
procurement_pathways.typical_award_size: RECALL: low single-digit $M to ~$15M prototype OTs; production follow-ons can reach tens/hundreds of $M (verify against GAO-25-106856).
procurement_pathways.timeline: RECALL: DIU targets 60-90 days from solicitation close to award; solicitation windows typically 2-4 weeks.

procurement_pathways.fit_for_two_founder_startup: MEDIUM-LOW at $250k: DIU wants an existing commercial product with demonstrated traction and the ability to deliver a prototype in months; a pre-product team should first build with SOCOM/NSIN/xTech-type doors and return to DIU with a product.

Needs specialist legal review.

procurement_pathways.fit_for_two_founder_startup: MEDIUM for the engineer-led team if eligible; non-dilutive and standard for university spinouts.
procurement_pathways.eligibility_notes: SBIR/STTR requires a for-profit U.S. small business more than 50% owned and controlled by U.S. citizens or permanent resident aliens (or by other such small businesses). With one founder expected to be a permanent resident and one non-U.S.-person founder, the cap table must keep majority ownership/control with U.S. persons; the SBIR/STTR Extension Act of 2022 also requires foreign-affiliation disclosures. Germany and Indonesia are not 'countries of concern', but the ownership test is binding. Needs specialist legal review; do not assume eligibility.

joint.how_a_startup_gets_in: Sequenced plan for a two-founder, $250k team at the joint/OSD level. (0) Legal pre-work before any submission: structure the cap table so U.S. persons hold >50% ownership and control if SBIR/STTR is wanted; get an export-control classification of the product (ITAR USML XI/XXI vs EAR) and a written plan for the non-U.S.-person founder's technical-data access; decide early whether to pursue a facility clearance (FOCI mitigation would be triggered) or to stay unclassified. (1) Register in SAM.gov and get a CAGE code; prepare an SBOM and SWFT-style assurance artifacts from the first build. (2) Month 1-3, credential cheaply: submit a 5-minute video to the CDAO Tradewinds Solutions Marketplace (monthly windows through May 2027) to obtain 'awardable' status; attend SOFWERX events and the next Small Business Boot Camp; enter NSIN/DIU early-stage programs to find a unit problem owner. (3) Month 3-9, find a funded user, not a policy office: PEO-SDA (SOCOM) CSO for a small prototype OT; CENTCOM REJTF/TF-59/TF-99 for an in-theater trial (contracted through DIU or SOCOM); a service-level door (AFWERX, xTech, Army NGC2 ecosystem, SpaceWERX) if the product maps there. (4) Month 6-12, position inside the platform reality: apply for Open DAGIR onboarding/third-party app status on the Maven data environment and Palantir's startup/ATO-inheritance program, since the 2026 Maven program-of-record decision makes 'app on Maven' the dominant joint route; alternatively subcontract to SAIC on JFN. (5) Month 9-18, scale via OT: convert a successful prototype into a DIU or SOCOM production OT, and pursue GIDE participation via the CDAO sponsor. (6) Avoid: DISA/JWCC/Thunderdome direct pursuit, OSC loans, and DARPA as a first revenue source. (7) Hedge: NATO DIANA/Bundeswehr routes for the German founder. Throughout, track the DIU three-priority narrowing (autonomy/lethality emphasis) and DRPM-UxS: a C2 product that controls or tasks unmanned systems has a clearer joint-level sponsor in 2026 than a generic staff COP.

army.research_run_caveat: This run executed 16 successful WebSearch queries before the session-wide search budget (200/200, shared across agents) was exhausted. Every WebFetch attempt (40+ URLs across army.mil, dvidshub.net, gao.gov, sam.gov, comptroller.war.gov, sbir.gov, diu.mil, usaspending.gov, congress.gov, defensescoop.com, breakingdefense.com, executivegov.com, lockheedmartin.com, anduril.com, palantir.com, wikipedia.org and others) was blocked by the network egress proxy, and the Bigdata.com news connector returned out-of-credits. All facts below therefore come from search-result snippets and titles, not from full-document reads. Fields marked 'Public evidence insufficient' were not retrievable in this run and must not be treated as absent in reality. Recommend a re-run with fetch access before investment-grade use.

organizations.name: Capability Program Executive Command and Control Information Network (formerly PEO C3T -> PEO C3N -> CPE C3N)
organizations.parent: Office of the Assistant Secretary of the Army for Acquisition, Logistics and Technology (ASA(ALT)), Army acquisition portfolio structure
organizations.portfolio: Tactical and enterprise 'unified network': communications networks, tactical radios, satellite systems, C2 hardware and software, NGC2 prototype OTAs, C2 Fix. Workforce >1,600 (per CPE C2IN careers page snippet). Headquartered at Aberdeen Proving Ground, MD.
organizations.current_status_2026: FACT: PEO C3T redesignated PEO C3N on 2024-10-09 after absorbing PEO EIS network portfolios in the Oct-2023 'PEO Optimization' (army.mil/article/280427; defensescoop 2024-10-09). FACT: PEO C3N restructured into 'Capability Program Executive Command, Control, Communications, and Network (CPE C3N)' in a Dec-2025 'major reorganization' tied to NGC2 (army.mil/article/289377; Army DCS G-6 X post). FACT (MEDIUM): by Feb-2026 the organization is styled 'Capability Program Executive Command and Control Information Network (CPE C2IN)' (BG Taylor bio PDF dated Feb 2026 on api.army.mil; DVIDS unit page CPEC2IN; peoc3n.army.mil/Careers/About-CPE-C2IN). INFERENCE: the C3N->C2IN rename occurred between Dec-2025 and Feb-2026; exact effective date not retrieved. Reorganized sub-offices confirmed by snippet: 'PM C2 Infrastructure' (Col. Stuart McMillan, DPM Jonathan D'Aprile) and 'PL C2 Enablers' (Douglas Burbey, deputy Lisa Bell; interoperability enablers, 24/7/365 support). NOT VERIFIED in this run: whether 'PM C2 Applications', 'PM C2 Data/AI', 'PM C2 Transport', 'PM Tactical Radios', 'PM Tactical Network', 'PM Mission Command' exist under those names after the reorg. PM Interoperability, Integration and Services (PM I2S, stood up 2020; Matthew Maier PM from 2021-01-29) was still issuing an INB2 solicitation under 'PEO C3N' branding; its post-reorg status is unverified.
organizations.leader_title: Capability Program Executive: Brig. Gen. Jack 'Shane' Taylor (took command June 2025); Acting Deputy CPE: Roni Ewing (as of Dec 2025)
key_programs: Next Generation Command and Control (NGC2) division prototypes (4th ID / Team Anduril; 25th ID / Team Lockheed Martin)
C2 Fix (bridge C2/network baseline, fielded from 2024)
Integrated Network Operations Battalion and Below (INB2) - PM I2S solicitation
Tactical radios, SATCOM, unified network transport (legacy ITN/WIN-T replacement)
organizations.startup_relevance: HIGH. This is the program office that awarded both NGC2 prototype OTAs and that owns the four NGC2 layers (applications, data, infrastructure, transport) into which the Army is consolidating C2 funding lines. Practical entry for a two-founder startup is as a team member/subcontractor to an NGC2 team lead (Anduril or Lockheed) or via xTech/SBIR topics sponsored by CPE C2IN, not as a prime on a $26M-$100M OTA.

programs.name: Next Generation Command and Control (NGC2)
programs.owner: CPE C2IN (formerly PEO C3N) as acquirer; requirement side formerly Army Futures Command / C2 CFT, now T2COM (INFERENCE)
programs.description: Mobile, four-layer C2 architecture (applications, data, infrastructure, transport) built on a common/integrated data layer with government-approved, non-proprietary APIs between layers, intended to give commanders faster decisions and replace legacy mission command systems. programs.status_2026: FACT: PC-C5 (March 2025, NTC) 'proof of principle' -> prototype OTAs to Team Anduril (4ID, July 2025) and Team Lockheed Martin (25ID, Sept 2025) -> division-scale exercises (Ivy Mass; Lightning Surge 1 Jan 2026) -> PC-C6 (July 2026, NTC) planned as division-scale force-on-force NGC2 validation and likely start of fielding decisions. FACT: Army intends to field NGC2 to all 11 divisions over five years at 2-3 divisions/year (Breaking Defense 2026-05). FACT: Congress capped FY2026 NGC2 funding with conditions (Federal News Network 2026-02; details not retrieved). FACT: GAO-26-108019 (2026) found the Army needs better schedule and cost information to support scaling the battlefield network (title only retrieved). procurement_pathways.how_it_works_here: Army prize competitions (xTechSearch, xTechPacific, xTechOverwatch, xTechIgnite, AI Grand Challenge, etc.) run by the Army SBIR|STTR / FUZE office: white paper -> pitch -> demo at Army events (e.g., HMI Summit Oct 2025 for xTechOverwatch); winners get cash, an accelerator, and an invitation to submit an Army SBIR Phase I or Direct-to-Phase-II proposal.
procurement_pathways.typical_award_size: $15K participation prizes up to ~$500K per winner; xTechOverwatch pool up to $1M; xTechPacific paid $450K in prizes plus 'millions in follow-on contracts'.
procurement_pathways.timeline: Competition cycles of roughly 3-6 months; follow-on SBIR adds 3-6+ months (INFERENCE).

procurement_pathways.fit_for_two_founder_startup: HIGH - designed for exactly this profile; low cost of entry, soldier feedback, and a bridge to SBIR money.
procurement_pathways.eligibility_notes: Most xTech competitions are limited to 'eligible small businesses' and follow-on SBIR requires SBIR eligibility (small, for-profit, >50% owned by U.S. citizens or permanent residents or by other eligible entities). With one founder not a U.S. person, cap-table structure needs specialist review; the German founder counts toward the U.S.-ownership test only once a permanent resident (INFERENCE from the SBIR Policy Directive; verify). Some xTech tracks (xTechInternational) are open to foreign firms.

procurement_pathways.how_it_works_here: Army FUZE SBIR|STTR: after the 2026 reauthorization, the Army posted five funding opportunities; Army SBIR uses open topics and Direct-to-Phase-II; program reportedly shifting to portfolio-level ('the whole vs. the parts') management (FNN 2026-05). ARL/DEVCOM also issue SBIR/STTR topics.

procurement_pathways.timeline: Topic open ~30-60 days; award 3-6 months after close (INFERENCE).

army.how_a_startup_gets_in: Sequenced, based on retrieved evidence: (1) Pick one NGC2 layer problem the Army has named - a warfighting-function app (fires, intel, logistics, protection) on the data layer, or a NetOps/DDIL tool for S6s - and build against open standards so it can sit on a common data layer. (2) Enter an Army xTech competition (xTechSearch for general, xTechPacific for INDOPACOM 'tyranny of distance', xTechOverwatch for autonomy/sensor networks) to get cash, soldier feedback and the SBIR Phase I / Direct-to-Phase-II invitation; resolve SBIR ownership eligibility with counsel first given one non-U.S.-person founder. (3) In parallel, approach the NGC2 team leads - Anduril (4th ID; members incl. Palantir, Microsoft, Govini, Striveworks, ICE, RII; Rune Technologies joined later) and Lockheed Martin (25th ID data layer) - to be onboarded as a team member for Ivy Sting/Ivy Mass or Lightning Surge events; this is the only demonstrated route by which small software firms have entered NGC2 to date. (4) Engage the Army Applications Laboratory and CPE C2IN/CPE ISW industry engagements at Aberdeen Proving Ground (technical exchange meeting schedule not verified this run) and watch sam.gov NGC2 notices (an NGC2 notice and an updated presolicitation exist but could not be read). (5) Target Project Convergence Capstone events (PC-C6 July 2026; next cycle 2027) via a team lead or T2COM RFI, since those are where fielding decisions are informed. (6) For ISR/PED products, pursue CPE ISW's HYDRA API and the Palantir TITAN ecosystem now that TITAN is in production. Caution: Congress capped FY2026 NGC2 funds and GAO flagged cost/schedule gaps, so scaling beyond two divisions is not yet contractually evidenced.

daf.research_run_caveat: TOOLING CAVEAT: In this run the session-wide WebSearch budget was already exhausted (200/200, shared across agents) before this agent's first query; every WebFetch to .mil/.gov/news/wikipedia domains was blocked by the network egress proxy; and the Bigdata.com news connector returned out-of-credits. All evidence below was therefore gathered through ~45 GitHub code-search queries against public repositories that mirror or excerpt primary documents (congressional hearing transcripts, DoD/USAF news-release indexes, DoD contract announcements, parsed RDT&E justification-book text, SAM.gov notice scrapes, earnings-call transcripts, NIH/SBA SBIR notices) plus defense-newsletter archives. Snippets were read, not full documents, so quotations are partial and dates were taken from the mirrors. Fields marked 'Public evidence insufficient' mean not retrievable in THIS run, not absent in reality. Several items rest on Tier-4 compilations (e.g., the '~$951M FY26 ABMS' figure and 'BG Jason Voorheis as PAE C3BM' both come from a hobbyist PEO-tracker repo) and are labeled LOW/MEDIUM accordingly. Recommend a re-run with live fetch access to af.mil, aflcmc.af.mil, sam.gov, comptroller.war.gov (FY26/FY27 DAF RDT&E Vol II PE 0604003F), gao.gov and defensescoop.com before investment-grade use.

procurement_pathways.how_it_works_here: AFWERX runs the DAF SBIR/STTR program with three avenues: Open Topic (any dual-use idea; a DAF customer memo/endorsement strongly improves Phase II odds), Specific Topics (published per cycle; e.g., DAF26BZ01-NV008 'AF Runtime Assured Autonomy', DAF26BX02-NV502 'Project ATOM Auth-on-the-Move' closing June 3, 2026 under DoW SBIR FY26 Release 1), and STRATFI/TACFI. Proposals submitted via DSIP (dodsbirsttr.mil). Program lapsed Oct 1, 2025 - Apr 13, 2026; reauthorized through FY2031 with per-company application caps and mandatory foreign-risk due diligence (S.3971).
procurement_pathways.typical_award_size: Phase I ~$75K (SBIR) / ~$110K (STTR) for Open Topic per Feb 2026 tracker (LOW); Phase II typically ~$1.25M-$1.8M (INFERENCE from DAF norms; 2026 caps not retrieved).
procurement_pathways.timeline: Cycles roughly three per year (26.1 closed Mar 6, 2026; 26.2 closed Apr 6, 2026; 26.3 expected Sept 2026 - Tier 4). Phase I 3-6 months; Phase II 12-24 months.

procurement_pathways.fit_for_two_founder_startup: BEST FIRST DOLLAR for the software-only C2 startup: low proposal burden, no past performance, AFWERX culturally receptive. But it funds R&D, not fielding, and 2026 rules add application caps and foreign-affiliation screening.
procurement_pathways.eligibility_notes: For-profit U.S. small business (<=500 employees), >50% owned and controlled by U.S. citizens or permanent residents (or by other eligible small businesses); PI's primary employment (>50%) with the firm; work performed in the U.S. The German founder qualifies once a permanent resident; an Indonesian non-U.S.-person founder can hold equity only within the minority share and must be disclosed under the 2026 foreign-risk due-diligence regime (denial triggers include 'foreign country of concern' ties - Indonesia is not one, but disclosure is mandatory). Needs SBA/SBIR counsel review.

procurement_pathways.how_it_works_here: DAF/AFWERX has historically offered Direct-to-Phase-II (D2P2) topics letting firms with demonstrated feasibility skip Phase I; status of D2P2 in the 26.x cycles after reauthorization: Public evidence insufficient (MEDIUM that it persists, since S.3971 references 'Direct to Phase II' applications in agency caps).
procurement_pathways.typical_award_size: Up to Phase II ceiling (~$1.25M-$1.8M, INFERENCE).
procurement_pathways.timeline: Per cycle; 6-9 months from submission to award (INFERENCE).
procurement_pathways.fit_for_two_founder_startup: MEDIUM: requires an existing product with a DAF customer willing to sign a memorandum.
procurement_pathways.eligibility_notes: Same as SBIR.

procurement_pathways.how_it_works_here: AFWERX bridge funding for companies with a Phase II award: TACFI ($375K-$1.7M) and STRATFI ($3M-$15M), each requiring matching funds from a DAF/DoW program office and/or private investors (roughly 1:1 government match with additional private match for STRATFI). Air Force-specific; no Army/Navy analog. Remained active during the FY26 SBIR lapse.

daf.how_a_startup_gets_in: Sequenced plan for a two-founder, ~$250k C2-software startup targeting the DAF in FY2026-27. STEP 0 (month 0-1, prerequisites): register in SAM.gov, get a CAGE, resolve SBIR eligibility now (>50% ownership by U.S. citizens/permanent residents; document the Indonesian founder's share and the German founder's status), start an Iron Bank/containerization plan, and adopt NIST 800-171 practices because every DAF door flows down CUI/CMMC clauses. STEP 1 (month 1-3, find the operator): pick one DAF problem with a named unit - the 752 OSS TOC-L pathfinder (Tinker), the 805th CTS/ShOC-N (Nellis), an AOC using KRADOS, or the ACC Point Defense Task Force - and get a written customer memo. Attend the next C3BM Engagement Day (last held Dec 18, 2025, ~1,500 registrants) and AFA Warfare Symposium/AFCEA events where PAE C3BM's ABMS, Kessel Run and ORT divisions brief. STEP 2 (month 2-6, first dollar): submit to the AFWERX SBIR Open Topic in cycle 26.3 (expected Sept 2026; reauthorized Apr 13, 2026) with the customer memo, OR submit a solution brief to the JADC2 CSO (FA8612-21-S-C001, open to Nov 9, 2026), the Kessel Run DevSecOps CSO (FA8730-22-S-C001, open to Nov 29, 2027) or the ACC CSO (FA4890-CSO-0001-24); list a containerized product on the P1SM CSO (FA8307-24-S-C001, open to Dec 29, 2026) for distribution. Send AFRL/RI a white paper against the open BAA or JADPACT II if the work is research-grade (FY27 white papers reportedly due Sept 2, 2026). STEP 3 (month 6-12, prove it in an exercise): use a CRADA under C3BM's JADC2 BAA to get interface access and get onto a ShOC-N experiment, Bamboo Eagle, Red Flag or the new 'Ringleader' series; the post-Epic Fury portable-C2 requirement (Aug 2026) is an explicit open lane. STEP 4 (month 12-24, bridge): convert Phase II into TACFI ($375K-$1.7M) or STRATFI ($3M-$15M) with matching funds from PAE C3BM or ACC and/or private investors; in parallel subcontract to an ABMS DI Consortium member (Northrop, L3Harris) or the CBC2/JFN primes (SAIC, Lockheed) so the product touches fielded interfaces. STEP 5 (month 18-36, scale): pursue a prototype OT with a production option through AFLCMC, a DIU-sponsored transition, or a task order under the DI Consortium IDIQ; watch for the rumored 'Megatron' JADC2 follow-on IDIQ (unverified) and for the FY27 DAF Battle Network lines. Throughout: the DAF is mid-reorganization (PEO->PAE Jan 2026; ICC shelved Dec 2025; Kessel Run folded into an AOC program office; wartime reprioritization after Epic Fury), so verify office symbols and points of contact on every solicitation before submitting.

navy.access_constraints_note: RESEARCH LIMITATION (read first): this session's WebSearch budget was already exhausted (200/200) by sibling agents before this agent ran, and the egress proxy blocked WebFetch to every domain tried (navy.mil, navwar.navy.mil, peoc4i.navy.mil, marcorsyscom.marines.mil, gao.gov, dvidshub.net, navysbir.com, defensescoop.com, breakingdefense.com, wikipedia, duckduckgo, bing). Bigdata.com was out of credits. The only working external channel was GitHub code search (text fragments only; file reads were denied outside the user's repo). Findings therefore rest on (a) GitHub-mirrored copies of official texts (an Engineering Duty Officer study guide dated 2026-06-05 that cites navy.mil/navwar.navy.mil/DVIDS/peoc4i.navy.mil URLs with publication dates; a MARADMIN/MCO citation portal; NAVADMIN and DoD budget-table mirrors), (b) sibling agents' JSON files in this scratchpad, and (c) clearly labeled general knowledge. Every URL below should be re-verified at the primary source before investment use; confidence levels reflect this indirection.

procurement_pathways.how_it_works_here: Navy SBIR/STTR is run by ONR with topics sponsored by NAVWAR, NAVSEA, NAVAIR, MCSC and ONR; proposals go through the DoD DSIP portal on the DoD-wide BAA cycle (25.2 cycle: pre-release 2 Apr 2025, open 23 Apr, close 21 May 2025). Phase II awards in the low seven figures (example: Navy SBIR Phase II N68335-23-C-0585, $1,658,607, NAVAIR, 2023 - sibling B02). CAC2S AI-assistant topic was awarded to Leverege.
procurement_pathways.typical_award_size: Phase I ~$140K-$250K; Phase II ~$1M-$2M (general Navy norms; verify current BAA)
procurement_pathways.timeline: Three cycles per year; ~6 months from topic release to Phase I award; Phase II 24 months

recent_examples.what: AI-based C2 Digital Assistant for CAC2S (Marine Corps SBIR)
Navy SBIR Phase II N68335-23-C-0585 (NAVAIR Lakehurst)

procurement_pathways.fit_for_two_founder_startup: Good on paper for a U.S.-owned team; slow (6-9 months to first dollar), and Navy C2 topics often presume prior program knowledge.

navy.how_a_startup_gets_in: Sequenced plan grounded in the offices/events found (all dates should be re-verified at source). (1) Months 0-3, no-cost discovery: register in SAM; email the NAVWAR Small Business Office (navwarsbo.fct@navy.mil) and NIWC Pacific/Atlantic OSBP; attend a NavalX Tech Bridge outreach (Capital Tech Bridge/Carderock, Palmetto/Charleston, Pacific/San Diego) and the PEO Digital PMW 270 Quarterly Industry Engagement; join the IWRP consortium and attend its quarterly industry day to see NIWC Atlantic requirements (e.g., NEWT-style edge terminals). (2) Months 3-9, demonstrate: enter a NavalX/Tech Bridge prize challenge or the NICE CSO/ANTX cycle with a working software prototype; pursue a NIWC CRADA to get the product into a lab; if U.S.-ownership rules can be met, submit to the next Navy SBIR cycle on a NAVWAR- or MCSC-sponsored C2/ISR topic (25.2 timing: pre-release early April, close late May). (3) Months 6-18, first dollars: pitch an IWRP prototype OT against a NIWC requirement; respond to OTA-eligible sources-sought notices (e.g., 'Navy Collaborative' 2026-08-31, TacMobile Inc 3); for Marine edge software, engage MCWL (small FAR RDT&E awards like the $3.2M Farsight contract) and the Marine Corps Software Factory/MCTSSA as a TAK-plugin partner, clearing DC I governance early if any AI is involved (MARADMIN 018/26). (4) Months 12-24, path to Overmatch: containerize and push through the Overmatch Software Armory/RAISE 2.0 gates (SAST, SBOM, secrets, container scan, DAST, ISSM review, signing, registry) to inherit the platform ATO; seek a Navy-sponsored DIU CSO or Open DAGIR onboarding through CDAO; or subcontract to an integrator with Overmatch access. (5) Structural prerequisites to resolve in parallel with counsel: SBIR/STTR U.S.-ownership thresholds versus a German permanent-resident founder and an Indonesian non-U.S. founder; FOCI mitigation and facility clearance if any classified integration is required (Overmatch is largely Secret); ITAR/EAR classification of the product; CMMC readiness for CUI. Signals to watch: PAE Mission Systems and PAE Marine Corps industry days (new in 2026), MUSV-style PAE marketplaces spreading to mission systems, and the FY2027 justification books for Overmatch/CANES/CAC2S lines.

navy.saturation_statement: Not saturated. Coverage is strong on 2026 organizational structure (PAE reorganization of Mar-May 2026, DRPM Overmatch, PAE Marine Corps, DC I governance) because a well-sourced mirror of official releases was reachable, and adequate on pathways (IWRP, NICE CSO, NavalX, SBIR, MCWL, MCSWF). Coverage is weak on: current NAVWAR, PEO C4I and PEO Digital leaders; FY2026/FY2027 program-element dollar values for Overmatch, CANES, ADNS, DCGS-N, MCEN and CAC2S; named Overmatch vendors and any obligated contract values; NIWC CRADA and ANTX 2025-2026 specifics; Navy SBIR 26.x C2 topics; Aegis/ICS 2026 software contracting. Every item marked 'Public evidence insufficient' is a direct consequence of the blocked web access described in access_constraints_note, not evidence of absence. A follow-up pass with working WebSearch/WebFetch should prioritize comptroller.defense.gov FY2027 RDT&E N and PMC justification books, peoc4i.navy.mil leadership/tear-sheet pages, navwar.navy.mil leadership, sam.gov IWRP/NICE/PMW 270 notices, and the GAO-25-106454 Defense Command and Control report.

organizations.name: United States Space Force
organizations.portfolio: Organize, train and equip space forces; owns the RDT&E Space Force, Procurement Space Force and O&M Space Force appropriations. Provides forces to USSPACECOM and other combatant commands through service components (e.g., Space Forces-Space).
organizations.current_status_2026: FACT: Active. FY27 request sharply increases Space Force RDT&E (reported ~$38.4B, +159%, driven by Golden Dome and the new Space Data Network; Tier 3/4 reporting, Apr 2026). 2026 acquisition overhaul replaced program executive offices with nine Portfolio Acquisition Executives (PAEs) (DefenseScoop 2026-03-18; SpaceNews / Air & Space Forces mid-2026).
organizations.leader_title: Chief of Space Operations (CSO); Secretary of the Air Force is the civilian head. Space acquisition executive is the Assistant Secretary of the Air Force for Space Acquisition and Integration (SAF/SQ).
organizations.startup_relevance: The service is the budget owner; startups never contract with 'the Space Force' directly but with SSC/SDA/Space RCO/SpaceWERX contracting activities under the PAEs.

organizations.name: Office of the Assistant Secretary of the Air Force for Space Acquisition and Integration
organizations.portfolio: Service Acquisition Executive for space; approves acquisition strategies, milestone decisions, and (in 2026) the sorting of programs into PAE portfolios. Ainsworth (title not re-verified this session) told reporters in May 2026 that DAF was 'still working' to sort space programs into portfolios.
organizations.current_status_2026: FACT: Active; overseeing the PAE transition. INFERENCE: Because ~90-92% of contracting authority was reportedly delegated to PAEs, SAF/SQ is less a day-to-day gate for small prototype awards than before.
organizations.leader_title: Assistant Secretary of the Air Force (Space Acquisition and Integration) / acting officials in 2025-2026 (name not re-verified this session)
organizations.startup_relevance: Indirect: sets policy (e.g., commercial-first guidance, CSO usage) but is not a contracting office.

organizations.name: Space Systems Command
organizations.portfolio: Principal acquisition field command (Los Angeles AFB, CA) for satellites, ground systems, launch and C2/BMC3 software. Historically organized as five PEOs (Assured Access to Space; BMC3; Space Domain Awareness & Combat Power; MilComm & PNT; Space Sensing) plus System Deltas paired with SpOC Integrated Mission Deltas.
organizations.current_status_2026: FACT: In 2026 the Space Force replaced PEOs with nine PAEs: infrastructure; BMC3 and space intelligence (BMC3I); SATCOM and PNT; missile warning and tracking; space-based sensing and targeting; space access; electromagnetic warfare and cyber; space combat power; advanced capabilities. Final three PAEs were to stand up in the 'June-ish' 2026 timeframe (Breaking Defense 2026-04). SDA and Space RCO continue to exist but sit under the applicable PAE.
organizations.leader_title: Commander, Space Systems Command (Lieutenant General); PAEs are civilian SES or general-officer portfolio executives
key_programs: Space Data Network (portfolio assignment not verified)
organizations.startup_relevance: Primary buyer of C2/SDA software. Uses Commercial Solutions Openings (CSOs), OTAs (Space Enterprise Consortium), SBIR Phase III and FAR contracts. Runs a Commercial Space Office ('Front Door') for industry entry.

organizations.name: Portfolio Acquisition Executive for Battle Management, Command, Control, Communications and Space Intelligence
organizations.portfolio: Space command and control (ATLAS/Space C2), Kronos family of systems (C2, battle management, space intelligence), Unified Data Library, Warp Core data services, space-domain-awareness data/network modernization (SDANet), and related BMC3 ground software. SSC's public BMC3I page and fact sheet describe the mission.
organizations.current_status_2026: FACT: Shannon Pallone, previously PEO for BMC3I, is now the permanent PAE for BMC3I (SSC leadership page; Breaking Defense 2026-05). FACT: 'Space Intelligence' was added to the portfolio name (BMC3 -> BMC3I) before the 2026 PAE conversion (SSC program office page).
organizations.startup_relevance: The single most relevant office for a C2/SDA software startup: it ran the Kronos CSO whose first awards (Apr 2026) were sub-$1.5M prototypes to a small firm (MapLarge) and a large one (Leidos), and later added True Anomaly's Mosaic.

organizations.name: Portfolio Acquisition Executive for Missile Warning and Tracking
organizations.parent: Space Systems Command / Space Force acquisition enterprise
organizations.portfolio: Missile warning/tracking constellations including SDA's Tracking Layer and legacy/next-gen OPIR elements; SDA director Gurpartap Sandhoo was appointed PAE for missile warning and tracking (2026).
organizations.current_status_2026: FACT: Newly created in 2026 PAE overhaul; the SDA director dual-hats as PAE (ExecutiveGov / SpaceNews 2026). HYPOTHESIS: SDA's institutional identity may be absorbed into this PAE over time (National Defense Magazine 2026-08-03 discusses 'potential dissolution').
organizations.leader_title: Portfolio Acquisition Executive (Gurpartap Sandhoo, also Director SDA)
organizations.startup_relevance: Sensor-heavy portfolio; software openings are mainly BMC3/mission processing via SDA BAAs rather than direct C2 software buys.

organizations.name: Space Development Agency
organizations.parent: U.S. Space Force (since Oct 2022); in 2026 aligned under the applicable PAE
organizations.portfolio: Proliferated Warfighter Space Architecture (PWSA): Transport Layer (Tranche 0/1/2 launched or in production), Tracking Layer (Tranche 3 awarded Dec 2025), BMC3 layer (on-orbit compute plus BMC3 Application Factory run by SAIC), ground/ops centers. Uses OTAs and BAAs heavily.
organizations.current_status_2026: FACT: Tranche 3 Transport Layer was not funded in the FY27 request; requirements 'rolled into' the new Space Data Network backbone (DefenseScoop 2026-04-28; Breaking Defense 2026-04). FACT: SDA continues to exist under a PAE (Breaking Defense 2026-04). HYPOTHESIS (Tier 3, 2026-08-03): SDA could be dissolved as its functions migrate to PAEs; confidence LOW on timing.
organizations.leader_title: Director, SDA (Gurpartap Sandhoo, dual-hatted PAE MW&T)
organizations.startup_relevance: Historically the most open Space Force buyer of containerized mission software (BMC3 apps BAA). Transport-layer prime opportunities are now closed for startups; app-layer and ground-processing openings remain but are shrinking with T3 transport cancellation.

organizations.name: Space Rapid Capabilities Office
organizations.parent: U.S. Space Force (Kirtland AFB, NM); in 2026 under applicable PAE
organizations.portfolio: Rapid, often classified, space combat capabilities and the Rapid Resilient Command and Control (R2C2) cloud-based satellite C2 ground system for dynamic space operations.
organizations.current_status_2026: FACT: Continues to exist under a PAE after 2026 overhaul (Breaking Defense 2026-04). R2C2 IDIQ (est. $1B ceiling, 5-7 years) awarded June 2024 to 20 small businesses; first $12M in delivery orders Sept 26, 2024 (up to $600K each). DefenseScoop (2025-03-06) reported challenges scaling R2C2.
organizations.startup_relevance: R2C2 is small-business reserved (FACT) and agile/DevSecOps oriented; however the 20-vendor pool is closed unless an on-ramp is issued (not found this session). Anduril/Palantir are NOT R2C2 awardees (they are not small businesses); their Space Force C2-adjacent work is SDANet (Anduril) and Warp Core (Palantir).

organizations.name: SpaceWERX
organizations.parent: AFWERX (Air Force Research Laboratory) / Space Force innovation arm
organizations.portfolio: SBIR/STTR open topics, Direct-to-Phase-II, STRATFI/TACFI bridge funding, Orbital Prime (ISAM, $141M seeded since 2023), Tactically Responsive Space (TacRS) challenge with Space Safari, mission-focused cohorts tied to PAE/COCOM priorities.
organizations.current_status_2026: FACT: 2026 STRATFI cycle totaled $562.5M (SpaceWERX + program office + private capital; $245M private match) per Payload. FACT: Gravitics received a $60M STRATFI (PY 2025.1) for a TacRS orbital carrier (SpaceNews / Gravitics).
organizations.startup_relevance: Most realistic first-dollar path for a two-founder company IF SBIR ownership rules are met; program-office matching for STRATFI requires a sponsoring PAE customer.

organizations.name: SSC Commercial Space Office ('Front Door')
organizations.portfolio: Industry entry point for SSC; manages commercial integration efforts including the Commercial Augmentation Space Reserve (CASR) and, historically, Tactical Surveillance, Reconnaissance and Tracking (TacSRT) commercial data buys via the Global Data Marketplace (RECALL - not re-verified this session).
organizations.current_status_2026: FACT: CASR is moving out of pilot with next contracts planned in 2026 (Air & Space Forces Magazine). RECALL (MEDIUM): COMSO 'Front Door' remains the advertised submission portal for unsolicited capability briefs.
organizations.startup_relevance: Low-cost intake channel: submit a capability brief, get routed to a PAE; also the office that runs commercial-data purchase pilots where a data/analytics startup can sell directly.

organizations.name: Space Operations Command
organizations.parent: U.S. Space Force (field command, Peterson SFB, CO)
organizations.portfolio: Generates and presents space forces; Deltas include Delta 2 (space domain awareness; 18th/19th Space Defense Squadrons), Delta 3 (EW), Delta 4 (missile warning), Delta 5 (C2 / operations center support), Delta 6 (cyber and network ops), Delta 7 (ISR), Delta 8 (SATCOM/PNT), Delta 9 (orbital warfare), Delta 15 (NSDC support). Hosts the Joint Commercial Operations (JCO) cell that buys commercial SDA data on 4-6 week rolling contracts.
organizations.current_status_2026: FACT: In Sept 2025 SpOC explored reorganizing the commercial cell to push commercial monitoring data into operations (Breaking Defense 2025-09). RECALL (MEDIUM): Integrated Mission Deltas pair SpOC deltas with SSC System Deltas so operators and acquirers sit under one commander for sustainment.
organizations.startup_relevance: Source of operator pull; JCO rolling contracts are the fastest known direct-sale path for SDA data/analytics; delta-level CRADAs and user feedback are how requirements form.

organizations.name: Space Forces-Space
organizations.parent: U.S. Space Force service component to USSPACECOM (Vandenberg SFB, CA)
organizations.portfolio: Operates the Combined Space Operations Center (CSpOC) and, with USSPACECOM, the National Space Defense Center (NSDC); primary operational users of the space COP, ATLAS/SPADOC catalog, and Kronos battle-management tools. RECALL (MEDIUM): Joint Task Force-Space Defense functions were consolidated into S4S/NSDC around 2024-2025.
organizations.current_status_2026: FACT (Tier 3): S4S is the operational sponsor cited in Kronos and ATLAS coverage; Space Operations Command prepared a new shared domain-awareness tool for operators in late 2024 (Defense News 2024-12-23).
organizations.startup_relevance: Operational sponsor whose gaps drive SSC BMC3I CSOs; startups reach them via SSC industry days, JCO, and TEMs rather than direct sales.

organizations.name: United States Space Command
organizations.portfolio: Operational requirements for space domain awareness, space C2, and network modernization; e.g., mandated full deployment of the modernized Space Surveillance Network communications (SDANet) by end of 2026.
organizations.current_status_2026: FACT (Tier 3): USSPACECOM mandate on SDANet deployment by end-2026 reported May 2026. RECALL (LOW): HQ relocation to Huntsville, AL was ordered in 2025; status of move not verified this session.
organizations.startup_relevance: Requirement owner, not a buyer; influences urgency (e.g., ATLAS/SPADOC decommission, Kronos MVCs).

organizations.name: National Space Intelligence Center (Space Delta 18)
organizations.portfolio: Space intelligence production; its analysts are the intended users of Kronos 'space intelligence' capabilities (continuous adversary monitoring, multi-source data integration).
organizations.current_status_2026: RECALL (MEDIUM): Established June 2022; active. INFERENCE: Kronos's 'space intelligence' segment (SSC newsroom 2026-04) ties NSIC/Delta 7 analysts to BMC3I acquisition.
organizations.startup_relevance: Highly classified user base; startups without cleared staff can only reach it through cleared primes or unclassified data-layer work.

organizations.name: Space Training and Readiness Command
organizations.portfolio: Training, test (Delta 12), ranges/aggressors (Delta 11), doctrine; users of mission rehearsal and simulation tools.
organizations.current_status_2026: FACT (Tier 3): Slingshot Aerospace won a $69.2M Space Force contract (July 2026) for MENTAT, an AI mission-rehearsal platform; contracting office not verified.
key_programs: National Space Test and Training Complex
organizations.startup_relevance: Simulation/digital-twin and training software is a lower-classification entry point; Slingshot precedent shows scale is possible.

organizations.name: Air Force Research Laboratory Space Vehicles Directorate
organizations.parent: AFRL (Kirtland AFB, NM); supports Space Force S&T
organizations.portfolio: Space S&T including autonomy, SDA algorithms, resilient comms; funded under PE 1206310SF (Space Science and Technology R&D, $314M requested FY27 per Air & Space Forces Magazine).

programs.name: Space Command and Control (Space C2) / Advanced Tracking and Launch Analysis System (ATLAS) - 'Kobayashi Maru'
programs.owner: SSC PAE BMC3I (Space C2 software factory in Colorado Springs; program restructured FY2022)
programs.description: Replaces the 1980s Space Defense Operations Center (SPADOC) for catalog maintenance, conjunction/launch analysis and the space COP. ATLAS is the SPADOC-replacement baseline; the broader Space C2 effort delivers apps for operators at CSpOC/NSDC/Delta 2.
programs.status_2026: FACT: ATLAS achieved operational acceptance late 2025, but DOT&E's FY25 report (reported 2026-03) found it lacks minimum viable capability to decommission SPADOC, citing 'deficiencies consistent with system immaturity'. Officials plan SPADOC decommission by end of 2026 contingent on L3Harris 'astrometric tools' under a $90M contract awarded March 2025. Kronos was split out of Space C2 in May 2025.
vendors: Various software-factory support contractors (public evidence insufficient)

contract_evidence.vehicle: Contract for follow-on astrometric tools (vehicle type not verified)
contract_evidence.prototype_or_production: Production/sustainment enhancement of an operational system

budget.pe_number_or_line: Space Force RDT&E 'Space Command and Control' line historically (PE number not re-verified this session; verify in FY27 RDT&E Space Force J-book Vol 3). Related: PE 1206425SF Space Situation Awareness Systems (RECALL MEDIUM).
budget.fy27_request: Public evidence insufficient this session (FY27 J-books posted at af.mil SAF/FM Budget-2027 page).

programs.third_party_software_openness: INFERENCE: Space C2 was conceived as an app-based ecosystem with a software factory, and the 2025 split of Kronos (procured via CSO) indicates the government is deliberately opening the battle-management/intel layer to commercial software; ATLAS itself remains L3Harris-integrated. Confidence MEDIUM.

A 'Kronos Family of Systems Commercial Solutions Opening' is posted on sam.gov (via third-party mirror).

procurement_pathways.how_it_works_here: SpaceWERX (AFWERX) runs Space Force SBIR/STTR open topics and mission-focused cohorts; Phase I feasibility, Phase II prototype, Phase III sole-source follow-on by any DoD office (Bluestaq's UDL is the canonical Phase III success).
procurement_pathways.typical_award_size: Phase I roughly $75K-$150K; Phase II roughly $0.75M-$1.8M (RECALL MEDIUM)
procurement_pathways.timeline: Open-topic cycles 2-3x/year; ~3-6 months from submission to Phase I award; Phase II 12-24 months

UDL grew from 2019 SBIR to a $280M Phase III-type contract

procurement_pathways.fit_for_two_founder_startup: Best first-dollar path if eligible; software topics welcomed; requires a Space Force customer memo for Phase II open topics.
procurement_pathways.eligibility_notes: SBIR requires a for-profit US small business more than 50% owned and controlled by US citizens or permanent residents (a German permanent resident counts; an Indonesian non-US-person co-founder holding a large stake could break the >50% test); principal place of business and work in the US. Needs specialist review of the cap table before applying.

procurement_pathways.how_it_works_here: AFWERX/SpaceWERX D2P2 open topics allow skipping Phase I with evidence of feasibility (e.g., a working product with commercial traction).

procurement_pathways.how_it_works_here: SpaceWERX matches SBIR funds with program-office (PAE) money and private capital to bridge Phase II to production; 2026 cycle totaled $562.5M with $245M private match.

space.how_a_startup_gets_in: Sequenced plan for a two-founder, ~$250K company targeting Space Force C2/SDA software. (0) Legal first: get a cap-table and export-control review before anything else - SBIR requires >50% US-citizen/permanent-resident ownership (German LPR counts; Indonesian non-US-person stake must be sized accordingly), and space C2/SDA software can be ITAR-controlled; classified Kronos/NSDC work needs facility clearance and FOCI mitigation (specialist review, no legal judgment here). (1) Build on the Unified Data Library: register for UDL API access (unifieddatalibrary.com), ingest public/commercial catalog data and ship an unclassified analytic (e.g., maneuver detection, conjunction triage, sensor-tasking optimization) that demonstrates value in weeks; this is the integration layer every SSC/SpOC program uses. (2) Get operator pull: attend SSC BMC3I industry days and technical exchange meetings (SSC Space Industry Days, AFCEA LA), submit a capability brief through the SSC Commercial Space Office 'Front Door', and seek a no-cost CRADA or demo with Space Delta 2, the JCO cell, or AFRL/RV. (3) First dollars via SpaceWERX: submit to the next SpaceWERX/AFWERX open topic or 2026 challenge (afwerxchallenge.com/spacewerx26), ideally Direct-to-Phase-II with a customer memo from a delta or the BMC3I office; alternatively DIU Space CSO if SBIR-ineligible. (4) In parallel, sell commercially: onboard as a JCO commercial-data/analytics provider (4-6 week rolling competitions) and position for the 2026 CASR contract batch; consider allied buyers (Australia's classified UDL, German Weltraumkommando/GSSAC) where the German founder helps. (5) Target the Kronos Family of Systems CSO for a $0.5M-$1.5M prototype OT - the only Space Force C2 program in 2026 that awarded sub-$1M prototypes to small commercial software vendors - and/or the SDA BMC3 Battle Management mission-applications BAA while it lasts. (6) Team with primes and pool members: subcontract to Leidos/True Anomaly (Kronos), L3Harris (ATLAS), SAIC (BMC3 App Factory), Bluestaq (UDL), or an R2C2 small-business pool member; join the Space Enterprise Consortium (NSTXL) for RFP visibility. (7) Scale via STRATFI/TACFI (needs a PAE sponsor and private match) toward a Phase III or production OT. Avoid: pitching on-orbit transport (SDN is SpaceX-anchored), Golden Dome fire control (classified, prime-dominated), or hardware-heavy TacRS/ISAM cohorts.

space.saturation_statement: Coverage is strong on the 2026 acquisition reorganization (PAEs), Kronos, ATLAS/SPADOC status, SDA transport-to-SDN shift, R2C2 structure, SDANet, and commercial-SDA buying patterns, all with 2025-2026 sources. Gaps remaining after the 12-search budget: exact FY26/FY27 PE numbers and dollar figures for the Space C2/BMC3I lines (need FY27 RDT&E Space Force J-book, Vol 3), names of the 20 R2C2 awardees and any 2025-2026 on-ramp, the 2026 STRATFI awardee list, SDA BM mission-app BAA award recipients, BigBear.ai/Accelint/Kratos/Parsons Space Force C2 roles, and which PAE owns the Space Data Network and SDANet. Two WebFetch attempts to third-party sites were egress-blocked. Absence of found competitors in a niche is not evidence of opportunity; the SDA/space-C2 software niche is already contested by Slingshot, LeoLabs, COMSPOC, True Anomaly, MapLarge, Bluestaq, Palantir and Anduril (which now owns ExoAnalytic).

c4isr_products.name: Spacetime
c4isr_products.description: Temporospatial software-defined networking (SDN) orchestration platform that models the time-dynamic position/orientation of satellites, aircraft, ships and ground stations and continuously plans, schedules and steers directional links (RF and optical) across space/air/land/sea networks; deployable as single-tenant customer-owned Kubernetes instances (cloud, on-prem, classified/air-gapped per company claim). Includes a Federation ('Spacetime Fabric') feature to broker interconnect between separately orchestrated networks.
c4isr_products.input_process_output_user: INPUT: network model (platforms, antennas, interfaces, ephemerides/motion, weather, link budgets), service requests and traffic-engineering policies via NBI; telemetry from devices via SBI. PROCESS: temporospatial link planning, beam scheduling, routing/SR-TE path computation, re-planning as geometry changes. OUTPUT: beam/radio/flow control schedules pushed to devices; computed paths; simulations. USER: network operations engineers at satellite operators and military SATCOM/transport organizations (e.g., DIU HSA, AFRL SDNX, Telesat Lightspeed).

c4isr_products.name: Tightbeam
c4isr_products.description: Free-space optical (laser) communications terminals (T170x fixed, G170x gimballed; 170 mm aperture) claimed at up to 100 Gbps with demonstrated ground-to-air links approaching 200 km; six terminal generations rooted in LLNL work; native Spacetime integration; optical ground-segment 'network as a service' announced as coming.
c4isr_products.input_process_output_user: INPUT: IP traffic and Spacetime schedule/pointing commands. PROCESS: laser link acquisition/tracking and high-rate optical transport. OUTPUT: point-to-point 100 Gbps-class links between land/air (sea/space announced). USER: transport-layer operators needing high-capacity, low-probability-of-intercept backhaul.

companies.exact_problem_solved: Directional (narrow-beam RF and optical) links between moving platforms constantly break as geometry, weather and terrain change; Spacetime automates the planning, scheduling and re-routing of those links across heterogeneous multi-orbit/multi-domain networks so operators can run 'networks in motion' without manual link engineering. Tightbeam supplies the high-capacity optical links themselves.

companies.apis_sdks_open_interfaces: FACT (HIGH): Spacetime publishes open, Apache-2.0 gRPC/Protocol Buffers APIs at github.com/aalyria/api: Northbound Interface (Model, Provisioning/SR-TE, Solution, Simulation, Permissions, Audit), Southbound/CDPI (bidirectional scheduling stream + telemetry export; reference Go agent), Federation/East-West (interconnect and transponder capacity brokering), plus a Status API; nbictl CLI; Go/Python packages; developer portal docs.spacetime.aalyria.com. Third-party audit (API Evangelist, Aug 2026) counts 45 proto files, 13 services, 182 RPCs; no REST/OpenAPI, no public pricing or self-serve sign-up; per-customer instance domains with self-signed RS256 JWT auth. NBI was under migration in 2026 (third-party integrator note to pin to v21.0).
companies.security_classification_requirements: INFERENCE (MEDIUM) from job postings: openings for Information Systems Security Manager (ISSM), Alternate Facility Security Officer and Cleared Program Manager indicate facility-clearance and classified-program work; company states Spacetime can run in 'classified, air-gapped infrastructure'. Tightbeam hardware and defense work likely ITAR/EAR-relevant - specialist legal review required for non-U.S.-person founders.
companies.allied_international_activity: ESA contract funded by UK Space Agency and European arm/London (Dec 2023); Telesat (Canada) Lightspeed design-in; Airbus SpaceRAN (Europe); Series B release references allied government partners (unnamed). Rivada (Germany/US) selection Mar 2023, but Rivada deployment timeline uncertain.
companies.technical_differentiator: Temporospatial SDN that treats link geometry over time as a first-class scheduling input (Loon heritage), combined with open federation APIs and in-house 100 Gbps-class FSO terminals; deployable as customer-owned Kubernetes instances.
companies.suspected_moat: Google/Loon IP lineage and a decade of orchestration engineering; early design-in at Telesat Lightspeed (high switching cost once operational); progressive government selections (DIU, Space RCO, AFRL) and a former DIU director on the board. HYPOTHESIS: open APIs could become a de facto standard for multi-orbit orchestration if adopted by SDA/MILNET-class programs.
major_competitors: Northrop Grumman / Lockheed Martin / L3Harris (SATCOM management for programs of record)
CACI CrossBeam, Mynaric, Skyloom, General Atomics (optical terminals vs Tightbeam)
companies.obvious_weaknesses: No disclosed revenue, ARR, backlog or production deployments; commercial anchor customers (Telesat, Rivada) depend on constellation schedules and financing; government work is prototype/experimentation with undisclosed values; cloud-native microservice architecture assumes SRE-grade operators that tactical enclaves lack (third-party critique); FSO links are weather-limited.
companies.evidence_user_adoption: MEDIUM: government demonstrations attended by 150+ officials and repeated selections (DIU, Space RCO, AFRL); Telesat/Rivada/ESA/NASA named engagements. No public evidence of daily operational use by military units.
companies.evidence_repeat_procurement: MEDIUM: sequence DIU HSA (2022) -> Space RCO R2C2 delivery order (2024) -> DIU swarm connectivity (2024) -> AFRL SDNX (2026) shows repeat government selection, but each is a prototype/experimentation instrument and dollar values (except $8.7M) are undisclosed.
companies.evidence_prototype_to_production: Public evidence insufficient. No program-of-record production contract disclosed; Telesat Lightspeed is the first announced production integration but the constellation is not operational.
companies.tech_stack_inference_from_jobs: INFERENCE (MEDIUM): careers page (Rippling ATS, 2026) lists Communications DSP Engineer, IT Systems Engineer, Lead Product Security Engineer, Security and Compliance Lead, ISSM, Alternate FSO, Cleared Program Manager, Proposal Manager - implying a cleared-government delivery track alongside DSP/optical hardware engineering. Public repo shows Go (SBI agent), Java client samples, Bazel builds, gRPC/protobuf, Kubernetes deployment, OpenTelemetry metrics.
companies.confidence_notes: Corporate/funding facts HIGH-MEDIUM (multiple independent Feb 2026 reports and a PitchBook-derived dataset). Contract values LOW except DIU $8.7M (MEDIUM). Research environment limitation: company site, DIU, defense.gov and news domains were egress-blocked; evidence was retrieved from GitHub-mirrored copies of company API docs, third-party research packs (vibewatch, CTOx, API Evangelist) and a PitchBook-derived CSV. Treat any figure not repeated across sources as MEDIUM at best.

c4isr_products.name: Lattice OS / Lattice command and control
c4isr_products.description: AI-enabled C2 and sensor-fusion software that ingests feeds from radars, EO/IR, EW, drones and third-party systems, maintains a track/entity picture, and lets operators task effectors and autonomous systems. Selected by the Army as the common data layer baseline for NGC2 (June 2026), as fire-control platform for IBCS-M counter-UAS (Nov 2025), and as JIATF-401 enterprise counter-UAS C2 (Mar 2026).
c4isr_products.input_process_output_user: Input: sensor tracks, video, radio/vehicle telemetry, third-party app data. Users: air defense operators, division/brigade staffs (4th ID), SOF operators, CBP agents.

c4isr_products.name: Tiqker optical atomic clock
c4isr_products.description: Rack-mounted rubidium optical clock (company: 10^-15 short-term instability, ~100x better frequency stability than legacy clocks). Subject of an $11M DoD APFIT award (2024) for 'Rack-Mounted Optical Clocks'; tested on UK flights, U.S. Army ground vehicles in New Mexico and an autonomous submarine (world-first optical clock underwater, Royal Navy-related trial). First UK commercial sale 2024.
c4isr_products.input_process_output_user: Input: none external (self-contained atomic reference). Output: precise time/frequency (PTP/1PPS/10 MHz, INFERENCE) for holdover when GNSS timing is denied. User: network/timing engineers on ships, vehicles, comms nodes and datalinks.

c4isr_products.name: Quantum inertial sensors (atom-interferometer accelerometers/gyros) and cold-atom gravimeters
c4isr_products.description: GPS-denied positioning sensors; flight-trialed on a customised aircraft at a UK military test site in 2024 (UK MOD 'un-jammable quantum tech takes flight'); newer continuous-beam generation first tested Oct 2025. Australian Army Phase II 'Quantum Technology Exploit' contract.
c4isr_products.input_process_output_user: Input: atom-interferometer phase measurements. Output: low-drift acceleration/rotation for INS. User: platform navigation integrators (aircraft, submarines, ground vehicles).

c4isr_products.name: Quantum Spectrum (Rydberg-atom RF receiver)
c4isr_products.description: Antenna-less RF sensing spanning MHz to THz; demonstrated at U.S. Army C5ISR NetModX23 and UK-led Defence Cyber Marvel 3; co-developed with L3Harris.
c4isr_products.input_process_output_user: Input: ambient RF fields. Output: wideband spectrum/signal detection data. User: EW/spectrum-awareness and comms experimenters.

c4isr_products.name: Contextual ML for assured navigation and timing
c4isr_products.description: $2M U.S. Army contract for 'contextual machine learning for assured navigation and timing' (software layer fusing sensors).
c4isr_products.input_process_output_user: Input: multi-sensor PNT data. Output: assured PNT solution/integrity. User: Army PNT program offices (INFERENCE).

companies.exact_problem_solved: Provides timing holdover and navigation sensing that keep networks, datalinks and platforms synchronised and localised when GPS is jammed or spoofed, plus wideband RF sensing without conventional antennas.
primary_users: Navy/submarine and Royal Navy trial units
companies.hw_sw_mix: both - hardware sensors and clocks are the revenue core; Superstaq/Contextual ML are software.

companies.evidence_prototype_to_production: APFIT ($11M, 2024) is the strongest transition signal; fielded quantities undisclosed. Inertial sensors: none. Rating: partial.

c4isr_products.description: Distributed, identity-based zero-trust mesh that sits in front of OT/IT/cloud assets: multi-layer identity and access management, privileged access management, secure remote access/VPN replacement, zero-trust data exchange, multi-monitor remote operations, and (Sept 2025) 'Unified Zero Trust for AI' agents. Output: authenticated, least-privilege sessions to assets and audited data flows. Users: OT/space ground-segment operators, network defenders, mission-system administrators.

c4isr_products.name: PULSAR LEO PNT service
c4isr_products.description: Planned 258-satellite constellation at ~1,080 km broadcasting L-band navigation signals ~100x stronger than GPS at the ground, with encrypted/authenticated ranging ('watermark'; world-first authenticated pseudorange from orbit claimed from July 2025 Pulsar-0 transmissions) and centimeter-class accuracy with corrections. FCC authorised full deployment Aug 3, 2026 (16 sats initially; milestones 2032/2035). Existing GNSS chipsets adopt via firmware through 'Pulsar Verified' partners.
c4isr_products.input_process_output_user: Input (user side): Pulsar + GNSS RF signals. Process: multi-constellation receiver firmware from partners (Trimble, Septentrio, Topcon, Furuno, Murata, Locus Lock). Output: position/timing with anti-jam margin and spoof detection. Users: any GNSS-dependent platform; defense timing/navigation users are one of eight target verticals.

c4isr_products.description: 149 kg spacecraft (Aerospacelab bus) launched June 23, 2025 on SpaceX Transporter-14 to ~500 km; >350 live passes over four continents by Aug 2026; used to map GPS jamming across Europe and the Middle East (space.com, Jun 2026).
c4isr_products.input_process_output_user: Output: live Pulsar test signals and GNSS-interference observations. Users: receiver partners, timing customers, Xona engineers.

(collaborative autonomy, AFRL Phase III), Toyon Research (sensor fusion/tracking SBIRs), Charles River Analytics and Aptima (serial C2 decision-support SBIR performers - classic proto-purgatory exemplars), Mattermost (DDIL collaboration on Platform One), Rancher Government Solutions (edge Kubernetes), Hypori (Army BYOD/zero trust), Virtualitics (AFWERX STRATFI analytics), Anchore (Iron Bank scanning), Deepwave Digital and Bastille Networks (spectrum sensing), Slingshot Aerospace (space C2/SDA). CONTEXT: AFWERX lists 'Command, Control & Battle Management' among FY26 priorities and AFWERX/SpaceWERX reopened SBIR/STTR solicitations following reauthorization (https://www.dvidshub.net/news/564491/afwerx-spacewerx-open-new-sbir-sttr-solicitations-following-reauthorization); Army SBIR keeps a standing 'Generative AI Enabled Tactical Network' topic (https://armysbir.army.mil/topics/generative-ai-enabled-tactical-network/). STUDY IMPLICATION (INFERENCE, MEDIUM): the prize/SBIR funnel is producing many data-pipeline and edge-AI performers but the observable transitions in 2025-2026 (Rune, Rise8 STRATFI, NGC2 vendors) favor venture-backed, product-shaped companies that attach to a named program (NGC2, Dynamis, Warp Core) rather than SBIR-only firms; a two-founder team should treat SBIR as validation/non-dilutive runway, not as the go-to-market. FOUNDER CONSTRAINTS: SBIR/STTR eligibility requires a U.S.-based small business majority-owned by U.S. citizens or permanent residents (and xTech prize eligibility has similar rules); the Indonesian founder's ownership share and any ITAR/export-controlled technical data access need specialist legal review - no legal judgment is made here.
