score.title: Offline-capable zero-trust policy, key and replication enforcement for tagged data at the tactical edge (ZT Data Pillar under DDIL)
score.scoring_note: Scores are analytical heuristics, not facts. Labels: FACT / INFERENCE / HYPOTHESIS with confidence HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW. New fact this session: the Army T-ICAM OTA prototype vendor is Akamai (Breaking Defense, 2024-04, https://breakingdefense.com/2024/04/army-picks-akamai-for-prototype-battlefield-zero-trust-project-t-icam/ - FACT, HIGH); the same search found no funded PEO solicitation or award for a tactical ZT data-pillar/edge key-release capability beyond the DUCES RFI (2025-02) and Navy SBIR topics N244-P03 (2024) and DON26BZ03-NV059 (2026) - Public evidence insufficient for any production pull.

scores.rationale: FACT/HIGH: the Army CTO authorizing official rated the NGC2 prototype 'very high risk' because any user could see all data with no logging (CNBC 2025-10-03); Balikatan 2026 still needed JICOs/FDOs hand-tagging releasability after 8+ years (DVIDS 2026-05); WFX 24-03 regenerated Secret products by hand (MIPB 2025). Severe for the authorizing official and the FDO, but units keep operating on implicit trust, so it is not mission-stopping for the S6 - hence 4 not 5.

INFERENCE/MEDIUM: every disconnection event at a hub/spoke node and every coalition data exchange re-triggers the trade-off (implicit trust vs. unreadable objects, manual re-tagging); Ivy Mass / Ivy Sting deliberately test denied-network operation (army.mil 2026; E03-F9), so the pain recurs in every NGC2 exercise and daily in coalition enclaves.

Score of 1 explained - FACT/HIGH: the only money aimed at this capability is research-sized: DUCES is a sources-sought RFI with no award (Breaking Defense 2025-02; no follow-on found 2026-09), and Navy SBIR topics N244-P03 (2024) and DON26BZ03-NV059 (Phase I up to $315k, closed 2026-07-22). Adjacent NGC2 money (~$2.95B FY26 request, 50% obligation cap under FY26 NDAA - FNN 2026-02) and the CDAO Edge Data Mesh OTA ($100M, DefenseScoop 2024-12-03) are ceilings/portfolios controlled by primes, not lines this product bills against. No dedicated line: Public evidence insufficient. Not 0 because the SBIR topics are real, dated, funded asks.

FACT/HIGH (13 CFR 121.702): the primary vehicle (Army/Navy SBIR) requires >50% U.S.-citizen/PR ownership and control, which a two-founder cap table with one non-U.S. person fails until restructured with counsel; NGC2 entry is via prime subcontract (Anduril/Lockheed-Raft) at the prime's discretion; CSO/OTA and a C5ISR CRADA are open but slow and unfunded at start (E04-F2, E07-F28). Accessible in principle, gated in practice.

INFERENCE/MEDIUM: open baselines exist (OpenTDF KAS/attribute services, TAK federation, production CRDT tooling) so an offline PDP/KAS with time-boxed grants and a label-aware sync filter is buildable; but offline revocation under partition is a bounded-staleness trade-off rather than a solved problem, and NSA-approved crypto integration (FY26 NDAA condition) and FIPS-validated modules are outside a small team's reach without cleared partners.

INFERENCE/MEDIUM: the card's own PoC estimate ($150-300k for two founders plus a contract cryptographer for 6 months) consumes the entire founder capital and yields only an unaccredited synthetic-data demo; the next milestone ($1-2.5M credible military demo) is 4-10x the available capital. Only the non-crypto label-aware sync library fits inside $250k.

INFERENCE/MEDIUM: a two-laptop lab demo (cut link, show policy-correct deny/allow, three-node partition convergence) is 3-6 months away; a demo a program office would credit needs DoD PKI test integration, an exercise slot (Cyber Quest, T-REX, Ivy Sting) and cATO packaging, which the card puts at 12-18 months and $1-2.5M - slow relative to gaps that can demo on public data alone.

FACT/HIGH for the MVP: OpenTDF spec, ATAK-CIV/CoT schemas and the STANAG 4774/4778 and ACP-240 label syntaxes are public (some registration required), so synthetic tagged messages are fully obtainable. Real labeled operational data and government attribute feeds are classified/CUI, only reachable inside a sponsored experiment with cleared U.S.-person staff - the non-U.S.-person founder should assume no access.

Score of 1 explained - FACT/HIGH (constraints, not legal conclusions): the core differentiator (delegated key release/revocation) is cryptographic key-management software, export-controlled under EAR Category 5 Part 2 at minimum and possibly ITAR USML XI/XIII if specially designed for military use; the Indonesian founder cannot be assumed able to write or review that code without a deemed-export license/technology control plan; NSA-approved high-assurance encryption and classified attribute data require cleared U.S. persons and possibly a facility clearance with FOCI mitigation (32 CFR 117.11 treats even a permanent resident as a foreign interest); production requires an ATO/cATO. Only the SBIR-free OT/CSO route and an EAR99-style non-crypto core avoid the worst of this. Counsel required at every step.

FACT/HIGH: the MVP is fully unclassified (commercial laptops, OpenTDF, ATAK-CIV, synthetic US-only/REL FVEY/REL NATO messages). Deducted because the card rates classification dependence 'eventually' and the first government-furnished attribute feeds, exercise networks and NSA crypto integration arrive early on the credible-demo path, at which point one founder is walled off.

FACT (claims exist)/MEDIUM: no vendor publicly documents the full seam (offline PDP + delegated key release + label-aware convergent replication), but every adjacent piece is held by funded players: Virtru/OpenTDF (format owner, offline TDF and Multi-KAS claims), Xage ($1.5M Navy PMW 790 Phase II 2024-10; $17M Space Force 2023-09), Anduril+Booz Allen ('zero trust' on Lattice/Menace, BusinessWire 2026-05-18), Palantir Foundry ABAC, Raft, Ditto (STRATFI up to $28M), Akamai (T-ICAM), CDS vendors (Everfox-Virtru ACP-240 partnership 2025-10-16). Absence of an exact competitor is not evidence of opportunity.

INFERENCE/MEDIUM: the Army CTO memo proves the leading prime shipped a prototype without access control (2025-09), and the Army's stated preference for government-owned NGC2 APIs (army.mil 2026-06-22) creates a vendor-neutral seam primes dislike filling for each other. But the same prime announced a bundled ZT fix eight months later, Virtru can add an edge KAS, and the Army can declare cached identity plus enclave plus CDS 'target-level' - the incumbents' cheapest response is to absorb, and they have the money and cleared staff to do so.

FACT/HIGH on interfaces: TAK Server/ATAK-CIV and OpenTDF are open and government- or community-controlled, which is favorable; but the product must also sit inside proprietary meshes (Lattice Mesh, Raft federation, Ditto), federate with Army EICAM/T-ICAM (Akamai) and Naval Identity Service, and hand off to accredited CDS at boundaries (NSA/NCDSMO controlled). Label schemas differ across ISM/CAPCO, STANAG 4774/4778 and ACP-240. The card lists 'integration complexity' and 'proprietary incumbent architecture' as reasons the gap is unsolved.

INFERENCE/MEDIUM: defensibility exists only if a government sponsor treats the component as the accredited reference implementation (ATO artifacts, FIPS build, embedded in TAK/NGC2 baseline) - the OpenTDF-style position. The open ZTDF format is deliberately non-proprietary and the label-aware merge algorithm is publishable; without sponsor adoption the card itself concludes 'it is a feature primes copy'.

INFERENCE/MEDIUM: offline attribute-based key release and policy-aware sync map to sovereign/OT/maritime/mining/disaster-response disconnected-sync markets and OpenTDF already has commercial users via Virtru; but commercial buyers rarely need multi-releasability convergence, so the dual-use product competes on Ditto's and Xage's turf, not on defense-specific features.

HYPOTHESIS/LOW-MEDIUM: if a reference edge policy/key node were adopted it could extend across Army NGC2 nodes, Navy expeditionary sites, coalition MPE enclaves and NATO data-centric security (STANAG 4774/4778 are allied by construction; Germany D-LBO/TaWAN 2026-2029 needs label-aware edge data services); but each expansion runs through a different prime and accreditation regime, and a U.S. NSA-crypto build cannot simply be exported.

INFERENCE/MEDIUM: a fielded edge KAS/PDP would be licensed and sustained per node/unit with recurring accreditation and policy-update work, which is genuinely recurring revenue; but the most likely commercial form is a component priced inside a prime's NGC2 or Navy vehicle, so the recurring revenue accrues via subcontract at the prime's margin.

Score of 1 explained - FACT/HIGH on the constraints, INFERENCE on fit: the card marks four roles fatal-if-absent (applied cryptographer, CRDT distributed-systems engineer, cleared U.S.-person ZT/ICAM/labeling SME, export/immigration counsel) and states neither founder can fill the cleared-SME role; the crypto core is the export-controlled surface the Indonesian founder must be assumed unable to touch; the German founder is clearance-eligible only after naturalization (roughly 2031 at the earliest) and remains a FOCI 'foreign interest' as a permanent resident (32 CFR 117.11); SBIR ownership (13 CFR 121.702) fails on a 50/50 split. A 'strong engineer' is not, by default, an applied cryptographer or CRDT specialist, and the business founder has no documented DoD ZT network. The only part of the product the team can legally build alone is the part with the least moat.

market.summary: No program office owns 'tactical ZT data pillar' by name and no budget line exists; every dollar found is research money (DUCES RFI with no award 19 months on; two Navy SBIR cycles at Phase I scale); primes will bundle ZT into Lattice/Menace at zero incremental price and the Army can accept cached identity plus enclave plus CDS as target-level compliance; label-schema and mesh fragmentation push a small vendor toward bespoke integration work; the cleared-SME and export-control walls make the team's only path a services model its $250k cannot fund. Assessment: the strongest of the three; every load-bearing claim traces to the card's own evidence and was not contradicted by this session's search.

competition.summary: Virtru already advertises Multi-KAS / Private Keystore with disconnected and air-gapped TDF operation (vendor claim, tier 4); Booz Allen reports ZT logging/policy enforcement 'live' on Anduril Menace/Lattice (press release 2026-05-18); Raft, Ditto and Lattice Mesh already do DDIL convergence and can add policy filters incrementally; Palantir has mature ABAC; production money flows through incumbent vehicles. Assessment: partly overstated - none of the cited announcements documents label-aware convergent replication across releasability tiers or fielding at tactical echelon, and vendor marketing is not proof a product works - but the direction is correct: the format owner and the mesh owners are the natural home for this feature, and they have cleared staff the founders lack.

feasibility.summary: Xage, funded and Navy/Space Force-contracted, has not closed the full gap in 2-3 years; DUCES has not converted to an acquisition; three fatal-if-absent roles are unfilled and the core crypto is legally inaccessible to one founder; SBIR ownership fails on a 50/50 split and an outside raise worsens it; the capital ladder ($150-300k PoC, $1-2.5M credible demo, $5-12M production) outstrips $250k by 4-10x at the first credible milestone; offline revocation under partition is an unresolved trade-off. Assessment: accurate on eligibility and capital; the 'unresolved CAP trade-off' point is weaker (bounded staleness is an acceptable engineering answer that OpenTDF-style grants already use), but the founder-fit and capital arguments stand.

score.verdict_rationale: Three skeptics refute at strength 4 and, on the evidence, they are right about the two things that decide this gap for these founders. (1) The PROBLEM -> USER -> REQUIREMENT OWNER -> PROGRAM OFFICE -> CONTRACTING OFFICE -> BUDGET -> CONTRACT VEHICLE chain breaks at the fourth link and never recovers: the problem and users are real and dated (Army CTO memo 2025-09 via CNBC 2025-10-03; Balikatan 2026; WFX 24-03), the requirement owner is only an INFERENCE (Army G-6/DoD CIO ZT PfMO), no program office owns 'tactical ZT data pillar' by name (Public evidence insufficient), the contracting office is an INFERENCE, the budget line does not exist (only DUCES, an RFI with no award as of 2026-09, and Navy SBIR Phase I topics), and the only vehicles are SBIR topics the team is not eligible for on a 50/50 cap table (13 CFR 121.702) or a prime subcontract the prime has every incentive to withhold. The major penalty for a broken chain applies in full. This session's one verification search confirmed the picture: T-ICAM went to Akamai under an OTA in 2024-04 (identity pillar only) and nothing funded has appeared for the data pillar since. (2) Founder fit is 2.0 with two criteria at 1: the product's only defensible component - delegated offline key release and revocation - is the export-controlled crypto surface that the Indonesian founder must be assumed unable to build or review, the cleared U.S.-person ZT/labeling SME is fatal-if-absent and unfillable by either founder before roughly 2031, and the $150-300k PoC consumes all founder capital while the first credible milestone costs $1-2.5M. Market attractiveness is 2.6 on the team-independent criteria, which by itself would argue 'borderline' for a cleared U.S. team with a cryptographer; combined with a broken procurement chain and a founder-fit of 2.0 it is a kill for this team. The narrower versions the skeptics propose (a no-crypto label-aware sync filter, or an FDO releasability-tagging tool, EU-domiciled) are not G02: once the key/policy/revocation core is removed, what remains is a feature that Raft, Ditto, Anduril, Virtru or the TAK Product Center can add in a sprint, and its buyer is the coalition-tagging problem that GAO-25-106454 (2025-04-08) says no DoD entity owns and that DISA says stays network-centric until about 2027. That derivative belongs with the coalition-interoperability gap in the registry and should be evaluated there, not credited to G02. What would reverse this verdict: a funded PEO C3T / PMW 790 solicitation or production award naming edge key release / policy-aware replication with a dollar figure; a public program-office finding that the Booz Allen-Anduril or Virtru offerings fail label-aware convergence; or the team adding a cleared U.S.-person cryptographer as a co-founder with a compliant cap table.
score.narrower_version_if_borderline: Not applicable (verdict is kill). For the record, the only survivable derivative all three skeptics converge on is: drop key custody, offline KAS and all controlled cryptography; build an open-source, EAR99-candidate (counsel to confirm) label-aware sync/filter library for TAK federation and OpenTDF policy metadata using STANAG 4774/4778 and ACP-240 labels, aimed at the documented FDO/JICO hand-tagging workflow (Balikatan 2026, WFX 24-03), domiciled in a NATO nation for DIANA eligibility and Germany's D-LBO/TaWAN subcontract chain (Rheinmetall/blackned, delivery 2026-2029). That is a feature-sized wedge with no identified budget owner on either side of the Atlantic and should be scored under the coalition releasability/interoperability gap rather than under G02.
score.most_important_question_answer: If two exceptionally capable founders had $250,000 today and insisted on this gap, the only thing they could legally and affordably build first is the non-crypto half: an open-source label-aware sync filter and offline policy-decision sidecar for TAK Server / ATAK-CIV that reads OpenTDF policy metadata and STANAG 4774/4778 / ACP-240 labels and decides, deterministically and with provenance, which tagged objects a partitioned node may store and forward, with three laptops emulating US-only, REL FVEY and REL NATO nodes over a tens-of-kbit/s emulated link; they would show it to the DEVCOM C5ISR ESI Directorate (the DUCES RFI author), the DoD CIO ZT PfMO interoperable-data-tagging team, and the Raft / Anduril data-layer leads on NGC2, and the demonstration would prove zero unauthorized reads across partitions (fuzzed), convergence without manual de-duplication, and bandwidth overhead low enough for a tactical radio. The customer would care because the Army CTO memo said 'we cannot control who sees what' and Balikatan 2026 still hand-tags releasability, so a measurable, standards-anchored answer to those two findings is attractive on its face. But this is exactly where it fails: the demo does not include the piece that makes the product a product - delegated offline key release and revocation - because that piece is export-controlled crypto one founder cannot touch and a FIPS/NSA-approved build the team cannot afford; without it, what they have shown is a replication filter, which Raft, Ditto, Anduril or the TAK Product Center can copy in weeks once a sponsor signals interest, and Virtru can pair with its own KAS. An incumbent does not need to crush them; it needs only to add a policy hook to its merge function and let the Army declare cached identity plus enclave plus CDS 'target-level'. The milestone that would justify $2-5M - a named program office (PEO C3T CPE C2IN or PMW 790) funding an OTA or Phase II specifically for an edge KAS/PDP component, with a cleared U.S.-person cryptographer on the founding team and a SBIR-compliant or OT-based path - does not exist on public evidence as of 2026-09-25, and the founders cannot create it with $250k. That is why the gap fails for this team even though the pain is real.
score.bear_case_summary: Real, dated pain (Army CTO memo 2025-09; Balikatan 2026; WFX 24-03; DUCES RFI; two Navy SBIR cycles) but no program office, no budget line, no funded solicitation 19 months after the only Army RFI, primes bundling 'zero trust' into Lattice/Menace for free (2026-05-18) and Virtru claiming offline/Multi-KAS TDF, an Army that can declare cached identity (Akamai T-ICAM) plus enclave plus CDS 'target-level', a crypto core that is export-controlled and legally inaccessible to one founder, three unfillable fatal roles, SBIR ineligibility on a 50/50 cap table, and a capital ladder ($1-2.5M then $5-12M) that outstrips $250k by an order of magnitude at the first credible milestone. The likeliest outcome is absorption, not purchase.
score.bull_case_summary: The seam is genuinely unclaimed: no vendor publicly documents an offline policy decision point plus delegated key release plus label-aware convergent replication, and none is evidenced as fielded at tactical echelon; the DoD ZT target-level deadline (2027-09-30), NSA ZIGs (2026-01) naming ZTDF/IC-TDF (per Virtru, 2026-04, MEDIUM), the FY26 NDAA tying NGC2 money to DDIL resiliency and NSA-approved crypto, the Army's stated wish for government-owned NGC2 APIs (2026-06-22) and the DUCES/Navy SBIR asks all point the same way; OpenTDF and TAK give a small team open baselines; and the coalition version of the pain (GAO-25-106454, STANAG 4774/4778, ACP-240) is allied by construction, so an EU-domiciled entity has a NATO DIANA / D-LBO route. A cleared U.S. team with an applied cryptographer, entering via a C5ISR CRADA and an NGC2 prime subcontract, could plausibly become the accredited reference edge policy/key node - but that team is not these two founders.

verdicts.bear_case:
This is a real, dated technical pain point but not, on current public evidence, a fundable near-term product business for a two-student founder team — it is a research topic with no budget owner that incumbents will absorb as a feature.

1) No program office owns it. The card's own "customer" field says "no program office currently owns 'tactical ZT data pillar' by name — Public evidence insufficient," and its "budget" field rates confidence "LOW for any line this product could bill against directly" (G02.json, 2026-09 compilation). GAO-25-106454 (2025-04-08, gao.gov) independently found that overly restrictive classification hampering allied C2 data sharing has "no DoD entity" that owns the fix — i.e., the underlying problem may be a policy/classification-relaxation fix, not a technology a startup can sell.

2) Every dollar found is research money, not production money: DEVCOM C5ISR ESI's DUCES RFI (Breaking Defense, 2025-02, https://breakingdefense.com/2025/02/army-says-duces-to-cyber-hackers-new-rfi-looks-for-tactical-edge-zero-trust-solutions/) is explicitly a sources-sought market-research notice with "no award will be made as a result of this request" (confirmed again by a 2026-09 WebSearch: no follow-on solicitation or award found ~19 months later). Navy SBIR N244-P03 (2024) and DON26BZ03-NV059 (FY26 R3, closed 2026-07-22, Phase I up to $315k) are two SBIR cycles asking the same open-ended question — repeated research asks, not a converging production requirement. No Phase II/III for this specific data-pillar-in-DDIL capability was found.

3) The primes are positioned to absorb this as a bundled feature at zero incremental price, exactly as the card's own "killer_risk" concedes: Anduril/Booz Allen already announced "zero trust" on Lattice/Menace (2026-05-18 press release) and Palantir Foundry already has mature ABAC/markings. A prime that owns the mesh has every incentive to build (or paper over) access control internally rather than cede a security-critical seam to an outside two-person company — especially once Army accepts cached identity (T-ICAM) + enclave + boundary CDS as "target-level" ZT compliance, which is a plausible, cheaper political resolution to the FY2027 deadline than acquiring a new vendor.

4) The market is small and hard to access even if it exists: the only concretely dollarized comparable is Xage's $1.5M Navy SBIR Phase II (2024-10-09) and $17M Space Force award (2023-09-27) for a different, narrower capability (network/asset ZTNA, not object tagging + key release + label-aware replication convergence) — after several years neither shows evidence of scaling to a fielded, revenue-generating tactical-echelon deployment. The large adjacent pots (NGC2 ~$2.95-3.78B, CDAO Edge Data Mesh OTA $100M) are prime-controlled; third-party software gets in only via subcontract, which requires a prime's cooperation that point 3 makes doubtful. A startup's realistically billable near-term ceiling is SBIR Phase I/II (roughly $100k-$2M) before it needs a prime or OTA sponsor who may not want it.

5) Different-implementation-per-customer / consultancy risk: label schemas differ by service and coalition (US ISM/CAPCO vs. NATO STANAG 4774/4778 vs. ACP-240), and the product must plug into competing proprietary meshes (Anduril Lattice, Raft, Ditto, TAK). The card itself lists "integration complexity" and "proprietary incumbent architecture" among why_not_solved_reasons — this is a classic recipe for bespoke, low-margin integration work rather than a scalable product.

6) Fatal team/eligibility mismatch for these specific two founders: the card lists a cleared U.S.-person DoD ZT/ICAM SME as "fatal_if_absent" and states "neither founder can fill this." The Indonesian founder is explicitly flagged as unable to touch ITAR technical data, controlled crypto source, or classified/CUI attribute data under deemed-export rules (not a legal conclusion, but a serious operational wall on the crypto/key-management core that the card calls the product's central differentiator). Regulatory burden is rated "high" (EAR Cat 5 Part 2, possible ITAR USML XI/XIII, FOCI exposure even for the German founder once a permanent resident, per 32 CFR 117.11). This pushes the company toward hiring a cleared team to do classified-adjacent crypto plumbing for a government sponsor — i.e., toward a services/consultancy model, which the founders' own capital ($250k) cannot sustain past the $150-300k PoC stage before needing $1-2.5M for a credible demo and $5-12M for first production deployment, per the card's own capital_required estimates.

Net: the operational pain (Army CTO memo 2025-09-03 per CNBC 2025-10-03; Balikatan 2026 hand-tagging; WFX 24-03 manual regeneration) is real and well-documented, and the RFI/SBIR signal shows government awareness, but "awareness + exercises + RFIs + no program office + primes bundling it for free + export-control wall on one founder" is a strong pattern of a gap that gets absorbed or indefinitely deferred rather than bought from a startup — especially this specific two-founder team.
verdicts.strongest_single_argument: The gap card's own killer_risk section already concedes the bear case: "The most likely outcome is that the gap gets absorbed rather than bought" as primes bundle zero-trust into their meshes for free and the Army accepts cached-identity-plus-enclave as sufficient — combined with the card's own admission that no program office owns "tactical ZT data pillar" and budget-line confidence is rated LOW, there is no demonstrated buyer with money earmarked specifically for this capability, only RFIs and small SBIR research awards over 2+ years with no visible follow-on.
verdicts.narrower_survivable_version: Drop the crypto/key-management core entirely (which is both the export-control landmine for the Indonesian founder and the piece primes are most likely to build in-house) and instead build a narrow, non-ITAR SaaS tool that automates the one pain point that is documented as an actual manual human workflow today: coalition releasability tagging for foreign disclosure officers (STANAG 4774/4778 and ACP-240 attribute tagging, the Balikatan 2026 and WFX 24-03 hand-tagging workaround). Domicile the entity in the EU (leveraging the German founder, NATO DIANA-eligible regardless of founder nationality) and sell to NATO/allied MPE programs (e.g., Germany's D-LBO/TaWAN) rather than the U.S. SBIR/ITAR pathway, sidestepping the fatal cleared-U.S.-person and deemed-export constraints. This is smaller and slower to reach U.S. DoD dollars, but it targets money and pain that are independently corroborated (GAO-25-106454, Balikatan/WFX) rather than the unproven, prime-controlled tactical key/replication market.
verdicts.what_would_change_my_mind: A dated, sourced Program of Record or PEO-level budget line (not an RFI or SBIR topic) explicitly earmarked for tactical-edge zero-trust data-pillar (key/policy/replication) capability with a stated dollar figure and contracting office; or evidence of an actual production-scale (not SBIR Phase I/II) award to a third-party (non-prime) vendor for this specific capability; or a public NGC2/PEO statement that primes will NOT build this in-house and require an external vendor-neutral component.

verdicts.bear_case:
The specific technical gap (offline KAS + ABAC + label-aware convergent replication) is real on paper, but every piece of the "hard, unglamorous" wedge the card describes is already being assembled by incumbents who have far more capital, existing government relationships, and — critically — teams that are not barred by export control from touching the crypto core.

(1) Offline key/policy piece: Virtru already markets "Virtru Private Keystore" with Multi-Key Access Server (Multi-KAS) support, letting each party/nation run its own KAS with secure key synchronization, and states TDF objects "remain protected in disconnected environments and syncs securely once connectivity is restored," with forward-deployed units accessing protected intel "even in completely air-gapped environments" because policy/keys are embedded in the object (Virtru product/blog pages, accessed 2026-09; FACT that these are the vendor's current claims, INFERENCE on fielded scale — RECALL/WebSearch this session, tier 4/vendor marketing). This is Virtru advertising almost exactly technical_wedge component (1) and (4) of the gap card today, from the party that already owns the TDF/ZTDF format and reference KAS — the natural, lowest-friction place for this feature to land.

(2) ABAC/policy-enforcement/audit piece: Booz Allen's Zero Trust capabilities are reported as "live today" on Anduril's Menace/Lattice stack, providing "logging, policy enforcement and security controls" alongside Booz Allen's Sit(x) and DETS (Booz Allen/Anduril press release and coverage, 2026-05-18, confirmed via WebSearch 2026-09; FACT that the announcement describes live integration, INFERENCE on whether it satisfies DDIL/offline semantics — tier 3-4, press release). This directly answers the Sept 2025 Army CTO memo's "we cannot control who sees what" finding that the gap card leans on as its strongest evidence of an open hole — the exact prime named in that memo has since announced a live fix with its systems integrator partner, seven months before this session.

(3) Mesh/replication piece: Raft (NGC2 data-layer baseline holder), Ditto (AFWERX STRATFI up to $28M) and Anduril's own Lattice Mesh already solve DDIL-tolerant convergence for their own meshes; layering policy-aware filtering onto an existing merge function these teams already operate is incremental engineering for a well-funded incumbent, not a new invention requiring a standalone company — especially for Palantir, whose Foundry ABAC/markings engine is mature and could plausibly be extended to an edge KAS by a company with $9.2B cash on hand.

(4) No program office owns it and money is research-sized: the card's own evidence shows only an S&T RFI (DUCES, no award found), two SBIR topics (Phase I ~$100-315k), and no dedicated PEO or budget line — while adjacent, real production money ($2.95B NGC2, $10-20B enterprise vehicles) already flows to Anduril/Palantir, who have every incentive to bundle "zero trust" into their existing vehicle at no incremental government cost rather than let a vendor-neutral seam form. DISA's own position (GAO-25-106454) that MPE stays network-centric until ~2027 signals the government may simply accept enclave-plus-cached-identity as "good enough" through the target-level deadline, which is the card's own stated killer_risk.

(5) Founder-specific kill switch: even if the market gap were real, the card's own regulatory_burden section says the Indonesian founder should be assumed unable to touch the controlled crypto core, classified/CUI attribute data, or exercise networks, and that a cleared U.S.-person ZT/ICAM SME is fatal-if-absent and neither current founder can fill that role. That is not a bear argument about market size, it's a bear argument about whether this specific two-founder team (per the assignment's own constraints) can legally build the differentiating 20% of the product (the delegated key-release/revocation crypto) at all without first hiring a cleared American they don't have and don't have a channel to recruit reliably pre-funding.

Net: the demand signal (RFI, two SBIR cycles, NDAA funding conditions, Balikatan/WFX hand-tagging pain) is genuine and dated, so this is not "no evidence of pain" — but the competitive response is faster and closer than the gap card credits, the production money continues to flow through incumbent vehicles rather than a new line item, and the specific founder pair described is structurally blocked from the core technical differentiator without a hire that (a) doesn't yet exist on the team and (b) the German founder's PR status doesn't substitute for.
verdicts.strongest_single_argument: Virtru already ships (per its own 2026 marketing) a Multi-KAS / Private Keystore architecture that lets multiple parties run independent key servers with secure sync and claims TDF objects work "even in completely air-gapped environments" — i.e., the owner of the object format the startup would build on top of is already advertising offline, multi-party key release, which is technical_wedge component (1), the single most defensible/crypto-heavy piece of the proposed product and the one piece the non-U.S.-person founder is barred from building anyway.
verdicts.what_would_change_my_mind: A dated, sourced report (GAO, DoD IG, an exercise after-action report, or a program office solicitation) showing that after a real DDIL exercise, Virtru's Multi-KAS/offline-TDF claims or Booz Allen's "live" ZT-on-Menace failed specifically on label-aware convergent replication across releasability tiers (not just access control) — i.e., evidence the incumbents' announced fixes are marketing rather than working end-to-end at tactical echelon, combined with a named PEO or program of record actually budgeting a dedicated tactical ZT-data-pillar line (not just SBIR topics) that excludes the incumbents' current offerings as non-responsive.
verdicts.narrower_survivable_version: Do not build a company that owns the KAS/crypto/ABAC stack (that piece is being commoditized by Virtru/Booz Allen/Palantir and is where the non-U.S.-person founder is legally blocked anyway). Instead build and open-source a narrow, non-controlled, no-crypto library: a label-aware CRDT merge/sync-filter engine that sits alongside an existing KAS (OpenTDF/Virtru) and existing meshes (TAK federation, Lattice, Raft, Ditto) and decides only "which already-decrypted-or-not-yet-decrypted object gets forwarded to which node," using STANAG 4774/4778 and ACP-240 releasability labels as the filter key — explicitly targeting the coalition hand-tagging pain (Balikatan 2026, WFX 24-03) that Virtru's and Booz Allen's current announcements do not claim to solve (none of their public claims mention automated releasability-tier merge across coalition partners). Domicile the entity in the EU/NATO area (e.g., Germany) to route around U.S. SBIR ownership rules and ITAR/deemed-export exposure for the Indonesian founder, pursue NATO DIANA and Germany's D-LBO/TaWAN programs as the first customer rather than a U.S. Army production line, and keep any NSA-approved-crypto or classified-data work as a later, cleared-U.S.-subsidiary problem for a hire that doesn't exist yet.

FACT/HIGH: the card's own capital ladder — $150-300k PoC, then $1-2.5M for a "credible military demo," $5-12M for first production deployment, plus a 24-36 month sequence to reach a Phase III/production OTA sub — means the founders' $250k covers, at best, an unaccredited synthetic-data demo, not anything a program office would buy; the credible-demo step alone exceeds their entire capital by 4-10x and forces an outside raise that collides with the SBIR ownership test above. Taken together: thin/no program-office budget line, a well-resourced incumbent (Xage) already occupying the closest adjacent niche without having solved the full problem in years, a core differentiator that is legally inaccessible to one founder, a capital ladder that outstrips the team's funding by an order of magnitude at the very first "credible" milestone, and a genuinely unresolved distributed-systems/crypto tradeoff at the technical center — this is closer to a research program a national lab or a cleared incumbent completes than an independently foundable, two-student, $250k company.
verdicts.strongest_single_argument: Xage Security — a funded, venture-backed company with existing Navy PMW 790 ($1.5M, Oct 2024) and Space Force ($17M, Sept 2023) contracts and a multi-year head start on "zero trust access even when disconnected" — has not publicly shipped object-level tagging, TDF key release, or label-aware replication convergence; if the closest, best-resourced adjacent player hasn't closed this gap in years, a two-student team with $250k and one founder legally barred from the crypto core is not positioned to do so first, and the card's own "killer_risk" section independently concludes the more likely outcome is that primes (Anduril/Booz Allen, already announcing ZT-on-Lattice as of May 2026) and format owners (Virtru) absorb the requirement rather than a standalone company winning it.
verdicts.what_would_change_my_mind: A named PEO or program of record (not an S&T RFI) issuing a funded solicitation specifically for tactical ZT data-pillar/edge KAS capability with a dollar figure and a due date; public evidence that Xage, Virtru or the Anduril/Booz Allen ZT-on-Lattice integration has been formally evaluated and rejected/deferred by a program office for missing label-aware convergence (proving the seam is real and unclaimed, not just unannounced); or a credible non-dilutive path (CRADA/OTA, not equity) that lets the team reach the $1-2.5M "credible demo" milestone without breaching the >50% citizen/PR SBIR ownership threshold.
verdicts.narrower_survivable_version: Strip out the export-controlled crypto/key-management layer entirely and build only the open, EAR99-clean piece: a label-aware CRDT sync/filter library (no key custody, no offline KAS, no NSA-approved crypto) that runs as a TAK plugin / Kubernetes sidecar and works purely on public specs (OpenTDF policy metadata, STANAG 4774/4778 label syntax, ACP-240 attributes) to decide what to replicate, not to encrypt or grant keys — leaving the actual key-release and revocation cryptography to a partner (Virtru/OpenTDF or a cleared U.S. subcontractor) who plugs into it. This narrows the moat and revenue (it's a feature, not a platform) but is buildable inside $250k by both founders without deemed-export exposure, is open-source-compatible with OpenTDF's own positioning, and could be offered dual-use into commercial disconnected-sync markets (maritime, mining, disaster response, Ditto's/Xage's existing customer base) or pursued first through a NATO/EU-domiciled entity toward German Bundeswehr D-LBO/TaWAN programs (2026-2029), sidestepping U.S. ITAR/FOCI/clearance friction until the team can add a cleared U.S.-person crypto lead.

evidence.claim: Xage Security markets DDIL-tolerant zero-trust access with a $1.5M Navy PMW 790 SBIR Sequential Phase II (Oct 2024) and a $17M Space Force contract (Sept 2023), yet has not publicly documented object-level tagging, TDF key release, or replication convergence — the incumbent closest to this gap has not closed it in 2+ years despite funding and government relationships.

Booz Allen and Anduril announced 'zero trust' capabilities deployed on Menace/Lattice, the incumbent NGC2 data-layer stack, which the card's own killer_risk analysis treats as the most likely path to absorbing this gap rather than a startup capturing it.

DEVCOM C5ISR's DUCES RFI (Feb 2025) sought Zero Trust Data Pillar / DDIL capabilities but, per the gap card's own evidence, no public prototype award or follow-on solicitation was found as of 2026-09 — over 18 months with no acquisition conversion, indicating S&T interest without funded production pull.

SBIR/STTR eligibility (13 CFR 121.702) requires more than 50% ownership and control by U.S. citizens or permanent residents; the Indonesian founder's equity never counts and the German founder's counts only after green-card issuance, creating cap-table constraints on the team's primary near-term non-dilutive funding vehicle.

Personnel security clearances require U.S. citizenship (EO 12968, SEAD 4); naturalization typically requires ~5 years of permanent residence, so the German founder is clearance-eligible no earlier than roughly 2031, and any classified-dependent business model is 5+ years away for both founders.

Under 32 CFR 117.11 (FOCI), any non-citizen — including a lawful permanent resident — remains a 'foreign interest' for facility-clearance purposes, so even the German founder's eventual green card does not fully resolve FOCI exposure if a facility clearance is later needed.

card.title: DDIL geospatial data logistics: versioned delta-sync and prioritized distribution of basemaps, 3D terrain and overlays across TAK Server federations and NGC2 edge nodes
card.problem: Tactical units still pre-load basemaps and 3D terrain by hand and lose overlay consistency across devices and federated servers when links drop, because no fielded, vendor-neutral service versions, prioritizes and delta-syncs geospatial artifacts (tiles, 3D Tiles, overlays) across TAK Server federations and NGC2 hub/spoke edge nodes under bandwidth budgets.

user.exact_role: Brigade/battalion geospatial engineer (12Y) and TAK Server administrator (S6 section) who build and distribute map/terrain packages; team leaders who load devices before missions; division data-layer operators on NGC2 nodes
user.echelon: battalion/brigade primary; team/platoon as consumers; division as source
organization_examples: Army BCT S2 geospatial cell and S6 (e.g., 4ID and 25ID NGC2 prototype divisions)
SOF units running ATAK/TAK Server (USSOCOM)
USMC units expanding TAK deployment
DHS/CBP TAK users (unclassified first customer candidate)
Allied TAK adopters (NATO members, Australia) and Bundeswehr D-LBO/TaWAN units

current_workflow: Geospatial cell pulls imagery, elevation and OWT/3D terrain from enterprise sources (NGA/AGC, PEO STRI OWT, commercial) while on a good link and builds MBTiles/GeoPackage/KMZ/3D-tile packages.
Packages are sideloaded to end-user devices by hand (USB/'sneakernet') or pushed as TAK mission packages/data-sync missions before the mission; large 3D terrain is rarely refreshed once units move.

During operations, overlays (graphics, routes, targets) are edited on multiple ATAK/WinTAK/TAKX clients and on several TAK Servers; changes propagate via server data sync and federation when links are up.
When links drop, edits diverge; on reconnection the picture is reconciled by whole-object replay or overwritten, and staff manually decide which version is current.
Bulk resync after outages competes with voice, PLI and video for SATCOM/MANET capacity; there is no content-aware prioritization of what reaches the edge first.
Coalition partners exchange a translated subset of the picture (e.g., ASCA between TAK, SitaWare, FC BISA) with liaison officers filling gaps.
card.current_solution: TAK Server data sync ('missions'), mission packages and server-to-server federation (whole-object replication, not delta- or bandwidth-optimized - RECALL, not re-verified this session, MEDIUM); Ditto's Edge Sync plugin for ATAK (CRDT peer-to-peer sync of CoT/objects without a server, company-reported USSOCOM use); Immersive Wisdom's low/no-bandwidth collaboration platform (DoD-wide sole-source ordering contract); Anduril Lattice / Palantir edge-to-cloud mesh inside the NGC2 data layer for the two prototype divisions; Reveal Farsight for edge-generated 3D terrain; manual packaging and sideloading by geospatial cells.
card.failure: The failure is at TRANSPORT/DISSEMINATE between the source of geospatial truth (server or division node) and the disconnected edge device: (1) no delta encoding or content-addressing for tiles/3D Tiles/overlays, so reconnection replays whole objects; (2) no cross-server, cross-federation versioning of the picture, so divergent overlay edits are resolved by hand; (3) no bandwidth-budgeted prioritization, so terrain/basemap refreshes either saturate the link or never happen; (4) NGC2's data mesh explicitly does not yet extend to tactical echelons (UDRA RFI), leaving battalion-and-below on the TAK/mission-package model.

evidence.claim: PM Mission Command's 'Operational Mission Command Suite' notice requires the TAK solution to support on-prem, hybrid and cloud data services integrated via DDIL-robust protocols and architectures, alongside a common data model, data fabric and data catalog - i.e., DDIL-tolerant TAK data services are a stated Army requirement, not a solved feature.

card.why_existing_startups_havent_solved: The overlay/object-sync half is being attacked by Ditto (general-purpose CRDT sync SDK with an ATAK plugin) and Immersive Wisdom (collaboration UI), and the government's own TAK Server already ships data sync and federation for free, so venture-backed teams see a feature, not a product. The basemap/3D-terrain half is unglamorous data logistics: it needs radios and a field exercise to demonstrate, the buyers (TPC, PM MC, PEO STRI OWT, AGC, NGC2 data-layer prime) are fragmented so nobody owns end-to-end 'get the right terrain to the right device under a bandwidth budget', and the NGC2 primes (Anduril/Palantir) are expected to handle transport inside their data layer. Result: everybody assumes someone else owns it and the geospatial cells keep sneakernetting.
card.technical_wedge: A content-addressed, priority-aware sync engine for geospatial artifacts - raster/vector tiles (MBTiles/GeoPackage), 3D Tiles/OWT terrain, and overlays modeled as CRDT documents - exposed as (a) a TAK Server plugin / federation peer that computes per-client deltas against a versioned manifest and schedules transfers under a per-link bandwidth budget with mission-area priority (AO polygon, echelon, time-to-mission), and (b) an ATAK/TAKX client plugin that requests only missing chunks and merges overlay edits conflict-free on reconnection. Later: an NGC2-side adapter so division nodes publish versioned terrain/overlay data products consumable by TAK federations and coalition servers.

mvp.what: Two TAK Servers (federated) and 8-10 ATAK-CIV devices on a lab MANET/Wi-Fi with a WAN emulator (loss, 10-64 kbit/s, outages); a sync service that versions and delta-distributes an open basemap, a Cesium-ion/OSM-derived 3D-tile terrain set and shared overlays.
mvp.demonstrable_in_3_6_months: Measured bytes-to-converge and time-to-converge versus native TAK data sync/mission packages across scripted outage patterns; prioritized delivery of the mission-area terrain first; zero-manual-merge overlay convergence after partitions; a pre-mission 'what is stale on this device' report.
mvp.what_it_must_prove: A 5-10x reduction in bytes to converge after outages, deterministic conflict-free overlay merge, and that a geospatial NCO can replace USB loading with a policy ('keep AO tiles fresh within 24h') - plus that it runs as an unmodified-TAK-Server plugin so TPC/PM MC do not have to change the baseline.

data_requirement.what: Open basemaps and terrain (OSM, USGS 3DEP, Copernicus DEM, Cesium ion / OSM Buildings 3D Tiles), synthetic overlays and scripted link profiles; later CUI exercise data via a sponsor. No classified data needed for the MVP; OWT itself is government-furnished and not needed to prove the logistics layer.
data_requirement.legally_realistically_obtainable: Yes for the MVP (all open/commercial). OWT/TAK-MIL/TAK-GOV builds require sponsor access and are distribution-controlled; a non-U.S.-person founder's access to TAK-GOV/MIL and OWT needs counsel and sponsor approval.

incumbent_response.why_startup_still_wins_or_reject: A startup wins only as the neutral, TAK-native layer that works across TAK federations, non-NGC2 units (SOF, USMC, DHS, allies) and both NGC2 primes - a position the primes have no incentive to fill and TPC is slow to fill (INFERENCE). If the value is confined to NGC2 divisions, reject: the primes will absorb it. The defensible framing is 'geospatial artifact logistics under bandwidth budgets' (tiles/3D terrain/overlays as versioned data products), which is narrower and more specialized than Ditto's general sync SDK.

SBIR eligibility hinges on the U.S.-person ownership majority. These are constraints to work through with export-control and immigration counsel, not legal conclusions.

dual_use_potential.explanation: Offline-first, bandwidth-budgeted distribution of map tiles, 3D terrain and shared overlays maps to wildfire/incident management, search and rescue, border and maritime agencies, mining/energy field ops and humanitarian mapping (all TAK or ATAK-CIV adjacent). The commercial market is real but fragmented and price-sensitive; Ditto shows the generic-sync version sells commercially (airlines, retail), while the geospatial-specific version is narrower.

defensibility.explanation: Defensibility comes from being the TPC-listed/accredited plugin that units already run across federations, the artifact-aware scheduling heuristics tuned on real link telemetry, and adapters into OWT/NGC2/coalition servers. The core idea (CRDT + content-addressed delta sync) is not patentable moat; speed to deployment footprint and TPC/PM MC relationships are.

card.why_now: Three changes since 2023: (1) NGC2 (2025-2026) reframed Army C2 as an edge-to-cloud data layer with DDIL as a test objective (Ivy Sting 4, PC-C6) and the UDRA RFI admits the mesh stops above tactical echelons; (2) One World Terrain went to production (Feb 2026) and SBMC/TAK-compatible soldier devices multiply the 3D data that must reach the edge; (3) WinTAK sunset and TAKX (2026) reopen the plugin ecosystem, and CRDT/content-addressed sync tech (Ditto, IPFS-style chunking) is now mature enough to run on soldier devices. Also, SBIR/STTR was reauthorized in 2026 after the 2025 lapse, reopening the non-dilutive path.
card.killer_risk: The problem may already be 'good enough' solved by free and funded incumbents: TAK Server data sync/federation for overlays plus Ditto's ATAK Edge Sync plugin (well-capitalized, company-claimed SOF use) cover the object-sync half, and NGC2 primes will be assumed to own transport for the division half - leaving a startup with only the basemap/3D-terrain logistics sliver, whose demand this session could not verify with a primary source (the manual-USB workaround remains a hypothesis) and which buyers may treat as a feature TPC should ship.
