Kinetic/EW mitigation is out of scope and legally restricted.
regulatory_burden.non_us_person_founder_note: Both founders are foreign persons today: SBIR/STTR not viable; TAK-CIV plugins, OTAs/CSOs and xTech are viable; CUI access requires unit sponsorship and likely a TCP; 9D610-type technical data from Gauntlet vendors would need a BIS deemed-export license for the Indonesian founder (per E07 - describe, do not conclude; needs counsel). The German founder's PR later enables SBIR ownership counting and ITAR/EAR U.S.-person status but not clearance eligibility.

dual_use_potential.explanation: Public-safety drone units (DFR programs), wildfire/disaster response and critical-infrastructure operators need the same multi-vendor registry, airspace-check and evidence-forwarding workflow on ATAK-CIV/TAK; but commercial fleet-management software (Skydio Cloud, DroneDeploy-type tools, UTM providers) already serves those buyers, so dual-use is a proving ground more than a large revenue line.

defensibility.explanation: Vendor telemetry adapters, TAK-native workflow validated at a CTC, a unit-adopted registry/training ledger and a corpus of KLV-indexed unit collection become sticky; none is a hard moat, and the TAK Product Center or Anduril can replicate the workflow. Accreditation (plugin signing, ATO) and unit relationships are the realistic barriers.

card.why_now: July 2025 Drone Dominance directive and Gauntlet rounds put >12,000 multi-vendor drones in squads by Sept 2026 with 30,000 more inbound and 60,000 expected from Gauntlet 2; the Army's own doctrine response (CALL 25-14, Sept 2025) is procedural and units document hand workarounds (BARS marking) because drone tracks do not populate the COP; ATAK-CIV and its SDK are open source; multi-manufacturer coordination only became demonstrable in late 2025; TITAN entered production but only at division/corps; DCMA now runs Blue UAS as a marketplace including software.
card.killer_risk: The Army does not buy this as a product: its answer to unit-level deconfliction is doctrine plus TAK (free), its answer to fleet control is whichever vendor OS is on the airframe (Auterion, AV Kinesis, Skydio) or Lattice, and no RFI, requirement or budget line for a vendor-neutral unit layer exists; the mass drones are expendable one-way-attack systems where per-airframe registry adds little; so the best case is a TAK plugin feature that a government team or Anduril absorbs, not a company.

card.allied_extension: Somewhat more compelling with allies: Germany (Quantum Systems, Helsing, Auterion EU HQ), the UK and Poland are buying multi-vendor sUAS mass and NATO/France (Arcadia) explicitly want interoperable, sensor-agnostic drone C2 modeled on Ukraine's Delta; ATAK/TAK is widely used by allies and a German founder eases EU sales. But allied armies face the same 'doctrine plus TAK plus vendor OS' substitution, and Ukraine's Delta/Brave1 ecosystem already produced unit-level drone coordination tools that European buyers cite. Allied demand improves the story for a vendor-neutral layer but does not remove the killer risk.

score.title: Squad-to-battalion small-UAS fleet control, registry, deconfliction, tasking and collection forwarding for Drone Dominance mass (multi-vendor drones into company/battalion C2, S2 and training pipelines)

scores.rationale: FACT/HIGH: units hand-mark drone positions (BARS) and run procedural deconfliction because tracks do not populate the COP (3rd CAB pre-JMRC plan; CALL 25-14, army.mil, 2025-09), and 2-35 IN reports a doctrine/tooling gap at JPMRC 26-01 (Small Wars Journal, 2026-09-16); but the Army has judged the pain tolerable via procedure, so it is a real but coped-with pain, not a mission-stopping one.

FACT/HIGH: the pain recurs on every flight in every company/battalion receiving Gauntlet/SRR drones (12,080 accepted, 30,000 inbound, Military Times 2026-09-18), during every CTC rotation and every training event; frequency is the strongest part of the case.

Score of 1 explained: no program element, budget line, RFI or sources-sought for a unit-level sUAS fleet/airspace/collection software layer exists (card budget section, confidence LOW; search log negative). Adjacent money is airframe procurement (SRR/MRR/LRR per CRS IF12668, 2026-05) and an unappropriated FY27 reconciliation request ($53.6B Drone Dominance, Defense Daily 2026) - request is not appropriation, program ceiling is not obligation, and none of it is a software line. Not 0 only because xTech/OTA/CSO discretionary money and unit-level purchase authority exist in principle.

INFERENCE/MEDIUM: the requirement owner (T2COM via MCoE/USAACE) and program office (PEO Aviation PM UAS vs. TAK Product Center vs. RCCTO) are inferred, not identified; the only accessible on-ramps are xTech prizes, TAK.gov plugin submission and a unit-invited CTC trial, none of which is a purchase; the PROBLEM->USER->REQUIREMENT OWNER->PROGRAM OFFICE->CONTRACTING->BUDGET->VEHICLE chain breaks at REQUIREMENT OWNER and again at BUDGET.

FACT/HIGH for the MVP (ATAK-CIV SDK open-sourced per E07; MAVLink/PX4/ArduPilot telemetry self-collectable; CoT is an open schema), but the load-bearing assumption - cross-vendor telemetry from the drones that actually matter (Skydio, Auterion, Gauntlet vendors) without vendor cooperation - is unproven and vendor-gated (card data_requirement), and DDIL networks make any live fleet picture unreliable at company level.

Card estimates PoC at $60k-$120k (fits) but a credible military demo at $400k-$900k and first production deployment at $2M-$5M; $250k covers the PoC and travel to one field trial only if an xTech prize, OTA or vendor partner funds the rest - none secured. Confidence MEDIUM.

A three-drone field demo (CoT tracks, ACM conflict warning, offline ledger sync, clip-to-S2 inbox) is achievable in 3-6 months on commercial hardware; a demo a battalion S3 air would find credible (real vendor feeds, a CTC rotation) needs 9-12 months and a unit sponsor the team does not have. Confidence MEDIUM.

FACT/MEDIUM: PX4/ArduPilot telemetry and synthetic ACOs built from FM 3-52/CALL 25-14 are freely obtainable; but Skydio Cloud API and Auterion CoT need partner access, Gauntlet vendor telemetry formats are not public, real ACOs and unit operator records are CUI reachable only via unit sponsorship, and C-UAS track formats are controlled - the data that makes the product valuable is exactly the data the team cannot get.

Unclassified, software-only MVP on ATAK-CIV and commercial drones is EAR99-level per E07 (describe, do not conclude); burden rises with TAK.gov plugin signing/ATO, CUI handling of ACOs and unit records (NIST 800-171/CMMC), any 9D610-type Gauntlet technical data (BIS deemed-export review for the Indonesian founder - needs counsel), and C-UAS C2 integration. SBIR/STTR closed under 13 CFR 121.702 while both founders are foreign persons (E07, eCFR). Medium burden overall.

FACT/HIGH: ATAK-CIV and SDK are open source (deptofdefense GitHub per E07), PX4/ArduPilot drones are commercial, CoT and MISB KLV are public standards, synthetic airspace data can be built from public doctrine; nothing in the MVP requires a clearance or CUI. Not 5 because the militarily relevant version (real ACOs, Gauntlet telemetry) quickly leaves the unclassified/commercial envelope.

Score of 1 explained (5 = least intense): the seam is crowded on every side - Auterion Nemyx (cross-vendor CoT-to-ATAK, Gauntlet production award; The Defense Post 2025-09-05, vendor claim), AeroVironment/Tomahawk Kinesis (lead SW/systems integrator for HMIF Inc 1, avinc.com 2025-09-29), Anduril Lattice (JIATF-401 C-UAS C2 $87M task order and Army enterprise agreement, DefenseScoop 2026-03-14; multi-vendor tasking/deconfliction marketed - vendor claim), Skydio Cloud for the largest SRR fleet, and a free government-owned TAK UAS Tool plugin (tak.gov, per feasibility skeptic). Not 0 because no one sells a vendor-neutral, unit-owned registry/qualification layer per se.

INFERENCE/MEDIUM: each incumbent is vendor-locked (Auterion covers AuterionOS airframes, Skydio its own, AV its integrations) and the government fusion layer stops at division (TITAN 17 systems, DefenseScoop 2026-09-01), so a vendor-neutral seam exists; but the TAK Product Center and Anduril can each cover it at marginal cost, and vendors can close their APIs to an aggregator, so the vulnerability is narrow and temporary.

FACT/HIGH per card: the startup controls none of the interfaces (TAK/CoT and plugin signing by TAK Product Center; telemetry/API by each drone vendor; C-UAS C2 by JIATF-401/Anduril; TITAN by PEO IEW&S/Palantir); integrating 3-5 Gauntlet/SRR vendors per brigade set is the $2M-$5M cost curve that looks like bespoke systems integration rather than a product.

Score of 1 explained: the card's own defensibility section says none of the proprietary elements (adapters, workflow, footprint, relationships, data) is a hard moat and that TAK PC or Anduril can replicate the workflow; per-airframe registry adds little on expendable one-way-attack drones (the bulk of the mass); realistic barriers are plugin signing/ATO and unit relationships, which are earned, not owned. Not 0 because a CTC-validated, unit-adopted workflow plus vendor adapters would carry some switching cost.

Public-safety DFR programs, wildfire/disaster response and critical-infrastructure operators need the same multi-vendor registry, airspace-check and evidence-forwarding workflow on ATAK-CIV/TAK; but Skydio Cloud, DroneDeploy-type tools and UTM providers already serve them, so dual-use is a proving ground more than a revenue line (card: medium). Confidence MEDIUM.

Expansion paths (blue-drone feed into C-UAS C2, S2 collection indexing, allied armies buying multi-vendor sUAS mass, NATO sensor-agnostic drone C2 ambitions) exist but each runs into the same 'doctrine plus TAK plus vendor OS' substitution and into Ukraine-derived tools already cited by European buyers (card allied_extension); expansion widens the surface without removing the killer risk. Confidence MEDIUM.

A per-battalion subscription or sustainment line is conceivable, but no Army buying pattern for unit-level sUAS software exists today (units buy drones, doctrine is free), and expendable Gauntlet airframes do not create lifecycle-management renewals; realistic recurring revenue is services/support tied to a sponsor unit. Confidence MEDIUM.

The engineer can build ATAK-CIV plugins and MAVLink ingestion today (E07 calls TAK the best immediate fit); but two of three fatal-if-absent roles (former battalion S3 air/UAS master trainer with CTC experience; drone systems engineer with Skydio/Auterion API access) are absent, no unit relationship exists, SBIR is closed to the current cap table (13 CFR 121.702), and the Indonesian founder faces deemed-export exposure once Gauntlet technical data or CUI enters the company (needs counsel). Confidence MEDIUM.

market.summary: No budget owner, program element, RFI or requirement exists for a unit-level sUAS fleet/airspace/collection software layer; the Army's institutional answer (CALL Handbook 25-14, 2025-09) is $0 procedural airspace control designed for the degraded-comms case, TAK is free, TITAN deliberately stops at division (17 systems), Gauntlet mass is expendable one-way-attack drones with low registry value, and the integration cost curve ($60k PoC to $2-5M per brigade set) looks like bespoke systems integration; every seam is already being closed by Auterion, AV/Kinesis, Anduril or Skydio. Narrower version offered: offline-first qualification/training-readiness ledger as a free TAK-CIV plugin monetized via services with one sponsoring battalion/CTC.

competition.summary: Anduril Lattice for Mission Autonomy plus Menace-T/X already markets multi-vendor tasking/route/deconfliction at company-to-brigade echelon (vendor claim) on an awarded Army enterprise vehicle, with Raft contracted for registries/federation inside the NGC2 data layer; TAK/CoT already ingests drone telemetry for free; Skydio can extend Skydio Cloud into its ~60k-drone base; and the Army's residual problem is framed by leadership as training, not a C2 product. Narrower version offered: TAK-native, Lattice/NGC2-compatible training-and-readiness layer sold to schoolhouses/Guard/Reserve, sized as services-adjacent revenue.

feasibility.summary: The government's own free TAK 'UAS Tool' plugin already provides UAS SA/telemetry/FMV/C2 inside ATAK/WinTAK and the same office controls plugin signing; Army common-controller efforts have repeatedly restarted or been cancelled; cross-vendor telemetry from the vendors that matter is API-gated by competitors; SBIR is closed to the current cap table and the militarily useful version (real ACOs, Gauntlet telemetry, C-UAS feed) walks into CUI/9D610 exposure for the Indonesian founder; costs of $400k-$5M exceed $250k by 2-20x with a 5-year path to production as the base case. Narrower version offered: offline registry/qualification ledger plus procedural pre-flight checklist against unit-authored ACMs, acknowledged as small and hard to defend.

score.verdict_rationale: All three skeptics refute at strength 4 and I concur; the evidence they rely on is tier-1/2 and internally consistent with the gap card, and I found nothing in the research corpus that rebuts it. The decisive reason is the broken demand chain: PROBLEM (real, FACT/HIGH) -> USER (company drone team leads, S3 air, UAS master trainers - real) -> REQUIREMENT OWNER (T2COM/MCoE/USAACE - INFERENCE only; their published answer is CALL 25-14 procedure, army.mil 2025-09) -> PROGRAM OFFICE (none owns a software layer; PM UAS buys airframes, TAK PC ships free plugins) -> CONTRACTING OFFICE (unidentified for a software-only layer) -> BUDGET (none; only unappropriated reconciliation requests and airframe lines, CRS IF12668 2026-05) -> VEHICLE (only xTech prizes/OTAs contingent on a sponsor that does not exist). That is a major-penalty condition under the scoring rules. Three compounding facts make the penalty terminal rather than provisional: (a) the government already gives away the core wedge (TAK UAS Tool plugin, ATAK-CIV open source per E07; CoT tracks are free), so the startup would compete against a $0 government-owned baseline whose owner also controls plugin signing; (b) the vendor-neutral seam depends on telemetry access that the direct competitors (Auterion, Skydio, AV, Gauntlet vendors) control and have every incentive to withhold, while Anduril can expose blue-drone tracks inside Lattice for units already on its Army enterprise agreement (DefenseScoop 2026-03-14); (c) the volume driver is expendable one-way-attack drones (12,080 accepted, 30,000 inbound, Military Times 2026-09-18) where per-airframe registry adds little, and the Army's own fusion layer (TITAN, 17 systems, DefenseScoop 2026-09-01) deliberately stops at division. Absence of a competitor selling exactly this layer is not evidence of opportunity; here it reflects absence of a buyer. On the narrower version all three skeptics converge on (an offline qualification/training-readiness ledger as a TAK-CIV plugin): I judge it a feature or a services engagement, not a company - its buyer is a training-management workflow the Army already runs in its own enterprise training records system (RECALL - not re-verified this session, LOW-MEDIUM), it has no budget line either, and the skeptics themselves concede it 'may not clear the bar for venture-scale outcomes'. It can be a credibility project that opens a TiC battalion door for a different gap, which is why I record it below, but it does not rescue G09 to 'borderline'. Residual uncertainty: a T2COM/PEO Aviation RFI or OTA for a vendor-neutral unit-level sUAS registry/deconfliction layer with named funding, or evidence a battalion paid for such a third-party tool at a CTC, would reopen the question; none exists as of 2026-09-25 (public evidence insufficient for any demand signal in this exact form).
score.narrower_version_if_borderline: Not applicable (verdict is kill). For the record, the only form that survives at all is the one all three skeptics independently proposed: an offline-first, vendor-agnostic operator/airframe/battery/qualification and training-readiness ledger with a procedural pre-flight check against unit-authored ACMs, shipped as a free ATAK-CIV plugin and paid for (if at all) through a services/integration engagement with one sponsoring Transformation-in-Contact battalion or CTC, explicitly positioned as a complement to CALL 25-14 procedures and to whichever vendor OS/Lattice/Kinesis layer the unit already has. Treat it as a door-opening credibility project (3-4 months, under $60k) that earns a unit relationship and TAK.gov plugin experience reusable on another gap, not as the basis for a company or for raising $2-5M.
score.most_important_question_answer: If two exceptionally capable founders had $250,000 today and insisted on this gap, the only rational first build is the skeptics' narrow version: a free ATAK-CIV plugin plus a small offline-first edge service that (1) keeps a unit-owned registry of airframes, batteries, operators and qualifications that syncs opportunistically, (2) checks a planned sUAS flight against unit-entered altitude blocks/ROZs/launch points from CALL 25-14 and flags conflicts before launch, and (3) shows any drone that already emits CoT or MAVLink as a blue track - roughly $50-80k and 3-4 months, deliberately avoiding vendor-gated APIs, CUI and C-UAS integration. They would show it to a battalion S3 air NCO and UAS master trainer in a Transformation-in-Contact battalion (2-35 IN / 25th ID or a 4ID/101st unit), to the CTC O/C-T airspace cell that wrote CALL 25-14, and to an xTech panel; the demonstration would prove that the pre-flight check and ledger replace spreadsheet/binder tracking and BARS hand-marking without a network, and the unit would care because it removes real friction from every flight and every readiness report. That is where the case breaks: an incumbent can crush them trivially - the TAK Product Center already ships a free government UAS Tool plugin and controls the signing path the startup must pass through; Auterion, Skydio and AV own the telemetry the product would need to become more than a checklist; and Anduril can expose the same blue-drone view inside Lattice for units already on its Army enterprise agreement - and there is no milestone that unlocks $2-5M because no requirement owner, program office or budget line exists to buy the result. The milestone that would justify a $2-5M raise - a paying battalion or brigade contract, or a T2COM/PEO Aviation RFI or OTA naming a vendor-neutral unit-level sUAS registry/deconfliction layer with funds attached - has no identified owner as of 2026-09-25, so the demo would at best yield an xTech prize or a small services engagement. The founders should treat this as a relationship-building side project and redirect the $250k to a gap where a budget line and a program office already exist.
score.bear_case_summary: The pain is real but the Army has chosen a $0 answer (CALL 25-14 procedural airspace control plus free TAK/CoT), no requirement, RFI, program office or budget line exists for a unit-level sUAS software layer, TITAN deliberately stops fusion at division, the vendor-neutral seam depends on telemetry APIs that direct competitors (Auterion, Skydio, AV, Gauntlet vendors) control and Anduril can absorb inside Lattice, the government's own TAK UAS Tool plugin already ships free, the mass drones are expendable so registry value is low, the integration cost curve is bespoke systems integration rather than product, and the founding team lacks the fatal-if-absent military airspace/UAS operator, unit access and SBIR eligibility - so the best case is a feature absorbed by a government team or Anduril, not a company.
score.bull_case_summary: Tens of thousands of multi-vendor drones are reaching squads faster than doctrine and tooling (12,080 Gauntlet accepted, 30,000 inbound, 60,000 expected from Gauntlet 2; 2,500+ X10D), units document hand workarounds (BARS marking, spreadsheets) because tracks do not populate the COP, no vendor is structurally able to be neutral across Auterion/Skydio/AV/Gauntlet ecosystems, TITAN leaves company/battalion without any fusion node, ATAK-CIV and CoT give a free open delivery path with no citizenship test, xTech/OTAs are open to foreign-person founders, allied armies (Germany, UK, Poland, NATO) want sensor-agnostic drone C2, and a team that reached a CTC-validated, unit-adopted workflow first could become the acquisition target of a vendor or the reference for a future T2COM requirement - the bull case is an acquisition or a follow-on requirement, not a standalone revenue line, and it rests on a demand signal that has not yet appeared.

verdicts.bear_case:
The card's own evidence base, cross-checked against a fresh budget search, supports refuting this as a venture-scale opportunity for a two-person founder team, though not the underlying operational pain, which is real.

1) No budget owner, no program element, no revenue path even in the loosest sense. The card's own budget section says "No dedicated program or budget line for a unit-level sUAS fleet/airspace/collection software layer identified" (confidence LOW). A fresh search (WebSearch, 2026-09-25) confirms the FY2027 Army small-UAS lines are FoSUAS ($349.6M procurement/RDT&E) and LASSO ($168.8M) — both airframe/system programs, not software. This is the IDIQ-ceiling trap inverted: there isn't even a ceiling to point to, only adjacent hardware dollars that a founder could wrongly imply are addressable. QUALITY RULE reminder applies directly: program ceiling ≠ obligated funds ≠ a software revenue line, and here there isn't even a program.

2) The Army's chosen institutional answer costs $0 and is explicitly designed for the no-connectivity case this product targets. CALL Handbook 25-14 (Sept 2025, army.mil, tier-1 FACT in the card) prescribes procedural airspace control (altitude blocks, ROZs, ACMs) "because communications are assumed limited." That is the Army choosing doctrine over software specifically for the degraded-comms scenario the startup's MVP is built to solve — a strong signal the buyer does not want a live fleet-picture product for this problem, it wants procedures. TAK/ATAK-CIV, the delivery vehicle the entry-vehicle plan depends on, is free and government-owned, so the default substitute for any UI layer is also $0.

3) Every seam this product would plug is already being closed by a vendor or prime with a stronger position, not by empty space. Auterion Nemyx already does cross-vendor CoT-to-ATAK fusion and won a Gauntlet production award (thedefensepost.com, 2025-09-05, tier-3 FACT/vendor-claim). AeroVironment/Tomahawk Kinesis is the RCCTO-named lead software/systems integrator for HMIF Increment 1 (avinc.com, 2025-09-29, tier-4 FACT). Anduril Lattice already markets "mission autonomy" that "translates operator intent into trusted machine-speed route, timing, tasking, and deconfliction decisions" for multiple unmanned aircraft (Anduril product pages, per WebSearch 2026-09-25) and holds an $87M JIATF-401 C-UAS C2 task order plus a >$20B Army enterprise agreement (defensescoop.com, 2026-03-14) — i.e., deconfliction-as-a-feature is already a marketed capability inside the dominant C2/autonomy vendor's stack, for free to units that already buy Lattice. Skydio Cloud already does single-vendor fleet health/telemetry for the largest SRR vendor. A generic commercial "UAS Operations & Fleet Management Software" category also already exists (unmannedsystemstechnology.com/AlarisPro, found via WebSearch), evidence this is a known, already-served software category with unclear defensible margin, not an empty white space.

4) The government's own fusion investment stops one echelon above the target market on purpose. TITAN production is sized for 17 systems total at division/corps (defensescoop.com, 2026-09-01, tier-2 FACT) — a deliberate choice not to fund fusion below division, which cuts against "the Army just hasn't gotten to this yet" optimism; it looks more like a considered echelon boundary.

5) The mass-volume driver undercuts the value proposition. Gauntlet drones are one-way-attack, expendable munitions (the card notes 12,080 accepted by Sept 2026, 30,000 more inbound, ~60,000 expected from Gauntlet 2 — DefenseScoop/Military Times, both 2026-09-18, tier-2 FACT). Per-airframe registry, qualification tracking and lifecycle status have low marginal value on a drone flown once into a target; the bulk of the "mass" the pitch cites is precisely the segment least amenable to a lifecycle-registry product. ISR-class volume (Skydio X10D, 2,500+ units/$52M+) is smaller and already has a single-vendor cloud solution.

6) No RFI, sources-sought or requirement document for this exact capability was found across the research (the card's own search log records this as a checked-and-negative result), only adjacent hardware RFIs (Company Level SUAS challenge) and a differently-scoped C-UAS software RFI (JIATF-401, which is about detecting enemy drones, not managing one's own fleet). Absence of a demand signal in six months of an active, well-funded, high-visibility program (Drone Dominance, Gauntlet I and II both completed) after CALL 25-14 was published a year earlier is meaningful, not just "public evidence insufficient" — if this were an urgent, fundable requirement, a PEO Aviation or T2COM-issued RFI would be the cheapest, fastest way to source it, and none exists.

7) Structural "consultancy trap": the target integration is inherently heterogeneous (multi-vendor by program design) and per-unit-customized (different ACOs, different vendor mixes, CUI unit records reachable only via sponsorship), and the card's own capital-required table shows costs scaling from $60-120k PoC to $2-5M "first production deployment" just to integrate 3-5 vendors for one brigade — a cost curve that looks like bespoke systems integration, not a repeatable SaaS product, reinforcing the card's own "killer_risk" conclusion that "the best case is a TAK plugin feature that a government team or Anduril absorbs, not a company."

Net: the operational pain (BARS hand-marking, no COP population, ad hoc training logs) is well-evidenced and real, but there is no budget owner, no requirement, a free doctrinal substitute, and multiple better-positioned incumbents already selling adjacent or superior versions of the core feature. This reads as a feature two or three players will add to existing platforms, not a venture-fundable standalone company for a $250k-capitalized two-founder team.
verdicts.strongest_single_argument: CALL Handbook 25-14 — the Army's own institutional response, published a full year before this study, tier-1 sourced — prescribes procedural (not software) airspace deconfliction specifically because comms are assumed unavailable; the buyer has already chosen and doctrinally codified the $0 alternative to the exact product being proposed, and no RFI or budget line has appeared since to contradict that choice.
verdicts.narrower_survivable_version: Do not build a live multi-vendor fleet-control/C2 product. Instead build the one piece leadership explicitly says is still missing and that nobody above is selling: an offline-first, vendor-agnostic operator/airframe qualification and training-readiness ledger (not real-time telemetry fusion) distributed as a free TAK-CIV plugin, monetized via a services/integration contract with a single sponsoring TiC battalion or CTC (JPMRC/JMRC/NTC) rather than as licensed software, explicitly positioned as a complement to CALL 25-14 procedures and to whichever vendor OS/Lattice/Kinesis layer the unit already has, rather than as a substitute for any of them. This avoids the two hardest, most contested claims (that cross-vendor live telemetry is obtainable without vendor cooperation, and that a software budget line exists) while still using the team's TAK/ATAK expertise and the genuine, well-evidenced training/readiness pain point.
verdicts.what_would_change_my_mind: A published PEO Aviation, T2COM, or division-innovation-cell RFI, sources-sought, or OTA specifically requesting a vendor-neutral unit-level sUAS registry/deconfliction/collection-forwarding capability (not hardware, not C-UAS, not a single-vendor cloud) with an identified funding vehicle; or evidence that a battalion/brigade actually paid for (not just tested) a third-party product of this kind at CTC; or a GAO/IG report specifically naming the absence of this capability as a fielding risk with a directed remediation budget.

verdicts.bear_case:
The G09 "squad-to-battalion small-UAS fleet control/registry/deconfliction/tasking/forwarding" opportunity is largely pre-empted or about to be pre-empted by incumbents already occupying exactly this stack, and the parts that remain genuinely open look more like training/SOP gaps than software-product gaps.

(1) Anduril already sells the product. Lattice for Mission Autonomy is explicitly marketed (FACT, anduril.com, retrieved 2026-09) as letting "a single human operator command and coordinate large, heterogeneous teams of autonomous systems," translating intent into "machine-speed route, timing, tasking, and deconfliction decisions," and combining "platforms, sensors, and payloads from any vendor." Anduril has purpose-built company/battalion-echelon hardware for this: Menace-T (human-portable) and Menace-X (expeditionary, DDIL-hardened), described as operating at brigade/battalion/company level. Anduril is not a hypothetical 6-month threat; it already holds the Army's ~$20B, 10-year enterprise software/hardware vehicle (2026-03-13 award, company record) and was named lead of the NGC2 common data-layer baseline (2026-06-22) with Raft explicitly building "registries, transformation and federation" for that layer. A startup solving squad-to-battalion drone registry either duplicates work Raft/Anduril are already contracted to do inside the Army's chosen data architecture, or must subordinate itself as a feed into Lattice/Raft — a dependency, not a wedge. WebSearch, 2026-09-24, anduril.com/lattice/mission-autonomy.

(2) The "position not on COP" pain point is materially undercut by government-owned, free infrastructure. ATAK/TAK (TAK Product Center, tak.gov) already ingests drone telemetry, gimbal angle and video into the COP as live CoT tracks via a UAS plugin or third-party CoT translators (DroneSense, uas-forge.com, corvusintell.com — WebSearch 2026-09-24), and CoT is a serverless, vendor-agnostic standard already fielded to every soldier's ATAK client. The specific step-3 pain in the gap card ("drone's position is not automatically on the common operating picture... units mark it by hand") is a fielding/configuration gap, not evidence the capability doesn't exist — TAK's CoT pipeline is exactly this capability and is free.

(3) Skydio, the SRR-T2 hardware incumbent with ~60k drones and 3,800 customers already fielded, already runs Skydio Cloud / Remote Flight Deck / Dock fleet-management infrastructure (company record) it could extend into registry/tasking features with zero new customer-acquisition cost, riding its existing installed base and its LRIP production contract.

(4) The Army's own institutional response to this exact problem (CALL Handbook 25-14, Sept 2025, army.mil, FACT/HIGH) is procedural — altitude blocks, ROZs, BARS hand-marking — not a call for a fleet-control software buy, and both 3rd CAB (JMRC April 2026) and 2-35 IN (JPMRC 26-01) built unit-level SOPs/plans rather than adopting a COTS registry tool. The Army's newest 2026-08-03 Call for Solutions for a "Battalion Reconnaissance UAS" addresses this echelon with a hardware acquisition, not software — signaling money and institutional attention are flowing to airframes, not fleet-management middleware. Breaking Defense (2026-09) and Military Times (2026-09-18) both frame the residual problem explicitly as training/EMS-contested proficiency ("Army has enough drones... needs the training"), which is a training-pipeline and doctrine problem, weakly monetizable as enterprise software, not a C2 product gap.

(5) Switching/architecture costs are real: any registry/deconfliction tool must plug into the Army's chosen NGC2 data mesh (Lattice + Foundry + Raft) to be usable at brigade ADAM/BAE and above, meaning a startup's product is at best a subordinate feed into an architecture Anduril/Palantir/Raft already control contractually, capping both margin and differentiation and exposing the startup to being cloned as a Lattice feature.

Net: nobody may be "making billions" from this narrow slice specifically because it is being absorbed into three larger, already-funded plays (Anduril/Lattice+Menace, the Raft/NGC2 data-layer registry, and free TAK/CoT), while the part that isn't absorbed (training/currency/EMS proficiency at squad level) is a services/schoolhouse problem with poor software margins, not the fused C2 capability G09 describes.
verdicts.strongest_single_argument: Anduril's Lattice for Mission Autonomy plus Menace-T/Menace-X already ships exactly the described capability set (multi-vendor drone tasking, route/timing/deconfliction, company-to-brigade echelon, DDIL-hardened) and rides an already-awarded $20B, 10-year Army enterprise vehicle with Raft contractually building the underlying registry/data-federation layer inside NGC2 — so the "no one owns this yet" premise is false at the architecture level, even if fielding to every unit is incomplete.
verdicts.what_would_change_my_mind: Evidence that units outside the NGC2/4ID-25ID prototype cohort (i.e., the broader FY26-27 mass of BCTs receiving Gauntlet/SRR drones under non-NGC2 divisions) have no path to Lattice/Menace or TAK-CoT integration and are contractually/technically barred from it for 12+ months; a named program of record or RFI specifically for a standalone battalion-echelon drone registry/deconfliction tool that Anduril/Raft/TAK do NOT already cover; or evidence that Lattice's per-seat/per-unit licensing or NGC2 rollout pace leaves the vast majority of drone-receiving battalions without any COP-integrated fleet tool through FY28.
verdicts.narrower_survivable_version: A narrow, TAK-plugin-native and Lattice/NGC2-compatible training-and-readiness layer — not a competing C2/registry product — that tracks operator qualification, currency, EW-contested proficiency, maintenance/battery state and unit-level airspace-SOP compliance for multi-vendor squad drones, exporting CoT-compatible status to ATAK/TAK and (optionally) Lattice rather than replacing either. This targets the training-pipeline gap that Breaking Defense/Military Times (Sept 2026) and the Army's own leadership describe as the actual unresolved bottleneck, sells to schoolhouses/Guard/Reserve/COE UAS master-trainer programs where Anduril and Palantir have weak footprint, and avoids head-on collision with the $20B Lattice vehicle and the NGC2 data-layer baseline. Revenue would likely be smaller and services-adjacent (training-system-as-a-service), which the founders should size honestly rather than assume C2-platform-scale contracts.

evidence.claim: Lattice for Mission Autonomy lets one operator coordinate heterogeneous, multi-vendor autonomous system teams with machine-speed route/timing/tasking/deconfliction; Menace-T/Menace-X are company/battalion/brigade-echelon, DDIL-hardened C2 hardware for this.
Army awarded Anduril a $20B, 10-year enterprise vehicle (2026-03-13) with counter-drone as an early focus area.
Army awarded Anduril $20B contract to deploy Lattice AI open architecture for battlefield integration.

ATAK/TAK ingests drone telemetry, gimbal angle and video as CoT tracks into the COP via UAS plugin or third-party translators (DroneSense, uas-forge, corvusintell); CoT works serverless across TAK-connected units.

CALL Handbook 25-14 (Sept 2025) documents the Army's current institutional answer to sUAS airspace integration as procedural controls (altitude blocks, ROZs, ACMs), not a fleet-control software tool, drawn from Transformation in Contact/CTC rotations.
Army says it has enough drones fielded to units but the remaining work is training soldiers, especially in contested EMS, ahead of the end-of-Sept-2026 squad-fielding deadline.

Army Contracting Command issued an Aug 3, 2026 Call for Solutions for a battalion-organic Battalion Reconnaissance UAS (hardware acquisition, not a software/C2 tool) to close battalion-level recon/security gaps.
NGC2 common data-layer baseline (2026-06-22) names Raft for registries/transformation/federation under Team Anduril, inside the Army's chosen NGC2 architecture that other vendors must integrate into.

verdicts.bear_case: Six compounding problems refute G09 as a venture-scale opportunity for this team. (1) The government already gives away the core wedge for free: TAK Product Center's "UAS Tool" plugin (AFRL-origin, government-owned, free to all registered TAK.gov users) already provides UAS situational-awareness, telemetry, FMV and C2 integration inside ATAK/WinTAK -- the same layer the gap card's technical_wedge proposes to sell (FACT, confirmed this session: https://tak.gov/products, https://www.civtak.org/2021/09/22/uas-tool-now-publicly-available/). Whoever controls TAK/CoT and plugin signing (Army C5ISR Center/TAK Product Center) can ship a competing free government plugin at any time, and the gap card itself concedes "the startup controls none of them" for every listed interface (ATAK/TAK, vendor clouds, FAAD C2, TITAN). That directly answers "why isn't anyone making billions" -- because the baseline capability is government-owned infrastructure given away, not a purchasable product category. (2) This is not white space, it's a graveyard: the Army has repeatedly started and killed common-controller/cross-vendor UAS control efforts (BCT Common Controller, Unmanned Common Controller study, and most recently "Army halts tactical UAS competition without clear plan forward," Defense News, 2025-05-16, plus cancellation of the Future Tactical Uncrewed Aircraft Systems program). A two-person startup building "the common layer" is stepping into a documented pattern of institutional restart/cancellation, not an overlooked niche. (3) No demand signal exists in this exact form: the card's own evidence explicitly states no RFI or sources-sought for a unit-level multi-vendor fleet/registry/deconfliction layer was found, and the Army's actual fielded answer (CALL Handbook 25-14, Sept 2025) is procedure, which costs nothing -- a classic false-positive gap where absence of competition reflects absence of a buyer, not opportunity. (4) The load-bearing technical assumption fails for the fleet that matters: cross-vendor telemetry ingestion works for owned PX4/ArduPilot hobbyist drones, but Skydio requires Cloud API partner access, Auterion CoT requires partnership, and Gauntlet-vendor telemetry formats are "not public" per the card -- exactly the vendors (Auterion, winner of a Gauntlet production award; AeroVironment/Tomahawk, named lead integrator for HMIF) who have every commercial incentive to keep their APIs closed to a would-be aggregator competing with their own fleet-management products (Skydio Cloud, Nemyx, Kinesis). (5) Regulatory access blocks the militarily useful version specifically for this team: per E07, SBIR/STTR is closed to a majority-foreign cap table (13 CFR 121.702) until the German founder's PR is granted (timeline uncertain), the Indonesian founder's equity never counts; real ACOs and unit records are CUI reachable only via unit sponsorship and likely a Technology Control Plan; and 9D610-type technical data from Gauntlet vendors would trigger a BIS deemed-export review for the Indonesian founder. The unclassified/EAR99 MVP (synthetic ACO data, 3 hobbyist drones) that avoids these constraints is exactly the version no battalion S3-air NCO will adopt over CALL 25-14 procedures and spreadsheets, while the version units would actually value (real ACOs, real Gauntlet telemetry, C-UAS C2 feed) walks straight into the regime that structurally excludes this founding team today. (6) Cost and timeline exceed the stated resources on the card's own numbers: PoC is estimated at $60k-$120k (already at or above the "$100k MVP" bar before travel or vendor-partnership costs), credible military demo $400k-$900k, and first production deployment $2M-$5M over 18-24 months -- 10-20x the $250k founder capital, funded only if an OTA/CSO/xTech prize or vendor partner materializes, none of which is secured. Given the Army's history of 1-2+ year competition halts and multi-year controller-program restarts, a 5-year path to a real production contract is the base case, not a pessimistic one. The card's own incumbent-response section concedes the honest expectation is "acquisition or displacement by a TAK-native tool unless the team reaches a CTC-validated, unit-adopted workflow first" -- i.e., the analysts who built this card already flagged the moat as thin.
verdicts.strongest_single_argument: The exact product category (multi-vendor UAS telemetry/SA/C2 fused into ATAK/WinTAK) is already shipped for free by the government's own TAK Product Center "UAS Tool" plugin to every registered TAK.gov user, and that same office controls plugin signing for the platform the startup must live inside -- so the wedge is competing against a free, incumbent, government-owned baseline rather than filling an empty category.
verdicts.narrower_survivable_version: Strip out live cross-vendor telemetry fusion and C-UAS/C2 integration entirely (the parts that require vendor API cooperation and eventually CUI/deemed-export exposure). Build only an offline-first UAS operator/airframe/battery/qualification registry and training-readiness ledger, plus a procedural pre-flight deconfliction checklist that checks a planned flight against unit-authored (not real classified) ACO/ACM data -- sold to battalions/CTCs as a training-and-readiness administrative tool, not a live fleet-control or C2 product. This sidesteps vendor API gatekeeping, avoids CUI/9D610 exposure by using synthetic or unit-generated data, and doesn't compete head-on with the free TAK Product Center UAS Tool plugin or with Auterion/AeroVironment/Anduril's live C2 ecosystems -- but it is a much smaller, harder-to-defend product (paperwork/checklist software) that still needs a unit sponsor to matter and may not clear the bar for venture-scale outcomes.

card.title: Vendor-agnostic automated PACE/multi-path transport orchestration and single-pane tactical NetOps for S6/G6 at brigade and below (MANET, pLEO, GEO, private 5G, HF)
card.problem: Brigade-and-below units now carry three to five transports (MANET, pLEO, GEO, private 5G, HF) but path selection/failover and network status are still executed by signal soldiers through separate vendor consoles and paper PACE plans, so applications stall during jamming or movement and link/spectrum/cyber awareness is manual and slow.

user.exact_role: Battalion/brigade S6 (signal officer) and the brigade/division NetOps cell (25-series signal soldiers, network technicians 255A/255N), plus platform/vehicle crews who physically switch transports; NGC2 transport-layer integrators on the vendor side
user.echelon: Battalion through division, with the operational pain concentrated at brigade and below where signal staff are smallest

25th Infantry Division (NGC2/C2 Fix, Lightning Surge)
III Armored Corps and I Corps (baseline NGC2 recipients 2026)

NETCOM / Army CIO-G6 (Unified Network Plan 2.0 owner)
USSOCOM (TACLAN/SDN 'King for a Day' RFI, May 2026)

current_workflow: S6 writes the PACE plan for each echelon/net in an OPORD Annex H or spreadsheet before the mission; transport priorities are static and by-hand

Each transport is configured in its own tool: MANET radios (Silvus StreamCaster / Persistent MPU5 / L3Harris Falcon) in vendor managers or INB2, SATCOM terminals in the terminal vendor GUI, Starlink/pLEO in the provider app, private 5G in the core vendor console, crypto and routers separately
During operations a link degrades (jamming, terrain, movement, weather); the first indicator is usually user complaints (chat, voice, stalled COP/TAK sync) rather than an alert
A soldier diagnoses by checking consoles one by one or by radio call, then manually switches to the alternate transport: re-routes, re-keys, re-addresses, re-registers services
Applications (fires, COP, logistics, chat) re-sync or the data is re-entered by hand; some state is lost
Network status is transcribed into PowerPoint/Excel for the commander's update; spectrum deconfliction with S2/EW is done manually and after the fact
card.current_solution: Manual PACE plus a patchwork: CodeMettle INB2 (fielded battalion-and-below NetOps on the RAP-TR platform, monitoring tactical radios and waveforms); UNO/TNO prototypes (RII with CodeMettle, QinetiQ US, via the C5 consortium) for enterprise-to-tactical DODIN ops; Army 'Seeker' Auto-PACE software installed by PM Tactical Network to aggregate and fail over SATCOM/troposcatter/TRILOS/cellular links at higher echelons; vendor-native tools (Persistent Cloud Relay hub router, Silvus management, Anduril Lattice Mesh on Klas Voyager hardware); SD-WAN appliances; DARPA MINC research prototypes (Peraton Labs, BAE) for autonomous heterogeneous network control.
card.failure: No fielded, radio-vendor-agnostic controller at brigade and below that sees all transports (MANET from several vendors, pLEO, GEO, 5G, HF), measures per-link quality, and moves application flows by policy; Seeker-class Auto-PACE lives at the SATCOM/hub layer and does not reach into MANET vendors' management planes; INB2/UNO consolidate status views but do not automate failover across new commercial transports; each vendor fix (Persistent, Anduril/Klas, Silvus) re-creates single-vendor lock-in; DDIL-tolerant status collection and automated status reporting remain manual.

card.why_existing_startups_havent_solved: Three structural reasons. (1) The management planes a controller needs are owned by radio vendors (Silvus/Motorola, Persistent, L3Harris, TrellisWare) who monetise their own controllers and, for PoR radios, sit behind Type-1 crypto and ITAR technical data; startups without radios, clearances and U.S.-person staff cannot even collect the telemetry. (2) The buyer has already chosen owners for each half: CodeMettle INB2 is the fielded battalion-and-below NetOps product with a 2025 sole-source-style license/PDSS action, UNO/TNO prototypes went to RII/CodeMettle and QinetiQ US through the C5 consortium, Seeker-style Auto-PACE is run by PM Tactical Network, and NGC2 transport is integrated by Anduril (now owning Klas) and Lockheed teams - the Army's stated preference is for the team lead to own integration. (3) Prior attempts stalled in prototype purgatory: DARPA MINC (Peraton, BAE) has no public transition, DIU ORIENT awardees (Aalyria, Viasat, Higher Ground, IoT/AI) hold prototype OTs, and the UNO MA IDIQ promised for 2025-2026 still cannot be confirmed - accreditation of anything in the encrypted path (CSfC/ATO) and exercise-slot scarcity slow every entrant to program timelines.
card.technical_wedge: Not the orchestrator itself (incumbent-held) but the missing open glue beneath it: a radio-agnostic transport telemetry and policy adapter layer - a small Linux/container agent on the existing edge box that speaks each transport's northbound interface (SNMP/REST/CLI for MANET radios and SATCOM modems, Starlink and 5G CPE APIs, HF ALE controllers), normalises per-link latency/loss/jitter/RSSI/SNR into one open schema, evaluates a declarative 'PACE-as-code' policy, and exposes NGC2-style non-proprietary APIs that INB2/TNO, Lattice Mesh or an SD-WAN can consume. Sold as a component to UNO/NGC2 teams and as a DDIL-tolerant telemetry/store-and-forward collector with auto-generated network status reporting for S6 cells. A second, lower-risk variant is the DDIL network emulation/test harness the Army is already funding through SBIR (Generative AI Enabled Tactical Network topic), which needs no ITAR radio data.

mvp.what: Container-based transport telemetry + PACE policy agent with adapters for four commercial transports (Doodle Labs or Rajant mesh radio, Starlink terminal, a private 5G CPE, an HF ALE modem or a second mesh), a per-flow path-selection policy engine, a DDIL-tolerant local time-series store that syncs when connected, and a browser HMI that renders link health and an auto-generated network status slide; TAK/CoT and a video stream as the applications.
mvp.demonstrable_in_3_6_months: 8-10 node field test on commercial hardware with induced degradation (attenuators, antenna shading, vehicle movement, RF interference within FCC rules) showing sub-second detection and automated flow migration versus manual switching, with published telemetry schema and adapter SDK; plus a network-emulation mode replaying recorded link traces.
mvp.what_it_must_prove: That a vendor-agnostic adapter layer can be written against public/commercial interfaces without vendor cooperation, that automated failover measurably beats manual PACE on time-to-recover and packet loss, that it runs inside a 100-200 W edge box footprint, and that a signal NCO can author policy without the vendor - and, critically, that at least one PoR radio vendor or NGC2/UNO team is willing to expose a northbound interface.

data_requirement.what: Per-link telemetry (latency, loss, jitter, throughput, RSSI/SNR, neighbor tables) from each transport; realistic tactical traffic profiles (TAK/CoT, VoIP, video, fires messages); recorded link-outage traces from movement/jamming; spectrum plans and PACE plans (typically CUI); management-interface documentation for PoR radios (ITAR-controlled for many).
data_requirement.legally_realistically_obtainable: Commercial-radio telemetry (Doodle Labs, Rajant, Starlink, 5G CPE, HF ALE) is obtainable by purchase and public docs. PoR radio management docs (Silvus, Persistent, L3Harris Falcon) generally require NDAs, U.S.-person handling and often ITAR licensing - a non-U.S.-person founder cannot lawfully receive that technical data without an export authorization; needs export counsel. Real jamming performance and Army spectrum/PACE plans are CUI or classified and are not obtainable pre-award; use synthetic traces and open network emulators.

incumbent_response.could_anduril_palantir_l3harris_add_it: Yes, easily. Anduril now owns both the NGC2 data-layer baseline and, via Klas, the edge network box; Lattice Mesh already claims multi-path data distribution and Anduril could expose a PACE policy layer as a Lattice feature. L3Harris and GDMS own PoR radio management planes and could extend them across transports. Motorola/Silvus and Persistent can extend proprietary controllers. CodeMettle/RII can add automation to INB2/TNO under existing UNO OTAs. None needs a startup's help to do it.
incumbent_response.why_startup_still_wins_or_reject: Mostly REJECT as a standalone company. The only defensible startup position is a neutral, open adapter/telemetry layer that vendors will not build because it commoditises their controllers - and that neutrality is exactly what incumbents and the buyer's prime-led model do not reward. A narrow win is possible only if CPE C2IN enforces its 'government-approved non-proprietary API' rule on the transport layer and buys the adapter layer separately, or if a second buyer (USSOCOM, ACC AMIC, an ally) wants freedom from the Army stack; neither is evidenced yet.

regulatory_burden.explanation: Software that manages military radios and encrypted transports touches ITAR technical data (radio management interfaces, waveform behaviour), CUI (network and spectrum plans), RMF/ATO on DODIN-A, potential NSA CSfC requirements, and usually SIPR-level integration requiring facility and personnel clearances. Commercial-hardware MVPs avoid most of this until the first PoR integration, after which the burden arrives all at once.
regulatory_burden.non_us_person_founder_note: A non-U.S.-person co-founder cannot receive ITAR technical data without an export license, cannot hold a security clearance, and can trigger FOCI mitigation if holding significant ownership or control; SBIR requires >50% U.S.-citizen/permanent-resident ownership. These are constraints to design around with export, immigration and government-contracts counsel, not a definitive legal judgment here.

dual_use_potential.explanation: Multi-transport failover and single-pane monitoring have commercial analogues in public safety (FirstNet + LMR + satellite), mining/energy (Rajant-class mesh + LTE + SATCOM), maritime and disaster response, and commercial SD-WAN already solves the wired/cellular/SATCOM version. The specifically military parts (MANET vendor adapters, PACE-as-code, EW awareness, DDIL reporting) have a thin commercial market, so dual-use exists for the platform but not for the differentiating features.

defensibility.explanation: The adapter library for many radios/terminals and its accreditation footprint are the only durable assets; algorithms for path selection are well known (MINC, SD-WAN). Telemetry datasets from exercises could become valuable for DDIL emulation but are typically government-owned. Defensibility is weak against vendors who own the interfaces.

card.why_now: Since 2023: commercial pLEO became a fielded Army transport (pLEO IDIQ 2023, ceiling raised to $13B Oct 2024, SpaceX SDN Backbone $2.29B May 2026); private 5G carried a live call-for-fire path at Lightning Surge (2026-04) and a simulated M777 mission at C5ISR Center (2026-05); NGC2 codified a distinct transport layer with government-approved non-proprietary APIs and moved from prototype OTAs (July/Sept 2025) to baseline fielding to I Corps and III Armored Corps (2026-09); UNO moved to OTA prototypes (2024-12, 2025-10) and INB2 was re-competed as a license/PDSS action (2025-05); PC-C6 still logged semi-frequent connectivity drops (2026-07). The multi-transport problem now exists at scale for the first time, but the buyer is simultaneously locking in who solves it.
card.killer_risk: The slot is already taken and gated: CodeMettle INB2 (fielded, sole-source-style 2025 action) and the RII/CodeMettle/QinetiQ UNO prototypes own NetOps; PM Tactical Network already runs Seeker Auto-PACE; Anduril (with Klas) and Lockheed own NGC2 transport integration and the Army wants team leads to own integration; radio vendors own the APIs and have every incentive to keep them closed. A two-founder team with one non-U.S.-person founder cannot legally access the ITAR radio data needed to build cross-vendor adapters, so the MVP would be confined to commercial radios that the Army does not field at scale - producing a demo the buyer cannot use.

card.allied_extension: Somewhat more compelling with allies, for a specific reason: allied land forces (Germany D-LBO/TaWAN LBO with Rheinmetall/blackned, UK LE TacCIS/TRINITY, Nordic Bittium framework, Japan ATLA mobile comms prototype) are each buying new multi-transport tactical networks in 2025-2029 and are less locked to U.S. radio vendors, so a radio-agnostic adapter layer has more open interfaces to work against, and a German founder has a natural route into the Bundeswehr ecosystem (blackned, Rheinmetall) where ITAR does not gate the commercial radios used. Counterpoints: the allied 'integration layer' slot is also incumbent-held (Rheinmetall/blackned, Systematic, Thales), coalition interoperability is measured at CWIX/Bold Quest around FMN standards rather than PACE automation, and allied budgets for NetOps software are smaller and slower. Net: allied extension improves feasibility of building the product (interface access) more than it improves the market size.
