score.title: Vendor-agnostic automated PACE/multi-path transport orchestration and single-pane tactical NetOps for S6/G6 at brigade and below (MANET, pLEO, GEO, private 5G, HF)

scores.rationale: FACT/HIGH: the Army's own UNO page states the goal is to 'simplify and reduce the number of network management tools' S6s/G6s use (https://peoc3t.army.mil/i2s/uno.php, 2024-2025); FACT/MEDIUM: PC-C6 (July 2026) still logged 'semi-frequent connectivity drops' at division scale (DefenseScoop 2026-07-31). Stalled fires/COP traffic during jamming or movement is operationally serious, though not the single limiting factor for the formation.

INFERENCE/MEDIUM: every movement, terrain change or jamming event on a 3-5 transport network forces a manual PACE decision; the pain recurs in every exercise cited (Ivy Sting, Lightning Surge 2026-04, PC-C6 2026-07) and in daily garrison-to-field transitions. Not 5 because the sharpest failures cluster around contested/EW conditions rather than continuously.

FACT/MEDIUM: money exists in the NGC2 C2 Transport sub-line (~$1.36B FY26 request; DefenseScoop 2025-07-02) but it is integrated by team leads (Anduril, Lockheed), not disbursed to a neutral adapter vendor; UNO/INB2 licensing amounts are not public; FY26 NDAA 50% obligation cap and HASC FY27 $710M proposed cut (GAO-26-108019, 2026-08-20) constrain the line. No identifiable budget line buys 'vendor-agnostic orchestration' as such. Requests are not obligations.

Score of 1 explained: every slot is held by an incumbent under a live action - CodeMettle INB2 with a May-2025 sole-source-style license/PDSS notice (fbodaily 2025-05-30, FACT/MEDIUM), UNO prototype OTAs to RII/CodeMettle and QinetiQ US via C5 consortium (ASDNews 2024-12-30), NGC2 OTAs to Team Anduril and Team Lockheed (army.mil 287180, 2025-07) with the Army preferring team-lead integration. The UNO MA IDIQ cannot be confirmed as awarded (Public evidence insufficient). Only entry is as a sub-tier component supplier to one of these primes; no open competition a new entrant could win is evidenced.

INFERENCE/MEDIUM: policy-based multi-path failover over commercial transports is a solved SD-WAN-class problem and a container agent with SNMP/REST adapters is buildable; but the hard part - normalising MANET vendor telemetry and moving flows without vendor northbound APIs - is unproven (DARPA MINC with Peraton/BAE has no public transition; DIU ORIENT awardees remain prototype-stage per public evidence).

HYPOTHESIS (card estimates, unsourced): $150k-$350k buys a commercial-hardware proof of concept, but a credible military demo is estimated at $1.5M-$3M because it needs PoR-class radios, cleared U.S.-person engineers and exercise participation. $250k covers only the PoC, which the card itself says produces 'a demo the buyer cannot use'.

INFERENCE/MEDIUM: a commercial-transport field demo (Doodle Labs/Starlink/5G CPE/HF ALE) is achievable in 3-6 months, but a demo the Army recognises requires PoR radio adapters (ITAR/NDA-gated), a NetModX or exercise slot and prime sponsorship - 12-18 months minimum and gated on vendor cooperation that is not evidenced.

FACT/MEDIUM: commercial radio, Starlink and 5G CPE telemetry are obtainable by purchase and public docs; but PoR radio management-interface docs (Silvus, Persistent, L3Harris) require NDAs, U.S.-person handling and often ITAR authorisation, and real jamming traces, spectrum and PACE plans are CUI/classified and not obtainable pre-award (card data_requirement; E07).

Score of 1 explained: the product sits on ITAR technical data (radio management planes), CUI (network/spectrum plans), RMF/ATO on DODIN-A, potential NSA CSfC review and SIPR-level integration needing facility and personnel clearances (card regulatory_burden 'high'). Per E07 (FACT/HIGH): 22 CFR 120.62/126.18 give no deemed-export exception for a domestic foreign-person employee, so the Indonesian founder would need a DSP-5 license to receive PoR radio data; 32 CFR 117 FOCI treats any non-citizen as a foreign interest; SBIR requires >50% U.S.-citizen/LPR ownership (13 CFR 121.702). These are constraints requiring export, immigration and government-contracts counsel, not legal conclusions - but they are unusually dense for this gap.

INFERENCE/MEDIUM: the MVP is fully unclassified on commercial hardware with synthetic traces, and the DDIL emulation variant stays unclassified indefinitely; but the card rates classification dependence 'eventually' - the first PoR integration and any TNO/UNO SIPR work bring CUI, ITAR and clearance needs all at once.

Score of 1 explained (5 = least intense): eleven named competitor groups occupy every layer - CodeMettle (INB2, fielded), RII and QinetiQ US (UNO OTAs), Anduril+Klas and Lockheed (NGC2 full stacks), Persistent (Cloud Relay; NGC2 network selection 2025-10), Silvus/Motorola (closed 2025-08, SEC 8-K), L3Harris/GDMS (PoR radios), PM Tactical Network's Seeker Auto-PACE, Peraton/BAE (MINC), Aalyria/Viasat/Higher Ground/IoT-AI (ORIENT), REDCOM. Most are well capitalised and hold the interfaces.

FACT/MEDIUM: incumbents have visible weaknesses - tool sprawl persists despite INB2, PC-C6 still had connectivity drops, Seeker does not reach MANET management planes, and each vendor fix re-creates single-vendor lock-in - but they own the contracts and APIs and can each add automation under existing OTAs ('None needs a startup's help', card incumbent_response). Vulnerability is real for the buyer, not exploitable by an outsider.

Score of 1 explained: the card's who_controls_the_interface states a startup controls none of the required interfaces - radio/terminal vendors control device APIs, CPE C2IN and NGC2 team leads control NGC2 APIs (schemas 'still being co-defined'), PdM TCNO and its primes control TNO/INB2 points, NSA/CSfC governs the encrypted path. No PoR radio vendor is evidenced to expose a licensable northbound API to third parties, and vendors have commercial incentive not to (Persistent expanding closed Cloud Relay to Azure, 2025-09/10).

INFERENCE/MEDIUM: path-selection algorithms are well known (MINC, SD-WAN); the only durable assets would be an adapter library and an accreditation footprint, both of which depend on access the vendors control and which incumbents could replicate under their existing contracts (card defensibility: 'weak against vendors who own the interfaces').

INFERENCE/MEDIUM: multi-transport failover and single-pane monitoring have commercial analogues (public safety FirstNet+LMR+SATCOM, mining/energy mesh+LTE+SATCOM, maritime, disaster response), but commercial SD-WAN already covers the wired/cellular/SATCOM case and the differentiating military features (MANET adapters, PACE-as-code, EW awareness) have a thin commercial market (card dual_use 'medium').

FACT/MEDIUM: second buyers voice the same need (USSOCOM TACLAN/SDN 'King for a Day' RFI 2026-05-15; ACC AMIC Deployable Tactical Communications RFI, responses due 2026-02-25) and allied land forces (D-LBO, LE TacCIS) are re-buying multi-transport networks, so a working product could expand into spectrum/cyber awareness and other services - but these are RFIs, not awards, and the allied integration slot is also incumbent-held (Rheinmetall/blackned, Systematic, Thales).

INFERENCE/MEDIUM: NetOps software is bought as enterprise licenses plus PDSS/sustainment (INB2 May-2025 action shows the recurring-license model) and per-division-set deployment would recur across NGC2 fielding; but the amounts are not public and the recurring stream accrues to whoever holds the license, currently CodeMettle.

Score of 1 explained: three of five required roles the card marks fatal_if_absent (recent Army signal officer/255N, tactical RF/MANET engineer, cleared U.S.-person ITAR-handling engineer) are absent; the Indonesian founder cannot lawfully receive the PoR radio technical data the adapter layer needs without a DSP-5 (22 CFR 120.62/126.18, E07 FACT/HIGH) and cannot hold a clearance; the German founder is clearance-eligible only after naturalisation (~2031-2032 at earliest, INFERENCE); SBIR >50% U.S.-person ownership must be engineered on the cap table; and ~$250k is roughly one-tenth of the estimated cost of a credible military demo. The German founder's route into the Bundeswehr D-LBO/blackned ecosystem is the one genuine fit, but that is an allied market, not the founders' stated primary U.S. target.

market.summary: No distinct budget owner for vendor-agnostic PACE orchestration; NGC2 transport money is integrated by primes (Anduril/Klas, Lockheed), UNO/INB2 amounts are not public and Congress has capped/cut the NGC2 line; demand signal is RFI/exercise-shaped, not purchase-order-shaped (2022 requirement still unfielded cross-vendor in 2026); addressable spend for a neutral adapter vendor is plausibly tens of millions over several years versus $1.5M-$3M demo and $8M-$15M deployment cost estimates. Weighed: ACCEPTED - the card and my own read find no budget line or vehicle that pays a neutral third party.

competition.summary: Both halves are already government-assigned: CodeMettle INB2 (fielded, sole-source-style 2025 action) owns single-pane NetOps; PM Tactical Network runs Seeker Auto-PACE; Anduril and Lockheed hold NGC2 full-stack OTAs (transport through application) and Anduril's Klas acquisition closed the edge-box seam; radio vendors (Silvus/Motorola, Persistent, L3Harris) own the telemetry APIs with no incentive to open them; MINC and ORIENT stalled in prototype purgatory; UNO MA IDIQ unconfirmed. Weighed: ACCEPTED - the strongest of the three; the incumbent_response section of the card reaches the same 'mostly REJECT' conclusion.

feasibility.summary: ITAR (22 CFR 120.62/126.18) blocks the non-U.S.-person founder from PoR radio management data without a DSP-5; FOCI and clearance rules exclude both founders from SIPR-level integration for years; SBIR ownership test requires cap-table restructuring; capital covers ~10% of a credible military demo; the commercial-hardware MVP 'produces a demo the buyer cannot use'. Weighed: ACCEPTED - cross-checked against evidence/E07.json, which supports each regulatory claim at FACT/HIGH; these are constraints for counsel, not legal conclusions, but they are dispositive for sequencing.

score.verdict_rationale: All three skeptics refute with strength 4-5 and I find no evidence that rebuts them; the card's own incumbent_response ('Mostly REJECT as a standalone company') and killer_risk sections agree. Applying the chain test: PROBLEM (documented, FACT/HIGH) -> USER (S6/G6 NetOps cells, FACT) -> REQUIREMENT OWNER (Army CIO/G-6 Unified Network Plan 2.0, C2 CFT; INFERENCE) -> PROGRAM OFFICE (PdM TCNO / PM Tactical Network inside CPE C2IN; FACT, post-reorg names unverified) -> CONTRACTING OFFICE (ACC-APG, C5 consortium/CMG; INFERENCE) -> BUDGET (NGC2 transport sub-line and UNO/INB2 O&M; exists but prime-channelled and congressionally constrained) -> CONTRACT VEHICLE: BREAK. Every vehicle at the end of the chain (INB2 sole-source-style license, UNO OTAs to RII/QinetiQ, NGC2 OTAs to Anduril/Lockheed) is held by an incumbent, and the UNO MA IDIQ that would open competition cannot be confirmed awarded (Public evidence insufficient). The major penalty applies. Two independent, individually sufficient kill reasons remain: (1) market/structural - the buyer procures prime-led, vertically integrated stacks and radio vendors own the northbound interfaces, so a neutral orchestration layer has no buyer and no interface access, as four to five years of MINC/ORIENT/UNO prototype purgatory demonstrate; (2) team-specific - the one asset that would make the product usable by the Army (cross-PoR-vendor adapters) requires ITAR technical data the Indonesian founder cannot lawfully receive and clearances neither founder can hold, while $250k funds only a commercial-radio demo the card itself calls 'a demo the buyer cannot use'. Confidence in the kill is HIGH on direction even though several individual facts (Seeker article date, Persistent $87.5M award, UNO IDIQ status) are MEDIUM/LOW and not re-verified this session; none of them would flip the verdict if corrected. The narrower variants the skeptics offer (DDIL emulation harness; commercial-only SD-WAN for public safety/mining) are not G10 surviving - they address a different pain (test/training tooling; non-defense connectivity) and should be evaluated as separate candidates, not carried forward under this gap.
score.narrower_version_if_borderline: Not borderline - killed. For completeness, the only adjacent variant all three skeptics agree is survivable is NOT the orchestrator: a DDIL network-emulation / hardware-in-the-loop test harness (synthetic and recorded link traces, commercial mesh/Starlink/5G CPE hardware, no ITAR radio data, no crypto path) aimed at the Army SBIR 'Generative AI Enabled Tactical Network' topic (armysbir.army.mil, 2025) and sold to UNO/NGC2 primes as a test tool. It is legally accessible to both founders today but is a smaller, services-adjacent tooling market with the same SBIR >50% U.S.-person ownership constraint (13 CFR 121.702), and it should be scored as its own gap rather than as G10. A second adjacent path - the German founder entering the Bundeswehr D-LBO/blackned/Rheinmetall ecosystem where commercial radios are not ITAR-gated - improves interface access but not market size and contradicts the founders' primary U.S. focus.
score.most_important_question_answer: If two exceptionally capable founders had $250,000 today and insisted on this gap, the only thing they could legally and affordably build first is a container-based transport-telemetry and PACE-as-code agent on commercial hardware: Doodle Labs or Rajant mesh, a Starlink terminal, a private-5G CPE on Open5GS, an HF ALE modem, a per-flow policy engine, a DDIL-tolerant local time-series store and a browser HMI that auto-generates the S6's network status slide, with a published open telemetry schema and adapter SDK (roughly $150k-$350k, HYPOTHESIS). They would show it to a division G6 of an NGC2 unit (4ID, 25ID, III Corps, I Corps) and to PdM TCNO through a NetModX or xTech entry, and the 8-10 node field test with induced degradation would prove sub-second detection and automated flow migration versus manual PACE on time-to-recover and packet loss. The customer would care because PC-C6 still produced semi-frequent connectivity drops (DefenseScoop 2026-07-31) and the Army's own UNO goal is fewer tools and less signal-soldier workload. But this is exactly where it fails: the demo runs on radios the Army does not field at scale, and the step that would make it usable - adapters for Silvus, Persistent and L3Harris PoR radios - requires ITAR technical data and vendor NDAs that the Indonesian founder cannot receive without a DSP-5 and that the vendors have no incentive to grant, while Anduril (owning Lattice Mesh and the Klas edge box under an NGC2 full-stack OTA), Lockheed, CodeMettle/RII under existing UNO OTAs, and PM Tactical Network's Seeker can each add a policy layer inside contracts they already hold. An incumbent does not need to crush them; it only needs to keep the interface closed. The milestone that would justify the next $2-5M - a signed, licensable northbound API agreement with at least one PoR radio vendor plus a subcontract letter from a UNO or NGC2 prime for a specific component, with a U.S.-person-controlled cap table and a cleared engineer in place - is precisely the milestone this team, as constituted and capitalised, has no evidenced path to reach, which is why the gap is killed rather than deferred.
score.bear_case_summary: The problem is real but every slot is taken and gated: CodeMettle INB2 holds fielded battalion-and-below NetOps under a 2025 sole-source-style action; UNO prototypes belong to RII/CodeMettle and QinetiQ US; PM Tactical Network already runs Seeker Auto-PACE at the hub layer; Anduril (with Klas) and Lockheed own NGC2 transport-through-application stacks and the Army wants team leads to integrate; Silvus/Motorola, Persistent and L3Harris own the northbound APIs and are consolidating rather than opening them. Better-funded neutral attempts (DARPA MINC, DIU ORIENT) have not transitioned in 4-5 years. Budget exists only as prime-channelled NGC2 money that Congress has capped and proposed cutting, and no line buys a neutral orchestrator. For this team specifically, the adapter layer needs ITAR-controlled radio data the Indonesian founder cannot lawfully receive, clearances neither founder can hold for years, an SBIR cap table that must be restructured, and $1.5M-$3M for a demo the Army would recognise against $250k in hand.
score.bull_case_summary: The pain is documented by the Army itself (UNO's stated goal of fewer tools; PC-C6 connectivity drops; a 'multi-path transport-agnostic' requirement standing since December 2022), multi-transport networks (MANET, pLEO, GEO, private 5G, HF) now exist at scale for the first time, NGC2 nominally requires 'government-approved non-proprietary APIs' at the transport layer, second buyers (USSOCOM TACLAN/SDN, ACC AMIC) are asking the same question in 2026 RFIs, and allied forces re-buying tactical networks are less locked to U.S. radio vendors. A neutral, open adapter and PACE-as-code layer is something no incumbent wants to build because it commoditises their controllers. If CPE C2IN enforced the non-proprietary-API rule as a separately procured line, or a PoR radio vendor published a licensable northbound API, or the UNO MA IDIQ opened with room for new entrants, the technical wedge would become a fundable component business - but none of these is evidenced today, and none is within this team's control.

verdicts.bear_case: Ask "why isn't anyone already making billions from cross-vendor tactical NetOps orchestration" and the card's own evidence answers it: the slots are already claimed and the money does not flow to a neutral third party. (1) No distinct budget owner exists for "vendor-agnostic PACE orchestration" as a buyable line item. The only budget the card cites is the NGC2 C2 Transport sub-line (~$1.36B FY26 RDT&E+Procurement within ~$3B-3.3B FY26 total, ~$3.78B FY27 request per DefenseScoop 2025-07-02, tier 2, MEDIUM confidence) — but that money is explicitly integrated by NGC2 team leads (Anduril/Klas, Lockheed), not disbursed to component vendors for an open adapter layer. UNO/INB2 O&M and licensing dollars are "not public" per the card itself, and the FY26 NDAA capped NGC2 obligation at 50% pending a report while HASC's FY27 mark would cut $710M (GAO-26-108019, 2026-08-20) — congressional skepticism is compressing exactly the discretionary budget a startup component would need to ride on. FACT/INFERENCE, MEDIUM confidence. (2) Every layer of the stated problem already has an incumbent with a live contract action: CodeMettle INB2 is fielded on RAP-TR with a May-2025 sole-source-style license/PDSS solicitation (FACT, MEDIUM); UNO/TNO prototyping already went to RII (prime) and QinetiQ US via the C5 consortium OTA (2024-12-30, FACT, MEDIUM) with CodeMettle as the Oct-2025 Phase II subcontractor; PM Tactical Network already runs "Seeker" Auto-PACE at the SATCOM/hub layer; Anduril (now owning Klas hardware) and Lockheed own NGC2 transport integration end to end, and the Army's own posture ("government-approved non-proprietary APIs... schemas still being co-defined") gives the team leads, not a startup, control of the interface. This is precisely the "it HAS been solved" reason the card itself lists in why_not_solved_reasons. (3) The demand signal is exercise-and-RFI shaped, not purchase-order shaped: nearly every piece of evidence is an RFI ("King for a Day," ACC AMIC), a prototype OTA, an xTech topic, or an exercise observation (Lightning Surge, PC-C6) rather than a production buy of a cross-vendor orchestrator — a multi-year pattern (2022 Breaking Defense call for "transport-agnostic" capability -> 2026 still no fielded cross-vendor product) that is exactly the "appears mainly in exercises/RFIs" bear pattern. (4) The technical reality forces a per-unit, per-radio-vendor integration: the card's own "who_controls_the_interface" section says a startup controls none of MANET, SATCOM, 5G, or crypto APIs, and northbound interfaces differ by vendor (Silvus/Motorola, Persistent, L3Harris, TrellisWare) — meaning "vendor-agnostic" software would, in practice, require bespoke adapters plus vendor cooperation per radio family, pulling the company toward a services/integration business rather than a scalable product, which the card implicitly concedes by scoping the MVP to commercial (non-PoR) radios only. (5) The single hardest constraint is founder-specific and dispositive for this team: PoR radio management interfaces are gated by ITAR technical-data controls and NDAs requiring U.S.-person handling; a non-U.S.-person founder (the Indonesian co-founder) cannot lawfully receive that data without an export authorization, and SBIR/xTech-SBIR requires >50% U.S.-citizen/permanent-resident ownership — meaning the two-founder team as described cannot legally build the one thing (cross-PoR-vendor adapters) that would make the product usable by the Army, confining any demo to commercial radios the Army does not field at scale. The card's own killer_risk section states this outright: "the MVP would be confined to commercial radios that the Army does not field at scale — producing a demo the buyer cannot use." (6) Estimated realistic addressable spend for a standalone open-adapter-layer company (not the NGC2/UNO totals, which are prime-controlled) is unquantified in the card and, on the balance of evidence, is plausibly in the tens of millions at most for a subcontract/component role over several years — nowhere near sufficient to underwrite the $1.5M-$3M "credible military demo" and $8M-$15M "first production deployment" capital estimates the card itself gives (HYPOTHESIS, unsourced), against ~$250k founder capital.
verdicts.strongest_single_argument: The card's own incumbent_response section concedes the point without qualification: "Anduril now owns both the NGC2 data-layer baseline and, via Klas, the edge network box; Lattice Mesh already claims multi-path data distribution... None needs a startup's help to do it," and separately verdicts "Mostly REJECT as a standalone company" — the strongest bear case is the analysis's own author already reaching the same conclusion from the buyer/competition evidence, independent of the ITAR/founder-eligibility problem.
verdicts.what_would_change_my_mind: Public evidence of (a) CPE C2IN actually enforcing its "government-approved non-proprietary API" mandate at the transport layer and issuing a separate solicitation for an adapter/telemetry layer decoupled from the NGC2/UNO primes, or (b) a second buyer (USSOCOM TACLAN, ACC AMIC, or an allied MoD) issuing an actual contract (not RFI) for cross-vendor orchestration software with a named budget line, or (c) at least one PoR radio vendor (Silvus, Persistent, L3Harris) publicly exposing a documented, licensable northbound API to third parties rather than keeping it proprietary.
verdicts.narrower_survivable_version: A narrower, ITAR-light variant could survive: sell the DDIL network-emulation/test-harness product only (no live PoR radio telemetry, no crypto path) against the Army SBIR "Generative AI Enabled Tactical Network" topic and xTechIgnite's DDIL/NGC2 simulation ask — this needs no ITAR radio data, fits the founders' current legal structure without an export license, and the card explicitly flags it as "a second, lower-risk variant... which needs no ITAR radio data." Alternatively, pursue the allied route (German founder into Bundeswehr D-LBO/blackned/Rheinmetall ecosystem) where non-U.S. radios are not ITAR-gated for a German entity, though the card itself notes the allied integration-layer slot is also incumbent-held (Rheinmetall/blackned, Systematic, Thales) and allied NetOps software budgets are smaller and slower — so this survives the "no budget owner" critique only partially and the "market too small" critique not at all.

verdicts.bear_case: The G10 opportunity as framed (a standalone vendor-agnostic PACE/multi-path orchestration + single-pane NetOps company) is effectively closed to a new two-founder entrant, and the evidence card's own "incumbent_response" and "killer_risk" sections concede this. Four independent lines converge: (1) Interface ownership: every transport's management plane is owned by an incumbent with every incentive to keep it closed - Silvus/Motorola (acquired 2025-08, SEC 8-K), Persistent Systems (Wave Relay/Cloud Relay, expanded to Azure Sep-Oct 2025), L3Harris (AN/PRC-163/158C), and these are largely PoR radios behind ITAR technical-data controls. A startup with no radios and no clearances cannot even collect the telemetry needed to build the "neutral adapter" the wedge depends on. (2) Both halves of the problem already have a government-picked owner: CodeMettle's INB2 is "currently fielded and deployed" on RAP-TR for battalion-and-below NetOps, with a May-2025 Army sole-source-style license/PDSS solicitation - the single-pane half is incumbent-held, not empty. PM Tactical Network already runs a government-installed "Seeker" Auto-PACE that aggregates and self-heals across SATCOM/troposcatter/TRILOS/cellular. (3) NGC2 vertical integration accelerated through 2026: fresh reporting (DefenseScoop 2026-06-22, army.mil 2026-06/07) confirms Anduril leads the "full stack" operational implementation for 4th ID and Lockheed Martin leads the "full stack" for 25th ID - i.e., the Army is explicitly buying prime-led, vertically-integrated stacks (transport through application layer) rather than opening a neutral integration-layer market; NGC2 now has baseline fielding to I Corps and III Armored Corps (2026-09-21). Anduril's Klas acquisition (closed July 2025) gave it the edge network/compute box too, closing the seam a startup adapter would sit in. This is consistent with the assignment's premise that a top-tier integrator "adds this in ~6 months" - Anduril/Lockheed are not adding a capability, they already sit astride the whole transport-to-application stack by contract. (4) Prior neutral/agnostic attempts have stalled for years without transition: DARPA MINC (2021 launch, Peraton Labs up to $20M/42mo, reported completion ~Feb 2025) has no public program-of-record transition; DIU ORIENT prototype OTs (Aalyria, Viasat, Higher Ground, IoT/AI, Nov 2024) remain prototype-stage per public evidence; the UNO Multiple-Award IDIQ that was supposed to open competition (RFIs 2023-2024) still cannot be confirmed as awarded as of 2026-09. Layered on top, the export-control/immigration facts in the card are close to fatal on their own: a non-U.S.-person founder cannot lawfully receive ITAR-controlled PoR radio management-interface data or hold the clearance needed for SIPR-level UNO/TNO integration, and SBIR (a primary funded entry vehicle the card proposes) requires >50% U.S.-citizen/permanent-resident ownership - meaning the stated founding team, as composed, cannot execute the card's own "entry_vehicle" plan without either restructuring equity/control (diluting the Indonesian founder's role, pending counsel) or confining the MVP to commercial-only radios the Army does not field at scale, which "produces a demo the buyer cannot use" (the card's own words). Commercial-hardware MVP demonstrations are cheap to build (Doodle Labs/Starlink/5G CPE, $150k-350k) but that is exactly why they are not evidence of a defensible business - SD-WAN-style multi-path failover on commercial gear is a solved, commoditized problem; the differentiated, valuable part (radio-vendor adapters, ITAR data, exercise accreditation) is precisely the part this team cannot legally reach without a U.S.-person-controlled cap table and cleared engineers, which is a headcount/capital problem beyond ~$250k founder capital.
verdicts.strongest_single_argument: The buyer has already assigned ownership of both halves of this exact problem to incumbents with contractual and technical control the startup cannot match: CodeMettle/INB2 owns fielded single-pane NetOps (sole-source-style 2025 Army action), and as of mid-2026 Anduril and Lockheed Martin each own the "full stack" (transport through application layer) for their respective NGC2 divisions - meaning the orchestration layer this gap targets is not an open integration slot but part of a prime's exclusive full-stack contract, while radio vendors (Silvus/Motorola, Persistent, L3Harris) control the very telemetry APIs a neutral adapter would need and have no commercial incentive to expose them.
verdicts.what_would_change_my_mind: Public evidence that CPE C2IN/PdM TCNO is actually enforcing a "government-approved non-proprietary API" requirement at the transport layer and procuring the adapter/telemetry function as a separate, vendor-agnostic line item open to new entrants (not just co-defining schemas per the RFI language) - or evidence that at least one PoR radio vendor (Silvus, Persistent, L3Harris) has published or licensed a northbound telemetry API to third parties - or a second buyer (USSOCOM, ACC AMIC, or an allied MoD) issuing a solicitation that explicitly excludes the Army prime-led model and funds an independent orchestration layer.
verdicts.narrower_survivable_version: The card's own "technical_wedge" is the survivable version: not a standalone PACE-orchestration company, but a narrow, radio-agnostic telemetry-normalization and PACE-as-code policy component built on commercial-transport APIs (Doodle Labs/Rajant mesh, Starlink local API, open 5G core/CPE SNMP, HF ALE) with an open adapter SDK, sold as a subcontracted component into a UNO prime (RII, CodeMettle, QinetiQ US) or entered via C5 consortium/xTech/NetModX - deliberately avoiding PoR-radio ITAR data and SIPR integration until a U.S.-person-controlled team and capital exist to pursue it. An even lower-risk adjacent variant, fully avoiding export-control exposure for the non-U.S.-person founder in the near term, is the DDIL network-emulation/test-harness tool funded under the Army SBIR "Generative AI Enabled Tactical Network" topic - unclassified, commercial-hardware-only, no ITAR radio data required - though this is a smaller, services-adjacent tooling market, not the described multi-billion-dollar orchestration opportunity, and still requires restructuring the cap table to satisfy SBIR's >50% U.S.-person ownership rule.

Motorola Solutions closed its acquisition of Silvus Technologies (dominant MANET radio vendor) in 2025-08, consolidating ownership of a key transport's management plane.
Anduril acquired Klas (edge network/compute hardware), closing 2025-07, pairing Lattice Mesh software with the compute box it runs on and further vertically integrating the transport/compute layer.

DARPA MINC (2021 launch, autonomous heterogeneous tactical network control, Peraton Labs up to $20M/42mo, BAE also a performer) has no public evidence of transition to a program of record as of the research card's compilation.
DIU ORIENT prototype OTs (Aalyria, Viasat, Higher Ground, IoT/AI) for long-haul-to-mesh connectivity, awarded 2024-11-20 from 130 proposals, remain at prototype stage per public evidence.

PC-C6 (July 2026), the division-scale NGC2 validation, still logged overheating hardware, incomplete data displays and semi-frequent connectivity drops, and GAO-26-108019 (2026-08-20) found the Army lacks a life-cycle cost estimate for NGC2 despite ~$3.3B identified through FY2026 - transport reliability and program cost/schedule risk remain unresolved even inside the incumbent-led effort.

verdicts.bear_case: G10's own evidence card effectively refutes itself. First, the problem is not empty: the two halves the opportunity would combine are already incumbent-owned. CodeMettle INB2 is fielded battalion-and-below NetOps software with a May-2025 Army sole-source-style license/PDSS action (FBO 2025-05-30); PM Tactical Network already runs an Auto-PACE capability called 'Seeker' at the SATCOM/hub layer (army.mil article 274494); UNO/TNO prototyping went to RII/CodeMettle and QinetiQ US through the C5 consortium (ASDNews 2024-12-30; PRNewswire 2025-10); and NGC2 transport integration is owned by Anduril (which bought Klas, closing July 2025, giving it the edge network/compute box and Lattice Mesh) and Lockheed Martin, with the Army's explicit preference that the prime team lead own integration. None of these incumbents needs a startup's help, and all have direct commercial incentive to keep the orchestration layer proprietary -- Persistent Systems is simultaneously expanding its own closed Cloud Relay hub router to Azure rather than opening APIs (PRNewswire 2025-09/10). The vendor-agnostic 'northbound API' the wedge depends on requires Silvus/Motorola, Persistent, or L3Harris cooperation that none has given; the card's own killer_risk section states 'A startup controls none of these' interfaces. Second, the requirement has existed since December 2022 (Breaking Defense, Army network plan calling for 'multi-path transport-agnostic' capability) and is still unsolved cross-vendor at brigade-and-below almost four years later, despite DARPA MINC funding Peraton Labs up to $20M/42 months and BAE Systems with no confirmed transition to a program of record, and DIU's ORIENT effort drawing 130 proposals and awarding prototype OTs to Aalyria, Viasat, Higher Ground and IoT/AI (DefenseScoop, 2024-11-20) that remain prototype-stage. Well-capitalized, cleared, connected teams have already tried and stalled in prototype purgatory -- a strong signal the bottleneck is structural (interface ownership + buyer's prime-led procurement model), not merely under-resourced engineering. Third, founder-fit is the sharpest constraint. Per evidence/E07.json: the Indonesian founder's equity never counts toward SBIR's >50% U.S.-citizen/permanent-resident ownership test (13 CFR 121.702), AFWERX explicitly limits foreign-national participation on DoD SBIR to public-domain/fundamental research performed inside the U.S. (AFRL-2025-3235, 2025-07-02), and ITAR (22 CFR 120.62, 22 CFR 126.18) offers no deemed-export exception for a domestic foreign-person employee -- a DSP-5 license naming the employee is required before the Indonesian founder could lawfully receive PoR radio (Silvus, Persistent, L3Harris) management-interface technical data, which the gap card itself flags as the exact data the adapter layer needs. FOCI rules (32 CFR 117.11) treat any non-citizen, including a green-card holder, as a 'foreign interest,' and personnel clearances require citizenship (EO 12968, SEAD 4), so the German founder is clearance-eligible only around 2031-2032 at the earliest via naturalization, and the Indonesian founder later still -- meaning for most of the company's early life neither founder can personally do the ITAR-gated radio integration work the wedge requires without walling themselves off and hiring a cleared U.S.-citizen engineer (a fatal_if_absent role the card itself lists). Fourth, the capital math does not close: the card's own founder-grade estimates put a credible military demo at $1.5M-$3M and first production deployment at $8M-$15M, while explicitly noting the founders' ~$250k 'covers only the proof of concept' -- and even that $150k-$350k proof of concept, built only on commercial hardware (Doodle Labs/Rajant mesh, Starlink, 5G CPE, HF ALE) because PoR radios are legally inaccessible to the team as structured, produces -- in the card's own words -- 'a demo the buyer cannot use,' since the Army does not field those commercial transports at scale. Fifth, PC-C6 (July 2026) still logged 'semi-frequent connectivity drops' after years of NGC2 investment (DefenseScoop, 2026-07-31), showing the underlying multi-transport reliability problem is harder than a policy-engine abstraction suggests, likely requiring RF/EW expertise, exercise access and vendor telemetry a two-person team cannot obtain quickly. Taken together: the buyer has already assigned owners to every layer of this problem, the interfaces a startup would need are controlled by parties with no incentive to open them, better-resourced federal efforts have not transitioned in ~4-5 years, and the specific legal status of one founder blocks the team from lawfully touching the data the product needs -- while the founders' capital covers roughly one-tenth of the estimated cost to reach a credible military demo.
verdicts.strongest_single_argument: The interfaces the product needs (PoR radio management planes) are ITAR-controlled technical data that a non-U.S.-person founder cannot lawfully receive without a DSP-5 export license (22 CFR 120.62/126.18), and the buyer has already assigned every adjacent layer of the problem to incumbents (CodeMettle/INB2, PM Tactical Network/Seeker, Anduril+Klas/NGC2, Persistent/Cloud Relay) who have both the access and the incentive to keep it closed -- so the achievable MVP is confined to commercial radios the Army does not field at scale, producing, in the gap card's own words, 'a demo the buyer cannot use.'
verdicts.what_would_change_my_mind: Evidence that (a) CPE C2IN has actually begun enforcing its 'government-approved non-proprietary API' rule as a separate acquisition line for the transport-telemetry layer rather than folding it into NGC2 prime scope, (b) at least one PoR radio vendor (Silvus, Persistent, L3Harris) has published or committed to a northbound telemetry API usable without an NDA/ITAR gate, (c) the UNO multiple-award IDIQ has actually been awarded with room for new entrants rather than remaining a RII/CodeMettle/QinetiQ-held prototype line, or (d) a credible non-defense (public safety, mining, disaster response) commercial multi-transport NetOps revenue base that could fund the defense wedge without upfront defense capital.
verdicts.narrower_survivable_version: Do not build the orchestrator itself. Instead build (1) the DDIL network-emulation/hardware-in-the-loop test harness explicitly flagged in the gap card as the lower-risk variant, sold into the Army SBIR 'Generative AI Enabled Tactical Network' topic and to UNO/NGC2 primes as a test tool -- it uses no ITAR radio data, only synthetic/recorded traces and commercial hardware, and is legally accessible to both founders; and (2) in parallel, a pure commercial-market multi-transport SD-WAN/NetOps product for public safety, mining, or maritime/disaster response (FirstNet+LMR+SATCOM analogues), generating non-defense revenue while the German founder's green card and eventual U.S.-citizen hires are secured, with the Indonesian founder kept structurally on the business/product side and walled off from any ITAR-touching engineering. Only after a cleared U.S.-citizen technical lead is hired and cap-table/SBIR ownership math is fixed should the team attempt a component subcontract into a UNO/NGC2 prime for the adapter layer.

card.title: Sensor-agnostic own-signature/EM COP fusion as a TAK plugin, with disconnected tactical spectrum management (JRFL, assignments, interference tickets) and emitter-library distribution to cheap sensor fleets
card.problem: Brigade and division CEMA cells and spectrum managers are receiving heterogeneous cheap spectrum sensors (S2AS kits, MOTH, Dragonfly, TLS-BCT manpacks) whose detections do not fuse into one government-owned, DDIL-tolerant electromagnetic picture inside TAK/EWPMT-X, while frequency plans, JRFLs and interference reports still depend on reach-back to DISA enterprise tools (Spectrum XXI/JSDR/EMBM-J).

user.exact_role: Brigade/division CEMA section chief and EW technician (170A/17E), brigade and division Electromagnetic Spectrum Manager (Army MOS 25E; USMC 0681-type spectrum managers), EW platoon leader in the Multifunctional Reconnaissance Company; secondary: JFMO/JEMSO cell staff
user.echelon: Brigade combat team and division main/tactical command posts; secondary corps/JTF JEMSO cell
organization_examples: 2nd Brigade, 25th Infantry Division (TiC)
2nd Brigade, 101st Airborne Division (TiC)
2nd Brigade, 10th Mountain Division (TiC)
1st Armored Brigade, 3rd ID (Combined Resolve 2025)
2nd Cavalry Regiment
USMC MEF/MEU spectrum sections
Combatant command J6 JFMO cells

current_workflow: EW platoon and command-post staff run vendor sensors (S2AS kit, TLS-BCT manpack, MOTH, Dragonfly, ad hoc SDRs) and read each vendor's own GUI or laptop app.
Detections and own-emission observations are relayed by voice/chat or typed into ATAK as Cursor-on-Target points; screenshots go into PowerPoint for the commander's update.

The 25E spectrum manager compares observed emitters against frequency assignments exported from Spectrum XXI/JSDR (SFAF records) and against the JRFL built per CJCSM 3320.01D, usually in spreadsheets when disconnected.
Interference (EMI) reports arrive by voice/chat; the spectrum manager triages manually against assignments and EW schedules and re-enters results into Spectrum XXI/JSDR when connectivity returns.
The CEMA officer builds the EM overlay in EWPMT/Raven Claw (being replaced by EWPMT-X on TAK) or by hand; higher echelons receive the picture hours later.
Sensor signal-of-interest libraries are updated per vendor through proprietary tools or reprogramming-center channels, not through a common distribution mechanism.
card.current_solution: Own-signature: S2AS (3dB Labs, production contract June 2026, UCA pathway, 9 systems delivered by late Aug 2026, 46 planned by July 2027). Threat/EW picture: TLS-BCT manpack (Mastodon Design/CACI, ~$100M award July 2024) with its own visualization; EWPMT/Raven Claw (Raytheon lineage) being re-hosted as EWPMT-X on TAK with USMC. Spectrum management: DISA Spectrum XXI/JSDR/GEMSIS and the cloud EMBM-J (initial features Dec 2023; EMBM-J Decision Support launched Apr 2025 with a Palantir-built prototype). Workarounds: spreadsheets, chat, PowerPoint, ad hoc ATAK plugins (Parsons TEMS, CTIC TAKX-RF, open-source ATAKRR).
card.failure: At the seam between many vendor sensor feeds and the government-owned TAK/EWPMT-X picture: no common detection schema or time-aligned fusion across S2AS, TLS-BCT, REWSI sensors and ad hoc SDRs; no offline-first tactical client for assignments/JRFL/EMI tickets that later syncs to JSDR/EMBM-J; and no cross-vendor mechanism to push updated signal libraries to cheap sensor fleets under DDIL. The government now owns the framework (TAK) but has not yet contracted anyone specifically to own the sensor-agnostic fusion logic (the EWPMT-X integrator is not public).

card.why_existing_startups_havent_solved: Sensor companies (Heaviside, RII, Distributed Spectrum, Anduril Pulsar/Lattice, 3dB Labs) monetize hardware plus their own visualization and have no incentive to build a vendor-neutral fusion layer; the government host only became fixed when the Army declared TAK the EWPMT-X framework in 2024, and the EWPMT-X integrator (not public) is the natural owner of fusion. The spectrum-management slice has a single captive buyer (DISA DSO) whose data of record (JSDR) is CUI and whose sanctioned answer is EMBM-J (Palantir prototype, GEMSIS sustainment contractor); a few thousand spectrum managers is too small a user base for venture returns. Emitter libraries are classified and vendor-channelled. Existing TAK RF plugins (TEMS, TAKX-RF, ATAKRR) show the plumbing is easy, which means the value is in exercise access, accreditation and data agreements rather than code.
card.technical_wedge: A government-ownable TAK Server microservice plus ATAK/WinTAK plugin that ingests detections from any sensor through an open schema (SigMF metadata plus Cursor-on-Target extensions, adapters for S2AS/MOTH/Dragonfly/TLS exports as they become available), time-aligns and deduplicates them under DDIL using CRDT-style replication, renders friendly-emitter heat maps and a command-post signature score against the unit's own frequency assignments (SFAF import), and produces JSIR-format interference tickets that queue offline and sync to Spectrum XXI/EMBM-J when connected. Emitter-library distribution is out of scope for a startup (classified, vendor-owned).

mvp.what: ATAK-CIV plugin + TAK Server plugin: open detection schema, adapters for two commercial SDR sensors (KrakenSDR for AoA, USRP/RTL-SDR for occupancy), DDIL sync, friendly-emitter heat map, own-signature score versus an imported SFAF assignment list, offline JSIR-style EMI ticket queue.
mvp.demonstrable_in_3_6_months: Two-founder build on ATAK-CIV SDK: live demo at a university/ROTC or National Guard field exercise showing a command post's emission footprint, sensor-agnostic ingest from two sensor types, and picture convergence after a simulated 30-minute network outage.
mvp.what_it_must_prove: (1) that heterogeneous sensor detections fuse into one picture with acceptable false-track rate; (2) that the picture survives DDIL and reconverges; (3) that a 25E can build a JRFL/EMI ticket offline faster than with spreadsheets; (4) that PM EW&C or the EWPMT-X integrator will accept a third-party TAK microservice rather than build it.

data_requirement.what: Sensor detections (frequency, bandwidth, power, bearing, timestamps, position), unit radio/emitter inventories, frequency assignments (SFAF/JSDR records - CUI), JRFL (CUI), exercise recordings of own emissions (CUI), and eventually threat emitter parametrics (classified).
data_requirement.legally_realistically_obtainable: Own-signature and commercial-band data can be self-collected with COTS SDRs at unclassified events; SFAF-format sample data and public ATP/CJCSM documents allow synthetic assignment data; real JSDR/JRFL and vendor sensor formats require a government sponsor (CRADA, OTA or SBIR) and CUI handling under DFARS 7012; threat libraries are classified and inaccessible to an uncleared team.

regulatory_burden.explanation: Software specially designed for military EW/ES/direction-finding is likely to be reviewed under USML Category XI (ITAR), triggering DDTC registration and deemed-export controls; commercial spectrum-monitoring on COTS SDRs may fall under EAR (5A001/5D001 or EAR99) depending on design intent - only a commodity jurisdiction/classification review by counsel can settle this. All DoD frequency plans, unit signatures and sensor positions are CUI from the first exercise (DFARS 252.204-7012, NIST SP 800-171, CMMC clause effective 2025-11-10). Threat emitter libraries and EWPMT-X classified integration require facility and personnel clearances (U.S. citizenship required).
regulatory_burden.non_us_person_founder_note: If the product is ITAR-controlled, sharing technical data with the Indonesian co-founder is a deemed export requiring DDTC authorization or a compartmented structure; the German founder becomes a U.S. person for ITAR only on issuance of permanent residence (22 CFR 120.62). Both founders are years from clearance eligibility. SBIR eligibility fails unless >50% of ownership/control is held by U.S. citizens/permanent residents. FOCI review (32 CFR 117.11; DoDI 5205.87 for some unclassified contracts) will surface both founders. Scoping the first product to EAR99/EAR dual-use spectrum monitoring (own-signature and interference only, no threat ID) is the usual mitigation; all of this requires specialist export-control and immigration counsel - no legal judgment made here.

dual_use_potential.explanation: Sensor-agnostic RF occupancy fusion, offline frequency-plan management and interference ticketing have civil analogues (public-safety event spectrum management, range and test-site monitoring, telecom interference hunting, regulators, airports/critical infrastructure C-UAS RF awareness), and TAK is used by DHS/CBP/public-safety agencies. But those buyers are few and price-sensitive (Aurora Insight ended in a Maxar acquisition rather than scale), so dual use reduces ITAR exposure more than it creates a large market.

defensibility.explanation: Code is not defensible (multiple TAK RF plugins exist and ATAK-CIV is open). Defensibility would come from vendor adapters negotiated with S2AS/REWSI vendors, SFAF/JSDR/EMBM-J interface agreements with DISA, TAK-GOV accreditation and ATO, exercise-derived own-signature datasets, and a 25E-validated workflow. All of these are controllable by the government and can be handed to an incumbent, so defensibility is low-to-medium at best.

card.why_now: 2024: Army cancelled EWPMT follow-on and fixed TAK as the EW/spectrum host (EWPMT-X), opening a plugin path. 2025-2026: S2AS moved from a ~$6.1M prototype OTA to a $350M-ceiling production contract on the UCA pathway with fielding underway; REWSI produced two production sensor IDIQs (~$196M ceilings) demanding MOSA/API/NGC2 integration; DISA launched EMBM-J DS (Apr 2025) and is recompeting EMBM-J SA; NGC2 common data baseline and Lightning Surge showed EW data must feed the common data layer. Ukraine-style signature targeting made own-signature awareness a commander-level priority. Cheap SDRs, edge compute and RF ML make sensor-agnostic fusion technically cheap for the first time.
card.killer_risk: The two highest-value slices were just awarded: own-signature to 3dB Labs (production, June 2026) and joint spectrum management to DISA's EMBM-J (Palantir prototype, SA recompete), while the residual fusion layer sits inside EWPMT-X scope that the Army can assign to its integrator or require from sensor vendors under REWSI's open-architecture terms; combined with likely ITAR Category XI jurisdiction, CUI-only data, a few-thousand-person user base and a non-U.S.-person co-founder, there is no venture-scale, founder-accessible company here - at most a small TAK-plugin subcontracting business.
