score.title: Bandwidth-aware prioritized sync and store-and-forward data movement between edge applications and the NGC2/TAK data layer (policy-driven 'what leaves first, at what fidelity' and COP-edit reconciliation on reconnect)

scores.rationale: Real but partially solved pain: DDIL links of 1 Mbps-1 kbps are the stated operating regime (DARPA FLUID, darpa.mil, 2025-03-28, FACT/HIGH) and the hub-and-spoke NGC2 redesign was driven by bandwidth/latency problems (Federal News Network, 2025-10, FACT/MEDIUM); but the store-and-forward/re-sync primitive already works at division scale (Ivy Mass, army.mil, 2026-06, FACT/HIGH), and the residual pain (manual deconfliction of COP objects, arrival-order replication) is an INFERENCE with LOW confidence - no public government document quantifies it. Public evidence insufficient to rate above 3.

Partition and reconnect events happen in every DDIL exercise and would happen continuously in contested operations; Ivy Mass deliberately injected EMI, cyber and comms loss (army.mil, 2026-06, FACT/HIGH), and FLUID's whole premise is chronic rather than episodic link scarcity (INFERENCE, MEDIUM). Not a 5 because in garrison and benign-network training the pain is largely absent.

Money exists nearby but none is addressed to this layer: NGC2 ~$3.3B identified through FY2026 with no life-cycle estimate and a 50% FY26 NDAA obligation cap (GAO-26-108019, 2026-08-20, FACT/HIGH); AFLCMC's Ditto contract is $28M ceiling with ~$5.3M obligated (GlobalSecurity, 2025-07-11, FACT/HIGH) - ceiling is not revenue; DARPA FLUID funds research performers. No RFI, SBIR topic or budget line names a standalone prioritization/reconciliation policy layer (Public evidence insufficient).

Score of 1 explained: every route to the user passes through an incumbent-owned gate. The Army formally assigned the NGC2 common data layer baseline to Anduril with Palantir Foundry and Raft (army.mil, 2026-06-22, FACT/HIGH); the Air Force sole-sourced Ditto (2025-07-11, FACT/HIGH); TAK Product Center owns the Mission API. The card's own entry path is 'subcontractor to a prime or TAK plugin'. SBIR - the only open competitive lane for this class of software - is gated by the >50% U.S.-person ownership test (13 CFR 121.702, FACT/HIGH) that excludes the Indonesian founder's equity, and SBIR authority lapsed Sep 30, 2025 with reauthorization in progress in 2026 (DefenseScoop, 2026-04-29, FACT/MEDIUM). No independent PROGRAM OFFICE -> CONTRACTING OFFICE -> VEHICLE chain exists for a standalone vendor.

A mission-priority scheduler, fidelity-degradation pipeline and auditable merge-rule engine over CoT/TAK objects are well-understood distributed-systems work (priority queues, CRDT/DTN patterns per RFC 9171, netem link shaping); ATAK-CIV and TAK Server docs are public (github.com/deptofdefense/AndroidTacticalAssaultKit-CIV; docs.opentakserver.io, FACT/MEDIUM). Not a 5 because the hard part - correct merge semantics for C2 objects edited on both sides of a partition without silent data loss - is subtle and unvalidated without real exercise data.

The card's capital table (HYPOTHESIS, no direct public data) puts a proof of concept at $150k-$300k, so $250k reaches a lab demo; but a credible military demo is $1M-$2.5M and requires an integrator sprint slot, and the PoC alone proves nothing to buyers who already have Ditto and Lattice Mesh in production. Capital reaches the first rung of a ladder whose upper rungs are not funded.

A side-by-side shaped-link demo (naive TAK replication vs policy-driven) on commercial laptops, SBCs and throttled Starlink/mesh radios is realistic in 4-6 months (card MVP section, HYPOTHESIS/MEDIUM). A demo the actual buyer treats as credible (inside an Ivy Sting-type sprint via a prime, or with TAK-GOV) depends on a third party's calendar and is 12-24 months out at best.

CoT schemas, ATAK-CIV source and TAK Server Mission API docs are public (FACT/HIGH-MEDIUM); representative message mixes and link traces can be synthesized or self-measured on commercial mesh radios and Starlink. The data that would make the policy library valuable - real exercise partition events, message mixes per mission phase and reconciliation actions - is CUI and only reachable inside an NGC2 team or via a C5ISR Center CRADA (card data_requirement; E07-F30 on CUI access, FACT/MEDIUM).

The MVP is unclassified, EAR-territory software on open TAK-CIV and commercial radios (card regulatory_burden 'medium'; E07-F32 on encryption being a notification step, FACT/MEDIUM). Beyond MVP: TAK-GOV/MIL distribution control, CUI exercise data, ATO inheritance inside a prime's environment, possibly ITAR-adjacent radio technical data, and deemed-export/FOCI questions for the Indonesian founder (E07-F3, E07-F7, E07-F30, FACT). These are constraints requiring export-control and immigration counsel, not a legal determination here.

Everything needed for the first 6-12 months is open: ATAK-CIV, OpenTAKServer/TAK Server docs, Linux tc/netem, commercial hardware, synthetic data; classification dependence is 'eventually' (card), i.e., only when tuning against real exercise data or deploying inside NGC2. Not a 5 because the commercially decisive validation step (real partition data, TAK-GOV) is controlled or CUI.

Score of 1 explained: the field is occupied by well-capitalized, contracted incumbents at every layer - Ditto (~$136M raised incl. $82M Mar 2025, TechCrunch 2025-03-12; AFLCMC $28M-ceiling sole-source; DIU COD success memo; ATAK Edge Sync plugin), Anduril Lattice Mesh (CDAO 3-year production agreement Dec 2024, Breaking Defense; NGC2 data-layer lead Jun 2026), Palantir Foundry edge, Raft, government-owned TAK Server Mission API, DARPA FLUID performers generating government-funded IP through 2028, transport vendors (Persistent, Silvus, goTenna) with their own QoS, and commodity local-first stacks (PowerSync, ElectricSQL, Couchbase Lite) that lower primes' build cost. All FACT/HIGH-MEDIUM from the card's sources.

Score of 1 explained: the incumbents own the sync loop, the link telemetry and the APIs; the card's own analysis (INFERENCE, HIGH) is that a priority scheduler plus merge-rule engine is 'weeks-to-months of work' for Anduril/Palantir, Ditto or TAK Product Center, and each has a lock-in incentive to build it in-house. Anduril opened the Lattice Mesh SDK to third parties under CDAO's ecosystem model (Breaking Defense, 2024-12, FACT/MEDIUM), which invites plugins on its terms rather than exposing it to displacement. No GAO/IG or after-action finding evidences operator dissatisfaction with current re-sync behavior (Public evidence insufficient).

Technically the hooks exist (TAK Server Mission API/Data Sync, Lattice SDK gRPC/REST opened to third parties, Ditto SDK), but the startup controls none of them (card integration_requirement, FACT/MEDIUM); deployment inside NGC2 hubs requires the prime's Kubernetes environment and ATO inheritance; link telemetry from MANET/pLEO radios needs vendor API access. Integration is feasible only with the interface owner's cooperation, which is exactly what a competing policy layer would not receive.

Score of 1 explained: the only proposed proprietary assets are a policy library, measured link models and per-object merge rules - all of which the engine owners can observe and replicate from the same exercise data they already hold; a sidecar accrues no network effects, no accreditation moat and no data exclusivity (card defensibility, INFERENCE/HIGH). The DDIL harness variant has impartiality as its value, which is a positioning, not a moat.

Generic bandwidth-aware sync has commercial analogues (aviation, maritime, retail, IoT, disaster-response TAK-CIV users such as FEMA/CBP/wildland fire), but that generic demand is already served by Ditto's commercial business and open-source local-first stacks; the differentiating pieces (mission-phase policy, C2-object merge semantics) are military-specific with little commercial pull (card dual_use 'medium'; scored below the card's label because the differentiated part is the non-dual-use part, INFERENCE/MEDIUM).

Adjacent moves exist on paper - Air Force expeditionary comms (ACC AMIC RFI asks for application-level QoS inside a comms kit, sam.gov, 2026-01, FACT/MEDIUM), Navy COD, allied TAK users (NATO, UK Project Asgard, German D-LBO) - but each has its own incumbents (blackned, Systematic, Thales, Anduril UK) and a plugin/subcontractor position does not compound into a platform; the card's allied_extension concludes it is a niche service business.

If adopted inside a prime's stack the software would be sustained and re-licensed annually through the prime's OTA/task orders, and TAK plugins can be re-bought by many units; but the buyer relationship is intermediated, the incumbent can absorb the feature at any renewal, and no independent recurring line exists (INFERENCE/MEDIUM).

One strong engineer plausibly covers the distributed-systems/CRDT core, and the business founder can run SBIR/xTech and BD; but three fatal-if-absent roles are missing (TAK/NGC2 integration engineer, former S6/G6 or fires-cell operator to define credible mission-phase policies, export/FOCI counsel), the Indonesian founder cannot count toward the SBIR >50% U.S.-person majority or be technical lead on an AFWERX award without restructuring (E07-F3, E07-F7, FACT/HIGH), the German founder's equity only counts post-green-card, and the team has no prime relationships. Fit is real on the technical wedge and weak on every access dimension; requires counsel, not a legal judgment here.

market.summary: Not unsolved (Ivy Mass re-sync demonstrated May 2026); every interface is owned by a contracted incumbent (Ditto AFLCMC $28M ceiling; Anduril/Palantir/Raft NGC2 data-layer baseline Jun 2026; TAK Mission API); no budget line for 'prioritization policy'; government funds the residual as DARPA FLUID research, not a product buy; NGC2 itself is under a 50% obligation cap with no cost estimate (GAO-26-108019). Outcome is plugin shop or small acqui-hire. Narrower survivable form: a DDIL sync-behavior test harness.

competition.summary: Three incumbent engines (Ditto, Lattice Mesh/Foundry, TAK Server) already ship the primitive at the target echelon and DDIL regime; two services have formally picked owners for this interface (Army NGC2 baseline, AFLCMC sole-source); the residual policy/merge layer is weeks-to-months of work for teams that own the sync loop and have lock-in incentives; the acquisition environment is tightening around primes, not opening. Narrower survivable form: vendor-agnostic DDIL test/certification tooling.

feasibility.summary: MVP is unclassified and cheap, but $250k buys only a PoC that proves nothing to buyers already running Ditto/Lattice; credible demo ($1-2.5M) and production ($5-10M, subcontractor-only) require a prime or PEO C3N sponsor on a 3-5 year chain with no funded step; SBIR ownership (13 CFR 121.702) and AFWERX foreign-national limits (E07-F3/F7) block the Indonesian founder from the qualifying majority and technical lead; missing operator and integration expertise. Narrower survivable form: netem/tc-based DDIL harness sold to program offices and primes, with a U.S.-person-compliant structure.

score.verdict_rationale: All three skeptics refute at strength 5 and this analyst agrees; no evidence in the card, the E01/E02 findings or the E07 regulatory sweep contradicts them. The decisive reason is structural, not technical: there is no identifiable independent path PROBLEM -> USER -> REQUIREMENT OWNER -> PROGRAM OFFICE -> CONTRACTING OFFICE -> BUDGET -> CONTRACT VEHICLE for a standalone 'prioritization and reconciliation policy layer'. The requirement owner (Army Futures Command/Network CFT, T2COM) and program office (PEO C3N) have already routed the data-layer function to a prime-owned baseline (Anduril lead with Palantir Foundry and Raft, army.mil 2026-06-22, FACT/HIGH); the Air Force routed its equivalent to Ditto by sole-source (GlobalSecurity 2025-07-11, FACT/HIGH); the government-owned TAK baseline provides the reconnect re-sync primitive for free (OpenTAKServer docs, FACT/MEDIUM); and the residual application-aware load-reduction problem is being funded as DARPA FLUID research (darpa.mil 2025-03-28, FACT/HIGH), not solicited as a product. The store-and-forward/re-sync capability the founders would headline was demonstrated at division scale in Ivy Mass (army.mil 2026-06, FACT/HIGH). What remains is a feature that four interface owners can add in weeks-to-months (INFERENCE, HIGH), leaving a two-person team with a $250k PoC and no funded next step, no unclaimed acquisition lane, an SBIR ownership problem (13 CFR 121.702, FACT/HIGH), and a best case of TAK-plugin subcontracting or a small acqui-hire. Major penalty applied for the missing procurement chain. The user-pain is real (criteria 1-2 score 3-4) but the market-side criteria for budget, access, competition, incumbent vulnerability and moat all score 1-2, producing market attractiveness 2.1; founder fit of 3.0 reflects only that the unclassified MVP is cheap and open, not that the founders can reach a buyer.
score.narrower_version_if_borderline: Not enough to lift G17 to borderline, but worth logging as a separate candidate: a vendor-agnostic DDIL network-emulation and sync-behavior test harness (Linux tc/netem link profiles from 1 Mbps to 1 kbps, scripted partition/reconnect storms across ~10 simulated ATAK-CIV/TAK Server nodes, scoring time-to-arrival of priority CoT objects, duplicate/conflicting objects after reconnect, link saturation on reconnect, with a reconcile-log audit). Its only evidenced demand signal is the Army SBIR topic 'Generative AI Enabled Tactical Network' asking for a DDIL modeling environment (armysbir.army.mil, 2025, FACT/HIGH), which is a measurement/modeling ask rather than a certification-harness buy; plausible buyers (PEO C3N, DEVCOM C5ISR Center, prime T&E organizations, DOT&E) are HYPOTHESIS with LOW confidence and no dedicated budget line. It is a tooling/services business, SBIR-gated (so it needs a >50% U.S.-person cap table and a U.S.-person technical lead per E07-F3/F7, counsel required), and is not venture-scale. It should be scored as its own gap with its own evidence card rather than treated as a rescue of G17.
score.most_important_question_answer: If two exceptionally capable founders insisted on spending $250k here, the only defensible first build is not the policy layer but the measuring instrument: an open, reproducible DDIL sync test bench - ATAK-CIV clients and TAK Server (later a Ditto SDK adapter, and a Lattice SDK adapter if access is granted) on ~10 commercial SBCs/laptops behind Linux tc/netem profiles spanning 1 Mbps to 1 kbps with scripted 30-minute partitions and reconnect storms, producing a scored report of what arrived first, at what fidelity, how many duplicate or conflicting COP objects appeared after reconnect, and whether the link saturated. They would show it to DEVCOM C5ISR Center tactical-network S&T leads, the TAK Product Center, a Team Anduril or Team Lockheed data-layer lead, and an AFWERX/AFLCMC BES program manager who already funds Ditto; the demonstration would prove, with numbers no vendor marketing provides, whether the fielded engines deliver mission-priority behavior under thin links and where reconciliation fails. A program office would care because GAO-26-108019 (2026-08-20, FACT/HIGH) has just criticized NGC2 for missing cost and schedule evidence and Congress has capped obligations pending a report, so objective before/after metrics for the data layer have near-term bureaucratic value, and primes would care because such evidence supports their own acceptance testing. An incumbent cannot trivially crush the harness because its value is impartiality - Anduril or Ditto scoring their own stack is not evidence a program office can use - though nothing stops the government from building it in-house or a prime from ignoring it. The milestone that would justify the next $2-5M is a funded, named instrument: a SBIR Phase II or PEO C3N/C5ISR Center task order that adopts the harness as an acceptance-test capability, plus a signed integrator letter agreeing to consume a policy API produced from its findings - which is the only credible way the original G17 policy-layer idea ever re-enters. Absent that, the honest answer is that G17 fails because the money and the interface are already assigned: the store-and-forward primitive works (Ivy Mass, May 2026), the residual policy/merge layer is a modest extension for four interface owners, DARPA is funding the research path through FLUID, no buyer has asked for a standalone policy product, and SBIR ownership rules complicate the one open lane for this team; the founders should carry the harness forward as a separate small candidate and put their venture-scale ambitions elsewhere.
score.bear_case_summary: Feature, not product. The re-sync primitive is fielded inside the prime's NGC2 stack (Ivy Mass, army.mil, 2026-06, FACT/HIGH), the interfaces are owned by Anduril/Palantir/Raft (NGC2 baseline, 2026-06-22, FACT/HIGH), Ditto (AFLCMC sole-source $28M ceiling, ~$5.3M obligated, 2025-07-11, FACT/HIGH) and the government-owned TAK Server Mission API; no RFI, SBIR topic or budget line asks for a standalone prioritization/reconciliation policy layer (Public evidence insufficient); DARPA FLUID funds the residual problem as research (2025-03-28, FACT/HIGH); NGC2 has no life-cycle cost estimate and a 50% obligation cap (GAO-26-108019, 2026-08-20, FACT/HIGH); incumbents can add the layer in weeks-to-months (INFERENCE, HIGH); SBIR ownership (13 CFR 121.702) and AFWERX foreign-national rules exclude the Indonesian founder from the qualifying majority and technical lead (E07-F3/F7, FACT/HIGH); $250k buys a PoC that proves nothing to buyers already running Ditto and Lattice. Best case is a TAK plugin subcontract or a small acqui-hire.
score.bull_case_summary: The pain is real and recurring: DDIL is the stated regime (DARPA FLUID 1 Mbps-1 kbps), NGC2 was re-architected hub-and-spoke because of bandwidth/latency (Federal News Network, 2025-10, FACT/MEDIUM), ACC's AMIC RFI asks for application-level QoS (sam.gov, 2026-01, FACT/MEDIUM), and the Army is still funding tooling to model DDIL data delivery (Army SBIR topic, 2025, FACT/HIGH). Anduril opened the Lattice Mesh SDK to third parties (Breaking Defense, 2024-12, FACT/MEDIUM), TAK is a plugin ecosystem with allied reach, and the MVP is unclassified, cheap and open-source-buildable. If a program office or integrator ever wants an engine-agnostic, auditable mission-priority and merge-policy layer - or an impartial DDIL certification harness - a small team that has already built and measured one is the natural partner or acqui-hire (HYPOTHESIS, LOW). This bull case describes a good sub-scale services or tooling business and a possible small exit, not a venture-scale independent company.

verdicts.bear_case: The evidence in the G17 card itself is close to decisive against a standalone company, and the card's own authors already reach that conclusion in incumbent_response.why_startup_still_wins_or_reject ("Reject as a standalone company"). Five separate facts compound: (1) The core primitive is NOT unsolved - Ivy Mass (May 2026, army.mil) publicly demonstrated units tracking locally and re-syncing after losing division-cloud access, using the existing prime stack. What remains is a thin policy/ordering layer on top of a working system, not a missing capability. (2) Every plausible interface is owned by a well-capitalized incumbent with a live government contract: Ditto (~$136M raised, $28M-ceiling AFLCMC sole-source FFP awarded Jul 2025, DIU COD prototype success, ATAK Edge Sync plugin already shipping) sells exactly "sync that survives intermittent links"; Anduril's Lattice Mesh has a Dec 2024 CDAO production agreement AND was named lead (with Palantir Foundry and Raft) for the entire NGC2 common data-layer baseline in June 2026 - i.e., the incumbent now controls the very layer a G17 startup would need to plug into; TAK Server's government-owned Mission API already re-syncs missed changes for free. (3) No independent budget line exists for "prioritization policy" anywhere in the evidence: the $3.3B NGC2 figure (GAO-26-108019, Aug 2026) is portfolio-wide with no cost estimate or line-item detail, and NDAA FY26 caps obligation at 50% pending a report Army hasn't delivered - this is a program in active congressional distress, not a stable pipeline a subcontractor can count on. The Ditto award, DARPA FLUID and DIU COD money all flow to other named companies, not to an open "policy layer" requirement. (4) The government's own posture toward the specific residual problem (application-aware load reduction/message re-encoding under 1 Mbps-1 kbps) is to fund it as RESEARCH via DARPA FLUID performers (posted Mar 2025, work through 2028) rather than solicit it as a product buy - a strong signal DoD does not yet see this as a product-shaped, near-term-purchasable capability. (5) Adding a mission-priority scheduler and auditable merge-rule engine is explicitly characterized in the card as "weeks-to-months of work for teams that already own the sync loop and link telemetry" (Anduril/Palantir/Ditto/TAK Product Center) - i.e., a feature any of four well-funded incumbents can ship faster and with less integration risk than a two-person startup building on top of APIs it doesn't control. The realistic commercial outcomes named in the card are being a TAK plugin/subcontractor to a prime, or an acqui-hire at a small multiple - neither is venture-scale for two students with ~$250k. Layer on the SBIR >50% U.S.-person ownership rule (blocking the Indonesian founder from the qualifying majority) and CUI/ITAR access questions for a non-U.S.-person founder even in an unclassified MVP scenario, and the entry path narrows further to "OTA subcontractor via a prime," which structurally caps upside and independence.
verdicts.strongest_single_argument: The store-and-forward/re-sync requirement is not merely theoretically solvable but was PUBLICLY DEMONSTRATED WORKING at division scale (Ivy Mass, May 2026) inside the very prime stack (Anduril Lattice/Palantir Foundry) that was then named the official NGC2 data-layer baseline owner the following month (June 2026) - meaning the single most plausible customer for this product now controls both the demonstrated-working primitive and the standard interface, closing the door on an independent seat at the table before a startup could plausibly reach a pilot.
verdicts.what_would_change_my_mind: A public solicitation, RFI, or SBIR/xTech topic explicitly asking for a vendor-neutral "mission-data prioritization policy" or "DDIL sync-behavior test harness" as a standalone deliverable (not bundled into a comms/network RFI), issued by PEO C3N, TAK Product Center, or AFLCMC BES, with a dedicated budget line or ceiling value - none of which appears in this card's evidence or the E01/E02 findings reviewed. Evidence that Anduril/Palantir/Ditto have explicitly declined or been slow to add mission-priority queuing (e.g., a GAO/IG finding citing operator complaints about arrival-order-only replication) would also weaken the "incumbents will just build it" argument.
verdicts.narrower_survivable_version: A DDIL network-emulation and sync-behavior test/certification harness (already flagged in the card as the Army's own SBIR/xTech ask) that scores any vendor's sync stack (Ditto, Lattice, TAK Server) against reproducible link-degradation profiles ("what arrived first, at what fidelity, how many duplicate/conflicting objects after reconnect") - sold to PEO C3N, DEVCOM C5ISR Center, or a prime's T&E organization as an independent evaluation tool rather than a data-layer product. This survives the critique because it does not compete with or require access to the incumbents' proprietary sync internals, has a credible near-term buyer (program offices and primes need objective before/after metrics for their own compliance and source-selection processes), and is buildable end-to-end with open ATAK-CIV, netem/tc link shaping, and commercial hardware - i.e., it is a tooling/services business, not an attempt to out-build Anduril, Palantir, or Ditto on the sync engine itself.

verdicts.bear_case: The store-and-forward/reconnect-resync primitive that G17 frames as "unsolved" is already shipping and demonstrated at the exact echelon and DDIL regime this gap targets, by three separate incumbent-owned engines that all control the interfaces a startup would need. (1) Ditto: DittoLive's cloud-to-edge CRDT sync platform has an ATAK Edge Sync plugin, ~$136M raised (incl. $82M Mar 2025, TechCrunch 2025-03-12), a DIU Common Operational Database "success memo" for DDIL unmanned-systems sync (ExecutiveGov 2024-09), and a $28M-ceiling sole-source FFP contract from AFLCMC (GlobalSecurity, 2025-07-11) explicitly to extend a Phase II SBIR into "the full Ditto cloud-to-edge sync platform" through 2028 - i.e., the Air Force already pays one vendor to own this exact function. (2) Anduril: Lattice Mesh is marketed as DDIL-optimized, has a CDAO three-year production agreement (Dec 2024, Breaking Defense) that explicitly opened the mesh SDK to third-party developers, and in June 2026 Anduril was named lead of the Army's NGC2 common data layer baseline (with Palantir Foundry providing edge-to-cloud mesh and Raft providing registries/federation) - meaning the sync/prioritization layer for the Army's flagship C2 program now sits inside a prime-controlled stack by government decision. (3) TAK Server's Mission API/Data Sync already re-syncs missed changes on reconnect for free, in government-owned software used across the whole ATAK/WinTAK ecosystem. Crucially, Ivy Mass (May 2026, army.mil) publicly demonstrated units losing division-cloud connectivity, continuing to fight on local state, and resynchronizing on reconnect at division scale under simulated EMI/cyberattack - the core store-and-forward primitive the gap describes is not hypothetical, it is exercised and working today inside the prime's stack. What remains - mission-phase prioritization policy and auditable conflict-merge rules - is, per the gap card's own "incumbent_response" analysis, "weeks-to-months of work for teams that already own the sync loop and the link telemetry," and none of Ditto, Anduril/Palantir, or TAK Product Center have any reason to let an outside vendor own that policy layer rather than build it themselves, since it is a natural extension of an engine they already sell/operate. The government's own posture confirms this: DARPA FLUID (posted 2025-03-28) is funding the *research* into application-aware load reduction through performers, not soliciting a commercial product buy, and no procurement instrument anywhere in the evidence trail (RFI, SBIR topic, or program budget) names "prioritization/reconciliation policy layer" as a standalone acquisition category - money flows through the NGC2 prime OTA, AFLCMC's Ditto contract, or DARPA grants, never to an independent sync-policy vendor. Switching cost/architecture control is near-total: PEO C3N is the government owner of the NGC2 data layers and the Army has now formally assigned the vendor triad (Anduril/Palantir/Raft) as baseline; a startup cannot get to G6/S6 or fires-cell users except by becoming a subcontractor plugin inside Team Anduril, Team Lockheed, or the TAK Product Center's own roadmap. Given GAO-26-108019 (2026-08-20) reporting the Army has no NGC2 life-cycle cost estimate and Congress capping obligations at 50% pending that report, the acquisition environment is if anything tightening around the primes, not opening lanes for outside sync vendors. This is the textbook "billions not being made" answer: the money is being captured by Ditto (via sole-source extension) and by Anduril/Palantir/Raft (via the NGC2 baseline award), not left on the table.
verdicts.strongest_single_argument: The Army did not leave this problem open for a startup to solve - in June 2026 it formally assigned NGC2's common data-layer baseline (which includes exactly the edge-to-cloud sync/mesh function G17 targets) to Anduril as lead integrator with Palantir Foundry and Raft, while the Air Force independently converted a Ditto SBIR into a $28M-ceiling sole-source production contract for the same class of capability (AFLCMC, 2025-07-10) - two different services have already picked incumbent owners for this exact interface, both before this gap analysis was written, leaving no unclaimed acquisition lane, only a subcontractor/plugin role.
verdicts.what_would_change_my_mind: Evidence that PEO C3N or TAK Product Center has issued (or is about to issue) a procurement instrument - RFI, SBIR topic, sources-sought, or OTA - that names mission-phase prioritization or COP-edit conflict reconciliation as a standalone, engine-agnostic requirement open to non-incumbent bidders (rather than folded into the Anduril/Palantir/Raft baseline or the Ditto contract); or evidence that Ivy Mass/Ivy Sting after-action reporting identifies the current re-sync behavior as an operationally significant failure serious enough to trigger a new competitive acquisition rather than an internal engineering backlog item for the incumbents.
verdicts.narrower_survivable_version: A DDIL network-emulation and sync-behavior test/certification harness (the "technical_wedge" alternative already named in the gap card) - i.e., not a data-layer product but tooling that scores any vendor's sync stack (Lattice, Ditto, TAK Server) on "what arrived first, at what fidelity, with what conflicts" against Army/AFLCMC-defined link profiles (1 Mbps-1 kbps, partition/reconnect storms). This has a plausible independent buyer (Army SBIR "Generative AI Enabled Tactical Network" topic already asks for a DDIL modeling/simulation environment; T&E organizations, DOT&E, or PEO C3N could buy it as an acceptance-test capability) and does not require owning or replacing any incumbent's sync engine, so it sidesteps the "feature not product" and "interface controlled by incumbent" objections. It is a much smaller, services/tooling-flavored business, not a venture-scale data-layer platform.

verdicts.bear_case: G17 fails on nearly every axis a red-team should test, and the gap card's own research effectively concedes the case. (1) NOT UNSOLVED: the store-and-forward/re-sync primitive already works in production-adjacent systems. Ditto holds an AFLCMC sole-source FFP contract with a $28M ceiling (~$5.3M obligated, GlobalSecurity, 2025-07-11, FACT/HIGH) covering the full cloud-to-edge sync platform, has an ATAK Edge Sync plugin, and won DIU's Common Operational Database prototype (Ditto/Syntiant/HarperDB, ExecutiveGov 2024-09, FACT/MEDIUM) with Navy reportedly moving toward production. TAK Server's Mission API already re-syncs missed changes for disconnected clients in the government-owned baseline (OpenTAKServer docs, tier-3 but corroborated). Ivy Mass (army.mil, 2026-06, FACT/HIGH) publicly demonstrated units tracking locally after losing division-cloud access and synchronizing on reconnect at division scale -- i.e., the headline capability the founders would pitch is already fielded, not hypothetical. (2) INTERFACE CAPTURE: the residual piece -- mission-phase prioritization policy and auditable COP-conflict merge rules -- lives inside engines a startup does not own. Anduril leads the Army's NGC2 common-data-layer baseline (with Palantir Foundry and Raft) as of 2026-06-22 (army.mil/DefenseScoop, FACT/HIGH) and already opened Lattice Mesh's SDK to third parties (Breaking Defense, 2024-12) specifically because CDAO wanted the ecosystem play under its control, not competition on the sync loop. TAK Product Center owns the Mission API. Adding a priority queue/merge-rule layer is "weeks to months of work for teams that already own the sync loop and the link telemetry" per the card's own incumbent-response analysis -- and those teams have every incentive to do it before an outside vendor gets traction, since it defends their platform lock-in. (3) NO INDEPENDENT BUYER EVIDENCED: no RFI, SBIR topic, or budget line asks for "prioritization policy" as a standalone product; DARPA FLUID (2025-03-28, FACT/HIGH) funds the adjacent research question (application-aware load reduction under 1 Mbps-1 kbps) through performers, not through an open competitive buy a startup could win as prime. The Army SBIR "Generative AI Enabled Tactical Network" topic (2025) is still funding tooling merely to *measure* the problem. This is the textbook "why hasn't a startup already made billions" answer: because the money that exists flows to the primes who own the data layer, and the government is choosing to fund research (FLUID) rather than acquire a product. (4) REGULATORY/FOUNDER-FIT: per E07 and G17's own regulatory_burden, the MVP itself is low-friction EAR/TAK-CIV territory, so the "cannot touch it at all" bear case is weaker here than for classified-dependent gaps -- but the eligibility math still bites. SBIR is the accessible non-dilutive path DoD components actually use for this kind of software (Ditto's own award came via SBIR Phase II extension), yet 13 CFR 121.702 excludes the Indonesian founder's equity from the >50% U.S.-citizen/PR test entirely, and the German founder only counts after green-card issuance (E07-F3, FACT/HIGH); AFWERX Open Topic additionally caps foreign-national participation to public-domain/fundamental research performed in the U.S. (E07-F7, FACT/HIGH) -- meaning the Indonesian technical co-founder cannot be lead engineer on a DoD SBIR contract without restructuring around him. OTAs avoid the ownership test but require reaching the government only "as a subcontractor" to an NGC2 integrator team (Anduril/Lockheed) -- i.e., the startup's own entry_vehicle analysis says the only credible paths are subcontract-to-a-prime or plugin-inside-TAK, and the only credible exit is being acqui-hired by Ditto/Raft/Anduril "at a small multiple." (5) CAPITAL AND TIMELINE: the card's own capital_required table puts a credible military demo at $1-2.5M and first production deployment at $5-10M "realistically only as a subcontractor" -- the $250k founder capital covers proof-of-concept only, which proves nothing to a buyer who already has Ditto and Lattice Mesh in production. Even the optimistic entry_vehicle sequence (xTech/SBIR Phase I -> CRADA/pilot -> SBIR Phase II with integrator letter -> Phase III/OTA task order) is a 3-5 year chain with no funded step until an integrator or PEO C3N chooses to sponsor it, and PEO C3N's own program (GAO-26-108019, 2026-08-20, FACT/HIGH) has no life-cycle cost estimate or fielding schedule for 2032, meaning the buying organization itself cannot commit budget on a predictable timeline. Taken together: this is a feature that incumbents already ship, inside interfaces they control, with government money going to research rather than acquisition, sized for a company with a $28M-ceiling contract and $136M raised (Ditto) rather than two students with $250k -- the classic "not a venture-scale independent opportunity" pattern the card's own killer_risk section names explicitly ("Feature, not product... becomes a plugin shop dependent on a prime or is acqui-hired at a small multiple").
verdicts.strongest_single_argument: The gap card's own evidence shows the core capability already fielded at division scale (Ivy Mass, May 2026) inside a prime-owned data layer (Anduril/Palantir/Raft, June 2026 baseline) that just opened its SDK to third parties specifically to keep the ecosystem under its control -- while the only public government money for the exact residual problem (DARPA FLUID) funds research performers, not a product buy, and no RFI or budget line names "prioritization policy" as something anyone is purchasing standalone.
verdicts.what_would_change_my_mind: A concrete, named RFI/SBIR topic or OTA solicitation explicitly asking for a vendor-agnostic mission-priority/merge-policy layer as its own line item (not bundled into a comms kit or the NGC2 program), evidence that Anduril/Ditto/TAK Product Center have explicitly declined or deprioritized building this despite operator demand, or a signed letter of intent/pilot from an NGC2 integrator or TAK Product Center indicating they would rather integrate a third party's policy engine than build it in six months internally.
verdicts.narrower_survivable_version: A DDIL network-emulation and sync-behavior test/certification harness -- i.e., the tooling wedge the card itself proposes as the "alternative, narrower wedge with clearer buyer": build the netem/tc-based link-shaping and scoring tool (time-to-arrival of priority CoT objects, duplicate-track detection, reconcile-log auditing) that the Army's own SBIR topics show it needs just to *measure* whether Ditto, Lattice, or TAK Server actually deliver mission-priority behavior under 1 Mbps-1 kbps links. This is a tooling/QA business sold to program offices and primes (who need independent verification of vendor claims), not a data-layer business competing with the incumbents for the sync loop itself; it needs no ATO inheritance inside a prime's Kubernetes environment, is inherently vendor-agnostic (its value proposition is impartiality), and could plausibly be built and demoed for under $150-300k as the card's own capital table suggests. It still requires an Indonesian-founder-aware cap-table/personnel structure for any SBIR path (per E07-F3/F7) and a U.S.-citizen-led team for AFWERX-specific awards, but avoids the "policy layer nobody will buy from an outsider" trap.

card.title: Battalion-and-below DDIL-native orders, planning and battle-tracking app bridging dismounted TAK and Onebrief-class HQ planning (structured orders, reports and tracking that survive displaced, low-bandwidth command posts)
card.problem: Between the dismounted TAK client and the division-level planning suite, company and battalion staffs still run orders, reports and battle tracking on voice, MMC/TAK chat, PowerPoint and paper in displaced, low-bandwidth command posts, and neither TAK (no structured orders/planning objects) nor Onebrief-class tools (HQ collaboration design center, offline tactical mode still 'in development') natively covers that echelon under DDIL.

user.exact_role: Battalion S3/S2/S4 staff officers and battle captains/battle NCOs in the TOC or mobile command post; company commanders, XOs and 1SGs on Nett Warrior/ATAK end-user devices; SOF team leaders
user.echelon: Company through battalion (brigade as the consumer of reports and the source of orders)
organization_examples: 4th Infantry Division and 25th Infantry Division NGC2/TiC formations
IBCT infantry battalions (Infantry Magazine mobile-CP authors, Winter 2024-25)
75th Ranger Regiment (SBMC phase-one testing)
Army National Guard infantry/cavalry battalions
Allied light forces (Bundeswehr Jaeger battalions, TNI-AD infantry battalions) and public-safety incident-command TAK users

current_workflow: 1. Receive higher's OPORD/FRAGO as a PDF/PowerPoint or a WinTAK data package over an intermittent ITN/MMC-T link, or by courier when the network is down.
2. Build the battalion/company order and graphics in PowerPoint, Word and on a paper map board; hand-draw or re-digitize graphics into WinTAK/ATAK as CoT overlays and data packages.
3. Disseminate the order by voice on TSM/PRC-163 nets, by MMC/TAK chat, and by physically pushing data packages to leaders' end-user devices.

4. Track combat power, LOGSTAT, PERSTAT, SITREP and SPOTREP by voice and free-text chat; a battle NCO re-keys them into an Excel/PowerPoint battle-tracking chart and a paper 'analog' COP for when the digital picture dies.
5. Re-brief higher by phone, chat or a slide deck; when the CP jumps or the link drops, the running estimate and report history are lost or diverge between nodes and are reconciled by hand afterward.
card.current_solution: Voice (TSM/PRC-163), MMC/JBC-P (ATAK-based MMC-S) for chat and PLI, WinTAK/ATAK for graphics and COP, PowerPoint/Excel/paper for orders and battle tracking; in NGC2 prototype divisions, the Anduril-led baseline (Lattice UI, Palantir data layer, Onebrief as the planning layer) claims DDIL data exchange and squadron-level battle tracking when cut off from the division cloud; SBMC (Anduril/Rivet) will supply a company-and-below C2 client that must be backward compatible with ATAK; allied forces use Systematic SitaWare Edge/Frontline (with a tasking function) or Ukraine's Delta (works offline).
card.failure: Structured content (orders, tasks, reports, running estimates) has no native object model in TAK, so it travels as chat text, slides and data packages that do not merge when nodes reconnect after a displacement; Onebrief's structured planning objects live at division/corps with an offline tactical mode still 'in development' (company statement); the result is manual re-keying at the battalion TOC, divergent pictures between the main CP, the mobile CP and companies, and reports that are lost when the CP jumps.

evidence.claim: Infantry Magazine authors state IBCT command posts have lost the art of mobility, survivability and minimal connectivity while keeping a COP, and describe the battalion-and-below stack as voice over TSM/PRC-163, graphics/COP over WinTAK and chat/PLI over MMC - i.e., no structured orders/reports layer below brigade.
evidence.source_title: Utilizing the Integrated Tactical Network in Mobile Command Posts (Infantry Magazine, Winter 2024-2025; reprinted RealClearDefense 2025-03-01)
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: The Army's SBMC Request for Solutions (SAM.gov, April 2025) defines SBMC as the future situational awareness and mission command platform for company level and below dismounted operations and requires backward compatibility with the ATAK architecture - the dismounted C2 client will remain TAK-shaped through at least FY2028.
evidence.source_title: Soldier Borne Mission Command (SBMC) Other Transaction Opportunity (SAM.gov)
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: SBMC prototype agreements: Anduril $159M and Rivet $195M (Sept 2025, 18-month sprints; prototype awards, not production); Anduril reported moving from phase one to phase two in Aug 2026 after testing with the 75th Ranger Regiment.
evidence.source_title: Army awards more than $350M in contracts for Soldier Borne Mission Command system prototypes; Anduril redesigns tech for Army's SBMC program (DefenseScoop)
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: PM Mission Command 'Operational Mission Command Suite' notice requires the TAK solution to support on-prem, hybrid and cloud data services integrated via DDIL-robust protocols and architectures (from earlier-stage evidence E02-F8; SAM.gov primary page blocked this session).
evidence.source_title: Operational Mission Command Suite (SAM.gov)
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: GAO-26-108019 quotes a soldier who tested NGC2 'in a denied, degraded, intermittent, and limited environment where we were essentially cut off from the division's cloud, but we were still able to battle track and execute our tasks at the squadron level internally'; Army says the NGC2 baseline provides real-time data exchange in DDIL. This is evidence the incumbent NGC2 stack already addresses part of this gap at battalion-equivalent echelon (weakens the gap), while the Army still lacks a unit-by-year schedule and life-cycle cost estimate.
evidence.source_title: GAO-26-108019 Army Modernization: Better Schedule and Cost Information Needed to Support Scaling Battlefield Network
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: Onebrief states that 'development of fully offline access for tactical units in austere environments is underway' and that planners used it 'inside displaced, low-bandwidth command posts' during Ivy Sting - a company claim that the offline tactical mode is not yet shipped and that its results are self-reported (no independent measurement found).
evidence.source_title: Onebrief Compresses Army Planning Timelines from Hours to Minutes as NGC2 Scales to a Full Division (Business Wire press release)
evidence.label: INFERENCE

evidence.claim: Ivy Sting 4 (early 2026) deliberately tested C2 of maneuver from division to battalion under denied network conditions - DDIL C2 at battalion is an explicit Army test objective, not an edge case.
evidence.source_title: 4th Infantry Division Leads NGC2 Prototyping with Ivy Sting 4 (CPE C2IN LinkedIn post)
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: Practitioner critique (former Army officer) that vendors treat DDIL as an edge case; 25th ID's 'first mile, last mile' focus (LinkedIn post; RECALL from earlier stage - not re-verified this session).
evidence.source_title: Tom Keane LinkedIn post on Ivy Sting 5 / 'own the edge'
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: The TAK community keeps building low-bandwidth transports and offline map tooling (Akita-MeshTAK for Meshtastic/Reticulum; takwerx map-depot), and no TAK Product Center plugin for structured operations orders or mission planning was found in this session's search - demand for DDIL operation exists but the orders/planning object layer is missing from the open ecosystem.
evidence.source_title: Akita-MeshTAK (GitHub); TAK.gov products/plugins listing
evidence.label: INFERENCE

evidence.claim: Allied/foreign incumbents already ship partial answers: Systematic added a tasking function to SitaWare Frontline and SitaWare Edge so units 'plan and follow missions in real time' over its low-bandwidth STC protocol; Ukraine's Delta 'can work offline' and at least one NATO country explored adopting it (April 2025). Shows the feature is buildable and that the allied market has entrenched vendors.
evidence.source_title: SitaWare Edge: Situational Awareness for Dismounted Commanders (Systematic product page); Delta (situational awareness system) (Wikipedia)
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: Immersive Wisdom holds a DoD-wide five-year sole-source ordering contract (ceiling $25M through GFY2029, awarded by the USAF) for TRL-9 no-/low-bandwidth collaboration software, plus an AFWERX STRATFI with three DoD commands - a paying buyer exists for the DDIL collaboration primitive (ceiling is not revenue; obligations unknown).
evidence.source_title: SOF Week 2024: Immersive Wisdom awarded DoD-wide five-year sole-source $25MM ordering contract (PR Newswire)
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: Onebrief received an Army Contracting Command enterprise IDIQ (W9128Z-26-D-A014, $20M ceiling, Sept 2026) usable by any DoD warranted contracting officer - the HQ planning layer is now on an enterprise vehicle, so the incumbent can be ordered at any echelon once its offline mode ships (ceiling, not revenue).
evidence.source_title: Onebrief enterprise contract press release (Business Wire, 2026-09-17) and B02 company record
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: III Armored Corps is receiving baseline NGC2 capabilities (Sept 2026), i.e., the Anduril/Palantir/Onebrief baseline is spreading beyond the two prototype divisions before any third-party battalion orders app exists.
evidence.source_title: III Armored Corps receiving baseline NGC2 capabilities (DefenseScoop)
evidence.label: FACT

card.why_existing_startups_havent_solved: The echelon has no program office of its own: dismounted C2 belongs to PEO Soldier (Nett Warrior/SBMC, now with Anduril and Rivet owning the UI), the TOC belongs to CPE C2IN (NGC2 baseline led by Anduril with Onebrief as the planning layer), and TAK itself is government-owned with TAK-MIL distribution controlled by the TAK Product Center, so a battalion orders app has no natural buyer or budget line and must ride as a plugin or a team-member subcontract. Venture-backed entrants (Onebrief, Anduril) went to the division/corps and program-of-record money first and are now moving down-echelon; DDIL-consistent sync (CRDT/merge of orders, graphics and reports across nodes that reconnect out of order) is technically demanding and unglamorous; unit-level budgets are GPC-card sized; and allied markets are held by Systematic (NATO standard) and national systems, so no startup has found an economic wedge at this echelon.
card.technical_wedge: A DDIL-native 'orders and reports object layer' for battalion and below: an ATAK/WinTAK plugin plus lightweight TAK Server-side service that represents OPORD/FRAGO, tasks, control measures, sync matrix and standard reports (SITREP, LOGSTAT, PERSTAT, SPOTREP, 9-line) as structured, versioned objects synchronized with a CRDT/merge model over any TAK transport (TSM, MANET, Meshtastic/goTenna-class mesh, SATCOM) so that displaced nodes reconcile without re-keying; it imports higher's products (Onebrief export, PDF/PPT parsing) and emits CoT/data packages downward and structured reports upward, and can later map to the NGC2 common data baseline and Lattice SDK. The startup competes on the merge model, the small-screen orders UX and the open TAK footprint, not on the map or the transport.

mvp.what: ATAK-CIV plugin + companion web client + open TAK Server extension implementing structured orders/tasks/reports with offline-first, conflict-free sync and a 'CP jump' recovery mode; unclassified, built on public doctrine formats (FM 6-0 order/report templates).
mvp.demonstrable_in_3_6_months: Three to five Android EUDs and one laptop 'TOC' on a Meshtastic/goTenna-class mesh with deliberate partitions: issue an order, task subordinates, submit reports while disconnected, jump the TOC, reconnect out of order and show every node converging on the same order version and report log with no manual reconciliation; benchmark bytes-per-order and convergence time against sending the same content as chat and data packages.
mvp.what_it_must_prove: That structured orders/reports (not just PLI and chat) can be authored, disseminated and reconciled at kilobit-class bandwidth with partition tolerance; that battle captains and company XOs prefer it to chat + PowerPoint in a field exercise (measured re-keying time and report loss); and that it installs and runs within the TAK plugin process without TPC-controlled binaries.

data_requirement.what: Unclassified doctrinal formats for orders and reports (FM 6-0, ATP 6-0.5, unit SOPs and TACSOP report formats), CoT/TAK data-package schemas, sample graphics (MIL-STD-2525 symbology), and realistic network-partition traces; no operational or classified data needed for MVP.
data_requirement.legally_realistically_obtainable: Yes for the MVP: doctrine and symbology are public; ATAK-CIV and the TAK SDK are open source; unit TACSOPs can be obtained from National Guard or allied units under CRADA/exercise participation. Real unit report data and NGC2 data-baseline schemas require a government sponsor or team-lead partnership and may be CUI.
sources: Army Publishing Directorate (FM 6-0 Commander and Staff Organization and Operations; ATP 6-0.5 Command Post Organization and Operations)

systems: ATAK / WinTAK / MMC-S (ATAK-based) end-user clients
TAK Server (and TAK-GOV/MIL distributions for military users)
Onebrief (import of higher's plan products; API surface exists per third-party profile)
NGC2 common data baseline / Anduril Lattice SDK and Palantir data layer (later)
SBMC client (Anduril/Rivet) via ATAK backward compatibility
Tactical transports: TSM/PRC-163, MMC-T, MANET, Meshtastic/goTenna-class mesh
interfaces_protocols: Onebrief export/API (availability to third parties unverified)
Lattice SDK (partner program) and NGC2 data-baseline APIs from Operation Jailbreak (access unverified)
integration_requirement.who_controls_the_interface: TAK Product Center (CCDC C5ISR Center) controls TAK-GOV/MIL distribution and plugin signing; Anduril controls the Lattice SDK and, with Palantir, the NGC2 common data baseline; Onebrief controls its export/API; PEO Soldier controls the SBMC baseline; the startup controls none of them.

customer.user: Battalion S3/battle captain and company commanders/XOs in TiC/NGC2 divisions, Ranger/SOF elements, National Guard battalions; allied light infantry
customer.champion: Division or brigade S3/G3 or a battalion commander in a TiC formation; TAK Product Center product owner or PM Mission Command TAK lead; Army Applications Laboratory problem-set lead
customer.contract_signer: Army Contracting Command (ACC-APG for CPE C2IN programs - inferred; ACC-Orlando/others for SBIR), or the NGC2 team lead (Anduril/Lockheed) as a subcontract
customer.requirement_owner: T2COM / C2 CFT for NGC2 characteristics of need (placement unverified); PEO Soldier PM IVAS/SBMC for dismounted C2; Maneuver Center of Excellence for battalion-and-below mission command doctrine
customer.program_office: CPE C2IN (formerly PEO C3T/C3N) PM Mission Command (TAK and Operational Mission Command Suite) for the TOC side; PEO Soldier for SBMC/Nett Warrior
customer.contracting_office: Not confirmed; INFERENCE ACC-APG for CPE C2IN and PEO Soldier-aligned contracting at APG; Army SBIR/xTech via Army Applied SBIR office

budget.program_or_line: NGC2 C2 Applications (FY2026 request ~$488.4M RDT&E per buyer map; PE not verified) and the SBMC prototype agreements ($159M Anduril + $195M Rivet, prototype not production); no dedicated line for a battalion orders app exists.
budget.evidence: GAO-26-108019: ~$3.3B identified for NGC2 through FY2026 in PB2026 documentation, no life-cycle cost estimate or unit-by-year schedule; SBMC production decision reported for FY2028 (CRS IF13022, July 2026). A startup would be paid from a team-lead subcontract, a SBIR/xTech award or unit-level GPC/OTA money, not from a named line.

entry_vehicle.primary: TAK plugin published through TAK.gov (ATAK-CIV first, then TAK-GOV review) plus an Army xTech/SBIR Direct-to-Phase-II or AAL problem-set award, with an allied/public-safety paying pilot in parallel
sequence: 1. Open-source ATAK-CIV plugin + TAK Server extension; field test with a National Guard battalion, public-safety incident-command TAK users or a German/Indonesian light unit on unclassified networks (CRADA/no-cost)
2. xTechSearch/xTechIgnite or Army SBIR Phase I/D2P2 (eligibility contingent on ownership rules) or Bundeswehr Cyber Innovation Hub / NATO DIANA pilot for the allied path
3. Team-member subcontract under an NGC2 team lead (Anduril or Lockheed) or Lattice partner-program onboarding as the 'orders/reports' app; SBMC ecosystem via ATAK compatibility
4. Enterprise ordering via an existing vehicle (Onebrief-style Army IDIQ, or a SBIR Phase III) once a unit sponsor exists
entry_vehicle.eligibility_notes: SBIR/STTR requires >50% ownership by U.S. citizens or permanent residents (and the xTech-linked SBIR route inherits this); with one founder not assumed to be a U.S. person, the cap table must be structured so U.S.-person owners hold the majority, or the SBIR path is unavailable - needs counsel. TAK-GOV/MIL access and plugin signing require a U.S. government sponsor; ATAK-CIV is open. Allied entry (Bundeswehr CIHBw, NATO DIANA) may be easier for a German founder but does not lead to U.S. Army budget.

competition.how_close: Very close from above: NGC2 planning layer at 4th ID, Army enterprise IDIQ (Sept 2026), $2.15B valuation; states fully offline access for tactical units is 'underway'.
Very close from below: SBMC prototype UI owners for company-and-below; Lattice is the NGC2 baseline UI; both must be ATAK-backward-compatible.

competition.company: TAK Product Center / PM Mission Command (government)
competition.how_close: Owns ATAK/WinTAK/TAK Server and MMC-S; could add structured orders natively; Operational Mission Command Suite notice already asks for DDIL-robust TAK data services.
Close in allied markets: tasking function to plan and follow missions in real time over its STC low-bandwidth protocol; NATO standard HQ system.
Adjacent: ultra-low-bandwidth collaborative war room on SIPR for SOF/AOC, not TAK-native structured orders.
competition.evidence: PR Newswire 2024-05 sole-source $25M ordering contract; E03-F29

competition.how_close: Proof that an offline-capable, unit-built situational-awareness/tasking app can be fielded nationally; not a U.S. competitor but an allied-market alternative.

competition.company: PAR Government, Booz Allen, Cloud-RF, Lyntris/Accelint, goTenna/Somewear (Forterra)
competition.how_close: TAK plugin/services vendors and mesh transports; partial pieces (transport, RF planning, plugins-as-services) but no structured orders layer found.

incumbent_response.could_anduril_palantir_l3harris_add_it: Yes, easily: Anduril already owns the SBMC and Lattice UIs and the NGC2 baseline lead; Onebrief has publicly committed to offline tactical access; the TAK Product Center could add order objects to ATAK/WinTAK; Systematic already has a tasking function. Any of them can ship a 'good enough' battalion orders feature within one prototype cycle.
incumbent_response.why_startup_still_wins_or_reject: A startup wins only if it treats this as an open, transport-agnostic TAK-native layer that incumbents do not prioritize (they optimize for their own stacks), proves a measurably better partition-tolerant merge model, and sells first where incumbents are absent (National Guard, public safety, allied light forces), then enters the NGC2/SBMC ecosystems as a partner app. Honest assessment: as a standalone U.S. Army venture the wedge is likely to be absorbed; it is more credible as a feature company that gets acquired or as a partner-program app, or as an allied-first product.

capital_required.proof_of_concept_usd: $150k-$300k (two founders + one contract Android/TAK engineer, 6 months, commercial EUDs and mesh radios)
capital_required.credible_military_demo_usd: $1M-$2.5M (12-18 months: TAK-GOV review, security hardening, a field exercise with a Guard or allied battalion, an SBIR D2P2 or xTech award, one ex-battalion S3 on staff)
capital_required.first_production_deployment_usd: $5M-$12M (ATO/RMF or riding an NGC2 team lead's authorization, TAK-MIL packaging, CMMC, sustained field support for one division or an allied brigade; assumes subcontract or SBIR Phase III rather than a program of record)
capital_required.assumptions: Software-only, unclassified through demo; no hardware; heavy dependence on a government sponsor for TAK-GOV/MIL access; SBIR only if ownership structure qualifies; figures are analyst estimates (HYPOTHESIS, LOW confidence).

expertise_required.role: Former battalion S3/XO or battle captain (recent TiC/CTC experience) as product lead or co-founder
expertise_required.why: Defines the order/report object model, SOP variance and TOC workflow; opens unit-level pilots; credibility with PM MC and TPC.

expertise_required.role: Distributed-systems engineer with CRDT/offline-first sync and Android (ATAK SDK) experience
expertise_required.why: Partition-tolerant merge of orders/graphics/reports across intermittent mesh links is the core technical claim.

expertise_required.role: TAK ecosystem engineer (TAK Server, CoT, data packages, TAK.gov plugin submission)
expertise_required.why: Distribution and interoperability with ATAK/WinTAK/MMC-S; navigating TPC review.

expertise_required.role: Tactical-network / RF engineer (TSM, MANET, Meshtastic/goTenna)
expertise_required.why: Bandwidth budgeting and realistic partition testing; can be contract or advisor.

expertise_required.role: Government BD / contracts advisor (SBIR eligibility, OTA team-member subcontracts, ATO)
expertise_required.why: Finding the buyer in a fragmented echelon and structuring the cap table for SBIR.

regulatory_burden.explanation: Unclassified, software-only C2 tooling built on open-source ATAK-CIV can be developed without licenses; but TAK-GOV/MIL access and plugin signing are government-controlled, deployment on Army networks requires RMF/ATO (or riding a team lead's authorization), CMMC applies once CUI flows, and a military-specific C2 application may be ITAR-controlled (USML Category XI/XXI) or EAR-controlled depending on design - requires export-control counsel before sharing code with the non-U.S.-person founder or allied units.
regulatory_burden.non_us_person_founder_note: If the Indonesian founder is not a U.S. person, giving them access to ITAR-controlled technical data or TAK-GOV/MIL software could be a deemed export; SBIR ownership rules and FOCI considerations for any facility clearance also apply. Mitigations (keeping the codebase EAR99/commercial, using ATAK-CIV only, separating controlled work) need counsel - no legal judgment made here.

dual_use_potential.explanation: Public-safety incident command (wildland fire, SAR, disaster response) already uses TAK and suffers the same offline structured-tasking gap (ICS forms), and mining/energy/expedition operations need offline tasking; but the military-specific orders/reports model is the core value and commercial demand for partition-tolerant tasking is niche.

defensibility.explanation: Defensibility is weak: the merge/sync algorithms are replicable, ATAK is open, and incumbents own the surrounding UIs. What can compound is the installed base in units and allied forces, TAK.gov-approved status, integrations with Onebrief/Lattice/NGC2 data baseline, and a validated orders/report object schema units adopt in their SOPs.

card.why_now: Transformation in Contact and NGC2 put weekly vendor-unit iteration and DDIL testing at battalion level (Ivy Sting 4, early 2026); SBMC/Nett Warrior will put an ATAK-compatible C2 client on every leader by ~FY2028; the Army opened APIs through Operation Jailbreak (May 2026) and declared an NGC2 common data baseline (June 2026); ATAK-CIV and its SDK are open source; cheap mesh radios (Meshtastic/goTenna) and mature CRDT libraries make offline-first sync buildable by a small team; and the Ukraine war normalized unit-built, offline-capable C2 apps (Delta).
card.killer_risk: The gap is being closed from both sides by funded incumbents before a startup can reach a buyer: Onebrief states offline tactical access is in development and now holds an Army enterprise IDIQ, Anduril/Rivet own the SBMC dismounted UI (ATAK-compatible) and Anduril leads the NGC2 baseline that GAO already quotes as enabling squadron-level battle tracking when cut off from the division cloud; there is no program office or budget line for a battalion orders app, so the most likely outcome is a feature absorbed into Lattice, Onebrief or ATAK itself.

procurement_signal_timeline.event: Joint Staff RDT&E justification cites warfighter demand for functional DDIL C2 (RECALL from earlier stage; mirrored J-book, no URL)
Immersive Wisdom DoD-wide sole-source $25M ordering contract for no-/low-bandwidth collaboration software (May 2024); MMC-T validated at NTC (Jan 2024)

Infantry Magazine mobile-CP article (Mar); SBMC RFS requires ATAK backward compatibility (Apr); NGC2 prototype OTAs to Anduril ($99.6M, Jul) and Lockheed ($26M, Sep); SBMC prototype awards $354M (Sep)

Ivy Sting 4 tests division-to-battalion C2 under denied networks (Feb); Operation Jailbreak (May); NGC2 common data baseline (Jun); Onebrief says offline tactical access underway (Jun); GAO-26-108019 (Aug); Anduril SBMC phase two (Aug); Onebrief Army enterprise IDIQ (Sep); III Armored Corps receives NGC2 baseline (Sep)
NGC2 scaling to additional divisions/corps (no detailed schedule per GAO); SBMC production decision reported for FY2028

card.allied_extension: More compelling for entry, less for scale: allied light forces (Bundeswehr, Nordic, Baltic, Indonesian and Philippine units) and NATO partners already use ATAK or SitaWare Edge and face the same low-bandwidth orders problem, and a German founder can use Bundeswehr CIHBw/NATO DIANA channels without U.S.-person constraints; but Systematic is the NATO standard with its own tasking function, Ukraine's Delta is a free-of-charge national alternative attracting NATO interest, and allied budgets at this echelon are small, so allies improve pilot access and dual-track credibility rather than the total market.

score.title: Battalion-and-below DDIL-native orders, planning and battle-tracking app bridging dismounted TAK and Onebrief-class HQ planning (structured orders, reports and tracking that survive displaced, low-bandwidth command posts)

scores.rationale: FACT/HIGH: Infantry Magazine (Winter 2024-25, lineofdeparture.army.mil, 2025-03-01) documents battalion-and-below orders/reports riding voice, MMC chat, PowerPoint and paper, and Ivy Sting 4 (CPE C2IN, 2026-02) made division-to-battalion C2 under denied networks an explicit test objective; re-keying and lost report history on CP jumps is real, recurring staff pain. Not a 5 because doctrine treats voice/paper 'analog' fallback as an acceptable and even desired degradation mode (the Infantry article frames minimal-connectivity survivability as a goal), so the pain is tolerated rather than mission-stopping.

INFERENCE/MEDIUM: the pain recurs every orders cycle, every CP displacement and every CTC rotation, and DDIL is treated as a standing condition by the Army (GAO-26-108019, 2026-08-20; Ivy Sting objectives). Not 5 because in garrison and in well-connected training the network holds and staffs fall back to familiar tools without much friction.

SCORE 1 EXPLAINED: the card and all three skeptics agree no dedicated budget line exists. score.verdict_rationale: KILL as a venture for these two founders in their stated primary market (U.S. defense). Three independent skeptics refute at strength 4 and, after checking their citations against the card and the E07 regulatory findings, I do not find grounds to overrule them. The decisive reason is the broken buyer chain, which the task instructs me to penalise heavily: PROBLEM (FACT, HIGH: Infantry Magazine 2025-03-01; Ivy Sting 4 objectives 2026-02) and USER (battalion S3/battle captain, company XO) are real, but REQUIREMENT OWNER is unverified, no PROGRAM OFFICE owns a battalion-and-below orders app (dismounted C2 sits with PEO Soldier/SBMC, the TOC with CPE C2IN/NGC2, TAK with TAK Product Center), the CONTRACTING OFFICE is only inferred, there is no BUDGET line, and every CONTRACT VEHICLE that touches this layer belongs to an incumbent (Onebrief IDIQ W9128Z-26-D-A014, Business Wire 2026-09-17; SBMC OTAs to Anduril/Rivet, DefenseScoop 2025-09-08) or to a subcontract whose terms the startup does not control. Second, the window is closing from both sides: GAO-26-108019 (2026-08-20, FACT HIGH) already records a soldier battle-tracking at squadron level while cut off from the division cloud on the Anduril-led NGC2 baseline, Anduril is in SBMC phase two (DefenseScoop 2026-08-17), the baseline is spreading to III Armored Corps (DefenseScoop 2026-09-21), and Onebrief publicly says offline tactical access is underway (Business Wire 2026-06-26; its 2026 marketing goes further, but that is company marketing and not proof it works). Third, the card's own authors conclude the standalone U.S. Army wedge is 'likely to be absorbed'. Fourth, for this specific pair, the primary non-dilutive channel (SBIR/xTech) requires >50% U.S.-person ownership (13 CFR 121.702, E07-F3 FACT HIGH), which one non-U.S.-person founder and one not-yet-permanent-resident founder likely cannot meet without restructuring, and a 'specially designed' military C2 app risks ITAR/600-series drift that would complicate the Indonesian founder's access to the codebase (E07-F16/F17/F18; needs counsel). Where I differ from the skeptics: the GAO quote is one soldier's self-report about battle tracking in a prototype test, not evidence that structured orders and reports merge after partition, and the OTA/CSO route carries no ownership test (E07-F22), so the technical white space is somewhat wider and the founder constraints somewhat narrower than they state. Those corrections raise incumbent_vulnerability and regulatory scores by a point but do not create a budget owner, and without one this remains a feature, not a company. Confidence MEDIUM: the strongest counter-evidence would be a documented battalion-level DDIL failure of the NGC2/SBMC stack in a CTC AAR or GAO/IG report after the 2026 rollouts, or a TPC statement declining to add order objects; neither exists in public evidence this session (Public evidence insufficient).
score.narrower_version_if_borderline: Not borderline, but for completeness the residual form all three skeptics converge on is: an open, ATAK-CIV-only, EAR99-by-design structured orders/tasks/reports object layer with CRDT merge, sold first to public-safety incident command (ICS 201/204/209-style forms over Meshtastic-class mesh), Army National Guard battalions on unclassified networks and allied light units via Bundeswehr CIHBw or NATO DIANA, with the explicit business model of licensing or selling the merge model and schema to Onebrief, the Lattice partner program, TAK Product Center or Systematic. I do not rate this as a survivable version of G18 for these founders because it abandons the stated primary market (U.S. defense budget), has small GPC-card-sized budgets, and its realistic exit is an acquihire; if pursued it should be re-registered as a separate public-safety/allied candidate and scored on its own evidence rather than kept alive under G18.
score.most_important_question_answer: If two exceptionally capable founders had $250,000 today and insisted on this gap, the only defensible first build is an open-source ATAK-CIV plugin plus a small TAK Server extension that represents OPORD/FRAGO, tasks, control measures and the standard reports (SITREP, LOGSTAT, PERSTAT, SPOTREP, 9-line) as versioned objects with a CRDT merge model, demonstrated on five Android EUDs and a laptop TOC over a Meshtastic-class mesh with deliberate partitions and a 'CP jump' in the middle, measuring bytes-per-order and convergence time against the same content sent as chat and data packages. They would show it to a National Guard infantry battalion S3 and battle captain (reachable without a program office), a wildland-fire incident management team that already runs TAK, and the TAK Product Center product owner and PM Mission Command TAK lead, and the demonstration would prove that structured orders and reports, not just PLI and chat, can be authored, disseminated and reconciled at kilobit bandwidth with no manual re-keying after reconnection. The customer would care because report history and the running estimate are lost or diverge every time the CP displaces, which Ivy Sting 4 (2026) and the Infantry Magazine mobile-CP authors (2025) both frame as a live problem. But this is exactly where the plan fails: an incumbent can crush them because Onebrief already owns the enterprise vehicle and says offline tactical mode is underway, Anduril and Rivet own the ATAK-compatible SBMC client with $354M of prototype funding and are required to be backward compatible with TAK, and the government owns ATAK itself and can direct TPC to add order objects; the founders control none of the six interfaces the product must plug into, have no former battalion S3 (fatal per the card), and probably cannot use SBIR without restructuring the cap table. The milestone that would justify the next $2-5 million would be a signed, paying unit or agency pilot (Guard, public safety or allied) plus a written commitment from TPC, an NGC2 team lead or Onebrief to adopt or integrate the schema; absent that commitment, the money would buy a feature that the adjacent incumbents can replicate in one prototype cycle, which is why the gap is killed rather than funded.

(1) No budget owner: the card itself admits "no dedicated line for a battalion orders app exists" — the ~$488.4M NGC2 RDT&E figure is an architecture-wide PE, not a line a startup can bid into, and the only concrete vehicles are Onebrief's own $20M enterprise IDIQ ceiling (an incumbent's vehicle, not a competitor's) and SBMC's $159M+$195M prototype OTAs already awarded to Anduril and Rivet — both of whom own the UI at the exact echelon (company/battalion) this gap targets. (2) Being closed from both directions by funded incumbents faster than a startup can reach a buyer: GAO-26-108019 (Aug 2026) already quotes a soldier saying the Anduril-led NGC2 baseline let a unit "battle track and execute tasks at the squadron level" while cut off from the division cloud — i.e., DDIL battle-tracking already partly exists in the fielded prototype, not just on paper. More decisively, Onebrief's own current marketing (onebrief.com/platform/features, checked 2026-09) has moved well past the card's "underway" framing to claiming "resilient, DDIL-ready architecture," "offline-first collaboration," and function "at the forward, tactical level... across all echelons" with automatic sync on reconnect — this is company marketing, not independently verified, but it shows the $2.15B-valued incumbent that already holds the Army enterprise IDIQ is actively positioning to close precisely this seam before a startup could reach a first unit pilot. (3) Government could simply direct its own asset: TAK is government-owned, TAK Product Center controls ATAK/WinTAK/TAK Server, and PM Mission Command's own Operational Mission Command Suite notice already asks for DDIL-robust TAK data services — the cheapest fix, if the Army prioritizes it, is a government-directed TAK update, not a venture-funded product.
