score.title: Build a competing general-purpose military data fabric / data mesh platform

scores.rationale: Real, documented pain exists in the data layer (swivel-chair reconciliation, thumb-drive coalition sharing, undocumented APIs per Jailbreak, GAO classification findings), but that pain is about seams in the fielded stack. The pain this gap actually addresses - a program office wanting an alternative general-purpose platform - has no documented sufferer; Army and CDAO leaders publicly champion government-owned interfaces and multi-vendor onboarding rather than a second fabric.

Data-movement friction is daily for staffs, but the platform-level decision is made once per decade (10-year enterprise agreements, June 2026 baseline). A vendor selling a competing fabric would encounter the buying moment roughly once per program generation.

Large budgets exist in the layer (NGC2 FY27 request ~$3.78B; >$2B FY27 for Maven/JFN; $30B of enterprise-agreement ceilings), which is why this is not a 0, but every dollar is executed through designated teams and enterprise licenses; no line, RFI or solicitation for an alternative platform was found. Ceilings are not obligations.

The Army closed the competition with the June 2026 baseline and the joint level chose Maven; the only ways in are as a sub to a team lead or through SBIR/TAK/Tradewinds doors that admit components, not platforms. A 1 rather than 0 because Jailbreak, Open DAGIR and Right to Integrate do keep third-party onboarding formally open.

Open-source building blocks (CRDT sync, schema registries, protobuf/gRPC, Kubernetes at the edge) make a fabric technically buildable, but reaching parity with Lattice/Foundry (multi-level security, ATO at Secret, hundreds of adapters, SDK ecosystem) is a multi-year, multi-hundred-engineer effort.

Scored 0 because $250k cannot fund even a proof of concept of a general-purpose military data fabric: the government's own prototype OTAs for the layer were $99.6M and $26M, the incumbents' relevant contract ceilings are in the tens of billions, and a credible demo requires cleared staff and exercise access. $250k funds only a three-node open-standards component demo, which is a different gap.

A lab demo of sync/catalog features is possible in 6 months, but a demo the Army or CDAO would treat as credible for a fabric requires participation in Ivy Sting / Lightning Surge / PC-C class events under a team lead, realistically 18-36 months away for a new firm with no clearances.

Open standards (CoT/TAK, STANAG-style schemas, DMRA/UDRA public documents) and synthetic feeds support a component prototype, but the data a platform must actually handle (NGC2 API baseline, Maven ontology, program-of-record ICDs, exercise data) is CUI or vendor-gated and obtainable only via sponsorship.

Highest-burden profile in the study: CUI at minimum, Secret for division data layers, SCI for Maven feeds, ATO required, facility clearance and FOCI review for a firm with a non-U.S.-person co-founder, possible ITAR technical data for weapon/C2 adapters, SBIR eligibility in doubt. Not a 0 because an unclassified component demo on open standards remains legal and possible.

Partly: a sync/catalog component can start on open standards and synthetic data, but anything that would justify calling it a competing fabric requires classified integration immediately (classification_dependence: immediate).

Scored 0 (most intense) because the slot is occupied by designation: Anduril leads the Army baseline, Palantir owns the ontology and Maven PoR, Raft holds registries/federation, Lockheed integrates 25th ID, AFS integrates the enterprise, government-owned TAK/Open DAGIR commoditize the interface, and Ditto, Picogrid, Tangram, XRDefense and PLANK crowd the component tier. Absence of a rival platform reflects buyer consolidation, not opportunity.

Some cracks exist (Army CTO 'very high risk' security memo Oct 2025, GAO schedule/cost warning Aug 2026, Advana churn and IG findings, official lock-in concern behind Open DAGIR/R2I), but they are being addressed inside the incumbents' vehicles, not through a recompete. Not a 0 because a future administration or GAO/IG pressure could reopen the architecture.

A platform must integrate everything: Lattice SDK and Palantir OSDK are vendor-gated, program-of-record APIs remain prime-controlled even after Jailbreak documented them, and each sensor or vehicle protocol is bespoke (Shift5 took two months for one telemetry integration). A new entrant would face every seam with none of the incumbents' access.

The government intends to own the interfaces (UDRA, Open DAGIR, Right to Integrate) and the platform owners can absorb components; nothing a new fabric vendor builds becomes proprietary except onboarded adapters and exercise-proven deployments inside someone else's stack.

Data-mesh, registry and offline-first sync technology has a genuine commercial market (Ditto funds defense work from commercial revenue), so the technology is portable, but the commercial data-fabric market is itself dominated by Databricks, Snowflake, Confluent and hyperscalers.

If a firm somehow held the fabric slot, expansion across services and allies would be enormous (Anduril and Palantir demonstrate this), but the conditional is not credible; realistic expansion is that of a component riding a platform owner's growth.

Enterprise software licenses and task orders in this layer recur annually under the enterprise agreements and Maven's ceiling raises show demand exceeding scope; the recurring revenue is real, it just accrues to the designated vendors.

Scored 0 because nothing the platform play requires matches the team: no cleared U.S.-citizen personnel (neither founder can currently hold a clearance), a non-U.S.-person co-founder that complicates FOCI/SBIR/deemed-export status, no program-office or exercise relationships, $250k against incumbents spending at four to five orders of magnitude more, and no prior data-platform operating experience at scale. The same team could fit a narrow open-standards component, which is scored under other gaps.

market.summary: No budget owner wants a second platform: NGC2 money executes through the June 2026 baseline team under decade-long enterprise agreements, joint money goes to Maven as program of record, enterprise money went to an integrator; the only 'demand' is government preference for owning interfaces, which favors free standards, not a new vendor. The pain is real but is felt at seams the incumbents are funded to close.

competition.summary: Anduril, Palantir and Raft do not need six months to add it; they are the designated fabric, hold the SDKs every third party must use, and can absorb any demonstrated feature. Government-owned TAK/Open DAGIR/UDRA commoditize the interface layer, and switching cost after fielding at 4th ID, 25th ID and I Corps rises every quarter.

feasibility.summary: A platform cannot be demonstrated credibly without Secret-level exercise access, an ATO, cleared staff and a facility clearance; a two-student team with a non-U.S.-person co-founder and $250k faces FOCI, SBIR-eligibility and deemed-export constraints before writing an adapter. The government's own prototype OTAs for this layer were $26M-$99.6M; a $250k MVP proves nothing a buyer would act on.

score.verdict_rationale: Decisive reason: the platform slot was filled by designation (Army NGC2 common data-layer baseline, June 22 2026; Maven program of record, March 2026; AFS enterprise integration, July 2026) and is locked behind 10-year enterprise agreements with $10B and $20B ceilings, so the PROBLEM -> USER -> REQUIREMENT OWNER -> PROGRAM OFFICE -> CONTRACTING OFFICE -> BUDGET -> VEHICLE chain exists but every link already terminates at Anduril/Palantir/Raft; there is no buyer, no vehicle and no feasible demo for a $250k two-student team with a non-U.S.-person co-founder. Market attractiveness 1.7 and founder fit 1.0 with the major no-path penalty applied. The registry's LOW pre-rating is confirmed; the gap should be eliminated explicitly.
score.narrower_version_if_borderline: Not borderline. The survivable descendants are already tracked separately as seam components sold through a team lead or a government-owned door: UDRA-conformant tactical-echelon data-product catalog for DDIL nodes (cf. G02/G05), automated conformance and contract-test tooling for the government-approved NGC2 API baseline and Jailbreak API marketplace (cf. G07), and policy-aware releasability tagging and sync for coalition enclaves (cf. G17). None of these is a 'competing data fabric'.
score.most_important_question_answer: With $250,000 today, two exceptionally capable founders should not build a competing data fabric at all; if they insist on this layer, the only defensible first build is a small open-standards component - a DDIL-tolerant data-product catalog and schema registry on a rugged edge node that ingests CoT/TAK and open protobuf feeds, applies releasability labels, and syncs conflict-free across partitions - demonstrated on three commercial nodes with synthetic data. They should show it to the third-party onboarding leads of the NGC2 team stacks (Anduril Lattice SDK and Lockheed/Raft teams), the TAK Product Center plugin pipeline, and an Army or Air Force SBIR TPOC, and the demo must prove that onboarding a new feed takes hours instead of the two months Shift5 needed and that nothing is lost across partition and reconnection. The customer cares because the UDRA RFI concedes the mesh stops above tactical echelons and Jailbreak showed onboarding is the bottleneck. An incumbent cannot trivially crush them only if the component is positioned as something they would rather license or acquire than rebuild, which is a licensing/acqui-hire outcome, not a platform company. The milestone that would justify $2-5M is a signed subcontract or Phase II/III with a team lead plus successful participation in an Ivy Sting / Lightning Surge class event; absent that within 12-18 months the idea fails because there is no independent buyer. As framed (a general-purpose competing fabric), it fails on day one for lack of a buyer, a vehicle and a feasible demo.
score.bear_case_summary: The Army just chose (June 2026), the joint level chose Maven (PoR March 2026), the enterprise chose an integrator (AFS, July 2026), and both platform owners hold decade-long vehicles with $10B and $20B ceilings; the government's stated strategy is to own interfaces, not to buy a second platform; standalone middleware startups in this layer sit in SBIR purgatory (Tangram since 2020, XRDefense $4.75M Phase III); every real integration needs CUI/Secret access, an ATO and cleared staff that a two-student, non-U.S.-person-inclusive team cannot supply; and $250k is four to five orders of magnitude below the incumbents' spend on the same layer.
score.bull_case_summary: Strongest honest bull case: the layer is where the money is (NGC2 ~$3.78B FY27 request, >$2B FY27 for Maven/JFN), the government has publicly conceded the seams (undocumented APIs, classification, tagging, mesh stopping at division, IG-documented enterprise ingest failures), Open DAGIR/UDRA/Right to Integrate signal official discomfort with lock-in, an Army CTO memo and GAO have flagged security and schedule risk in the chosen stack, and team leads have proven they pull small vendors in within months (Rune, Shift5, Accelint, Striveworks). Even this bull case supports a seam component with an acquisition exit, not a competing fabric.

verdicts.bear_case: There is no budget owner for a second general-purpose fabric. NGC2 funding (~$3.78B FY27 request) executes through the June 2026 common data-layer baseline team; joint CJADC2 funding (>$2B FY27) buys Maven licenses under a program of record; the enterprise layer went to a cost-plus integrator (AFS, up to $821M). The pain that is real - swivel-chair reconciliation, coalition thumb drives, undocumented APIs, classification-blocked sharing - is exercise- and staff-level pain at the seams that the designated vendors are contractually funded to close. Market research (CDAO data-mesh RFI 2023, DIA CDF RFI 2024) ended in awards to Anduril and Palantir, not in an open competition. A startup pitching a platform would drift into integration consultancy under a team lead, which is a services business, not a product company.
verdicts.strongest_single_argument: The Army designated Anduril (with Palantir and Raft) to lead the NGC2 common data-layer baseline on June 22 2026 and executes the work under a 10-year, up-to-$20B enterprise agreement; the buying moment for this layer has passed for roughly a program generation.
verdicts.what_would_change_my_mind: A published Army or CDAO solicitation to recompete the common data layer or to onboard a second fabric vendor; a GAO/IG finding that leads Congress to direct a competitive alternative; or evidence that a service other than the Army (Navy Overmatch, DAF Battle Network) is running an open competition for a general-purpose fabric that a small firm could win outright.
verdicts.narrower_survivable_version: A seam component with a named budget line inside an existing program: e.g., a UDRA-conformant tactical-echelon data-product catalog sold as a third-party capability under an NGC2 team lead or as a TAK plugin, with an explicit licensing/acquisition exit.

verdicts.bear_case: Anduril, Palantir and Raft do not have to add this capability in six months; they are the designated capability. Every third-party app onboards through Lattice SDK or Palantir OSDK, so the incumbents control the APIs a challenger would need; program-of-record APIs exposed at Jailbreak remain prime-controlled; government-owned TAK, Open DAGIR and UDRA commoditize the interface layer so there is no price point between 'free standard' and 'bundled by the platform owner'. Switching cost rises with every division fielded (4th ID, 25th ID, I Corps next) and with every ATO granted. Ditto, Picogrid, Tangram Flex, XRDefense, PLANK and Striveworks already occupy the component niches, mostly at SBIR scale, which shows how hard it is to grow past a Phase III in this layer. L3Harris (ABMS DI), Northrop (IBCS) and Systematic (SitaWare) hold the domain and coalition fabrics.
verdicts.strongest_single_argument: The incumbents own the interfaces a challenger would have to integrate with (Lattice SDK, Foundry OSDK, the government-approved NGC2 API baseline executed under their vehicles), so any feature a startup demonstrates can be absorbed within a release cycle while the startup cannot even reach the data without their permission.
evidence: https://orangeslices.ai/contract-award-5m-air-force-sbir-phase-iii-zero-trust-data-fabric/ (2025, FACT, MEDIUM - shows Phase III scale ceiling for standalone fabric startups)
verdicts.what_would_change_my_mind: Evidence that the Army enforces vendor-neutral, government-owned APIs strongly enough that a second fabric can plug in without Anduril/Palantir consent (e.g., a published, non-CUI NGC2 API baseline with open conformance tests), or an incumbent exit/termination for cause that reopens the layer.
verdicts.narrower_survivable_version: Conformance and contract-test tooling for the government-approved NGC2 API baseline and Jailbreak API marketplace, positioned as something the government (not the platform owners) wants to own and that reduces the incumbents' onboarding burden rather than competing with them.

verdicts.bear_case: A competing fabric cannot be credibly demonstrated without Secret-level exercise access (division data layers run at Secret; Maven feeds involve SCI), an ATO, cleared U.S.-citizen engineers and a facility clearance. Neither founder can currently hold a clearance; a non-U.S.-person co-founder with equity or control triggers FOCI review, may bar SBIR/STTR eligibility, and complicates deemed-export handling of interface control documents (constraints to review with counsel, not legal conclusions). The government's own prototype OTAs for the layer were $99.6M and $26M, so a $250k MVP demonstrates a lab toy that no program office would treat as evidence, and the path to a task order under a team-lead vehicle is realistically 18-36 months and $2-5M away even for a component. Building the platform itself would consume $30M-$100M+ before a first production deployment.
verdicts.strongest_single_argument: Classification dependence is immediate and every meaningful integration requires CUI/Secret access, an ATO and cleared staff, none of which a two-student team with a non-U.S.-person co-founder and $250k can obtain in the timeframe of the money.

https://www.gao.gov/products/gao-26-108019 (2026-08-20, FACT, HIGH; fielding schedule undefined, so even a sub's timeline is uncertain)
verdicts.what_would_change_my_mind: A restructured cap table with U.S.-person control and a cleared technical co-founder or early hire, a sponsored unclassified sandbox (e.g., a TAK or Open DAGIR reference environment with published schemas) sufficient for a credible demo, and a team-lead letter of intent to onboard the component into an exercise within 12 months.
verdicts.narrower_survivable_version: An unclassified, open-standards DDIL sync/catalog component demonstrated on commercial hardware with synthetic data, entered through the TAK plugin pipeline or a Tradewinds awardable video, with the non-U.S.-person founder kept on the commercial/NATO-EU product line while counsel resolves FOCI and SBIR eligibility.

card.title: Vendor-neutral DDIL test and conformance harness for tactical software (link emulation, multi-node TAK/CoT sync scoring, pre-Jailbreak API contract tests, TAK plugin RBAC/audit conformance)
card.problem: Small vendors, prime integration teams and program-office T&E cells have no reproducible, vendor-neutral way to prove before a live event how a tactical application behaves over 1 Mbps to 1 kbps links, partitions and reconnect storms, or whether it conforms to the government-baselined TAK/CoT and NGC2 interfaces and the Army AO's RBAC/audit expectations, so integration and resilience are still proven at expensive in-person events (Operation Jailbreak, Ivy Sting, NetModX, Radio Rodeo).

user.exact_role: Integration and test engineer at a small sensor/vehicle/app vendor preparing for a Jailbreak-series sprint or NGC2 onboarding; prime T&E engineer (Team Anduril / Team Lockheed data-layer or app leads); government network T&E engineer at DEVCOM C5ISR Center, ATEC or the APG/Huntsville software integration labs; TAK plugin developer submitting through the TAK.gov pipelines
user.echelon: Program office, prime and vendor engineering (pre-fielding); indirectly brigade/division units whose exercises absorb the failures
organization_examples: MatrixSpace, Adyton, Shift5-class Jailbreak participants
Anduril and Lockheed Martin NGC2 team-lead T&E cells
DEVCOM C5ISR Center (Radio Rodeo, NetModX)
ATEC and the Huntsville / Aberdeen software integration labs
TAK Product Center third-party pipeline users
4ID / 25ID NGC2 unit tech teams

current_workflow: 1. Vendor builds a TAK plugin, CoT feed or Lattice SDK integration against documentation and a free vendor sandbox (Lattice Sandboxes) or a self-hosted TAK Server with no link degradation.
2. Vendor and team lead do ad hoc lab tests on an office LAN; bandwidth limits, partitions and reconnect behaviour are rarely scripted.

3. Integration is proven at an in-person event: Operation Jailbreak (Fort Carson, May 2026, ~600 people, 55-80 firms), Ivy Sting / Lightning Surge iterations, or a C5ISR Center Radio Rodeo / NetModX slot.

4. Failures (firewall surprises, undocumented APIs, lag under denied conditions, missing access control and audit logging) are found live and 'fixed in almost real time' by industry engineers during the exercise.

5. Government labs (C5ISR Center, ATEC, APG/Huntsville SILs, Army Software Factory validation of jailbroken interfaces) then harden and validate the capability using their own emulation infrastructure.
6. The next vendor, unit or sprint repeats the cycle; results are not published as reusable, comparable metrics.
card.current_solution: Government-owned emulation and test infrastructure (DEVCOM C5ISR Center laboratory DDIL effects used in the March-April 2026 Radio Rodeo; NetModX persistent experimentation; ATEC support to Jailbreak; APG and Huntsville software integration labs); government-sponsored open-source emulators NRL EMANE and CORE (with Adjacent Link SRW/WNW waveform ports); commercial network emulators (Keysight EXata / JNE, Apposite, iTrinegy, Linux tc/netem); platform-owner sandboxes (Anduril Lattice Sandboxes, free with unlimited API calls); TAK Server's own takcl test framework and the TAK.gov third-party signing pipeline; generic API contract-test tooling (OpenAPI/protobuf validators, Pact-style contract tests); and, for the DDIL data-load modelling ask, the Army SBIR topic A254-019 selected Assured Information Security's GRUNTS through xTechIgnite 2025.
card.failure: The pieces exist separately and are owned by parties who have no incentive to publish neutral, comparable scores: link emulation is a government or commercial-appliance product, API sandboxes are platform-owner products, conformance validation is a government lab function, and no one offers a small vendor a single self-hosted run that says 'your feed and plugin survive a 30-minute partition at 4 kbps, reconcile without duplicate tracks, pass the TAK/CoT and Lattice schema contracts, and emit AO-visible audit events' before the sprint date.

This is the only public solicitation naming DDIL tactical-network test/simulation tooling as a deliverable, and it is a $250k Phase I, not a certification-harness buy.

card.why_existing_startups_havent_solved: Because the pieces are already owned by parties for whom they are a means, not a product: link emulation is free government-sponsored software (NRL EMANE/CORE) or a mature commercial appliance market (Keysight EXata/JNE, Apposite, iTrinegy) sold to labs and primes; the API-side test environment is given away by the platform owner (Anduril Lattice Sandboxes, free, unlimited calls) because it grows its ecosystem; TAK's signing pipeline is free and government-run; and conformance/validation of jailbroken interfaces is a statutory-style government function performed by ATEC, C5ISR Center and the APG/Huntsville software integration labs. The one solicited piece of DDIL test tooling (A254-019 GRUNTS) was routed through xTechIgnite to an established SBIR performer (Assured Information Security). What remains for a startup is the scoring/scenario layer that stitches these together for small vendors - useful, but a low-price, episodic B2B purchase that never becomes a mandated acceptance gate unless a government body designates it, and no evidence shows one intends to.
card.technical_wedge: An open-source, self-hosted 'DDIL bench': (1) a scenario runner that drives Linux tc/netem or EMANE/CORE link profiles from 1 Mbps to 1 kbps with scripted partitions and reconnect storms across roughly 10 containerised ATAK-CIV / TAK Server nodes (later Ditto SDK and Lattice SDK adapters); (2) a scorer that reports time-to-arrival of priority CoT objects, duplicate or conflicting objects after reconnect, link saturation on reconnect and a reconcile-log audit; (3) a contract-test pack that validates a vendor's CoT/TAK Server Mission API and public Lattice protobuf/OpenAPI usage from a capture or spec; (4) an ATAK plugin conformance module that exercises a plugin with synthetic roles and tagged data and emits an RBAC matrix, audit-event coverage and SBOM as a signed, machine-readable (OSCAL-style) bundle. The only proprietary asset would be the scenario library and scoring rubric, which a platform owner or government lab can replicate.

mvp.what: Dockerised TAK DDIL bench: 8-10 ATAK-CIV emulator/TAK Server nodes behind netem (or EMANE/CORE) profiles, a YAML scenario language for link profiles and partition schedules, a scorer producing an HTML/JSON report, plus a contract-test CLI for CoT/TAK Mission API and public Lattice schemas and an ATAK plugin RBAC/audit conformance module.
mvp.demonstrable_in_3_6_months: Yes: run three public TAK plugins and a synthetic MAVLink/CoT sensor feed through a 30-minute 4 kbps partition-and-reconnect scenario and show comparable scored reports; run the plugin conformance module against an open-source ATAK plugin and emit a signed OSCAL-style results bundle.
mvp.what_it_must_prove: That an independent, reproducible score reveals behaviours (arrival order, duplicates after reconnect, link saturation, missing audit events) that vendors and team leads currently discover only at Jailbreak/Ivy Sting, and that at least one vendor and one government or prime T&E engineer will treat the report as pre-event evidence.

data_requirement.what: Synthetic CoT/TAK traffic and mission data; public Lattice SDK schemas (buf.build) and TAK Server API documentation; representative DDIL link profiles (bandwidth, latency, loss, partition schedules); ideally recorded traces from real tactical radios and exercise networks for realism.
data_requirement.legally_realistically_obtainable: Synthetic traffic, public schemas and generic link profiles: yes, today, by both founders. Real PoR radio traces, SRW/WNW EMANE waveform models and exercise network captures: no - these are distribution-controlled or CUI/ITAR-adjacent and require a government sponsor and U.S.-person handling (constraint for counsel, not a legal determination). Realism of the harness therefore plateaus at 'generic DDIL' unless a lab adopts it.

score.title: Vendor-neutral DDIL test and conformance harness for tactical software (link emulation, multi-node TAK/CoT sync scoring, pre-Jailbreak API contract tests, TAK plugin RBAC/audit conformance)

scores.rationale: Real but episodic: Operation Jailbreak needed ~600 people from 55-80 firms to expose interfaces (DefenseScoop 2026-05-29, FACT/HIGH); Ivy Sting 4-5 found DDIL and code faults live with industry 'fixing the code in almost real time' (DVIDS 2026-03-30, FACT/HIGH); the Sept 2025 AO memo made missing RBAC/audit an authorization blocker (CNBC 2025-10-03, RECALL/MEDIUM). But the pain is absorbed by exercise time and engineer hours, not by lost missions, and the government has already stood up labs (Radio Rodeo, ATEC/SIL hardening) to reduce it.

Integration events now recur on a monthly-to-quarterly cadence (Ivy Sting iterations, Jailbreak series incl. Falcon Fury, NetModX persistent experimentation) so the vendor population feels it repeatedly, but any single vendor faces a pre-sprint deadline only a few times a year.

Explained 1: no budget line, RFI, OTA or task order for a neutral test/conformance harness was found. The only solicited demand is Army SBIR A254-019 (Phase I up to $250k, 2025-02, FACT/HIGH), routed through xTechIgnite to Assured Information Security's GRUNTS (xtech.army.mil 2025-05, FACT/MEDIUM), i.e. already assigned and Phase I-scale. NGC2's ~$3.78B FY27 request (Breaking Defense 2026-04) and 50% obligation cap (FNN 2026-02) fund primes and government labs, not test tooling; government T&E is institutionally funded inside C5ISR Center and ATEC. Not 0 because A254-019 proves the Army will spend at least Phase I money on DDIL test tooling.

Vendor B2B sales need no vehicle but are tiny; the government route runs through xTech/SBIR (ownership-gated for this team, 13 CFR 121.702) or an unsolicited C5ISR Center / prime T&E task order with no precedent found; NetModX and xTech hackathons offer access to users but not purchase orders.

Explained 5: every component exists as open or public software - ATAK-CIV and TAK Server (government open source), NRL EMANE/CORE and Linux netem for link emulation, public Lattice SDK schemas and free Sandboxes, standard contract-test and SBOM/OSCAL tooling. Building a scenario runner and scorer on top is engineering, not research.

Explained 5: proof of concept estimated at $40-90k and a credible lab demo at $150-400k (HYPOTHESIS), well inside $250k for the first two stages; no hardware beyond ~10 SBCs/laptops or cloud containers; no ATO or classified access needed.

A scored multi-node TAK DDIL run and a plugin conformance report are achievable in 3-4 months; 'credible military demo' still requires an event slot (NetModX, Radio Rodeo, Jailbreak-series) whose timing the founders do not control.

Synthetic CoT/MAVLink traffic, public TAK and Lattice schemas and DARPA FLUID's published 1 Mbps-1 kbps regime cover the MVP; real PoR radio traces, SRW/WNW EMANE waveform models and exercise captures are controlled and unobtainable without a sponsor, which caps realism.

Open-core software on public inputs carries low export-control and no ATO burden; deductions for SBIR ownership rules (13 CFR 121.702, FACT/HIGH), AFWERX foreign-national limits (2025-07-02, FACT/HIGH) and the need for a technology control plan if any controlled inputs are touched. Counsel required; no legal determination.

Explained 5: the entire product is unclassified by construction - ATAK-CIV is open source, TAK.gov's third-party pipeline is open to anyone not on the Denied Parties List, Lattice Sandboxes are free and public, EMANE/CORE are public; classification only enters if a government lab later feeds it controlled traces.

Each layer is occupied: government labs (C5ISR Center Radio Rodeo 2026-03/04, ATEC and APG/Huntsville SILs), free government-sponsored emulators (NRL EMANE/CORE with SRW/WNW ports), commercial emulators (Keysight EXata/JNE, Apposite, iTrinegy), platform sandboxes (Anduril Lattice Sandboxes, free), TAK Server's own takcl test framework, and the xTechIgnite winner AIS GRUNTS for the GenAI DDIL simulation ask. Only the cross-vendor scoring layer is unoccupied, and absence of a competitor there is not evidence of demand.

Explained 1: the parties that would have to buy or bless a neutral harness (Army CTO/AO, C5ISR Center, ATEC, TAK Product Center, NGC2 team leads) already own the acceptance authority and run their own labs, and the platform owners give the API-side test environment away for free to grow their ecosystems; none is exposed by, or needs, an outside scorer.

TAK/CoT and the TAK Server Mission API are open and documented; Lattice SDK schemas are public with free sandboxes; Ditto SDK is licensable commercially; the closed parts (PoR radio management planes, CUI ICDs) can be excluded from the harness without breaking the core value.

Explained 1: scenario libraries and scoring rubrics are replicable in weeks by Anduril, Ditto, TAK Product Center or a government lab; there is no owned data, interface, accreditation or credential gate; the only durable asset would be a government designation of the report as accepted evidence, for which no signal exists.

Offline-first and network-partition testing has commercial analogues (public safety apps, maritime, mining, retail edge), but generic chaos-engineering and WAN-emulation tools already serve them and the TAK/AO-specific modules have no commercial pull.

Could extend to Ditto/Lattice adapters, allied TAK users (NATO, Bundeswehr D-LBO ecosystem) and T&E services, but every extension stays inside a lab-tool and services niche whose ceiling is well below venture scale.

Per-sprint readiness engagements and lab licences recur, but at low price points ($5-25k per engagement, INFERENCE) from a vendor base of ~50-80 firms per event, and government labs would more likely adopt an open-source bench than pay per run.

The strong engineer can build the whole bench on public code, and the non-U.S.-person founder is not blocked from the open-core work (INFERENCE; counsel to confirm); the business founder can sell readiness runs to vendors. Missing: any tactical-network T&E credibility, operator or lab relationships, and an SBIR-eligible cap table - the first is rated fatal if not recruited.

market.summary: No requirement owner, program office, contracting office, budget line or vehicle exists for a neutral harness; the government performs test and conformance itself (C5ISR Center Radio Rodeo, NetModX, ATEC and APG/Huntsville SILs), the one solicited DDIL test-tooling ask was a $250k Phase I already routed to AIS via xTechIgnite, and the residual vendor market is episodic and low-price, so the business drifts into consultancy.

competition.summary: Every layer already has a free or entrenched supplier - NRL EMANE/CORE, Keysight/Apposite, Anduril's free Lattice Sandboxes, TAK Server's takcl framework and signing pipeline - and the platform owners or labs can publish their own DDIL benchmark in weeks; the startup's only differentiator, impartiality, matters only if a government body designates its report, which nothing evidences.

feasibility.summary: This lens does not kill the gap: the harness is fully unclassified, buildable on public code for well under $250k, and the non-U.S.-person founder can work on the open core; the constraints (SBIR ownership, controlled waveform models and radio traces, lack of T&E credibility) limit growth and realism, not the ability to build and demonstrate.

score.verdict_rationale: KILL as a venture; keep as a sub-$60k open-source credibility asset. Applying the chain test: PROBLEM (real, FACT/HIGH) -> USER (vendor, prime and lab T&E engineers, FACT) -> REQUIREMENT OWNER: the DDIL-resilience and interface-conformance requirements are owned by CPE C2IN, the Army CTO/AO and ADOC, who have chosen to satisfy them through government labs (C5ISR Center Radio Rodeo 2026-03/04; ATEC and APG/Huntsville SIL hardening of 74+ jailbroken capabilities; Army Software Factory validation) and prime T&E -> PROGRAM OFFICE: none for test tooling -> CONTRACTING OFFICE: none identified (Public evidence insufficient) -> BUDGET: no line; the only solicited money is Army SBIR A254-019 (Phase I up to $250k) already routed through xTechIgnite to Assured Information Security's GRUNTS -> VEHICLE: BREAK, and the one open rail (SBIR) is ownership-gated for this team. The major penalty applies. Two independently sufficient kill reasons: (1) the function is government-owned and already resourced, on top of free government-sponsored emulators (NRL EMANE/CORE) and free platform sandboxes (Anduril Lattice Sandboxes), so a neutral harness has no buyer who needs it; (2) the residual buyer set (50-80 small vendors per sprint) is an episodic, low-price services market with a replicable product and no moat. Market attractiveness 2.4 (budget 1, incumbent vulnerability 1, moat 1); founder fit 4.2 is high precisely because the thing is cheap, open and legal to build - which is also why it is not a company. Confidence HIGH on the venture-scale question; MEDIUM on individual facts drawn from search summaries (AIS GRUNTS selection, ATEC article details) and RECALL items from parent cards.
score.narrower_version_if_borderline: Not borderline - killed as a venture. The residual, survivable form is explicitly not a company: an open-source 'TAK DDIL bench' (netem/EMANE link profiles, ~10 ATAK-CIV/TAK Server nodes, sync-scoring report) plus an ATAK plugin RBAC/audit/SBOM conformance module, released publicly and used (a) to sell a handful of fixed-fee pre-sprint readiness runs to Jailbreak-series vendors, (b) as the entry into a NetModX / C5ISR Center persistent-experimentation slot or xTech hackathon, and (c) as the credibility asset that gets the founders into an NGC2 sub-vendor, a prime T&E cell or a TAK plugin shop. Size it at $30-60k and 3-4 months, expect no government purchase, and treat any lab adoption as a relationship, not revenue.
score.most_important_question_answer: If two exceptionally capable founders with $250,000 insisted on this gap, they should spend no more than $30-60k and four months building the open-source TAK DDIL bench: containerised ATAK-CIV and TAK Server nodes behind netem or EMANE/CORE profiles spanning 1 Mbps to 1 kbps with scripted 30-minute partitions and reconnect storms, a scorer reporting time-to-arrival of priority CoT objects, duplicates and conflicts after reconnect and link saturation, a CoT/TAK Mission API and public-Lattice-schema contract-test CLI, and an ATAK plugin module that emits an RBAC matrix, audit-event coverage and SBOM as a signed OSCAL-style bundle. They would show it to three or four small vendors facing the next Jailbreak-series date (MatrixSpace/Adyton-class), a C5ISR Center tactical-network S&T lead through a NetModX or Radio Rodeo application, and a Team Anduril or Team Lockheed T&E engineer. The demo would prove that a reproducible score exposes, before the event, the failures (arrival order, duplicate tracks after reconnect, saturation, missing audit events) that today are discovered live at Ivy Sting and Jailbreak, and the vendor would care because failing at the sprint costs a fielding window while the lab would care because comparable numbers help it triage 50-80 vendors. An incumbent cannot be bothered to crush it - Anduril already gives away Lattice Sandboxes, TAK Product Center ships its own test framework, and C5ISR Center and ATEC run the labs - which is exactly the problem: nobody needs to buy it, and any of them can publish an equivalent benchmark in weeks if it ever mattered. The only milestone that would justify $2-5M is an external designation - a C5ISR Center, Army CTO/AO or TAK Product Center statement that the bench's report is accepted pre-event or acceptance evidence, backed by a task order or Phase II-scale award and a prime subcontract to run it - and no public evidence suggests that event is coming inside the founders' runway; the one solicited dollar for DDIL test tooling already went to an established SBIR firm. So it fails as a company: build it small, publish it, use it to earn relationships and a first subcontract, and put the venture-scale ambition and the $250k elsewhere.
score.bear_case_summary: Test and conformance of tactical software is a government-owned function the Army is resourcing itself: C5ISR Center's laboratory DDIL effects (Radio Rodeo, March-April 2026, FACT/HIGH), NetModX persistent experimentation (FACT/HIGH), ATEC-supported hardening of 74+ jailbroken capabilities at Huntsville and APG SILs (FACT/MEDIUM) and Army Software Factory validation of jailbroken interfaces (RECALL/MEDIUM). The emulation layer is free government software (NRL EMANE/CORE, FACT/HIGH) or a mature commercial appliance market (Keysight, Apposite), the API-side test environment is free from the platform owner (Lattice Sandboxes, FACT/HIGH), TAK signing is free and government-run, and the only solicited DDIL test-tooling money (A254-019, Phase I up to $250k) is already routed to AIS via xTechIgnite (FACT/MEDIUM). There is no requirement owner, program office, budget line or vehicle for a neutral harness; SBIR is ownership-gated for this cap table (13 CFR 121.702, FACT/HIGH); the residual market is 50-80 small vendors buying episodic readiness runs, which is a consultancy. Confidence HIGH.
score.bull_case_summary: The pain is real and now has dates: Jailbreak is a series (Fort Carson May 2026, Falcon Fury), Ivy Sting iterates monthly, NGC2 must scale across divisions and corps, the common data baseline (2026-06), API Marketplace (2026-05) and public Lattice schemas make conformance testable, DARPA FLUID and A254-019 define the DDIL regime, and the Sept 2025 AO memo made RBAC/audit evidence an authorization gate. The MVP is unusually accessible - unclassified, open-source-buildable for tens of thousands of dollars, legal for the non-U.S.-person founder to build (INFERENCE; counsel to confirm), and exportable to allied TAK users. If a C5ISR Center lab, TAK Product Center or an NGC2 team lead adopted a neutral bench as its pre-event gate, the first mover would hold a small, recurring, mandated niche across NGC2, TAK and allied TAK ecosystems. This is a credible open-source project and services wedge, and a plausible acqui-hire, not a venture-scale company; the adoption event it depends on is unevidenced (HYPOTHESIS/LOW).

verdicts.bear_case: There is no budget owner for a vendor-neutral DDIL test and conformance harness because the Army already performs the function itself. DEVCOM C5ISR Center ran a Radio Rodeo (March-April 2026) using its own laboratory infrastructure to create DDIL effects for NGC2 vendors and runs NetModX as persistent experimentation; ATEC supports Operation Jailbreak and the Army is hardening the 74+ jailbroken capabilities at its own software integration labs in Huntsville and Aberdeen; the Army Software Factory validates jailbroken interfaces (RECALL from G07). The only solicited demand for DDIL test tooling is Army SBIR A254-019 'Generative AI Enabled Tactical Network' - a Phase I of up to $250k - and it was routed through xTechIgnite 2025 to Assured Information Security's GRUNTS, so even that dollar is assigned. NGC2's ~$3.78B FY27 request funds primes and government activity under a 50% obligation cap; no sub-line, RFI, OTA or task order names test tooling. What is left is 50-80 small vendors per sprint who might pay a few thousand dollars for a readiness run before a Jailbreak-series date: episodic, price-capped, and exactly the shape of a consultancy. The pain is exercise-time pain, absorbed by engineers and labs, and the primes and government are visibly solving it themselves.
verdicts.strongest_single_argument: The customer has already built and staffed the product: C5ISR Center's laboratory DDIL effects (Radio Rodeo 2026), ATEC/SIL validation of jailbroken capabilities and free government emulators (NRL EMANE/CORE) mean the requirement owner has no need to buy a neutral harness, and the one solicited dollar for DDIL test tooling (A254-019, $250k Phase I) already went to an established SBIR firm.

verdicts.bear_case: Every layer of the proposed harness already has a free or entrenched supplier, and the parties that control conformance are the platform owners and government labs, not a startup. Link emulation: NRL's EMANE and CORE are free, government-sponsored (OSD NCCP, ARL cooperation) and carry Adjacent Link's SRW/WNW waveform ports; Keysight EXata/JNE and Apposite sell tactical DDIL emulation to labs and primes; Linux netem is a one-liner. API contract tests: Anduril's Lattice Sandboxes are free with unlimited API calls and simulated data, and TAK Server ships its own takcl test framework while TAK.gov signs third-party plugins for free. RBAC/audit conformance: Anduril and Palantir own the SDKs and Defense Unicorns, Second Front and RegScale-class vendors cover pipeline and compliance evidence (RECALL from G14). Government validation: ATEC, C5ISR Center and the Army Software Factory. The startup's residual differentiator - an impartial cross-vendor score across TAK, Lattice and Ditto - is replicable in weeks by any of them and has value only if a government body designates it; Anduril, Ditto or TAK Product Center could publish their own DDIL benchmark in one release. Switching cost is nil because the harness owns no interface, and the government already owns the software that matters (TAK, EMANE/CORE).
verdicts.strongest_single_argument: The government already owns free versions of the hardest parts (NRL EMANE/CORE for emulation, TAK Server's test framework and the TAK.gov signing pipeline for conformance) and the platform owner gives away the API test environment (Lattice Sandboxes), so the startup would be selling a scoring wrapper around other people's free tools to buyers who can assemble the same wrapper themselves.

verdicts.bear_case: Feasibility is the one lens that does not kill this gap, and the bear case here is about ceiling, not possibility. The harness is unclassified by construction (ATAK-CIV open source, TAK.gov pipeline open to non-U.S. persons, Lattice Sandboxes public, EMANE/CORE public), costs $40-90k to prove and $150-400k to demonstrate credibly (HYPOTHESIS), and the Indonesian founder can plausibly work on the open core (INFERENCE from public-input, EAR99-type software; counsel must confirm and screen dependencies such as SRW/WNW EMANE ports, which are distribution-controlled). The real constraints are: (1) realism plateaus without PoR radio traces, controlled waveform models or exercise captures, which require a government sponsor and U.S.-person handling; (2) the only government rail that has ever paid for DDIL test tooling (SBIR via xTech) fails 13 CFR 121.702 for a 50/50 cap table until the German founder holds a green card and U.S.-person investors or hires dilute the Indonesian founder below control, and AFWERX-style topics bar a foreign national as technical lead; (3) neither founder has tactical-network T&E credibility, so a lab or prime has no reason to trust the rubric; (4) a credible military demo depends on an event slot (NetModX, Radio Rodeo, Jailbreak-series) the founders do not control. None of this prevents a demo in four months; all of it prevents the demo from converting into a funded program.
verdicts.strongest_single_argument: The MVP is cheap, open and legal for this team, which is precisely why it is not defensible: anything two students can build in four months on NRL and TAK public code for under $60k, a government lab or platform owner can also build, and the gate that would turn it into revenue (SBIR eligibility, a lab sponsor, T&E credibility) is the part this team lacks.

Failures are logged; fixes deferred to the next spiral/CWIX; compliance registry updated
In operations and exercises, releasability of objects that were never labelled at source is decided by FDOs/JICOs by hand (WFX 24-03, Balikatan 2026) or products are regenerated on the REL enclave
card.current_solution: Vendor label libraries and products (Isode, Fortra Data Classification/Titus-Boldon James, archTIS NC Protect, Janusnet, Nexor), the open-source Spiffing SPIF/label/clearance library (Surevine), NATO ACT's CWIX and INSPECT, NCIA's own IV&V bundled into DCS COTS procurements, OGC/AWS DCS reference implementations, and CWIX-preparation consultancies (Corvus Intelligence, Thalorin, Mility). On the FVEY/U.S. side the ACP-240/ZTDF wrapper is Virtru/OpenTDF paired with Everfox guards; there is no public conformance linter for ACP-240 and Joint Staff J6 tests it at Bold Quest.
card.failure: Conformance is checked late and by the parties that own the registry (NATO ACT via CWIX/INSPECT) or bundled into COTS IV&V (NCIA DCS), so a third-party linter has no owner; the releasability that a partner will actually derive from a label plus SPIF plus its clearance is opaque to producers, but the ground truth needed to validate a derivation simulator (national SPIFs, REL decisions) is restricted; and the adapter kit half competes with SitaWare's native multi-standard support and government-owned TAK federation.

card.why_existing_startups_havent_solved: They have, in the only forms the market pays for: (1) label syntax/binding libraries and products are sold by Isode, Fortra, archTIS, Janusnet and Nexor, several with a decade of CWIX participation; (2) the open-source Spiffing library already provides a free SPIF/label/clearance engine; (3) year-round conformance is owned by NATO ACT (INSPECT) and CWIX, and NCIA bundles IV&V into its DCS COTS procurement (RFQ-CO-424368-DCS) rather than buying a separate linter; (4) the compliance-tooling and CWIX-preparation layer is already served by small consultancies (Thalorin, Corvus, Mility) - which is exactly the consultancy-shaped end state this gap would converge to. What no one sells is a producer-side releasability-derivation simulator for machine-generated tactical objects, but validating one requires national SPIFs and real REL decisions that are restricted, and the buyer for that (U.S. MPE/NGC2, NCIA later DCS milestones) either killed the parent gaps or has not tendered it.
card.technical_wedge: An open-source, deterministic toolkit: (a) a STANAG 4774/4778 + ADatP-5636 SPIF linter (XML and JSON/JOSE encodings) that validates syntax, binding signatures, SPIF consistency and FMN spiral profile constraints and produces a machine-readable report; (b) an ACP-240/ZTDF assertion checker built on the public OpenTDF spec; (c) a 'would-this-pass' releasability simulator that, given a label, a synthetic SPIF and a synthetic partner clearance matrix, shows which partner enclaves would derive access and where dominance/NOFORN-style rules block aggregation; (d) NFFI/NVG/MIP-JC3IEDM and CoT export adapters with schema validation; packaged as a CI job vendors run before CWIX and as a demo at TIDE Hackathon / CWIX Innovation Sandbox. It is buildable, but nothing in it is proprietary.

mvp.what: Command-line and web linter for STANAG 4774/4778 labels and SPIFs with an ACP-240/ZTDF assertion checker, a releasability-derivation simulator on synthetic SPIFs/clearances, and CoT-to-NFFI/NVG exporters with regression dashboard
mvp.demonstrable_in_3_6_months: Yes - 2-4 months for one engineer using public STANAG/ADatP texts, the OpenTDF spec and the Spiffing test corpus; the constraint is getting a CWIX/TIDE slot (annual) or a vendor willing to run it, not the build
mvp.what_it_must_prove: That it catches label/binding/SPIF and coalition-format regressions a vendor would otherwise discover at CWIX, in minutes rather than at the June event; that its simulated derivations agree with a reference implementation (Isode/Spiffing) on a shared synthetic corpus; and that at least one vendor or national cell values this enough to pay

regulatory_burden.explanation: Public NATO standards and synthetic data carry no ITAR/EAR technical-data burden; no ATO, CDS accreditation or clearance is required for the tool itself. Burden appears only when the team needs NATO RESTRICTED spiral profiles or CWIX test cases (nation-controlled) or wants an NCIA contract (BOA plus national Declaration of Eligibility, security clearances for staff on some RFQs). German export rules for military-end-use software need counsel.
regulatory_burden.non_us_person_founder_note: The Indonesian co-founder can lawfully work on everything built from public standards and synthetic data. Constraints to describe, not judge: NATO RESTRICTED material is released per nation and a non-NATO national's access is not assured; DIANA/NIF and NCIA eligibility tests look at ownership and control and may require the German founder to hold majority control; U.S. SBIR is closed to this cap table. All need counsel.

dual_use_potential.explanation: NATO confidentiality labels, SPIFs, ACP-240 and NFFI/NVG/MIP have no commercial analogue; the nearest commercial adjacency (enterprise data classification) is already served by Fortra/Microsoft Purview. Only the generic 'schema conformance CI' pattern is reusable, and it is not a business.

defensibility.explanation: Nothing durable. The standards are public, the data is synthetic by design, the reference engine is open source (Spiffing), the authoritative harness is government-owned (INSPECT/CWIX) and the ACP-240 reference implementation is Virtru/OpenTDF. At best the team accumulates a curated synthetic regression corpus and relationships at ACT/NCIA/vendors - the assets of a consultancy.

card.why_now: FMN Spiral 4 became mandatory for missions 2025-2027 and Spiral 5 is in development; NCIA started procuring DCS labelling in 2026 (Milestone 1) with more milestones implied; NATO ACT is moving conformance from an annual event to continuous INSPECT checks; NSA's April 2026 guideline anchored ACP-240/ZTDF on the FVEY side; DISA targets a data-centric MPE by 2027; DIANA and the Rapid Adoption Action Plan (2025-06-25) opened faster allied on-ramps. These make the standards matter more, but they also show the requirement owners (ACT, NCIA, NSA/Virtru) are solving the conformance layer themselves.
card.killer_risk: There is no buyer for a standalone linter/simulator: NATO ACT owns conformance (INSPECT/CWIX) and gives it to affiliates for free, NCIA buys labelling as COTS from established vendors with IV&V bundled, vendors already hold the libraries, and the residual demand (CWIX preparation, DCS readiness) is already served by consultancies at a scale that cannot support a venture.

score.title: NATO/FMN-first security-label conformance linter, releasability-derivation simulator and coalition-format adapter kit (STANAG 4774/4778, ACP-240/ZTDF, NFFI/NVG/MIP) built on public standards and synthetic data

scores.rationale: The downstream pain (FDO/JICO hand-tagging, WFX 24-03 regeneration, GAO-25-106454) is real and tier-1, but the tool's actual user - a vendor or national conformance engineer - suffers annoyance-level pain: defects surface at CWIX and are fixed next spiral. Nobody is losing a mission over a malformed label today.
Conformance pain for the tool's user recurs on the annual CWIX/spiral cadence (act.nato.int 2025-06, 2026-06); the daily hand-tagging pain belongs to operators the linter does not serve directly.

One dated line exists: NCIA RFQ-CO-424368-DCS Basic Labelling (~EUR 1.6M reported, deadline 2026-07-23), but it buys a COTS labelling product from an established vendor with IV&V bundled - not a linter. Other money is services (Bundeswehr CWIX support tender), DIANA EUR 100k challenge contracts, ACT's internal INSPECT funding and Joint Staff J6 demonstration lines. No budget line for a third-party conformance linter or releasability simulator was found.

NCIA requires a Basic Ordering Agreement and national Declaration of Eligibility; DIANA is a EUR 100k accelerator with topic and deadline constraints (2027 deadline passed 2026-07-03); CWIX Innovation Sandbox needs DIANA/national nomination; vendor licence sales are possible but tiny. Accessible for a German-led GmbH in principle, slow and gatekept in practice.

5 because nothing is technically hard: schema/signature validation of public XML/JSON label formats, SPIF consistency checks, deterministic derivation on synthetic clearance matrices and public NFFI/NVG/MIP schemas; an open-source engine (Spiffing) already exists to validate against.
5 because the PoC is USD 40-80k and a credible allied demo (TIDE/CWIX Sandbox) USD 120-250k; the whole scope fits the founders' capital with margin. Ease is itself a warning about defensibility.
A working linter/simulator in 2-4 months; not 5 because 'credible' requires a CWIX/TIDE slot or a vendor pilot on an annual cadence and a nation sponsor for restricted spiral profiles.

ADatP-4774/4778/5636, OpenTDF/ZTDF, NFFI/NVG/MIP schemas and Spiffing test data are public; FMN spiral profiles, CWIX test cases and national SPIFs are partly NATO RESTRICTED and real REL decisions are unobtainable - replaced by synthetic data by design.
No ITAR/EAR technical data, no ATO, no clearance for the tool itself; friction only at NATO RESTRICTED access, NCIA eligibility and German dual-use export rules (counsel).
5 because the gap is defined as public-standards-plus-synthetic-data; classification dependence is none.

1 because every layer is occupied: government harness (NATO ACT INSPECT/CWIX), label products (Isode, Fortra, archTIS, Janusnet, Nexor), open-source engine (Spiffing), ACP-240 reference implementation (Virtru/OpenTDF with Everfox), C2 vendor self-certification (Systematic), and compliance consultancies (Thalorin, Corvus, Mility). Absence of competitors is not the problem; abundance is.

1 because the incumbents are specialist DCS vendors with a decade of CWIX trials and the requirement owner is fielding its own harness; a linter is a quarter's work for Isode or Fortra and free from NATO. No incumbent is exposed.

A standalone CI linter integrates with nothing that can refuse it; the adapter-kit half needs SitaWare/TAK interfaces that Systematic and the TAK Product Center control, and INSPECT has no known public API.

1 because public standards, synthetic data, an open-source reference engine and a government-owned registry leave nothing to own; the only accumulations (synthetic corpus, ACT/NCIA relationships) are consultancy assets.
1 because NATO labels, SPIFs, ACP-240 and NFFI/NVG/MIP have no commercial analogue and commercial data classification is already Fortra/Purview territory.

Could grow toward system-to-system DCS labelling (NCIA later milestones, HYPOTHESIS) or ABAC policy tooling, but each adjacent step lands on Isode/Fortra/Virtru or on the parent gaps this study already killed.
An annual CWIX-preparation subscription from a handful of vendors and national cells at EUR 20-100k is conceivable; that is a consultancy's recurring revenue, not a product company's.

The German founder fits DIANA/Bundeswehr channels and the engineer can build the whole thing; the Indonesian co-founder is not blocked by public-standards work. But the founders have no NATO DCS/CWIX network, no domain SME, their stated primary interest is the U.S. market where this gap has no buyer, and DIANA/NCIA ownership tests need counsel.

market.summary: No budget owner for a third-party linter: NATO ACT owns conformance (INSPECT/CWIX, free to affiliates), NCIA buys labelling as COTS with IV&V bundled (RFQ-CO-424368-DCS, ~EUR 1.6M for the whole enterprise milestone), nations buy CWIX support as services, and the residual demand is already served by consultancies - a consultancy-shaped niche at best.

competition.summary: Every layer is occupied: Isode/Fortra/archTIS/Janusnet/Nexor products, open-source Spiffing, Virtru/OpenTDF+Everfox for ACP-240, Systematic self-certifying, Thalorin/Corvus/Mility on compliance tooling, and the government's own INSPECT. Any of them adds a linter in a quarter; none needs to.

feasibility.summary: Fully buildable unclassified with under USD 100k by this team including the non-U.S.-person co-founder; residual friction is NATO RESTRICTED spiral access, DIANA/NCIA eligibility and German export counsel. The ease is evidence of no moat, not of an opportunity.

score.verdict_rationale: Kill. Evaluated on its own merits, the narrower form fails the buyer test the parents failed, just more cheaply. The PROBLEM (late conformance defects; hand-tagging) and USER (vendor/national conformance engineers) exist, and this session found a real dated budget line the parents lacked - NCIA's Data Centric Security Milestone 1 Basic Labelling RFQ (2026-07, ~EUR 1.6M reported) - but that line buys a COTS labelling product from an established vendor and bundles the verification and validation inside the contract; the REQUIREMENT OWNER for conformance (NATO ACT) is fielding its own continuous harness (INSPECT) and gives CWIX results to affiliates; no PROGRAM OFFICE, CONTRACTING OFFICE or VEHICLE exists for a third-party linter or a releasability simulator, so the chain breaks at program office and the major penalty applies. Competition is the second decisive reason: five specialist label vendors (Isode, Fortra, archTIS, Janusnet, Nexor), an open-source reference engine (Spiffing), the ACP-240 reference implementation (Virtru/OpenTDF with Everfox), a self-certifying C2 incumbent (Systematic) and at least three compliance consultancies (Thalorin, Corvus, Mility) already occupy every layer this kit would sit in - the market has answered the question and its answer is 'feature or consultancy'. Founder fit is high (4.2) precisely because the work is easy, unclassified and legal for both founders, which is why it has no moat (criteria 11, 12, 14 at 1). Not borderline: the pain the founders would be solving is annoyance-level for the paying user, the addressable revenue is a few dozen vendors and cells at EUR 20-100k, and the founders' stated primary market (U.S.) has no buyer for it at all. Confidence MEDIUM: INSPECT's 2026 fielding status, the DIANA Secure Information Sharing challenge content and NCIA's later DCS milestones could not be read this session (egress blocked); a NATO tender for system-to-system labelling tooling open to non-BOA startups would be the fact most likely to move this to borderline.
score.narrower_version_if_borderline: Not applicable (kill). Recorded for completeness: the only defensible use is tactical - release the STANAG 4774/4778 + ACP-240 linter and synthetic-SPIF releasability simulator as open source, enter TIDE Hackathon 2027 / CWIX 2027 Innovation Sandbox under a German sponsor, and use the resulting credibility to (a) subcontract to a BOA-holding COTS labelling vendor if NCIA tenders a system-to-system DCS milestone (HYPOTHESIS), or (b) carry the allied credential into a different gap. If the founders insist on a company here, it must be a German GmbH majority-controlled by the German founder, selling DCS-readiness services - a consultancy, not a venture.
score.most_important_question_answer: If two exceptionally capable founders had USD 250,000 today and insisted on G30, they should spend under USD 60,000 and three months building an open-source STANAG 4774/4778 + ADatP-5636 linter with an ACP-240/ZTDF assertion checker and a 'would-this-pass' releasability simulator on synthetic SPIFs and partner clearances, cross-validated against Spiffing, and show it to one Isode- or Systematic-class interoperability lead, the NATO ACT Federated Interoperability branch (TIDE Sprint syndicate) and the Bundeswehr CWIX cell; the demo would prove it catches label, binding and coalition-format regressions in a CI run months before CWIX and that its derivations agree with a reference implementation. The customer would care mildly - late-surfacing defects at CWIX are irritating and NCIA has just started buying DCS labelling (RFQ-CO-424368-DCS, 2026-07) - but not enough to pay a product price, because NATO ACT's INSPECT does the authoritative version for free, NCIA bundles IV&V into the COTS contract it awards to established vendors, and the vendors already hold the libraries. No incumbent needs to crush them: Isode or Fortra can publish an equivalent linter in a quarter, Virtru owns the ZTDF reference, and Thalorin/Corvus already sell the compliance-tooling wrapper. There is no milestone that justifies USD 2-5M: two paid pilots at EUR 50-100k each and a CWIX Sandbox appearance would describe a competent consultancy with no proprietary asset, no repeatable product buyer and no U.S. path for a team whose primary interest is the U.S. market. It fails on market and moat, not on feasibility or founder legality; the honest use of this gap is as a low-cost allied credential while the founders' capital goes to a gap with a product buyer.
score.bear_case_summary: Requirement owner (NATO ACT) is building the harness itself; the only dated budget (NCIA DCS MS1, ~EUR 1.6M) buys COTS labelling from incumbents with verification bundled; five label vendors, an open-source engine, the ZTDF reference owner and three compliance consultancies already occupy the niche; the paying user's pain is annual and annoyance-level; nothing becomes proprietary; no dual use; no U.S. buyer; the end state is a services shop.
score.bull_case_summary: The standards are becoming mandatory (FMN Spiral 4/5, NSA naming ZTDF/IC-TDF in 2026, DISA data-centric MPE by 2027), NATO has begun spending on DCS labelling with more milestones implied, a German-led GmbH can reach DIANA, TIDE/CWIX Sandbox and Bundeswehr channels without SBIR/ITAR friction, and the whole thing is buildable unclassified for under USD 100k by both founders - a cheap credential and relationship-builder in the allied interoperability community, and a possible subcontract feeder into later NCIA DCS milestones if system-to-system labelling is tendered.

verdicts.bear_case: There is no budget owner for a third-party conformance linter or releasability simulator. NATO ACT owns FMN conformance and runs CWIX and the near-fielded INSPECT continuous-conformance platform for affiliates at no charge (act.nato.int 2025-06; CWIX 2026 concluded 2026-06). The one dated budget line found this session - NCIA RFQ-CO-424368-DCS 'Data Centric Security Milestone 1 - Basic Labelling' (2026-07, ~EUR 1.6M reported) - procures a COTS labelling tool for email and Office documents from an established vendor and bundles adaptation plus independent verification and validation inside that contract; it is evidence NATO buys labelling as COTS-plus-IV&V, not a linter, and the entire enterprise milestone is smaller than a seed round. Nations buy CWIX participation as contractor services (Bundeswehr 2025/2026 tender); Joint Staff J6 funds demonstrations, not products; DIANA gives EUR 100k. The paying user's pain is annual and annoyance-level. The residual demand - CWIX preparation and DCS readiness - is already met by consultancies (Thalorin, Corvus, Mility), which is what this gap would become.
verdicts.strongest_single_argument: The requirement owner for conformance is building the harness itself (INSPECT) and the only dated labelling budget (NCIA DCS MS1) buys a COTS product with verification bundled, so the PROBLEM -> USER -> REQUIREMENT OWNER chain terminates inside government and incumbent contracts with no program office, budget or vehicle for a third-party tool.
verdicts.what_would_change_my_mind: An NCIA or national MoD tender explicitly for vendor-side conformance/pre-check tooling or a releasability-derivation service open to non-BOA startups; or two allied C2 vendors signing paid pilots above EUR 100k/year each before CWIX 2027; or public evidence that INSPECT has stalled and ACT is inviting industry to supply complementary harnesses.
verdicts.narrower_survivable_version: Not a company: an open-source linter/simulator used as a credential to enter the allied interoperability community, with any revenue coming as a subcontract to a BOA-holding COTS labelling vendor on later NCIA DCS milestones.

verdicts.bear_case: Every layer of this kit is already occupied. Label syntax/binding: Isode (DCS whitepaper citing CWIX 2025 and 2026 trials), Fortra Data Classification (dedicated STANAG conformance datasheet), archTIS, Janusnet, Nexor. Open-source engine: Surevine's Spiffing with STANAG 4774 test data. ACP-240/ZTDF: Virtru/OpenTDF as the reference implementation, named by NSA's April 2026 guideline and paired with Everfox guards (2025-10-16). Coalition formats: Systematic's SitaWare self-certifies FMN Spiral 4 and controls the interface an adapter kit would target; on the U.S. side transformation is assigned to the NGC2 integrator team. Compliance tooling: Thalorin (STANAG compliance tracking, CWIX certification support, DCS maturity assessment), Corvus Intelligence (4774/4778, MIP4-IES, CoT-to-NATO guides and services), Mility. Government: NATO ACT INSPECT. A linter is a quarter's work for Isode or Fortra from libraries they already ship, and the customers (vendors) are also the competitors.
verdicts.strongest_single_argument: The customers are the competitors: the allied C2 and labelling vendors who would buy the linter already hold the label libraries and CWIX track records, an open-source engine is free, and the registry owner is fielding its own harness - there is no position from which a startup is the credible neutral party rather than a redundant one.
verdicts.what_would_change_my_mind: Evidence that the incumbent label vendors' tools fail a documented class of conformance defects at CWIX that a neutral simulator catches, plus NATO ACT publicly stating INSPECT will not cover vendor-side pre-checks or system-to-system (non-document) labelling and inviting industry to fill it.
verdicts.narrower_survivable_version: Vendor-side pre-check tooling explicitly complementary to INSPECT, delivered as a feature of a COTS labelling vendor's product (subcontract) rather than as a standalone company; or a synthetic regression corpus contributed to the community as a credential.

verdicts.bear_case: This lens cannot kill the gap and does not try to. The scope is public standards (ADatP-4774/4778/5636, OpenTDF/ZTDF, NFFI/NVG/MIP) plus synthetic data, so there is no classified dependency, no ATO, no CDS accreditation, no ITAR technical data and no clearance requirement; the PoC costs USD 40-80k and a credible allied demo USD 120-250k, inside the founders' capital; the Indonesian co-founder can lawfully work on all of it. Residual friction is real but manageable: FMN spiral profiles and CWIX test cases are partly NATO RESTRICTED and released per nation, so a German or NATO-nation sponsor is needed and the non-NATO co-founder's access is not assured; DIANA/NIF and NCIA BOA eligibility look at ownership and control and may force the German founder into majority control; German dual-use export rules for military-end-use software need counsel; the founders lack a NATO DCS/CWIX network and a domain SME, and the CWIX/TIDE cadence is annual. None of this is a barrier - which is exactly the problem: what a two-student team can build in three months from public documents is not something a buyer needs to purchase from them.
verdicts.strongest_single_argument: Everything can be built and demonstrated unclassified for well under USD 100k by both founders - and that ease is itself the evidence that the artifact has no scarcity value.
evidence: Corpus E07-F34 and G24 entry_vehicle eligibility notes on DIANA/NCIA access and NATO RESTRICTED handling (HYPOTHESIS/LOW)
verdicts.what_would_change_my_mind: Nothing on this lens changes the verdict; feasibility is not the constraint. A confirmed German-majority cap table, a named Bundeswehr Cyber Innovation Hub or ACT sponsor granting Innovation Sandbox access, and counsel clearing the co-founder's access to restricted spiral material would raise founder fit further without creating a market.
verdicts.narrower_survivable_version: Same as the other lenses: an open-source linter/simulator as a credential, fronted by the German founder for any restricted material, with any commercial work done as a subcontract to an incumbent labelling or C2 vendor.

card.title: Drone-agnostic sensor-to-map TAK plugin (MISB KLV to georegistered footprints, incremental 3D Tiles and change-vs-baseline overlays on a commodity edge box) with bandwidth-budgeted delta distribution of terrain and basemap packages across TAK federations
card.problem: Small-unit and public-safety TAK users who fly commercial drones cannot, without cloud reach-back or a vendor-specific ground station, turn any MISB-KLV video feed into a georegistered footprint, a fresh 3D Tiles model and a change-vs-baseline alert on their own map, and cannot keep terrain and basemap packages current across federated TAK Servers over bandwidth-limited links.
echelons: TAK Server administrator (unit, agency or allied)

user.exact_role: Company/battalion small-UAS operator or S2 geospatial NCO (12Y) on ATAK; incident-management-team situation unit leader or drone-as-first-responder pilot on ATAK-CIV/iTAK; TAK Server administrator managing a federation
user.echelon: Company through brigade (Army/USMC/SOF); county/state incident management team (public safety); agency TAK Server admin (DHS/CBP, allied)
organization_examples: Army brigade S2 geospatial cells and company sUAS teams flying Skydio X10D / Parrot / Anduril Ghost-class MISB-emitting drones
USSOCOM teams (Reveal Farsight was developed with USSOCOM)
CAL FIRE and California incident management teams that reviewed helicopter video in ATAK (Caldor Fire)
DHS S&T TAK program users (wildland fire, CBP, FEMA)
Allied ATAK users (UK, NATO SOF, Australia) and German civil-protection agencies (public evidence on German TAK adoption insufficient)

current_workflow: Drone streams RTSP/H.264 with a MISB 0601 KLV track to the controller; the operator opens the stream in ATAK's video tool or the free government UAS Tool plugin, which draws the drone icon, sensor point of interest (SPI) and, when four-corner metadata is present, the video footprint on the map in real time.

For a 3D product, the operator either uses the drone vendor's onboard/controller modelling (Skydio Onboard Modeling produces a textured mesh on the controller within minutes), a vendor edge app (Reveal Farsight builds 2D/3D 'in moments' and exports tiles to ATAK), or uploads imagery post-flight to a cloud (DroneDeploy, Pix4D, Skydio Cloud, WebODM) and waits hours.
Change relative to the previous flight is judged by eye, side by side, or is not done at all; enterprise change detection (Vantor/BlackSky under NGA Luno) never reaches the edge device.

Basemaps and 3D terrain (MBTiles/GeoPackage, OWT/Cesium 3D Tiles) are pre-packaged by the geospatial cell or pulled with community tools (takwerx map-depot) and sideloaded by USB or pushed as TAK mission packages; refreshes during an operation are rare.
After a link outage, TAK Server mission sync and federation re-converge CoT and mission content; large packages saturate the link or are simply not re-sent.
card.current_solution: Government-owned free software (ATAK core video tool + TPC/PAR UAS Tool plugin + MediaMTX) for KLV footprint/SPI overlay; drone-vendor onboard modelling (Skydio X10/X10D) and vendor edge apps (Reveal Farsight, Edgybees Argus for georegistration) for 3D; cloud photogrammetry (DroneDeploy, Pix4D, DJI, WebODM/OpenDroneMap) when connectivity exists; TAK Server mission sync/federation, CloudTAK package sync, community map-depot plugin and AGC Releasable Basemap Tiles for map distribution; Ditto Edge Sync for overlay sync; manual sideloading otherwise.
card.failure: The remaining unmet slice is narrow: (1) no free or government-owned tool computes change-vs-baseline overlays from drone imagery on the edge device; (2) no drone-agnostic, vendor-neutral edge service turns any KLV feed into incremental 3D Tiles that TAK displays without a Skydio or Reveal licence; (3) no fielded service prioritises and delta-distributes 3D terrain and basemap packages across TAK federations under a bandwidth budget. The first item (live KLV footprint on the map) is already solved by free government software.

card.why_existing_startups_havent_solved: Because most of it is solved, just not by startups: the live KLV-to-footprint step is a free government plugin, on-drone 3D is a stock Skydio feature, edge 3D for SOF/Army is Reveal's product, native 3D Tiles and basemap packaging are on the TPC/AGC roadmap, and package/overlay sync is TAK Server, CloudTAK and Ditto. The pieces that remain (edge change-vs-baseline overlays, bandwidth-budgeted priority delta of 3D terrain across federations) are features whose users get the surrounding stack free, so no startup can charge enough to fund them, and the natural owners (TPC, AGC, Reveal, Skydio) can add them as increments. Vendor-neutrality is a disincentive for every drone maker and an indifference for the government, which already owns the neutral layer (TAK).
card.technical_wedge: If anything: an open-source ATAK-CIV plugin plus a headless Jetson/laptop service that (a) ingests any MISB 0601 KLV stream and stores keyframes with pose, (b) runs incremental OpenDroneMap-class reconstruction to 3D Tiles that ATAK/Cesium renders, (c) computes change-vs-baseline overlays (raster diff and mesh diff against the last flight or against USGS 3DEP/OWT-class baselines) with a tunable false-alarm threshold, and (d) exposes a content-addressed chunk manifest so a companion TAK Server plugin can delta-distribute 3D terrain and basemap packages mission-area-first under a per-link bandwidth budget. Items (c) and (d) are the only parts not already free or stock.

mvp.what: ATAK-CIV plugin + Jetson Orin edge service: any KLV drone feed -> footprint (existing), incremental 3D Tiles within ~5 minutes of landing, change-vs-baseline overlay with confidence, plus a TAK Server federation plugin that delta-syncs the resulting tiles and an AGC-format basemap package over a WAN-emulated 64 kbit/s link, mission-area-first.
mvp.demonstrable_in_3_6_months: Yes on open data and commercial hardware: two commercial drones (or recorded MISB sample streams), a Jetson Orin, two federated TAK Servers built from public source, a WAN emulator; approximately $60k-150k including one contracted photogrammetry engineer.
mvp.what_it_must_prove: Measured georegistration error against RTK ground truth; time-to-3D-Tiles per hectare on a Jetson; change-detection precision/recall on a staged scene (vehicles, berms, debris); bytes- and time-to-converge for terrain packages after an outage versus native TAK mission packages; and, decisively, that a real user (wildfire IMT, SAR team, or S2 cell) will choose it over the free ATAK/UAS Tool + Skydio/Reveal status quo and that some office will pay for it.

data_requirement.what: MISB 0601 KLV video with pose (drone-vendor streams or public sample files), drone still imagery for photogrammetry, baseline terrain and imagery (USGS 3DEP, Copernicus DEM, NAIP, OpenStreetMap, Cesium World Terrain), staged change scenes; no military FMV or OWT data needed for the MVP.
data_requirement.legally_realistically_obtainable: Yes; entirely open or self-collected. Military FMV, OWT/CUI data and TAK-GOV/MIL builds are sponsor-gated and would be needed only for a defense-validated demo.

Months 3-6: five-to-ten user interviews (wildfire IMT, SAR, S2/12Y, TAK Server admins) and one TPC engineer conversation to confirm change-detection and priority delta-sync are not on the ATAK/TAK Server roadmap
Months 6-12: one paid public-safety or allied pilot; xTech entry; DHS S&T engagement
Months 12-24: SBIR D2P2 or DIU/other OT only if the ownership structure is resolved; otherwise partner or sell the team to Reveal/Skydio/a TAK integrator
entry_vehicle.eligibility_notes: SBIR/STTR requires a small business more than 50% owned and controlled by U.S. citizens or permanent residents (13 CFR 121.702; armysbir.army.mil eligibility); the Indonesian founder's equity does not count and the German founder's counts only after permanent residency, so a naive 50/50 cap table fails (needs SBIR counsel). AFWERX limits foreign-national participation on awards to public-domain/fundamental research with work performed in the U.S. (AFRL-2025-3235 FAQ). DHS and allied civil-protection contracts and open-source distribution carry no SBIR ownership test but may involve FOCI-style or export review. TAK-GOV/MIL builds are distribution-controlled and would not be available to the non-U.S.-person founder without sponsor authorization. These are constraints to scope with counsel, not legal conclusions.

incumbent_response.could_anduril_palantir_l3harris_add_it: Yes, but the relevant incumbents are smaller and closer: TPC can add change overlays and priority sync as ATAK/TAK Server releases (it already has the Cesium 3D Tiles program and AGC basemap packaging on its 2026 agenda); Reveal can add change-vs-baseline to Farsight and already exports to ATAK; Skydio can add change detection to Onboard Modeling; Ditto can extend Edge Sync to tile manifests. Each could do so in one or two release cycles (INFERENCE, MEDIUM). Anduril/Palantir do not need to respond because the government-owned free layer already occupies the vendor-neutral position.
incumbent_response.why_startup_still_wins_or_reject: Reject as a standalone company. The vendor-neutral, standards-based, free position that a startup would claim is already held by the government (TAK/UAS Tool/AGC/TPC), the drone-locked position by Skydio, and the paid defense edge-3D position by Reveal. The residual features have no requirement owner and a zero revealed price point among public-safety users. The only 'win' is speed to an open-source plugin that gets adopted and leads to an acqui-hire or a services relationship - a consultancy/acqui-hire path, not venture scale.
