score.title: Independent track-provenance and after-action audit tool for C-UAS and unit drone operations, with a friendly-flight declaration adapter (MAVLink/GCS to CoT flight-intent extension) and an offline-first UAS operator/airframe qualification and readiness ledger

scores.rationale: Fratricide/hesitation and hand-marked friendly flights are severe (Ukraine ~50% friendly losses pre-DroneID, MWI IFF recommendation), but this narrow form deliberately excludes live identification; the pain it addresses is post-hoc reconstruction (felt by oversight staff a few times per exercise) and administrative readiness tracking (annoying, not mission-critical). Moderate.

Every flight requires a friendly declaration and an operator-currency check, every CTC serial produces an AAR, and 12,080+ Gauntlet drones plus 2,500+ X10Ds make this daily at unit level. Frequent even if shallow.

Score 1 because no program element, RFI, SBIR/xTech topic or CSO call names any of the three functions; the records function is already funded as DTMS, the audit function as government test/oversight labor, and the adapter as a free TAK plugin. The only named money in the vicinity is a $500k DIU prize pool for theater-level blue-object data. Public evidence insufficient for a line.

Open on-ramps exist (ATAK-CIV plugin, xTech, JIATF-401 CSO and industry demos, OTAs with no citizenship test) but none is attached to a funded requirement for this product; access is by unit invitation and prize money.

All three pieces are commodity software (CoT schema extension, offline sync, log replay/diff, record matching); one strong engineer can build them. The only hard part is data access, which is scored elsewhere.

Adapter, ledger and a range-data audit demo cost $40-90k, well inside $250k; but a credible military demo needs sponsor logs, a US-person enclave, counsel and an exercise slot ($400-900k), so the capital buys a PoC and a pilot, not the milestone that matters.
Adapter and ledger in 8-12 weeks, range-data replay in 4-6 months; a demo on real exercise logs is 9-15 months away and depends entirely on a sponsor that does not yet exist.

MVP data is self-generated and open (MAVLink, commercial sensors, Remote ID, synthetic ACMs). The data that would make the audit credible - Lattice/FAAD C2 engagement logs and exercise ground truth - is CUI, vendor-format and sponsor-gated; real training records contain PII and live in DTMS.

Two of three pieces are EAR99-level and buildable by both founders on open-source TAK; the audit half touches export-controlled CUI that is effectively US-person-only, needs a TCP and counsel, plus TPC plugin signing and an ATO for fielded use. Medium burden, concentrated in the only valuable piece.
Yes: ATAK-CIV, PX4/ArduPilot, commercial c-UAS sensors and synthetic data support a fully unclassified start for all three functions; classification enters only with real exercise captures.

Each function already has an occupant: the free government UAS Tool and Auterion CoT feeds (adapter), DTMS plus AirData/Aloft/DroneSense and Skydio Cloud (ledger), Lattice/FAAD C2 logs, civil forensics vendors and government test teams (audit), and certified hardware IFF for friendly ID. Not a 1 only because no single vendor sells the bundle.

Incumbents are structurally unmotivated to grade their own fusion, which is the one genuine opening; but they own the logs, the export formats and the JIATF-401 relationship, and the government already sources independence from its own testers rather than from a vendor.

Every interface is controlled by someone else: CoT schema and plugin signing (TPC), C2 log exports (Anduril, Northrop), drone telemetry (Skydio, Auterion, Gauntlet vendors), training records (DTMS), ACOs (TAIS). A CIV plugin integrates trivially; anything beyond it needs cooperation the startup cannot compel.

Score 1 because nothing compounds: the data belongs to the government or the C2 vendor, the algorithms are commodity, the interfaces are owned by others, and a TAK plugin can be cloned or superseded by the TAK Product Center. Only a unit workflow and an O/C-T relationship would be proprietary, and neither transfers.

Civil C-UAS incident forensics and public-safety drone compliance are real unclassified markets, but crowded (SkySafe/D-Fend/Dedrone forensics; AirData/Aloft/DroneSense consolidating under Versaterm).
Could grow sideways into exercise data analytics or test-and-evaluation tooling, both services-shaped and small; no path to a platform.
Per-exercise audit support and per-unit ledger seats are plausible but small and services-like; a prize or pilot does not imply recurring purchase.

The engineer can build all of it on ATAK-CIV; but the team lacks the fatal-if-absent O/C-T or JICO insider and export counsel, the non-US-person co-founder is excluded from the audit data, neither founder is clearance-eligible for years, SBIR is unavailable at the current cap table, and the natural business shape (test-support services) does not fit two students seeking a venture-scale company.

market.summary: No requirement owner, program office, budget line or solicitation exists for any of the three functions (searches 2026-09-25: none found). The records function is already funded as DTMS; the friendly-flight bridge is a free government TAK plugin plus a schema the TAK Product Center owns; the audit function is funded as government test/oversight labor and FFRDC data collection (RECALL), and the customer's revealed preference at Falcon Peak 26.2 (2026-09-23) was to make the incumbent stack the measurement baseline. The natural commercial shape is a test-support/SETA services engagement or a free plugin - consultancy drift, single-digit buyers, exercise-only pain for the audit half. Analyst assessment: sustained; the chain breaks at requirement owner and budget, triggering the major penalty.

competition.summary: Every piece has an occupant: TAK UAS Tool (free, government, MAVLink-class drones into ATAK as CoT since 2021) and Auterion's CoT feed for the adapter; DTMS, Skydio Cloud and mature AirData/Aloft/DroneSense compliance tools (consolidating under Versaterm 2025-26) for the ledger; Lattice/FAAD C2 logs, civil forensics vendors (D-Fend, SkySafe) and government test organizations for the audit; certified micro-IFF hardware (Sagetech MX12B, uAvionix, ACS optical) for friendly identity. Anduril and Northrop own the export formats and can ship replay/lineage as a feature; TPC can add a flight-intent field to the UAS Tool in one release. Analyst assessment: sustained; the only defensible slice (grading the incumbent's fusion) is one the government already staffs itself.

feasibility.summary: The cheap halves (adapter, ledger: <$90k, 3 months, EAR99-level, buildable by both founders) prove nothing an investor or program office would fund; the valuable half (independent audit) depends on export-controlled CUI engagement logs in vendor formats that the non-US-person co-founder cannot handle (E07-F30/F18), that no sponsor has offered, and that the founders have no insider (O/C-T, JICO, T&E) to obtain. SBIR is closed at the current cap table; a credible demo costs $400-900k, 2-4x founder capital; fielded use needs TPC signing and an ATO under a host system. Analyst assessment: sustained; MVP is under $100k but the milestone that matters is unreachable with $250k and no sponsor.

score.verdict_rationale: All three skeptics refute at strength 4 and the corpus supports them. Evaluated on its own merits (not the parent kill), G33 fails the value-chain test at the same links as its parents: PROBLEM (real) -> USER (real: O/C-Ts, S3 air, master trainers) -> REQUIREMENT OWNER (none for the audit or the CoT extension; T2COM's answer for records is CALL 25-14 plus DTMS) -> PROGRAM OFFICE (none; TPC ships the free UAS Tool; PM UAS buys airframes) -> CONTRACTING OFFICE (unidentified) -> BUDGET (none; adjacent money funds incumbents, exercises and DTMS) -> VEHICLE (only unfunded plugins, prizes and CSO white papers). That is the major-penalty condition. Three findings make the penalty terminal rather than provisional: (1) two of the three functions duplicate free or mandated government artifacts (TAK UAS Tool since 2021; DTMS as system of record) and the third duplicates an institutional role (government testers and FFRDC data collection at events like Falcon Peak, where Lattice itself was made the measurement baseline on 2026-09-23); (2) the only piece with oversight value depends on export-controlled logs the team cannot access and the non-US-person co-founder cannot handle, so the demo that would matter is unreachable with $250k and no sponsor; (3) the bundle's natural commercial form is a services/test-support engagement or a free plugin, which the parent G09 skeptics already conceded 'may not clear the bar for venture-scale outcomes'. Market attractiveness 2.3 and founder fit 2.8 are both below a survivable threshold. Absence of a vendor selling this bundle reflects absence of a buyer. Residual uncertainty: a JIATF-401 or T2COM solicitation explicitly asking for a C2-independent provenance/after-action capability or a CoT flight-intent standard, or a CTC paying for a third-party readiness ledger, would reopen the question; none exists as of 2026-09-25 (public evidence insufficient).
score.narrower_version_if_borderline: Not applicable (verdict is kill). For the record, the only residue worth keeping is not a company: (1) a free ATAK-CIV plugin (friendly-flight declaration CoT extension + offline readiness ledger) built in 8-12 weeks for under $30k as a credibility project that earns one TiC battalion or CTC relationship and TAK.gov signing experience reusable on a different gap; (2) the replay/provenance engine as portable IP offered to a government test organization or FFRDC data-collection team as a subcontract, or to a civil C-UAS test site (DHS/FAA), explicitly sized as services revenue. Neither justifies founder capital beyond a few weeks of effort or a $2-5M raise.
score.most_important_question_answer: If two exceptionally capable founders had $250,000 today they should not build G33 as a company. The rational first build, if they insist on touching this space, is an ATAK-CIV plugin that emits a friendly-flight declaration as a CoT extension from a PX4/ArduPilot GCS, keeps an offline operator/airframe/battery/qualification ledger that syncs through TAK Server, and replays a scripted range serial from two or three commercial sensor feeds with per-source lineage - roughly $40-90k and 3-6 months, buildable by both founders without touching CUI. They would show it to a CTC airspace O/C-T cell (the authors of CALL 25-14), a Transformation-in-Contact battalion S3 air NCO and sUAS master trainer, JIATF-401 technical staff at an open industry demo, and the TAK Product Center. The demo would prove that declared flights can be matched to detected tracks with measurable precision when cooperative signals are removed, that a labelled timeline can be reconstructed after the fact, and that the ledger replaces spreadsheets offline. The customer would care only to the extent that lock-in anxiety about the $20B Lattice enterprise agreement or a fratricide near-miss has made 'government-owned, vendor-independent record' a stated need - and no office has stated it. An incumbent can crush the adapter and ledger trivially (TPC adds a field to the free UAS Tool; Anduril exposes lineage and replay; DTMS already holds the records), and the audit slice they are unmotivated to build is one the government already sources from its own test organizations and FFRDCs while making Lattice the Falcon Peak measurement baseline. The milestone that would justify $2-5M - a JIATF-401, T2COM or CTC solicitation or funded pilot that names a C2-independent provenance/after-action capability or a CoT flight-intent standard, paired with a CRADA granting exported exercise logs to a US-person enclave and an O/C-T or JICO advisor on the team - has no identified owner as of 2026-09-25, so the demo would at best yield an xTech prize, an unfunded pilot or a test-support subcontract. The founders should treat the plugin as a two-month door-opener and redirect the capital to a gap with a named requirement owner and budget line.
score.bear_case_summary: Three features, no buyer: the friendly-flight adapter duplicates the free government TAK UAS Tool and a CoT schema the TAK Product Center controls; the readiness ledger duplicates DTMS, Skydio Cloud and mature commercial compliance tools; the independent audit depends on export-controlled Lattice/FAAD C2 logs the founders cannot access and the non-US-person co-founder cannot handle, and duplicates a role the government already fills with test organizations and FFRDCs (Falcon Peak 26.2 made Lattice itself the measurement baseline). No requirement owner, program office, budget line, RFI or topic exists for any piece; hardware IFF is the funded direction for friendly identity; the natural business shape is a free plugin or a test-support services engagement; founder fit is dragged down by missing fatal-if-absent roles, SBIR ineligibility and CUI exclusion.
score.bull_case_summary: The pain is documented and growing: 12,080+ Gauntlet drones and 2,500+ X10Ds at squads, BARS hand-marking and CALL 25-14 procedural workarounds, Ukraine's ~50% friendly-fire drone losses before DroneID, MWI's friendly-UAS IFF recommendation, GAO's finding that no mechanism captures experimentation lessons, and the Army CTO's own memo that NGC2 lacked activity logging. A $20B single-vendor enterprise agreement and Lattice's 'baseline standard' role create genuine lock-in anxiety that a government-owned, vendor-neutral record answers; incumbents are structurally unmotivated to grade their own fusion; ATAK-CIV, the free UAS Tool and open MAVLink make the plumbing buildable by both founders unclassified in weeks; OTAs, CSOs and xTech carry no citizenship test; and an allied (Bundeswehr/NATO) mixed-fleet customer could value the same ledger and declaration standard. The bull case is a unit-adopted plugin that becomes the reference for a future TPC or JIATF-401 standard and earns an acquisition or a follow-on requirement - it rests on a demand signal that has not appeared.

verdicts.bear_case: There is no budget owner for any of the three functions. The Army's answer to unit sUAS records is DTMS (system of record for course completions and individual training) plus the expanding SUAS Master Trainer Course - a training pipeline, not a records product. Its answer to friendly-flight deconfliction is CALL Handbook 25-14's procedural control, written for degraded comms, plus the free TAK UAS Tool that already puts MAVLink-class drones on the picture as CoT; a flight-intent extension is a schema decision for the TAK Product Center and JIATF-401, which nobody pays a vendor for. The after-action audit is exercise-only pain felt by a handful of O/C-T and JIATF-401 staff, institutionally served by government test organizations and FFRDC data-collection teams (RECALL - not re-verified), and the customer's revealed preference on 2026-09-23 was to make Lattice itself the 'baseline standard against which all commercial assets are measured'. Searches on 2026-09-25 found no RFI, SBIR/xTech topic or CSO call for any piece. The only named adjacent money is a $500k DIU prize pool for theater-level blue-object data. The commercial shape that results is a free plugin plus a test-support services engagement - consultancy drift into a single-digit-buyer niche.
verdicts.strongest_single_argument: Every one of the three functions already has a $0 or institutional occupant that the customer chose deliberately - DTMS for records, CALL 25-14 plus the free TAK UAS Tool for friendly flights, and government testers with Lattice as the measurement baseline for after-action assessment - so there is no requirement owner, program office or budget line to attach a product to, which is the major-penalty condition.
verdicts.what_would_change_my_mind: A JIATF-401, T2COM, CTC or ATEC solicitation, CSO call or xTech/SBIR topic that explicitly asks for a C2-independent track-provenance/after-action capability or a CoT flight-intent declaration standard with funds attached; or evidence a CTC or battalion paid (not just piloted) a third party for a UAS readiness ledger; or a GAO/IG finding naming the absence of vendor-independent C-UAS engagement records as a risk with directed remediation.
verdicts.narrower_survivable_version: Not a company. Ship the friendly-flight declaration and readiness ledger as a free ATAK-CIV plugin (8-12 weeks, <$30k) purely to earn a CTC/TiC relationship and TAK.gov signing experience, and offer the replay engine as a subcontract to a government test organization or FFRDC data-collection team - explicitly services revenue, not a venture thesis.

verdicts.bear_case: The bundle is three features, each of which an incumbent or the government already owns or can add in one release. Adapter: the government-owned TAK UAS Tool has published MAVLink-class drone position, telemetry and FMV as CoT since 2021 and the TAK Product Center controls both the CoT schema and plugin signing, so a flight-intent extension is theirs to adopt in a point release; Auterion already feeds ATAK with CoT, and certified micro-IFF hardware (Sagetech MX12B AIMS-certified Mode 5, uAvionix, ACS optical ID) is the funded path for friendly identity that would reduce any software declaration to a consumer of their signal. Ledger: DTMS is the mandated system of record, Skydio Cloud syncs fleet health and battery telemetry after every mission, and AirData/Aloft/DroneSense already track pilot currency across 880+ certificate types and are consolidating into Versaterm's public-safety dispatch platform (2025-26). Audit: Anduril and Northrop own the engagement logs and export formats and can expose lineage and replay as a feature; civil detection vendors (D-Fend 'forensic readiness', SkySafe flight history with Cellebrite) already market forensics; and the government's independent measurement role is staffed by its own test organizations and FFRDCs (RECALL). Switching cost for the customer is zero because the startup would sit beside, not inside, the systems of record; APIs and formats are controlled by TPC, Anduril, Northrop, Skydio, Auterion and Gauntlet vendors.
verdicts.strongest_single_argument: The two buildable pieces compete against a free government plugin (TAK UAS Tool) and a mandated government system (DTMS), and the one piece incumbents would not build - grading their own fusion - is already performed by government testers who on 2026-09-23 made the incumbent's own Lattice the yardstick at Falcon Peak 26.2, leaving no seam a startup can own.
verdicts.what_would_change_my_mind: A JIATF-401 or Army policy statement that engagement/provenance records must be held in a government-owned store independent of the C2 vendor with a solicitation to build it; evidence that Lattice/FAAD C2 export formats are open and that TPC has declined to add flight-intent to the UAS Tool by policy; or a documented case of a unit or CTC paying a third party for readiness-ledger or after-action tooling rather than using DTMS and vendor replay.
verdicts.narrower_survivable_version: Only a partner role: build the replay/provenance engine as a component licensed to, or subcontracted under, a government test organization, an FFRDC data-collection team or a C-UAS integrator that needs vendor-neutral scoring at exercises, and contribute the flight-intent CoT extension to the TAK community as an open proposal rather than a product. Services-shaped and small.

verdicts.bear_case: The parts this team can build cheaply are exactly the parts nobody will pay for, and the part someone might value is the part they cannot build credibly. Adapter and ledger: ATAK-CIV is open source, MAVLink tooling is EAR99-level and synthetic data suffices, so both founders can ship them in 8-12 weeks for under $30k - but that demo proves plumbing, not value, and the government already ships the plumbing free. Audit: its credibility rests on real Lattice/FAAD C2 engagement logs and exercise ground truth, which are CUI at minimum, vendor-formatted and sponsor-gated; export-controlled CUI is effectively US-person-only (E07-F30) and ITAR technical data has no deemed-export exception for domestic foreign-person employees (E07-F18), so the Indonesian co-founder is excluded from the half that matters, a technology control plan and counsel are prerequisites, and neither founder is clearance-eligible for years. No sponsor, CRADA or exercise slot exists; the team lacks the fatal-if-absent O/C-T/JICO insider who would define an acceptable reconstruction; SBIR is unavailable at the current cap table (E07-F3); fielded use requires TPC plugin signing and an ATO under a host system. A credible demo on sponsor data costs $400-900k (2-4x capital) and is 9-15 months away conditional on a sponsor that has not appeared; production is a bespoke integration per unit/CTC. Timeline to any recurring revenue is 3-5 years and services-shaped.
verdicts.strongest_single_argument: The only component with oversight value - the independent after-action audit - can be demonstrated credibly only on export-controlled C-UAS engagement logs that no sponsor has offered, that the non-US-person co-founder cannot legally handle without licensing, and that the founders have no insider to obtain, so $250k buys a plugin the government already gives away and a replay engine tested only on the founders' own range data.
evidence: E07-F30 CUI access by foreign nationals limited by export controls; E07-F18 no ITAR deemed-export exception; E07-F3 SBIR ownership test (eCFR 13 CFR 121.702)
https://www.cnbc.com/2025/10/03/anduril-palantir-army-memo-ngc2.html (audit/logging gap is being fixed inside the incumbent-led data layer)
verdicts.what_would_change_my_mind: A signed CRADA or OTA giving the team exported, unclassified-releasable exercise track/engagement logs with ground truth and a named O/C-T or JIATF-401 sponsor; a US-person engineering enclave and export counsel already in place; an unclassified multi-sensor C-UAS dataset with ground truth public enough to validate the audit engine without a sponsor; or confirmation that the 2026 SBIR reauthorization relaxed foreign-founder constraints enough for the current cap table (E07-F2, unverified).
verdicts.narrower_survivable_version: Keep only the unclassified plugin (friendly-flight declaration CoT extension + offline readiness ledger) as a credibility project and point the replay engine at civil C-UAS test sites (DHS/FAA) or ranges where sensor data is unclassified - accepting that this is a small, crowded, services-adjacent market and not a basis for raising $2-5M.

card.title: Offline-first, EAR99-by-design structured orders, tasks, reports and LOGSTAT object layer with CRDT merge for TAK-CIV, sold first to public-safety incident command, National Guard and allied light units, with the merge model licensable to HQ planning and C2 platform owners
card.problem: Incident commanders, National Guard battalion staffs and allied light units that already run TAK on unclassified networks still move orders, assignments, status reports and sustainment/resource status as paper ICS forms, chat, voice and spreadsheets that do not merge cleanly when nodes reconnect after working disconnected, so the picture diverges between the command post, field elements and higher headquarters.

user.exact_role: Incident commander / planning section chief / resource unit leader on an all-hazards or wildland incident management team; National Guard battalion S3/S4 and battle captain on state active duty or Title 32 domestic missions; allied light-infantry company/battalion staff on ATAK
user.echelon: Incident (Type 1-4) and battalion/company
organization_examples: State wildland fire agencies and interagency IMTs using WFTAK (Colorado CoE, FAM IM Tools)
Municipal fire departments using TAK with FirstNet (e.g., Green Bay Metro Fire, 2025)
Army/Air National Guard elements on domestic response (147th ASOS Hurricane Harvey use of ATAK; 2025 wildfire response)
Bundeswehr light units via Cyber Innovation Hub pilots; NATO DIANA 2027 'operational resilience' challenge cohort

current_workflow: Incident: IC fills ICS 201 briefing and ICS 202/204/209 on paper or Word/PDF templates; assignments are read out at briefings; resources tracked on T-cards/whiteboards or an IMS web app that needs connectivity; TAK shows PLI and markers only
Field elements report status by radio/phone/chat; planning section re-keys into forms each operational period; disconnected divisions bring paper back to the ICP

Guard battalion: receives WARNORD/OPORD as PDF/PowerPoint over intermittent links; tracks tasks, SITREP/LOGSTAT/PERSTAT on spreadsheets and chat; ATAK data packages carry graphics; on reconnect, reports are re-typed into higher's format
Allied light unit: SitaWare Edge/Frontline where fielded, otherwise ATAK plus voice; orders as documents
After each displacement/reconnect, staff manually reconcile which version of the assignment or report is current
card.current_solution: Paper NIMS ICS forms (FEMA ICS forms booklet); TAK Server 'Data Sync' missions (government, free) that re-sync map items, files, logs and chat missed while disconnected but carry no structured order/report/LOGSTAT objects and no CRDT merge; commercial incident-management software (Tablet Command, Resgrid IC with offline-first ICS-201 timeline, Intterra, Juvare WebEOC, Veoci and the 10+ products in the DHS SAVER 2022 market survey); Ditto's Edge Sync plugin for ATAK (company claim) for peer-to-peer CRDT sync of ATAK objects; on the military side Onebrief (offline tactical access 'underway', company statement), SBMC clients (Anduril/Rivet, ATAK-backward-compatible), Systematic SitaWare Edge tasking; Meshtastic/goTenna mesh transports for TAK.
card.failure: Structured content has no object model in TAK: it travels as files, chat and data packages, so two nodes that edited the same assignment or report while partitioned cannot merge and someone re-keys by hand; commercial IMS tools are cloud-first (Resgrid excepted, queue-and-replay not multi-writer merge) and not TAK-native; ~80% of wildland responders carry iOS devices where iTAK accepts no third-party plugins, so an ATAK-CIV plugin alone cannot reach them; the Guard has no program office or budget line for a battalion orders/reports app and the allied path is small pilots.

card.why_existing_startups_havent_solved: Three structural reasons, none of which a new entrant changes. (1) The layer is split across owners who each solve their own slice: the TAK Product Center ships free Data Sync missions for map items/files/chat; Ditto sells the CRDT sync engine for ATAK; public-safety IMS vendors (Tablet Command, Resgrid, Intterra, WebEOC, Veoci) own the ICS forms workflow in web/iOS apps; Onebrief/Anduril/Rivet/Systematic own the military orders layer. Nobody has combined 'structured order/report objects + multi-writer merge + TAK-native' because each owner's customers are satisfied enough by their slice. (2) The public-safety buyer base is thousands of agencies with GPC/grant-sized software budgets, iOS-majority devices (iTAK has no plugin architecture), and adoption barriers that are training and community rather than features (TAK Public Safety 501(c)(3) exists for exactly this). (3) The 'license the merge model' thesis fails on commoditization: CRDT engines are open source (Automerge, Yjs) or already sold (Ditto), and the domain schemas (NIMS ICS forms, FM 6-0/FM 4-0 report formats) are public standards, so the only proprietary asset would be integration work, which is services.
card.technical_wedge: A TAK-Server-side 'structured objects' service (extending the documented mission/Data Sync API) plus an ATAK-CIV plugin and an iOS/web companion app, that represents ICS 201/204/209/214 (public safety) and WARNORD/FRAGO tasks, SITREP/LOGSTAT/PERSTAT (Guard/allied) as versioned JSON objects with a CRDT merge model tuned to forms (per-field last-writer-wins with causal history, list merges for assignments/resources, explicit conflict surfacing for quantities), transported as compact CoT/mission deltas over Meshtastic/goTenna/FirstNet, so that field elements that edit while disconnected reconcile automatically on reconnect without re-keying.

mvp.what: Open-source TAK Server extension + ATAK-CIV plugin + iOS/web companion implementing ICS 204/209/214 and a LOGSTAT/SITREP object with CRDT merge, running on commercial Android/iOS devices and Meshtastic radios
mvp.demonstrable_in_3_6_months: Yes: five EUDs plus a laptop ICP/TOC with deliberate partitions and a command-post jump; measure convergence time, bytes per object, zero manual re-keying; demo at a state wildland exercise or a Guard battalion drill weekend (no program office needed)
mvp.what_it_must_prove: That multi-writer edits to assignments, resource status and LOGSTAT quantities made during a 6-hour partition merge with no duplicates or lost updates, on iOS as well as Android, and that a planning section produces the next operational period's ICS 204s faster than with paper/Word; and that at least one agency will pay for it rather than use free TAK Data Sync plus its existing IMS

incumbent_response.could_anduril_palantir_l3harris_add_it: Yes. dual_use_potential.explanation: The product is dual-use by construction: NIMS ICS forms for public safety and doctrinal orders/reports for Guard/allied units share the same object-and-merge core; TAK itself is used by both communities. The catch is that dual-use here means two small, fragmented markets rather than one large commercial one.

defensibility.explanation: Weak. CRDT merge is commoditized (Automerge/Yjs/Ditto); schemas are public standards; TAK is government-owned and free; switching cost for an agency is low. Only an installed base across many agencies and IMTs, plus becoming the de facto TAK ICS-object schema, would create modest lock-in - and that is a community/standards outcome, not a proprietary one.

card.why_now: Public-safety TAK adoption has crossed from pilots to routine use (DHS S&T iTAK release, WFTAK interagency server, TAK Public Safety nonprofit founded 2024, FirstNet-paired municipal use 2025); cheap LoRa mesh (Meshtastic ATAK forwarder; Feb 2026 iOS built-in TAK server) makes disconnected multi-node operation common outside the military; CRDT libraries are production-grade; and the Army's own 2025-2026 DDIL focus (Ivy Sting 4, SBMC ATAK compatibility) has normalized the idea of structured content over tactical links. Against this, the same period saw Ditto, Resgrid and TPC Data Sync ship the adjacent pieces, so the window is for a niche product, not a category.
card.killer_risk: The venture thesis rests on licensing a merge model that is already commoditized (open-source CRDTs; Ditto's funded ATAK sync plugin) into markets that are either fragmented and grant-sized (thousands of public-safety agencies, iOS-majority devices that reject plugins, adoption gated by training) or unfunded at this layer (Guard has no program office or line; allied entry is EUR 100k DIANA grants and CIHBw pilots) - so even success is a small SaaS/open-source-plus-services business or an acquihire, not a venture-scale company, and TPC or an IMS vendor can add structured offline forms in one release.

score.title: Offline-first, EAR99-by-design structured orders, tasks, reports and LOGSTAT object layer with CRDT merge for TAK-CIV, sold first to public-safety incident command, National Guard and allied light units, with the merge model licensable to HQ planning and C2 platform owners

scores.rationale: Real but tolerated: paper ICS forms and spreadsheets work well enough that agencies keep using them; the acute failure (divergent pictures after partition) is episodic. Military-side pain is documented (Ivy Sting 4, LG-DA 2025) but that buyer is not this gap's first customer.
Every incident operational period and every Guard/allied order cycle regenerates forms and reports; disconnected multi-writer conflicts are less frequent than the form-filling itself.

HSGP $1.008B FY25 (FACT) and AFG exist but are fragmented across thousands of agencies and not evidenced for this product class; Guard has no line (Public evidence insufficient); licensing buyers unproven; DIANA EUR 100k.

Public-safety direct sales need no SBIR or ATO, which fits this cap table, but SLED buying runs on references, grant cycles and cooperative contracts with 12-24 month cycles; Guard and allied paths are pilots without a program office.
CRDT libraries, ATAK-CIV SDK and a documented mission API make it buildable; iTAK's no-plugin architecture forces a companion-app/server-side design and doubles mobile work.
PoC $80k-$150k on commercial devices and synthetic data; $250k covers PoC plus one or two exercises but not a sales function.
3-5 months to a partition-and-merge demo on five devices; a credible demo to a buyer (live exercise) adds a season.
ICS forms, doctrinal report formats and TAK schemas are public; only real Guard LOGSTAT data needs a sponsor and is not required for the first product.

Civil, open-source, plausibly EAR99 product with no clearance/ATO for public safety; not 5 because Guard/allied variants bring TAK-GOV gating, possible defense-service and CUI questions that need counsel.

Entirely unclassified by design: public-safety users, ATAK-CIV/TAK Server open builds, public schemas, commercial mesh; no CUI or classified dependency at any stage of the first product - the one criterion where this gap is unambiguously strong.

Every slice is occupied: TPC's free Data Sync (disconnect re-sync), Ditto's funded CRDT ATAK plugin (merge engine), Resgrid/Tablet Command/Intterra/WebEOC/Veoci (ICS forms, Resgrid offline-first), Onebrief/Anduril-Rivet/Systematic (military orders), plus open-source CRDTs; the DHS SAVER 2022 survey shows a mature multi-vendor IMS category.

TPC can add form objects to missions, Ditto can ship a schema pack, IMS vendors can add multi-writer merge; none is locked into an architecture that prevents it. Slight vulnerability only because none currently combines all three and public-safety vendors are slow.

ATAK-CIV plugin SDK and TAK Server mission API are open and documented; iTAK is closed to plugins, TAK-GOV/MIL gated, and every military HQ platform API (Onebrief, Lattice, SitaWare) is incumbent-controlled.

CRDT merge is commoditized (Automerge, Yjs, Ditto), the schemas are public NIMS/FM standards, TAK is free government software and switching cost for an agency is near zero; the only conceivable moat (de facto community schema plus installed base) is a standards/community outcome, not proprietary.
Genuinely dual-use core (ICS forms and military orders/LOGSTAT share the object-and-merge engine) and both communities already use TAK; not 5 because both markets are small and fragmented.

Expansion from public safety into the Guard/Army layer runs into the same incumbents that killed G18/G06; the 'license the merge model' expansion is refuted by commoditization; adjacent IMS features would just make it another IMS vendor.
Per-agency SaaS subscriptions renew annually and grant cycles recur, but ACVs are small (low five figures) and churn to free TAK Data Sync or an incumbent IMS is easy.

Better than the parents: no SBIR, no CUI, non-U.S.-person founder unconstrained on an EAR99/open-source civil product, engineer can build the core. Still 2 because the team lacks the fatal-if-absent incident-command/fire-service domain founder and any SLED sales experience, and the founders' stated goal is the U.S. defense market, which this gap abandons.

market.summary: No budget owner: public-safety money is HSGP/AFG/local budgets spread over thousands of agencies with no evidence of purchases in this product class; the Guard has no program office or line for a battalion orders/reports app (Public evidence insufficient); allied entry is EUR 100k DIANA grants (2027 window closed 2026-07-03) and CIHBw pilots; the 'license the merge model' revenue line has no evidenced buyer and competes with open-source CRDTs and Ditto. TAK Public Safety's own charter says adoption is gated by training, not features. Even a successful outcome is a low-ACV niche SaaS or acquihire - consultancy/feature drift is the base case.

competition.summary: Each component already has an owner: TPC's free Data Sync re-syncs missions after disconnect and TPC could add form objects; Ditto (~$136M) sells CRDT sync for ATAK and claims USSOCOM use; Resgrid IC already markets offline-first ICS-201 and Tablet Command/Intterra/WebEOC/Veoci own agency IMS relationships (DHS SAVER 2022); Onebrief/Anduril-Rivet/Systematic hold the military orders layer. Open-source CRDT libraries and the FreeTAKTeam/Meshtastic community can replicate the rest. Switching cost is near zero and the interfaces that matter (iTAK, TAK-GOV, Onebrief/Lattice/SitaWare APIs) are controlled by others.

feasibility.summary: Not refuted: the product is unclassified, buildable for under $150k on commercial devices with public schemas, needs no ATO/CUI/SBIR for its first customers, and the non-U.S.-person founder can work on an EAR99/open-source civil codebase (counsel still required). Residual weaknesses are iTAK's closed plugin model (doubles mobile work), the missing fatal-if-absent incident-command domain founder and SLED sales capability, and classification/defense-service drift if the Guard or allied variants add military-specific integration.

score.verdict_rationale: KILL as a venture, with an explicit note that it is a legitimate bootstrapped/open-source niche business. Applying the same standard as the parent red teams: the buyer chain exists only in its civil half (PROBLEM -> incident commander -> agency chief -> no program office -> municipal/state procurement -> HSGP/local budget -> direct SaaS sale) and is fragmented across thousands of small buyers with no evidence of purchases in this product class; the Guard half has no requirement owner, program office, budget or vehicle (Public evidence insufficient), which draws the major chain penalty for that segment; the allied half is EUR 100k grants with the 2027 DIANA window already closed. Market attractiveness is 2.7, dragged by competitive intensity (1) and moat (1): TPC's free Data Sync, Ditto's funded CRDT ATAK plugin, Resgrid's offline-first ICS-201 and the mature IMS category (DHS SAVER 2022) occupy every slice, and the 'licensable merge model' - the one piece of the thesis that could have been venture-scale - is refuted by open-source CRDTs and Ditto's existing product. Founder fit is the highest of the family at 3.8 because everything is unclassified, cheap, EAR99-plausible and needs no SBIR, so the feasibility skeptic could not refute it; but strong feasibility of a small business does not make a venture, and the founders' stated primary interest (U.S. defense) is abandoned by this form. Confidence MEDIUM: a signed multi-agency state contract, a TPC statement declining to add form objects, or evidence that Ditto/IMS vendors will not cover offline multi-writer forms would raise it to borderline.
score.narrower_version_if_borderline: Not borderline. For the record, the only form worth keeping alive is as a non-venture: an open-source 'ICS objects for TAK' schema and TAK Server extension (ICS 201/204/209/214 as CRDT-merged mission objects, iOS/Android/web companion) stewarded with TAK Public Safety and WFTAK, monetized through hosting/support to state wildland agencies and IMTs - a lifestyle/open-source business or a path to an acquihire by Ditto, a TPC contractor or an IMS vendor, with the Guard/allied and merge-model-licensing lines dropped.
score.most_important_question_answer: If two exceptionally capable founders had $250,000 today and insisted on G34, the first build is a TAK Server extension plus ATAK-CIV plugin plus a thin iOS/web companion that stores ICS 204 assignments, ICS 209/214 status and a LOGSTAT-style resource ledger as CRDT-merged mission objects, transported as compact deltas over Meshtastic/goTenna/FirstNet - about $100k and four months, entirely unclassified and buildable by the non-U.S.-person founder. They would show it to a state wildland fire technology lead running WFTAK, a Type 2 IMT planning section chief, the TAK Public Safety community and one Guard battalion S3 on a drill weekend; the demo proves that six hours of disconnected multi-writer edits to assignments and quantities merge with zero re-keying on both Android and iOS, and that the next operational period's ICS 204s are produced faster than on paper. The customer cares because forms are re-keyed every period and pictures diverge after every displacement. But an incumbent can crush it: TPC can add form objects to its free Data Sync missions, Ditto already sells CRDT sync for ATAK, Resgrid already markets offline-first ICS-201, and Tablet Command/Intterra own the agency relationships; the schema is a public standard and the merge engine is open source, so nothing becomes proprietary. The milestone that would justify $2-5M - twenty-plus paying agencies or a state-level enterprise contract plus a signed licensing/integration LOI from TPC, Onebrief, Ditto or Systematic - is unlikely to be reached because the licensing buyer has no reason to pay for what it can take from open source, and the agency ACVs are too small to fund a sales team. That is why it fails as a venture while remaining a reasonable open-source niche business or acquihire path.
score.bear_case_summary: Fragmented grant-sized public-safety budgets with no evidence of purchases in this class; no Guard program office, requirement or line; allied channel limited to EUR 100k DIANA grants (2027 window closed) and CIHBw pilots; every technical slice already occupied (TPC Data Sync, Ditto CRDT ATAK plugin, Resgrid offline ICS-201, mature IMS vendors, Onebrief/Anduril/Systematic on the military side); iTAK blocks plugins for the iOS-majority wildland users; CRDT and schemas are commodities so no moat; the licensing thesis has no evidenced buyer; team lacks a fire-service/incident-command founder and SLED sales; realistic upside is an acquihire.
score.bull_case_summary: Public-safety TAK use is real and growing (DHS S&T, WFTAK, TAK Public Safety 2024, FirstNet-paired municipal use 2025), cheap mesh has made disconnected multi-node operation routine, the product is unclassified, EAR99-plausible, buildable for ~$100k with no SBIR/ATO/CUI, the non-U.S.-person founder is unconstrained, NATO DIANA's 2027 challenges name almost exactly this problem, no one has yet combined structured ICS/orders objects with multi-writer merge inside TAK, and an installed base plus a de facto TAK ICS-object schema could make the team an attractive acquihire for Ditto, a TPC contractor, Onebrief or an IMS vendor.

verdicts.bear_case: There is no budget owner for this product in any of its three target segments. Public safety: FY25 HSGP is $1.008B (FACT) but it is sub-granted to states and thousands of agencies, no purchase of TAK-native structured-forms or offline-IMS software under it was found, agencies already buy from a mature IMS category (DHS SAVER 2022), and TAK Public Safety's own charter says the adoption barrier is training and community, not features. National Guard: no requirement owner, program office, line or vehicle for a battalion orders/reports app (Public evidence insufficient) - the same chain break that killed G18. Allied: DIANA's 2027 challenges fit but closed 2026-07-03 with EUR 100k awards; CIHBw pilots are small. The 'merge model licensable to HQ platform owners' line has no evidenced buyer and competes with free Automerge/Yjs and Ditto. Even success is low-five-figure ACVs across dozens of agencies - a consultancy/open-source-services or acquihire outcome.
verdicts.strongest_single_argument: The only venture-scale element of G34 - licensing the merge model to Onebrief/Anduril/TPC/Systematic - has no evidenced buyer and is commoditized by open-source CRDTs and Ditto's existing ATAK sync product, leaving a fragmented, grant-funded public-safety niche whose own advocacy nonprofit says the binding constraint is training, not missing features.
evidence: Parent G18-score: no Guard/Army program office or line at this layer
E04-F25: M&A is the dominant graduation for TAK-adjacent software firms
verdicts.what_would_change_my_mind: A state-level or multi-agency enterprise contract (or FEMA/USFA program) explicitly funding offline structured ICS forms on TAK; an NGB or state JFHQ solicitation for a battalion-and-below orders/reports app; or a signed paid licensing/integration agreement from TPC, Onebrief, Ditto or Systematic for a third-party merge model.
verdicts.narrower_survivable_version: An open-source 'ICS objects for TAK' schema and server extension stewarded with TAK Public Safety/WFTAK, monetized via hosting and support to state wildland agencies and IMTs - a bootstrapped business, not a venture.

verdicts.bear_case: Every layer of the proposed stack already has an owner who can close the remaining seam in one release. Disconnect re-sync: TPC's free Data Sync plugin re-syncs mission map items, files, logs and chat after a device reconnects and TPC could add form objects. Merge engine: Ditto (~$136M raised, $82M Series B 2025-03) sells a CRDT edge-sync platform with an ATAK plugin it says USSOCOM uses; Automerge/Yjs/RxDB/PowerSync are open source. Forms workflow: Resgrid IC already markets offline-first ICS-201 with local queue and replay; Tablet Command, Intterra, WebEOC and Veoci own agency relationships. Military orders: Onebrief (enterprise IDIQ, offline 'underway'), Anduril/Rivet SBMC (ATAK-backward-compatible) and Systematic SitaWare Edge. The interfaces that matter are controlled by others - Apple blocks iTAK plugins (80% of wildland devices), TAK-GOV/MIL is gated, HQ platform APIs are closed. Switching cost for an agency is near zero and the schemas are public NIMS/FM standards, so no moat forms.
verdicts.strongest_single_argument: The CRDT-merge-for-TAK layer that G34 treats as its proprietary core is already a shipped, funded product (Ditto's Edge Sync plugin for ATAK) and an open-source commodity, while the free government Data Sync plugin already handles disconnect re-sync - leaving only public-standard forms as the startup's contribution, which any IMS vendor or TPC can add.
evidence: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.atakmap.android.datasync.plugin (TPC Data Sync: mission re-sync after disconnect)
Corpus B03 Ditto record: Edge Sync plugin for ATAK, ~$136M funding (company claims on usage)
verdicts.what_would_change_my_mind: A TPC statement that structured form/order objects are out of scope for Data Sync; independent evidence that Ditto's ATAK plugin is not used or not extensible to forms; or 12 months of the IMS vendors failing to ship multi-writer offline merge while agencies publicly ask for it.
verdicts.narrower_survivable_version: Position as the schema/community layer on top of Ditto or TAK Data Sync rather than a competing merge engine: an open ICS-object standard plus iOS/web companion, built to be adopted (or acquired) by Ditto, a TPC contractor or an IMS vendor.

verdicts.bear_case: Feasibility is the gap's strength and cannot be refuted: unclassified by design, public schemas, open-source ATAK-CIV and documented mission API, mature CRDT libraries, PoC under $150k on commercial devices, no SBIR (so the >50% U.S.-person ownership test, 13 CFR 121.702, does not bind), no ATO or CUI for public-safety pilots, and the Indonesian founder can work on an EAR99/open-source civil codebase (E07-F17, E07-F25) - counsel should confirm EAR99 status but no legal judgment is made. The residual concerns are real but not fatal: iTAK accepts no plugins, so reaching the iOS-majority wildland users requires a companion app or server-side design that doubles mobile engineering; the team lacks a fire-service/incident-command domain founder (fatal if absent) and any SLED sales capability; a Guard or allied variant reintroduces TAK-GOV gating, possible CUI/CMMC and ITAR defense-service questions (E07-F15); and DHS S&T SBIR, if ever used, brings the ownership test back.
verdicts.strongest_single_argument: The team can legally and cheaply build and demonstrate this, but a two-student team with no incident-command or fire-service founder and no agency references cannot sell it: public-safety adoption is gated by training, references and grant cycles (TAK Public Safety's stated reason for existing), and the iOS-majority user base cannot be reached by the ATAK-CIV plugin the thesis names.
verdicts.what_would_change_my_mind: Nothing needed on feasibility; what would raise the overall verdict is a committed incident-command/fire-service co-founder or advisor with agency references, plus a first paying state agency or IMT pilot.
verdicts.narrower_survivable_version: Public-safety-only, iOS-and-Android companion plus TAK Server extension (no Guard/allied variant in the first 18 months, no military-specific integration) to keep the codebase unambiguously civil/EAR99 and avoid every defense-side access constraint.

card.title: Autonomy and PNT conformance and test-and-evaluation tooling: machine-to-machine conformance suites for MAVLink/STANAG 4586/UMAA/FANTOM-style interfaces, DDIL scenario replay, and an ASPN synthetic-measurement generator with pntOS plug-in conformance checks scored against the DHS Resilient PNT framework
card.problem: Vendors that must plug into government autonomy and PNT reference interfaces, and the lab staff who assess them, prove conformance and degraded-environment behavior only at capacity-limited government events and live tests, because no affordable, vendor-neutral software harness exists for the open subset of those interfaces.

user.exact_role: Integration and test engineer at a small autonomy or alternative-PNT vendor preparing for a government assessment event, SBIR Phase I/II deliverable or milestone NAVWAR-compliance review; secondarily a government lab T&E engineer (SOFWERX/PEO-SDA UxSAI, C5ISR Center PNT, PMS 406) who runs vendor software through scenario sets
user.echelon: Vendor engineering / program-office T&E
organization_examples: Drone Dominance and Blue UAS Framework component vendors (MAVLink/PX4-based)
USV/UUV autonomy vendors implementing UMAA services
Alt-PNT sensor vendors (DIU TQS cohort, MagNav, vision-nav, LEO-PNT) writing pntOS plug-ins
SOFWERX / PEO-SDA UxSAI assessment staff
Army C5ISR Center PNT and PM PNT test engineers
Civil timing operators (telecom, utilities) buying under CISA federal PNT acquisition guidance

current_workflow: 1. Vendor obtains the interface specification: MAVLink and PX4 (public), UMAA ICDs (AUVSI, registration), ASPN-ICD YAML and pntOS-C API (public GitHub), STANAG 4586 (NATO-controlled document, obtained via program or national standards office), FANTOM Core M2M API (government-controlled, program access only).
2. Vendor writes the adapter or plug-in and tests it against ad hoc scripts, a vendor HIL rig, or (for PNT) an RF simulator (Spirent, Safran Skydel) if it can afford one.
3. Vendor waits for a government slot: SOFWERX assessment event, PNTAX/APEX, CCA/A-GRA phase, PMS 406 lab, or SBIR Phase I demonstration.
4. Government staff run the vendor's software through their own scenario sets and government M&S (MDQDA, GIANT/CIGNM, program simulators) and report defects late.
5. For PNT-using programs, the milestone decision authority demands NAVWAR-compliance evidence (DoDI 4650.08); the evidence table is assembled manually per program.
6. Repeat per software drop, per program and per interface family.
card.current_solution: Government-furnished compliance test tools for Army UAS/IOP and STANAG 4586 (Army states such tools are available to programs and eligible vendors); MITRE UMAA reference implementation (RECALL - not re-verified this session); vendor-specific HIL rigs; Spirent PNT X/PNT Xe and Safran Skydel (RF-level GNSS scenario simulators with Python automation) for PNT; Applied Intuition's simulation and validation tooling and the CDAO 'Autonomy Factory' for enterprise autonomy validation; government-run assessment events (SOFWERX UxSAI Mission Autonomy Systems AE and Synthetic Data Modeler AE, 2026); annual PNTAX; for civil PNT, vendor self-attestation against the DHS Resilient PNT Conformance Framework v2.0 with no certification body.
card.failure: Conformance and degraded-mode behavior are validated only at the government's cadence and inside its tooling, so vendors discover integration failures late and cannot reproduce them; alt-PNT M&S fidelity is 'poorer' than GNSS models and engagement-level trade tools 'do not yet exist' (GAO-21-320SP); civil resilience-level claims are self-declared and single-number resilience scores have been shown to be decision-unstable under framework-aligned weighting (arXiv 2607.05415, July 2026) - so there is no trusted independent yardstick. But the failure is one of capacity and cadence, not absence of tooling: the government and its consortia already own or plan the tools for each interface family.

evidence.claim: Army planned a compliance toolkit to auto-verify pntOS plug-ins; alt-PNT M&S fidelity is 'poorer' than GNSS models; the ability to model multiple integrated technologies 'does not yet exist'; SOF are 'reluctant to accept modeling and simulation results'; field tests require shutting down civil airspace; DoD MOSA-PNT initiative funded at $17M FY2020-2024.
evidence.source_title: GAO-21-320SP, Defense Navigation Capabilities: DOD is Developing Positioning, Navigation, and Timing Technologies to Complement GPS
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: NAVWAR compliance must be determined and reported at each acquisition milestone with T&E plans sufficient to validate it - structural, recurring demand for compliance evidence.
evidence.source_title: DoDI 4650.08 Positioning, Navigation, and Timing (PNT) and Navigation Warfare (NAVWAR), Change 1
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: Navy NAVWAR open topic NP004 accepts synthetic ASPN/pntOS data for Phase I and states 'innovation required on the ingestion of disparate types' - the one concrete government acceptance of synthetic ASPN streams as SBIR-grade input (topic closed 2026-09-23).
evidence.source_title: Navy SBIR 26.5 DON26BX05-NP004 topic and Q&A
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: SOFWERX with PEO-SDA ran a UxSAI Synthetic Data Modeler Assessment Event (milestones June-October 2026) to select synthetic-data generation for EO/IR computer-vision model development, and a separate UxSAI Mission Autonomy Systems Assessment Event (whitepapers, downselect, government-run T&E). The synthetic-data buy is CV imagery, not interface conformance or scenario replay; T&E is performed by the government.
evidence.source_title: sam.gov: UxSAI Synthetic Data Modeler Assessment Event (AE); Soldier Systems Daily: SOFWERX UxSAI Mission Autonomy Systems Assessment Event; DefenseScoop: SOCOM planning to test new mission autonomy software
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: Army UAS interoperability program states that 'many software test tools are available to programs and eligible vendors to help demonstrate compliance with applicable standards, and these test tools continue to evolve to further automate compliance testing' (STANAG 4586-based IOP messages) - the STANAG 4586/IOP conformance slot is served by government-furnished tooling.
evidence.source_title: U.S. Army UAS Interoperability (army.mil article 293795)
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: ISTO announced the PNT Standards Consortium, founded by Leidos, IS4S and TRX Systems, to govern pntOS and ASPN through an open consensus process - the natural home for an official (free) conformance suite; IS4S markets pntOS commercially.

evidence.claim: RF-level PNT scenario incumbents keep moving down-market and toward automation: Spirent (now Keysight) launched PNT Xe to extend GNSS simulation 'to more users across the development lifecycle' (Nov 2025); Safran launched Skydel AI, which configures scenarios via natural language by generating Python code (ION GNSS+ Sept 2025). Neither result mentions ASPN message output - public evidence insufficient on ASPN support.
evidence.source_title: Spirent press release; Safran Navigation & Timing: Skydel AI
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: DHS Resilient PNT Conformance Framework v2.0 defines resilience Levels 0-4 with Prevent/Respond/Recover behaviors; CISA's Federal PNT Services Acquisitions guidance (March 2024) directs federal buyers to specify resilience expectations; the results show vendors (Oscilloquartz/ADVA, VIAVI) self-declare conformance and no certification or accredited test body appears - so demand for independent scoring is latent, not funded.

evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: A July 2026 arXiv study finds single-number PNT resilience ratings are decision-unstable under framework-aligned weighting - i.e., the 'score against the DHS framework' output this gap proposes is scientifically contested as a ranking instrument.
evidence.source_title: How Stable Is a PNT Resilience Score? Decision-Instability of Single-Number Resilience Ratings under Framework-Aligned Weighting (arXiv 2607.05415)
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: DIU established third-party 'Recognized Assessors' (as of Sept 2025) to perform standardized assessments of drone platforms and components against the Blue UAS standard (NDAA/cybersecurity), delivering reports to DIU for a certification decision - DoD does outsource compliance assessment to third parties, but for supply-chain/cyber compliance, not interface conformance, and to accredited organizations.
evidence.source_title: DIU: seeking recognized assessors to support Blue UAS NDAA compliance; Mobilicom Blue UAS Framework overview
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: SOCOM requires vendors to integrate flight controllers with government-owned FANTOM Core via M2M API and/or BMS - the FANTOM-style interface is government-controlled and reachable only inside a program.
evidence.source_title: sam.gov: USSOCOM Air Loitering Munition notice
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: CDAO selected Applied Intuition to underpin a DoD-wide 'Autonomy Factory' shared environment to develop, validate and certify autonomous systems (announced 2026-05-14; CDAO production contract ceiling up to $171.1M over three years reported 2025-01-14; ceiling is not obligations, production status unverified). Public evidence insufficient on whether it covers PNT/pntOS conformance.
evidence.source_title: Applied Intuition press release via PRNewswire; InsideDefense (from parent G19 verification)
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: Academic search-based UAS testing frameworks are validated only in nominal and fault edge cases, not jamming, DDIL or sensor denial - degraded-environment replay remains an open T&E problem in the literature.

evidence.label: INFERENCE

card.why_existing_startups_havent_solved: Because the customers are also the toolmakers. Each interface family already has an owner that furnishes or plans free tooling: Army PM UAS furnishes STANAG 4586/IOP compliance test tools to programs and eligible vendors (army.mil), MITRE supports UMAA compliance (RECALL - not re-verified), the Army planned an automatic pntOS plug-in compliance toolkit in 2021 (GAO-21-320SP) and the pntOS/ASPN authors now govern the standards through the ISTO consortium (2026-06), SOCOM runs its own UxSAI assessment events and buys CV synthetic data rather than interface tooling (2026), and CDAO has selected Applied Intuition for enterprise autonomy validation. Tangram Flex (Dayton, ~$11M 2024 revenue per company index, RECALL) already sells interface-code generation and verification to USAF programs, which shows the slot supports a services-heavy small business rather than a venture. On the PNT side, RF simulator incumbents (Spirent, Safran Skydel) own the scenario-generation budget, and civil DHS-framework conformance is self-attested with no certifying body, so nobody pays for an independent score.
card.technical_wedge: The only piece a startup could plausibly own is a software-only, message-level (not RF-level) degraded-PNT scenario generator that emits ASPN-2023 measurement streams (GNSS, IMU, clock, magnetometer, RF-ranging) under scripted jamming, spoofing, multipath and dropout profiles, plus a CI runner that executes a vendor's pntOS-C plug-in against those streams and produces a schema-conformance report, a Resilient-PNT-Framework behavior checklist (Prevent/Respond/Recover per level, reported as pass/fail behaviors rather than a single score) and a draft DoDI 4650.08 evidence table. A MAVLink/PX4 DDIL replay harness (link-loss, latency, GNSS-loss injection into SITL) is a natural second module. UMAA over DDS is feasible from public ICDs; STANAG 4586 and FANTOM Core are out of reach without program access and are excluded from the wedge.

mvp.what: Open-core 'PNT interface digital twin': ASPN-2023 synthetic-measurement generator with degradation profiles grounded in public datasets (TEXBAT spoofing scenarios, public MagNav flight data - RECALL, not re-verified), a pntOS-C plug-in CI runner, and a report generator (schema conformance, RPCF behavior checklist, NAVWAR evidence table); plus a PX4 SITL DDIL replay module.
mvp.demonstrable_in_3_6_months: Yes for the open subset: run the public pntOS-C example plug-in and two open-source estimators through ten scripted degradation scenarios in CI and emit the reports; show a PX4 SITL mission replayed under link-loss and GNSS-loss profiles with pass/fail against declared behaviors.
mvp.what_it_must_prove: That harness findings reproduce real integration failures on at least two real vendors' pntOS plug-ins under NDA; that a NAVWAR/PM PNT or SBIR reviewer accepts the synthetic streams and evidence table as milestone-grade input (NP004 Q&A is the only public precedent); and that a vendor will pay $25k-$100k for it rather than wait for the consortium's free suite.

data_requirement.what: Public interface specifications (ASPN-ICD YAML, pntOS-C API, MAVLink XML, UMAA ICDs), public GNSS spoofing/jamming datasets to calibrate degradation profiles, realistic sensor error models for alternative PNT sources, and - for credibility - real vendor plug-ins and logs under NDA.
data_requirement.legally_realistically_obtainable: Public specs and datasets: yes, unclassified and Distribution A. Realistic alt-PNT error models: partly (published literature; the government's own models are internal and GAO says fidelity is poor). Vendor plug-ins/logs: only by partnership and NDA. STANAG 4586 document: NATO-controlled, obtainable via a program or national body - likely not for a non-U.S.-person founder without counsel. FANTOM Core API and A-GRA: government-controlled, program access only.
sources: TEXBAT and MagNav public datasets (RECALL - not re-verified this session)

integration_requirement.who_controls_the_interface: The government and its consortia control every interface: Army C5ISR Center / ISTO PNT Standards Consortium (ASPN/pntOS), Navy PMS 406 via AUVSI (UMAA), NATO (STANAG 4586), SOCOM PEO-SDA (FANTOM Core), Dronecode/PX4 community (MAVLink). The startup controls none and cannot influence versioning.

Vendor-paid pilots and civil work carry no such barrier. Needs counsel.

incumbent_response.could_anduril_palantir_l3harris_add_it: Yes, and most do not need to: Applied Intuition already sells validation tooling and holds the CDAO enterprise slot; Anduril and Shield AI run internal A-GRA/Lattice test rigs; Spirent/Safran can add ASPN export in one release; the consortium can publish a free suite; Tangram Flex already sells interface verification. A six-month response is realistic for any of them if the market proved real.
incumbent_response.why_startup_still_wins_or_reject: Reject as a venture. The startup's only structural advantage is vendor-neutrality (no CCA competitor can be the arbiter), but the government and the standards consortium are more neutral still and price at zero. The residual is a services-heavy devtools niche or an acqui-hire into IS4S/Leidos/Applied Intuition/Tangram Flex.

capital_required.assumptions: INFERENCE/LOW. PoC = two founders for 6 months on the open subset plus cloud CI. Credible demo adds one senior navigation/estimation engineer (12 months), two vendor pilots under NDA, and legal counsel on export classification. 'Production deployment' here means a government lab or consortium adopting the runner as reference plus a paid OTA to integrate with its M&S - which additionally requires U.S.-person staff and CUI handling (CMMC L2), and likely program access that this team lacks.

expertise_required.role: Navigation/estimation engineer who has built a pntOS/ASPN plug-in or a multi-sensor PNT fusion filter
expertise_required.why: Realistic alt-PNT error models and degradation profiles are the product; without them the generator is a toy that reviewers will reject (GAO notes SOF distrust of M&S)

expertise_required.role: Autonomy T&E engineer with government assessment-event or program-lab experience (SOFWERX, PNTAX, PMS 406)
expertise_required.why: Knows what evidence reviewers actually accept and how DDIL scenarios are scored

expertise_required.role: Strong systems/software engineer (CI, DDS, MAVLink, C/C++ and Python)
expertise_required.why: Builds the runner, replay and report tooling; the engineer co-founder covers this

expertise_required.role: Export-control and government-contracts counsel
expertise_required.why: Classify the tooling (publicly available/EAR99 vs. ITAR-adjacent when adapted to military interfaces) and structure SBIR eligibility

regulatory_burden.explanation: The open-subset harness (public ASPN/pntOS-C, MAVLink, UMAA ICDs, DHS framework) can plausibly be built as unclassified, publicly available software; no ATO is needed for vendor-side CI tooling. Burden rises sharply when the tool is adapted to military-controlled interfaces (STANAG 4586, FANTOM Core, A-GRA), touches vendor CUI logs (CMMC Level 2), or is used inside a government lab (ATO, U.S.-person staff). Whether test tooling 'specially designed' for military autonomy interfaces is ITAR technical data is a counsel question, not a judgment made here.
regulatory_burden.non_us_person_founder_note: The Indonesian co-founder can work on the public-standards core and the civil DHS-RPCF product; access to STANAG 4586 documents, FANTOM Core APIs, vendor CUI logs and any SOFWERX/program engagement would need a deemed-export and CUI review by counsel and may be foreclosed. SBIR is closed to the current cap table regardless. Describe constraints; do not treat as a legal determination.

dual_use_potential.explanation: The PNT half has a real civil twin (DHS RPCF v2.0, NIST IR 8323r1, CISA federal PNT acquisition guidance March 2024, IEEE P1952 - RECALL) and civil timing vendors already market conformance, but conformance is self-attested with no certifying body or mandate, so a paying civil buyer for independent scoring is a HYPOTHESIS. MAVLink/PX4 replay has some commercial drone-QA demand but is served by open-source SITL tooling and vendor CI.

defensibility.explanation: Scenario libraries and degradation profiles could become a modest asset, and consortium standing plus a lab's adoption of the runner as reference would be the real moat - but standards are open, the government and consortium can publish free suites, RF-simulator incumbents can replicate degradation profiles, and the scoring output is scientifically contested (arXiv 2607.05415). No data, accreditation or network-effect moat is visible.

card.why_now: 2025-2026 moved reference interfaces from paper to practice: ASPN-ICD (2026-01) and pntOS-C (2026-04) went public, the ISTO PNT Standards Consortium formed (2026-06), SOCOM mandated FANTOM Core in solicitations (2026-06) and stood up UxSAI assessment events (2026-08), first A-GRA validation flights occurred (2026-02), NAVWAR accepted synthetic ASPN data as SBIR input (2026-08), DIU created third-party Blue UAS assessors (2025-09), and GPS-denied operation became routine (dozen-plus monthly domestic interference tests per NAVCEN). The counter-signal is equally recent: the same period saw the government and consortium claim the tooling role for themselves.
card.killer_risk: There is no requirement owner and no budget for third-party conformance tooling because every interface owner furnishes or plans its own free tools (Army STANAG 4586/IOP test tools, planned pntOS toolkit, ISTO consortium, MITRE UMAA, SOCOM's own assessment pipeline, CDAO's Applied Intuition environment), so the paid market collapses to a few dozen vendors buying a $25k-$100k stopgap - a consultancy or acqui-hire outcome, not a company that justifies $2-5M, and the civil 'score against the DHS framework' output has no certifying customer and is scientifically contested.
