score.title: Autonomy and PNT conformance and test-and-evaluation tooling: machine-to-machine conformance suites for MAVLink/STANAG 4586/UMAA/FANTOM-style interfaces, DDIL scenario replay, and an ASPN synthetic-measurement generator with pntOS plug-in conformance checks scored against the DHS Resilient PNT framework

scores.rationale: Real and documented but non-existential: vendors re-test per program and find failures late; GAO-21-320SP (2021-05-10, FACT/HIGH) says alt-PNT M&S fidelity is 'poorer' and integrated trade tools 'do not yet exist'; DoDI 4650.08 forces NAVWAR evidence at every milestone. But the pain is capacity and cadence of government assessment, which the government is actively addressing itself (UxSAI AEs 2026, planned pntOS toolkit).

Recurs per software drop, per assessment cycle and per interface family, but the cadence is set by capacity-limited government events (annual PNTAX; SOFWERX UxSAI AEs Jun-Dec 2026; CCA six-month phases), so the felt frequency for any one vendor is a few times a year.

Score 1 because no budget owner for third-party conformance/replay tooling can be identified: the only dedicated open-architecture PNT figure is $17M DoD-wide FY2020-2024 (GAO-21-320SP); the 2026 SOCOM UxSAI Synthetic Data Modeler AE buys EO/IR computer-vision synthetic data, not interface conformance (sam.gov, MEDIUM); NP004 (Phase I OT up to $200k+$115k) funds the vendor's own product, not tooling; CISA's federal PNT guidance creates no funded certification. Not 0 because these adjacent lines prove money exists in the neighborhood.

Vendor-paid B2B pilots need no vehicle, which keeps this above 1. Government-side access is narrow: SBIR is closed to this cap table under 13 CFR 121.702; SOFWERX AEs are U.S.-company events whose T&E is government-performed; a lab adopting a runner has no contracting office identified. Public evidence insufficient for any vehicle that buys third-party conformance tooling.

Schema/contract checking against public ASPN-ICD YAML, pntOS-C, MAVLink and UMAA IDL is straightforward engineering; PX4 SITL replay with link/GNSS-loss injection is standard. The hard parts are realistic alt-PNT error models (GAO says government fidelity itself is poor) and a defensible resilience score (arXiv 2607.05415, 2026-07, shows single-number scores are decision-unstable), which cap the credibility of the core output.

An open-subset proof of concept fits ($60k-$120k, INFERENCE/LOW), but a demo a reviewer would credit needs real vendor plug-ins under NDA, a senior navigation/estimation engineer (fatal-if-absent) and export counsel, estimated $400k-$900k; $250k does not reach the milestone that would justify further capital.

A public pntOS-C plug-in and PX4 SITL run through ten scripted degradation scenarios in CI is demonstrable in 4-6 months. 'Credible' to a NAVWAR/PM PNT reviewer or SOFWERX assessor adds 6-12 months for vendor partnerships and validation of degradation profiles against real logs.

The open subset is genuinely available (ASPN-ICD, pntOS-C Apache-2.0, MAVLink, UMAA ICDs via AUVSI, DHS RPCF v2.0, cisagov/pnt-integrity); public spoofing/MagNav datasets exist (RECALL - not re-verified). STANAG 4586 (NATO-controlled), FANTOM Core and A-GRA are unreachable; realistic alt-PNT error models and vendor logs require partnerships.

The open-standards core and the civil DHS-RPCF product can plausibly be built as unclassified, publicly available software with no clearance or ATO (counsel to confirm classification). Burden rises to CUI/CMMC L2 and possible ITAR-adjacency once the tool is adapted to military-controlled interfaces or handles vendor logs - exactly where the defense value is.

The MVP uses only public specifications, open datasets, simulated data and commercial compute; classification dependence is 'eventually' (A-GRA/FANTOM Core/JNWC threat conditions). Not 5 because the interfaces with money behind them are controlled from day one.

Score 1 because every interface family already has a zero-priced or entrenched supplier: Army says STANAG 4586/IOP compliance test tools are 'available to programs and eligible vendors' (army.mil, FACT/MEDIUM); Army planned an automatic pntOS toolkit (GAO 2021); the ISTO PNT Standards Consortium (Leidos/IS4S/TRX, 2026-06) governs pntOS/ASPN; MITRE supports UMAA (RECALL); SOCOM runs its own UxSAI assessments; CDAO selected Applied Intuition for enterprise autonomy validation (2026-05); Spirent PNT Xe and Skydel AI (2025) automate PNT scenarios; Tangram Flex sells interface verification; DIU Recognized Assessors hold the third-party role for Blue UAS.

Score 1 because there is no evidence incumbents are failing customers in a way a startup can exploit: buyers are building or have just bought their tooling (UxSAI AEs, Applied Intuition, consortium), and the only visible weakness - poor alt-PNT M&S fidelity - is a problem the startup cannot solve better than the sensor vendors and the government's own models.

Open interfaces are well documented and CI/container integration is routine (pntOS-C C API, UMAA over DDS, MAVLink). But the startup controls none of the interfaces, the government/consortium controls versioning, and the two interfaces with growing money (FANTOM Core, STANAG 4586/A-GRA) are excluded from what the team can integrate.

Score 1 because standards are open, the government or consortium can publish free suites, RF-simulator incumbents can replicate degradation profiles in one release, the scoring output is scientifically contested, and no data, accreditation or network-effect moat is visible; the only moat (a lab adopting the runner as reference) is a government relationship the team cannot reach today.

A civil twin exists (DHS RPCF v2.0, NIST IR 8323r1, CISA federal PNT acquisition guidance 2024-03, IEEE P1952 - RECALL) and civil vendors market conformance, but conformance is self-attested with no certifying body or mandate, so paying civil demand for independent scoring is a HYPOTHESIS; MAVLink replay has thin commercial QA demand served by open SITL tooling.

Expansion paths exist on paper (allied navies converging on UMAA/STANAG-style C2 via AUKUS Maritime Big Play 2025-08; civil timing operators; program-office licences), but each interface family has its own owner and free tooling, so expansion multiplies small niches rather than compounding.

In principle a per-drop, per-cycle subscription; in practice the paid market is a few dozen vendors buying a $25k-$100k stopgap until the consortium or government suite ships, and civil buyers have no recurring compliance obligation.

Better than the parents because the open-subset devtool is buildable unclassified by a strong engineer and the civil PNT product carries no ITAR/FOCI/SBIR barrier for the Indonesian founder. Still 2 because both fatal-if-absent roles (navigation/estimation engineer with a real pntOS/ASPN plug-in; autonomy T&E engineer with assessment-event experience) are missing, SBIR is closed to the cap table, and the team has no route to the controlled interfaces or lab relationships that would make the product matter.

market.summary: No requirement owner and no budget: the only 2026 procurements in the neighborhood (SOCOM UxSAI Synthetic Data Modeler and Mission Autonomy AEs) buy EO/IR CV synthetic data and government-performed T&E, not third-party interface conformance or replay; the pntOS toolkit is planned in-house and the standards now sit with the ISTO consortium; civil DHS-RPCF conformance is self-attested with no certifying body; the addressable paid market is a few dozen vendors buying a stopgap - consultancy drift is the base case.

competition.summary: The slot is occupied at zero price for every interface family: Army-furnished STANAG 4586/IOP test tools, planned Army pntOS toolkit, ISTO consortium (Leidos/IS4S/TRX), MITRE UMAA (RECALL), SOCOM's own assessment pipeline, CDAO's Applied Intuition environment, Spirent/Skydel scenario automation, Tangram Flex interface verification, DIU Recognized Assessors for Blue UAS; any of them can add ASPN export or a DDIL replay module in one release, and APIs and versioning are controlled by the government.

feasibility.summary: The open subset is genuinely buildable, unclassified and within $250k - an improvement over the parents - but the demo that matters requires real vendor plug-ins under NDA, a senior navigation engineer the team lacks, access to controlled documents (STANAG 4586, FANTOM Core) the non-U.S.-person founder likely cannot touch, SBIR eligibility the cap table does not have, and a resilience score whose validity the literature disputes.

score.verdict_rationale: Kill as a venture. Evaluated on its own merits, the narrower form removes the parents' worst defects (no orchestrator, no live multi-vehicle demo, an unclassified open-subset MVP that fits $250k), which is why founder fit rises to 2.8 from 1.8/2.7. But the PROBLEM -> USER -> REQUIREMENT OWNER -> PROGRAM OFFICE -> CONTRACTING OFFICE -> BUDGET -> VEHICLE chain breaks at REQUIREMENT OWNER and BUDGET: no office owns 'third-party conformance tooling', and every dollar found in 2026 funds government-run assessment (UxSAI AEs), CV synthetic data, government-owned toolkits, or the vendor's own SBIR deliverable - the major penalty applies. Competition refutes at strength 5 because the Army states STANAG 4586/IOP test tools are already furnished to programs and vendors, the standards owners (ISTO consortium, MITRE, C5ISR Center) can publish free suites, and Applied Intuition, Spirent/Skydel and Tangram Flex already sell the adjacent products. The civil DHS-framework scoring leg, which was meant to give the non-U.S.-person founder an unrestricted market, has no certifying body, no mandate, self-attesting vendors, and a July 2026 paper showing single-number resilience scores are decision-unstable. Market attractiveness 2.1 is the parents' level; the surviving business is an open-core devtools/consulting niche or an acqui-hire into IS4S/Leidos/Applied Intuition/Tangram Flex, not a company to capitalize with $2-5M.
score.narrower_version_if_borderline: Not applicable (verdict is kill). For the record, the non-venture form that could exist: an open-source pntOS-C/ASPN conformance runner and ASPN degraded-measurement generator contributed to the ISTO PNT Standards Consortium as a credibility project, monetized through 2-4 vendor-paid integration/test engagements ($25k-$100k) with alt-PNT vendors preparing for APEX/NP004-style deliverables, and a behavior-checklist (not single-score) service for civil timing operators under CISA's federal PNT acquisition guidance. Sized as a lifestyle/services business or an acqui-hire path; and better treated as a credibility feature inside a different gap (e.g., the S11 assured-PNT awareness gap) than as a standalone company.
score.most_important_question_answer: With $250,000 today the two founders should build, first, an open-core ASPN-2023 synthetic-measurement generator (GNSS, IMU, clock, magnetometer, RF-ranging streams under scripted jamming, spoofing and dropout profiles calibrated to public datasets) plus a CI runner that executes any pntOS-C plug-in against those streams and emits a schema-conformance report, a DHS-RPCF Prevent/Respond/Recover behavior checklist and a draft DoDI 4650.08 evidence table, with a PX4 SITL DDIL replay module as the autonomy-side proof. They should show it first to the IS4S/TRX/Leidos engineers who steward pntOS/ASPN through the ISTO consortium, then to three or four second-tier alt-PNT vendors preparing NP004-style or APEX deliverables, and only then to a C5ISR Center pntOS lead or SOFWERX UxSAI staff. The demo must prove that the harness reproduces real plug-in integration failures on two vendors' code under NDA and that a NAVWAR or PM PNT reviewer accepts synthetic ASPN streams and the evidence table as milestone-grade input (the NP004 Q&A of 2026-08-08 is the one public precedent). The customer cares because assessment slots are annual and capacity-limited, failures surface late, and NAVWAR evidence is assembled by hand. The honest answer to 'why can't an incumbent crush them' is that they can and largely have: the Army already furnishes STANAG 4586/IOP test tools, the consortium can publish an official suite for free, Spirent or Skydel can add ASPN export in a release, and Applied Intuition holds the enterprise validation slot. The milestone that would justify $2-5M - a named program office or lab adopting the runner as its conformance reference with a funded OTA, or a CISA/NIST-recognized RPCF assessment scheme that requires independent scoring - depends on decisions the government has shown no sign of making and on U.S.-person staff and SBIR eligibility the team does not have. It fails not on pain but on the absence of a buyer who is not also the builder.
score.bear_case_summary: The buyer is the builder and prices at zero. No office owns or funds third-party conformance tooling; the 2026 SOCOM UxSAI buys are CV synthetic data and government-run T&E; the Army furnishes STANAG 4586/IOP test tools and planned its own pntOS toolkit; the pntOS/ASPN authors now govern the standards through the ISTO consortium; CDAO picked Applied Intuition for enterprise autonomy validation; Spirent/Skydel own PNT scenario generation; the civil DHS-framework score has no certifying customer and is scientifically contested; the controlled interfaces (STANAG 4586, FANTOM Core, A-GRA) are unreachable for a non-U.S.-person founder and the cap table is SBIR-ineligible. The residual is a few dozen vendors buying a $25k-$100k stopgap.
score.bull_case_summary: The reference interfaces went public and operational in 2025-2026 (ASPN-ICD, pntOS-C, UMAA 6.0, FANTOM Core mandate, first A-GRA flights), a standards consortium now exists to adopt a reference runner, NAVWAR accepted synthetic ASPN data as SBIR input, DIU has shown it will outsource compliance assessment to third parties (Blue UAS Recognized Assessors), CISA tells federal buyers to specify resilience levels, and GAO documents that government M&S fidelity for alt-PNT is poor. A vendor-neutral open-core runner that becomes the consortium's reference could earn a small, real devtools business and an acqui-hire - and it can be built unclassified by this team.

verdicts.bear_case: There is no requirement owner and no budget line for third-party conformance, replay or synthetic-PNT tooling. The 2026 money in this neighborhood went to government-run assessment (SOFWERX/PEO-SDA UxSAI Mission Autonomy Systems AE, with T&E performed by the government) and to EO/IR computer-vision synthetic data (UxSAI Synthetic Data Modeler AE, milestones June-October 2026) - neither is interface conformance or DDIL replay. The Army planned its own pntOS compliance toolkit in 2021 and has since handed pntOS/ASPN stewardship to an ISTO consortium founded by Leidos, IS4S and TRX (June 2026), which is the natural publisher of a free official suite. NAVWAR's NP004 topic accepted synthetic ASPN data, but it funds the vendor's product, not tooling, and closed 2026-09-23. On the civil side, the DHS Resilient PNT Conformance Framework has no certifying body, CISA's acquisition guidance asks agencies to specify levels but not to require independent assessment, and vendors (Oscilloquartz/ADVA, VIAVI) self-attest. The paying market is therefore a few dozen small vendors buying a $25k-$100k stopgap, which is a consultancy, not a venture.
verdicts.strongest_single_argument: Every dollar that touches this problem in 2026 pays the government to assess, or a standards owner to publish, or a vendor to build its own deliverable - none pays a third party for conformance tooling, and the one civil market that could have had no such gatekeeper (DHS RPCF) has no certification requirement at all.

Each additional ecosystem (NGC2 team-lead review, Armory RAISE, a second AO) receives a re-cut of the same evidence, re-scoped to that ecosystem's template

card.current_solution: GRC platforms (eMASS government-furnished; Telos Xacta; RegScale incl. open-sourced OSCAL Hub; Paramify; Vanta/Drata for 20x), host-provided inheritance and evidence (Iron Bank compliance reports and provenance data; UDS/Lula; Game Warden), supply-chain metadata tools (Anchore, Sonatype, Chainguard, GUAC/Kusari), open-source OSCAL toolchains (OSCAL Compass compliance-trestle and C2P; FedRAMP 20x ksi-harness-type projects) and, for TAK, the tak.gov build-and-sign pipeline plus manual code review. Glue between these is scripts, spreadsheets and consultant labor.
card.failure: It fails at two seams: (1) between pipeline artifacts and the assessor - the SBOM, scan and attestation objects are not linked by content hash to the OSCAL assessment-results items an AO/3PAO reads, so re-collection and re-adjudication happen per ecosystem and reciprocity does not occur; (2) before pipeline submission for TAK/marketplace plugins, where no automated conformance check (RBAC, audit events, data handling, SBOM) exists, so failures are found by human reviewers after submission (as the Sept 2025 Army CTO memo showed for NGC2 third-party apps).

card.why_existing_startups_havent_solved: They largely have, in pieces, and the pieces are free: GUAC already is an open-source, content-addressed evidence graph for SBOMs, attestations and vulnerabilities (OpenSSF incubating, maintained by venture-backed Kusari); OSCAL Compass C2P already converts tool results into OSCAL assessment results (CNCF, IBM/Red Hat); ksi-harness-type projects emit FedRAMP 20x artifacts; RegScale open-sourced an OSCAL Hub; Iron Bank publishes provenance and compliance reports for its containers. What no one has solved is the part that is not software: getting an AO or 3PAO to accept a machine-generated package from an unknown party without re-adjudication (State of DevSecOps 2025: AOs 'biased to caution'). Defense Unicorns tried the DoD-native open-source evidence layer (Lula 1), put it in maintenance mode and raised $136M for the delivery platform instead - the platform owner concluded the evidence layer is not where value accrues. For TAK, TPC owns the pipeline and has not asked for a conformance tester; plugin developers are numerous but individually tiny spenders.
card.technical_wedge: Two thin, open-source pieces of glue rather than a platform: (a) 'evidence crosswalk' plugins that take a GUAC graph (or raw CycloneDX/SPDX + Grype/Trivy + cosign/in-toto + InSpec/CKL) and emit OSCAL assessment-results and SWFT/20x-shaped bundles in which every finding carries the content hash of the artifact it came from and a signed reviewer-decision record; (b) an ATAK-CIV plugin conformance kit (synthetic roles and tagged data, RBAC matrix, audit-event coverage, SBOM, signed OSCAL results) that developers run before tak.gov submission. Both plug into what hosts and pipelines already run (UDS/Big Bang/Iron Bank, tak.gov build-and-sign) and compete with nothing that has a budget.

mvp.what: Open-source CLI + GitHub Action: ingest SBOM/scan/attestation/InSpec outputs from a UDS Core or Big Bang sample pipeline (or a GUAC instance), emit a hash-linked OSCAL assessment-results bundle plus a 20x-style KSI file, with a reviewer web view recording accept/reject per item; and an ATAK-CIV conformance tester run against three open-source sample plugins that produces a signed OSCAL results fragment.
mvp.demonstrable_in_3_6_months: Yes: all inputs are open formats and all target ecosystems (ATAK-CIV SDK, UDS Core, Big Bang, GUAC, compliance-trestle) are public; two engineers can ship a demonstrable version in 3-4 months for well under $100k.
mvp.what_it_must_prove: That one 3PAO or one platform ISSM accepts the generated bundle with measured re-work hours saved versus their current workflow, and that a single evidence item is reused across two regimes (e.g., SWFT-style and 20x) without re-collection; for TAK, that a plugin flagged by the tester would have failed human review and that TPC or a plugin shop values the pre-check.

data_requirement.what: SBOMs, scan outputs, attestations and STIG/InSpec results from representative pipelines; OSCAL catalogs/profiles (NIST 800-53 rev5, FedRAMP 20x KSIs); sample ATAK-CIV plugins; and, to prove acceptance, real assessor decisions on real packages.
data_requirement.legally_realistically_obtainable: Pipeline artifacts, OSCAL content, ATAK-CIV SDK and sample plugins: yes, all public. Real DoD packages and AO/3PAO decisions: no - they are CUI and held by programs/assessors; obtainable only after a contract or a host partnership, and the non-U.S.-person founder would need to be walled off from them.

incumbent_response.could_anduril_palantir_l3harris_add_it: Yes. incumbent_response.why_startup_still_wins_or_reject: Reject as a company thesis. The only non-commodity asset would be a cross-vendor record of what assessors actually accepted, and that requires acceptance the team cannot obtain first. As an open-source contribution to GUAC/OSCAL Compass and a TAK developer tool it has real utility and credibility value, but no incumbent needs to crush it - they can simply adopt it.

Credible demo: one pilot with 2-3 hosted ISVs and a 3PAO plus a part-time former SCA/ISSM adviser, tenant fees on a host sandbox, 9-15 months. Production: a U.S.-person compliance lead, CUI-handling practices (DFARS 7012/CMMC L2 readiness), an embedding agreement with a host, eMASS OSCAL import testing; the product itself may need an authorization if offered as SaaS to DoD users.

expertise_required.why: The whole product is crosswalk correctness; errors destroy assessor trust.

expertise_required.why: Cap-table (SBIR), CUI role separation and any deemed-export exposure need structuring before a government-side pilot.

regulatory_burden.explanation: The MVP is open-source software on public standards with no CUI, no ITAR technical data and no government system access; burden becomes medium only when the tool touches real DoD packages (CUI, DFARS 252.204-7012/CMMC L2 readiness), eMASS (DISA-gated) or is hosted as SaaS for DoD users (needs its own authorization). Not legal advice; needs counsel.
regulatory_burden.non_us_person_founder_note: A non-U.S.-person co-founder can build, publish and sell the open-source component and the TAK developer tool. Access to real DoD assessment packages, vulnerability findings and eMASS is governed by contract clauses and need-to-know and may involve export-controlled data; role separation and possibly a technology control plan would be needed, and SBIR eligibility (>50% U.S. citizen/permanent-resident ownership and control) must be checked with counsel. Germany and Indonesia are not 'countries of concern' for SBIR disclosure purposes.

dual_use_potential.explanation: The same evidence-graph-to-assessment-results glue serves FedRAMP 20x/Rev5 machine-readable packages (RFC-0024), SOC 2, StateRAMP, CMMC and EU obligations (Cyber Resilience Act SBOM/vulnerability-handling duties phasing in 2026-2027 - RECALL, not re-verified this session, MEDIUM). This is also the problem: the commercial market is where Vanta/Drata/Paramify and free harnesses already compete.

defensibility.explanation: Nothing proprietary accrues to an open-source component by design; the only durable asset would be an acceptance-precedent record (which assessor accepted which evidence item), and building it requires the acceptance the team lacks. Integrations are with interfaces others control. Defensibility is low.

card.why_now: SWFT (Apr 2025), CSRMC (Sep 2025), FedRAMP RFC-0024 (Jan 2026) and 20x GA (Aug 2026) all make machine-readable evidence mandatory or expected, the AI Strategy memo (Jan 2026) demands ATO reciprocity, GUAC and OSCAL Compass have matured to usable open-source substrates, and NGC2's Sept 2025 AO memo plus C2APPSRFI-1 (May 2026) show the Army standing up app onboarding. Against that, the same signals have already drawn Kusari, IBM/Red Hat, RegScale, Paramify, Vanta and Defense Unicorns into the space.
card.killer_risk: The thing described already exists as free, better-maintained open source (GUAC for the evidence graph; OSCAL Compass C2P for assessment results; ksi-harness for 20x) and the only remaining value - assessor acceptance - is a policy/relationship asset no two-student team can earn first; with no buyer, budget line or vehicle for a vendor-neutral component, the outcome is a well-regarded repo and an acquihire, not a company.

score.title: ATO-evidence tooling: open-source evidence graph (SBOM, scans, attestations to OSCAL assessment results with content-addressed provenance) and TAK/marketplace plugin conformance tester, offered as a vendor-neutral component to hosting platforms and app pipelines rather than as a GRC product

scores.rationale: Real and documented (ATO the longest step; SWFT RFI 500+ responses citing inconsistent attestation demands; Sept 2025 NGC2 AO memo), but for the narrowed component the pain is re-work hours for vendors and platform engineers, not mission failure, and hosts already absorb most of it for tenants.
Recurs on every release, every new ecosystem and every plugin submission; SWFT/CSRMC/20x make it continuous.

Score 1: no appropriation, PE, O&M line, RFI or solicitation funds a vendor-neutral evidence component or a TAK plugin conformance tester; the sole tooling-specific signal is a closed AF SBIR D2P2 topic the cap table likely cannot use; SWFT back-end review is described as government tooling inside eMASS; commercial ISV compliance budgets exist but already flow to Paramify/Vanta/Drata and free harnesses. Not 0 only because ISV/host budgets for compliance tooling demonstrably exist.

No government procurement is needed (commercial/open-source sale), which is accessible in principle, but every adoption path runs through a gatekeeper's permission (Defense Unicorns, TPC, Platform One, GRC vendor, NGC2 pipeline lead) and no path leads to a purchase order from a government office.
All inputs and targets are open standards with mature substrates (GUAC, compliance-trestle, Sigstore, ATAK-CIV SDK); the remaining crosswalk work is well understood engineering.
PoC is $40-90k; a first open-source release plus ISV/3PAO pilot fits inside $250k. Not 5 because a credible acceptance demonstration needs a U.S.-person assessor adviser and host sandbox fees.
A working evidence crosswalk and TAK conformance kit is demonstrable in 3-4 months; a demo that proves assessor acceptance takes 9-15 months.

Pipeline artifacts, OSCAL content, sample plugins are public; real assessment packages and AO/3PAO decisions (the data that would make the tool credible) are CUI and unavailable to the team, especially the non-U.S.-person founder.

Open-source, EAR99-class software on public standards with no CUI or ITAR in the MVP; burden rises (CUI, DFARS 7012/CMMC, eMASS gating, own authorization for SaaS) only at the government-side stage. Not legal advice.

Score 5: every input (SBOM, scans, attestations, OSCAL catalogs, ATAK-CIV SDK, UDS/Big Bang open repos, GUAC) is public and unclassified; the product can be built, published and used by non-U.S. persons without any government access.

Score 1: the described open-source evidence graph already exists (GUAC, OpenSSF incubating, Kusari-maintained, v1.1.0 Mar 2026); the tool-output-to-OSCAL-assessment-results converter exists (OSCAL Compass C2P, CNCF); free 20x harnesses exist; RegScale open-sourced OSCAL Hub; Defense Unicorns, Anchore/Chainguard/Sonatype, Paramify/Vanta/Drata, Telos and government Iron Bank/eMASS tooling occupy every adjacent layer. The delta available to a new entrant is glue.

Score 1: incumbents have first look at SWFT/CSRMC schemas, own the consumer interfaces (eMASS, tak.gov, UDS admission, NGC2 pipeline) and can adopt any open-source component the startup publishes rather than compete with it; Defense Unicorns' choice to shelve Lula 1 shows the layer is optional to them, not a weakness.

Input integration is easy (open formats); output integration depends on interfaces controlled by DISA, TPC, Defense Unicorns, Platform One, GRC vendors and the future NGC2 pipeline lead, none of which the startup can compel.

Score 1: an open-source vendor-neutral component is designed to have no proprietary lock-in; the only conceivable moat (an acceptance-precedent record) requires assessor acceptance the team cannot obtain first and, if it worked, would need DoD CIO sponsorship that would more likely be given to a government or incumbent tool.
The same glue serves FedRAMP 20x/Rev5 machine-readable packages, SOC 2, StateRAMP, CMMC and EU CRA-driven SBOM obligations (RECALL); high dual-use is also why the commercial layer is already crowded.

Expansion from a component means becoming a GRC or supply-chain platform, i.e., competing head-on with funded incumbents; the honest expansion path is absorption into a host or GRC vendor (acquihire).
Open-source components earn support or embedding fees only if a host embeds them; TAK plugin developers are many but tiny spenders; no government repeat purchase exists for the component.

A strong engineer can build both pieces and a non-U.S.-person founder is not blocked from the open-source/TAK work; but the team lacks the fatal-if-absent SCA/ISSM/3PAO perspective, has no assessor relationships, and the German founder's NATO adjacency adds little because the buyer problem is U.S. acceptance, not access.

market.summary: No budget owner, line, RFI or vehicle exists for a vendor-neutral evidence component or a TAK conformance tester (budget confidence LOW; the one tooling topic is a closed AF SBIR D2P2 the cap table likely cannot use); the requirement owners (DoD CIO for SWFT/CSRMC, TPC for TAK, PM C2 Applications for NGC2) are building or buying their own pipelines and back-end review inside eMASS; the payer (ISV/host) is not the acceptor (AO/3PAO, 'biased to caution'); commercial ISV budgets already go to Paramify/Vanta/Drata and free harnesses; the residual revenue is support fees from plugin shops and one possible embedding deal - consultancy or feature economics, not a market.

competition.summary: The exact artifact G36 proposes already exists as free, better-resourced open source: GUAC (OpenSSF incubating, Kusari-maintained, v1.1.0 Mar 2026) is the content-addressed evidence graph for SBOMs/attestations/vulns; OSCAL Compass C2P (CNCF, IBM/Red Hat) converts tool results into OSCAL assessment results; ksi-harness-class projects emit FedRAMP 20x artifacts; RegScale open-sourced OSCAL Hub; Iron Bank publishes provenance and compliance reports; Defense Unicorns built and shelved Lula 1. Every consumer interface (eMASS, tak.gov, UDS, NGC2 pipeline) is owned by a party that can adopt the component instead of buying it. Verified this session (FACT, HIGH) for GUAC and OSCAL Compass.

feasibility.summary: The feasibility skeptic does NOT refute: the MVP is fully unclassified, buildable for $40-90k in 3-4 months from public SDKs and standards, legally open to the non-U.S.-person founder (open-source EAR99-class software; TAK pipeline open to non-denied parties), and needs no clearance or ATO to demonstrate. The feasibility caveats are real but secondary: proving assessor acceptance needs CUI packages and a U.S.-person SCA/ISSM adviser, and SBIR is likely unavailable. Feasibility is precisely the problem - the thing is so buildable that it is a feature, not a company.

score.verdict_rationale: KILL as a venture; keep only as an open-source side project. The PROBLEM -> USER -> REQUIREMENT OWNER -> PROGRAM OFFICE -> CONTRACTING OFFICE -> BUDGET -> VEHICLE chain breaks at REQUIREMENT OWNER (neither DoD CIO, TPC nor PM C2 Applications has asked for a vendor-neutral evidence component or a plugin conformance tester), at PROGRAM OFFICE and BUDGET (none exists for the component; the only tooling money is a closed AF SBIR D2P2 topic the cap table likely cannot use), and at VEHICLE (commercial embedding at a gatekeeper's discretion only), so the major penalty applies. Independently of the penalty, the decisive new fact verified this session is that the 'open-source evidence graph with content-addressed provenance' already exists (GUAC, OpenSSF incubating, venture-backed maintainer Kusari, v1.1.0 March 2026) and the OSCAL assessment-results converter already exists (OSCAL Compass C2P, CNCF); the parent skeptics' narrower form was framed as if the substrate were unbuilt, and it is not. What remains is crosswalk glue plus a TAK developer tool with no buyer that signs purchase orders, no moat by design, and incumbents (Defense Unicorns, RegScale, Kusari, TPC, Anduril/Palantir, eMASS) who would adopt rather than fight it. Market skeptic strength 4 and competition skeptic strength 5 are accepted; the feasibility skeptic is not accepted (strength 2) because the team can genuinely build and demonstrate it - which is why it should be treated as a credibility asset (contributions to GUAC/OSCAL Compass, an ATAK-CIV conformance kit), sized under $50k, while founder capital goes to a gap with an identified buyer. Confidence HIGH for this team; MEDIUM as a general market call, because a DoD CIO or TPC mandate for a neutral evidence format would re-open a small but real niche.
score.narrower_version_if_borderline: Not borderline - killed. For completeness, the only defensible residual: (1) contribute an OSCAL assessment-results exporter with hash-linked provenance to GUAC and/or OSCAL Compass rather than forking a new graph, and (2) publish an ATAK-CIV plugin conformance kit (RBAC matrix, audit-event coverage, SBOM, signed OSCAL fragment) for TAK plugin developers with optional paid support - both as an under-$50k open-source portfolio while pursuing a different primary gap. Revisit only if TPC or DoD CIO publishes a neutral evidence/conformance requirement, or a host (Defense Unicorns/Second Front) signs an embedding LOI.
score.most_important_question_answer: If two exceptionally capable founders had $250,000 today, they should not build G36 as a company. What they would build first is small: a GUAC-to-OSCAL exporter (every OSCAL assessment-results finding carrying the content hash of the SBOM/scan/attestation it came from, plus a signed reviewer-decision record) packaged as a GitHub Action for UDS Core/Big Bang pipelines, and an ATAK-CIV plugin conformance kit that drives a plugin with synthetic roles and tagged data and emits a signed OSCAL fragment - about $40-90k and 3-4 months. They would show it to a 3PAO, two ISVs hosted on Game Warden or UDS Army facing FedRAMP 20x or SWFT third-party assessment, a Defense Unicorns or Platform One product owner, the GUAC and OSCAL Compass maintainers, and TPC's pipeline operators. The demo would have to prove, in measured hours, that an assessor accepts the generated bundle with less re-work than the ISV's current Vanta/spreadsheet flow, that one evidence item is reused across two regimes without re-collection, and that the TAK kit catches a plugin a human reviewer would have rejected. The customer would care because RFC-0024, 20x GA (Aug 2026), SWFT's third-party phase and CSRMC make machine-readable evidence dated and unavoidable. The honest answer to 'why can't an incumbent trivially crush them' is that no incumbent needs to: GUAC and OSCAL Compass already exist and can absorb the exporter as a contribution, Kusari/RegScale/Paramify can ship the same crosswalk in a quarter with first look at SWFT/CSRMC schemas, Defense Unicorns and TPC own the admission interfaces and can add the checks to their own pipelines, and the only scarce asset - a record of what assessors actually accepted - requires the acceptance the team is trying to earn. The milestone that would justify $2-5M would be two AOs or 3PAOs from different components accepting the same machine-generated package without re-adjudication plus a host contractually embedding the component; public evidence shows no non-incumbent achieving that, and no requirement owner asking for it. So it fails as a company: the $250k would buy a respected open-source contribution and an acquihire path into Defense Unicorns, Kusari or a GRC vendor. Correct use: spend under $50k on the open-source pieces as a credibility asset and put the rest into a gap with a named buyer.
score.bear_case_summary: The proposed open-source evidence graph already exists (GUAC, OpenSSF incubating, Kusari-maintained) and the OSCAL assessment-results converter already exists (OSCAL Compass C2P, CNCF); free 20x harnesses, RegScale's open OSCAL Hub, Iron Bank's provenance reports and eMASS's SWFT back-end fill the rest; Defense Unicorns shelved Lula 1 after raising $136M, showing the platform owner does not value the layer; no requirement owner, program office, budget line or vehicle exists for a vendor-neutral component or a TAK conformance tester; the acceptor (AO/3PAO, 'biased to caution') is not the payer; every consumer interface is owned by someone who can adopt the component instead of buying it; TAK plugin developers are numerous but tiny; the team lacks a U.S.-person SCA/ISSM and likely SBIR eligibility; and defensibility is nil by design. Feature or acquihire, not a company.
score.bull_case_summary: The pain is real, recurring and now dated by policy (SWFT Apr 2025 and reported Phase 2 Nov 2026; CSRMC Sep 2025; FedRAMP RFC-0024 Jan 2026 and 20x GA Aug 2026; AI Strategy demand for ATO reciprocity Jan 2026); the MVP is entirely unclassified, cheap (<$100k), fast (3-4 months) and legally open to the non-U.S.-person founder; open substrates (GUAC, OSCAL Compass, Sigstore, ATAK-CIV) mean the team builds only the missing crosswalk; the TAK pipeline is public with one owner and a NATO-wide developer base; dual-use demand spans FedRAMP, SOC 2, CMMC and EU CRA; and if TPC or DoD CIO ever mandates a neutral evidence/conformance format, the first credible open-source implementation with a hosting-platform embedding could hold a small, recurring niche. As a credibility asset and acquihire path it is genuinely useful; as a venture it is not.

verdicts.bear_case: There is no buyer with a budget for a vendor-neutral ATO-evidence component or a TAK plugin conformance tester. DoD CIO is building SWFT review into eMASS and has published no schema; TPC runs its own build-and-sign pipeline and has not asked for a conformance stage; PM C2 Applications is buying an NGC2 pipeline through a lead-entity teaming model (C2APPSRFI-1, May 2026) with no line for assurance tooling and no award found. The only tooling-specific money is a closed AF SBIR D2P2 topic (2025) that this cap table likely cannot use. On the commercial side, ISV compliance budgets exist but already flow to Paramify, Vanta, Drata, RegScale and free 20x harnesses, and hosting platforms absorb evidence assembly for tenants. What is left is support fees from TAK plugin shops and, at best, one embedding deal at a host's discretion: consultancy or feature economics. The payer (ISV/host) is not the acceptor (AO/3PAO), who is documented as 'biased to caution', so even a working tool does not convert into willingness to pay.
verdicts.strongest_single_argument: Nobody in the PROBLEM -> REQUIREMENT OWNER -> PROGRAM OFFICE -> BUDGET -> VEHICLE chain has asked for this component or holds money for it; the requirement owners are building their own pipelines and back-end review.

verdicts.bear_case: The second-generation card assumed the open-source substrate was unbuilt. It is built. GUAC - an OpenSSF incubating project maintained by venture-backed Kusari, co-created with Google, Purdue and Citi - ingests SBOMs, in-toto/SLSA attestations, vulnerability and Scorecard data into a content-addressed, GraphQL-queryable graph and shipped v1.1.0 in March 2026. OSCAL Compass (CNCF sandbox since June 2024, IBM/Red Hat origin, NIST-presented) already converts policy-validation-point results into OSCAL assessment results via C2P. ksi-harness-class projects already emit schema-valid FedRAMP 20x artifacts; RegScale open-sourced an OSCAL Hub in Dec 2025; Iron Bank publishes provenance and compliance reports for 1000+ containers; eMASS hosts the SWFT back-end. Every consumer interface (eMASS/DISA, tak.gov/TPC, UDS admission/Defense Unicorns, Big Bang/Platform One, the NGC2 pipeline lead, GRC vendors) is owned by a party that can adopt any open-source component the startup publishes rather than buy it. Defense Unicorns built the DoD-native version (Lula 1), shelved it, and raised $136M for the delivery layer - the platform owner's revealed preference is that this layer is optional. What remains is crosswalk glue and a TAK developer tool, which Kusari, RegScale, Paramify, Defense Unicorns or TPC can each ship in one release cycle with first look at SWFT/CSRMC schemas the startup does not have.

The MVP uses only public artifacts (CycloneDX/SPDX, Grype/Trivy JSON, cosign/in-toto, InSpec/CKL, NIST OSCAL catalogs, FedRAMP 20x KSIs, the open ATAK-CIV SDK, UDS Core/Big Bang/GUAC repos), needs no clearance, CUI, ATO or government system access, and can be built by two engineers for $40-90k in 3-4 months. Open-source EAR99-class software on public standards is legally publishable and sellable by a non-U.S.-person founder (not legal advice), and the TAK third-party pipeline is open to any developer not on a denied-parties list. The real feasibility caveats are secondary: (1) proving assessor acceptance requires real packages and assessor decisions that are CUI and held by programs/3PAOs, so the demo can prove format validity and re-work reduction with a friendly 3PAO but not AO acceptance; (2) the team lacks a fatal-if-absent U.S.-person SCA/ISSM/3PAO adviser and has no assessor relationships; (3) SBIR/STTR is likely unavailable under the >50% U.S.-person ownership and control test, and any government-side integration (eMASS, DoD packages) would require role separation for the Indonesian founder. None of these stops the build; they stop the build from becoming a business. The strongest feasibility-lens point is therefore a founder-fit one: a $250k team with no assessor credibility cannot earn the acceptance precedent that would be the only asset.
verdicts.strongest_single_argument: This is one of the very few gaps in the study that the team can legally and cheaply build and demonstrate today - which is exactly why it is a feature or open-source project rather than a company; the binding constraint is acceptance and buyer, not feasibility.

tech.title: Unified assured-PNT operational awareness and decision support (single pane for source health, composite confidence, jam/spoof triage, fallback recommendation) with a formation-level PNT interference picture feeding the C2/EW COP
tech.version_designed_for: NARROWER VERSION ONLY (verdict was BORDERLINE, G04-score.json). This diligence designs the vendor-neutral composite-assurance ENGINE: an ASPN 2023 / pntOS-C-conformant plug-in that ingests 3-8 heterogeneous PNT sources at 1-10 Hz and emits per-source health, composite confidence with attributed evidence, explainable fault/jam/spoof classification and a fallback recommendation, plus a synthetic scenario generator and a replay/audit library validated against public recordings (TEXBAT, Jammertest 2025) and DHS Resilient PNT Conformance Framework v2.0 behaviors. It explicitly does NOT design the single-pane HMI as the product (a thin demo window only) and does NOT design the formation-level PNT interference picture / EW COP feed (killed: classified-adjacent, NGC2-absorbable). Every plan stage and milestone below is built to test the decisive doubt from the score file: does a named buyer with a budget line or vehicle exist for this engine (NP004 Phase I awardees ~Q1 2027, the GPNTS integrator, the next NAVWAR open-topic/D2P2 cycle, an OT/CSO sponsor, or a paying civil/allied maritime pilot)? All kill criteria are measurable. Nothing here is a legal judgment on ITAR/EAR/FOCI/SBIR eligibility or immigration; those items are flagged for counsel.

architecture.prose: INPUTS. The engine consumes time-stamped PNT observables from three classes of source. (a) A synthetic scenario generator that emits ASPN 2023 schema-conformant messages (GNSS PVT and raw measurements, IMU, clock/timing, an 'alternate source' such as a simulated eLoran/radar-fix/celestial-fix channel) for a strait-transit vignette with scripted jamming onset, spoofing pull-off, INS drift, clock holdover and hardware faults. (b) Public real-world recordings: TEXBAT RF spoofing captures (UT Austin Radionavigation Lab, 25 Msps, 400 s scenarios) replayed through the GPL-3 GNSS-SDR software receiver to produce observables, and the Jammertest 2025 HDF5 interference dataset on Zenodo (CW, PRN, chirp, multi-emitter, spoofing, meaconing, with time-aligned ground truth). (c) Commercial receiver and IMU telemetry from bench hardware: u-blox ZED-F9P boards (UBX-MON-RF jamInd, AGC, per-satellite C/N0, NMEA/UBX), a MEMS IMU (Xsens MTi-3 class), and a bench timing reference for clock-holdover modelling; RF recordings are injected by CONDUCTED cable into a shielded enclosure only, never radiated. In a government phase the same ingest layer takes GPNTS ICD adapters and pntOS fusion-engine outputs (government-furnished post-award; FACT that ICDs are post-award, G04.json). COMPUTE is commodity: an x86 laptop or NUC-class box running an OCI container (Docker/Podman) fully disconnected; target footprint under one CPU core and 2 GB RAM at 10 Hz so it can co-host on a shipboard CANES-class server later (HYPOTHESIS on hosting; the Navy has not published GPNTS hosting specs). CORE SOFTWARE has seven modules: K1 ingest/normalisation (ASPN 2023 YAML-generated codecs, a pntOS-C plugin shim, NMEA-0183/UBX adapters); K2 per-source health monitors (ICD-compliance checks, C/N0-AGC anomaly tests, clock-drift/holdover model, RAIM-style residual tests, INS-GNSS divergence, position/velocity jump tests) modelled on the BSD-3 DHS PNT Integrity Library's check structure; K3 the composite confidence and consensus engine, which builds a cross-source consistency graph, weights sources by their health, and outputs a calibrated composite confidence with an attributed-evidence list (which checks fired, on which source, at what time); K4 an explainable classifier that separates hardware fault, jamming, spoofing and environmental degradation using a rule/likelihood hybrid whose every output carries a human-readable rationale; K5 a fallback recommender that maps the classified state and the health of alternates to a recommended mode (alternate source, INS-only, degraded-ops workflow) keyed to the DHS CF Respond/Recover behaviours and to the operator's own TTP table (the TTP table is customer-configurable, not embedded doctrine); K6 an append-only audit/replay store; K7 a scenario/evaluation harness that batch-runs the scenario library and computes the metrics. INTERFACES: ASPN integrity/status messages out through the pntOS plugin API; a language-neutral streaming API (gRPC/WebSocket) for any HMI or fusion engine; a replay file format (HDF5/Parquet); and a deferred, compact interference-report message shape that could later feed a COP (out of scope for this version). OUTPUTS are the six artefacts the Navy's NP004 text asks for in substance: per-source health, composite confidence with evidence, classification with rationale, fallback recommendation with rationale, an auditable timeline, and an evaluation report on held-out scenarios. USERS of the engine are, first, integrators (NP004 Phase I awardees, the GPNTS integrator, allied fusion-engine houses) who embed it behind their own HMI; second, test and evaluation staff who need the replay/audit library; and only third, via the customer's HMI, the ETV/navigation team. A thin ECDIS-style demo window exists solely to make the engine's outputs legible in an operator study.

architecture.hardest_problem: Producing a composite confidence that is CALIBRATED and a classification that is CORRECT across heterogeneous sources whose failure modes overlap (a smooth spoofing pull-off, an INS bias ramp and a receiver clock fault can all look like slow divergence), while keeping every decision explainable and while the real military threat signatures remain classified (GAO-21-320SP: 'determination of assurance is an active research area', FACT/HIGH). The engineering answer is a consensus-plus-physics architecture: per-source physical plausibility checks (C/N0-AGC signatures, clock-drift bounds, IMU-propagated position bounds) to separate jamming from spoofing from faults, cross-source residual voting to bound composite confidence, and a rule/likelihood hybrid rather than an opaque model so rationale is always available. The residual risk is domain shift: an engine tuned on TEXBAT/Jammertest and synthetic data will meet unseen signatures in a Navy data set; the mitigation is to design for post-award retraining/retuning with a documented calibration procedure rather than claiming generality (INFERENCE/MEDIUM).

architecture.integration_burden: MVP: low-to-moderate and entirely under the founders' control (open schemas, COTS serial telemetry, file-based replay). Military prototype: HIGH and outside the founders' control - the government owns every decisive interface (GPNTS ICDs post-award, ASPN stewardship reportedly moving to the ISTO consortium in 2026 (MEDIUM), RAISE/OSA accreditation, CANES hosting via PMW 160), and the GPNTS integrator controls day-to-day access; each Navy/Army/allied customer needs its own ICD-conformance adapter, which is the 'consultancy trap' the score file warns about. The architecture limits the burden by keeping all customer-specific code in the K1 adapter layer and by making the pntOS plugin API the only contract the core engine depends on. Expected effort per new military integration: 3-9 engineer-months plus government test time (HYPOTHESIS/LOW).

performance_metrics.metric: Detection latency from anomaly onset to first health/confidence change
performance_metrics.target: < 1 s at 1-10 Hz input (median < 500 ms)
performance_metrics.why: NP004 specifies 1-10 Hz ingest and the Navy's success metric is 'speed to decision during an anomaly' (FACT, G04.json); sub-second engine latency keeps the human, not the software, as the bottleneck

performance_metrics.metric: Classification accuracy (hardware fault vs jamming vs spoofing vs environmental) on held-out synthetic + public real recordings
performance_metrics.target: >= 90% correct on held-out synthetic; report per-class confusion on TEXBAT ds1-ds8 and Jammertest 2025 scenarios with no cherry-picking
performance_metrics.why: The Navy's metric is 'threat comprehension accuracy'; TEXBAT and Jammertest provide ground truth so the number is auditable (targets are HYPOTHESIS - no published Navy threshold)

performance_metrics.target: < 1 alert per 24 h of clean transit data (clean static/dynamic TEXBAT, clean Jammertest segments, own bench logs)
performance_metrics.why: Watchstanders ignore noisy tools; DHS CF v2.0 notes 'untrustworthy does not always mean the current solution is incorrect' (FACT), so alarms must be evidence-attributed and rare

performance_metrics.target: Reliability diagram / Brier score reported; confidence within +/-10% of empirical correctness per bin on held-out scenarios
performance_metrics.why: An uncalibrated 'confidence gauge' is the dashboard failure mode the score file says will be absorbed; calibration is the engine's differentiator

performance_metrics.metric: Correct-fallback selection and time-to-fallback in an operator study
performance_metrics.target: >= 30% faster median time to correct fallback and fewer wrong selections vs a fragmented-display baseline, n >= 6 former ETV/QM/navigators, pre-registered protocol
performance_metrics.why: NP004 Q&A 2026-08-26 names 'decision accuracy (e.g., correct fallback selection)' as a success metric (FACT); this is the evidence integrators and the GPNTS office can cite

performance_metrics.target: 100% of outputs carry an evidence list; bit-identical re-run of any logged scenario
performance_metrics.why: NP004 asks for 'explainable rationale and auditable trace'; after-action review and accreditation reviewers need determinism

performance_metrics.target: 100% schema-valid ASPN 2023 messages in and out; loads as a pntOS-C plugin without modification of the host
performance_metrics.why: The Navy allowed synthetic ASPN/pntOS data in Phase I and any Phase II swaps in GPNTS ICDs; conformance is the price of admission for integrators

performance_metrics.metric: Continuity of output under a compromised source
performance_metrics.target: Output continues, with degraded confidence flagged, while a source is excluded and re-admitted automatically (DHS CF Level 2/3 behaviour)
performance_metrics.why: DHS CF v2.0 defines Respond/Recover behaviours by level (FACT); civil/allied buyers can test against it

performance_metrics.target: < 1 CPU core, < 2 GB RAM, < 200 MB container image, zero network egress
performance_metrics.why: Air-gapped container deployment is an explicit NP004 requirement; co-hosting on existing shipboard servers avoids a hardware line (HYPOTHESIS on host specs)

mvp.demo: A 60-minute, fully offline demonstration on a commercial laptop: (1) the scenario harness plays a synthetic ASPN-2023 strait-transit vignette (8 sources: two GNSS receivers, INS, clock, radar-fix channel, celestial/DR channel, an alternate RF-PNT channel, a timing source) with scripted jamming onset, a slow spoofing pull-off, an INS bias ramp and a receiver hardware fault; the engine, loaded as a pntOS-C plugin, streams per-source health, composite confidence with an evidence list, an explainable classification and a fallback recommendation in under one second per event, into a thin ECDIS-style window; (2) the same engine, unchanged, ingests observables derived from TEXBAT ds3/ds7 and a Jammertest 2025 CW/chirp/spoofing segment and produces the evaluation report (latency, confusion matrix, false-alert rate, calibration); (3) a live bench segment: two u-blox ZED-F9P boards and an MTi-3 IMU inside a shielded enclosure receive a CONDUCTED gps-sdr-sim/bladeRF stimulus that shifts the fix, and the engine flags the receiver-level divergence against the IMU and the second receiver; (4) replay of any moment in the session, bit-identical, with the audit trail; (5) a summary of the operator study (n >= 6 former ETV/QM/navigators) comparing time-to-correct-fallback with and without the engine's outputs. The HMI is deliberately plain; the pitch to integrators is 'drop this plugin behind your screen'.
must_prove: Buyer test (the decisive doubt): at least one named integrator or sponsor with money agrees in writing to evaluate the plugin - an NP004 Phase I awardee (announced ~Q1 2027), the GPNTS integrator, an IWRP/NavalX/DIU sponsor, or a civil/allied maritime operator - otherwise the venture thesis fails regardless of the technology
Composite confidence and classification are correct and calibrated on held-out synthetic AND public real recordings, with a quantified false-alert rate and sub-second latency at 1-10 Hz
Former watchstanders reach the correct fallback faster and with fewer errors when the engine's outputs are present than with fragmented displays (pre-registered protocol, n >= 6)
Every recommendation is explainable and every session is replayable bit-for-bit
The engine consumes a pntOS/ASPN stream unchanged, so a government phase can swap synthetic streams for GPNTS ICD adapters without touching the core
The container runs fully disconnected on commodity hardware within the resource targets and is structured to pass Iron Bank/RAISE-style hardening later (SBOM, no network egress, non-root)
uses: public/open data (TEXBAT 1.1, Jammertest 2025 Zenodo dataset, FGI-JSDR, public GPS ICDs, NOAA ENC cells)
simulated military data (synthetic ASPN 2023 strait-transit vignettes; no real threat signatures)
unclassified architecture (Distribution A schemas, Apache-2.0 API, BSD-3 integrity library)
commercial compute (laptop/NUC, OCI containers, cloud CI for non-CUI regression)
open standards (ASPN 2023, pntOS-C, NMEA 0183, DHS Resilient PNT Conformance Framework v2.0 behaviours)

build_plan.work: Customer-discovery sprint runs in parallel with engineering for the whole plan. Engineering: generate ASPN 2023 codecs from the YAML model; stand up the pntOS-C plugin skeleton (Meson wrap); define the internal event model and the replay format; download TEXBAT and Jammertest 2025; build the GNSS-SDR pipeline that converts TEXBAT RF to observables. Business: retain counsel for the eligibility/CUI memo; contact NAVWAR Small Business Office, NavalX, Open-PNT/ISTO community; list likely NP004 bidders and civil/allied maritime operators.

Implement per-source health monitors (K2) on the PNT-Integrity check structure: C/N0-AGC anomaly, clock-drift/holdover, RAIM residuals, position/velocity jump, INS-GNSS divergence. Build the synthetic scenario generator with 10 strait-transit vignettes and ground truth. Order and bench the COTS stack in the shielded enclosure. Recruit the fractional PNT-integrity engineer and the former-watchstander advisor.

Implement composite confidence/consensus (K3) and the explainable classifier (K4) with attributed evidence; first evaluation report on held-out synthetic and TEXBAT/Jammertest data; iterate on calibration. Run the fallback-policy workshop with the watchstander advisor to produce the configurable TTP schema and a sample table (customer-owned content).

Implement fallback recommender (K5), audit/replay (K6) and the streaming API; build the thin ECDIS-style demo window; conducted-RF bench demo with gps-sdr-sim/bladeRF into the receivers. Freeze the pre-registered operator-study protocol; recruit 6-8 former ETV/QM/navigators. Show a private build to 2-3 candidate integrators for feedback (kill-criterion checkpoint 1).

Run the operator study; harden the container (non-root, SBOM, zero egress, size/footprint targets); regression suite over the full scenario library; write the evaluation report. Present at a NavalX/Tech Bridge or ION-type venue; pursue an evaluation agreement/LOI with an integrator or a civil/allied operator.

Buffer and decision month: publish the reference-plugin package (conformance tests, sample streams) to the Open-PNT community as credibility; finalise go/no-go against the kill criteria; if go, prepare the next-cycle NAVWAR open-topic / D2P2 / OT proposal or the subcontract SOW with an awardee.

kill_criteria: By month 4: fewer than 3 substantive technical conversations with likely NP004 bidders, the GPNTS integrator, or allied/civil fusion-engine houses, or none expresses intent to evaluate the plugin -> stop (no buyer signal)
By month 6: no written evaluation agreement, teaming LOI, CRADA path, or paid civil/allied pilot term sheet -> stop or pivot; do not continue on 'interest'

By month 6: the fractional PNT-integrity engineer and the former Navy watchstander are not engaged (paid) -> stop; without them the product is a dashboard (score file: reject if not recruited within six months)

Technical: held-out classification accuracy < 80% or false-alert rate > 4 per 24 h on clean data after month 5 tuning -> the engine is not differentiated; stop or reduce to a services offer without venture framing
Operator study shows no measurable improvement (time-to-correct-fallback not better than baseline at n >= 6) -> the awareness thesis fails for this design

Counsel memo concludes no compliant structure exists for SBIR AND no OT/CSO sponsor is found by month 9 AND no civil/allied paying pilot -> stop (eligibility plus single-customer dependence, the score file's killer risk)

Within 18 months: no funded Navy Phase II/OT (or subcontract on one) with GPNTS ICDs in hand, no scheduled PNTAX/fleet demonstration, and no paying civil/allied pilot -> stop (score file's stated stop rule)

capital_map.does_250k_reach_next_fundable_milestone: YES for Stages 0 and 1 (combined $85k-$190k, typically ~$130k), which is the next FUNDABLE milestone for this borderline opportunity: a validated, standards-conformant assurance engine with an auditable evaluation report and operator-study evidence, PLUS the result of the buyer test (a written evaluation agreement/LOI from an NP004 awardee, the GPNTS integrator, an OT/CSO sponsor, or a paying civil/allied operator). $250k leaves $60k-$165k of runway to keep two founders alive for 3-6 more months while converting that LOI into a funded agreement. $250k does NOT reach Stage 2 (credible field demonstration, $250k-$600k) on its own and does not approach Stage 3 ($0.8M-$2.5M); those require a seed round, an SBIR/OT award, or a subcontract. Important honesty: the milestone that justifies $2-5M of outside capital (score file) is Stage 3's funded Navy Phase II/OT or subcontract with GPNTS ICDs in hand plus one paying civil/allied pilot and a counsel-cleared cap table - $250k buys the evidence needed to get there, not the milestone itself. If Stage 1 ends without a buyer signal, the honest outcome is a services/licensing business or a shutdown, not a venture.

engineering_risks.risk: Overlapping failure signatures (slow spoof pull-off vs INS bias ramp vs clock fault) make the classifier ambiguous and the composite confidence miscalibrated.
engineering_risks.mitigation: Design K2 as physics-based per-source tests (C/N0-AGC, clock bounds, IMU-propagated position bounds) and K3 as cross-source consensus; report calibration curves in the demo on held-out TEXBAT/Jammertest and synthetic data; the demo's evaluation report makes the ambiguity measurable instead of hidden.

engineering_risks.risk: Domain shift: public and synthetic data do not contain real military threat signatures (classified per GAO), so field performance is unknown.
engineering_risks.mitigation: Ship a documented retune/recalibration procedure and a replay harness so a government team can re-validate on its own data post-award; keep rule/likelihood structure inspectable; the demo shows the harness working on two unrelated data sets (TEXBAT vs Jammertest) as a proxy for shift.

engineering_risks.risk: Standards drift: ASPN stewardship reportedly moving to the ISTO consortium (2026, MEDIUM); pntOS-C is a young repo (10 commits at fetch); the government message set is gated.
engineering_risks.mitigation: Generate codecs from the YAML model so schema updates are mechanical; isolate all schema-facing code in K1; participate in the Open-PNT community; the demo proves 'unchanged engine, swapped stream'.

engineering_risks.risk: GPL contamination from GNSS-SDR or OpenCPN into the proprietary engine.
engineering_risks.mitigation: Run GPL tools as separate processes with file/stream boundaries; license audit in Stage 1 legal line; the container image documents its SBOM.

engineering_risks.risk: RF legality: any radiated GNSS-band test signal is illegal; a bench mistake could end the company.
engineering_risks.mitigation: Conducted-only injection inside a shielded enclosure with attenuators and dummy loads; written lab procedure; real over-the-air exposure only in authority-controlled arenas (Jammertest-type) or aboard a partner operator in advisory-listed regions, recording only.

engineering_risks.risk: Operator study is underpowered or biased (small n, founders facilitating).
engineering_risks.mitigation: Pre-register the protocol with the watchstander advisor, counterbalance scenario order, n >= 6, report effect sizes and confidence intervals; treat a null result as a kill signal, not something to explain away.

engineering_risks.risk: The thin demo HMI becomes the product by accident, recreating the absorbable 'dashboard'.
engineering_risks.mitigation: Keep the HMI in a separate repo with a public API contract; sell and demo the plugin to integrators first; the demo's third segment (bench receivers, no HMI, API output only) proves the engine stands alone.

engineering_risks.risk: Integration burden per customer turns the company into a consultancy (score file's warning).
engineering_risks.mitigation: Adapter-only customer code in K1; price adapters as NRE and the core as a license; the Stage 1 conformance test suite lets integrators self-integrate.

engineering_risks.risk: Eligibility/CUI: the non-U.S.-person co-founder cannot touch government data or the gated ASPN message set; SBIR ownership/control test unresolved.

gtm.title: Unified assured-PNT operational awareness and decision support (single pane for source health, composite confidence, jam/spoof triage, fallback recommendation) with a formation-level PNT interference picture feeding the C2/EW COP
gtm.version_designed_for: NARROWER VERSION per G04-score.json (verdict: borderline). This plan is designed ONLY for the vendor-neutral composite-assurance engine: an ASPN 2023 / pntOS-C-conformant plug-in that ingests 3-8 heterogeneous PNT sources, emits per-source health, composite confidence with attributed evidence, explainable fault/jam/spoof classification and a fallback recommendation, plus a synthetic scenario generator and a replay/audit library validated against public recordings (TEXBAT-type) and DHS Resilient PNT Conformance Framework v2.0 behaviors. It is NOT designed for the single-pane HMI as the product (a thin demo HMI is only a window onto the engine) and NOT for the formation-level PNT interference picture / EW COP feed (killed in the score file as classified-adjacent and NGC2-absorbable). Every milestone below tests the decisive doubt from the score file: does a named buyer with a budget line or vehicle exist for this software layer, and can this founding team lawfully reach it? Honest framing: until a Phase II/OT or Phase III appears, this is a credibility-and-evidence path with SBIR-scale money (single-digit $M), not yet a venture-scale company.

links.value: Shipboard navigation watchstanders monitor several fragmented GPS/INS/GPNTS/alternate-source displays and must manually infer hardware fault vs jamming vs spoofing and pick a fallback, with no composite confidence, explainable rationale or audit trail.
links.detail: FACT: Navy CSO open topic DON26BX05-NP004 text and Q&A state operators 'interact with multiple interfaces and data sources', that this 'fragmented environment increases cognitive workload... and slows decision-making', and that success metrics are speed to decision during an anomaly, threat comprehension accuracy and correct fallback selection (topic posted 2026-08-05; Q&A 2026-08-08 to 2026-09-01, read via mirror in the G04 card). OPNAVINST 9420.1C 5.a(11) (2019-09-30) has required operator degradation indication and interference reporting to electronic support since 2019.

money_map.weakest_link: BUDGET (and, tied to it, CONTRACT VEHICLE). The buyer chain from problem to program office is now verified end-to-end - PMW/A 170 exists, owns GPNTS, and has bought PNT situational-awareness software at SBIR scale twice (2024/2025 BlueRISC, 2026 NP004) - but no program budget line, Phase III, ECP or production award for this software layer is evidenced; the only open vehicle closed on 2026-09-23; and the sole path into the fielded system runs through Raytheon's software-support IDIQ, which the founders cannot access directly.
money_map.penalty_note: Major penalty retained from the score file. Evidenced money is SBIR caps plus one $750K Phase II; IDIQ ceilings ($452.85M hardware) must not be read as software demand; a prototype award (BlueRISC Phase II) is not deployment; and the pattern Phase I -> Phase II -> new open topic without a production step is the proto-purgatory GAO described. The plan below is therefore structured to produce evidence quickly and to kill quickly: if no named PMW 170 or NP004-awardee counterpart engages by week 12, and no second vehicle (IWRP/CRADA/D2P2/civil pilot) is in motion by month 9, the company should not raise venture money on this opportunity.

procurement_signal.rationale: Upgraded from the card's 'Emerging' on new evidence: the program office has now issued repeated prototype solicitations for this software layer (2024 Phase I -> 2025 Phase II $750K -> 2026 broader CSO open topic with multiple Phase I awards planned), the host system is in hardware production (2021 IDIQ) with a software-support prime whose ceiling was exhausted early by 'emergent fleet needs', and open interfaces (ASPN/pntOS) became public in 2026. But there is no follow-on-to-production step for any awareness/decision-support software, no budget line, and the assurance determination problem is still called 'an active research area' by GAO. The five-year sequence is RFI (policy 2019) -> prototype award (2024) -> follow-on (Phase II 2025) -> repeat prototype solicitation (2026), which is the signature of Prototyping, not Transitioning. Confidence MEDIUM; the NDIA PMW 170 brief that would settle the transition question was blocked.

PNTAX requires a government sponsor and may involve classified threat conditions - U.S.-person staff only. None of this is a legal judgment; counsel must clear the structure before any self-certification.

questions: Walk me through the last time you saw a GPS or navigation-source anomaly on watch: what did you see first, on which display, and what did you do in the first 60 seconds?
Which indicators did you actually look at to decide whether it was a hardware fault, jamming or spoofing, and in what order? What did you ignore?
How did you decide which fallback to use (alternate source, INS-only, celestial/radar/DR), and who had to agree before you shifted?
What did you write in the navigation workbook or report afterwards, and who, if anyone, received the interference information (EW cell, IWC, NAVCEN, fleet)?
Show me, on a whiteboard, every display and panel you monitor during a contested-strait transit and which system each belongs to.
When GPNTS or a receiver reports 'degraded', how much do you trust it, and what have you seen it get wrong?
Tell me about a time the team disagreed about whether you were being spoofed; how was it resolved and how long did it take?
If you had to explain to the CO after the fact why you shifted sources at 0213, what evidence would you want to be able to pull up?
How were you trained on jam/spoof triage, and what parts of the training did not match what you saw at sea?
For the program-office and engineering roles: walk me through how a new software capability gets onto GPNTS today, from idea to fleet install, and where it usually stalls.
What did the last GPNTS situational-awareness effort deliver, and what would you need to see from a vendor-neutral assurance component before you would let it sit under your display?
For the pntOS/ASPN roles: walk me through how a third-party plug-in is accepted into the ecosystem and tested, and what integrity or assurance messages you wish plug-ins emitted.
For commercial masters: walk me through your last GPS-disruption transit, what your company's disruption plan told you to do, and what you actually reported to NAVCEN or your DPA.
Which of your current tools or vendors would you expect to add this kind of composite confidence next, and why haven't they?
What would make you stop trusting an automated fallback recommendation, and what would it take to earn that trust back?

first_deployment_path.path: Two-track. Track A (government, evidence): become the assurance-engine component inside an NP004 Phase I awardee's prototype (or inside the incumbent SBIR vendor's follow-on) so that the engine runs on GPNTS-furnished ICD data in their Phase I/II, then demonstrate it at an ANTX/NICE event or JNC 2027 and, through an NIWC Pacific CRADA, on a NIWC lab GPNTS string. Track B (paying, unclassified): a pilot on 2-5 commercial vessels of one operator with routine Red Sea/Baltic transits (or one allied navy training/hydrographic vessel), consuming NMEA/IEC 61162 receiver telemetry plus INS, running the same engine air-gapped on bridge hardware, producing real interference recordings and audit logs. Track B is the first deployment the founders control; Track A is the one the Navy will credit.
first_deployment_path.evidence_it_produces: For a Navy Phase II/D2P2 or OT: measured detection latency, classification accuracy and false-alert rate on both synthetic and real recordings; an operator study against the Navy's own NP004 metrics (speed to decision, threat comprehension accuracy, correct fallback selection) with former ETVs/QMs; a conformant ASPN/pntOS plug-in exercised on a lab GPNTS string (CRADA); a demonstration record at ANTX/JNC. For a seed/Series A or STRATFI-equivalent (Navy has no branded STRATFI; analog is Phase II sequential/enhancement funding): one paying pilot with renewal, a government-funded Phase II or OT (or a subcontract on one), a named transition owner in PMW 170, and a counsel-cleared U.S.-person-controlled cap table. For DIU-style production: a fielded pilot on a government platform with an ATO path (RAISE/OSA container) - not reachable inside 12 months by public evidence.
alternatives: Army route: pntOS plug-in accepted by C5ISR Center and run at PNTAX (annual, WSMR) under a government sponsor - requires a sponsor and U.S.-person staff for threat data; longer path, larger fleet of MAPS/DAPS hosts.
Prime's demo: offer the engine to Raytheon's GPNTS software support team as a candidate ECP component; yields ICD access but risks becoming a work-for-hire feature with no data rights.

NATO DIANA 2026/2027 cohort (Electromagnetic Resilience / Data-Assisted Decision Making challenges; 150 companies selected from 3,600+ in 2026) - allied test-centre access and a non-U.S. funding line; German entity may be required.
DHS/CISA critical-infrastructure timing pilot under the Resilient PNT Conformance Framework v2.0 - civil, unclassified, but a different product variant (cloud-tolerant, single-receiver).

allied_extension.bigger_with_allies: Moderately bigger and materially de-risking, but not transformative in evidenced dollars. Allies face harsher real-world interference (Baltic, Black Sea, Eastern Mediterranean, Red Sea) and have no citizenship gate on an unclassified, EAR-only engine; NATO DIANA explicitly solicits 'Electromagnetic Resilience' (sensing, navigation, data link in contested EMS) and 'Data-Assisted Decision Making' (E06-F1, 2026 cohort); Project Overmatch's Five Eyes arrangement gives a coalition C2 context; and the German founder's network is a real asset in Germany. No allied program of record for a PNT awareness/decision layer was verified this session - Public evidence insufficient - so allied demand is INFERENCE/MEDIUM, and allied revenue is plausible only for the unclassified operator/assurance layer, never for aggregated threat pictures (DoDI 4650.08 transfer limits; coalition releasability unresolved).
allied_extension.what_changes: (1) Product must stay EAR-only and vendor-neutral (public ASPN YAML, NMEA/IEC 61162, S-52/BAM-compatible outputs) with no U.S.-CUI-derived signatures in the allied build - two code trains (U.S. CUI build vs releasable build) from day one. (2) Corporate structure: a U.S. Inc. for DoD plus a possible German GmbH for EDF/DIANA/Bundeswehr work; E06-F38 says single-jurisdiction structuring is lossy in every direction and counsel must map ITAR deemed-export, EDF/EDIP control and German clearance rules against the first customer. (3) Interfaces multiply: each navy runs different fusion engines and ECDIS suppliers, so the ASPN plug-in plus a small adapter set is the only scalable form. (4) Evidence base improves: allied and commercial recordings of real interference feed the scenario library, which is the moat. (5) Timing: DIANA application windows are annual; JNC 2027 and European Navigation Conference are the venues.
