most_important_question.build_first: Build the assurance engine, not the screen: an ASPN 2023 / pntOS-C-conformant integrity service, packaged as an air-gapped OCI container, that consumes a synthetic strait-transit scenario generator (3-8 sources at 1-10 Hz: GNSS jamming onset, spoofing pull-off, INS drift, clock holdover, hardware fault) and emits per-source health, composite confidence with attributed evidence, an explainable fault/jam/spoof classification, a fallback recommendation with rationale, and a replayable audit timeline - validated against held-out synthetic scenarios, public real recordings (TEXBAT-type) and DHS Resilient PNT Conformance Framework v2.0 Respond/Recover behaviors. Add a thin ECDIS-style demo HMI only as a window onto the engine, and publish a reference plug-in subset to the Open-PNT community so the engine becomes the thing others plug into. Budget: roughly $80K over 90 days and $100-150K over 4-5 months, within founder capital.
most_important_question.show_it_to: In order: (1) NP004 Phase I awardees as soon as selections post (~Q1-Q2 2027) and the incumbent SBIR vendor (BlueRISC, whose $750K GPNTS SA Tool Phase II ended 2026-05-25) - as a component supplier; (2) the PMW/A 170 GPNTS office (NP004 TPOC via the NAVWAR Small Business Office) and the NIWC Pacific GPNTS/Raytheon software-support engineers - as the candidate for the next open-topic cycle, a D2P2 or a GPNTS ECP, via a CRADA; (3) the Open-PNT / ISTO ASPN community and Army C5ISR Center pntOS engineers - as a reference plug-in; (4) one commercial operator with Red Sea/Baltic transits or one allied navy officer - as an unclassified paid pilot; (5) JNC 2027 (2027-06-07 to 06-10, Covington KY) as the single public venue where all of the above are in one room.
most_important_question.demo_proves: Against the Navy's own NP004 metrics: detection latency under 1 s at 1-10 Hz; correct fault/jam/spoof classification on held-out synthetic and public real recordings with a quantified false-alert rate (targets: >=90% classification accuracy on synthetic, >=80% on public real recordings, <5% false alerts); former watchstanders reach the correct fallback measurably faster and with fewer errors than with fragmented displays (n>=6 operator study); every recommendation carries an evidence chain and can be replayed for after-action review; and the same container consumes an ASPN/pntOS stream unchanged, so a Phase II can swap in GPNTS ICDs without rework.
most_important_question.why_customer_cares: PMW 170 wrote the problem in its own words (NP004, 2026-08-05) and has now paid for PNT situational-awareness software at least twice (2024 Phase I, 2025 Phase II $750K) and re-solicited it more broadly in 2026 with multiple awards planned, so it is not satisfied with what it has; OPNAVINST 9420.1C 5.a(11) has required degradation indication and interference reporting since 2019 and systems that cannot comply must seek waivers; the GPNTS software-support ceiling was exhausted early by 'emergent fleet needs'; GPS denial is routine (12 DoD interference tests in Aug-Sep 2026 per NAVCEN; MARAD 2026-008 global advisory) and M-code remains late in all three segments (GAO-24-106841, 2024-09-09); and every Phase I awardee will need validated assurance analytics they do not have.
most_important_question.why_incumbent_cant_crush: Honestly, this is a speed-and-evidence defense, not a structural one, which is why the verdict is borderline. What protects the founders: receiver primes (Collins, BAE, L3Harris, Safran) have no incentive to ship vendor-neutral assurance that commoditizes their boxes; Raytheon as GPNTS prime is a systems house on a ceiling-exhausted support contract and has not fielded this layer in seven years; BlueRISC's effort is an AI/ML module tied to GPNTS rather than an open ASPN/pntOS-conformant engine with a scenario/replay library; NGC2/Overmatch integrators lack PNT-integrity depth; and IS4S - the one competitor who could build this - is committed to Army NorthStar (up to $41M, April 2026) and AF design-agent work and may prefer to license a validated component. The founders lose if they build a dashboard; they can hold only if the validated algorithms, the scenario/replay library with real recordings from civil/allied pilots, the operator-study evidence and conformance to open standards make them the reference implementation everyone else plugs in.
most_important_question.milestone_for_next_2_5m: All four within 18 months, or stop: (1) a funded Navy Phase II, D2P2 or OT - or a paid subcontract on one - with GPNTS ICDs in hand and a scheduled fleet, ANTX or PNTAX demonstration; (2) at least one paying unclassified civil or allied pilot with a renewal; (3) a named PMW 170 transition owner and a documented path (ECP, RAISE/OSA container, or Phase III) into GPNTS or pntOS; (4) a counsel-cleared U.S.-person-controlled cap table plus a CMMC Level 2 self-assessment and a CUI enclave. If, at 18 months, the only money is Phase I-scale and the government has taken the layer GOTS or bought it from the standard-setter, the founders should stop - this opportunity's evidenced money is single-digit millions and a $2-5M raise is justified only by a transition owner with a vehicle, not by prototypes.

tech.title: Vendor-neutral DDIL test and conformance harness for tactical software (link emulation, multi-node TAK/CoT sync scoring, pre-Jailbreak API contract tests, TAK plugin RBAC/audit conformance)
tech.version_designed_for: NARROWER VERSION ONLY. G29 was KILLED as a venture (G29-score.json verdict 'kill', confidence HIGH: no requirement owner, program office, budget line or vehicle; the government resources DDIL test and conformance itself through C5ISR Center Radio Rodeo / NetModX, ATEC and the APG/Huntsville software integration labs, and - new this session - the Reveille Forge Integrated Development Environment opened in July 2026 (Breaking Defense 2026-07, FACT/MEDIUM)). This diligence therefore designs the residual form named in the score file: an OPEN-SOURCE 'TAK DDIL bench' (containerised ATAK-CIV / TAK Server nodes behind Linux tc/netem or EMANE/CORE link profiles from 1 Mbps to 1 kbps with scripted partitions and reconnect storms, a sync scorer, a CoT/TAK Mission API and public-Lattice-schema contract-test CLI) plus an ATAK plugin RBAC/audit/SBOM conformance module that emits a signed OSCAL-style bundle. It is sized at $30-60k and 3-4 months, is explicitly a credibility and validation asset and a small fixed-fee readiness service, NOT a venture-scale company, and every plan and milestone below is built to TEST the decisive doubt: does a named sponsor with a budget line or vehicle exist (PdM Application Store and Pipeline under PM C2 Applications, DEVCOM C5ISR Center, ATEC, Reveille Forge, a Team Anduril / Team Lockheed T&E cell, TAK Product Center, or paying Jailbreak-series vendors) within 90 days of first demo? If the kill criteria trip, the founders stop at the open-source release, keep the relationships and put the remaining capital elsewhere. Nothing here is a legal determination on ITAR/EAR/FOCI/SBIR/immigration; constraints are described for counsel.

architecture.prose: INPUTS. Three input classes enter the bench: (1) a scenario file (YAML) that declares a link profile - bandwidth from 1 Mbps down to 1 kbps as in the DARPA FLUID regime (darpa.mil 2025-03-28, FACT/HIGH), latency, jitter, loss, and a timed schedule of partitions and reconnect storms across a named node topology; (2) synthetic traffic - a CoT generator that emits position, chat, markers, mission-data-sync objects and simulated sensor tracks (MAVLink-derived UAS positions from ArduPilot SITL converted to CoT), with a ground-truth ledger of every object, its priority tag and emission time; (3) the system under test (SUT) - a vendor's ATAK plugin APK, a CoT feed/gateway, a TAK Server Mission API client, or a Lattice SDK client exercised against the free Lattice Sandbox (developer.anduril.com sandboxes page, FACT/HIGH that sandboxes exist; licence terms not retrievable this session - EGRESS_BLOCKED). Public schemas (CoT XML event schema, TAK Protocol Version 1 protobuf, TAK Server Marti REST / Mission API documentation, Lattice protobufs on the Buf Schema Registry) and role/tag fixtures (synthetic users, roles and data tags) are the fourth input. COMPUTE. The whole bench runs on one commodity x86 host (mini PC or workstation, 32-64 GB RAM) running Docker/Podman: TAK Server containers, ATAK-CIV in Android emulators (x86_64 system images) or on a handful of physical Android phones via ADB, a netem/tc controller (or, for MANET-style topologies, an EMANE + CORE node), a capture/ledger service, the scorer and the report builder. Cloud is optional (a single large VM) for parallel runs. CORE SOFTWARE. Six modules: (a) Scenario Runner - translates the YAML into per-link tc/netem qdiscs (or EMANE event-service commands) on the container network namespaces and executes the partition schedule with wall-clock precision; (b) Traffic Generator and Ledger - emits CoT with unique IDs, priority tags and timestamps into the source nodes and records ground truth; (c) Multi-node Sync Scorer - captures what each ATAK-CIV/TAK Server node actually received (via TAK Server logs, Marti API queries and an instrumented observer plugin on the emulators) and computes time-to-arrival of priority objects, duplicates and conflicting versions after reconnect, missing objects, ordering violations and offered load versus link capacity during the reconnect storm; (d) Contract-Test Engine - drives OpenAPI-based property tests (Schemathesis-style) against a vendor's Mission API usage and buf/protobuf breaking-change and lint checks against Lattice protos, from a capture or spec; (e) Plugin Conformance Module - installs the plugin on emulator nodes, drives it with Appium/ADB scripts under synthetic roles and tagged data, and produces an RBAC matrix (which role could see/do what), an audit-event coverage table (which security-relevant actions produced a log entry, mapped to a NIST SP 800-53 AU-2-style list), a static-permission/manifest review and an SBOM (CycloneDX via Syft); (f) Report/Bundle Signer - renders HTML/JSON and an OSCAL assessment-results-style JSON bundle, signs it with Sigstore cosign. INTERFACES. CoT over TLS (TAK Server streaming port) and TAK Protocol v1 protobuf; TAK Server Marti REST / Mission API; Lattice gRPC/REST against the sandbox; Linux tc/netem via netlink and the EMANE event API; ADB/Appium to Android nodes; OSCAL, CycloneDX/SPDX and JSON out. OUTPUTS. A scored, reproducible report per run; a signed OSCAL-style conformance bundle; an SBOM; and an anonymised comparative leaderboard across SUTs. USERS. Vendor integration engineers preparing for a Jailbreak-series sprint or PdM ASaP onboarding; prime and government T&E engineers who need comparable pre-event numbers; and AO/ISSM reviewers who consume the RBAC/audit bundle. Everything is unclassified by construction; realism plateaus at 'generic DDIL' unless a lab supplies controlled waveform models or traces, which would require U.S.-person handling (constraint for counsel).

An external definition of 'conformant' does not exist today; the Army AO memo (2025-09, RECALL/MEDIUM) and NIST SP 800-53 AU/AC families are the only public anchors for the RBAC/audit rubric, so the rubric must be labelled as the bench's own until a government body endorses one.
architecture.hardest_problem: Making a synthetic, netem-driven score MEAN something to the people who own acceptance. Technically the hardest sub-problem is faithful, reproducible multi-node reconciliation scoring: attributing every CoT object observed on every node to a ground-truth emission across partitions and reconnect storms (object IDs re-used, stale-time semantics, mission-sync versus streaming paths, emulator clock drift, TAK Server's own dedupe and stale handling) so that 'duplicate', 'conflict', 'late' and 'lost' are counted identically run to run and match what a soldier would see. netem models bandwidth/latency/loss on a point-to-point link but not MANET dynamics (routing churn, hidden nodes, half-duplex contention), so the bench must be honest that it measures application behaviour under specified link states, not radio behaviour - EMANE/CORE narrows but does not close this gap without controlled waveform models. The non-technical half of the hardest problem dominates: no government body has said what a passing score is, and until one does the report is an opinion. That is why every milestone below tests sponsor existence, not feature completeness.

must_be_proprietary: Nothing needs to be closed for the design to work; the score file's finding is that any proprietary layer is replicable in weeks by Anduril, TAK Product Center, Ditto or a lab. The only assets worth holding privately (as know-how, not code) are: the curated scenario library calibrated against whatever real-exercise anecdotes the T&E advisor can share; the scoring rubric weights and the RBAC/audit checklist mapping to AO expectations; and the anonymised cross-vendor results dataset. Even these should be published in part, because openness is the credibility mechanism for this narrower version.

performance_metrics.metric: Scenario reproducibility (coefficient of variation of headline scores across 3 identical runs)
performance_metrics.target: < 5% CV on time-to-arrival P95 and exact match on duplicate/conflict counts
performance_metrics.why: A score nobody can reproduce is an anecdote; reproducibility is the only differentiator against 'fixing the code live at Ivy Sting' (DVIDS 2026-03-30)

performance_metrics.metric: Link fidelity (configured vs measured throughput, latency and loss per link)
performance_metrics.target: within 10% of configured values from 1 Mbps to 1 kbps; partitions start within 1 s of schedule
performance_metrics.why: The DARPA FLUID 1 Mbps-1 kbps regime (2025-03-28) is the public DDIL definition buyers recognise; the bench must demonstrably hit it

performance_metrics.metric: Time-to-arrival of priority CoT objects after reconnect (P50/P95 per node)
performance_metrics.target: measured to +/-1 s across all nodes; report, do not prescribe, since no government threshold exists
performance_metrics.why: This is the number a commander feels ('lag under denied conditions', G29 current_workflow step 4) and the one a lab could compare across 50-80 vendors

performance_metrics.metric: Duplicate and conflicting objects after reconnect (per 1,000 ground-truth objects)
performance_metrics.target: zero false positives in the ledger; SUT results reported as raw counts
performance_metrics.why: Duplicate tracks after reconnect are a classic sync failure that TAK Server dedupe, mission sync and vendor feeds each handle differently

performance_metrics.metric: Object loss and ordering violations under a 30-minute partition at 4 kbps
performance_metrics.target: complete accounting of every ledger object (delivered / late / lost / superseded)
performance_metrics.why: Shows whether a feed degrades gracefully or silently drops data, which today is discovered only at events

performance_metrics.metric: Reconnect saturation (peak offered load / link capacity during the first 60 s after reconnect)
performance_metrics.target: reported as a ratio with time series; flag > 1.0 sustained > 10 s
performance_metrics.why: Reconnect storms are what break real tactical links; vendors rarely script them (G29 current_workflow step 2)

performance_metrics.target: 10 ATAK-CIV emulator nodes + 2 TAK Servers on a 64 GB host without emulator starvation
performance_metrics.why: A bench a vendor can run on one machine before a sprint is the entire value proposition

performance_metrics.target: < 15 minutes from YAML to a running scenario; full 30-minute scenario plus report in < 45 minutes
performance_metrics.why: Pre-sprint engineers will not adopt a bench that takes a day to configure

performance_metrics.target: 100% of the Mission API / Lattice endpoints the SUT actually calls are exercised; schema-level lint/breaking checks pass or list violations
performance_metrics.why: Undocumented or misused APIs were a top Jailbreak failure class (DefenseScoop 2026-05-29)

performance_metrics.target: every declared role x action pair tested; percent of security-relevant actions producing an audit record, mapped to a NIST SP 800-53 AU-2-style list
performance_metrics.why: Missing access control and logging were the AO's stated reason for the 'very high risk' NGC2 rating (CNBC 2025-10-03, RECALL/MEDIUM)

performance_metrics.target: OSCAL-style JSON validates against schema; cosign signature verifies; SBOM lists 100% of plugin dependencies detected by Syft
performance_metrics.why: ISSMs and pipeline owners need machine-checkable evidence, not PDFs

mvp.demo: A single-host, Dockerised 'TAK DDIL bench' demonstrated live and published on GitHub: 8-10 ATAK-CIV nodes (emulators plus 2-4 physical phones) and two TAK Servers behind netem profiles stepping from 1 Mbps to 4 kbps, a scripted 30-minute partition and reconnect storm, three public/open-source ATAK plugins and one synthetic UAS CoT feed run through the same scenario, producing side-by-side scored reports (time-to-arrival, duplicates/conflicts, loss, saturation); a contract-test CLI run against the same feed's Mission API usage and, if the Lattice licence permits, a Lattice sandbox client; and the plugin conformance module run against one open-source plugin to emit a signed OSCAL-style RBAC/audit/SBOM bundle. The demo is shown to (1) three or four MatrixSpace/Adyton-class vendors facing the next Jailbreak-series or PdM ASaP onboarding date, (2) a C5ISR Center or ATEC T&E contact via a NetModX / Reveille Forge / xTech application, and (3) a Team Anduril or Team Lockheed T&E engineer - and the demo's success criterion is a sponsor signal, not applause.
must_prove: That an independent, reproducible score (CV < 5% across repeated runs) exposes concrete failure classes - arrival delay, duplicate tracks after reconnect, silent loss, reconnect saturation, missing audit events - in real plugins and feeds BEFORE an event, matching the failure types reported from Jailbreak and Ivy Sting
That the bench runs end to end on one commodity machine in under 45 minutes per scenario, so a vendor engineer would actually use it in the week before a sprint

That the RBAC/audit bundle is machine-checkable (schema-valid OSCAL-style JSON, verified signature, complete SBOM) and that at least one ISSM/AO-adjacent reviewer says it is the shape of evidence they would accept

DECISIVE: that at least one named party with money or a vehicle - a vendor paying a fixed fee, PdM ASaP / PM C2 Applications, C5ISR Center, ATEC, Reveille Forge, TAK Product Center, or a prime T&E cell - commits in writing to use the report (paid readiness run, CRADA, evaluation agreement, task-order intent or pipeline inclusion) within 90 days of the first demo

build_plan.work: Set up TAK Server containers and 4 ATAK-CIV emulator nodes; implement the netem scenario runner with YAML link profiles (1 Mbps, 256 kbps, 64 kbps, 16 kbps, 4 kbps, 1 kbps) and partition scheduler; build the CoT traffic generator with ground-truth ledger (pytak/takproto); engage counsel (formation, EAR self-classification, technology control plan, copyleft review); start 90-day sponsor discovery: 15 outreach conversations targeted at Jailbreak-participant vendors, PdM ASaP / PM C2 Applications, C5ISR Center NetModX, ATEC industry-partner programme (NDM 2026-07-24), Reveille Forge, TAK Product Center.

Observer plugin on ATAK-CIV nodes; capture/ledger service and first sync scorer (time-to-arrival, loss, duplicates); scale to 8-10 nodes plus 2-4 physical phones; reproducibility runs (3x) and link-fidelity calibration; publish repo v0.1 with a 5-minute video; first three vendor demos; submit NetModX persistent-experimentation / Reveille Forge / xTech applications.

Contract-test CLI (Schemathesis against Mission API usage; buf lint/breaking against Lattice protos; Pact for CoT gateways); plugin conformance module v0.1 (Appium role drive, RBAC matrix, audit-event coverage, Syft SBOM, OSCAL-style bundle, cosign); run three open-source plugins and a synthetic UAS feed through the reference scenario; publish anonymised comparative results; demo to one prime T&E engineer and one government lab contact; ask each for a written statement of what evidence they would accept.

Harden: one-command install, 45-minute end-to-end run, docs; optional EMANE/CORE mode for a 3-hop topology; first paid fixed-fee readiness run if a vendor signs ($5-15k); decision gate against kill criteria; if a sponsor exists, scope Stage 2 (adapter for Lattice or Ditto, event slot); if not, freeze as a maintained open-source project and stop spending.

(Only if month-4 gate passes) Lattice or Ditto adapter, second scenario family (division-to-battalion multi-server federation), CRADA/evaluation-agreement paperwork with the sponsor, NIST SP 800-171 self-assessment planning if CUI is in prospect.

(Only if gate passed) Field-adjacent demonstration at the sponsor's venue or a NetModX / Reveille Forge slot with commercial radios in the loop; publish the sponsor-endorsed rubric; decide whether the residual business is a service line or a joinable team (acqui-hire / prime T&E subcontract).

kill_criteria: By day 45: fewer than 10 substantive conversations with target buyers (Jailbreak-participant vendors, PdM ASaP / PM C2 Applications, C5ISR Center, ATEC, Reveille Forge, TAK Product Center, prime T&E) or none of them names a budget, pipeline step or vehicle through which a third-party DDIL/conformance report could be consumed -> stop building beyond the open-source v0.1

By day 90 after first demo: no vendor has paid a fixed fee (>= $5,000) for a readiness run AND no government or prime party has signed a CRADA, evaluation agreement, task-order intent or pipeline-inclusion letter -> freeze the project as an open-source credibility asset; do not raise or spend further
By month 4: the bench cannot achieve < 5% CV reproducibility or < 10% link fidelity across 1 Mbps-1 kbps on one host -> the technical premise (a comparable score) fails; stop

At any point: a government body (C5ISR Center, TAK Product Center, PdM ASaP, Anduril for Lattice) publishes an equivalent open bench or declares its own report the only accepted evidence -> stop and contribute upstream instead

At any point: counsel finds the Lattice SDK licence prohibits third-party benchmarking/publication or the TAK Server/ATAK-CIV copyleft terms make the intended open-source release non-viable -> drop the affected module; if both, reassess whether any residual asset remains
Total spend cap: $60,000 excluding founder stipends before a signed sponsor exists; exceeding it without a sponsor is itself a kill

capital_map.does_250k_reach_next_fundable_milestone: YES, with a large margin - but the binding constraint is not money. Stages 0 and 1 together cost $38k-$84k (typically about $60k including stipends), which is the next milestone: a published, reproducible open-source TAK DDIL bench with a signed conformance bundle PLUS the result of the 90-day sponsor test. $250k would also cover the low end of Stage 2 ($120k-$300k) if a sponsor emerges. However, the score file's verdict is that no requirement owner, budget line or vehicle exists, so the 'fundable' event is not a technical deliverable but an external signal: a paying vendor, a CRADA/evaluation agreement with PdM ASaP, C5ISR Center, ATEC or Reveille Forge, or a prime T&E subcontract. The founders should cap spend at $60k (excluding stipends) until that signal exists, and treat the remaining ~$190k as reserved for a different opportunity. If the signal never comes, $250k does not change the outcome; it only funds a longer consultancy.
capital_map.next_milestone: Published v0.3 bench with reproducible comparative results for 3+ SUTs and one signed OSCAL-style conformance bundle, AND a documented answer to the decisive doubt within 90 days of first demo: either (a) >= 1 paid readiness run (>= $5k) plus >= 1 written government/prime commitment (CRADA, evaluation agreement, pipeline inclusion or task-order intent), which unlocks Stage 2; or (b) neither, which freezes the project as a credibility asset

A sponsor relationship (PdM ASaP / PM C2 Applications, C5ISR Center, ATEC, Reveille Forge, TAK Product Center or a prime T&E cell): not expertise but access; its absence after 90 days is the kill trigger

engineering_risks.risk: netem models point-to-point link states, not MANET radio dynamics (routing churn, contention, half-duplex), so scores may not predict field behaviour
engineering_risks.mitigation: State scope honestly ('application behaviour under specified link states'); add an EMANE/CORE mode with generic models for multi-hop topologies in month 4; calibrate scenarios with the T&E advisor; treat any sponsor-supplied emulation effects as the calibration target in Stage 2

engineering_risks.risk: Android emulators diverge from physical devices (timers, background limits, radio stack), corrupting time-to-arrival and reconnect behaviour
engineering_risks.mitigation: Mix 2-4 physical phones with emulators in every run; report emulator/physical split; measure emulator-vs-phone delta as a bench metric

engineering_risks.risk: Attribution errors in the ledger (CoT UID reuse, stale-time semantics, mission-sync versus streaming paths, TAK Server dedupe) produce false duplicates or losses
engineering_risks.mitigation: Tag every synthetic object with a bench-unique detail attribute plus emission time; validate the scorer against a zero-degradation control run that must score perfect; publish the counting rules

engineering_risks.risk: TAK Server / ATAK-CIV version drift and CIV-vs-GOV/MIL behaviour differences make results non-comparable over time
engineering_risks.mitigation: Pin versions per scenario and embed them in the report; keep a compatibility matrix; state explicitly that GOV/MIL builds are out of scope

engineering_risks.risk: Lattice SDK licence (updated 2026-07-31, terms unverified) may forbid publishing benchmark results or third-party test tooling
engineering_risks.mitigation: Counsel reads the licence before any Lattice work; keep the Lattice module optional and separable; fall back to TAK-only and Ditto adapters

engineering_risks.risk: Copyleft terms of TAK Server / ATAK-CIV may constrain how the bench is packaged and licensed
engineering_risks.mitigation: Keep bench code in separate processes communicating over sockets/APIs; license the bench itself permissively (Apache-2.0) where possible; counsel review before release

engineering_risks.risk: No authoritative definition of 'conformant' for RBAC/audit; the rubric is the founders' opinion and can be dismissed
engineering_risks.mitigation: Anchor every check to a public control (NIST SP 800-53 AU-2/AC-3-style), publish the mapping, and ask an ISSM/AO-adjacent reviewer to critique it in month 3; the demo's purpose is to get a government party to endorse or correct the rubric

engineering_risks.risk: Vendors 'teach to the test' or dispute scores, turning the bench into a liability
engineering_risks.mitigation: Randomise partition timings within declared bounds; publish counting rules; anonymise comparative results; frame outputs as diagnostics, not certification

engineering_risks.risk: Host resource starvation with 10 emulators plus servers skews timing
engineering_risks.mitigation: Cap at the measured node count where CPU steal is < 10%; use a 64 GB host; move to a cloud VM for larger runs; report host utilisation in every run

engineering_risks.risk: Clock alignment across nodes for sub-second time-to-arrival
engineering_risks.mitigation: All emulators share the host clock; physical phones sync via NTP to the host before each run; report residual offset

engineering_risks.risk: Deemed-export or CUI exposure if a lab shares link profiles, waveform models or traces with the non-U.S.-person founder
engineering_risks.mitigation: Technology control plan from month 1: controlled inputs handled only by the U.S.-person advisor/engineer in a segregated enclave; the bench stays synthetic-only until counsel clears anything else

engineering_risks.risk: A government body or platform owner publishes its own bench and the founders' work is stranded
engineering_risks.mitigation: This is an explicit kill criterion; the mitigation is speed to publication (month 2) and contributing upstream so the founders' names travel with the work

engineering_risks.risk: The whole effort produces credibility but no sponsor, and drifts into unpaid support
engineering_risks.mitigation: Hard $60k cap and the 90-day sponsor test; pre-agreed stop decision; treat the asset as a portfolio piece for joining a prime T&E cell, TAK plugin shop or NGC2 sub-vendor

gtm.title: Vendor-neutral DDIL test and conformance harness for tactical software (link emulation, multi-node TAK/CoT sync scoring, pre-Jailbreak API contract tests, TAK plugin RBAC/audit conformance)
gtm.status: KILLED as a venture (G29-score.json verdict: kill, market attractiveness 2.4, founder fit 4.2). This GTM file designs ONLY for the narrower surviving version and is explicitly a credibility-and-validation path, not a company plan.
gtm.version_designed_for: The narrower version named in G29-score.json 'narrower_version_if_borderline': an open-source 'TAK DDIL bench' (Linux netem or NRL EMANE/CORE link profiles from 1 Mbps to 1 kbps, ~8-10 containerised ATAK-CIV/TAK Server nodes, scripted partitions and reconnect storms, a sync-scoring report) plus an ATAK plugin RBAC/audit/SBOM conformance module emitting a signed OSCAL-style bundle, sized at $30-60k and 3-4 months, used (a) to sell a handful of fixed-fee pre-sprint readiness runs to Jailbreak-series vendors, (b) as the entry into a C5ISR Center NetModX persistent-experimentation slot or an xTech hackathon, and (c) as the credibility asset that gets the founders into an NGC2 team-member T&E cell, a prime T&E cell or a TAK plugin shop. No government purchase is expected; any lab adoption is a relationship, not revenue. Every milestone below tests the decisive doubt: does ANY named buyer with a budget line or vehicle exist for a neutral harness? The default expectation, per the score file, is that the answer is no and the 90-day plan ends with a documented kill and a reusable open-source asset.

links.value: Tactical software resilience under DDIL (1 Mbps to 1 kbps, partitions, reconnect storms) and conformance to government-baselined TAK/CoT and NGC2 interfaces plus the Army AO's RBAC/audit expectations are still proven live at in-person events, not by a reproducible pre-event test.

Absence of a competitor in the cross-vendor scoring layer is not evidence of opportunity. entry_sequence.office_or_event: Army FUZE SBIR|STTR / xTech program office (xTechIgnite-style topic competitions; five FUZE funding opportunities posted after the 2026-04-13 reauthorisation); Army Applications Laboratory; DIU CSO (HQ0845-20-S-C001 successor) only if a C2 test-and-evaluation area of interest appears (none found this session); C5 or IWRP-type OTA consortia (membership fees ~$500-2,500/yr, INFERENCE) as a hedge.

entry_sequence.eligibility_notes: FACT: SBIR/STTR requires a small business more than 50% owned and controlled by U.S. citizens or permanent residents (13 CFR 121.702); options and convertibles count as exercised under 13 CFR 121.103; eligibility is self-certified at award with fraud exposure for misstatement (GAO-24-105470). The Indonesian founder's equity never counts and DoD components restrict foreign-national technical participation (AFWERX Open Topic FAQs 2025-07-02) - they cannot be PI on SBIR work. Whether the 2026 reauthorisation (S. 3971) changed the ownership or foreign-ties tests is unverified (HYPOTHESIS/LOW). OTA/CSO: nontraditional-defense-contractor status is automatic for a new company (10 U.S.C. 3014) and there is no ownership test, but agreements officers can impose U.S.-person or CUI terms. Counsel required.
entry_sequence.what_it_yields: If SBIR-eligible: a $150-250k Phase I-scale award (INFERENCE from Army norms; 2026 caps not retrieved) that is the first government dollar for the bench - still not a deployment. If not eligible: a subcontract that pays for adapting the bench to one prime's stack, which is a services engagement, not a product company. Either outcome is compatible only with the 'credibility asset' framing.

entry_sequence.vehicle: Allied lab-tool hedge: TAK ecosystem and NATO/German channels (no U.S. vehicle)
entry_sequence.office_or_event: TAK Offsite 2027 (international participants attend; 2026 edition 2026-08-18/20); NATO CWIX 2027 (expected June 2027 at JFTC Bydgoszcz; 2026 edition 2026-06-08/26; entry only through a national delegation or a system owner); Bundeswehr Cyber Innovation Hub (CIHBw) pilot channel and D-LBO integrators (Rheinmetall, blackned) via the German founder; NATO DIANA 2027 challenge call (2026 cohort had a 'Data Assisted Decision Making' challenge; a DDIL/test challenge is not evidenced - HYPOTHESIS).
entry_sequence.timing: Months 6-18, opportunistic; only if step 2 fails in the U.S. or a German pilot sponsor appears first.
entry_sequence.eligibility_notes: TAK.gov third-party pipeline is open to anyone not on the Denied Parties List. CWIX and DIANA do not screen founder nationality but national security authorities do; a German GmbH would be needed for EDF/EDIP eligibility and would complicate a later U.S. FOCI picture. Dual structures are heavy for a $250k team (E06 founder analysis). Counsel required.
entry_sequence.what_it_yields: Widens the lab-tool niche to allied TAK users without changing its ceiling; produces a second reference lab at most.

questions: Walk me through the last time you prepared a plugin, feed or app for an Army integration event (Jailbreak, Ivy Sting, NetModX, Radio Rodeo): what did you test the week before, on what network, with which tools, and who ran it?

Tell me about the last failure that was discovered live at the event rather than beforehand - what was it (arrival order, duplicates after reconnect, saturation, a firewall or auth surprise, missing audit events), how long did it take to fix, and what did that cost you in fielding time?
How do you today reproduce a degraded link - 4 kbps, 30-minute partition, reconnect storm - in your own lab? Who set that up, and what happened when you tried to make it repeatable across releases?
When the team lead or the government lab tests your component, what do they send back, in what form, and how long after the event? What do you do with that report?
Show me how a new app gets onto the NGC2 data layer or into the API Marketplace from your side: which documents, sandboxes, sign-offs and people are involved, and where does the most waiting happen?

Describe the last time the AO or an ISSM asked for evidence about access control, audit logging or the software bill of materials for a third-party app - who produced it, in what format, and what did they reject?
What did you use Lattice Sandboxes (or the TAK Server test framework, or EMANE/CORE) for in the last month, and what did you have to build around them yourself?
If ATEC's assessment report arrived showing a defect in your component two weeks after the event, walk me through what happens next in your organisation and on the contract.
Who inside your company or team decides that a component is 'ready' for an event, and what evidence do they look at to decide?

Have you ever paid an outside party for test or emulation capability (Keysight, Apposite, iTrinegy, a lab, a consultant)? Tell me about that purchase - who approved it, what budget it came from, and what it replaced.
How many integration or exercise deadlines does your team face in a year, and which of them would a two-week-earlier warning have changed?

In the government lab (C5ISR Center / CJSIL / Huntsville): walk me through how a vendor's component gets scheduled, instrumented and scored today, and what tooling you would refuse to let a vendor bring in.
What data, link profiles or traces would a pre-event test need to be believable to you, and which of those can never leave your lab?
Tell me about the last tool you adopted from outside the lab or the prime - how did it get in, who paid, and what would have stopped it?

first_deployment_path.path: The realistic first 'deployment' is not a government purchase but an ADOPTION: (1) publish the open-source TAK DDIL bench and plugin conformance module; (2) run 3-5 paid or free pre-sprint readiness runs for Jailbreak-series vendors and publish anonymised comparative results; (3) use those results and a former-C5ISR/ATEC advisor to secure a DEVCOM C5ISR Center NetModX persistent-experimentation slot (CRADA, 2027 campaign) or an NGC2 team-member T&E cell agreeing to run the bench before an Ivy Sting / Lightning Surge iteration; (4) bring the bench to the next xTech hackathon and TAK Offsite 2027 as the demonstration artefact. Project Convergence, ANTX, Bold Quest and CWIX are government-run interoperability venues where the bench could only appear inside a participating system owner's delegation, not as its own entry - treat them as later, opportunistic.
first_deployment_path.evidence_it_produces: Evidence for a follow-on decision (not a Series A - the score file rules that out): (a) a reproducible score that predicted, before an event, at least one class of failure later observed live (arrival order, duplicate tracks after reconnect, saturation on reconnect, missing audit events), with vendor attestation; (b) a written statement from a C5ISR Center, ATEC/CJSIL or team-lead T&E engineer that the report was used as pre-event evidence; (c) paid engagements with logos and prices; (d) an NGC2 team-member or prime subcontract or a NetModX CRADA. For a STRATFI/TACFI-style or DIU production step this would still be insufficient - those require a Phase II or CSO prototype award and a program-office transition memo, neither of which has a path here. What the evidence CAN justify is (i) a small services business, (ii) an acqui-hire or hire into a prime/lab T&E cell, or (iii) redeploying the founders and their credibility to a different gap.
alternatives: NGC2 team-lead demo: a Team Anduril or Team Lockheed Martin T&E engineer runs the bench against a team member's component before an Ivy Sting / Lightning Surge iteration (fastest, requires a warm introduction; yields a prime reference, not revenue).

University or ROTC-adjacent unit pilot: a National Guard signal unit or university ROTC exercise runs ATAK-CIV through the bench's scenarios on commercial hardware (cheap, produces soldier feedback, no acquisition standing).
TAK Offsite 2027 demonstration and CivTAK community adoption of the plugin conformance module (produces community usage numbers and TAK Product Center attention; TPC can replicate it).
Allied buyer: a Bundeswehr D-LBO integrator (Rheinmetall/blackned) or a CWIX 2027 national delegation uses the bench in its own lab (produces an allied reference; needs a German entity or partner).
Anduril Lattice / Ditto partner-adapter route: add adapters and seek listing in their developer ecosystems (produces distribution but hands the incumbent the design).

allied_extension.bigger_with_allies: Marginally, not decisively. TAK is used across NATO and the TAK.gov third-party pipeline is open to non-U.S. persons, so a TAK DDIL bench is exportable as a lab tool to allied TAK users; NATO's CWIX (June 2026: ~780 systems, 46 nations) shows allied interoperability testing is large but government-run; Germany's 2026 defence budget (EUR 82.69bn) and D-LBO (EUR 11.5bn, prime-led through 2029) create integrator T&E demand; the UK's Digital Targeting Web and Asgard framework favour incremental software delivery. But allied T&E is likewise a government or prime function with its own labs and commercial emulators, budgets are smaller and slower (EDF/EDIP 12-18 months to grant), and the Lattice/NGC2/AO-conformance half of the product is U.S.-specific. Allies widen the lab-tool niche without changing its ceiling (E06 verdict: HYPOTHESIS, MEDIUM).
allied_extension.what_changes: Product: drop the NGC2/Lattice/AO modules and keep the TAK/CoT sync scoring and generic DDIL profiles; add FMN/STANAG-oriented message sets only if a CWIX delegation asks. Structure: a German GmbH (or partner) is needed for CIHBw pilots and EDF/EDIP eligibility, which complicates a later U.S. FOCI picture and is heavy for a $250k team; the German founder's U.S. permanent residence may pull management outside the EU for EU control tests (E06, specialist review required). Regulatory: no ITAR on the open core, but the Indonesian founder faces slower German personnel-security processes for any classified role. Go-to-market: through primes, NCIA and national hubs, never standalone.
markets: Germany (CIHBw pilots; D-LBO integrators Rheinmetall/blackned; German founder adjacency) - first allied option, still a lab-tool sale
NATO (CWIX 2027 via a national delegation; DIANA 2027 call if a resilient-C2 or test challenge appears - HYPOTHESIS)
United Kingdom (DASA, Asgard framework, DTW integrators) - open for entry, medium for revenue
Australia (ASCA, AUKUS Pillar II challenges) - only for a U.S./UK/AU-domiciled entity
Japan and Singapore - year-5+ markets, LOW near-term accessibility (E06)

goals: Answer the decisive doubt with evidence, not opinion: does any named office, lab, prime or vendor have money or a vehicle for a neutral DDIL/conformance bench?
Recruit the fatal-if-absent advisor: a former C5ISR Center / ATEC / JITC tactical-network T&E engineer on an equity or small-stipend basis.
Get counsel's written constraint memo on SBIR eligibility (13 CFR 121.702/121.103), the Indonesian founder's role, EAR classification of the open core, and a minimal technology control plan.
deliverables: 12-18 completed workflow interviews across at least 8 of the 12 target roles, transcribed and coded against the 14 questions
Written 'money map v1' naming, for each interviewee, the budget or vehicle they used for their last outside test purchase (or 'none')
Advisor letter of engagement signed
Counsel memo received; cap-table scenario model showing whether SBIR eligibility is reachable within 12 months
Event calendar with confirmed dates for TEM 16, NetModX 2027 call, next xTech hackathon, TAK Offsite 2027 and the next Jailbreak-series sprint (or documented that dates are not public)
weeks_1_3.owner: Business founder leads interviews, advisor recruiting and counsel; engineer founder attends every lab/prime interview and drafts the bench architecture in parallel
kill_criteria: KILL if fewer than 2 of the interviewed vendor or prime engineers can name a budget, PO or contract line under which they bought ANY outside test/emulation capability in the last 24 months.

KILL if zero of the government-side interviewees (C5ISR Center, ATEC/CJSIL, Army SWF/CTO pipeline, TAK Product Center) say a vendor-produced pre-event score would be read, and at least one says the CJSIL/NetModX infrastructure already covers it.
KILL if no qualified T&E advisor accepts by day 21 (score file: fatal if absent).
KILL (the venture framing, not the open-source build) if counsel confirms SBIR is unreachable within 12 months AND no non-SBIR sponsor candidate emerged from interviews.

goals: Prove technically that a reproducible score exposes DDIL failures that today surface live, using only public inputs.
Establish which link profiles and scenarios the advisor and at least one lab/prime interviewee consider realistic enough to matter.
deliverables: Dockerised bench v0.1: 8-10 ATAK-CIV emulator / TAK Server nodes behind Linux netem profiles (1 Mbps, 64 kbps, 16 kbps, 4 kbps, 1 kbps) with a YAML scenario language for partition schedules and reconnect storms; EMANE/CORE integration as a stretch goal only
Scorer v0.1 reporting time-to-arrival of priority CoT objects, duplicates/conflicts after reconnect, link saturation on reconnect, and a reconcile log, as JSON plus HTML

Experiment log: three public ATAK plugins or open CoT feeds run through a 30-minute 4 kbps partition-and-reconnect scenario, with at least one failure class reproduced across repeated runs (variance reported)
Advisor-reviewed link-profile and rubric note stating what is and is not realistic without controlled data
weeks_4_6.owner: Engineer founder builds and runs; business founder continues 4-6 further interviews (especially prime T&E and TAK Product Center) and starts the vendor pipeline for weeks 10-12
kill_criteria: KILL if the bench cannot reproduce at least one failure class (arrival order, duplicate tracks after reconnect, saturation) deterministically (same verdict in 4 of 5 repeated runs) by end of week 6.
KILL if the advisor and at least one lab/prime engineer judge that without controlled waveform models or radio traces the scores would not change any decision they make.
KILL if total build cost run-rate projects above $60,000 for the full 90 days (the surviving version is capped at $30-60k).

goals: Turn the experiment into a demonstrable prototype with the conformance module and a contract-test pack, packaged for a vendor to self-run.
Secure written commitments for at least three readiness runs and one lab or prime evaluation.
deliverables: ATAK plugin conformance module v0.1: exercises a plugin with synthetic roles and tagged data, emits an RBAC matrix, audit-event coverage and an SBOM (SPDX or CycloneDX) as a signed OSCAL-style assessment-results bundle; validated against one open-source ATAK plugin
Contract-test CLI v0.1 for CoT/TAK Server Mission API usage from a capture or spec; public Lattice schema validation included only if an interviewee asked for it
Public repository with documentation, a one-command demo and anonymised week-6 results; permissive licence chosen with counsel (data rights posture for a future SBIR/OTA documented)

Signed statements of intent: 3 vendors for a fixed-fee readiness run (target $5-15k each; free allowed for the first if it yields a named reference) and 1 lab or prime T&E cell agreeing to run the bench before its next event
NetModX 2027 / xTech hackathon / TAK Offsite 2027 applications drafted, with submission as soon as calls open
weeks_7_9.owner: Engineer founder (module, CLI, packaging); business founder (vendor commitments, lab/prime agreement, applications); advisor reviews the OSCAL bundle with an ISSM interviewee
kill_criteria: KILL if fewer than 3 vendors sign a statement of intent by end of week 9, or if all three insist on $0 - that confirms the 'episodic, low-price' market the score file predicted.
KILL if no government lab, ATEC/CJSIL contact or NGC2 team-lead T&E cell agrees in writing to run the bench (free) before an event - this is the direct test of 'no buyer needs it'.
KILL if an ISSM/AO-staff interviewee states the OSCAL-style bundle would carry no standing without government designation and no designation route can be named.

goals: Run the readiness engagements and the lab/prime evaluation; measure whether the report changed a decision.
Produce the final go/no-go memo on the venture question and the disposition of the open-source asset.
deliverables: 3 completed readiness runs with scored reports delivered to vendors, each followed by a 30-minute debrief recording what they changed (or not) as a result
1 lab or prime evaluation completed, with a written statement of whether the report was used and what it would take to be accepted as pre-event evidence
Live demonstration (TEM 16 networking, xTech hackathon, TAK Offsite 2027 or a team-lead session, whichever falls first) with a recorded run and Q&A notes

Final memo: revenue collected, cost to date, named sponsor candidates with budget/vehicle (or 'none'), and a decision among (a) continue as a small services line, (b) donate the bench to the community and pivot the founders to another gap, (c) pursue a subcontract/acqui-hire
If and only if the SBIR path is confirmed reachable: a draft xTech/SBIR white paper aligned to the next Army FUZE topic cycle
weeks_10_12.owner: Business founder runs engagements, debriefs and the memo; engineer founder runs the bench, fixes defects found in engagements and prepares the demo
kill_criteria: KILL if paid revenue by day 90 is under $10,000 total or fewer than 2 vendors say in the debrief that they changed code or configuration because of the report.
KILL if the lab or prime evaluation concludes with no written path to the report being accepted as evidence (no named office, no named event where it would be used).

KILL the venture question definitively if by day 90 no interviewee, lab, prime or office has named a budget line, task order, CSO area, OTA or SBIR topic under which a neutral bench could be bought within 12 months - and record this as the expected outcome, not a surprise.

CONTINUE (as a credibility/services asset only) if 2+ paying vendors, 1 lab/prime user and 1 documented pre-event prediction exist; escalate to a venture conversation ONLY on the milestone in most_important_question.milestone_for_next_2_5m.

most_important_question.build_first: A Dockerised, open-source TAK DDIL bench: 8-10 containerised ATAK-CIV/TAK Server nodes behind Linux netem (EMANE/CORE optional) profiles from 1 Mbps to 1 kbps with scripted 30-minute partitions and reconnect storms, a scorer that reports time-to-arrival of priority CoT objects, duplicate or conflicting objects after reconnect, link saturation on reconnect and a reconcile-log audit, plus an ATAK plugin conformance module that emits an RBAC matrix, audit-event coverage and an SBOM as a signed OSCAL-style bundle. Build nothing for Lattice or Ditto until an interviewee asks; keep the whole thing on public code and synthetic data so the non-U.S.-person founder can build it (INFERENCE; counsel to confirm). Cap: $30-60k and 3-4 months.
most_important_question.show_it_to: In this order: (1) three or four small vendors facing the next Jailbreak-series or Ivy Sting date (MatrixSpace/Adyton/AeroVironment-class and smaller API Marketplace participants); (2) one NGC2 team-member T&E engineer (Team Anduril or Team Lockheed Martin) and, through them, the team lead's T&E manager; (3) a DEVCOM C5ISR Center tactical-network S&T lead via the NetModX 2027 persistent-experimentation call and an ATEC/CJSIL integration engineer via the advisor; (4) a TAK Product Center engineer at TAK Offsite 2027. Do not lead with the Army CTO or CPE C2IN leadership - they have no test-tooling requirement to hand you.
most_important_question.demo_proves: That a reproducible, vendor-neutral score exposes, before an event, the specific failure classes that today are discovered live at Jailbreak and Ivy Sting - arrival order of priority objects, duplicate tracks after reconnect, saturation on reconnect, missing audit events - and that the same scenario file yields the same verdict across vendors and repeated runs. It also proves what it cannot do: it cannot reproduce PoR waveform behaviour or exercise captures without a lab sponsor, so realism plateaus at 'generic DDIL'.
most_important_question.why_customer_cares: A small vendor cares because failing at the sprint costs a fielding window and engineer weeks on site (~600 people at Fort Carson for one event), and a two-week-earlier warning is cheap relative to that. A team-lead T&E cell cares because comparable numbers help it triage dozens of members before an iteration. A government lab would care only if the bench saved instrumented lab time - but ATEC now embeds collection in each prototype and reports in 1-2 weeks, and C5ISR Center runs its own DDIL infrastructure, so the government's marginal need is close to zero (FACT: army.mil/article/295218; army.mil/article/293742).
most_important_question.why_incumbent_cant_crush: Honest answer: they can, and the more important point is that they need not bother. Anduril already gives away Lattice Sandboxes; TAK Product Center ships takcl and controls what 'conformant' means; Ditto can publish its own benchmark; C5ISR Center and ATEC/CJSIL own the labs and the acceptance authority. The startup's only differentiator is impartiality across TAK, Lattice and Ditto, which has value only if a government body designates the report as accepted evidence - and no public signal shows one intends to. The asset that is genuinely hard to copy is not the code but the founders' earned relationships with lab and prime T&E engineers and the published, comparable result set; that is a credibility asset and a hiring/acqui-hire lever, not a moat (score file: moat 1, incumbent vulnerability 1).
most_important_question.milestone_for_next_2_5m: Only an external designation would justify $2-5M: a written statement from DEVCOM C5ISR Center, ATEC, the Army CTO/AO or TAK Product Center that the bench's report is accepted pre-event or acceptance evidence, backed by a funded instrument (a task order under ACC-APG, a Phase II-scale SBIR or D2P2 after the cap table is eligible, or a CSO/OTA prototype agreement) AND at least one NGC2 team-lead subcontract to run it across its members - i.e., a named requirement owner, office, budget line and vehicle where today there are none. Measurable form: one signed government instrument of at least $500k plus one prime subcontract, and 10+ paying vendors at $10k+ each within 12 months. No public evidence suggests this event is coming inside the founders' runway; the plan above is designed to detect its absence cheaply and end with a reusable open-source asset and relationships rather than a company.

tech.title: Offline-first, EAR99-by-design structured orders, tasks, reports and LOGSTAT object layer with CRDT merge for TAK-CIV, sold first to public-safety incident command, National Guard and allied light units, with the merge model licensable to HQ planning and C2 platform owners
tech.version_designed_for: NARROWER NON-VENTURE VERSION named in G34-score.json (verdict: KILL as a venture; best-available bootstrappable path). Designed here: an open-source 'ICS objects for TAK' schema plus a TAK Server-side extension that stores ICS 201/204/209/214 and a resource/status ledger (the civil analogue of LOGSTAT) as CRDT-merged mission objects, with an ATAK-CIV plugin, a thin iOS companion app (iTAK accepts no plugins) and a web companion for the incident command post, transported over TAK Server Data Sync missions, FirstNet/LTE and Meshtastic LoRa. Stewarded with the TAK Public Safety community and WFTAK; monetised only through hosting, support and training to state wildland agencies and incident management teams. The Guard variant is kept ONLY as a no-cost drill-weekend probe of willingness to pay (no program office exists), the allied variant is deferred to a possible NATO DIANA 2028 application, and the 'license the merge model to HQ/C2 platform owners' line is DROPPED (CRDT engines are open source; Ditto already sells CRDT sync for ATAK). Every milestone below tests the decisive doubt: does any named agency, IMT, Guard unit or platform owner pay for this rather than use free TAK Data Sync plus its existing IMS? This is an open-source-plus-services or acquihire path, not a venture-scale company, and the plan is written so the founders can kill it cheaply.

architecture.prose: INPUTS. Structured entries typed by the planning section (ICS 201 briefing, 202 objectives, 204 assignment lists, 209 status summary, 214 unit log) and by field elements (division/group status, resource check-in, quantities of crews/engines/water/fuel, the civil analogue of a LOGSTAT); ATAK position (PLI) and map markers already flowing as Cursor-on-Target (CoT); CSV/PDF exports from an existing IMS (WebEOC, Tablet Command, Intterra) or from the interagency resource ordering system where an MOU allows; and public incident data (perimeters, weather) used only as demo context. COMPUTE. Commercial Android end-user devices running ATAK-CIV with the plugin; iOS phones/tablets running a native companion app (because iTAK has no third-party plugin model, FACT from the Meshtastic 2026-02 blog in G34 evidence); a command-post laptop or small server running TAK Server (open source, GPLv3, FACT from the TAK-Product-Center/Server LICENSE.md fetched 2026-09-25) with the structured-objects extension, or OpenTAKServer where an agency prefers it; an optional hosted multi-tenant instance for agencies without IT staff. CORE SOFTWARE. (1) A public JSON schema for ICS objects (form, field, list-of-assignments, resource ledger entries) versioned and published under Apache-2.0 so TPC, IMS vendors and the community can adopt it; (2) a CRDT document per incident built on Automerge (MIT; 3.0 in 2025 cut memory 10x, FACT per BigGo 2025-08) or Loro (MIT; smaller encodings per loro.dev benchmarks) with a form-tuned merge policy: per-field last-writer-wins with causal history for text, add-wins list/set merges for assignment rosters, and a counter/ledger discipline for quantities in which each node records signed deltas against a named resource rather than overwriting totals, so a partition never silently double-subtracts; (3) an explicit conflict surface that flags any quantity or assignment where two nodes made incompatible decisions (same crew assigned to two divisions) for a human to resolve; (4) a compact delta codec (protobuf, ~100-300 bytes per field edit) with store-and-forward queueing sized for LoRa; (5) a form renderer and PDF exporter producing the standard FEMA ICS form layouts (NIMS ICS Forms Booklet, public) so the paper-era workflow is preserved; (6) an audit/history view (who changed what, when, from which node) that doubles as the ICS 214 unit log. INTERFACES. TAK Server Mission API / Data Sync (missions hold CoT, files, logs and change feeds and re-sync data missed while disconnected, FACT per TAK Server README and OpenTAKServer docs): the extension stores each CRDT change as a mission content item so any TAK Server, including government ones the team never touches, can carry the deltas; CoT XML/protobuf for map overlays of assignments (division boundaries, resource icons); the ATAK-CIV plugin SDK 5.5 (Jetpack Compose support, FACT per RIIS blog 2026) for the Android UI; the Meshtastic protobuf/ATAK-forwarder path for LoRa transport between nodes with no server reachable (peer-to-peer CRDT gossip); EDXL-SitRep 1.0 (OASIS, 2013) export, which already maps ICS-201/203/207/209/215 (FACT per OASIS docs), for handoff to WebEOC-class systems; REST/WebSocket for the iOS and web companions. OUTPUTS. The next operational period's ICS 204s and the incident's 209 generated from merged objects; a resource status board; PDF/printed forms; a TAK map overlay of assignments; an EDXL-SitRep/CSV handoff to the agency's existing IMS. USER. Incident commander, planning section chief, resource unit leader and division supervisors on a Type 1-4 incident; the equivalent staff on a Guard drill weekend (S3/S4/battle captain) as a probe; later, a state wildland agency technology lead as the buyer of hosting/support.

architecture.hardest_problem: Not the CRDT algorithm (commodity) but the FORM SEMANTICS of merge under partition: ICS assignments and quantities are decisions, not text, so a mathematically correct merge can be operationally wrong (two divisions each 'take' the last engine; a crew is on two 204s; a 209 total is summed from stale ledgers). The hard engineering is (a) a schema and merge policy in which quantities are ledgers of signed deltas with causal context, assignments are add-wins sets with uniqueness invariants, and every invariant violation is surfaced to a named role rather than auto-resolved; (b) making that policy identical across three code bases (Kotlin plugin, Swift companion, TypeScript web) with a shared Rust/WASM core so behaviour never diverges; and (c) carrying the deltas across heterogeneous transports (TAK mission sync via server, peer-to-peer LoRa with ~200-byte packets and loss, LTE) with idempotent, reorderable application and bounded queue growth over a 6-12 hour partition. The demo must show convergence and correct conflict surfacing on all three platforms simultaneously; that is where prior tools (queue-and-replay IMS, Data Sync missions) stop.

must_be_proprietary: Honest answer: almost nothing can be proprietary and the score file says so. The only assets worth holding back from open source are (1) the hosted multi-tenant service, its tenancy/security hardening and GovRAMP artifacts, (2) the agency-specific import/export adapters (WebEOC, Tablet Command, state resource systems) built under paid pilots, and (3) training curricula and exercise playbooks. architecture.integration_burden: Medium for the demo, high for revenue. Demo: one TAK Server with the extension, one ATAK plugin, one iOS app, one web page and Meshtastic nodes - all interfaces are documented and open, so two founders plus one iOS contractor can integrate them in 3-5 months. Revenue: every paying agency has a different IMS (WebEOC, Tablet Command, Intterra, Veoci; DHS SAVER 2022 lists 10+), different resource-ordering exports, different device policies (MDM, iOS majority) and different security reviews; each adds 2-6 weeks of adapter and onboarding work, which is services revenue, not product. mvp.demo: A 'partition-and-merge' exercise on commercial hardware: five field devices (three Android with ATAK-CIV plugin, two iOS with the companion app) and one command-post laptop running TAK Server plus the structured-objects extension, all seeded with a synthetic Type 3 wildland incident (public perimeter data, fictional resources). The command post publishes ICS 202 objectives and ICS 204s for operational period 1. Networks are then deliberately cut: two devices continue on Meshtastic LoRa only, two go fully dark, the laptop 'displaces' (restarts on a second machine restoring from local state). For 6 simulated hours every node edits the same assignments, check-ins and quantities (crews moved between divisions, engines reassigned, water and fuel consumed, a 214 log kept on each device). On reconnect the observer measures convergence time, bytes transferred, lost updates (must be zero) and the conflict queue (which must contain exactly the double-assignment and over-allocation cases scripted into the scenario). The planning section then generates operational period 2's ICS 204s and the 209 from the merged state, timed against a control group doing the same on paper/Word. The same engine is shown a second time with FRAGO/SITREP templates for a Guard S3 on a drill weekend, purely to ask whether anyone there would pay.
must_prove: Multi-writer edits to assignments, check-ins and quantities made during a 6-hour partition merge with zero lost updates and no duplicates on Android, iOS and web simultaneously (technical doubt)
Decision conflicts (same crew on two 204s, over-allocated resource) are surfaced, not silently merged, and are resolved by the resource unit leader in under a minute each (semantic doubt)
Deltas fit LoRa: a 6-hour partition of realistic edits syncs over a Meshtastic-only path within 10 minutes (transport doubt)
The next period's ICS 204s and 209 are produced at least 40% faster than the paper/Word control with fewer transcription errors (value doubt)

DECISIVE: at least one named agency, IMT or Guard unit with a budget line or purchasing vehicle states in writing that it would pay (LOI or purchase intent for a paid pilot of at least $10k) rather than use free TAK Data Sync plus its existing IMS; and TPC/TAK Public Safety do not signal that form objects are coming natively (market doubt - this is what the kill verdict rests on)

build_plan.work: Customer discovery in parallel with architecture: 10-15 interviews (IMT planning section chiefs, state wildland technology leads incl. WFTAK/Colorado CoE, TAK Public Safety board, two municipal fire TAK users, one Guard S3, one IMS vendor). Choose CRDT engine (Automerge vs Loro) by benchmarking encoded delta size for ICS 204 edits; publish v0.1 ICS object JSON schema (201/204/209/214 + resource ledger) on GitHub under Apache-2.0; stand up TAK Server + OpenTAKServer test rigs; write the partition test harness (scripted edit streams, network cut/restore, metrics capture).

Core: Rust/WASM merge core with form-tuned policy (LWW text, add-wins assignment sets, signed-delta quantity ledger, invariant checker producing a conflict queue); protobuf delta codec; TAK Server-side structured-objects service writing deltas as mission content and consuming the mission change feed. Web companion (TypeScript) for the command post with 204/209 rendering and PDF export. Start iOS contractor on the Swift companion against the REST/WebSocket API.

ATAK-CIV plugin (SDK 5.5, Compose UI) with offline local store, mission-content sync and CoT overlay of assignments; Meshtastic transport path (delta fragmentation, ack/idempotent apply, gossip between nodes with no server). First end-to-end partition test on three Android + web; fix convergence and queue-growth issues; measure bytes per edit against the < 200-byte target.

iOS companion reaches parity for all object types; full five-device + displacement test run three times with metrics recorded; conflict-surfacing accuracy tuned on scripted double-assignment cases; ICS 214 audit view; EDXL-SitRep export of 201/209. Advisor review of form fidelity against the FEMA booklet. Package: install guide (< 15 min target), TAK Server docker image, TAK.gov CIV plugin submission prepared.

Field demo #1 at a state wildland exercise, IMT training or TAK Public Safety event under MOU, with a paper/Word control group timed on producing the next period's 204s; collect written feedback and the decisive question: who would pay, from which line, via which vehicle. Optional Guard drill-weekend probe with FRAGO/SITREP templates on synthetic data only.

Decision month: compile evidence against kill criteria; if at least one paid-pilot commitment exists, scope the hosted tier and GovRAMP Snapshot/Core self-assessment and apply for the TAK.gov plugin listing; if none exists, hand the schema and reference implementation to TAK Public Safety/WFTAK as open source and stop, or pursue acquihire conversations (Ditto, TPC contractors, IMS vendors) with the demo as the asset.

kill_criteria: By end of month 6, no named agency, IMT or Guard unit with identified budget authority has committed in writing to a paid pilot of at least $10,000 or signed an LOI for a hosting/support subscription (the decisive market test)

Fewer than 4 of 12+ discovery interviewees rank 'picture diverges after disconnect / re-keying forms each period' among their top three operational pains, or most say free TAK Data Sync plus their existing IMS is sufficient
TPC, WFTAK or an IMS vendor (Tablet Command, Intterra, Resgrid) publicly announces or ships structured ICS objects with multi-writer offline merge before month 6
iOS companion cannot reach object-type parity within the $30k contractor budget, leaving the iOS-majority wildland user base unreachable
Technical targets missed after two fix cycles: any lost update in the five-device test, convergence over LoRa > 30 min for the 6-hour scenario, or conflict false-flag rate > 15%
The exercise control group produces period-2 forms as fast as the tool (no measured time saving), indicating the value is in the partition case only, which is too episodic to sell
Counsel advises the product or its intended Guard/allied use cannot be kept within EAR jurisdiction without excluding the non-U.S.-person founder from core development

capital_map.does_250k_reach_next_fundable_milestone: Yes for the bootstrapping milestone, no for a venture milestone. $250k covers Stage 0 ($6-20k), Stage 1 ($55-100k) and most or all of Stage 2 ($110-240k) at the low-to-mid assumptions, i.e., a working three-platform partition-and-merge MVP, a live exercise with a named agency and the decisive answer on willingness to pay, with $20-80k of headroom if founders take minimal stipends. It does NOT reach the milestone that the score file says would justify $2-5M of venture capital (20+ paying agencies or a state enterprise contract plus a licensing/integration LOI from a platform owner), and this analysis agrees that milestone is unlikely to be reached at all because the licensing buyer has no reason to pay for an open-source merge model and agency ACVs are too small to fund a sales team. The realistic 'next fundable' events after $250k are: (a) a state or multi-agency hosting/support contract that funds Stage 3 from revenue (bootstrapping), (b) a DHS S&T or NSF-style non-dilutive award only if the cap table is restructured to pass the >50% U.S.-person ownership test (needs counsel), or (c) an acquihire. Founders should treat $250k as the budget to get a clean yes/no by month 9-11, not as seed capital for a company.
capital_map.next_milestone: Stage 2 exit: a live exercise with a named state wildland agency or IMT showing >= 40% faster period-2 ICS 204 production with zero re-keying across Android/iOS/web after a 6-hour partition, plus at least one signed paid pilot (>= $10k) or state-level hosting/support LOI naming the budget line and vehicle, plus a written position from TPC/WFTAK on whether native form objects are planned
capital_map.assumptions: All figures are analyst estimates (HYPOTHESIS, LOW-MEDIUM confidence) for a software-only, unclassified, EAR-jurisdiction (EAR99 or 5D002/ENC per E07-F32, counsel to confirm) product with no SBIR, no ATO and no CUI in Stages 0-2. Hardware prices for LoRa nodes are FACT from June 2026 price surveys; EUD prices are RECALL not re-verified. GovRAMP/StateRAMP cost figures are ranges because the program publishes tiers (Snapshot/Core without 3PAO; Ready/Authorized with 3PAO) but not fixed prices (FACT per GovRAMP FAQ and consultancy guides, 2025-2026). Guard and allied lines are probes only; if either is pursued seriously, compliance and legal lines roughly double (TAK-GOV gating, Army network ATO, ITAR defense-service review per E07-F15) and the non-U.S.-person founder's role would need counsel. Salaries assume founders and early hires accept below-market pay; market-rate salaries raise Stage 3-4 by 40-60%.

engineering_risks.risk: Generic CRDT merge silently produces operationally wrong results for decisions and quantities (double-assigned crews, over-allocated resources, stale totals)
engineering_risks.mitigation: Design the schema as ledgers and sets with explicit invariants; the demo scripts these exact cases and must show them in the conflict queue, not auto-resolved; measure false-flag rate

engineering_risks.risk: Three code bases (Kotlin plugin, Swift companion, TypeScript web) diverge in merge behaviour
engineering_risks.mitigation: Single Rust core compiled to JNI/WASM/Swift bindings; a shared conformance test suite of recorded partition scenarios run in CI against all three; the demo runs all three platforms simultaneously

engineering_risks.risk: Deltas do not fit LoRa packet and duty-cycle limits, so the Meshtastic path is unusable for real incident volumes
engineering_risks.mitigation: Benchmark Automerge vs Loro encodings in month 1; fragment and prioritise (assignments and quantities before free text); the demo measures bytes per edit and LoRa-only convergence for a 6-hour scenario; if it fails, restrict LoRa to status/quantity objects and rely on FirstNet for text

engineering_risks.risk: TAK Server Mission API or ATAK plugin API changes across releases break the extension
engineering_risks.mitigation: Store deltas as opaque mission content (the most stable primitive), test against TAK Server and OpenTAKServer in CI, and keep a server-independent peer path; budget one maintenance sprint per ATAK release

engineering_risks.risk: GPLv3 copyleft on TAK Server entangles the extension or the hosted service
engineering_risks.mitigation: Run the structured-objects service as a separate process using the public Mission API; get written counsel on the boundary in Stage 1; publish the core as Apache-2.0 anyway since openness is the adoption strategy

engineering_risks.risk: iOS App Store review or MDM policies block the companion app or its background sync
engineering_risks.mitigation: Design for foreground sync with push-to-refresh plus a background-fetch budget; use standard location permissions; test with one agency's MDM early; keep the web companion as the fallback for iPads

engineering_risks.risk: Agencies store responder PII and location, triggering security reviews and CJIS-adjacent expectations the founders cannot meet
engineering_risks.mitigation: Minimise PII in the schema (roles and resource IDs, not personal data), encrypt at rest, offer on-prem TAK Server deployment as the default and hosted only as the paid tier; GovRAMP Snapshot self-assessment in Stage 2

engineering_risks.risk: The value shows only in the partition case, which is episodic; day-to-day form production is no faster than paper
engineering_risks.mitigation: The exercise includes a timed control group on period-2 form production; if there is no measured saving the kill criterion fires and the schema is donated to the community

engineering_risks.risk: TPC adds form objects to Data Sync, or an IMS vendor adds offline multi-writer merge, during the build
engineering_risks.mitigation: Ask TPC and WFTAK directly in Stage 0 and record the answer; keep the build short (4 months) and open source so the outcome is still a usable community asset or acquihire portfolio, not a stranded product

engineering_risks.risk: Scope drift toward Guard/allied features pulls the codebase or the team's activities toward controlled technical data or ITAR 'defense services' (E07-F15) and complicates the non-U.S.-person founder's role
engineering_risks.mitigation: Keep the Guard drill weekend a synthetic-data probe on TAK-CIV only; no unit data, no TAK-GOV builds, no integration work for a foreign military without export-control counsel; document the EAR classification memo before any such contact

gtm.title: Offline-first, EAR99-by-design structured orders, tasks, reports and LOGSTAT object layer with CRDT merge for TAK-CIV, sold first to public-safety incident command, National Guard and allied light units, with the merge model licensable to HQ planning and C2 platform owners
gtm.version_designed_for: NARROWER NON-VENTURE VERSION named in G34-score.json narrower_version_if_borderline: an open-source 'ICS objects for TAK' schema plus TAK Server extension (ICS 201/204/209/214 and a resource/LOGSTAT-style ledger as CRDT-merged Data Sync mission objects) with an ATAK-CIV plugin and an iOS/web companion, stewarded with the TAK Public Safety community and the WFTAK/COTAK state wildland programs, monetized through hosting/support subscriptions to state wildland agencies and incident management teams. The Guard line is kept ONLY as an unfunded drill-weekend credibility test, the allied line ONLY as an optional 2028 DIANA application, and the 'license the merge model' revenue line is DROPPED (commoditized by Automerge/Yjs/Ditto). Verdict was KILL as a venture; this plan therefore treats G34 as a bootstrappable open-source-plus-hosting business whose 90 days must answer one decisive doubt: does ANY named agency, state TAK program or IMT with a budget line pay for structured offline ICS objects rather than using free TAK Data Sync plus its existing IMS? Every milestone below tests that doubt with a measurable kill criterion. This is not a venture-scale company and the plan does not pretend it is.

links.value: Incident command posts, field divisions and higher coordination centers that already run TAK on unclassified networks still carry assignments (ICS 204), status (ICS 209/214) and resource/sustainment status as paper, chat, voice and spreadsheets; when nodes reconnect after working disconnected, edits made in parallel do not merge and staff re-key by hand, so the picture diverges between ICP, field and higher.
links.detail: FACT that TAK Data Sync re-syncs map items/files/chat but carries no structured form objects and no multi-writer merge (Google Play Data Sync listing, TPC; OpenTAKServer Mission API docs 2025-2026). FACT that public-safety TAK use is routine (DHS S&T/HS Today; WFTAK; Green Bay Fire + FirstNet 2025). INFERENCE that the disconnected multi-writer conflict is episodic rather than daily (score file criterion 1 = 3/5); the daily pain is form re-keying per operational period. Severity is tolerated today.

links.value: Incident commander, planning section chief, resource unit leader and situation unit leader on Type 1-3 incident management teams; state wildland fire dispatch/technology leads running WFTAK or a state TAK program (COTAK, Colorado); municipal fire TAK administrators; secondary: National Guard battalion S3/S4 and battle captain on state active duty (unfunded credibility test only).

FACT: COTAK runs a 2026 COTAK Summit (cotak.gov schedule page surfaced 2026-09; date not verified - .gov blocked). FACT: Guard units use ATAK on domestic missions (nationalguard.mil ATAK video; CivTAK National Guard archive) but no Guard requirement for structured offline reports found - Public evidence insufficient.

Each agency/IMT sets its own; NWCG (National Wildfire Coordinating Group) sets interagency wildland standards and hosts IM Tools & Technology/WFMRDA but does not buy; FEMA NIMS defines ICS form standards but does not buy; for the Guard, no validated requirement exists (Public evidence insufficient).

This is the first weak link.

procurement_signal.rationale: There is no government RFI -> sources sought -> prototype -> production sequence for this product because the civil buyer never runs one: public-safety incident management software is a mature, multi-vendor commercial category (DHS SAVER 2022, FACT HIGH) bought agency by agency on grants and operating budgets, and TAK itself is free government software whose sync layer (Data Sync) is already in production. The only formal procurement signals are on the military side (PM MC OMCS RFI, SBMC prototype awards, Onebrief follow-on) and those are being closed by funded incumbents, which is exactly why G34 retreated to public safety. The TAK-native structured-objects slice is 'Emerging' in the narrow sense that nobody ships it, but absence of a vendor is not evidence of demand; the recurring signals (annual HSGP NOFO, annual CivTAK/TAK Offsite, TAK Public Safety founded 2024) show a mature adoption curve for TAK in public safety, not a procurement pipeline for this feature. Confidence MEDIUM.

entry_sequence.eligibility_notes: No ownership test for direct commercial sales or OTS (E07-F22). SBIR/STTR (DHS, Army) is NOT available without a >50% U.S.-person-owned cap table (13 CFR 121.702) - counsel; STRATFI/TACFI are therefore also closed (they require SBIR Phase II lineage). Hosted service may trigger state security reviews, CJIS-adjacent questions and StateRAMP for some buyers - budget for it only after a paying customer asks. Register in SAM.gov and obtain a UEI early (federal), and register as a vendor with each state.
entry_sequence.what_it_yields: The first revenue and the only metric that matters for the kill decision: paying agencies and ACV. If 12 months after CivTAK 2026 there are fewer than 3 paying agencies or ARR under $50k, the business is a hobby or an acquihire pitch, not a company.
